1979.english:
We currently believe that equity markets in 1980 are likely to evolve in a manner that will result in an underperformance by our portfolio for the first time in recent years.  We very much like the companies in which we have major investments, and plan no changes to try to attune ourselves to the markets of a specific year.

Since we have covered our philosophy regarding equities extensively in recent annual reports, a more extended discussion of bond investments may be appropriate for this one, particularly in light of what has happened since yearend.  An extraordinary amount of money has been lost by the insurance industry in the bond area - notwithstanding the accounting convention that allows insurance companies to carry their bond investments at amortized cost, regardless of impaired market value.  Actually, that very accounting convention may have contributed in a major way to the losses; had management been forced to recognize market values, its attention might have been focused much earlier on the dangers of a very long-term bond contract.
1979.chinese:
我们目前认为，1980年股票市场可能呈现一种变化，使我们的投资组合多年来第一次落后于市场表现。我们非常喜欢自己主要投资的那些公司，也不打算为了适应某一年的股市行情而调整持仓。

由于近年来的年报已经充分讨论了我们的股票投资哲学，今年更有必要较详细地谈谈债券投资，尤其要考虑年末之后已经发生的事情。保险业在债券投资上损失了极其巨额的资金——尽管会计惯例允许保险公司无论债券市值遭受多大损害，仍按摊余成本计价。实际上，正是这项会计惯例可能在很大程度上促成了亏损：假如管理层必须确认债券的市场价值，也许会更早注意到超长期债券合同的危险。

1979.english: Ironically, many insurance companies have decided that a one-year auto policy is inappropriate during a time of inflation, and six-month policies have been brought in as replacements. “How,” say many of the insurance managers, “can we be expected to look forward twelve months and estimate such imponderables as hospital costs, auto parts prices, etc.?” But, having decided that one year is too long a period for which to set a fixed price for insurance in an inflationary world, they then have turned around, taken the proceeds from the sale of that six-month policy, and sold the money at a fixed price for thirty or forty years.
1979.chinese: 讽刺的是，许多保险公司认为，在通货膨胀时期，一年期汽车保险保单不合适，于是用六个月保单代替。一些保险经理会问：“我们怎么可能预测未来十二个月的住院费用、汽车零件价格等如此难以估量的事情？”但他们刚刚认定，在通胀世界里，为保险固定价格整整一年都太久，转过身来，却把出售六个月保单获得的资金，以固定价格借出去三十年、四十年。

1979.english: The very long-term bond contract has been the last major fixed price contract of extended duration still regularly initiated in an inflation-ridden world.  The buyer of money to be used between 1980 and 2020 has been able to obtain a firm price now for each year of its use while the buyer of auto insurance, medical services, newsprint, office space - or just about any other product or service - would be greeted with laughter if he were to request a firm price now to apply through 1985.  For in virtually all other areas of commerce, parties to long-term contracts now either index prices in some manner, or insist on the right to review the situation every year or so.
1979.chinese: 长期债券合同，是在通胀肆虐的世界里，仍然经常新订立的最后一种期限极长的固定价格合同。1980年至2020年期间需要使用资金的借款人，如今却能事先锁定这些年份每一年的资金使用价格；而想购买汽车保险、医疗服务、新闻纸、办公空间——或者几乎任何其他产品或服务的人，如果要求今天就锁定直到1985年的价格，只会招来嘲笑。因为在几乎所有其他商业领域里，长期合同的当事人如今不是以某种方式将价格与指数挂钩，就是坚持每隔大约一年重新审视价格的权利。

1979.english:
A cultural lag has prevailed in the bond area.  The buyers (borrowers) and middlemen (underwriters) of money hardly could be expected to raise the question of whether it all made sense, and the sellers (lenders) slept through an economic and contractual revolution.

For the last few years our insurance companies have not been a net purchaser of any straight long-term bonds (those without conversion rights or other attributes offering profit possibilities).  There have been some purchases in the straight bond area, of course, but they have been offset by sales or maturities.  Even prior to this period, we never would buy thirty or forty-year bonds; instead we tried to concentrate in the straight bond area on shorter issues with sinking funds and on issues that seemed relatively undervalued because of bond market inefficiencies.
1979.chinese:
债券领域出现了文化上的滞后。买钱的人（借款者）和中间商（承销商）当然不能指望会主动质疑这种安排是否合理；而卖钱的人（贷款者）却在这场经济与合同制度的变革中睡了过去。

过去几年，我们的保险公司没有成为任何普通长期债券的净买家；这里的“普通”是指没有转换权或其他潜在获利特征的债券。当然，我们买过一些普通债券，但都被卖出或到期收回的债券抵消了。即使在更早的时候，我们也从不购买三四十年期债券，而是尽量在普通债券中，集中买入有偿债基金安排的较短期限债券，以及因债券市场效率不足而显得相对低估的品种。

1979.english: However, the mild degree of caution that we exercised was an improper response to the world unfolding about us.  You do not adequately protect yourself by being half awake while others are sleeping.  It was a mistake to buy fifteen-year bonds, and yet we did; we made an even more serious mistake in not selling them (at losses, if necessary) when our present views began to crystallize. (Naturally, those views are much clearer and definite in retrospect; it would be fair for you to ask why we weren’t writing about this subject last year.)
1979.chinese: 不过，面对正在我们周围展开的世界，我们的谨慎程度仍然不够。别人都在睡觉时，你只是半睡半醒，仍不足以保护自己。购买十五年期债券是错误，而我们确实买了；更严重的错误是，当如今的看法开始逐渐成形时，我们没有及时卖掉它们——即使必须承受损失也应该卖。（当然，这些看法在回顾过去时总显得更清楚、更确定；各位完全有理由问，我们为什么去年不写这个问题。）

1979.english: Of course, we must hold significant amounts of bonds or other fixed dollar obligations in conjunction with our insurance operations.  In the last several years our net fixed dollar commitments have been limited to the purchase of convertible bonds.  We believe that the conversion options obtained, in effect, give that portion of the bond portfolio a far shorter average life than implied by the maturity terms of the issues (i.e., at an appropriate time of our choosing, we can terminate the bond contract by conversion into stock).
1979.chinese: 当然，为了经营保险业务，我们必须持有相当数量的债券或其他固定美元支付义务。近几年，我们在固定美元投资方面的净新增投入，仅限于购买可转换债券。我们认为，获得的转换权实际上使这部分债券组合的平均期限，大大短于其法律到期日所显示的期限。（也就是说，我们可以在自己选择的合适时间，通过转股来终止债券合同。）

1979.english: This bond policy has given us significantly lower unrealized losses than those experienced by the great majority of property and casualty insurance companies.  We also have been helped by our strong preference for equities in recent years that has kept our overall bond segment relatively low.  Nevertheless, we are taking our lumps in bonds and feel that, in a sense, our mistakes should be viewed less charitably than the mistakes of those who went about their business unmindful of the developing problems.
1979.chinese: 这种债券政策，使我们未实现的损失显著低于绝大多数财产及意外伤害保险公司。近几年我们强烈偏好股票，使债券投资在总体资产中的比重比较低，这也给了我们帮助。但即便如此，我们在债券上仍承受了损失，而且从某种意义上说，我们的错误比那些对发展中的问题浑然不觉、照常做生意的人更不值得原谅。

1979.english:
Harking back to our textile experience, we should have realized the futility of trying to be very clever (via sinking funds and other special type issues) in an area where the tide was running heavily against us.

We have severe doubts as to whether a very long-term fixed- interest bond, denominated in dollars, remains an appropriate business contract in a world where the value of dollars seems almost certain to shrink by the day.  Those dollars, as well as paper creations of other governments, simply may have too many structural weaknesses to appropriately serve as a unit of long term commercial reference.  If so, really long bonds may turn out to be obsolete instruments and insurers who have bought those maturities of 2010 or 2020 could have major and continuing problems on their hands.  We, likewise, will be unhappy with our fifteen-year bonds and will annually pay a price in terms of earning power that reflects that mistake.
1979.chinese:
回想纺织业务的经验，我们本应意识到：在大趋势明显对自己不利的领域，即使试图通过偿债基金安排和其他特殊债券品种来表现得格外聪明，最终也可能徒劳无功。

我们严重怀疑，在美元价值似乎几乎肯定逐日缩水的世界里，以美元计价的超长期固定利率债券，是否仍是一种合适的商业合同。美元以及其他政府创造的纸币，或许在结构上存在太多弱点，无法恰当地充当长期商业价值的计量单位。如果确实如此，真正的长期债券可能会成为过时的工具，那些购买了2010年或2020年到期债券的保险公司，就可能面对重大而持续的问题。同样，我们持有的十五年期债券也会让自己不快，未来每年都要以盈利能力受损的方式，为这一错误付出代价。

1979.english:
Some of our convertible bonds appear exceptionally attractive to us, and have the same sort of earnings retention factor (applicable to the stock into which they may be converted) that prevails in our conventional equity portfolio.  We expect to make money in these bonds (we already have, in a few cases) and have hopes that our profits in this area may offset losses in straight bonds.

And, of course, there is the possibility that our present analysis is much too negative.  The chances for very low rates of inflation are not nil.  Inflation is man-made; perhaps it can be man-mastered.  The threat which alarms us may also alarm legislators and other powerful groups, prompting some appropriate response.
1979.chinese:
有些可转换债券对我们而言显得格外有吸引力，它们对应的可转换股票具有与我们普通股投资组合类似的留存利润因素。我们预计会在这些债券上赚钱（个别案例已经赚到钱），并希望这方面的利润能够抵消普通债券上的亏损。

当然，也存在另一种可能：我们现在的分析过于悲观。出现非常低通胀率的可能性并非为零。通胀是人造成的；也许人能够制服它。令我们担忧的威胁，也可能同样引起立法者和其他有影响力团体的警觉，从而促使他们采取适当措施。

1979.english: Furthermore, present interest rates incorporate much higher inflation projections than those of a year or two ago.  Such rates may prove adequate or more than adequate to protect bond buyers.  We even may miss large profits from a major rebound in bond prices.  However, our unwillingness to fix a price now for a pound of See’s candy or a yard of Berkshire cloth to be delivered in 2010 or 2020 makes us equally unwilling to buy bonds which set a price on money now for use in those years.  Overall, we opt for Polonius (slightly restated): “Neither a short-term borrower nor a long-term lender be.”
1979.chinese: 此外，当前利率已包含了远高于一两年前的通胀预期。这样的利率也许足够、甚至绰绰有余，能够保护债券买家。我们甚至可能错失债券价格大幅反弹带来的巨额利润。但我们既然不愿意今天就为2010年或2020年交付的一磅喜诗糖果或一码伯克希尔布料约定固定价格，也同样不愿购买今天就为那些年份使用的资金规定固定价格的债券。总体而言，我们选择接受波洛涅斯（Polonius）那句略加改写的忠告：“既不做短期借款人，也不做长期贷款人。”

1979.english:
Banking

This will be the last year that we can report on the Illinois National Bank and Trust Company as a subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway.  Therefore, it is particularly pleasant to report that, under Gene Abegg’s and Pete Jeffrey’s management, the bank broke all previous records and earned approximately 2.3% on average assets last year, a level again over three times that achieved by the average major bank, and more than double that of banks regarded as outstanding.  The record is simply extraordinary, and the shareholders of Berkshire Hathaway owe a standing ovation to Gene Abegg for the performance this year and every year since our purchase in 1969.
1979.chinese:
## 银行业务

这将是我们最后一年能够把伊利诺伊国民银行及信托公司（Illinois National Bank and Trust Company）作为伯克希尔子公司向各位报告。因此，格外令人高兴的是，我们能够报告：在吉恩·阿贝格（Gene Abegg）和皮特·杰弗里（Pete Jeffrey）的管理下，银行再次打破所有历史纪录，去年利润约相当于平均资产的2.3%。这一比例又一次超过大型银行平均水平的三倍，也超过那些被认为十分出色的银行的两倍。这样的经营记录确实非同凡响。对于今年的成绩，以及我们1969年收购以来每一年的表现，伯克希尔·哈撒韦的股东都应该起立向吉恩·阿贝格鼓掌致敬。

1979.english: As you know, the Bank Holding Company Act of 1969 requires that we divest the bank by December 31, 1980.  For some years we have expected to comply by effecting a spin-off during 1980. However, the Federal Reserve Board has taken the firm position that if the bank is spun off, no officer or director of Berkshire Hathaway can be an officer or director of the spun-off bank or bank holding company, even in a case such as ours in which one individual would own over 40% of both companies.
1979.chinese: 各位知道，《1969年银行控股公司法》要求我们在1980年12月31日之前剥离这家银行。几年来，我们一直预计会在1980年通过分拆分配股权的方式履行这项要求。然而，美联储理事会采取了明确立场：如果银行被分拆出去，伯克希尔的任何高管或董事都不得再担任这家分拆银行或其控股公司的高管或董事，即使是在我们这样的特殊情形下——同一个人将同时拥有两家公司超过40%的股权。

1979.english: Under these conditions, we are investigating the possible sale of between 80% and 100% of the stock of the bank.  We will be most choosy about any purchaser, and our selection will not be based solely on price.  The bank and its management have treated us exceptionally well and, if we have to sell, we want to be sure that they are treated equally as well.  A spin-off still is a possibility if a fair price along with a proper purchaser cannot be obtained by early fall.
1979.chinese: 在这种条件下，我们正在研究出售银行80%至100%股份的可能性。我们会非常谨慎地选择买家，绝不会只看价格。这家银行及其管理团队一直以非凡的方式对待我们；如果必须出售，我们也希望确保他们获得同样良好的待遇。如果到初秋仍找不到合适的买家和公平的价格，分拆仍是一个选择。

1979.english:
However, you should be aware that we do not expect to be able to fully, or even in very large part, replace the earning power represented by the bank from the proceeds of the sale of the bank.  You simply can’t buy high quality businesses at the sort of price/earnings multiple likely to prevail on our bank sale.

## Financial Reporting

During 1979, NASDAQ trading was initiated in the stock of Berkshire Hathaway This means that the stock now is quoted on the Over-the-Counter page of the Wall Street journal under “Additional OTC Quotes”.  Prior to such listing, the Wall Street journal and the Dow-Jones news ticker would not report our earnings, even though such earnings were one hundred or more times the level of some companies whose reports they regularly picked up.
1979.chinese:
不过，各位应当知道，我们不认为银行出售所得的资金，能够帮助我们完全、甚至在很大程度上取代这家银行所代表的盈利能力。因为，按照出售我们银行时可能采用的市盈率水平，根本买不到同样高质量的企业。

## 财务报告

1979年，伯克希尔·哈撒韦股票开始在纳斯达克（NASDAQ）交易。这意味着，如今《华尔街日报》场外交易（OTC）版的“补充场外报价”栏目也会刊载我们的股价。在此之前，《华尔街日报》和道琼斯新闻行情系统都不会报道我们的利润，尽管这些利润可能是某些它们经常报道的公司利润的100倍甚至更多。

1979.english:
Now, however, the Dow-Jones news ticker reports our quarterly earnings promptly after we release them and, in addition, both the ticker and the Wall Street journal report our annual earnings.  This solves a dissemination problem that had bothered us.

In some ways, our shareholder group is a rather unusual one, and this affects our manner of reporting to you.  For example, at the end of each year about 98% of the shares outstanding are held by people who also were shareholders at the beginning of the year.  Therefore, in our annual report we build upon what we have told you in previous years instead of restating a lot of material.  You get more useful information this way, and we don’t get bored.
1979.chinese:
不过，如今道琼斯新闻行情系统会在我们发布季度利润后迅速报道，而行情系统及《华尔街日报》也都会报道我们的年度利润。这解决了长期困扰我们的一个信息传播问题。

在某些方面，我们的股东群体很不寻常，这也影响了我们向各位报告的方式。例如，每年年末，约98%的流通股份仍由年初时已经持有它们的股东持有。因此，在年报中，我们会在过去已告知各位的内容基础上继续深入，而不是重复大量旧材料。这样，各位能够得到更多有用的信息，我们自己也不至于觉得无聊。

1979.english:
Furthermore, perhaps 90% of our shares are owned by investors for whom Berkshire is their largest security holding, very often far and away the largest.  Many of these owners are willing to spend a significant amount of time with the annual report, and we attempt to provide them with the same information we would find useful if the roles were reversed.

In contrast, we include no narrative with our quarterly reports.  Our owners and managers both have very long time- horizons in regard to this business, and it is difficult to say anything new or meaningful each quarter about events of long-term significance.
1979.chinese:
另外，也许有90%的股份由那些把伯克希尔作为最大证券持仓的投资者持有，而且通常远远大于他们的其他持仓。这些股东中有许多人愿意花大量时间阅读年报，我们努力提供这样一种信息：假如双方的身份互换，我们自己也会觉得有用。

相反，我们的季报没有文字说明。各位股东和管理者都对这门生意抱有很长远的时间视野，而每过一个季度，就真正具有长期意义的事情提出新的、有价值的看法，实在很困难。

1979.english: But when you do receive a communication from us, it will come from the fellow you are paying to run the business.  Your Chairman has a firm belief that owners are entitled to hear directly from the CEO as to what is going on and how he evaluates the business, currently and prospectively.  You would demand that in a private company; you should expect no less in a public company.  A once-a-year report of stewardship should not be turned over to a staff specialist or public relations consultant who is unlikely to be in a position to talk frankly on a manager- to-owner basis.
1979.chinese: 但当各位收到我们的正式沟通时，它一定来自各位付钱雇来经营这家公司的人。你们的董事长坚信，所有者有权直接听到首席执行官讲述企业正在发生什么，以及他怎样评价公司当前的经营和未来前景。在私人公司里，各位一定会这样要求；在上市公司里，也不应该接受更低标准。一年一次的受托经营报告，不应交给内部专员或公关顾问代写，因为他们很可能无法以管理者对所有者的身份坦诚交流。

1979.english: We feel that you, as owners, are entitled to the same sort of reporting by your manager as we feel is owed to us at Berkshire Hathaway by managers of our business units.  Obviously, the degree of detail must be different, particularly where information would be useful to a business competitor or the like. But the general scope, balance, and level of candor should be similar.  We don’t expect a public relations document when our operating managers tell us what is going on, and we don’t feel you should receive such a document.
1979.chinese: 我们觉得，作为股东，各位有权从自己的管理者那里获得同样性质的报告，就像我们认为伯克希尔旗下业务的管理者有义务向我们报告一样。当然，详细程度可以有所不同，特别是涉及对竞争对手有用的信息时；但报告的总体范围、正反方面的平衡以及坦率程度，应当大致相当。我们的业务经理向我们汇报时，我们不期望收到一份公关材料；我们也不认为各位应该收到这种东西。

1979.english:
In large part, companies obtain the shareholder constituency that they seek and deserve.  If they focus their thinking and communications on short-term results or short-term stock market consequences they will, in large part, attract shareholders who focus on the same factors.  And if they are cynical in their treatment of investors, eventually that cynicism is highly likely to be returned by the investment community.

Phil Fisher, a respected investor and author, once likened the policies of the corporation in attracting shareholders to those of a restaurant attracting potential customers.  A restaurant could seek a given clientele - patrons of fast foods, elegant dining, Oriental food, etc. - and eventually obtain an appropriate group of devotees.  If the job were expertly done, that clientele, pleased with the service, menu, and price level offered, would return consistently.  But the restaurant could not change its character constantly and end up with a happy and stable clientele.  If the business vacillated between French cuisine and take-out chicken, the result would be a revolving door of confused and dissatisfied customers.
1979.chinese:
在很大程度上，公司会吸引到自己努力争取、也与其行为相称的那类股东。如果它们的思考和沟通总是围绕短期业绩或者短期股价影响，吸引来的股东多半也会关注同样的因素。如果它们对投资者采取玩世不恭的态度，那么最终投资界也极有可能以同样的态度回应。

受尊敬的投资者兼作家菲尔·费雪（Phil Fisher），曾经把公司吸引股东的政策，比作一家餐馆吸引潜在顾客的方式。一家餐馆可以选择某类客群——喜欢快餐、精致餐饮、东方菜肴等的顾客——最终获得适合自己的忠实拥趸。如果经营得好，这些顾客会因满意服务、菜品和价格水平而不断回来。但是，一家餐馆不可能经常改变自己的经营特色，同时又拥有满意而稳定的客群。如果一家餐馆一会儿做法式料理、一会儿改卖外带炸鸡，结果只会是困惑、不满的顾客不断进进出出。

1979.english:
So it is with corporations and the shareholder constituency they seek.  You can’t be all things to all men, simultaneously seeking different owners whose primary interests run from high current yield to long-term capital growth to stock market pyrotechnics, etc.

The reasoning of managements that seek large trading activity in their shares puzzles us.  In effect, such managements are saying that they want a good many of the existing clientele continually to desert them in favor of new ones - because you can’t add lots of new owners (with new expectations) without losing lots of former owners.
1979.chinese:
公司和自己希望吸引的股东群体之间，也是同样的道理。你不可能同时讨好所有人：既想吸引主要看重当前高股息收益的股东，又想吸引追求长期资本增值的股东，还想吸引热衷股市价格烟火表演的人。

那些努力让自己股票产生大量交易的管理者，其思路令我们困惑。实际上，他们是在说，希望现有顾客中不断有很多人离开，再换进一批新顾客——因为你不可能在大量增加带着新期望的新股东的同时，又不失去大量老股东。

1979.english: We much prefer owners who like our service and menu and who return year after year.  It would be hard to find a better group to sit in the Berkshire Hathaway shareholder “seats” than those already occupying them.  So we hope to continue to have a very low turnover among our owners, reflecting a constituency that understands our operation, approves of our policies, and shares our expectations.  And we hope to deliver on those expectations.
1979.chinese: 我们更喜欢那些喜欢我们的服务和菜单、年复一年回来的所有者。很难找到比现在坐在伯克希尔股东“座位”上的这些人更好的股东群体。因此，我们希望股东的流动率继续很低，反映出这样一群人：理解我们的经营、赞同我们的政策，并与我们分享同样的期望。我们也希望能够不辜负这些期望。

1979.english:
Prospects

Last year we said that we expected operating earnings in dollars to improve but return on equity to decrease.  This turned out to be correct.  Our forecast for 1980 is the same.  If we are wrong, it will be on the downside.  In other words, we are virtually certain that our operating earnings expressed as a percentage of the new equity base of approximately $236 million, valuing securities at cost, will decline from the 18.6% attained in 1979.  There is also a fair chance that operating earnings in aggregate dollars will fall short of 1979; the outcome depends partly upon the date of disposition of the bank, partly upon the degree of slippage in insurance underwriting profitability, and partly upon the severity of earnings problems in the savings and loan industry.
1979.chinese:
## 前景

去年我们曾说，预计以美元金额衡量的经营利润会改善，但股东权益回报率会下降。事实证明，这个预测是正确的。我们对1980年的预测也是如此。如果我们预测错误，那很可能是实际业绩比预测更差。换句话说，我们几乎确信，以按成本计价证券、约2.36亿美元的新股东权益基数计算，经营利润的回报率将低于1979年达到的18.6%。经营利润的美元总额也有相当可能低于1979年；结果部分取决于出售银行的时间，部分取决于保险承保盈利能力下降的程度，还部分取决于储蓄与贷款行业盈利问题的严重程度。

1979.english:
We continue to feel very good about our insurance equity investments.  Over a period of years, we expect to develop very large and growing amounts of underlying earning power attributable to our fractional ownership of these companies.  In most cases they are splendid businesses, splendidly managed, purchased at highly attractive prices.

Your company is run on the principle of centralization of financial decisions at the top (the very top, it might be added), and rather extreme delegation of operating authority to a number of key managers at the individual company or business unit level. We could just field a basketball team with our corporate headquarters group (which utilizes only about 1500 square feet of space).
1979.chinese:
我们对保险公司的股票投资仍然非常看好。随着时间推移，我们预计，自己作为这些企业的部分所有者所享有的底层盈利能力，将积累到非常可观、而且持续增长的规模。多数情况下，它们都是非凡的企业，由杰出的管理者经营，并且我们是在非常有吸引力的价格下买入的。

你们的公司遵循一种经营原则：财务决策集中在最高层（可以补充一句，是绝对的最高层），而经营管理权限则极大程度地下放到各家公司或业务部门的少数关键管理者手中。我们的集团总部人员刚好可以凑成一支篮球队（总部只使用约1,500平方英尺的办公空间）。

1979.english:
This approach produces an occasional major mistake that might have been eliminated or minimized through closer operating controls.  But it also eliminates large layers of costs and dramatically speeds decision-making.  Because everyone has a great deal to do, a very great deal gets done.  Most important of all, it enables us to attract and retain some extraordinarily talented individuals - people who simply can’t be hired in the normal course of events - who find working for Berkshire to be almost identical to running their own show.

We have placed much trust in them - and their achievements have far exceeded that trust.

Warren E. Buffett, Chairman March 3, 1980
1979.chinese:
这种方式偶尔会导致严重失误；如果采取更密切的经营控制，有些错误原本可能被消除或减轻。但是，这种方法也消除了大批管理层级和成本，并大幅加快决策速度。因为每个人都有许多事要做，整个组织也确实完成了大量工作。最重要的是，它使我们能够吸引并留住一些才能非凡的人——这些人通常不可能通过普通招聘获得，而他们觉得在伯克希尔工作与经营自己的企业几乎没有区别。

我们给予他们很大的信任，而他们取得的成绩远远超过了这份信任。

沃伦·E·巴菲特，董事长

1980年3月3日

1980.english:
BERKSHIRE HATHAWAY INC.

To the Shareholders of Berkshire Hathaway Inc.:

Operating earnings improved to $41.9 million in 1980 from $36.0 million in 1979, but return on beginning equity capital (with securities valued at cost) fell to 17.8% from 18.6%. We believe the latter yardstick to be the most appropriate measure of single-year managerial economic performance.  Informed use of that yardstick, however, requires an understanding of many factors, including accounting policies, historical carrying values of assets, financial leverage, and industry conditions.
1980.chinese:
伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司

致伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司的股东：

1980年，我们的经营利润从1979年的3,600万美元提高到4,190万美元，但按年初股东权益计算的回报率（其中证券按成本计价）却由18.6%降至17.8%。我们认为，后一项指标是衡量单年度管理层经济业绩最合适的尺度。不过，要正确使用这一尺度，就必须了解许多因素，包括会计政策、资产的历史入账价值、财务杠杆和行业状况。

1980.english:
In your evaluation of our economic performance, we suggest that two factors should receive your special attention - one of a positive nature peculiar, to a large extent, to our own operation, and one of a negative nature applicable to corporate performance generally.  Let’s look at the bright side first.

## Non-Controlled Ownership Earnings

When one company owns part of another company, appropriate accounting procedures pertaining to that ownership interest must be selected from one of three major categories.  The percentage of voting stock that is owned, in large part, determines which category of accounting principles should be utilized.
1980.chinese:
评价我们的经济业绩时，我们建议各位特别关注两个因素：一个在很大程度上是我们自身业务特有的有利因素，另一个则是普遍影响公司经营表现的不利因素。先说好消息。

## 非控股股权投资的收益

当一家公司拥有另一家公司的一部分股权时，对这一所有权权益的会计处理，必须从三大类方法中选择。应采用哪一类会计原则，在很大程度上取决于所持有的表决权股份比例。

1980.english: Generally accepted accounting principles require (subject to exceptions, naturally, as with our former bank subsidiary) full consolidation of sales, expenses, taxes, and earnings of business holdings more than 50% owned.  Blue Chip Stamps, 60% owned by Berkshire Hathaway Inc., falls into this category.  Therefore, all Blue Chip income and expense items are included in full in Berkshire’s Consolidated Statement of Earnings, with the 40% ownership interest of others in Blue Chip’s net earnings reflected in the Statement as a deduction for “minority interest”.
1980.chinese: 按照公认会计原则，持股超过50%的企业，通常须将其销售、费用、税款与利润全部合并报表（当然也存在例外，例如我们以前的银行子公司）。伯克希尔拥有Blue Chip Stamps约60%的股份，属于这一类。因此，Blue Chip的全部收入及费用项目均完整列入伯克希尔的合并利润表，其他股东持有Blue Chip的40%股权所对应的净利润，则在利润表中作为“少数股东权益”扣除。

1980.english: Full inclusion of underlying earnings from another class of holdings, companies owned 20% to 50% (usually called “investees”), also normally occurs.  Earnings from such companies - for example, Wesco Financial, controlled by Berkshire but only 48% owned - are included via a one-line entry in the owner’s Statement of Earnings.  Unlike the over-50% category, all items of revenue and expense are omitted; just the proportional share of net income is included.  Thus, if Corporation A owns one-third of Corporation B, one-third of B’s earnings, whether or not distributed by B, will end up in A’s earnings.  There are some modifications, both in this and the over-50% category, for intercorporate taxes and purchase price adjustments, the explanation of which we will save for a later day. (We know you can hardly wait.)
1980.chinese: 对于另一类持股，即拥有被投资企业20%至50%股权的情况（这类企业通常称为“权益法被投资企业”），其基础利润通常也会计入投资者报表。例如，Wesco Financial虽由伯克希尔控制，但伯克希尔只拥有48%的股份，因此其利润通过利润表中的单独一行计入。不同于持股超过50%的情形，这里不再列出被投资企业的所有收入与费用，只计入按持股比例分得的净利润。于是，如果A公司持有B公司三分之一股份，B公司三分之一的利润无论是否分配，都会进入A公司的利润表。对于公司间税款和收购价款调整，这一类以及持股超过50%的一类都还有一些修正规定，解释留待以后再说。（我们知道，各位一定迫不及待地想听。）

1980.english: Finally come holdings representing less than 20% ownership of another corporation’s voting securities.  In these cases, accounting rules dictate that the owning companies include in their earnings only dividends received from such holdings. Undistributed earnings are ignored.  Thus, should we own 10% of Corporation X with earnings of $10 million in 1980, we would report in our earnings (ignoring relatively minor taxes on intercorporate dividends) either (a) $1 million if X declared the full $10 million in dividends; (b) $500,000 if X paid out 50%, or $5 million, in dividends; or (c) zero if X reinvested all earnings.
1980.chinese: 最后一类是持有另一家公司不足20%的表决权股份。对此，会计规则规定，持有方只能把从该投资取得的股息计入自身利润，而忽略被投资公司的未分配利润。比如，如果我们持有X公司10%的股份，而X公司1980年盈利1,000万美元，那么忽略公司间股息税收方面相对较小的影响后，我们会报告的利润可能是：（a）如果X公司将1,000万美元利润全部作为股息派发，我们计入100万美元；（b）如果X公司派发50%、即500万美元，我们计入50万美元；或者（c）如果X公司将利润全部留存，我们计入零。

1980.english: We impose this short - and over-simplified - course in accounting upon you because Berkshire’s concentration of resources in the insurance field produces a corresponding concentration of its assets in companies in that third (less than 20% owned) category.  Many of these companies pay out relatively small proportions of their earnings in dividends.  This means that only a small proportion of their current earning power is recorded in our own current operating earnings.  But, while our reported operating earnings reflect only the dividends received from such companies, our economic well-being is determined by their earnings, not their dividends.
1980.chinese: 之所以要给各位上这堂简短而高度简化的会计课，是因为伯克希尔将大量资源集中于保险业务，因而也有相当大一部分资产投向了第三类企业，即持股不足20%的公司。许多这类公司只将利润的很小一部分作为股息派发。于是，它们当前盈利能力中，只有一小部分反映在我们当期报告的经营利润里。然而，虽然我们报告的经营利润只体现从它们收到的股息，真正决定我们经济利益的却是它们的利润，而不是股息。

1980.english: Our holdings in this third category of companies have increased dramatically in recent years as our insurance business has prospered and as securities markets have presented particularly attractive opportunities in the common stock area. The large increase in such holdings, plus the growth of earnings experienced by those partially-owned companies, has produced an unusual result; the part of “our” earnings that these companies retained last year (the part not paid to us in dividends) exceeded the total reported annual operating earnings of Berkshire Hathaway.  Thus, conventional accounting only allows less than half of our earnings “iceberg” to appear above the surface, in plain view.  Within the corporate world such a result is quite rare; in our case it is likely to be recurring.
1980.chinese: 近几年，随着保险业务繁荣，以及股票市场提供了特别有吸引力的买入机会，我们在第三类企业中的持股显著增加。持股规模的大幅增长，加上这些部分持有企业自身利润的增长，带来一个不寻常的结果：去年这些企业为我们所持股权留存、而没有以股息支付给我们的那部分“属于我们”的利润，超过了伯克希尔全年报告的经营利润总额。因此，按传统会计方法，我们的利润“冰山”只有不到一半露出水面，能够被直接看见。在公司世界里，这种情况相当罕见；而在我们这里，它可能会反复出现。

1980.english: Our own analysis of earnings reality differs somewhat from generally accepted accounting principles, particularly when those principles must be applied in a world of high and uncertain rates of inflation. (But it’s much easier to criticize than to improve such accounting rules.  The inherent problems are monumental.) We have owned 100% of businesses whose reported earnings were not worth close to 100 cents on the dollar to us even though, in an accounting sense, we totally controlled their disposition. (The “control” was theoretical.  Unless we reinvested all earnings, massive deterioration in the value of assets already in place would occur.  But those reinvested earnings had no prospect of earning anything close to a market return on capital.) We have also owned small fractions of businesses with extraordinary reinvestment possibilities whose retained earnings had an economic value to us far in excess of 100 cents on the dollar.
1980.chinese: 我们对利润经济实质的分析，与公认会计原则有所不同，尤其是在通胀率高而且不确定的环境中。（不过，批评会计规则比改进它容易得多。固有的问题极其复杂。）我们曾100%拥有某些企业，尽管从会计角度说，我们完全控制其利润的用途，但它们每1美元报告利润对我们而言，经济价值却远不到1美元。（所谓“控制”不过是理论上的：如果不把利润全部重新投入，原有资产的价值就会严重恶化；而这些重新投入的利润，又根本不可能获得接近市场水平的资本回报。）我们也曾持有某些企业的一小部分股份，它们具有非凡的再投资机会，留存的每1美元利润对我们的经济价值远远超过1美元。

1980.english: The value to Berkshire Hathaway of retained earnings is not determined by whether we own 100%, 50%, 20% or 1% of the businesses in which they reside.  Rather, the value of those retained earnings is determined by the use to which they are put and the subsequent level of earnings produced by that usage. This is true whether we determine the usage, or whether managers we did not hire - but did elect to join - determine that usage. (It’s the act that counts, not the actors.) And the value is in no way affected by the inclusion or non-inclusion of those retained earnings in our own reported operating earnings.  If a tree grows in a forest partially owned by us, but we don’t record the growth in our financial statements, we still own part of the tree.
1980.chinese: 留存利润对伯克希尔的价值，并不取决于我们持有这些企业100%、50%、20%还是1%的股份。决定其价值的，是这笔利润被用于何处，以及使用之后能创造多少收益。无论资金用途由我们决定，还是由我们并未亲自聘请、但主动选择与其合作的管理者决定，道理都一样。（重要的是所做的事，而不是做事的人。）留存利润是否计入我们报告的经营利润，也完全不会影响其价值。如果一棵树在我们拥有部分权益的森林里生长，即使我们的财务报表没有记录这种生长，那棵树仍有一部分属于我们。

1980.english:
Our view, we warn you, is non-conventional.  But we would rather have earnings for which we did not get accounting credit put to good use in a 10%-owned company by a management we did not personally hire, than have earnings for which we did get credit put into projects of more dubious potential by another management - even if we are that management.

(We can’t resist pausing here for a short commercial.  One usage of retained earnings we often greet with special enthusiasm when practiced by companies in which we have an investment interest is repurchase of their own shares.  The reasoning is simple: if a fine business is selling in the market place for far less than intrinsic value, what more certain or more profitable utilization of capital can there be than significant enlargement of the interests of all owners at that bargain price?  The competitive nature of corporate acquisition activity almost guarantees the payment of a full - frequently more than full price when a company buys the entire ownership of another enterprise.  But the auction nature of security markets often allows finely-run companies the opportunity to purchase portions of their own businesses at a price under 50% of that needed to acquire the same earning power through the negotiated acquisition of another enterprise.)
1980.chinese:
先提醒各位，我们这种看法并不合常规。不过，我们宁愿让一家只持有10%股份、管理层也不是我们亲自聘请的公司，把不计入我们报表的利润用在好地方；也不愿让另一班管理者，把已经计入报表的利润投入前景更可疑的项目——哪怕那班管理者就是我们自己。

（这里请允许我们忍不住插播一小段广告。对于我们持股的企业，如果它们将留存利润用于回购自己的股票，我们通常特别高兴。理由很简单：如果一家优秀企业在市场上的售价远远低于其内在价值，那么还有什么比以这种便宜价格显著增加全体股东的所有权比例，更确定、也更有利可图的资本用途呢？企业收购活动的竞争性质，几乎保证一家公司购买另一家企业的全部股权时，要支付充分的、往往还高于充分的价格。可是证券市场的竞价性质，却经常使经营出色的企业有机会以不到通过协商收购另一家企业、获得同等盈利能力所需价格一半的成本，买回自己的一部分业务。）

1980.english:
## Long-Term Corporate Results

As we have noted, we evaluate single-year corporate performance by comparing operating earnings to shareholders’ equity with securities valued at cost.  Our long-term yardstick of performance, however, includes all capital gains or losses, realized or unrealized.  We continue to achieve a long-term return on equity that considerably exceeds the average of our yearly returns.  The major factor causing this pleasant result is a simple one: the retained earnings of those non-controlled holdings we discussed earlier have been translated into gains in market value.
1980.chinese:
## 长期公司经营成果

前面说过，我们以经营利润与股东权益（证券按成本计价）之比，衡量单年度公司的经营表现。但长期业绩的衡量标准，则包括所有已实现和未实现的资本利得或损失。长期以来，我们的股东权益回报显著超过各年度回报率的平均值。造成这一令人高兴的结果，主要原因非常简单：前面讨论的那些非控股投资企业所留存的利润，最终转化成了市场价值的增长。

1980.english: Of course, this translation of retained earnings into market price appreciation is highly uneven (it goes in reverse some years), unpredictable as to timing, and unlikely to materialize on a precise dollar-for-dollar basis.  And a silly purchase price for a block of stock in a corporation can negate the effects of a decade of earnings retention by that corporation.  But when purchase prices are sensible, some long-term market recognition of the accumulation of retained earnings almost certainly will occur.  Periodically you even will receive some frosting on the cake, with market appreciation far exceeding post-purchase retained earnings.
1980.chinese: 当然，这种从留存利润到股价上涨的转化过程极不均匀（有些年份甚至倒退），发生时间不可预测，也不太可能严格按照每留存1美元就增值1美元的比例实现。而如果买入一家企业股票时支付了愚蠢的价格，即使该公司此后连续十年留存利润，其成果也可能被高价买入的错误完全抵消。不过，只要购买价格合理，市场迟早几乎必然会在一定程度上承认企业长期积累的留存利润。有时蛋糕上还会多一层糖霜：股价上涨幅度大大超过购买之后留存利润的总额。

1980.english: In the sixteen years since present management assumed responsibility for Berkshire, book value per share with insurance-held equities valued at market has increased from $19.46 to $400.80, or 20.5% compounded annually. (You’ve done better: the value of the mineral content in the human body compounded at 22% annually during the past decade.) It is encouraging, moreover, to realize that our record was achieved despite many mistakes.  The list is too painful and lengthy to detail here.  But it clearly shows that a reasonably competitive corporate batting average can be achieved in spite of a lot of managerial strikeouts.
1980.chinese: 现任管理层接手伯克希尔的16年间，将保险子公司持有的股票按市价计值后，每股账面价值由19.46美元增长到400.80美元，年复合增长率为20.5%。（各位的表现还要好些：过去十年，人体所含矿物质的价值每年复合增长22%。）更令人鼓舞的是，我们虽然犯下了许多错误，仍然取得了这样的成绩。错误清单既漫长又痛苦，我们就不在这里一一列举了。但这清楚说明，即使管理层屡屡被三振出局，企业总体上仍可能交出一个相当不错的安打率。

1980.english: Our insurance companies will continue to make large investments in well-run, favorably-situated, non-controlled companies that very often will pay out in dividends only small proportions of their earnings.  Following this policy, we would expect our long-term returns to continue to exceed the returns derived annually from reported operating earnings.  Our confidence in this belief can easily be quantified: if we were to sell the equities that we hold and replace them with long-term tax-free bonds, our reported operating earnings would rise immediately by over $30 million annually.  Such a shift tempts us not at all.
1980.chinese: 我们的保险公司将继续大量投资于经营良好、具有有利竞争地位的非控股企业。这些公司往往只将利润的很小一部分作为股息发放。按照这一政策，我们预计长期回报仍将高于每年报告的经营利润所反映的回报。我们对这一看法的信心很容易用数字说明：如果我们卖掉目前持有的股票，转而购买长期免税债券，每年报告的经营利润会立即增加3,000多万美元。但这种转变对我们毫无吸引力。

1980.english:
So much for the good news.

## Results for Owners

Unfortunately, earnings reported in corporate financial statements are no longer the dominant variable that determines whether there are any real earnings for you, the owner.  For only gains in purchasing power represent real earnings on investment. If you (a) forego ten hamburgers to purchase an investment; (b) receive dividends which, after tax, buy two hamburgers; and (c) receive, upon sale of your holdings, after-tax proceeds that will buy eight hamburgers, then (d) you have had no real income from your investment, no matter how much it appreciated in dollars. You may feel richer, but you won’t eat richer.
1980.chinese:
好消息就说到这里。

## 所有者的实际回报

不幸的是，公司财务报表中的利润，如今已不再是决定各位股东是否真正赚到钱的最主要因素。因为，只有购买力的增加才代表投资的真实收益。假如你：（a）放弃购买10个汉堡包，把这笔钱用于投资；（b）收到股息，扣税后可以买两个汉堡包；（c）卖出持股后，扣税所得又能买8个汉堡包；那么（d）无论投资的美元价值上涨了多少，你都没有获得任何真实收益。你也许觉得自己更富了，可吃得并没有更好。

1980.english: High rates of inflation create a tax on capital that makes much corporate investment unwise - at least if measured by the criterion of a positive real investment return to owners.  This “hurdle rate” the return on equity that must be achieved by a corporation in order to produce any real return for its individual owners - has increased dramatically in recent years. The average tax-paying investor is now running up a down escalator whose pace has accelerated to the point where his upward progress is nil.
1980.chinese: 高通胀率相当于对资本征税。至少以能否为所有者带来正的实际投资回报为标准，它使许多公司投资变得不明智。近几年，企业必须达到的那道“门槛回报率”——即公司必须取得怎样的股东权益回报，才能给个人股东带来实际收益——已经大幅提高。一般需要纳税的投资者，如今像是在一条不断向下运行的自动扶梯上往上跑；扶梯下行得越来越快，以至于他根本无法向上移动。

1980.english: For example, in a world of 12% inflation a business earning 20% on equity (which very few manage consistently to do) and distributing it all to individuals in the 50% bracket is chewing up their real capital, not enhancing it. (Half of the 20% will go for income tax; the remaining 10% leaves the owners of the business with only 98% of the purchasing power they possessed at the start of the year - even though they have not spent a penny of their “earnings”).  The investors in this bracket would actually be better off with a combination of stable prices and corporate earnings on equity capital of only a few per cent.
1980.chinese: 例如，在通胀率为12%的世界里，一家股东权益回报率达到20%的企业（极少有公司能持续做到），如果把全部利润分配给适用50%税率的个人，实际上是在消耗股东的真实资本，而不是增加它。（20%回报的一半要交所得税；剩下的10%，使企业所有者年末的购买力只有年初的98%，尽管他一分钱“收益”也没花。）对于处在这个税档的投资者而言，物价稳定、而企业股东权益回报率只有几个百分点，实际上反而更好。

1980.english: Explicit income taxes alone, unaccompanied by any implicit inflation tax, never can turn a positive corporate return into a negative owner return. (Even if there were 90% personal income tax rates on both dividends and capital gains, some real income would be left for the owner at a zero inflation rate.) But the inflation tax is not limited by reported income.  Inflation rates not far from those recently experienced can turn the level of positive returns achieved by a majority of corporations into negative returns for all owners, including those not required to pay explicit taxes. (For example, if inflation reached 16%, owners of the 60% plus of corporate America earning less than this rate of return would be realizing a negative real return - even if income taxes on dividends and capital gains were eliminated.)
1980.chinese: 如果没有通胀带来的隐性税负，单靠显性的所得税，再高也无法把企业的正回报变成股东的负回报。（即使股息和资本利得的个人所得税率都达到90%，只要通胀为零，股东还是会剩下一些实际收益。）但通胀税并不受报告利润的限制。与近年经历相差不远的通胀率，就能使大多数企业的正回报，对所有者而言变成负的实际回报——包括那些不必缴纳显性税款的所有者。（例如，如果通胀达到16%，美国公司中60%以上的企业，其股东权益回报率低于这一数字；即使完全取消股息和资本利得所得税，这些企业的所有者仍然会得到负的实际回报。）

1980.english:
Of course, the two forms of taxation co-exist and interact since explicit taxes are levied on nominal, not real, income. Thus you pay income taxes on what would be deficits if returns to stockholders were measured in constant dollars.

At present inflation rates, we believe individual owners in medium or high tax brackets (as distinguished from tax-free entities such as pension funds, eleemosynary institutions, etc.) should expect no real long-term return from the average American corporation, even though these individuals reinvest the entire after-tax proceeds from all dividends they receive.  The average return on equity of corporations is fully offset by the combination of the implicit tax on capital levied by inflation and the explicit taxes levied both on dividends and gains in value produced by retained earnings.
1980.chinese:
当然，两种税同时存在、相互作用，因为显性的所得税按名义收入而不是实际收入征收。也就是说，如果用购买力不变的美元衡量，股东本来已经出现亏损，却仍然需要为名义上的“利润”缴纳所得税。

按照当时的通胀率，我们认为，中高税率档的个人投资者（不同于养老基金、慈善机构等免税主体），即使将收到的全部税后股息重新投资，也不应指望从一般美国公司获得长期的实际回报。公司平均股东权益回报，会被通胀对资本征收的隐性税，以及股息和留存利润形成资本增值时缴纳的显性税，完全抵消。

1980.english:
As we said last year, Berkshire has no corporate solution to the problem. (We’ll say it again next year, too.) Inflation does not improve our return on equity.

Indexing is the insulation that all seek against inflation. But the great bulk (although there are important exceptions) of corporate capital is not even partially indexed.  Of course, earnings and dividends per share usually will rise if significant earnings are “saved” by a corporation; i.e., reinvested instead of paid as dividends.  But that would be true without inflation. A thrifty wage earner, likewise, could achieve regular annual increases in his total income without ever getting a pay increase - if he were willing to take only half of his paycheck in cash (his wage “dividend”) and consistently add the other half (his “retained earnings”) to a savings account.  Neither this high- saving wage earner nor the stockholder in a high-saving corporation whose annual dividend rate increases while its rate of return on equity remains flat is truly indexed.
1980.chinese:
正如我们去年所说，伯克希尔在公司层面没有解决这一问题的办法。（明年我们还会再说一遍。）通胀不会提高我们的股东权益回报率。

大家都希望通过某种指数化机制抵御通胀。但公司资本中的绝大部分（当然也有重要例外）甚至没有实现部分指数化。当然，如果一家企业把大量利润“储蓄”起来，即不作股息派发而是留存再投资，它的每股利润和每股股息通常会上升。然而，即使没有通胀，这种增长也会发生。同样，一位节俭的雇员，即使从来没有获得加薪，只要每次工资只拿一半现金（他的工资“股息”），另一半（他的“留存利润”）定期存进储蓄账户，也能使自己的总收入每年持续增长。无论是这位高储蓄率的雇员，还是持有一家高留存率企业股票的股东——尽管后者每股年度股息在增加，而股东权益回报率保持不变——都没有真正实现抗通胀的指数化。

1980.english:
For capital to be truly indexed, return on equity must rise, i.e., business earnings consistently must increase in proportion to the increase in the price level without any need for the business to add to capital - including working capital - employed.  (Increased earnings produced by increased investment don’t count.) Only a few businesses come close to exhibiting this ability.  And Berkshire Hathaway isn’t one of them.

We, of course, have a corporate policy of reinvesting earnings for growth, diversity and strength, which has the incidental effect of minimizing the current imposition of explicit taxes on our owners.  However, on a day-by-day basis, you will be subjected to the implicit inflation tax, and when you wish to transfer your investment in Berkshire into another form of investment, or into consumption, you also will face explicit taxes.
1980.chinese:
要让资本真正随着通胀指数化，股东权益回报率就必须上升。换句话说，企业的利润必须持续按物价上涨的比例增长，而不需要增加所投入的资本，包括营运资金。（通过追加投资获得的利润增长不算。）只有极少数企业接近具备这种能力。伯克希尔·哈撒韦也不是其中之一。

当然，我们在公司层面采取留存和再投资利润、追求增长、多元化及财务实力的政策，其附带效果是尽量减少股东当前承担的显性税款。不过，日复一日，各位仍在承受隐性的通胀税；而当你希望把伯克希尔的投资转换为其他投资或用于消费时，还将面临显性税款。

1980.english:
## Sources of Earnings

The table below shows the sources of Berkshire’s reported earnings.  Berkshire owns about 60% of Blue Chip Stamps, which in turn owns 80% of Wesco Financial Corporation.  The table shows aggregate earnings of the various business entities, as well as Berkshire’s share of those earnings.  All of the significant capital gains and losses attributable to any of the business entities are aggregated in the realized securities gains figure at the bottom of the table, and are not included in operating earnings.  Our calculation of operating earnings also excludes the gain from sale of Mutual’s branch offices.  In this respect it differs from the presentation in our audited financial statements that includes this item in the calculation of “Earnings Before Realized Investment Gain”.

From this table, you can see that our sources of underlying earning power are distributed far differently among industries than would superficially seem the case. (If translated dollar for dollar into a combination of eventual market value gain and dividends, this figure would have to be reduced by a significant, but not precisely determinable, amount of tax; perhaps 25% would be a fair assumption.) Thus, we have a much larger economic interest in the aluminum business than in practically any of the operating businesses we control and on which we report in more detail.  If we maintain our holdings, our long-term performance will be more affected by the future economics of the aluminum industry than it will by direct operating decisions we make concerning most companies over which we exercise managerial control.
