Our controlled and non-controlled businesses operate over such a wide spectrum that detailed commentary here would prove too lengthy.  Much financial and operational information regarding the controlled businesses is included in Management’s Discussion on pages 34-39, and in the narrative reports on pages 45-61.  However, our largest area of business activity has been, and almost certainly will continue to be, the property-casualty insurance area.  So commentary on developments in that industry is appropriate.

## Insurance Industry Conditions
1982.chinese:
我们的控股和非控股企业业务范围极广，在此逐一详细评论，会使篇幅过长。本报告第34—39页的管理层讨论，以及第45—61页的文字报告，提供了许多有关控股企业的财务与经营资料。不过，我们最大的业务领域一直是财产及意外伤害保险，而且几乎肯定还会如此，因此有必要评论该行业的变化。

## 保险行业状况

1982.english:
Source:   Best’s Aggregates and Averages.

The Best’s data reflect the experience of practically the entire industry, including stock, mutual and reciprocal companies.  The combined ratio represents total operating and loss costs as compared to revenue from premiums; a ratio below 100 indicates an underwriting profit, and one above 100 indicates a loss.

For reasons outlined in last year’s report, as long as the annual gain in industry premiums written falls well below 10%, you can expect the underwriting picture in the next year to deteriorate.  This will be true even at today’s lower general rate of inflation.  With the number of policies increasing annually, medical inflation far exceeding general inflation, and concepts of insured liability broadening, it is highly unlikely that yearly increases in insured losses will fall much below 10%.
1982.chinese:
资料来源：Best’s Aggregates and Averages。

贝斯特（Best’s）的数据几乎涵盖全行业，包括股份制、相互制和互惠制保险公司。综合成本率表示经营费用与赔款成本合计，相对于保费收入的比例；低于100表示承保盈利，高于100表示承保亏损。

正如去年报告所述，只要行业签单保费年度增幅明显低于10%，就可以预期下一年的承保局面会恶化。即使在目前总体通胀率较低的情况下，也仍然如此。保单数量每年增加，医疗通胀远高于总体通胀，保险责任的认定范围不断扩大；在这些条件下，保险赔款每年的增幅很不可能显著低于10%。

1982.english: You should be further aware that the 1982 combined ratio of 109.5 represents a “best case” estimate.  In a given year, it is possible for an insurer to show almost any profit number it wishes, particularly if it (1) writes “long-tail” business (coverage where current costs can be only estimated, because claim payments are long delayed), (2) has been adequately reserved in the past, or (3)	is growing very rapidly.  There are indications that several large insurers opted in 1982 for obscure accounting and reserving maneuvers that masked significant deterioration in their underlying businesses.  In insurance, as elsewhere, the reaction of weak managements to weak operations is often weak accounting. (“It’s difficult for an empty sack to stand upright.”)
1982.chinese: 各位还应注意，1982年109.5的综合成本率，是一种“最乐观情况”下的估计。在某个特定年份，保险公司几乎可以报告任何自己想要的利润数字，尤其是在以下情况下：（1）经营“长尾”业务，即赔款支付大幅滞后，因此当期成本只能估计的险种；（2）过去计提了充足准备金；或（3）业务增长极快。有迹象表明，1982年几家大型保险公司，采用了隐晦的会计和准备金操作，掩盖基础业务的显著恶化。保险业与其他领域一样，软弱管理层面对疲弱经营时，反应往往是采用同样软弱的会计处理。（“空口袋很难直立。”）

1982.english:
The great majority of managements, however, try to play it straight.  But even managements of integrity may subconsciously be less willing in poor profit years to fully recognize adverse loss trends.  Industry statistics indicate some deterioration in loss reserving practices during 1982 and the true combined ratio is likely to be modestly worse than indicated by our table.

The conventional wisdom is that 1983 or 1984 will see the worst of underwriting experience and then, as in the past, the “cycle” will move, significantly and steadily, toward better results.  We disagree because of a pronounced change in the competitive environment, hard to see for many years but now quite visible.
1982.chinese:
不过，绝大多数管理层都力图如实行事。但即使管理层正直，在利润不佳的年份，也可能下意识地不太愿意充分确认赔款趋势的恶化。行业统计显示，1982年的赔款准备金计提做法有所恶化，真实综合成本率很可能比表中显示的略差。

普遍看法是，1983年或1984年的承保业绩将触底，随后“周期”会像以往一样，明显而稳步地转好。我们并不同意，因为竞争环境已经发生重大变化；这一变化多年难以看清，如今却已经相当明显。

1982.english: To understand the change, we need to look at some major factors that affect levels of corporate profitability generally. Businesses in industries with both substantial over-capacity and a “commodity” product (undifferentiated in any customer-important way by factors such as performance, appearance, service support, etc.) are prime candidates for profit troubles.  These may be escaped, true, if prices or costs are administered in some manner and thereby insulated at least partially from normal market forces.  This administration can be carried out (a) legally through government intervention (until recently, this category included pricing for truckers and deposit costs for financial institutions), (b) illegally through collusion, or (c) “extra- legally” through OPEC-style foreign cartelization (with tag-along benefits for domestic non-cartel operators).
1982.chinese: 要理解这种变化，需要先看几个通常会影响企业盈利水平的重要因素。一个行业若同时存在严重过剩产能和“同质化商品”产品，即产品在性能、外观、服务支持等顾客重视的方面缺乏差别，那么其中的企业最容易遇到利润问题。诚然，如果价格或成本以某种方式受到管理，从而至少部分不受正常市场力量影响，这些问题也许可以避免。这种管理可以通过以下方式实现：（a）合法的政府干预；直到不久前，货车运输定价和金融机构存款成本仍属于这一类；（b）非法串谋；或（c）类似石油输出国组织（OPEC）的外国卡特尔所形成的“法域之外”的安排，国内不属于卡特尔的经营者也会搭便车受益。

1982.english:
If, however, costs and prices are determined by full-bore competition, there is more than ample capacity, and the buyer cares little about whose product or distribution services he uses, industry economics are almost certain to be unexciting. They may well be disastrous.

Hence the constant struggle of every vendor to establish and emphasize special qualities of product or service.  This works with candy bars (customers buy by brand name, not by asking for a “two-ounce candy bar”) but doesn’t work with sugar (how often do you hear, “I’ll have a cup of coffee with cream and C & H sugar, please”).
1982.chinese:
但如果成本和价格由充分竞争决定，产能绰绰有余，买方又不太在意使用谁的产品或分销服务，那么行业经济特性几乎肯定平淡无奇，甚至很可能糟糕透顶。

因此，每个卖方都不断努力建立并强调产品或服务的独特品质。这对糖果棒有效，顾客会按品牌购买，而不是要求“一根两盎司糖果棒”；但对食糖却无效。你有多常听到有人说：“请给我一杯咖啡，加奶油和C & H牌糖”？

1982.english:
In many industries, differentiation simply can’t be made meaningful.  A few producers in such industries may consistently do well if they have a cost advantage that is both wide and sustainable.  By definition such exceptions are few, and, in many industries, are non-existent.  For the great majority of companies selling “commodity”products, a depressing equation of business economics prevails: persistent over-capacity without administered prices (or costs) equals poor profitability.

Of course, over-capacity may eventually self-correct, either as capacity shrinks or demand expands.  Unfortunately for the participants, such corrections often are long delayed.  When they finally occur, the rebound to prosperity frequently produces a pervasive enthusiasm for expansion that, within a few years, again creates over-capacity and a new profitless environment.  In other words, nothing fails like success.
1982.chinese:
在许多行业，差异化根本无法形成实际意义。少数生产者如果拥有幅度大且能持久的成本优势，或许可以持续表现良好。但按定义，这种例外很少；在许多行业，根本不存在。对绝大多数销售同质化商品的公司而言，一条令人沮丧的企业经济等式始终成立：持续产能过剩，加上价格或成本不受管理，等于盈利能力低下。

当然，产能过剩最终可能随着产能收缩或需求扩大而自行纠正。遗憾的是，对业内参与者而言，这样的纠正常常迟迟不来。等它终于出现，景气复苏又往往带来普遍的扩张热情，几年之内就再次造成产能过剩，进入新的无利可图环境。换句话说，没有什么比成功更容易埋下失败的种子。

1982.english:
What finally determines levels of long-term profitability in such industries is the ratio of supply-tight to supply-ample years.  Frequently that ratio is dismal. (It seems as if the most recent supply-tight period in our textile business - it occurred some years back - lasted the better part of a morning.)

In some industries, however, capacity-tight conditions can last a long time.  Sometimes actual growth in demand will outrun forecasted growth for an extended period.  In other cases, adding capacity requires very long lead times because complicated manufacturing facilities must be planned and built.
1982.chinese:
这类行业的长期盈利水平，最终取决于供应紧张年份与供应充裕年份之比。这个比率常常很糟。（我们纺织业务最近一次供应紧张，好像已经是几年前；那次紧张大概持续了一个上午的大半时间。）

不过，在某些行业，产能紧张可以持续很长时间。有时，实际需求增长会长时间超过预期；另一些时候，由于必须规划和建造复杂的制造设施，增加产能需要很长的前置时间。

1982.english: But in the insurance business, to return to that subject, capacity can be instantly created by capital plus an underwriter’s willingness to sign his name. (Even capital is less important in a world in which state-sponsored guaranty funds protect many policyholders against insurer insolvency.) Under almost all conditions except that of fear for survival - produced, perhaps, by a stock market debacle or a truly major natural disaster - the insurance industry operates under the competitive sword of substantial overcapacity.  Generally, also, despite heroic attempts to do otherwise, the industry sells a relatively undifferentiated commodity-type product. (Many insureds, including the managers of large businesses, do not even know the names of their insurers.) Insurance, therefore, would seem to be a textbook case of an industry usually faced with the deadly combination of excess capacity and a “commodity” product.
1982.chinese: 但回到保险业，资本加上承保人愿意签名，就能立即创造承保能力。（当各州支持的保障基金可以保护许多保户，使其免受保险公司破产影响时，连资本都不那么重要了。）除了可能由股市崩盘或真正重大自然灾害引发的生存恐惧之外，在几乎所有情况下，保险业都在大量过剩承保能力这把竞争利剑之下经营。总体而言，尽管行业竭力尝试有所不同，出售的仍是差异较小的同质化商品。（许多投保人，包括大型企业的管理者，甚至不知道自己保险公司的名字。）因此，保险业似乎正是一个教科书式的行业案例：通常面临过剩产能与同质化商品这一致命组合。

1982.english: Why, then, was underwriting, despite the existence of cycles, generally profitable over many decades? (From 1950 through 1970, the industry combined ratio averaged 99.0. allowing all investment income plus 1% of premiums to flow through to profits.) The answer lies primarily in the historic methods of regulation and distribution.  For much of this century, a large portion of the industry worked, in effect, within a legal quasi-administered pricing system fostered by insurance regulators.  While price competition existed, it was not pervasive among the larger companies.  The main competition was for agents, who were courted via various non-price-related strategies.
1982.chinese: 那么，既然如此，为什么尽管存在周期，保险承保业务在几十年中总体仍能盈利？从1950年至1970年，行业综合成本率平均为99.0，意味着全部投资收入，加上相当于保费1%的金额，都可成为利润。答案主要在于历史上的监管和分销方式。本世纪相当长的一段时间内，很大一部分行业，实际上是在保险监管者推动的合法、近似行政管理的定价体系中经营。价格竞争虽然存在，但在大型公司之间并不普遍。主要的竞争，是争取代理人；公司通过各种与价格无关的策略招揽他们。

1982.english:
For the giants of the industry, most rates were set through negotiations between industry “bureaus” (or through companies acting in accord with their recommendations) and state regulators.  Dignified haggling occurred, but it was between company and regulator rather than between company and customer. When the dust settled, Giant A charged the same price as Giant B - and both companies and agents were prohibited by law from cutting such filed rates.

The company-state negotiated prices included specific profit allowances and, when loss data indicated that current prices were unprofitable, both company managements and state regulators expected that they would act together to correct the situation. Thus, most of the pricing actions of the giants of the industry were “gentlemanly”, predictable, and profit-producing.  Of prime importance - and in contrast to the way most of the business world operated - insurance companies could legally price their way to profitability even in the face of substantial over- capacity.
1982.chinese:
对行业巨头来说，多数费率由行业“费率组织”，或遵照其建议行动的公司，与各州监管者谈判确定。双方也会体面地讨价还价，但发生在公司与监管者之间，而不是公司与顾客之间。尘埃落定后，巨头A与巨头B收取相同价格；法律还禁止公司及代理人降低这些已备案费率。

公司与州监管者商定的价格，包含明确的利润额度。当赔款数据显示现行价格无法盈利时，公司管理层与州监管者都预期，双方会共同采取行动纠正。因此，行业巨头大多数定价行为都是“绅士式”的、可以预测，而且能产生利润。最关键的是，与大多数商业领域不同，即使承保能力大量过剩，保险公司也可以合法地通过调整价格实现盈利。

1982.english:
That day is gone.  Although parts of the old structure remain, far more than enough new capacity exists outside of that structure to force all parties, old and new, to respond.  The new capacity uses various methods of distribution and is not reluctant to use price as a prime competitive weapon.  Indeed, it relishes that use.  In the process, customers have learned that insurance is no longer a one-price business.  They won’t forget.

Future profitability of the industry will be determined by current competitive characteristics, not past ones.  Many managers have been slow to recognize this.  It’s not only generals that prefer to fight the last war.  Most business and investment analysis also comes from the rear-view mirror.  It seems clear to us, however, that only one condition will allow the insurance industry to achieve significantly improved underwriting results.  That is the same condition that will allow better results for the aluminum, copper, or corn producer - a major narrowing of the gap between demand and supply.
1982.chinese:
那个时代已经过去。旧体系虽然仍部分存在，但体系之外新增的承保能力已经绰绰有余，足以迫使新老所有参与者作出反应。这些新增承保能力采用各种分销方式，毫不迟疑地把价格作为主要竞争武器，甚至乐在其中。在这个过程中，顾客已经明白，保险不再是一个只有统一价格的行业。他们不会忘记。

行业未来的盈利能力，将由当前而非过去的竞争特征决定。许多管理者很晚才认识到这一点。喜欢打上一场战争的，并不只是将军；大多数企业与投资分析，也同样来自后视镜。不过，我们很清楚，只有一种条件能让保险业的承保结果显著改善；这与铝、铜或玉米生产者取得更好结果所需的条件相同——需求与供给之间的差距大幅缩小。

1982.english:
Unfortunately, there can be no surge in demand for insurance policies comparable to one that might produce a market tightness in copper or aluminum.  Rather, the supply of available insurance coverage must be curtailed.  “Supply”, in this context, is mental rather than physical: plants or companies need not be shut; only the willingness of underwriters to sign their names need be curtailed.

This contraction will not happen because of generally poor profit levels.  Bad profits produce much hand-wringing and finger-pointing.  But they do not lead major sources of insurance capacity to turn their backs on very large chunks of business, thereby sacrificing market share and industry significance.
1982.chinese:
遗憾的是，保险保单需求不可能像铜或铝那样，突然激增到造成市场紧张的地步。因此，必须削减可提供的保险保障。在这里，“供给”是心理层面的，而不是实物层面的：不需要关闭工厂或公司，只需减少承保人签名承保的意愿。

这种收缩不会仅仅因为总体利润不佳而发生。糟糕的利润会引发许多焦虑和相互指责，却不会让主要承保能力提供者放弃大块业务，从而牺牲市场份额和行业地位。

1982.english:
Instead, major capacity withdrawals require a shock factor such as a natural or financial “megadisaster”.  One might occur tomorrow - or many years from now.  The insurance business - even taking investment income into account - will not be particularly profitable in the meantime.

When supply ultimately contracts, large amounts of business will be available for the few with large capital capacity, a willingness to commit it, and an in-place distribution system. We would expect great opportunities for our insurance subsidiaries at such a time.
1982.chinese:
相反，要使大量承保能力退出，需要自然或金融“超级灾难”这样的冲击。它可能明天就发生，也可能多年之后才发生。在此之前，即使把投资收入计算在内，保险业也不会特别有利可图。

当供给最终收缩时，那些少数资本实力雄厚、愿意投入资本，而且已经拥有分销体系的公司，就能承接大量业务。我们预计，届时旗下保险子公司将迎来巨大机会。

1982.english: During 1982, our insurance underwriting deteriorated far more than did the industry’s.  From a profit position well above average, we, slipped to a performance modestly below average. The biggest swing was in National Indemnity’s traditional coverages.  Lines that have been highly profitable for us in the past are now priced at levels that guarantee underwriting losses. In 1983 we expect our insurance group to record an average performance in an industry in which average is very poor.
1982.chinese: 1982年，我们保险承保业务的恶化程度，远大于全行业。从明显高于平均水平的盈利地位，我们滑落到略低于平均水平的表现。变化最大的是国家赔偿保险公司（National Indemnity）的传统险种。过去为我们带来高额利润的业务，如今的定价已注定造成承保亏损。1983年，我们预期保险集团只能取得行业平均表现，而这个行业的平均表现本身会很差。

1982.english:
Two of our stars, Milt Thornton at Cypress and Floyd Taylor at Kansas Fire and Casualty, continued their outstanding records of producing an underwriting profit every year since joining us. Both Milt and Floyd simply are incapable of being average.  They maintain a passionately proprietary attitude toward their operations and have developed a business culture centered upon unusual cost-consciousness and customer service.  It shows on their scorecards.

During 1982, parent company responsibility for most of our insurance operations was given to Mike Goldberg.  Planning, recruitment, and monitoring all have shown significant improvement since Mike replaced me in this role.
1982.chinese:
我们的两位明星——赛普拉斯保险公司（Cypress）的米尔特·桑顿（Milt Thornton），以及堪萨斯火灾与意外保险公司（Kansas Fire and Casualty）的弗洛伊德·泰勒（Floyd Taylor）——继续保持加入我们以来每年承保盈利的出色记录。米尔特和弗洛伊德，根本不会甘于平庸。他们对各自业务怀有强烈的主人翁意识，并培育出一种格外重视成本意识和客户服务的企业文化。这一切，都反映在他们的成绩单上。

1982年，母公司对我们大部分保险业务的管理职责，交给了迈克·戈德伯格（Mike Goldberg）。自从迈克替代我担任这一角色，规划、招聘和监督都有显著改善。

1982.english: GEICO continues to be managed with a zeal for efficiency and value to the customer that virtually guarantees unusual success. Jack Byrne and Bill Snyder are achieving the most elusive of human goals - keeping things simple and remembering what you set out to do.  In Lou Simpson, additionally, GEICO has the best investment manager in the property-casualty business.  We are happy with every aspect of this operation.  GEICO is a magnificent illustration of the high-profit exception we described earlier in discussing commodity industries with over- capacity - a company with a wide and sustainable cost advantage. Our 35% interest in GEICO represents about $250 million of premium volume, an amount considerably greater than all of the direct volume we produce.
1982.chinese: 盖可继续以极大的热情追求效率与客户价值，这几乎保证了它能取得非凡成功。杰克·伯恩和比尔·斯奈德（Bill Snyder），实现了人类最难实现的目标之一：让事情保持简单，并记住自己最初要做什么。此外，有卢·辛普森（Lou Simpson）在，盖可拥有财产及意外伤害保险业最出色的投资经理。我们对这项业务的每个方面都很满意。盖可生动地体现了前面讨论产能过剩的同质化商品行业时提到的高利润例外：它拥有幅度大、可持续的成本优势。我们在盖可35%的权益，代表约2.5亿美元的保费规模，远远超过我们直接经营业务的全部保费规模。

1982.english:
## Issuance of Equity

Berkshire and Blue Chip are considering merger in 1983.  If it takes place, it will involve an exchange of stock based upon an identical valuation method applied to both companies.  The one other significant issuance of shares by Berkshire or its affiliated companies that occurred during present management’s tenure was in the 1978 merger of Berkshire with Diversified Retailing Company.

Our share issuances follow a simple basic rule: we will not issue shares unless we receive as much intrinsic business value as we give.  Such a policy might seem axiomatic.  Why, you might ask, would anyone issue dollar bills in exchange for fifty-cent pieces?  Unfortunately, many corporate managers have been willing to do just that.
1982.chinese:
## 发行股权

伯克希尔和蓝筹印花公司正在考虑于1983年合并。如果实现，将对两家公司采用相同的估值方法，确定换股安排。在现任管理层任内，伯克希尔或其关联公司另外一次重要股票发行，是1978年伯克希尔与多元化零售公司（Diversified Retailing Company）合并时发生的。

我们发行股份，遵循一条简单的基本原则：除非获得的内在企业价值，至少与付出的一样多，否则就不发行股份。这条政策看起来像是不言而喻。各位也许会问，谁会愿意拿1美元纸币，去换50美分的硬币？遗憾的是，许多公司管理者愿意这样做。

1982.english: The first choice of these managers in making acquisitions may be to use cash or debt.  But frequently the CEO’s cravings outpace cash and credit resources (certainly mine always have). Frequently, also, these cravings occur when his own stock is selling far below intrinsic business value.  This state of affairs produces a moment of truth.  At that point, as Yogi Berra has said, “You can observe a lot just by watching.” For shareholders then will find which objective the management truly prefers - expansion of domain or maintenance of owners’ wealth.
1982.chinese: 这些管理者收购时的首选，或许是现金或借款。但首席执行官的欲望，常常超过现金与信贷资源，我自己的欲望向来如此。而且，这种欲望还常常出现在自家公司股票售价远低于内在企业价值的时候。这便到了关键的考验时刻。正如约吉·贝拉（Yogi Berra）所说，“只要留心看，就能观察到很多。”因为股东此时会发现，管理层真正偏爱的目标，究竟是扩大管理疆域，还是维护所有者财富。

1982.english: The need to choose between these objectives occurs for some simple reasons.  Companies often sell in the stock market below their intrinsic business value.  But when a company wishes to sell out completely, in a negotiated transaction, it inevitably wants to - and usually can - receive full business value in whatever kind of currency the value is to be delivered.  If cash is to be used in payment, the seller’s calculation of value received couldn’t be easier.  If stock of the buyer is to be the currency, the seller’s calculation is still relatively easy: just figure the market value in cash of what is to be received in stock.
1982.chinese: 之所以必须在这两个目标之间选择，原因很简单。公司的股票，在市场上经常以低于内在企业价值的价格交易。但当一家公司希望通过谈判把自己整体出售时，不管最终以何种货币支付，它都必然希望、而且通常能够，获得完整的企业价值。如果以现金支付，卖方计算所得价值再容易不过。如果支付工具是买方股票，卖方的计算仍然比较简单：只要算出将收到的股票，其现金市值是多少即可。

1982.english:
Meanwhile, the buyer wishing to use his own stock as currency for the purchase has no problems if the stock is selling in the market at full intrinsic value.

But suppose it is selling at only half intrinsic value.  In that case, the buyer is faced with the unhappy prospect of using a substantially undervalued currency to make its purchase.

Ironically, were the buyer to instead be a seller of its entire business, it too could negotiate for, and probably get, full intrinsic business value.  But when the buyer makes a partial sale of itself - and that is what the issuance of shares to make an acquisition amounts to - it can customarily get no higher value set on its shares than the market chooses to grant it.
1982.chinese:
与此同时，如果买方希望用自己的股票作为支付货币，而股票在市场上正按完整内在价值交易，就不存在问题。

但假设股票售价只有内在价值的一半，买方面临的，就会是用一种被严重低估的货币进行收购的难堪处境。

讽刺的是，如果买方转而整体出售自己，同样可以谈判争取、而且很可能拿到完整的内在企业价值。但当买方只出售自己的一部分——*发行股份进行收购，本质上就是如此*——通常就无法让自己股份获得高于市场愿意给予的价值。

1982.english: The acquirer who nevertheless barges ahead ends up using an undervalued (market value) currency to pay for a fully valued (negotiated value) property.  In effect, the acquirer must give up $2 of value to receive $1 of value.  Under such circumstances, a marvelous business purchased at a fair sales price becomes a terrible buy.  For gold valued as gold cannot be purchased intelligently through the utilization of gold - or even silver - valued as lead.
1982.chinese: 收购方若仍贸然推进，最终就是用一种被低估的货币，按市场价值计价，去支付一项足额估值的资产，按谈判价值计价。实际上，收购方必须放弃2美元价值，才能取得1美元价值。在这种情况下，即使按公平出售价格买到一家卓越企业，也会成为一笔糟糕透顶的交易。因为你不可能明智地用被按铅估值的金子，甚至银子，去购买按黄金估值的黄金。

1982.english:
If, however, the thirst for size and action is strong enough, the acquirer’s manager will find ample rationalizations for such a value-destroying issuance of stock.  Friendly investment bankers will reassure him as to the soundness of his actions. (Don’t ask the barber whether you need a haircut.)

A few favorite rationalizations employed by stock-issuing managements follow:

(a) “The company we’re buying is going to be worth a lot more in the future.” (Presumably so is the interest in the old business that is being traded away; future prospects are implicit in the business valuation process.  If 2X is issued for X, the imbalance still exists when both parts double in business value.)
1982.chinese:
不过，如果对规模和行动的渴望足够强烈，收购方管理者就能为这种摧毁价值的发股行为，找到大量自圆其说的理由。友好的投资银行家会向他保证，这样做很合理。（别问理发师你是否需要理发。）

发行股票的管理层，常用的几个理由如下：

（a）“我们正在收购的公司，未来会值钱得多。”（想必，为此换出去的原有企业权益，未来也会值钱得多；企业估值过程中，本来就包含未来前景。如果付出2X，只换回X，那么当双方企业价值都翻倍时，不平衡仍然存在。）

1982.english: (b) “We have to grow.” (Who, it might be asked, is the “we”? For present shareholders, the reality is that all existing businesses shrink when shares are issued.  Were Berkshire to issue shares tomorrow for an acquisition, Berkshire would own everything that it now owns plus the new business, but your interest in such hard-to-match businesses as See’s Candy Shops, National Indemnity, etc. would automatically be reduced.  If (1) your family owns a 120-acre farm and (2)  you invite a neighbor with 60 acres of comparable land to merge his farm into an equal partnership - with you to be managing partner, then (3) your managerial domain will have grown to 180 acres but you will have permanently shrunk by 25% your family’s ownership interest in both acreage and crops. Managers who want to expand their domain at the expense of owners might better consider a career in government.)
1982.chinese: （b）“我们必须增长。”（但也许应该问，“我们”是谁？对现有股东而言，现实是：发行股份时，他们在所有现有业务中的权益都会缩水。如果伯克希尔明天为收购发行股份，伯克希尔将拥有目前的一切，再加上新企业；但*各位在喜诗糖果商店、国家赔偿保险公司等难以匹敌的企业中的权益*，却会自动减少。假如：（1）你家拥有一座120英亩的农场；（2）你邀请拥有60英亩同等土地的邻居，把农场合并为双方各占一半的合伙企业，由你担任管理合伙人；那么，（3）你的管理疆域扩大到180英亩，但你家对土地和农作物的所有者权益，却永久缩减了25%。那些希望以所有者利益为代价扩大管理疆域的管理者，或许更适合考虑在政府任职。）

1982.english: (c) “Our stock is undervalued and we’ve minimized its use in this deal - but we need to give the selling shareholders 51% in stock and 49% in cash so that certain of those shareholders can get the tax-free exchange they want.” (This argument acknowledges that it is beneficial to the acquirer to hold down the issuance of shares, and we like that.  But if it hurts the old owners to utilize shares on a 100% basis, it very likely hurts on a 51% basis. After all, a man is not charmed if a spaniel defaces his lawn, just because it’s a spaniel and not a St. Bernard. And the wishes of sellers can’t be the determinant of the best interests of the buyer - what would happen if, heaven forbid, the seller insisted that as a condition of merger the CEO of the acquirer be replaced?)
1982.chinese: （c）“我们的股票被低估了，这笔交易中也已经尽量少用了；但我们仍须向卖方股东支付51%的股票和49%的现金，才能让其中一些股东获得他们想要的免税换股待遇。”（这一说法承认，控制发股数量对收购方有利，这一点我们赞同。但如果100%用股票支付会损害原有所有者，使用51%的股票支付，也很可能同样有害。毕竟，西班牙猎犬弄坏了一个人的草坪，他不会仅仅因为那是一只西班牙猎犬，而不是圣伯纳犬，就觉得开心。而且，卖方的愿望不能决定什么最符合买方利益；假如卖方竟坚持把更换收购方首席执行官作为合并条件，那又该怎么办？）

1982.english: There are three ways to avoid destruction of value for old owners when shares are issued for acquisitions.  One is to have a true business-value-for-business-value merger, such as the Berkshire-Blue Chip combination is intended to be.  Such a merger attempts to be fair to shareholders of both parties, with each receiving just as much as it gives in terms of intrinsic business value.  The Dart Industries-Kraft and Nabisco Standard Brands mergers appeared to be of this type, but they are the exceptions. It’s not that acquirers wish to avoid such deals; it’s just that they are very hard to do.
1982.chinese: 在为收购发行股份时，有三种办法可以避免损害原有所有者价值。第一，真正按企业价值对等交换，正如伯克希尔与蓝筹印花公司计划中的合并所希望做到的那样。这样的合并，力图对*双方股东*公平，使各自在内在企业价值上得到的与付出的一样多。达特工业与卡夫（Dart Industries-Kraft），以及纳贝斯克与标准品牌（Nabisco Standard Brands）的合并，看起来属于这一类，但它们是例外。并不是收购方想避开这种交易，只是实在很难做到。

1982.english: The second route presents itself when the acquirer’s stock sells at or above its intrinsic business value.  In that situation, the use of stock as currency actually may enhance the wealth of the acquiring company’s owners.  Many mergers were accomplished on this basis in the 1965-69 period.  The results were the converse of most of the activity since 1970: the shareholders of the acquired company received very inflated currency (frequently pumped up by dubious accounting and promotional techniques) and were the losers of wealth through such transactions.
1982.chinese: 第二种办法，是收购方股票售价达到或超过其内在企业价值。在这种情况下，用股票作为支付货币，实际上可能增加收购公司所有者的财富。1965—1969年，许多合并正是如此完成。结果与1970年以来多数交易恰好相反：*被收购公司的股东*，收到的是价值被严重高估的货币，这种高估常常由可疑的会计与宣传手法推高，因此在交易中损失财富。

1982.english:
During recent years the second solution has been available to very few large companies.  The exceptions have primarily been those companies in glamorous or promotional businesses to which the market temporarily attaches valuations at or above intrinsic business valuation.

The third solution is for the acquirer to go ahead with the acquisition, but then subsequently repurchase a quantity of shares equal to the number issued in the merger.  In this manner, what originally was a stock-for-stock merger can be converted, effectively, into a cash-for-stock acquisition.  Repurchases of this kind are damage-repair moves.  Regular readers will correctly guess that we much prefer repurchases that directly enhance the wealth of owners instead of repurchases that merely repair previous damage.  Scoring touchdowns is more exhilarating than recovering one’s fumbles.  But, when a fumble has occurred, recovery is important and we heartily recommend damage-repair repurchases that turn a bad stock deal into a fair cash deal.
1982.chinese:
近几年，能够采用第二种办法的大公司非常少。例外主要是那些身处热门或靠宣传推动的行业、市场暂时给予等于或高于内在企业价值估值的公司。

第三种办法，是收购方先完成收购，随后回购与合并中新发行股数相等的股份。这样，原本以股换股的合并，实际上就可以转化为以现金买股的收购。这类回购属于修补损害。经常阅读本报告的股东会正确猜到，比起仅仅弥补过去损失的回购，我们远更喜欢直接增加所有者财富的回购。达阵得分，总比抢回自己掉落的球更令人兴奋。但既然已经掉球，抢回来就很重要；我们衷心建议，采用这种修补型回购，把糟糕的换股交易变为公平的现金交易。

1982.english: The language utilized in mergers tends to confuse the issues and encourage irrational actions by managers.  For example, “dilution” is usually carefully calculated on a pro forma basis for both book value and current earnings per share.  Particular emphasis is given to the latter item.  When that calculation is negative (dilutive) from the acquiring company’s standpoint, a justifying explanation will be made (internally, if not elsewhere) that the lines will cross favorably at some point in the future. (While deals often fail in practice, they never fail in projections - if the CEO is visibly panting over a prospective acquisition, subordinates and consultants will supply the requisite projections to rationalize any price.) Should the calculation produce numbers that are immediately positive - that is, anti-dilutive - for the acquirer, no comment is thought to be necessary.
1982.chinese: 合并中使用的语言，往往让问题变得混乱，并鼓励管理者作出不理性的行动。例如，人们通常会用备考报表，仔细计算每股账面价值和当期每股利润的“稀释”，尤其重视后者。如果从收购方角度计算，结果为负、即发生稀释，就会给出解释，至少在内部如此：未来某个时点，合并后与不合并的利润线会发生有利交叉。（交易在实践中常会失败，在预测里却从不失败；如果首席执行官显然已对潜在收购迫不及待，下属和顾问就会提供所需预测，为任何价格找出理由。）如果计算结果对收购方立即为正，即反稀释，就被认为无需任何解释。

1982.english:
The attention given this form of dilution is overdone: current earnings per share (or even earnings per share of the next few years) are an important variable in most business valuations, but far from all powerful.

There have been plenty of mergers, non-dilutive in this limited sense, that were instantly value destroying for the acquirer.  And some mergers that have diluted current and near- term earnings per share have in fact been value-enhancing.  What really counts is whether a merger is dilutive or anti-dilutive in terms of intrinsic business value (a judgment involving consideration of many variables).  We believe calculation of dilution from this viewpoint to be all-important (and too seldom made).
1982.chinese:
对这种形式的稀释，关注得过了头。当期每股利润，甚至未来几年的每股利润，在多数企业估值中都是重要变量，却远非决定一切的因素。

许多合并在这种有限意义上没有稀释，却立即摧毁了收购方的价值。另一些合并虽然稀释了当期和近期每股利润，实际上却增加了价值。真正重要的是，合并在内在企业价值上究竟造成稀释，还是增厚；这一判断需要考虑许多变量。我们认为，从这个角度计算稀释极为重要，而且人们做得太少。

1982.english: A second language problem relates to the equation of exchange.  If Company A announces that it will issue shares to merge with Company B, the process is customarily described as “Company A to Acquire Company B”, or “B Sells to A”.  Clearer thinking about the matter would result if a more awkward but more accurate description were used: “Part of A sold to acquire B”, or “Owners of B to receive part of A in exchange for their properties”.  In a trade, what you are giving is just as important as what you are getting.  This remains true even when the final tally on what is being given is delayed.  Subsequent sales of common stock or convertible issues, either to complete the financing for a deal or to restore balance sheet strength, must be fully counted in evaluating the fundamental mathematics of the original acquisition. (If corporate pregnancy is going to be the consequence of corporate mating, the time to face that fact is before the moment of ecstasy.)
1982.chinese: 第二个语言问题，与交换关系有关。如果A公司宣布发行股份与B公司合并，人们通常描述为“A公司收购B公司”，或“B卖给A”。如果改用一种较拗口、却更准确的说法，思考会更清楚：“出售A的一部分，以收购B”，或“B的所有者以自己的资产，换取A的一部分”。交易中，付出什么与得到什么同样重要。即使最终付出多少，要过一段时间才能结算，这一点也不变。后续出售普通股或发行可转换证券，无论是为了补足交易融资，还是恢复资产负债表实力，在评价原始收购的基本账目时，都必须充分计入。（如果企业交配会导致企业怀孕，面对这个事实的时机，应该在狂喜的那一刻之前。）

1982.english: Managers and directors might sharpen their thinking by asking themselves if they would sell 100% of their business on the same basis they are being asked to sell part of it.  And if it isn’t smart to sell all on such a basis, they should ask themselves why it is smart to sell a portion.  A cumulation of small managerial stupidities will produce a major stupidity - not a major triumph. (Las Vegas has been built upon the wealth transfers that occur when people engage in seemingly-small disadvantageous capital transactions.)
1982.chinese: 管理者和董事不妨这样追问自己，促使思路更清晰：如果按现在被要求出售部分股权的同样条件，出售整家企业的100%股权，自己愿不愿意？如果这样整体出售不明智，就应该继续问，为什么只出售一部分就明智？许多小小的管理蠢事积累起来，只会形成一件大蠢事，不会形成一次大胜利。（拉斯维加斯就是建立在人们进行看似很小、却对自己不利的资本交易时发生的财富转移之上。）

1982.english:
The “giving versus getting” factor can most easily be calculated in the case of registered investment companies. Assume Investment Company X, selling at 50% of asset value, wishes to merge with Investment Company Y.  Assume, also, that Company X therefore decides to issue shares equal in market value to 100% of Y’s asset value.

Such a share exchange would leave X trading $2 of its previous intrinsic value for $1 of Y’s intrinsic value.  Protests would promptly come forth from both X’s shareholders and the SEC, which rules on the fairness of registered investment company mergers.  Such a transaction simply would not be allowed.
1982.chinese:
对于注册投资公司，“付出与所得”这一因素最容易计算。假设投资公司X的股票售价为资产价值的50%，它希望与投资公司Y合并。再假设，X因此决定发行股票，使所发行股票的市值相当于Y资产价值的100%。

这样的换股，会使X用原有内在价值中的2美元，换取Y的1美元内在价值。X的股东，以及负责裁定注册投资公司合并是否公平的美国证券交易委员会（SEC），都会立即提出抗议。这种交易根本不会得到允许。

1982.english: In the case of manufacturing, service, financial companies, etc., values are not normally as precisely calculable as in the case of investment companies.  But we have seen mergers in these industries that just as dramatically destroyed value for the owners of the acquiring company as was the case in the hypothetical illustration above.  This destruction could not happen if management and directors would assess the fairness of any transaction by using the same yardstick in the measurement of both businesses.
1982.chinese: 制造、服务、金融等公司的价值，通常不像投资公司那样容易精确计算。但我们见过这些行业的某些合并，给收购公司所有者造成的价值破坏，与上述假设例子同样严重。如果管理层与董事在衡量两家企业时采用同一把尺子，来评价交易是否公平，这种破坏就不会发生。

1982.english: Finally, a word should be said about the “double whammy” effect upon owners of the acquiring company when value-diluting stock issuances occur.  Under such circumstances, the first blow is the loss of intrinsic business value that occurs through the merger itself.  The second is the downward revision in market valuation that, quite rationally, is given to that now-diluted business value.  For current and prospective owners understandably will not pay as much for assets lodged in the hands of a management that has a record of wealth-destruction through unintelligent share issuances as they will pay for assets entrusted to a management with precisely equal operating talents, but a known distaste for anti-owner actions.  Once management shows itself insensitive to the interests of owners, shareholders will suffer a long time from the price/value ratio afforded their stock (relative to other stocks), no matter what assurances management gives that the value-diluting action taken was a one- of-a-kind event.
1982.chinese: 最后，还应谈谈稀释价值的发股，对收购公司所有者造成的“双重打击”。第一击，是合并本身导致的内在企业价值损失。第二击，是市场相当理性地进一步下调对已经被稀释的企业价值的估值。因为对于一家曾因不明智发股而损害财富的管理层所掌握的资产，现有和潜在所有者愿意支付的价格，理所当然会低于另一家经营才能完全相同、但明确厌恶损害所有者行为的管理层所掌握的资产。一旦管理层表现出漠视所有者利益，不管如何保证这种稀释价值的行为仅此一次，股东都将长期承受其股票相对于其他股票较低的价格／价值比。

1982.english: Those assurances are treated by the market much as one-bug- in-the-salad explanations are treated at restaurants.  Such explanations, even when accompanied by a new waiter, do not eliminate a drop in the demand (and hence market value) for salads, both on the part of the offended customer and his neighbors pondering what to order.  Other things being equal, the highest stock market prices relative to intrinsic business value are given to companies whose managers have demonstrated their unwillingness to issue shares at any time on terms unfavorable to the owners of the business.
1982.chinese: 市场对这种保证的看法，就像餐厅顾客听到“沙拉里只有这一只虫子”的解释。即使换来一位新服务员，也无法阻止受冒犯的顾客，以及旁边正在考虑点什么的人，减少对沙拉的需求，从而降低其市场价值。在其他条件相同的情况下，股票价格相对于内在企业价值最高的公司，是那些管理者已经证明，自己绝不愿在对企业所有者不利的条件下发行股份的公司。

1982.english:
At Berkshire, or any company whose policies we determine (including Blue Chip and Wesco), we will issue shares only if our owners receive in business value as much as we give.  We will not equate activity with progress or corporate size with owner- wealth.

Miscellaneous

This annual report is read by a varied audience, and it is possible that some members of that audience may be helpful to us in our acquisition program.

We prefer:
1982.chinese:
在伯克希尔，或任何由我们决定政策的公司，包括蓝筹印花公司和韦斯科，我们只会在所有者获得的企业价值，至少等于付出价值时，才发行股份。我们不会把忙碌等同于进步，也不会把公司规模等同于所有者财富。

## 其他事项

阅读本年报的群体十分多样，其中一些人，也许能够帮助我们推进收购计划。

我们偏好：

1982.english:
(1) large purchases (at least $5 million of after-tax earnings),

(2) demonstrated consistent earning power (future projections are of little interest to us, nor are “turn-around” situations),

(3) businesses earning good returns on equity while employing little or no debt,

(4) management in place (we can’t supply it),

(5) simple businesses (if there’s lots of technology, we won’t understand it),

(6) an offering price (we don’t want to waste our time or that of the seller by talking, even preliminarily, about a transaction when price is unknown).
1982.chinese:
（1）大额收购，税后利润至少为500万美元；

（2）已经证明具有持续盈利能力的企业；我们对未来预测兴趣不大，对“扭亏为盈”的情形也一样；

（3）很少使用债务，或完全不用债务，同时能取得良好股东权益回报率的企业；

（4）已有管理团队的企业；我们无法提供管理团队；

（5）简单的企业；如果涉及大量技术，我们会看不懂；

（6）有明确要价；价格未知时，我们不愿浪费自己或卖方的时间，哪怕只是初步讨论交易。

1982.english:
We will not engage in unfriendly transactions.  We can promise complete confidentiality and a very fast answer as to possible interest - customarily within five minutes.  Cash purchases are preferred, but we will consider the use of stock when it can be done on the basis described in the previous section.

---

Our shareholder-designated contributions program met with enthusiasm again this year; 95.8% of eligible shares participated.  This response was particularly encouraging since only $1 per share was made available for designation, down from $2 in 1981.  If the merger with Blue Chip takes place, a probable by-product will be the attainment of a consolidated tax position that will significantly enlarge our contribution base and give us a potential for designating bigger per-share amounts in the future.
1982.chinese:
我们不会参与敌意交易。我们可以承诺完全保密，并迅速答复是否可能有兴趣，通常在五分钟以内。我们偏好现金收购，但如果能够按上一节所述原则进行，也会考虑使用股票。

\* * * * *

今年，我们的股东指定捐款计划再次受到热烈欢迎，符合资格股份的95.8%参与了计划。这一回应尤其令人鼓舞，因为今年每股仅提供1美元供股东指定，低于1981年的2美元。如果与蓝筹印花公司的合并实现，可能带来的一个附带结果，是形成合并纳税的税务状况，从而显著扩大可捐款基础，为未来指定更高的每股金额提供可能。

1982.english:
If you wish to participate in future programs, we strongly urge that you immediately make sure that your shares are registered in the actual owner’s name, not a “street” or nominee name.  For new shareholders, a more complete description of the program is on pages 62-63.

---

In a characteristically rash move, we have expanded World Headquarters by 252 square feet (17%), coincidental with the signing of a new five-year lease at 1440 Kiewit Plaza.  The five people who work here with me - Joan Atherton, Mike Goldberg, Gladys Kaiser, Verne McKenzie and Bill Scott - outproduce corporate groups many times their number.  A compact organization lets all of us spend our time managing the business rather than managing each other.
1982.chinese:
*如果各位希望参与未来的计划，我们强烈建议，立即确认股票登记在实际所有者名下，而不是以证券经纪商的“街名”或其他代名人名义登记。*对于新股东，本报告第62—63页对该计划有更完整的说明。

\* * * * *

我们又作出了一次一贯“鲁莽”的行动：在1440 Kiewit Plaza签订新的五年租约时，把全球总部扩大了252平方英尺，即17%。与我共同在这里工作的五位同事——琼·阿瑟顿（Joan Atherton）、迈克·戈德伯格、格拉迪丝·凯泽（Gladys Kaiser）、弗恩·麦肯齐（Verne McKenzie）和比尔·斯科特（Bill Scott）——其产出超过人数多出数倍的企业团队。精简的组织，让我们所有人都能把时间用于管理企业，而不是相互管理。

1982.english:
Charlie Munger, my partner in management, will continue to operate from Los Angeles whether or not the Blue Chip merger occurs.  Charlie and I are interchangeable in business decisions. Distance impedes us not at all: we’ve always found a telephone call to be more productive than a half-day committee meeting.

---

Two of our managerial stars retired this year: Phil Liesche at 65 from National Indemnity Company, and Ben Rosner at 79 from Associated Retail Stores.  Both of these men made you, as shareholders of Berkshire, a good bit wealthier than you otherwise would have been.  National Indemnity has been the most important operation in Berkshire’s growth.  Phil and Jack Ringwalt, his predecessor, were the two prime movers in National Indemnity’s success.  Ben Rosner sold Associated Retail Stores to Diversified Retailing Company for cash in 1967, promised to stay on only until the end of the year, and then hit business home runs for us for the next fifteen years.
1982.chinese:
我的管理合伙人查理·芒格（Charlie Munger），不论蓝筹印花公司的合并是否发生，都会继续在洛杉矶办公。查理和我在经营决策上可以相互替代。距离完全不妨碍我们；我们一直发现，一通电话比半天的委员会会议更有效。

\* * * * *

今年，我们两位管理明星退休了：国家赔偿保险公司的菲尔·利舍（Phil Liesche）65岁，联合零售商店公司（Associated Retail Stores）的本·罗斯纳（Ben Rosner）79岁。他们两位，使各位作为伯克希尔股东，比没有他们时富裕了不少。国家赔偿保险公司一直是伯克希尔成长中最重要的业务，菲尔和他的前任杰克·林沃尔特（Jack Ringwalt），是其成功的两大推动者。本·罗斯纳1967年以现金把联合零售商店公司卖给多元化零售公司时，只答应留任到当年年底；随后，他却为我们连续十五年打出了商业上的本垒打。

1982.english:
Both Ben and Phil ran their businesses for Berkshire with every bit of the care and drive that they would have exhibited had they personally owned 100% of these businesses.  No rules were necessary to enforce or even encourage this attitude; it was embedded in the character of these men long before we came on the scene.  Their good character became our good fortune.  If we can continue to attract managers with the qualities of Ben and Phil, you need not worry about Berkshire’s future.

Warren E. Buffett Chairman of the Board
1982.chinese:
本和菲尔为伯克希尔经营企业时，所投入的每一分用心和干劲，与他们个人拥有企业100%股权时会付出的一样。无需任何规则来强制、甚至鼓励这种态度；早在我们出现以前，它就已经深植于这两位的品格之中。他们的好品格，成了我们的好运气。如果我们能继续吸引具备本和菲尔这些品质的管理者，各位就不必为伯克希尔的未来担心。

沃伦·E·巴菲特

董事会主席

1983.english:
Chairman's Letter - 1983

BERKSHIRE HATHAWAY INC.

To the Shareholders of Berkshire Hathaway Inc.:

This past year our registered shareholders increased from about 1900 to about 2900.  Most of this growth resulted from our merger with Blue Chip Stamps, but there also was an acceleration in the pace of “natural” increase that has raised us from the 1000 level a few years ago.

With so many new shareholders, it’s appropriate to summarize the major business principles we follow that pertain to the manager-owner relationship:

o Although our form is corporate, our attitude is partnership.  Charlie Munger and I think of our shareholders as owner-partners, and of ourselves as managing partners.  (Because of the size of our shareholdings we also are, for better or worse, controlling partners.) We do not view the company itself as the ultimate owner of our business assets but, instead, view the company as a conduit through which our shareholders own the assets.

o In line with this owner-orientation, our directors are all major shareholders of Berkshire Hathaway.  In the case of at least four of the five, over 50% of family net worth is represented by holdings of Berkshire.  We eat our own cooking.

o Our long-term economic goal (subject to some qualifications mentioned later) is to maximize the average annual rate of gain in intrinsic business value on a per-share basis.  We do not measure the economic significance or performance of Berkshire by its size; we measure by per-share progress.  We are certain that the rate of per-share progress will diminish in the future - a greatly enlarged capital base will see to that.  But we will be disappointed if our rate does not exceed that of the average large American corporation.

o Our preference would be to reach this goal by directly owning a diversified group of businesses that generate cash and consistently earn above-average returns on capital.  Our second choice is to own parts of similar businesses, attained primarily through purchases of marketable common stocks by our insurance subsidiaries.  The price and availability of businesses and the need for insurance capital determine any given year’s capital allocation.

o Because of this two-pronged approach to business ownership and because of the limitations of conventional accounting, consolidated reported earnings may reveal relatively little about our true economic performance.  Charlie and I, both as owners and managers, virtually ignore such consolidated numbers.  However, we will also report to you the earnings of each major business we control, numbers we consider of great importance.  These figures, along with other information we will supply about the individual businesses, should generally aid you in making judgments about them.

o Accounting consequences do not influence our operating or capital-allocation decisions.  When acquisition costs are similar, we much prefer to purchase $2 of earnings that is not reportable by us under standard accounting principles than to purchase $1 of earnings that is reportable.  This is precisely the choice that often faces us since entire businesses (whose earnings will be fully reportable) frequently sell for double the pro-rata price of small portions (whose earnings will be largely unreportable).  In aggregate and over time, we expect the unreported earnings to be fully reflected in our intrinsic business value through capital gains.

o We rarely use much debt and, when we do, we attempt to structure it on a long-term fixed rate basis.  We will reject interesting opportunities rather than over-leverage our balance sheet.  This conservatism has penalized our results but it is the only behavior that leaves us comfortable, considering our fiduciary obligations to policyholders, depositors, lenders and the many equity holders who have committed unusually large portions of their net worth to our care.

o A managerial “wish list” will not be filled at shareholder expense.  We will not diversify by purchasing entire businesses at control prices that ignore long-term economic consequences to our shareholders.  We will only do with your money what we would do with our own, weighing fully the values you can obtain by diversifying your own portfolios through direct purchases in the stock market.

o We feel noble intentions should be checked periodically against results.  We test the wisdom of retaining earnings by assessing whether retention, over time, delivers shareholders at least $1 of market value for each $1 retained.  To date, this test has been met.  We will continue to apply it on a five-year rolling basis.  As our net worth grows, it is more difficult to use retained earnings wisely.

o We will issue common stock only when we receive as much in business value as we give.  This rule applies to all forms of issuance - not only mergers or public stock offerings, but stock for-debt swaps, stock options, and convertible securities as well.  We will not sell small portions of your company - and that is what the issuance of shares amounts to - on a basis inconsistent with the value of the entire enterprise.

o You should be fully aware of one attitude Charlie and I share that hurts our financial performance: regardless of price, we have no interest at all in selling any good businesses that Berkshire owns, and are very reluctant to sell sub-par businesses as long as we expect them to generate at least some cash and as long as we feel good about their managers and labor relations. We hope not to repeat the capital-allocation mistakes that led us into such sub-par businesses.  And we react with great caution to suggestions that our poor businesses can be restored to satisfactory profitability by major capital expenditures.  (The projections will be dazzling - the advocates will be sincere - but, in the end, major additional investment in a terrible industry usually is about as rewarding as struggling in quicksand.) Nevertheless, gin rummy managerial behavior (discard your least promising business at each turn) is not our style.  We would rather have our overall results penalized a bit than engage in it.

o We will be candid in our reporting to you, emphasizing the pluses and minuses important in appraising business value.  Our guideline is to tell you the business facts that we would want to know if our positions were reversed.  We owe you no less. Moreover, as a company with a major communications business, it would be inexcusable for us to apply lesser standards of accuracy, balance and incisiveness when reporting on ourselves than we would expect our news people to apply when reporting on others.  We also believe candor benefits us as managers: the CEO who misleads others in public may eventually mislead himself in private.

o Despite our policy of candor, we will discuss our activities in marketable securities only to the extent legally required.  Good investment ideas are rare, valuable and subject to competitive appropriation just as good product or business acquisition ideas are.  Therefore, we normally will not talk about our investment ideas.  This ban extends even to securities we have sold (because we may purchase them again) and to stocks we are incorrectly rumored to be buying.  If we deny those reports but say “no comment” on other occasions, the no-comments become confirmation.

That completes the catechism, and we can now move on to the high point of 1983 - the acquisition of a majority interest in Nebraska Furniture Mart and our association with Rose Blumkin and her family.
1983.chinese:
# 巴菲特1983年度致股东信｜完整中文译文

伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司

**沃伦·E·巴菲特｜1984年3月14日**

致伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司股东：

过去一年，我们的登记股东人数从约1,900人增加到约2,900人。新增股东多数来自我们与蓝筹印花公司（Blue Chip Stamps）的合并，不过，“自然增长”的速度也有所加快；就在几年前，我们的股东人数还只有约1,000人。

既然现在有了这么多新股东，我们有必要概述一下我们遵循的、与管理者和所有者关系有关的主要经营原则：

- **尽管公司采用股份公司形式，我们却以合伙企业的态度经营。** 查理·芒格和我把股东视为所有者合伙人，把自己视为经营合伙人。（由于我们持股比例很大，不论好坏，我们也是控股合伙人。）我们并不认为公司本身才是业务资产的最终所有者，而是把公司视为股东持有这些资产的载体。

- 与这种所有者导向一致，伯克希尔的董事都是公司的大股东。五位董事中至少四位，其家庭净资产的50%以上由伯克希尔股票构成。我们自己也吃自己做的饭。

- 我们的长期经济目标（须受后文提到的某些条件限制），是使**每股内在商业价值的年均增长率最大化**。我们不以规模衡量伯克希尔的经济意义或经营表现，而是衡量每股取得了多大进步。我们确信，未来每股价值的增长速度会下降——大幅扩大的资本基础必然导致这一结果。但如果我们的增长率不能超过美国大型企业的平均水平，我们仍会感到失望。

- 我们首选的实现方式，是直接拥有一组多元化企业；这些企业能够产生现金，并持续取得高于平均水平的资本回报。其次是持有类似企业的部分权益，主要由保险子公司购买可交易普通股实现。企业的价格与可获得性，以及保险业务对资本的需求，共同决定每年的资本配置。

- 由于这种双轨企业所有权方式，加上传统会计方法的局限，合并报表中的利润对我们的真实经济表现可能说明不了多少问题。无论作为所有者还是管理者，查理和我实际上都几乎不理会这种合并数字。不过，我们也会向各位报告每家主要控股企业的利润，这些数字在我们看来十分重要。结合我们提供的各企业其他信息，它们通常能帮助各位进行判断。

- 会计结果不会左右我们的经营或资本配置决策。在收购成本相近的情况下，比起购买按照标准会计原则能够计入我们报表的1美元利润，我们更愿意购买不能计入的2美元利润。我们经常面临这种选择，因为收购整家企业（其利润可全部并表）的价格，常常是购买小比例权益（其利润大部分不能并表）按比例计算价格的两倍。我们预计，从总体上看，经过一段时间，这些未在报表中体现的利润会通过资本利得充分反映在我们的内在商业价值中。

- 我们很少大量举债；确实需要举债时，也尽力采用长期固定利率的安排。我们宁愿放弃有吸引力的机会，也不愿使资产负债表承担过高杠杆。这样的谨慎确实拖累了业绩，但考虑到我们对保单持有人、存款人、贷款人，以及将家庭净资产中异常大的一部分交托给我们的众多股东所负有的受托责任，只有这种做法才让我们安心。

- 我们不会用股东的钱满足管理层的“愿望清单”。我们不会为了多元化而以忽视股东长期经济后果的控制权价格收购整家公司。使用各位的资金时，我们只会做自己也愿意拿自己的钱做的事，并充分权衡各位直接在股票市场购买证券、实现个人投资组合多元化所能获得的价值。

- 我们认为，高尚的意图应当定期接受结果检验。我们检验留存利润是否明智的方法是：长期来看，每留存1美元利润，能否至少为股东创造1美元市场价值。迄今这一标准已得到满足。今后我们将继续以滚动五年为周期进行检验。随着净资产增长，明智地运用留存利润也变得更加困难。

- 只有在我们获得的商业价值至少等于我们交出的商业价值时，才会发行普通股。这一规则适用于各种形式的发行——不仅包括合并或公开发行股票，也包括以股抵债、股票期权以及可转换证券。发行股票实际上是在出售各位所拥有公司的部分权益，我们不会以与企业整体价值不一致的条件出售这些股份。

- 各位应充分了解查理和我共有的一种态度，它会损害我们的财务表现：无论报价有多高，我们都完全没有兴趣出售伯克希尔旗下任何优秀企业；对经营欠佳的企业，只要我们预计它们仍能产生一些现金，而且我们认可管理者与劳资关系，我们也非常不愿出售。我们希望不再犯下当初使我们进入这些平庸业务的资本配置错误。有人建议投入大量资本支出，把这些糟糕企业恢复到令人满意的盈利水平时，我们也会格外谨慎。（预测数据会令人目眩，提议者也是真心实意，但最终，向糟糕行业投入大笔额外资金，往往和在流沙中挣扎一样难有收获。）尽管如此，像玩金拉米纸牌那样每回合丢掉最差一张牌的管理风格，并不符合我们的做法。我们宁愿让总体业绩受到一点影响，也不愿如此行事。

- 我们会坦诚地向各位报告，重点说明影响企业价值判断的有利因素与不利因素。我们的标准是：如果双方身份互换，我们希望知道哪些经营事实，就向各位报告哪些事实。这是我们至少应尽的责任。此外，既然公司拥有重要的传媒业务，在报告自身情况时，如果我们在准确性、平衡性和洞察力方面的标准低于要求新闻从业者报道别人时遵守的标准，那就不可原谅。我们还认为，坦诚也有利于管理者自身：一位在公开场合误导他人的首席执行官，最终可能在私下里也误导自己。

- 尽管我们坚持坦诚，涉及可交易证券的投资活动，我们只会披露法律要求披露的内容。优秀的投资想法罕见、宝贵，也像好的产品构想或企业收购机会一样，可能被竞争者据为己有。因此，我们通常不会谈论自己的投资想法。禁令甚至适用于已经卖出的证券（因为我们可能再次买入），以及市场误传我们正在买入的股票。如果我们否认某些传闻，却在另外一些时候回答“无可奉告”，这种沉默就成了变相确认。

以上就是我们的信条。现在可以转向1983年的重头戏：收购内布拉斯加家具城（Nebraska Furniture Mart）的多数权益，并与罗丝·布拉姆金（Rose Blumkin）及其家族结为合作伙伴。

1983.english:
## Nebraska Furniture Mart

Last year, in discussing how managers with bright, but adrenalin-soaked minds scramble after foolish acquisitions, I quoted Pascal: “It has struck me that all the misfortunes of men spring from the single cause that they are unable to stay quietly in one room.”

Even Pascal would have left the room for Mrs. Blumkin.

About 67 years ago Mrs. Blumkin, then 23, talked her way past a border guard to leave Russia for America.  She had no formal education, not even at the grammar school level, and knew no English.  After some years in this country, she learned the language when her older daughter taught her, every evening, the words she had learned in school during the day.

In 1937, after many years of selling used clothing, Mrs. Blumkin had saved $500 with which to realize her dream of opening a furniture store.  Upon seeing the American Furniture Mart in Chicago - then the center of the nation’s wholesale furniture activity - she decided to christen her dream Nebraska Furniture Mart.

She met every obstacle you would expect (and a few you wouldn’t) when a business endowed with only $500 and no locational or product advantage goes up against rich, long- entrenched competition.  At one early point, when her tiny resources ran out, “Mrs.  B” (a personal trademark now as well recognized in Greater Omaha as Coca-Cola or Sanka) coped in a way not taught at business schools: she simply sold the furniture and appliances from her home in order to pay creditors precisely as promised.

Omaha retailers began to recognize that Mrs. B would offer customers far better deals than they had been giving, and they pressured furniture and carpet manufacturers not to sell to her. But by various strategies she obtained merchandise and cut prices sharply.  Mrs. B was then hauled into court for violation of Fair Trade laws.  She not only won all the cases, but received invaluable publicity.  At the end of one case, after demonstrating to the court that she could profitably sell carpet at a huge discount from the prevailing price, she sold the judge $1400 worth of carpet.

Today Nebraska Furniture Mart generates over $100 million of sales annually out of one 200,000 square-foot store.  No other home furnishings store in the country comes close to that volume. That single store also sells more furniture, carpets, and appliances than do all Omaha competitors combined.

One question I always ask myself in appraising a business is how I would like, assuming I had ample capital and skilled personnel, to compete with it.  I’d rather wrestle grizzlies than compete with Mrs. B and her progeny.  They buy brilliantly, they operate at expense ratios competitors don’t even dream about, and they then pass on to their customers much of the savings.  It’s the ideal business - one built upon exceptional value to the customer that in turn translates into exceptional economics for its owners.

Mrs. B is wise as well as smart and, for far-sighted family reasons, was willing to sell the business last year.  I had admired both the family and the business for decades, and a deal was quickly made.  But Mrs. B, now 90, is not one to go home and risk, as she puts it, “losing her marbles”.  She remains Chairman and is on the sales floor seven days a week.  Carpet sales are her specialty.  She personally sells quantities that would be a good departmental total for other carpet retailers.

We purchased 90% of the business - leaving 10% with members of the family who are involved in management - and have optioned 10% to certain key young family managers.

And what managers they are.  Geneticists should do handsprings over the Blumkin family.  Louie Blumkin, Mrs.  B’s son, has been President of Nebraska Furniture Mart for many years and is widely regarded as the shrewdest buyer of furniture and appliances in the country.  Louie says he had the best teacher, and Mrs. B says she had the best student.  They’re both right. Louie and his three sons all have the Blumkin business ability, work ethic, and, most important, character.  On top of that, they are really nice people.  We are delighted to be in partnership with them.
1983.chinese:
## 内布拉斯加家具城

去年谈到一些头脑聪明、却被肾上腺素冲昏了头的管理者争相进行愚蠢收购时，我引用了帕斯卡尔的一句话：“我发现，人类所有的不幸，都源于同一个原因：他们无法安静地待在一个房间里。”

不过，即便是帕斯卡尔，也会为了布拉姆金夫人走出房间。

大约67年前，23岁的布拉姆金夫人说服一名边境警卫，得以离开俄国前往美国。她没有接受过正规教育，甚至没有上过小学，也不会英语。来美国几年后，她的长女每天晚上把在学校学到的单词教给她，她才逐渐学会英语。

1937年，经过多年卖旧衣服，她终于存下500美元，实现了开家具店的梦想。她曾见到芝加哥的美国家具市场——当时全国家具批发业的中心——于是决定把自己的梦想命名为“内布拉斯加家具城”。

一家只有500美元资本、没有地理位置或产品优势的小企业，要和根基深厚、资金充裕的对手竞争，自然会碰到你能想到的所有障碍（以及一些意想不到的障碍）。早期有一次，她仅有的一点钱花光了，“B夫人”（这个个人品牌如今在大奥马哈地区的知名度可与可口可乐或Sanka咖啡相提并论）采取了一种商学院不教的办法：卖掉自己家里的家具和电器，按承诺一分不差地还清债权人。

奥马哈的零售商开始意识到，B夫人给顾客的价格远比他们优惠，于是施压家具和地毯制造商，要求不要向她供货。但她通过各种办法获得商品，并大幅降价。随后，有人以违反公平交易法为由将她告上法庭。她不仅赢得了所有官司，还获得了极有价值的宣传。在其中一场诉讼结束时，她向法庭证明自己即使以远低于通行价格的折扣销售地毯仍有利润，随后又卖给法官价值1,400美元的地毯。

如今，内布拉斯加家具城仅凭一家面积20万平方英尺的商店，每年就创造超过1亿美元销售额。美国没有其他家居用品商店能够在单店销售额上接近这一水平。这家商店出售的家具、地毯和电器，也超过奥马哈所有竞争对手的总和。

评价一家企业时，我总会问自己一个问题：假设我拥有充裕资金和能干的人才，我愿意怎样与它竞争？和B夫人及她的后代竞争，我宁可去与灰熊摔跤。他们采购精明，经营费用率低到竞争对手连想都不敢想，又把由此节省的大部分成本让利给顾客。这是一门理想的生意：为顾客提供超凡价值，进而为所有者带来卓越的经济效益。

B夫人不仅精明，也很有智慧。出于长远的家族考虑，她去年愿意出售企业。我已经欣赏这家人和这门生意几十年了，交易很快就达成。不过，现年90岁的B夫人可不会回家闲着，冒着用她的话说“脑子生锈”的风险。她仍担任董事长，而且每周七天都在卖场。地毯是她的专长，她个人的销量足以成为别家零售商整个部门的可观业绩。

我们购买了这家企业90%的权益，留下10%给参与管理的家族成员，并向一些年轻的核心家族管理人员授予购买10%权益的期权。

这些管理者实在了不起。遗传学家应该为布拉姆金家族欢呼雀跃。B夫人的儿子路易·布拉姆金（Louie Blumkin）多年来一直担任家具城总裁，被广泛认为是全美国最精明的家具和电器采购者。路易说自己拥有最好的老师，B夫人说自己拥有最好的学生。他们说得都对。路易和他的三个儿子都继承了布拉姆金家族的商业才能、工作精神，以及最重要的品格。除此之外，他们还都是非常友善的人。我们很高兴能够成为他们的合伙人。

1983.english:
## Corporate Performance

During 1983 our book value increased from $737.43 per share to $975.83 per share, or by 32%.  We never take the one-year figure very seriously.  After all, why should the time required for a planet to circle the sun synchronize precisely with the time required for business actions to pay off?  Instead, we recommend not less than a five-year test as a rough yardstick of economic performance.  Red lights should start flashing if the five-year average annual gain falls much below the return on equity earned over the period by American industry in aggregate. (Watch out for our explanation if that occurs as Goethe observed, “When ideas fail, words come in very handy.”)

During the 19-year tenure of present management, book value has grown from $19.46 per share to $975.83, or 22.6% compounded annually.  Considering our present size, nothing close to this rate of return can be sustained.  Those who believe otherwise should pursue a career in sales, but avoid one in mathematics.

We report our progress in terms of book value because in our case (though not, by any means, in all cases) it is a conservative but reasonably adequate proxy for growth in intrinsic business value - the measurement that really counts. Book value’s virtue as a score-keeping measure is that it is easy to calculate and doesn’t involve the subjective (but important) judgments employed in calculation of intrinsic business value. It is important to understand, however, that the two terms - book value and intrinsic business value - have very different meanings.

Book value is an accounting concept, recording the accumulated financial input from both contributed capital and retained earnings.  Intrinsic business value is an economic concept, estimating future cash output discounted to present value.  Book value tells you what has been put in; intrinsic business value estimates what can be taken out.

An analogy will suggest the difference.  Assume you spend identical amounts putting each of two children through college. The book value (measured by financial input) of each child’s education would be the same.  But the present value of the future payoff (the intrinsic business value) might vary enormously - from zero to many times the cost of the education.  So, also, do businesses having equal financial input end up with wide variations in value.

At Berkshire, at the beginning of fiscal 1965 when the present management took over, the $19.46 per share book value considerably overstated intrinsic business value.  All of that book value consisted of textile assets that could not earn, on average, anything close to an appropriate rate of return.  In the terms of our analogy, the investment in textile assets resembled investment in a largely-wasted education.

Now, however, our intrinsic business value considerably exceeds book value.  There are two major reasons:

(1) Standard accounting principles require that common stocks held by our insurance subsidiaries be stated on our books at market value, but that other stocks we own be carried at the lower of aggregate cost or market. At the end of 1983, the market value of this latter group exceeded carrying value by $70 million pre-tax, or about $50 million after tax.  This excess belongs in our intrinsic business value, but is not included in the calculation of book value;

(2) More important, we own several businesses that possess economic Goodwill (which is properly includable in intrinsic business value) far larger than the accounting Goodwill that is carried on our balance sheet and reflected in book value.

Goodwill, both economic and accounting, is an arcane subject and requires more explanation than is appropriate here.  The appendix that follows this letter - “Goodwill and its Amortization: The Rules and The Realities” - explains why economic and accounting Goodwill can, and usually do, differ enormously.

You can live a full and rewarding life without ever thinking about Goodwill and its amortization.  But students of investment and management should understand the nuances of the subject.  My own thinking has changed drastically from 35 years ago when I was taught to favor tangible assets and to shun businesses whose value depended largely upon economic Goodwill.  This bias caused me to make many important business mistakes of omission, although relatively few of commission.

Keynes identified my problem: “The difficulty lies not in the new ideas but in escaping from the old ones.” My escape was long delayed, in part because most of what I had been taught by the same teacher had been (and continues to be) so extraordinarily valuable.  Ultimately, business experience, direct and vicarious, produced my present strong preference for businesses that possess large amounts of enduring Goodwill and that utilize a minimum of tangible assets.

I recommend the Appendix to those who are comfortable with accounting terminology and who have an interest in understanding the business aspects of Goodwill.  Whether or not you wish to tackle the Appendix, you should be aware that Charlie and I believe that Berkshire possesses very significant economic Goodwill value above that reflected in our book value.
1983.chinese:
## 公司业绩

1983年，每股账面价值从737.43美元增长至975.83美元，增幅为32%。我们从来不会过分看重单一年度的数字。毕竟，一颗行星绕太阳一圈所需要的时间，凭什么恰好与经营措施产生效果所需的时间同步呢？相反，我们建议至少用五年作为衡量经济表现的粗略尺度。如果五年平均年增长率远低于同一时期美国整个工业部门的股东权益回报率，警示灯就应该亮起。（届时也要留心我们的解释。歌德曾说：“当思想失效时，语言就特别管用。”）

现任管理层执掌伯克希尔的19年间，每股账面价值从19.46美元增长到975.83美元，年复合增长率为22.6%。考虑到我们现在的规模，绝不可能持续取得接近这一水平的回报。相信可以的人，不妨从事销售工作，但最好不要从事数学工作。

我们用账面价值报告进展，是因为对伯克希尔而言（绝不是对所有企业都如此），它是内在商业价值增长的一个比较保守、但相当合适的替代指标；真正重要的衡量标准是内在商业价值。账面价值的优点在于容易计算，不涉及估算内在商业价值时必需的主观判断。但必须理解，这两个词——账面价值和内在商业价值——含义截然不同。

**账面价值是会计概念，记录股东投入资本和留存利润积累起来的财务投入；内在商业价值是经济概念，估计未来能够取得的现金流折算到今天值多少钱。账面价值告诉你投入了多少，内在商业价值估计可以取出多少。**

打个比方，假设你花同样的钱供两个孩子读完大学。那么两人的教育账面价值（按财务投入衡量）相同，但未来教育回报的现值（内在商业价值）可能相差极大——从零到教育成本的许多倍都有可能。同样，投入相同资金的企业，最后也可能拥有截然不同的价值。

1965财年初，现任管理层接手伯克希尔时，19.46美元的每股账面价值大大高于内在商业价值。所有账面价值都由纺织资产构成，而这些资产的平均回报远远达不到适当水平。按照刚才的比喻，投到纺织资产里的钱，就像花在一场基本上被浪费的教育上。

如今则不同，我们的内在商业价值明显高于账面价值，主要有两个原因：

（1）标准会计原则要求保险子公司持有的普通股按市值入账，但我们持有的其他股票则按总体成本与市值孰低计价。1983年末，后一组股票市值比账面金额高出税前7,000万美元，税后约5,000万美元。这部分差额属于内在商业价值，却没有计入账面价值。

（2）更重要的是，我们拥有若干具有重大经济商誉的企业；它们的经济商誉（理应包含在内在商业价值之中），远远大于资产负债表记录、并反映在账面价值中的会计商誉。

商誉——无论经济商誉还是会计商誉——都是一个晦涩的话题，需要比此处更多的解释。本信后附的《商誉及其摊销：规则与现实》，将说明为什么经济商誉和会计商誉可能、而且通常确实相差极大。

一个人即使从不考虑商誉及其摊销，也完全可以过上充实而有意义的一生。但是研究投资和经营管理的人，应当理解其中细微的差别。35年前我所受的教育要求我偏爱有形资产、回避主要依靠经济商誉体现价值的企业；与那时相比，我自己的思想已经发生了根本变化。这种偏见使我错过了许多重要的商业机会，虽然因主动做错事造成的错误相对较少。

凯恩斯指出了我的问题：“困难不在于接受新思想，而在于摆脱旧思想。”我很晚才摆脱旧观念，部分原因是同一位老师教给我的大多数其他知识当时极为宝贵，而且今天仍然如此。最终，亲身经历和观察他人的经营经验，使我如今强烈偏爱那些拥有大量持久经济商誉、同时只需要少量有形资产的企业。

我向熟悉会计术语、并有兴趣理解商誉商业含义的读者推荐附录。不论是否准备研读附录，各位都应知道，查理和我认为，伯克希尔拥有的经济商誉价值，远远高于账面价值所反映的金额。

## Buffalo Evening News

First, a clarification: our corporate name is Buffalo Evening News, Inc. but the name of the newspaper, since we began a morning edition a little over a year ago, is Buffalo News.

In 1983 the News somewhat exceeded its targeted profit margin of 10% after tax.  Two factors were responsible: (1) a state income tax cost that was subnormal because of a large loss carry-forward, now fully utilized, and (2) a large drop in the per-ton cost of newsprint (an unanticipated fluke that will be reversed in 1984).

Although our profit margins in 1983 were about average for newspapers such as the News, the paper’s performance, nevertheless, was a significant achievement considering the economic and retailing environment in Buffalo.

Buffalo has a concentration of heavy industry, a segment of the economy that was hit particularly hard by the recent recession and that has lagged the recovery.  As Buffalo consumers have suffered, so also have the paper’s retailing customers. Their numbers have shrunk over the past few years and many of those surviving have cut their linage.

Within this environment the News has one exceptional strength: its acceptance by the public, a matter measured by the paper’s “penetration ratio” - the percentage of households within the community purchasing the paper each day.  Our ratio is superb: for the six months ended September 30, 1983 the News stood number one in weekday penetration among the 100 largest papers in the United States (the ranking is based on “city zone” numbers compiled by the Audit Bureau of Circulations).

In interpreting the standings, it is important to note that many large cities have two papers, and that in such cases the penetration of either paper is necessarily lower than if there were a single paper, as in Buffalo.  Nevertheless, the list of the 100 largest papers includes many that have a city to themselves.  Among these, the News is at the top nationally, far ahead of many of the country’s best-known dailies.

Among Sunday editions of these same large dailies, the News ranks number three in penetration - ten to twenty percentage points ahead of many well-known papers.  It was not always this way in Buffalo. Below we show Sunday circulation in Buffalo in the years prior to 1977 compared with the present period.  In that earlier period the Sunday paper was the Courier-Express (the News was not then publishing a Sunday paper).  Now, of course, it is the News.

```text
   Average Sunday Circulation
   --------------------------
Year                    Circulation
----                    -----------
1970                      314,000
1971                      306,000
1972                      302,000
1973                      290,000
1974                      278,000
1975                      269,000
1976                      270,000
```

1984 (Current)            376,000

We believe a paper’s penetration ratio to be the best measure of the strength of its franchise.  Papers with unusually high penetration in the geographical area that is of prime interest to major local retailers, and with relatively little circulation elsewhere, are exceptionally efficient buys for those retailers.  Low-penetration papers have a far less compelling message to present to advertisers.

In our opinion, three factors largely account for the unusual acceptance of the News in the community.  Among these, points 2 and 3 also may explain the popularity of the Sunday News compared to that of the Sunday Courier-Express when it was the sole Sunday paper:

(1) The first point has nothing to do with merits of the News.  Both emigration and immigration are relatively low in Buffalo.  A stable population is more interested and involved in the activities of its community than is a shifting population - and, as a result, is more interested in the content of the local daily paper. Increase the movement in and out of a city and penetration ratios will fall.

(2) The News has a reputation for editorial quality and integrity that was honed by our longtime editor, the legendary Alfred Kirchhofer, and that has been preserved and extended by Murray Light.  This reputation was enormously important to our success in establishing a Sunday paper against entrenched competition.  And without a Sunday edition, the News would not have survived in the long run.

(3) The News lives up to its name - it delivers a very unusual amount of news.  During 1983, our “news hole” (editorial material - not ads) amounted to 50% of the newspaper’s content (excluding preprinted inserts). Among papers that dominate their markets and that are of comparable or larger size, we know of only one whose news hole percentage exceeds that of the News.  Comprehensive figures are not available, but a sampling indicates an average percentage in the high 30s.  In other words, page for page, our mix gives readers over 25% more news than the typical paper.  This news-rich mixture is by intent. Some publishers, pushing for higher profit margins, have cut their news holes during the past decade.  We have maintained ours and will continue to do so.  Properly written and edited, a full serving of news makes our paper more valuable to the reader and contributes to our unusual penetration ratio.

Despite the strength of the News’ franchise, gains in ROP linage (advertising printed within the newspaper pages as contrasted to preprinted inserts) are going to be very difficult to achieve.  We had an enormous gain in preprints during 1983: lines rose from 9.3 million to 16.4 million, revenues from $3.6 million to $8.1 million.  These gains are consistent with national trends, but exaggerated in our case by business we picked up when the Courier-Express closed.

On balance, the shift from ROP to preprints has negative economic implications for us.  Profitability on preprints is less and the business is more subject to competition from alternative means of delivery.  Furthermore, a reduction in ROP linage means less absolute space devoted to news (since the news hole percentage remains constant), thereby reducing the utility of the paper to the reader.

Stan Lipsey became Publisher of the Buffalo News at midyear upon the retirement of Henry Urban.  Henry never flinched during the dark days of litigation and losses following our introduction of the Sunday paper - an introduction whose wisdom was questioned by many in the newspaper business, including some within our own building.  Henry is admired by the Buffalo business community, he’s admired by all who worked for him, and he is admired by Charlie and me.  Stan worked with Henry for several years, and has worked for Berkshire Hathaway since 1969.  He has been personally involved in all nuts-and-bolts aspects of the newspaper business from editorial to circulation.  We couldn’t do better.

## 布法罗晚报

首先澄清一下：公司的法定名称仍是布法罗晚报公司（Buffalo Evening News, Inc.），但自一年多前开始发行晨报之后，报纸的名称就改为《布法罗新闻报》（Buffalo News）。

1983年，《新闻报》的税后利润率略高于设定的10%目标，有两个原因：（1）此前积累的大额可抵扣亏损，使州所得税支出低于正常水平，而这部分抵扣现已用尽；（2）每吨新闻纸成本大幅下降，这是一件未曾预料的幸运事，1984年将会逆转。

尽管1983年《新闻报》的利润率与同类报纸的平均水平大致相当，但考虑到布法罗的经济与零售环境，这依然是一项重要成就。

布法罗重工业集中，而重工业在最近一次经济衰退中受到格外严重的冲击，复苏也相对滞后。布法罗的消费者受到影响，报纸的零售商广告客户同样如此。近几年，这些零售商数量有所减少，许多幸存企业也削减了广告行数。

在这种环境中，《新闻报》拥有一项非凡优势：深受当地公众欢迎。这可以通过“渗透率”衡量，即社区内每天购买报纸的家庭所占比例。我们的渗透率非常优秀：截至1983年9月30日的六个月中，按发行量稽核局编制的市区数据，在美国规模最大的100份报纸中，《新闻报》的工作日渗透率位居第一。

解读排名时必须考虑，许多大城市有两家报纸；在这种情况下，各家报纸的渗透率必然低于布法罗这种只有一家报纸的城市。不过，百强名单里同样有许多报纸在各自城市独家经营。即使与这些报纸比较，《新闻报》仍遥遥领先于全国其他许多著名日报。

在这批大型日报的星期日版中，《新闻报》的渗透率排名第三，比许多著名报纸高出10—20个百分点。布法罗过去并非如此。下表将1977年以前布法罗的星期日报纸发行量，与现在作比较。过去那段时期，星期日报纸是《信使快报》（Courier-Express），当时《新闻报》还没有星期日版。现在当然是《新闻报》了。

**平均星期日发行量**

|---|---:|

| 1973 | 290,000 |

我们认为，渗透率是衡量报纸特许经营地位强弱的最佳指标。如果一份报纸在当地主要零售商最关注的地理区域拥有异常高的渗透率，而其他地区发行量相对较少，那么零售商就能极为有效地利用它投放广告。渗透率较低的报纸，很难向广告商提出同样有说服力的价值主张。

在我们看来，《新闻报》在社区内受到如此广泛欢迎，主要有三个原因。其中第二和第三点，也可能解释了《新闻报》星期日版为何比过去独占当地市场的《信使快报》星期日版更受欢迎：

（1）第一点与《新闻报》本身的优点无关。布法罗的人口迁入和迁出都相对较少。与人口流动频繁的城市相比，稳定的居民更关心并参与社区活动，因此也更关注本地日报内容。城市迁入迁出的人口越多，报纸渗透率就越低。

（2）《新闻报》以编辑质量和诚信著称。这一声誉由我们长期任职、堪称传奇的编辑阿尔弗雷德·基尔希霍费尔（Alfred Kirchhofer）打下基础，并由默里·莱特（Murray Light）继承和发扬。当我们面对根基深厚的竞争者推出星期日版时，这一声誉对成功极为重要。没有星期日版，《新闻报》从长期看也无法生存。

（3）《新闻报》名副其实——它提供的新闻内容特别多。1983年，我们的“新闻版面比例”（新闻及编辑内容，不含广告）达到报纸总内容的50%（不包括预印插页）。在市场占主导地位、规模与我们相当或更大的报纸中，据我们所知，只有一家这一比例高于我们。虽然缺乏全面统计，但抽样显示平均比例处于30%多的较高区间。也就是说，按相同页数计算，我们给读者提供的新闻比一般报纸多25%以上。这种重新闻内容的结构是有意选择的。过去十年，一些出版商为了提高利润率缩减新闻版面。我们一直保持新闻比例，今后也会如此。经过妥善采写和编辑的充足新闻内容，会提高报纸对读者的价值，也有助于形成我们异常高的渗透率。

尽管《新闻报》的特许经营地位很强，报纸正文广告（ROP，即直接印在报纸版面上的广告，与预印插页相区别）的行数今后很难继续增加。1983年，我们的预印插页广告增长巨大：行数从930万增至1,640万，收入从360万美元增至810万美元。这种增长与全国趋势一致，但《信使快报》停刊后我们承接了一部分业务，使我们的增长更加突出。

总体上，从报纸正文广告转向预印插页，对我们的经济性有不利影响。插页广告利润率较低，而且更容易受到其他投递方式竞争。与此同时，正文广告行数减少，也意味着新闻内容的绝对版面减少（因为新闻版面比例保持不变），从而降低报纸对读者的效用。

亨利·厄本（Henry Urban）退休后，斯坦·利普西（Stan Lipsey）于年中出任《布法罗新闻报》发行人。在我们推出星期日版之后，曾经历诉讼和亏损的艰难时期，新闻业内很多人——包括我们自己办公楼里的一些人——都怀疑这一决定是否明智，亨利却从未退缩。布法罗商界敬重他，与他共事过的人敬重他，查理和我也敬重他。斯坦曾与亨利合作多年，自1969年起便在伯克希尔工作，亲自参与过报纸从编辑到发行的所有具体业务。我们找不到更合适的人选。

## See’s Candy Shops

The financial results at See’s continue to be exceptional. The business possesses a valuable and solid consumer franchise and a manager equally valuable and solid.

In recent years See’s has encountered two important problems, at least one of which is well on its way toward solution.  That problem concerns costs, except those for raw materials.  We have enjoyed a break on raw material costs in recent years though so, of course, have our competitors.  One of these days we will get a nasty surprise in the opposite direction.  In effect, raw material costs are largely beyond our control since we will, as a matter of course, buy the finest ingredients that we can, regardless of changes in their price levels.  We regard product quality as sacred.

But other kinds of costs are more controllable, and it is in this area that we have had problems.  On a per-pound basis, our costs (not including those for raw materials) have increased in the last few years at a rate significantly greater than the increase in the general price level.  It is vital to our competitive position and profit potential that we reverse this trend.

In recent months much better control over costs has been attained and we feel certain that our rate of growth in these costs in 1984 will be below the rate of inflation.  This confidence arises out of our long experience with the managerial talents of Chuck Huggins.  We put Chuck in charge the day we took over, and his record has been simply extraordinary, as shown by the following table:

The other problem we face, as the table suggests, is our recent inability to achieve meaningful gains in pounds sold.  The industry has the same problem.  But for many years we outperformed the industry in this respect and now we are not.

The poundage volume in our retail stores has been virtually unchanged each year for the past four, despite small increases every year in the number of shops (and in distribution expense as well).  Of course, dollar volume has increased because we have raised prices significantly.  But we regard the most important measure of retail trends to be units sold per store rather than dollar volume.  On a same-store basis (counting only shops open throughout both years) with all figures adjusted to a 52-week year, poundage was down .8 of 1% during 1983.  This small decline was our best same-store performance since 1979; the cumulative decline since then has been about 8%.  Quantity-order volume, about 25% of our total, has plateaued in recent years following very large poundage gains throughout the 1970s.

We are not sure to what extent this flat volume - both in the retail shop area and the quantity order area - is due to our pricing policies and to what extent it is due to static industry volume, the recession, and the extraordinary share of market we already enjoy in our primary marketing area.  Our price increase for 1984 is much more modest than has been the case in the past few years, and we hope that next year we can report better volume figures to you.  But we have no basis to forecast these.

Despite the volume problem, See’s strengths are many and important.  In our primary marketing area, the West, our candy is preferred by an enormous margin to that of any competitor.  In fact, we believe most lovers of chocolate prefer it to candy costing two or three times as much. (In candy, as in stocks, price and value can differ; price is what you give, value is what you get.) The quality of customer service in our shops - operated throughout the country by us and not by franchisees is every bit as good as the product.  Cheerful, helpful personnel are as much a trademark of See’s as is the logo on the box.  That’s no small achievement in a business that requires us to hire about 2000 seasonal workers.  We know of no comparably-sized organization that betters the quality of customer service delivered by Chuck Huggins and his associates.

Because we have raised prices so modestly in 1984, we expect See’s profits this year to be about the same as in 1983.

## 喜诗糖果店

喜诗糖果的财务表现继续十分出色。这门生意拥有宝贵而坚实的消费者特许经营优势，也拥有一位同样宝贵而可靠的管理者。

近年来喜诗遇到了两个重要问题，其中至少有一个正朝着解决方向取得明显进展。这个问题涉及除原材料外的成本。近年原材料成本给了我们一些有利条件，竞争对手当然也同样受益。总有一天，情况会反过来，让我们吃上一惊。实际上，原材料成本大体不受我们控制，因为无论价格如何变动，我们都会一如既往地采购能够买到的最好原料。我们认为产品质量不容妥协。

不过，其他成本更容易控制，而我们恰恰在这方面遇到了问题。近几年，按每磅糖果计算的成本（不包括原材料），增长速度明显快于总体物价水平。要保持竞争地位和利润潜力，我们必须扭转这一趋势。

最近几个月，成本控制已明显改善，我们确信1984年这些成本的增长速度会低于通货膨胀率。这种信心来自我们对查克·哈金斯（Chuck Huggins）管理才能的长期了解。我们收购当天就任命查克负责喜诗，他的业绩极为出色，如下表所示。

从表格可以看出，我们面对的另一个问题，是最近无法实现有意义的销量增长。整个行业也存在相同问题，但过去许多年，我们在销量方面一直跑赢行业，现在却不再如此。

尽管每年门店数量略有增加（配送费用也随之提高），最近四年各零售店售出的糖果重量几乎没有变化。当然，由于我们大幅提高了价格，销售金额仍然有所增加。但在我们看来，衡量零售趋势最重要的指标，是每家门店售出的件数或数量，而不是销售金额。按同店口径（只计入比较两年均完整营业的门店），并把所有数字调整为52周的会计年度，1983年的销售重量下降了0.8%。这是自1979年以来我们最好的同店表现；自那时以来累计降幅约为8%。批量订购业务占总销量约25%，在20世纪70年代销量大幅增长后，近年也进入了平台期。

我们不确定，无论零售门店还是批量订购业务，销量停滞究竟有多大程度源于定价政策，又有多大程度源于行业总销量不增长、经济衰退，以及我们在核心市场已经拥有极高的市场份额。1984年我们的提价幅度比过去几年温和得多，希望明年可以报告更好的销量数字，但我们没有依据进行预测。

尽管销量存在问题，喜诗仍有许多重要优势。在我们主要的西部市场，消费者对喜诗糖果的偏好远远超过任何竞争对手。实际上，我们认为许多巧克力爱好者更喜欢喜诗，而不是价格为喜诗两三倍的糖果。（糖果和股票一样，价格与价值可能不同；价格是你付出的，价值是你得到的。）我们全国门店均为直营而非加盟，店内客户服务质量毫不逊色于产品。热情、乐于助人的员工，就像包装盒上的商标一样，是喜诗的标志。对于一家需要雇用约2,000名季节性员工的企业，这并不是小成就。在我们所知的同等规模企业中，没有哪家提供的客户服务质量能超过查克·哈金斯及其同事。

由于1984年提价幅度相当温和，我们预计喜诗今年的利润将与1983年大致持平。

## Insurance - Controlled Operations

We both operate insurance companies and have a large economic interest in an insurance business we don’t operate, GEICO.  The results for all can be summed up easily: in aggregate, the companies we operate and whose underwriting results reflect the consequences of decisions that were my responsibility a few years ago, had absolutely terrible results. Fortunately, GEICO, whose policies I do not influence, simply shot the lights out.  The inference you draw from this summary is the correct one.  I made some serious mistakes a few years ago that came home to roost.

The industry had its worst underwriting year in a long time, as indicated by the table below:

```text
                          Yearly Change      Combined Ratio
                           in Premiums        after Policy-
                           Written (%)      holder Dividends
                          -------------     ----------------
1972 ....................     10.2                96.2
1973 ....................      8.0                99.2
1974 ....................      6.2               105.4
1975 ....................     11.0               107.9
1976 ....................     21.9               102.4
```
