The combined ratio represents total insurance costs (losses incurred plus expenses) compared to revenue from premiums; a ratio below 100 indicates an underwriting profit, and one above 100 indicates a loss.

For a number of years, we have told you that an annual increase by the industry of about 10% per year in premiums written is necessary for the combined ratio to remain roughly unchanged.  We assumed in making that assertion that expenses as a percentage of premium volume would stay relatively stable and that losses would grow at about 10% annually because of the combined influence of unit volume increases, inflation, and judicial rulings that expand what is covered by the insurance policy.
1984.chinese:
贝氏的数据几乎覆盖整个行业，包括股份制、相互制及互惠制保险公司。综合成本率，是保险成本总额（已发生赔款加费用）与保费收入的比率；低于100表示承保盈利，高于100表示承保亏损。

多年来，我们一直告诉各位：行业签单保费每年必须增长约10%，综合成本率才大致能够维持不变。作出这一判断时，我们假设费用占保费的比例相对稳定，而赔款则会因业务量增加、通胀，以及司法判决扩大保单保障范围的共同作用，每年增长约10%。

1984.english: Our opinion is proving dismayingly accurate: a premium increase of 10% per year since 1979 would have produced an aggregate increase through 1984 of 61% and a combined ratio in 1984 almost identical to the 100.6 of 1979.  Instead, the industry had only a 30% increase in premiums and a 1984 combined ratio of 117.7. Today, we continue to believe that the key index to the trend of underwriting profitability is the year-to-year percentage change in industry premium volume.
1984.chinese: 我们的看法正准确得令人沮丧：若自1979年起保费每年增长10%，到1984年累计增幅就是61%，1984年的综合成本率也会与1979年的100.6几乎相同。实际情况却是：行业保费只增长30%，1984年的综合成本率达到117.7。今天，我们仍认为，判断承保盈利趋势的关键指标，是行业保费总额的同比增幅。

1984.english: It now appears that premium volume in 1985 will grow well over 10%.  Therefore, assuming that catastrophes are at a “normal” level, we would expect the combined ratio to begin easing downward toward the end of the year.  However, under our industrywide loss assumptions (i.e., increases of 10% annually), five years of 15%-per-year increases in premiums would be required to get the combined ratio back to 100.  This would mean a doubling of industry volume by 1989, an outcome that seems highly unlikely to us.  Instead, we expect several years of premium gains somewhat above the 10% level, followed by highly- competitive pricing that generally will produce combined ratios in the 108-113 range.
1984.chinese: 如今看来，1985年保费总额的增幅会明显超过10%。因此，假设巨灾处于“正常”水平，我们预计综合成本率将在年底前开始缓慢下降。不过，按我们对全行业赔款的假设（即每年增加10%），保费必须连续五年每年增长15%，综合成本率才能回到100。这意味着到1989年行业保费总额要翻一番；我们觉得这种结果很不可能。相反，我们预计保费会连续几年以略高于10%的速度增长，然后价格竞争变得激烈，综合成本率通常会落在108—113之间。

1984.english: Our own combined ratio in 1984 was a humbling 134. (Here, as throughout this report, we exclude structured settlements and the assumption of loss reserves in reporting this ratio.  Much additional detail, including the effect of discontinued operations on the ratio, appears on pages 42-43).  This is the third year in a row that our underwriting performance has been far poorer than that of the industry.  We expect an improvement in the combined ratio in 1985, and also expect our improvement to be substantially greater than that of the industry.  Mike Goldberg has corrected many of the mistakes I made before he took over insurance operations.  Moreover, our business is concentrated in lines that have experienced poorer-than-average results during the past several years, and that circumstance has begun to subdue many of our competitors and even eliminate some. With the competition shaken, we were able during the last half of 1984 to raise prices significantly in certain important lines with little loss of business.
1984.chinese: 我们自己1984年的综合成本率为134，实在叫人抬不起头。（此处及本报告其他地方报告这一比率时，均剔除结构化赔付和赔款准备金承接业务。第42—43页有大量补充细节，包括已终止经营业务对该比率的影响。）我们承保表现远逊行业，已是连续第三年。我们预计1985年综合成本率会改善，而且改善幅度将大大超过行业。迈克·戈德伯格接管保险业务前，我犯过不少错误，他已纠正了其中许多。此外，我们的业务集中在过去几年业绩差于行业平均的险种，这种局面已使许多竞争者元气大伤，甚至淘汰了一些。对手阵脚动摇，让我们能在1984年下半年，对若干重要险种大幅提价，而几乎没有流失业务。

1984.english:
For some years I have told you that there could be a day coming when our premier financial strength would make a real difference in the competitive position of our insurance operation.  That day may have arrived.  We are almost without question the strongest property/casualty insurance operation in the country, with a capital position far superior to that of well-known companies of much greater size.

Equally important, our corporate policy is to retain that superiority.  The buyer of insurance receives only a promise in exchange for his cash.  The value of that promise should be appraised against the possibility of adversity, not prosperity. At a minimum, the promise should appear able to withstand a prolonged combination of depressed financial markets and exceptionally unfavorable underwriting results.  Our insurance subsidiaries are both willing and able to keep their promises in any such environment - and not too many other companies clearly are.
1984.chinese:
几年来，我一直说，也许有一天，我们一流的财务实力会真正改变保险业务的竞争地位。这一天可能已经到了。我们几乎毫无疑问是全美财务实力最强的财产及意外责任保险经营机构，资本状况远胜一些名气很大、规模也大得多的公司。

同样重要的是，我们的公司政策，就是保持这种优势。买保险的人交出现金，换来的只是一份承诺。衡量承诺的价值，应看逆境中的可能遭遇，而非繁荣中的表现。至少，这份承诺应当经得住金融市场长期低迷与承保结果极度不利同时出现的考验。无论这种环境如何，我们的保险子公司既愿意、也有能力履行承诺；其他公司能明确做到这一点的，并没有多少。

1984.english: Our financial strength is a particular asset in the business of structured settlements and loss reserve assumptions that we reported on last year.  The claimant in a structured settlement and the insurance company that has reinsured loss reserves need to be completely confident that payments will be forthcoming for decades to come.  Very few companies in the property/casualty field can meet this test of unquestioned long-term strength. (In fact, only a handful of companies exists with which we will reinsure our own liabilities.)
1984.chinese: 在去年介绍过的结构化赔付与赔款准备金承接业务中，我们的财务实力尤其宝贵。结构化赔付的索赔人，以及把赔款准备金责任再保险出去的保险公司，都必须完全确信，未来数十年会持续收到付款。财产及意外责任保险领域，能通过这种长期实力毫无疑问的考验的公司，少之又少。（事实上，愿意让其再保险我们自身责任的公司，我们只找得出屈指可数的几家。）

1984.english:
We have grown in these new lines of business: funds that we hold to offset assumed liabilities grew from $16.2 million to $30.6 million during the year.  We expect growth to continue and perhaps to greatly accelerate.  To support this projected growth we have added substantially to the capital of Columbia Insurance Company, our reinsurance unit specializing in structured settlements and loss reserve assumptions.  While these businesses are very competitive, returns should be satisfactory.

At GEICO the news, as usual, is mostly good.  That company achieved excellent unit growth in its primary insurance business during 1984, and the performance of its investment portfolio continued to be extraordinary.  Though underwriting results deteriorated late in the year, they still remain far better than those of the industry.  Our ownership in GEICO at yearend amounted to 36% and thus our interest in their direct property/casualty volume of $885 million amounted to $320 million, or well over double our own premium volume.
1984.chinese:
这些新业务已经增长：我们为抵偿所承接负债而持有的资金，年内从1620万美元增至3060万美元。我们预计会继续增长，甚至可能大大加速。为支持预期增长，我们大幅增加了哥伦比亚保险公司的资本；这家再保险子公司，专营结构化赔付和赔款准备金承接。虽然这些业务竞争非常激烈，回报应仍令人满意。

GEICO的消息照例大多不错。1984年，该公司主要保险业务的保单业务量实现了出色增长，投资组合的表现继续非同寻常。虽然年末承保结果恶化，仍远优于行业。年末我们持有GEICO的36%，因而它8.85亿美元的直接财产及意外责任保险业务量中，归属于我们的份额为3.20亿美元，是我们自身保费总额的两倍多。

1984.english: I have reported to you in the past few years that the performance of GEICO’s stock has considerably exceeded that company’s business performance, brilliant as the latter has been. In those years, the carrying value of our GEICO investment on our balance sheet grew at a rate greater than the growth in GEICO’s intrinsic business value.  I warned you that over performance by the stock relative to the performance of the business obviously could not occur every year, and that in some years the stock must under perform the business.  In 1984 that occurred and the carrying value of our interest in GEICO changed hardly at all, while the intrinsic business value of that interest increased substantially.  Since 27% of Berkshire’s net worth at the beginning of 1984 was represented by GEICO, its static market value had a significant impact upon our rate of gain for the year.  We are not at all unhappy with such a result: we would far rather have the business value of GEICO increase by X during the year, while market value decreases, than have the intrinsic value increase by only 1/2 X with market value soaring.  In GEICO’s case, as in all of our investments, we look to business performance, not market performance.  If we are correct in expectations regarding the business, the market eventually will follow along.
1984.chinese: 过去几年，我向各位报告过，尽管GEICO本身的经营表现已相当出色，其股价表现仍大大超过了经营表现。那些年，我们资产负债表上GEICO投资的账面金额，增速高于GEICO企业内在价值。我提醒过各位，股票表现超过企业表现，显然不可能年年如此，总有些年份股票会落后于企业。1984年正是这样：我们所持GEICO权益的账面金额几乎未变，内在价值却大幅增加。1984年年初，GEICO占伯克希尔净资产的27%，所以它市值停滞，对我们全年的增长率影响显著。这样的结果，我们一点也不难过：我们宁愿GEICO的企业价值一年增长X、市值反而下降，也不愿内在价值只增长1/2 X、市值却飞涨。对GEICO，和对我们所有投资一样，我们看企业表现，而非市场表现。只要对企业的预期正确，市场终究会跟上来。

1984.english: You, as shareholders of Berkshire, have benefited in enormous measure from the talents of GEICO’s Jack Byrne, Bill Snyder, and Lou Simpson.  In its core business - low-cost auto and homeowners insurance - GEICO has a major, sustainable competitive advantage.  That is a rare asset in business generally, and it’s almost non-existent in the field of financial services. (GEICO, itself, illustrates this point: despite the company’s excellent management, superior profitability has eluded GEICO in all endeavors other than its core business.) In a large industry, a competitive advantage such as GEICO’s provides the potential for unusual economic rewards, and Jack and Bill continue to exhibit great skill in realizing that potential.
1984.chinese: 各位作为伯克希尔股东，已从GEICO的杰克·伯恩、比尔·斯奈德和卢·辛普森的才能中获得巨大好处。GEICO的核心业务——低成本汽车及房主保险——有一项重大而持久的竞争优势。在整个商界，这已属稀有资产；在金融服务业，几乎绝无仅有。（GEICO本身就说明了这一点：尽管管理优秀，核心业务以外的所有尝试，它始终未能获得超群的盈利水平。）在一个大行业里，GEICO这样的竞争优势蕴含着非凡经济回报的潜力；杰克和比尔继续以高超本领，将潜力兑现。

1984.english:
Most of the funds generated by GEICO’s core insurance operation are made available to Lou for investment.  Lou has the rare combination of temperamental and intellectual characteristics that produce outstanding long-term investment performance.  Operating with below-average risk, he has generated returns that have been by far the best in the insurance industry. I applaud and appreciate the efforts and talents of these three outstanding managers.

## Errors in Loss Reserving

Any shareholder in a company with important interests in the property/casualty insurance business should have some understanding of the weaknesses inherent in the reporting of current earnings in that industry.  Phil Graham, when publisher of the Washington Post, described the daily newspaper as “a first rough draft of history”.  Unfortunately, the financial statements of a property/casualty insurer provide, at best, only a first rough draft of earnings and financial condition.
1984.chinese:
GEICO核心保险业务产生的大部分资金，都交给卢去投资。卢兼具少见的性情与才智，正是这两者的结合，造就了出色的长期投资表现。他承担的风险低于平均水平，回报却遥遥领先保险行业。我赞赏并感激这三位出色经理人的努力和才干。

## 赔款准备金估计中的错误

如果一家公司的财产及意外责任保险权益举足轻重，其股东就应对该行业当期利润报告固有的缺陷有所了解。菲尔·格雷厄姆担任《华盛顿邮报》发行人时，曾把日报称为“历史的第一份粗略草稿”。不幸的是，财产及意外责任保险公司的财务报表，充其量也只能算利润和财务状况的第一份粗略草稿。

1984.english:
The determination of costs is the main problem.  Most of an insurer’s costs result from losses on claims, and many of the losses that should be charged against the current year’s revenue are exceptionally difficult to estimate.  Sometimes the extent of these losses, or even their existence, is not known for decades.

The loss expense charged in a property/casualty company’s current income statement represents: (1) losses that occurred and were paid during the year; (2) estimates for losses that occurred and were reported to the insurer during the year, but which have yet to be settled; (3) estimates of ultimate dollar costs for losses that occurred during the year but of which the insurer is unaware (termed “IBNR”: incurred but not reported); and (4) the net effect of revisions this year of similar estimates for (2) and (3) made in past years.
1984.chinese:
主要问题在于成本的确定。保险公司的成本，大部分来自理赔损失，而许多本应从当年收入中扣除的损失，极难估计。有时，损失到底多大，甚至损失是否存在，都要数十年后才知道。

财产及意外责任保险公司当期损益表计入的赔款费用包括：（1）年内发生并已支付的赔款；（2）年内发生、已向保险公司报案，但尚未结案的赔款估计；（3）年内已发生、保险公司却尚不知情的损失，其最终美元成本的估计（称为“IBNR”，即已发生但未报告）；（4）本年对往年按（2）与（3）所作类似估计进行修正的净影响。

1984.english: Such revisions may be long delayed, but eventually any estimate of losses that causes the income for year X to be misstated must be corrected, whether it is in year X + 1, or X + 10.  This, perforce, means that earnings in the year of correction also are misstated.  For example, assume a claimant was injured by one of our insureds in 1979 and we thought a settlement was likely to be made for $10,000.  That year we would have charged $10,000 to our earnings statement for the estimated cost of the loss and, correspondingly, set up a liability reserve on the balance sheet for that amount.  If we settled the claim in 1984 for $100,000, we would charge earnings with a loss cost of $90,000 in 1984, although that cost was truly an expense of 1979. And if that piece of business was our only activity in 1979, we would have badly misled ourselves as to costs, and you as to earnings.
1984.chinese: 这种修正可能拖延很久，但凡损失估计导致X年利润失实，最终总要纠正，无论是在X + 1年，还是X + 10年。这也就不可避免地使纠正年份的利润同样失实。例如，假设1979年，我们的一位被保险人使一位索赔人受伤，我们认为可能以10,000美元和解。当年，我们会把估计损失成本10,000美元计入损益表，并在资产负债表上设立等额的负债准备金。如果1984年最终以100,000美元结案，我们就会在1984年利润中扣除90,000美元赔款成本，尽管它实际属于1979年的费用。如果这笔业务是我们1979年唯一的业务，我们就会在成本上严重误导自己，在利润上严重误导各位。

1984.english: The necessarily-extensive use of estimates in assembling the figures that appear in such deceptively precise form in the income statement of property/casualty companies means that some error must seep in, no matter how proper the intentions of management.  In an attempt to minimize error, most insurers use various statistical techniques to adjust the thousands of individual loss evaluations (called case reserves) that comprise the raw data for estimation of aggregate liabilities.  The extra reserves created by these adjustments are variously labeled “bulk”, “development”, or “supplemental” reserves.  The goal of the adjustments should be a loss-reserve total that has a 50-50 chance of being proved either slightly too high or slightly too low when all losses that occurred prior to the date of the financial statement are ultimately paid.
1984.chinese: 财产及意外责任保险公司损益表里的数字，看起来精确得很，却难免误导；编制这些数字必须大量使用估计，所以管理层无论多么诚实，总会有误差渗入。为了尽量减少误差，多数保险公司采用各种统计方法，调整成千上万笔个别赔案估值（称为逐案准备金）；这些估值，是估计负债总额的原始数据。调整增加的准备金，有的叫“总括准备金”，有的叫“发展准备金”或“补充准备金”。调整的目标应是：当财务报表日以前发生的所有赔款最终付清时，赔款准备金总额被证明略高或略低的概率，各占50%。

1984.english:
At Berkshire, we have added what we thought were appropriate supplemental reserves but in recent years they have not been adequate.  It is important that you understand the magnitude of the errors that have been involved in our reserving.  You can thus see for yourselves just how imprecise the process is, and also judge whether we may have some systemic bias that should make you wary of our current and future figures.

The following table shows the results from insurance underwriting as we have reported them to you in recent years, and also gives you calculations a year later on an “if-we-knew-then- what-we think-we-know-now” basis.  I say “what we think we know now” because the adjusted figures still include a great many estimates for losses that occurred in the earlier years. However, many claims from the earlier years have been settled so that our one-year-later estimate contains less guess work than our earlier estimate:
1984.chinese:
在伯克希尔，我们增设了自认为恰当的补充准备金，但近年仍然不够。各位需要了解，我们计提准备金的误差究竟有多大。这样，您就能亲眼看出这套过程有多不精确，也能判断，我们是否存在某种系统性偏差，以致您应对我们目前及未来的数字保持警惕。

下表列出近年我们向各位报告的承保结果，并列出一年后重新计算的结果，其依据是：“如果当时就知道我们现在自以为知道的事。”我说“自以为知道”，是因为调整后的数字，仍包含大量对早年发生损失的估计。不过，早年的许多赔案已经结清，因此一年后的估计，比原先少了一些猜测：

1984.english:
Our structured settlement and loss-reserve assumption businesses are not included in this table.  Important additional information on loss reserve experience appears on pages 43-45.

To help you understand this table, here is an explanation of the most recent figures: 1984’s reported pre-tax underwriting loss of $45.4 million consists of $27.6 million we estimate that we lost on 1984’s business, plus the increased loss of $17.8 million reflected in the corrected figure for 1983.

As you can see from reviewing the table, my errors in reporting to you have been substantial and recently have always presented a better underwriting picture than was truly the case. This is a source of particular chagrin to me because: (1) I like for you to be able to count on what I say; (2) our insurance managers and I undoubtedly acted with less urgency than we would have had we understood the full extent of our losses; and (3) we paid income taxes calculated on overstated earnings and thereby gave the government money that we didn’t need to.  (These overpayments eventually correct themselves, but the delay is long and we don’t receive interest on the amounts we overpaid.)
1984.chinese:
本表不包括我们的结构化赔付与赔款准备金承接业务。第43—45页另有赔款准备金实际经验的重要补充资料。

为帮助理解此表，现解释最新数字：1984年报告的税前承保亏损4540万美元，包括我们估计1984年业务亏损的2760万美元，加上1983年修正数字所体现的亏损增加额1780万美元。

各位看表就能知道，我向各位报告时的误差相当大，而且近来一律把承保情况说得比实际更好。这让我尤其难堪，因为：（1）我希望各位能够相信我的话；（2）若当时了解全部亏损程度，我和保险业务经理人采取行动，无疑会更有紧迫感；（3）我们按虚高的利润缴了所得税，白白把本可不交的钱给了政府。（这些多缴税款最终会纠正，但要等很久，多缴部分也拿不到利息。）

1984.english: Because our business is weighted toward casualty and reinsurance lines, we have more problems in estimating loss costs than companies that specialize in property insurance. (When a building that you have insured burns down, you get a much faster fix on your costs than you do when an employer you have insured finds out that one of his retirees has contracted a disease attributable to work he did decades earlier.) But I still find our errors embarrassing.  In our direct business, we have far underestimated the mushrooming tendency of juries and courts to make the “deep pocket” pay, regardless of the factual situation and the past precedents for establishment of liability.  We also have underestimated the contagious effect that publicity regarding giant awards has on juries.  In the reinsurance area, where we have had our worst experience in under reserving, our customer insurance companies have made the same mistakes.  Since we set reserves based on information they supply us, their mistakes have become our mistakes.
1984.chinese: 我们的业务偏重意外责任险与再保险，因此比专营财产险的公司更难估计赔款成本。（一栋由您承保的楼房烧毁，确定成本要快得多；而若您承保的雇主发现，一位退休员工患病是数十年前工作所致，成本就难说了。）但我依然为我们的误差感到尴尬。在直接保险业务中，我们远远低估了一股愈演愈烈的倾向：陪审团和法院不顾事实情况与以往确立责任的判例，偏要让“财大气粗者”掏钱。我们也低估了巨额赔偿报道对陪审团的传染效应。准备金计提不足最严重的再保险领域，我们的客户保险公司犯了同样的错误；由于我们依据它们提供的资料计提准备金，它们的错误也就成了我们的错误。

1984.english: I heard a story recently that is applicable to our insurance accounting problems: a man was traveling abroad when he received a call from his sister informing him that their father had died unexpectedly.  It was physically impossible for the brother to get back home for the funeral, but he told his sister to take care of the funeral arrangements and to send the bill to him. After returning home he received a bill for several thousand dollars, which he promptly paid.  The following month another bill came along for $15, and he paid that too.  Another month followed, with a similar bill.  When, in the next month, a third bill for $15 was presented, he called his sister to ask what was going on.  “Oh”, she said.  “I forgot to tell you.  We buried Dad in a rented suit.”
1984.chinese: 最近听到一个故事，很适合说明我们的保险会计问题：一个人在国外旅行，接到姐妹打来的电话，说父亲突然去世。他实在赶不回去参加葬礼，便请她安排后事，把账单寄给他。回家后，他收到一张几千美元的账单，立即付清。次月，又来一张15美元的账单，他也付了。再过一个月，又是一张相同账单。到下个月，第三张15美元账单送来时，他打电话问她究竟怎么回事。“哦，”她说，“忘了告诉你，我们让爸爸穿着一套租来的西装下葬了。”

1984.english:
If you’ve been in the insurance business in recent years - particularly the reinsurance business - this story hurts.  We have tried to include all of our “rented suit” liabilities in our current financial statement, but our record of past error should make us humble, and you suspicious.  I will continue to report to you the errors, plus or minus, that surface each year.

Not all reserving errors in the industry have been of the innocent-but-dumb variety.  With underwriting results as bad as they have been in recent years - and with managements having as much discretion as they do in the presentation of financial statements - some unattractive aspects of human nature have manifested themselves.  Companies that would be out of business if they realistically appraised their loss costs have, in some cases, simply preferred to take an extraordinarily optimistic view about these yet-to-be-paid sums.  Others have engaged in various transactions to hide true current loss costs.
1984.chinese:
近年如果您做过保险，尤其是再保险，这个故事听着会疼。我们已尽量把所有“租西装”的负债都纳入本期财务报表；但过去的出错记录，应当让我们谦虚，也让各位多疑。今后每年浮现的误差，无论正负，我都会继续向各位报告。

行业里并非所有准备金误差，都属于无心而愚笨的那一类。近年承保结果如此糟糕，管理层在财务报表呈现上又有如此大的裁量权，人性中一些不太好看的部分就露了出来。有些公司，若如实估计赔款成本，本来已该关门，却干脆选择对尚未支付的金额作出极度乐观的估计；另一些则通过各种交易，掩盖真正的当期赔款成本。

1984.english:
Both of these approaches can “work” for a considerable time: external auditors cannot effectively police the financial statements of property/casualty insurers.  If liabilities of an insurer, correctly stated, would exceed assets, it falls to the insurer to volunteer this morbid information.  In other words, the corpse is supposed to file the death certificate.  Under this “honor system” of mortality, the corpse sometimes gives itself the benefit of the doubt.

In most businesses, of course, insolvent companies run out of cash.  Insurance is different: you can be broke but flush. Since cash comes in at the inception of an insurance policy and losses are paid much later, insolvent insurers don’t run out of cash until long after they have run out of net worth.  In fact, these “walking dead” often redouble their efforts to write business, accepting almost any price or risk, simply to keep the cash flowing in.  With an attitude like that of an embezzler who has gambled away his purloined funds, these companies hope that somehow they can get lucky on the next batch of business and thereby cover up earlier shortfalls.  Even if they don’t get lucky, the penalty to managers is usually no greater for a $100 million shortfall than one of $10 million; in the meantime, while the losses mount, the managers keep their jobs and perquisites.
1984.chinese:
这两种办法都可能“奏效”相当长的时间：外部审计师无法有效把关财产及意外责任保险公司的财务报表。若如实列示负债，就会发现负债已超过资产，那么主动报告这项噩耗的责任，落在保险公司自己身上。换句话说，尸体应当自己填死亡证明。在这种全凭自觉的死亡申报制度下，尸体有时会按“疑点利益归己”的原则，先饶自己一回。

当然，多数行业里，资不抵债的公司会耗尽现金。保险却不同：您可以破产，同时现金满兜。现金在保单起效时就进来了，赔款却很久以后才付，所以资不抵债的保险公司，要在净资产耗尽很久以后，才会耗尽现金。事实上，这些“行尸走肉”往往加倍卖力承揽业务，几乎什么价格、什么风险都接，只求现金继续流入。它们的心态像个把赃款赌光的挪用公款者，盼着下一批业务侥幸翻本，补上旧窟窿。即使运气没来，亏空1亿美元对经理人的惩罚，通常也不比亏空1000万美元更重；与此同时，损失不断增加，经理人却照样保住职位与待遇。

1984.english: The loss-reserving errors of other property/casualty companies are of more than academic interest to Berkshire.  Not only does Berkshire suffer from sell-at-any-price competition by the “walking dead”, but we also suffer when their insolvency is finally acknowledged.  Through various state guarantee funds that levy assessments, Berkshire ends up paying a portion of the insolvent insurers’ asset deficiencies, swollen as they usually are by the delayed detection that results from wrong reporting. There is even some potential for cascading trouble.  The insolvency of a few large insurers and the assessments by state guarantee funds that would follow could imperil weak-but- previously-solvent insurers.  Such dangers can be mitigated if state regulators become better at prompt identification and termination of insolvent insurers, but progress on that front has been slow.
1984.chinese: 其他财产及意外责任保险公司的准备金误差，对伯克希尔的影响绝非纯属学术。我们不仅要承受“行尸走肉”不计价格抢生意的竞争，还得在它们终于承认资不抵债时再吃一次亏。各州担保基金通过摊派征费，让伯克希尔最终分担这些破产保险公司的一部分资产缺口；错误报告延误了发现，缺口通常也因此越滚越大。甚至还可能出现连锁麻烦：几家大型保险公司倒下，随后的州担保基金摊派，可能危及那些原先虽未资不抵债、财务却已薄弱的公司。若州监管者能更及时地识别并终止资不抵债公司的经营，危险便可降低；但这方面进展缓慢。

1984.english:
## Washington Public Power Supply System

From October, 1983 through June, 1984 Berkshire’s insurance subsidiaries continuously purchased large quantities of bonds of Projects 1, 2, and 3 of Washington Public Power Supply System (“WPPSS”).  This is the same entity that, on July 1, 1983, defaulted on $2.2 billion of bonds issued to finance partial construction of the now-abandoned Projects 4 and 5. While there are material differences in the obligors, promises, and properties underlying the two categories of bonds, the problems of Projects 4 and 5 have cast a major cloud over Projects 1, 2, and 3, and might possibly cause serious problems for the latter issues.  In addition, there have been a multitude of problems related directly to Projects 1, 2, and 3 that could weaken or destroy an otherwise strong credit position arising from guarantees by Bonneville Power Administration.
1984.chinese:
## 华盛顿公共供电系统（Washington Public Power Supply System）

从1983年10月至1984年6月，伯克希尔的保险子公司持续大量买入华盛顿公共供电系统（简称WPPSS）第1、2、3号项目的债券。正是这家机构，在1983年7月1日，对为第4、5号项目部分建设融资而发行的22亿美元债券违约；这两个项目如今已被放弃。虽然两类债券背后的债务人、承诺与资产存在重大差异，第4、5号项目的麻烦仍给第1、2、3号项目投下巨大阴影，也可能给后者债券带来严重问题。此外，第1、2、3号项目本身也有诸多直接相关的问题，可能削弱甚至摧毁原本由邦纳维尔电力管理局担保所形成的强大信用基础。

1984.english:
Despite these important negatives, Charlie and I judged the risks at the time we purchased the bonds and at the prices Berkshire paid (much lower than present prices) to be considerably more than compensated for by prospects of profit.

As you know, we buy marketable stocks for our insurance companies based upon the criteria we would apply in the purchase of an entire business.  This business-valuation approach is not widespread among professional money managers and is scorned by many academics.  Nevertheless, it has served its followers well (to which the academics seem to say, “Well, it may be all right in practice, but it will never work in theory.”) Simply put, we feel that if we can buy small pieces of businesses with satisfactory underlying economics at a fraction of the per-share value of the entire business, something good is likely to happen to us - particularly if we own a group of such securities.
1984.chinese:
尽管有这些重大不利因素，查理和我认为，在我们当时买入的条件、以及伯克希尔支付的价格（远低于目前价格）下，获利前景足以补偿风险，而且绰绰有余。

各位知道，我们为保险公司买入可上市交易的股票，使用的标准与收购一家完整企业相同。这种企业估值方法，在专业资金管理者中并不普遍，还受到许多学者的嘲笑。不过，它一直让追随者受益良多（学者们对此仿佛在说：“好吧，实践上也许行得通，但理论上绝对不行。”）。简单说，我们认为，如果能用整家公司每股价值的一小部分，买到经济特性令人满意的企业的一小块，那么好事大概就会发生在我们身上；尤其当我们持有一组这样的证券时。

1984.english: We extend this business-valuation approach even to bond purchases such as WPPSS.  We compare the $139 million cost of our yearend investment in WPPSS to a similar $139 million investment in an operating business.  In the case of WPPSS, the “business” contractually earns $22.7 million after tax (via the interest paid on the bonds), and those earnings are available to us currently in cash.  We are unable to buy operating businesses with economics close to these.  Only a relatively few businesses earn the 16.3% after tax on unleveraged capital that our WPPSS investment does and those businesses, when available for purchase, sell at large premiums to that capital.  In the average negotiated business transaction, unleveraged corporate earnings of $22.7 million after-tax (equivalent to about $45 million pre- tax) might command a price of $250 - $300 million (or sometimes far more).  For a business we understand well and strongly like, we will gladly pay that much.  But it is double the price we paid to realize the same earnings from WPPSS bonds.
1984.chinese: 这种企业估值方法，也被我们用于购买WPPSS这样的债券。我们把年末WPPSS投资的1.39亿美元成本，同拿出1.39亿美元投资一家经营性企业作比较。WPPSS这门“生意”按合同每年赚取2270万美元税后收益（通过债券利息支付），而且这些收益当期就以现金交给我们。经济特性接近这个水平的经营性企业，我们买不到。只有相当少的企业能像我们的WPPSS投资一样，在不使用杠杆的资本上赚到16.3%的税后回报；而这些企业一旦出售，售价都会大大高于投入资本。在通常协商达成的企业交易中，不使用杠杆、税后赚2270万美元（约合税前4500万美元）的企业，可能要价2.50亿至3亿美元，有时高得多。如果我们很了解、也非常喜欢这家企业，会乐意付这个价。但这已是我们通过WPPSS债券获得同等收益所付价格的两倍。

1984.english: However, in the case of WPPSS, there is what we view to be a very slight risk that the “business” could be worth nothing within a year or two.  There also is the risk that interest payments might be interrupted for a considerable period of time. Furthermore, the most that the “business” could be worth is about the $205 million face value of the bonds that we own, an amount only 48% higher than the price we paid.
1984.chinese: 不过，在WPPSS这里，我们认为虽极小却确实存在一种风险：这门“生意”可能一两年内变得一文不值。利息支付也有中断相当长一段时间的风险。此外，这门“生意”最多只能值我们所持债券约2.05亿美元的面值，比买价仅高48%。

1984.english:
This ceiling on upside potential is an important minus.  It should be realized, however, that the great majority of operating businesses have a limited upside potential also unless more capital is continuously invested in them.  That is so because most businesses are unable to significantly improve their average returns on equity - even under inflationary conditions, though these were once thought to automatically raise returns.

(Let’s push our bond-as-a-business example one notch further: if you elect to “retain” the annual earnings of a 12% bond by using the proceeds from coupons to buy more bonds, earnings of that bond “business” will grow at a rate comparable to that of most operating businesses that similarly reinvest all earnings.  In the first instance, a 30-year, zero-coupon, 12% bond purchased today for $10 million will be worth $300 million in 2015.  In the second, a $10 million business that regularly earns 12% on equity and retains all earnings to grow, will also end up with $300 million of capital in 2015.  Both the business and the bond will earn over $32 million in the final year.)
1984.chinese:
上行潜力的这道天花板，是一项重要缺点。不过也应看到，绝大多数经营性企业，除非不断追加资本，上行潜力同样有限。原因在于，多数企业无法显著提高其平均股东权益回报率；即使处于通胀环境，也是如此，尽管人们曾以为通胀会自动提高回报率。

（让我们把“债券就是企业”的例子再推进一步：若您把一只收益率12%的债券每年支付的利息拿去买更多债券，从而选择“留存”年收益，这门债券“生意”的收益增速，就会与同样把全部利润再投资的多数经营性企业相当。第一种情况，今天花1000万美元买入一只30年期、收益率12%的零息债券，到2015年会值3亿美元。第二种情况，一家价值1000万美元的企业，若持续赚取12%的股东权益回报率，且把全部利润留作增长，到2015年也会拥有3亿美元资本。两者在最后一年，都会赚到超过3200万美元。）

1984.english: Our approach to bond investment - treating it as an unusual sort of “business” with special advantages and disadvantages - may strike you as a bit quirky.  However, we believe that many staggering errors by investors could have been avoided if they had viewed bond investment with a businessman’s perspective.  For example, in 1946, 20-year AAA tax-exempt bonds traded at slightly below a 1% yield.  In effect, the buyer of those bonds at that time bought a “business” that earned about 1% on “book value” (and that, moreover, could never earn a dime more than 1% on book), and paid 100 cents on the dollar for that abominable business.
1984.chinese: 我们把债券当作一种有特殊优缺点的非常规“生意”来投资，您可能觉得有点古怪。不过我们相信，投资者若从生意人的角度看债券，本来可以避免许多惊人的大错。例如，1946年，20年期AAA级免税债券的交易收益率略低于1%。实际上，当时买这类债券的人，是按每1美元“账面价值”付出100美分，买下一门账面回报率约1%的糟糕“生意”（而且它在账面价值上永远不可能多赚一分钱）。

1984.english: If an investor had been business-minded enough to think in those terms - and that was the precise reality of the bargain struck - he would have laughed at the proposition and walked away.  For, at the same time, businesses with excellent future prospects could have been bought at, or close to, book value while earning 10%, 12%, or 15% after tax on book.  Probably no business in America changed hands in 1946 at book value that the buyer believed lacked the ability to earn more than 1% on book. But investors with bond-buying habits eagerly made economic commitments throughout the year on just that basis.  Similar, although less extreme, conditions prevailed for the next two decades as bond investors happily signed up for twenty or thirty years on terms outrageously inadequate by business standards. (In what I think is by far the best book on investing ever written - “The Intelligent Investor”, by Ben Graham - the last section of the last chapter begins with, “Investment is most intelligent when it is most businesslike.” This section is called “A Final Word”, and it is appropriately titled.)
1984.chinese: 若投资者有足够的生意头脑，愿意如此思考——而这正是那笔交易的真实经济内容——他就会一笑置之，转身走人。因为与此同时，前景极佳、税后账面回报率达到10%、12%或15%的企业，按账面价值或接近账面价值就能买到。1946年，美国大概没有哪位买家，会按账面价值接手一家他认为连超过1%的账面回报率都赚不到的企业。但习惯买债券的投资者，全年都在热切地作出这种经济承诺。此后20年中，类似但没那么极端的状况一直存在：债券投资者欣然签下20年或30年的约定，而按做生意的标准，那些条件实在低得离谱。（在我看来，迄今最好的投资著作，是本·格雷厄姆的《聪明的投资者》。最后一章的最后一节，开篇写道：“投资越像做生意，就越明智。”这一节名为“最后的话”，这个标题十分贴切。）

1984.english: We will emphasize again that there is unquestionably some risk in the WPPSS commitment.  It is also the sort of risk that is difficult to evaluate.  Were Charlie and I to deal with 50 similar evaluations over a lifetime, we would expect our judgment to prove reasonably satisfactory.  But we do not get the chance to make 50 or even 5 such decisions in a single year.  Even though our long-term results may turn out fine, in any given year we run a risk that we will look extraordinarily foolish. (That’s why all of these sentences say “Charlie and I”, or “we”.)
1984.chinese: 我们再强调一次，WPPSS投资无疑有风险，而且属于很难评估的风险。如果查理和我一生中能作50次类似评估，我们预计自己的判断总体会相当令人满意。但一年之内，我们没有机会作50次，甚至连五次这样的决定都没有。即使长期结果可能不错，任何一个具体年份，我们仍有显得愚蠢透顶的风险。（所以这些句子全都写着“查理和我”，或者“我们”。）

1984.english:
Most managers have very little incentive to make the intelligent-but-with-some-chance-of-looking-like-an-idiot decision.  Their personal gain/loss ratio is all too obvious: if an unconventional decision works out well, they get a pat on the back and, if it works out poorly, they get a pink slip. (Failing conventionally is the route to go; as a group, lemmings may have a rotten image, but no individual lemming has ever received bad press.)

Our equation is different.  With 47% of Berkshire’s stock, Charlie and I don’t worry about being fired, and we receive our rewards as owners, not managers.  Thus we behave with Berkshire’s money as we would with our own.  That frequently leads us to unconventional behavior both in investments and general business management.
1984.chinese:
多数经理人几乎没有动力去作那种明智、却有几分机会让自己看起来像白痴的决定。他们个人得失的比率再清楚不过：不落俗套的决定若成功，得到的是拍拍肩膀；若失败，得到的是解雇通知。（循规蹈矩地失败，才是该走的路；旅鼠作为一个群体，形象也许糟透了，可从未有哪只旅鼠单独挨过媒体的骂。）

我们的算式不同。查理和我持有伯克希尔47%的股票，不用担心被解雇；我们的回报来自所有者身份，而非经理人身份。因此，我们对待伯克希尔的钱，就像对待自己的钱。这常使我们在投资与一般经营管理上，都采取不落俗套的做法。

1984.english: We remain unconventional in the degree to which we concentrate the investments of our insurance companies, including those in WPPSS bonds.  This concentration makes sense only because our insurance business is conducted from a position of exceptional financial strength.  For almost all other insurers, a comparable degree of concentration (or anything close to it) would be totally inappropriate.  Their capital positions are not strong enough to withstand a big error, no matter how attractive an investment opportunity might appear when analyzed on the basis of probabilities.
1984.chinese: 我们保险公司投资的集中程度，包括WPPSS债券在内，仍然异乎寻常。只有因为我们的保险业务财务实力极强，这样的集中才合理。对几乎所有其他保险公司来说，同样程度的集中，甚至接近这一程度，都完全不合适。即使某项投资按概率分析显得再诱人，它们的资本状况也不足以承受一次重大失误。

1984.english: With our financial strength we can own large blocks of a few securities that we have thought hard about and bought at attractive prices. (Billy Rose described the problem of over- diversification: “If you have a harem of forty women, you never get to know any of them very well.”) Over time our policy of concentration should produce superior results, though these will be tempered by our large size.  When this policy produces a really bad year, as it must, at least you will know that our money was committed on the same basis as yours.
1984.chinese: 有了我们的财务实力，就可以大量持有少数几种经过深思熟虑、以诱人价格买入的证券。（比利·罗斯这样形容过度分散的问题：“如果后宫里有四十位女人，您就没法真正了解其中任何一位。”）随着时间推移，集中投资政策应能带来更好的结果，只是我们庞大的规模会压低这些结果。等到这种政策带来一个真正糟糕的年份——它一定会来——各位至少知道，我们自己的钱和各位的钱，是按完全相同的原则押上的。

1984.english: We made the major part of our WPPSS investment at different prices and under somewhat different factual circumstances than exist at present.  If we decide to change our position, we will not inform shareholders until long after the change has been completed. (We may be buying or selling as you read this.) The buying and selling of securities is a competitive business, and even a modest amount of added competition on either side can cost us a great deal of money.  Our WPPSS purchases illustrate this principle.  From October, 1983 through June, 1984, we attempted to buy almost all the bonds that we could of Projects 1, 2, and 3. Yet we purchased less than 3% of the bonds outstanding.  Had we faced even a few additional well-heeled investors, stimulated to buy because they knew we were, we could have ended up with a materially smaller amount of bonds, purchased at a materially higher price. (A couple of coat-tail riders easily could have cost us $5 million.) For this reason, we will not comment about our activities in securities - neither to the press, nor shareholders, nor to anyone else - unless legally required to do so.
1984.chinese: 我们的WPPSS投资，大部分是在与现在不同的价格、以及略有不同的事实条件下作出的。如果决定改变持仓，我们会等到变动完成很久之后，才告知股东。（您读到这里时，我们可能正在买，也可能正在卖。）证券买卖是一门竞争性的生意，买方或卖方哪一边，即使只多一点竞争，也可能让我们多花很多钱。WPPSS的买入正说明这一点：1983年10月至1984年6月，我们尽量买进能买到的第1、2、3号项目债券，可买到的仍不到发行在外债券的3%。要是再多几个财力雄厚的投资者，因为知道我们在买而跟进，我们最终买到的债券数量，就可能少得多，价格却高得多。（几个搭便车的，就很容易让我们多花500万美元。）因此，除非法律要求，我们不会向媒体、股东或任何其他人评论我们的证券交易活动。

1984.english: One final observation regarding our WPPSS purchases: we dislike the purchase of most long-term bonds under most circumstances and have bought very few in recent years.  That’s because bonds are as sound as a dollar - and we view the long- term outlook for dollars as dismal.  We believe substantial inflation lies ahead, although we have no idea what the average rate will turn out to be.  Furthermore, we think there is a small, but not insignificant, chance of runaway inflation.
1984.chinese: 关于WPPSS投资，最后再说一点：在多数情况下，我们并不喜欢买大多数长期债券，近年也很少买。原因在于，债券有多可靠，取决于美元有多可靠；而我们认为美元的长期前景黯淡。我们相信，未来会有显著通胀，虽然完全不知道平均通胀率会是多少。此外，我们认为存在一个虽小却不可忽视的恶性通胀概率。

1984.english: Such a possibility may seem absurd, considering the rate to which inflation has dropped.  But we believe that present fiscal policy - featuring a huge deficit - is both extremely dangerous and difficult to reverse. (So far, most politicians in both parties have followed Charlie Brown’s advice: “No problem is so big that it can’t be run away from.”) Without a reversal, high rates of inflation may be delayed (perhaps for a long time), but will not be avoided.  If high rates materialize, they bring with them the potential for a runaway upward spiral.
1984.chinese: 眼下通胀率已降到这样的水平，这种可能性听起来也许荒唐。但我们认为，当前以庞大赤字为特征的财政政策，既极其危险，又难以逆转。（到目前为止，两党多数政客都遵循着查理·布朗的忠告：“没有什么问题大到你躲不开。”）如果不逆转，高通胀或许会推迟，甚至推迟很久，但无法避免。一旦高通胀出现，就可能发展成失控的向上螺旋。

1984.english: While there is not much to choose between bonds and stocks (as a class) when annual inflation is in the 5%-10% range, runaway inflation is a different story.  In that circumstance, a diversified stock portfolio would almost surely suffer an enormous loss in real value.  But bonds already outstanding would suffer far more.  Thus, we think an all-bond portfolio carries a small but unacceptable “wipe out” risk, and we require any purchase of long-term bonds to clear a special hurdle.  Only when bond purchases appear decidedly superior to other business opportunities will we engage in them.  Those occasions are likely to be few and far between.
1984.chinese: 当年通胀率处于5%—10%时，债券与股票这两大类资产或许没有太多优劣可言；但恶性通胀则完全不同。届时，分散的股票组合，其实际价值几乎必然遭受巨大损失；不过，已经发行的债券损失会严重得多。因此，我们认为，全部持有债券的组合，存在虽小却不可接受的“全军覆没”风险；购买任何长期债券，都必须跨过一道特别的门槛。只有当买债券明显优于其他生意机会时，我们才会出手，而这样的机会大概少之又少。

1984.english:
## Dividend Policy

Dividend policy is often reported to shareholders, but seldom explained.  A company will say something like, “Our goal is to pay out 40% to 50% of earnings and to increase dividends at a rate at least equal to the rise in the CPI”.  And that’s it - no analysis will be supplied as to why that particular policy is best for the owners of the business.  Yet, allocation of capital is crucial to business and investment management.  Because it is, we believe managers and owners should think hard about the circumstances under which earnings should be retained and under which they should be distributed.
1984.chinese:
## 股息政策

公司经常向股东报告股息政策，却很少解释。例如：“我们的目标，是将利润的40%至50%作为股息派发，并使股息增速至少与消费者价格指数的涨幅相等。”然后就没有下文了——为什么这项特定政策最有利于企业所有者，并无分析。然而，资本配置对企业与投资管理都至关重要。因此，我们认为，经理人和所有者应当认真思考：什么情况下应该留存利润，什么情况下应该分配。

1984.english: The first point to understand is that all earnings are not created equal.  In many businesses particularly those that have high asset/profit ratios - inflation causes some or all of the reported earnings to become ersatz.  The ersatz portion - let’s call these earnings “restricted” - cannot, if the business is to retain its economic position, be distributed as dividends.  Were these earnings to be paid out, the business would lose ground in one or more of the following areas: its ability to maintain its unit volume of sales, its long-term competitive position, its financial strength.  No matter how conservative its payout ratio, a company that consistently distributes restricted earnings is destined for oblivion unless equity capital is otherwise infused.
1984.chinese: 首先要理解，利润并非生而平等。许多企业，尤其是资产与利润比率很高的企业，会因通胀，使部分甚至全部报表利润变得有名无实。这部分利润，我们不妨称为“受限利润”；企业若想保持原有经济地位，就不能拿它派股息。若把它分掉，企业会在以下一个或多个方面倒退：维持实物销售量的能力、长期竞争地位、财务实力。无论分红比率多么保守，一家公司若不断分配受限利润，又没有另外注入股本，迟早注定消亡。

1984.english: Restricted earnings are seldom valueless to owners, but they often must be discounted heavily.  In effect, they are conscripted by the business, no matter how poor its economic potential. (This retention-no-matter-how-unattractive-the-return situation was communicated unwittingly in a marvelously ironic way by Consolidated Edison a decade ago.  At the time, a punitive regulatory policy was a major factor causing the company’s stock to sell as low as one-fourth of book value; i.e., every time a dollar of earnings was retained for reinvestment in the business, that dollar was transformed into only 25 cents of market value. But, despite this gold-into-lead process, most earnings were reinvested in the business rather than paid to owners. Meanwhile, at construction and maintenance sites throughout New York, signs proudly proclaimed the corporate slogan, “Dig We Must”.)
1984.chinese: 受限利润对所有者很少是一文不值，但通常必须大幅打折。实际上，无论企业经济前景多差，这些利润都已被企业强行征用。（十年前，联合爱迪生公司无意间用一种绝妙的讽刺方式，说出了这种“不管回报多差都得留存”的处境。当时，严苛的监管政策，是该公司股价跌至账面价值四分之一的一个主要原因；也就是说，每留存1美元利润用于再投资，就把它变成仅25美分的市值。尽管在进行这种点金成铅的炼金术，大部分利润仍被投入企业，没有付给所有者。与此同时，纽约各处施工与维修现场的牌子，还自豪地宣告公司的口号：“我们非挖不可。”）

1984.english:
Restricted earnings need not concern us further in this dividend discussion.  Let’s turn to the much-more-valued unrestricted variety.  These earnings may, with equal feasibility, be retained or distributed.  In our opinion, management should choose whichever course makes greater sense for the owners of the business.

This principle is not universally accepted.  For a number of reasons managers like to withhold unrestricted, readily distributable earnings from shareholders - to expand the corporate empire over which the managers rule, to operate from a position of exceptional financial comfort, etc.  But we believe there is only one valid reason for retention.  Unrestricted earnings should be retained only when there is a reasonable prospect - backed preferably by historical evidence or, when appropriate, by a thoughtful analysis of the future - that for every dollar retained by the corporation, at least one dollar of market value will be created for owners.  This will happen only if the capital retained produces incremental earnings equal to, or above, those generally available to investors.
1984.chinese:
在这次股息讨论中，受限利润无须再谈。现在转向价值高得多的非受限利润。这类利润，留在公司或分给股东，在可行性上都一样。依我们看，管理层应当选择对企业所有者更有利的那条路。

这个原则并非人人接受。经理人喜欢把可以随时分配的非受限利润扣在手中，理由很多：扩大自己统治的企业帝国，让公司的财务地位格外宽裕，等等。但我们认为，留存只有一个正当理由：必须有合理的前景，表明公司每留存1美元，至少能为所有者创造1美元市值，才应留存非受限利润。这种前景最好有历史证据支持，适当时也可依据对未来的周密分析。只有留存资本带来的新增收益，达到或超过投资者通常能获得的收益水平，才可能做到这一点。

1984.english: To illustrate, let’s assume that an investor owns a risk- free 10% perpetual bond with one very unusual feature.  Each year the investor can elect either to take his 10% coupon in cash, or to reinvest the coupon in more 10% bonds with identical terms; i.e., a perpetual life and coupons offering the same cash-or- reinvest option.  If, in any given year, the prevailing interest rate on long-term, risk-free bonds is 5%, it would be foolish for the investor to take his coupon in cash since the 10% bonds he could instead choose would be worth considerably more than 100 cents on the dollar.  Under these circumstances, the investor wanting to get his hands on cash should take his coupon in additional bonds and then immediately sell them.  By doing that, he would realize more cash than if he had taken his coupon directly in cash.  Assuming all bonds were held by rational investors, no one would opt for cash in an era of 5% interest rates, not even those bondholders needing cash for living purposes.
1984.chinese: 举例来说，假设一位投资者持有一只无风险、票息率10%的永续债券，它有一个极不寻常的特点：每年，投资者可以选择领取10%的现金票息，也可以把票息再投资于条款完全相同、票息率同为10%的债券；也就是说，新债券同样永不到期，票息也同样可以选择领取现金或再投资。若某年长期无风险债券的市场利率为5%，投资者选择现金票息就很愚蠢，因为他本可选择的10%债券，每1美元面值的价值将远高于100美分。此时，即使想拿到现金，也应该选择以新增债券领取票息，然后立即卖掉。这样得到的现金，会比直接领现金票息更多。假定所有债券都由理性投资者持有，那么在5%的利率时代，没有人会选现金，就连需要现金生活的债券持有人也不会。

1984.english: If, however, interest rates were 15%, no rational investor would want his money invested for him at 10%.  Instead, the investor would choose to take his coupon in cash, even if his personal cash needs were nil.  The opposite course - reinvestment of the coupon - would give an investor additional bonds with market value far less than the cash he could have elected.  If he should want 10% bonds, he can simply take the cash received and buy them in the market, where they will be available at a large discount.
1984.chinese: 反过来，若市场利率为15%，理性投资者就不会愿意让人替自己把钱投在10%的收益率上。他会选择领取现金票息，即使自己分文现金也不需要。选择相反的做法——把票息再投资——只能得到市值远低于本可领取现金的新增债券。若他真想要10%的债券，只需拿到现金，再到市场上买，那里有大幅折价的货。

1984.english: An analysis similar to that made by our hypothetical bondholder is appropriate for owners in thinking about whether a company’s unrestricted earnings should be retained or paid out. Of course, the analysis is much more difficult and subject to error because the rate earned on reinvested earnings is not a contractual figure, as in our bond case, but rather a fluctuating figure.  Owners must guess as to what the rate will average over the intermediate future.  However, once an informed guess is made, the rest of the analysis is simple: you should wish your earnings to be reinvested if they can be expected to earn high returns, and you should wish them paid to you if low returns are the likely outcome of reinvestment.
1984.chinese: 所有者思考公司非受限利润应留存还是分配时，也适合采用与上述假想债券持有人类似的分析。当然，分析难得多，也更容易出错，因为利润再投资的回报率，不像债券例子那样是合同写死的数字，而会波动。所有者必须估计中期未来的平均回报率。不过，一旦作出有依据的估计，剩下的分析便很简单：若预期能获得高回报，就应希望利润再投资；若再投资很可能只能得到低回报，就应希望公司把利润付给自己。

1984.english:
Many corporate managers reason very much along these lines in determining whether subsidiaries should distribute earnings to their parent company.  At that level,. the managers have no trouble thinking like intelligent owners.  But payout decisions at the parent company level often are a different story.  Here managers frequently have trouble putting themselves in the shoes of their shareholder-owners.

With this schizoid approach, the CEO of a multi-divisional company will instruct Subsidiary A, whose earnings on incremental capital may be expected to average 5%, to distribute all available earnings in order that they may be invested in Subsidiary B, whose earnings on incremental capital are expected to be 15%.  The CEO’s business school oath will allow no lesser behavior.  But if his own long-term record with incremental capital is 5% - and market rates are 10% - he is likely to impose a dividend policy on shareholders of the parent company that merely follows some historical or industry-wide payout pattern. Furthermore, he will expect managers of subsidiaries to give him a full account as to why it makes sense for earnings to be retained in their operations rather than distributed to the parent-owner.  But seldom will he supply his owners with a similar analysis pertaining to the whole company.
1984.chinese:
许多公司经理人在决定子公司是否向母公司上缴利润时，思路与此非常接近。在这个层面，他们毫无困难地像明智所有者那样思考。但到了母公司自己的分红决定，往往就是另一回事了。此时，经理人常常很难站到股东所有者的立场。

带着这种人格分裂式的思路，一家多事业部公司的首席执行官，会要求新增资本预期平均回报率为5%的A子公司，把所有可用利润都交上来，好投给新增资本预期回报率为15%的B子公司。他在商学院宣过的誓，不容许他做得更差。但如果他自己运用新增资本的长期成绩为5%，市场回报率为10%，他却很可能给母公司股东定下一套只是照搬历史或行业惯例的股息政策。此外，他还会要求子公司经理人全面解释：为什么利润留在子公司，而不上缴给作为所有者的母公司，才更合理；可他很少向自己的所有者提供有关整个公司的同类分析。

1984.english: In judging whether managers should retain earnings, shareholders should not simply compare total incremental earnings in recent years to total incremental capital because that relationship may be distorted by what is going on in a core business.  During an inflationary period, companies with a core business characterized by extraordinary economics can use small amounts of incremental capital in that business at very high rates of return (as was discussed in last year’s section on Goodwill).  But, unless they are experiencing tremendous unit growth, outstanding businesses by definition generate large amounts of excess cash.  If a company sinks most of this money in other businesses that earn low returns, the company’s overall return on retained capital may nevertheless appear excellent because of the extraordinary returns being earned by the portion of earnings incrementally invested in the core business.  The situation is analogous to a Pro-Am golf event: even if all of the amateurs are hopeless duffers, the team’s best-ball score will be respectable because of the dominating skills of the professional.
1984.chinese: 判断经理人是否应留存利润时，股东不应只把近年的新增利润总额与新增资本总额相比较，因为核心业务的情况可能扭曲这层关系。通胀期间，拥有极佳经济特性的核心业务，只需少量新增资本，就能赚取很高回报（去年商誉一节已讨论过）。但除非实物业务量增长惊人，优秀企业按其特性，必然产生大量多余现金。如果公司把其中大部分投进低回报的其他业务，留存资本的整体回报仍可能显得非常好，因为增投于核心业务的那部分利润，赚取了超常回报。这就像职业选手与业余选手混合组队的高尔夫比赛：即使所有业余选手都笨得无可救药，只要按最佳球计团队成绩，职业选手压倒性的技艺，照样能让全队分数过得去。

1984.english: Many corporations that consistently show good returns both on equity and on overall incremental capital have, indeed, employed a large portion of their retained earnings on an economically unattractive, even disastrous, basis.  Their marvelous core businesses, however, whose earnings grow year after year, camouflage repeated failures in capital allocation elsewhere (usually involving high-priced acquisitions of businesses that have inherently mediocre economics).  The managers at fault periodically report on the lessons they have learned from the latest disappointment.  They then usually seek out future lessons. (Failure seems to go to their heads.)
1984.chinese: 的确，许多公司在股东权益及整体新增资本上，一直呈现良好回报，却把很大一部分留存利润用在了经济上毫无吸引力、甚至灾难性的地方。它们出色的核心业务，利润年复一年增长，掩盖了别处资本配置的一再失败——通常是高价收购经济特性本就平庸的企业。犯错的经理人不时汇报，从最近一次失望中吸取了哪些教训。然后，他们通常又去寻找下一堂课。（看来，失败也会让人冲昏头脑。）

1984.english: In such cases, shareholders would be far better off if earnings were retained only to expand the high-return business, with the balance paid in dividends or used to repurchase stock (an action that increases the owners’ interest in the exceptional business while sparing them participation in subpar businesses). Managers of high-return businesses who consistently employ much of the cash thrown off by those businesses in other ventures with low returns should be held to account for those allocation decisions, regardless of how profitable the overall enterprise is.
1984.chinese: 遇到这种情况，若公司只留下扩张高回报业务所需的利润，其余用于分红或回购，股东的处境会好得多。回购既能增加所有者在优秀企业中的权益，又能免去他们参与劣等业务的负担。高回报企业的经理人，若不断把这些企业产生的大量现金投向其他低回报项目，就应当为这些配置决定负责，无论整家公司有多赚钱。

1984.english: Nothing in this discussion is intended to argue for dividends that bounce around from quarter to quarter with each wiggle in earnings or in investment opportunities.  Shareholders of public corporations understandably prefer that dividends be consistent and predictable.  Payments, therefore, should reflect long-term expectations for both earnings and returns on incremental capital.  Since the long-term corporate outlook changes only infrequently, dividend patterns should change no more often.  But over time distributable earnings that have been withheld by managers should earn their keep.  If earnings have been unwisely retained, it is likely that managers, too, have been unwisely retained.
1984.chinese: 以上讨论，丝毫不是主张股息随着每一丝利润或投资机会的波动，在季度之间跳来跳去。上市公司股东偏好股息稳定、可预期，这是可以理解的。因此，分红应反映对长期利润及新增资本回报的预期。企业长期前景并不常变，股息模式也不该变得更勤。不过，日子一长，经理人扣留的可分配利润，总得证明自己留得值得。若利润被不明智地留住了，经理人很可能也被不明智地留住了。

1984.english:
Let’s now turn to Berkshire Hathaway and examine how these dividend principles apply to it.  Historically, Berkshire has earned well over market rates on retained earnings, thereby creating over one dollar of market value for every dollar retained.  Under such circumstances, any distribution would have been contrary to the financial interest of shareholders, large or small.

In fact, significant distributions in the early years might have been disastrous, as a review of our starting position will show you.  Charlie and I then controlled and managed three companies, Berkshire Hathaway Inc., Diversified Retailing Company, Inc., and Blue Chip Stamps (all now merged into our present operation).  Blue Chip paid only a small dividend, Berkshire and DRC paid nothing.  If, instead, the companies had paid out their entire earnings, we almost certainly would have no earnings at all now - and perhaps no capital as well.  The three companies each originally made their money from a single business: (1) textiles at Berkshire; (2) department stores at Diversified; and (3) trading stamps at Blue Chip.  These cornerstone businesses (carefully chosen, it should be noted, by your Chairman and Vice Chairman) have, respectively, (1) survived but earned almost nothing, (2) shriveled in size while incurring large losses, and (3) shrunk in sales volume to about 5% its size at the time of our entry.  (Who says “you can’t lose ‘em all”?) Only by committing available funds to much better businesses were we able to overcome these origins. (It’s been like overcoming a misspent youth.) Clearly, diversification has served us well.
1984.chinese:
现在来看伯克希尔·哈撒韦，检验这些股息原则如何适用。历史上，伯克希尔留存利润的回报远高于市场水平，因而每留存1美元，就创造了超过1美元的市值。在这种情况下，任何分配都违背股东的经济利益，无论大股东还是小股东。

事实上，早年若大量分配，可能酿成灾难；回顾起点就能明白。当时，查理和我控制并管理三家公司：伯克希尔·哈撒韦、多元零售公司和蓝筹印花公司（如今全已合并到现在的业务中）。蓝筹只付少量股息，伯克希尔与多元零售分文不付。假如当时三家公司把全部利润都分掉，如今我们几乎肯定已无利润可赚，甚至资本也可能没了。三家公司原本各靠一项业务赚钱：（1）伯克希尔的纺织；（2）多元零售的百货商店；（3）蓝筹的交易印花。这些根基业务——请注意，都是由各位的董事长与副董事长精挑细选的——后来分别：（1）活了下来，却几乎不赚钱；（2）规模萎缩，同时大量亏损；（3）销售额缩到我们入主时约5%。（谁说“你不可能场场都输”？）我们只有把可用资金投进好得多的企业，才克服了这些出身的拖累。（就像设法弥补一段虚度的青春。）显然，多元化对我们大有好处。

1984.english: We expect to continue to diversify while also supporting the growth of current operations though, as we’ve pointed out, our returns from these efforts will surely be below our historical returns.  But as long as prospective returns are above the rate required to produce a dollar of market value per dollar retained, we will continue to retain all earnings.  Should our estimate of future returns fall below that point, we will distribute all unrestricted earnings that we believe can not be effectively used.  In making that judgment, we will look at both our historical record and our prospects.  Because our year-to-year results are inherently volatile, we believe a five-year rolling average to be appropriate for judging the historical record.
1984.chinese: 我们预计会继续多元化，同时支持现有业务增长。不过，正如已指出的，这些努力的回报肯定会低于历史水平。但只要预期回报仍高于“每留存1美元创造1美元市值”所需的水平，我们就会继续留存全部利润。若对未来回报的估计低于该门槛，我们会分配所有自认为无法有效运用的非受限利润。作出这一判断时，我们会兼顾历史记录与未来前景。由于年度业绩天生波动，我们认为，用五年滚动平均数来评价历史记录较为恰当。

1984.english: Our present plan is to use our retained earnings to further build the capital of our insurance companies.  Most of our competitors are in weakened financial condition and reluctant to expand substantially.  Yet large premium-volume gains for the industry are imminent, amounting probably to well over $15 billion in 1985 versus less than $5 billion in 1983.  These circumstances could produce major amounts of profitable business for us.  Of course, this result is no sure thing, but prospects for it are far better than they have been for many years.
1984.chinese: 我们目前的计划，是用留存利润进一步充实保险公司的资本。多数竞争者财务状况转弱，不愿大幅扩张。然而，行业保费总额的大幅增长已近在眼前：1985年的增量很可能远超150亿美元，而1983年不足50亿美元。这种局面，可能给我们带来大量有利润的业务。当然，结果绝无保证，但前景已远好于过去许多年。

1984.english:
Miscellaneous

This is the spot where each year I run my small “business wanted” ad.  In 1984 John Loomis, one of our particularly knowledgeable and alert shareholders, came up with a company that met all of our tests.  We immediately pursued this idea, and only a chance complication prevented a deal.  Since our ad is pulling, we will repeat it in precisely last year’s form:

We prefer: (1) large purchases (at least $5 million of after-tax earnings), (2) demonstrated consistent earning power (future projections are of little interest to us, nor are “turn-around” situations), (3) businesses earning good returns on equity while employing little or no debt, (4) management in place (we can’t supply it), (5) simple businesses (if there’s lots of technology, we won’t understand it), (6) an offering price (we don’t want to waste our time or that of the seller by talking, even preliminarily, about a transaction when price is unknown).
1984.chinese:
## 其他事项

每年，我都在这里登一则小小的“求购企业”广告。1984年，一位尤其见多识广、反应敏锐的股东约翰·卢米斯，找到一家符合我们全部条件的公司。我们立即跟进，若非偶然出现一个复杂因素，交易本已达成。既然广告有效，我们就按去年原样再登一次：

我们偏好：

（1）大额收购（税后利润至少500万美元）；

（2）已经证明的持续盈利能力（我们对未来预测兴趣不大，对“扭亏为盈”的故事也一样）；

（3）几乎不借债或完全不借债，却能获得良好股东权益回报的企业；

（4）现成的管理层（我们提供不了）；

（5）简单的生意（若技术太多，我们就看不懂）；

（6）明确的报价（连价格都不知道，就谈交易，哪怕只是初谈，我们也不愿浪费自己和卖方的时间）。

1984.english: We will not engage in unfriendly takeovers.  We can promise complete confidentiality and a very fast answer - customarily within five minutes - as to whether we’re interested.  We prefer to buy for cash, but will consider issuance of stock when we receive as much in intrinsic business value as we give.  We invite potential sellers to check us out by contacting people with whom we have done business in the past.  For the right business - and the right people - we can provide a good home.
1984.chinese: 我们不做敌意收购。我们承诺完全保密，并非常迅速地回答是否有兴趣，通常不超过五分钟。我们偏好现金收购；但若所获企业内在价值不少于付出的价值，也会考虑发行股票。欢迎潜在卖方向过去与我们交易过的人打听我们。对合适的企业、合适的人，我们能提供一个好归宿。

1984.english:
---

A record 97.2% of all eligible shares participated in Berkshire’s 1984 shareholder-designated contributions program. Total contributions made through this program were $3,179,000, and 1,519 charities were recipients.  Our proxy material for the annual meeting will allow you to cast an advisory vote expressing your views about this program - whether you think we should continue it and, if so, at what per-share level. (You may be interested to learn that we were unable to find a precedent for an advisory vote in which management seeks the opinions of shareholders about owner-related corporate policies.  Managers who put their trust in capitalism seem in no hurry to put their trust in capitalists.)
1984.chinese:
* * *

在伯克希尔1984年股东指定捐赠计划中，参与的合资格股份比例达97.2%，创下纪录。该计划共捐出3,179,000美元，惠及1,519家慈善机构。本次股东年会的委托投票材料，会让各位投一张咨询票，表达对计划的看法：是否应继续；如果继续，每股应捐多少。（各位或许有兴趣知道：管理层就关系到所有者的公司政策，征询股东意见的这种咨询投票，我们竟找不到先例。把信任交给资本主义的经理人，似乎并不急于把信任交给资本家。）

1984.english:
We urge new shareholders to read the description of our shareholder-designated contributions program that appears on pages 60 and 61.  If you wish to participate in future programs, we strongly urge that you immediately make sure that your shares are registered in the name of the actual owner, not in “street” name or nominee name.  Shares not so registered on September 30, 1985 will be ineligible for the 1985 program.

---

Our annual meeting will be on May 21, 1985 in Omaha, and I hope that you attend.  Many annual meetings are a waste of time, both for shareholders and for management.  Sometimes that is true because management is reluctant to open up on matters of business substance.  More often a nonproductive session is the fault of shareholder participants who are more concerned about their own moment on stage than they are about the affairs of the corporation.  What should be a forum for business discussion becomes a forum for theatrics, spleen-venting and advocacy of issues. (The deal is irresistible: for the price of one share you get to tell a captive audience your ideas as to how the world should be run.) Under such circumstances, the quality of the meeting often deteriorates from year to year as the antics of those interested in themselves discourage attendance by those interested in the business.
1984.chinese:
我们请新股东阅读第60和61页对股东指定捐赠计划的说明。如想参加今后的计划，我们强烈建议，立即确认您的股票登记在实际所有者名下，而不是券商代持名义或其他名义持有人名下。1985年9月30日未按此登记的股份，无资格参加1985年计划。

* * *

我们的年会将于1985年5月21日在奥马哈举行，希望各位参加。许多公司的年会，对股东和管理层都是浪费时间。有时，是因为管理层不愿坦诚谈论实质性的经营问题；更常见的，是参会股东更关心自己登台的片刻，而不是公司事务。原本应当讨论生意的论坛，变成演戏、泄愤和宣扬各种主张的舞台。（这买卖实在诱人：花一股股票的钱，就能让一群走不开的听众，听您讲世界该如何治理。）在这种情况下，关心自己的人胡闹，关心企业的人就不愿来了，会议质量往往一年不如一年。

1984.english: Berkshire’s meetings are a different story.  The number of shareholders attending grows a bit each year and we have yet to experience a silly question or an ego-inspired commentary. Instead, we get a wide variety of thoughtful questions about the business.  Because the annual meeting is the time and place for these, Charlie and I are happy to answer them all, no matter how long it takes. (We cannot, however, respond to written or phoned questions at other times of the year; one-person-at-a time reporting is a poor use of management time in a company with 3000 shareholders.) The only business matters that are off limits at the annual meeting are those about which candor might cost our company real money.  Our activities in securities would be the main example.
1984.chinese: 伯克希尔的年会却是另一番景象。到场股东每年略有增加，至今还没有遇到过愚蠢的问题，或纯为满足自我而发表的评论。相反，我们收到的是各种经过深思熟虑的经营问题。年会正是提这些问题的时间与地点，因此无论要花多久，查理和我都乐意一一作答。（但在一年中的其他时间，我们无法回答书面或电话问题：对一家有3000名股东的公司，逐个向人汇报，不是管理时间的好用法。）年会上，只有那些坦诚作答可能让公司真金白银受损的经营事项不能谈，证券交易活动就是主要例子。

1984.english:
We always have bragged a bit on these pages about the quality of our shareholder-partners.  Come to the annual meeting and you will see why.  Out-of-towners should schedule a stop at Nebraska Furniture Mart.  If you make some purchases, you’ll save far more than enough to pay for your trip, and you’ll enjoy the experience.

Warren E. Buffett February 25, 1985                          Chairman of the Board

Subsequent Event: On March 18, a week after copy for this report went to the typographer but shortly before production, we agreed to purchase three million shares of Capital Cities Communications, Inc. at $172.50 per share.  Our purchase is contingent upon the acquisition of American Broadcasting Companies, Inc. by Capital Cities, and will close when that transaction closes.  At the earliest, that will be very late in 1985.  Our admiration for the management of Capital Cities, led by Tom Murphy and Dan Burke, has been expressed several times in previous annual reports.  Quite simply, they are tops in both ability and integrity.  We will have more to say about this investment in next year’s report.
1984.chinese:
在这些篇页中，我们总爱稍稍夸耀一下股东合伙人的素质。来参加年会，您就知道为什么了。外地来的股东，请安排去一趟内布拉斯加家具卖场。如果买点东西，省下的钱会远远超过旅费，而且过程也会让您愉快。

沃伦·E.巴菲特

董事长

1985年2月25日

期后事项：3月18日，在本报告文稿交付排字一周后、正式制作前不久，我们同意以每股172.50美元，购入大都会传播公司（Capital Cities Communications, Inc.）300万股股票。这笔购买以大都会完成收购美国广播公司为前提，并将与该交易同时交割。最早也要到1985年很晚的时候。对于汤姆·墨菲和丹·伯克领导的大都会管理层，我们已在以往年报中多次表达赞赏。简单说，无论能力还是诚信，他们都是顶尖的。明年报告中，我们会更详细地谈这笔投资。

1985.english:
BERKSHIRE HATHAWAY INC.

To the Shareholders of Berkshire Hathaway Inc.:

You may remember the wildly upbeat message of last year’s report: nothing much was in the works but our experience had been that something big popped up occasionally.  This carefully- crafted corporate strategy paid off in 1985.  Later sections of this report discuss (a) our purchase of a major position in Capital Cities/ABC, (b) our acquisition of Scott & Fetzer, (c) our entry into a large, extended term participation in the insurance business of Fireman’s Fund, and (d) our sale of our stock in General Foods.
1985.chinese:
伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司

致伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司的股东：

各位也许还记得，去年报告里那段乐观得不得了的话：手头没什么大事，但按以往经验，大事偶尔会自己冒出来。这套精心制订的公司战略，1985年果然奏效。本报告后面将谈到：（a）我们大量买入大都会／美国广播公司的股票；（b）收购斯科特与费策公司；（c）长期、大比例参与消防员基金的保险业务；（d）出售我们持有的通用食品股票。

1985.english:
Our gain in net worth during the year was $613.6 million, or 48.2%. It is fitting that the visit of Halley’s Comet coincided with this percentage gain: neither will be seen again in my lifetime.  Our gain in per-share book value over the last twenty- one years (that is, since present management took over) has been from $19.46 to $1643.71, or 23.2% compounded annually, another percentage that will not be repeated.

Two factors make anything approaching this rate of gain unachievable in the future.  One factor probably transitory - is a stock market that offers very little opportunity compared to the markets that prevailed throughout much of the 1964-1984 period.  Today we cannot find significantly-undervalued equities to purchase for our insurance company portfolios.  The current situation is 180 degrees removed from that existing about a decade ago, when the only question was which bargain to choose.
1985.chinese:
本年净资产增加6.136亿美元，增长48.2%。这个百分比与哈雷彗星来访恰好赶在一起，倒很相称：我这辈子都不会再见到它们了。过去21年，也就是现任管理层接手以来，每股账面价值从19.46美元增至1643.71美元，年复合增长率为23.2%；这又是一个不会重现的百分比。

有两个因素，使未来不可能取得接近这种水平的增幅。第一个因素可能只是暂时的：与1964—1984年大部分时期相比，如今股市提供的机会少得可怜。现在，我们找不到显著低估的股票，供保险公司投资组合买入。这与约十年前相比，已转了180度；当时唯一的问题，是挑哪一件便宜货。

1985.english: This change in the market also has negative implications for our present portfolio.  In our 1974 annual report I could say: “We consider several of our major holdings to have great potential for significantly increased values in future years.” I can’t say that now.  It’s true that our insurance companies currently hold major positions in companies with exceptional underlying economics and outstanding managements, just as they did in 1974.  But current market prices generously appraise these attributes, whereas they were ignored in 1974.  Today’s valuations mean that our insurance companies have no chance for future portfolio gains on the scale of those achieved in the past.
1985.chinese: 市场的这种变化，对现有投资组合也有不利含义。在1974年年报里，我还可以说：“我们认为，几项主要持股很有潜力，在未来几年大幅增值。”现在我不能这么说了。不错，和1974年一样，我们的保险公司如今也大量持有经济特性极佳、管理层优秀的公司。但当前市价已经充分肯定了这些优点，1974年却完全忽视它们。今天的估值，意味着保险公司未来的组合增值，不可能再达到过去的规模。

1985.english: The second negative factor, far more telling, is our size. Our equity capital is more than twenty times what it was only ten years ago.  And an iron law of business is that growth eventually dampens exceptional economics. just look at the records of high- return companies once they have amassed even $1 billion of equity capital.  None that I know of has managed subsequently, over a ten-year period, to keep on earning 20% or more on equity while reinvesting all or substantially all of its earnings.  Instead, to sustain their high returns, such companies have needed to shed a lot of capital by way of either dividends or repurchases of stock.  Their shareholders would have been far better off if all earnings could have been reinvested at the fat returns earned by these exceptional businesses.  But the companies simply couldn’t turn up enough high-return opportunities to make that possible.
1985.chinese: 第二个不利因素更有分量，就是我们的规模。股本已超过仅仅十年前的20倍。商界一条铁律是：增长终会压低原本出众的经济回报。看看那些高回报公司，在积累了哪怕10亿美元股本后的记录就知道了。据我所知，没有一家能在随后十年，把全部或几乎全部利润继续投入，同时保持20%或以上的股东权益回报率。相反，为维持高回报，它们必须通过分红或回购，把大量资本退还出去。若这些出色企业能把所有利润都按原有丰厚回报率再投资，股东当然会好得多；可公司实在找不到足够多的高回报机会。

1985.english: Their problem is our problem.  Last year I told you that we needed profits of $3.9 billion over the ten years then coming up to earn 15% annually.  The comparable figure for the ten years now ahead is $5.7 billion, a 48% increase that corresponds - as it must mathematically - to the growth in our capital base during 1985. (Here’s a little perspective: leaving aside oil companies, only about 15 U.S. businesses have managed to earn over $5.7 billion during the past ten years.)
1985.chinese: 它们的问题，也就是我们的问题。去年我告诉各位，要在随后十年取得每年15%的回报，累计利润须达到39亿美元。现在向前看的十年，相应数字已变成57亿美元，增加48%；按算术必然如此，这与1985年资本基数的增长相对应。（提供一点参照：不算石油公司，过去十年，美国累计赚到超过57亿美元的企业，也只有约15家。）

1985.english: Charlie Munger, my partner in managing Berkshire, and I are reasonably optimistic about Berkshire’s ability to earn returns superior to those earned by corporate America generally, and you will benefit from the company’s retention of all earnings as long as those returns are forthcoming.  We have several things going for us: (1) we don’t have to worry about quarterly or annual figures but, instead, can focus on whatever actions will maximize long-term value; (2) we can expand the business into any areas that make sense - our scope is not circumscribed by history, structure, or concept; and (3) we love our work.  All of these help.  Even so, we will also need a full measure of good fortune to average our hoped-for 15% - far more good fortune than was required for our past 23.2%.
1985.chinese: 查理·芒格是我管理伯克希尔的搭档。对于伯克希尔能否赚取高于美国企业整体水平的回报，我们相当乐观；只要能获得这样的回报，公司留存全部利润就会使各位受益。我们有几项优势：（1）不用为季度或年度数字忧虑，可以专注于最能提高长期价值的行动；（2）凡有道理的领域，我们都能拓展，范围不受历史、组织结构或观念束缚；（3）我们热爱自己的工作。这些都有帮助。即便如此，要达到盼望中的平均15%，我们还得有十足的好运气——比过去赚23.2%时所需的运气多得多。

1985.english: We need to mention one further item in the investment equation that could affect recent purchasers of our stock. Historically, Berkshire shares have sold modestly below intrinsic business value.  With the price there, purchasers could be certain (as long as they did not experience a widening of this discount) that their personal investment experience would at least equal the financial experience of the business.  But recently the discount has disappeared, and occasionally a modest premium has prevailed.
1985.chinese: 投资这道算式里，还有一项须提及，它可能影响最近买入我们股票的人。历史上，伯克希尔股价略低于企业内在价值。按这样的价格买入，只要折价没有扩大，买家便可以确信，自己的投资结果至少与企业的财务表现相当。但最近折价已经消失，偶尔甚至出现小幅溢价。

1985.english: The elimination of the discount means that Berkshire’s market value increased even faster than business value (which, itself, grew at a pleasing pace).  That was good news for any owner holding while that move took place, but it is bad news for the new or prospective owner.  If the financial experience of new owners of Berkshire is merely to match the future financial experience of the company, any premium of market value over intrinsic business value that they pay must be maintained.
1985.chinese: 折价消失，意味着伯克希尔市值增长得比企业价值更快，而企业价值本身的增速已相当令人满意。对经历这段过程的持有人，这是好消息；对新买家或潜在买家，却是坏消息。新股东若想使自己的财务结果仅仅跟上公司未来的财务表现，他所支付的市值高于内在价值的溢价，就必须持续存在。

1985.english: Management cannot determine market prices, although it can, by its disclosures and policies, encourage rational behavior by market participants.  My own preference, as perhaps you’d guess, is for a market price that consistently approximates business value.  Given that relationship, all owners prosper precisely as the business prospers during their period of ownership.  Wild swings in market prices far above and below business value do not change the final gains for owners in aggregate; in the end, investor gains must equal business gains.  But long periods of substantial undervaluation and/or overvaluation will cause the gains of the business to be inequitably distributed among various owners, with the investment result of any given owner largely depending upon how lucky, shrewd, or foolish he happens to be.
1985.chinese: 管理层无法决定市价，尽管可以用信息披露和公司政策，鼓励市场参与者理性行事。各位大概猜得到，我个人希望市价始终接近企业价值。这样，每位所有者持有期间的财富增长，就恰好与企业的繁荣相称。市价在企业价值上下剧烈摆动，不会改变全体所有者最终所得的总收益；最终，投资者的收益必须等于企业的收益。但长时间的大幅低估或高估，会使企业收益在不同所有者之间分配得不公平，让某位所有者的投资结果，很大程度上取决于他碰巧有多幸运、多精明，或多愚蠢。

1985.english: Over the long term there has been a more consistent relationship between Berkshire’s market value and business value than has existed for any other publicly-traded equity with which I am familiar.  This is a tribute to you.  Because you have been rational, interested, and investment-oriented, the market price for Berkshire stock has almost always been sensible.  This unusual result has been achieved by a shareholder group with unusual demographics: virtually all of our shareholders are individuals, not institutions.  No other public company our size can claim the same.
1985.chinese: 长期来看，在我熟悉的所有上市股票中，伯克希尔市值与企业价值的关系最为稳定。这是各位的功劳。由于各位理性、关心企业，又以投资为本，伯克希尔股价几乎始终合理。这种不同寻常的结果，来自一个构成也不同寻常的股东群体：我们的股东几乎全是个人，而非机构。同等规模的其他上市公司，没有一家能这样说。

1985.english:
You might think that institutions, with their large staffs of highly-paid and experienced investment professionals, would be a force for stability and reason in financial markets.  They are not: stocks heavily owned and constantly monitored by institutions have often been among the most inappropriately valued.

Ben Graham told a story 40 years ago that illustrates why investment professionals behave as they do: An oil prospector, moving to his heavenly reward, was met by St. Peter with bad news.  “You’re qualified for residence”, said St. Peter, “but, as you can see, the compound reserved for oil men is packed. There’s no way to squeeze you in.” After thinking a moment, the prospector asked if he might say just four words to the present occupants.  That seemed harmless to St. Peter, so the prospector cupped his hands and yelled, “Oil discovered in hell.” Immediately the gate to the compound opened and all of the oil men marched out to head for the nether regions.  Impressed, St. Peter invited the prospector to move in and make himself comfortable.  The prospector paused.  “No,” he said, “I think I’ll go along with the rest of the boys.  There might be some truth to that rumor after all.”
1985.chinese:
您也许以为，机构拥有大批薪酬高、经验丰富的投资专业人士，会为金融市场带来稳定与理性。事实并非如此：机构大量持有、时刻紧盯的股票，往往反而是定价最失当的一批。

本·格雷厄姆40年前讲过一个故事，很能说明投资专家为何如此行事：一位石油勘探者去天堂领赏，圣彼得却带来坏消息。“您有资格入住，”圣彼得说，“可您看，给石油业人士住的院子已挤满了，实在塞不下您。”勘探者想了想，问能不能只向里面的人说四个英文单词。圣彼得觉得无妨。他便双手拢嘴，大喊：“地狱发现石油了！”院门立刻打开，石油人全体出发，奔向地府。圣彼得大为佩服，邀请他进去安居。勘探者迟疑了一下。“不了，”他说，“我想还是跟伙计们一起去吧。说不定那传闻真有几分根据呢。”

1985.english:
## Sources of Reported Earnings

The table on the next page shows the major sources of Berkshire’s reported earnings.  These numbers, along with far more detailed sub-segment numbers, are the ones that Charlie and I focus upon.  We do not find consolidated figures an aid in either managing or evaluating Berkshire and, in fact, never prepare them for internal use.

Segment information is equally essential for investors wanting to know what is going on in a multi-line business. Corporate managers always have insisted upon such information before making acquisition decisions but, until a few years ago, seldom made it available to investors faced with acquisition and disposition decisions of their own.  Instead, when owners wishing to understand the economic realities of their business asked for data, managers usually gave them a we-can’t-tell-you-what-is- going-on-because-it-would-hurt-the-company answer.  Ultimately the SEC ordered disclosure of segment data and management began supplying real answers.  The change in their behavior recalls an insight of Al Capone: “You can get much further with a kind word and a gun than you can with a kind word alone.”
1985.chinese:
## 报表利润的来源

下表列示伯克希尔报表利润的主要来源。这些数字，以及细得多的分项数字，才是查理和我关注的内容。我们认为，合并数字无助于管理或评价伯克希尔，实际上，内部使用时从不编制它们。

想了解多业务公司究竟在做什么，分部资料对投资者同样必不可少。企业经理人在作收购决定前，一向坚持索取这类资料；但直到几年前，却很少向同样必须决定买入或卖出的投资者提供。所有者想了解自家企业的经济实情，开口索取数据时，经理人通常回答：“我们不能告诉您发生了什么，因为会损害公司。”后来，美国证券交易委员会终于下令披露分部数据，管理层才开始认真回答。这种态度转变，令人想起阿尔·卡彭的一句洞见：“一句好话加一把枪，比光说好话管用得多。”

1985.english: In the table, amortization of Goodwill is not charged against the specific businesses but, for reasons outlined in the Appendix to my letter in the 1983 annual report, is aggregated as a separate item. (A compendium of the 1977-1984 letters is available upon request.) In the Business Segment Data and Management’s Discussion sections on pages 39-41 and 49-55, much additional information regarding our businesses is provided, including Goodwill and Goodwill Amortization figures for each of the segments.  I urge you to read those sections as well as Charlie Munger’s letter to Wesco shareholders, which starts on page 56.
1985.chinese: 表中商誉摊销不分摊给各个具体企业，而是汇总单列；理由已在我1983年年报股东信的附录中说明。（1977—1984年股东信合订本，可来函索取。）第39—41页的业务分部资料及第49—55页的管理层讨论，还提供了大量业务补充信息，包括各分部的商誉及商誉摊销。我请各位阅读这些部分，以及从第56页开始的查理·芒格致韦斯科股东信。

1985.english: Our 1985 results include unusually large earnings from the sale of securities.  This fact, in itself, does not mean that we had a particularly good year (though, of course, we did). Security profits in a given year bear similarities to a college graduation ceremony in which the knowledge gained over four years is recognized on a day when nothing further is learned.  We may hold a stock for a decade or more, and during that period it may grow quite consistently in both business and market value.  In the year in which we finally sell it there may be no increase in value, or there may even be a decrease.  But all growth in value since purchase will be reflected in the accounting earnings of the year of sale. (If the stock owned is in our insurance subsidiaries, however, any gain or loss in market value will be reflected in net worth annually.) Thus, reported capital gains or losses in any given year are meaningless as a measure of how well we have done in the current year.
1985.chinese: 1985年业绩中，出售证券带来的利润异常大。这一事实本身，并不意味着这一年特别好，虽然我们确实过得不错。某一年的证券利润，很像大学毕业典礼：四年学到的知识，在一个什么新东西也没学到的日子获得认可。我们可能持有一只股票十年甚至更久，在此期间，它的企业价值与市值都可能持续增长。最终出售的那一年，价值或许毫无增长，甚至下降；但自买入以来的全部增值，都会计入出售年份的会计利润。（不过，若股票由我们的保险子公司持有，其市值的每年增减都会反映在净资产中。）因此，任何单一年度列报的资本利得或损失，都不能用来衡量我们当年做得好不好。

1985.english: A large portion of the realized gain in 1985 ($338 million pre-tax out of a total of $488 million) came about through the sale of our General Foods shares.  We held most of these shares since 1980, when we had purchased them at a price far below what we felt was their per/share business value.  Year by year, the managerial efforts of Jim Ferguson and Phil Smith substantially increased General Foods’ business value and, last fall, Philip Morris made an offer for the company that reflected the increase. We thus benefited from four factors: a bargain purchase price, a business with fine underlying economics, an able management concentrating on the interests of shareholders, and a buyer willing to pay full business value.  While that last factor is the only one that produces reported earnings, we consider identification of the first three to be the key to building value for Berkshire shareholders.  In selecting common stocks, we devote our attention to attractive purchases, not to the possibility of attractive sales.
1985.chinese: 1985年已实现收益中，很大一部分来自出售通用食品股票：税前总额4.88亿美元中，有3.38亿美元来自这项出售。这批股票，我们大部分自1980年起一直持有，当时买价远低于我们认为的每股企业价值。吉姆·弗格森与菲尔·史密斯的经营努力，使通用食品的企业价值逐年大幅增长；去年秋天，菲利普莫里斯给公司的收购报价，体现了这种增长。我们因此受益于四个因素：便宜的买价、经济特性良好的企业、专心维护股东利益的能干管理层，以及愿意支付完整企业价值的买家。虽然只有最后一项会产生列报利润，我们认为，识别前三项才是为伯克希尔股东创造价值的关键。挑选普通股时，我们关注的是买得诱人，而不是有没有机会卖得诱人。

1985.english: We have again reported substantial income from special distributions, this year from Washington Post and General Foods. (The General Foods transactions obviously took place well before the Philip Morris offer.) Distributions of this kind occur when we sell a portion of our shares in a company back to it simultaneously with its purchase of shares from other shareholders.  The number of shares we sell is contractually set so as to leave our percentage ownership in the company precisely the same after the sale as before.  Such a transaction is quite properly regarded by the IRS as substantially equivalent to a dividend since we, as a shareholder, receive cash while maintaining an unchanged ownership interest.  This tax treatment benefits us because corporate taxpayers, unlike individual taxpayers, incur much lower taxes on dividend income than on income from long-term capital gains. (This difference will be widened further if the House-passed tax bill becomes law: under its provisions, capital gains realized by corporations will be taxed at the same rate as ordinary income.) However, accounting rules are unclear as to proper treatment for shareholder reporting.  To conform with last year’s treatment, we have shown these transactions as capital gains.
