1985.chinese: 今年，我们再次报告了数额可观的特别分配收入，来自《华盛顿邮报》和通用食品。（通用食品的这些交易，显然远在菲利普莫里斯提出收购之前。）这类分配是这样发生的：一家公司从其他股东手中回购股票时，我们同步把一部分持股卖回给它。出售股数由合同规定，确保交易前后我们的持股比例精确不变。我们作为股东，拿到了现金，所有权比例却未变，因此美国国税局把它看作实质等同于股息，完全恰当。这种税务处理对我们有利，因为与个人纳税人不同，公司纳税人对股息收入缴纳的税，远低于对长期资本利得缴纳的税。（若众议院已通过的税收法案成为法律，差距还会扩大：按其规定，公司实现的资本利得将与普通收入按同一税率征税。）不过，就向股东报告而言，会计准则对恰当处理并不明确。为与去年保持一致，我们把这些交易列作资本利得。

1985.english: Though we have not sought out such transactions, we have agreed to them on several occasions when managements initiated the idea.  In each case we have felt that non-selling shareholders (all of whom had an opportunity to sell at the same price we received) benefited because the companies made their repurchases at prices below intrinsic business value.  The tax advantages we receive and our wish to cooperate with managements that are increasing values for all shareholders have sometimes led us to sell - but only to the extent that our proportional share of the business was undiminished.
1985.chinese: 我们没有主动寻找这类交易，但在管理层提议时，曾几次同意。每次我们都认为，公司以低于企业内在价值的价格回购，使不出售的股东受益；他们也都有机会按与我们相同的价格出售。我们获得的税收优势，加上愿意配合那些为全体股东增值的管理层，有时会让我们选择出售；但前提始终是，我们在企业中的比例权益不减少。

1985.english: At this point we usually turn to a discussion of some of our major business units.  Before doing so, however, we should first look at a failure at one of our smaller businesses.  Our Vice Chairman, Charlie Munger, has always emphasized the study of mistakes rather than successes, both in business and other aspects of life.  He does so in the spirit of the man who said: “All I want to know is where I’m going to die so I’ll never go there.” You’ll immediately see why we make a good team: Charlie likes to study errors and I have generated ample material for him, particularly in our textile and insurance businesses.
1985.chinese: 说到这里，通常该讨论几家主要业务单位了。但在此之前，应先看一家小业务的失败。我们的副董事长查理·芒格，无论谈生意还是人生，总强调研究错误，胜过研究成功。他的精神，就像那位说过这句话的人：“我只想知道自己会死在哪里，这样我就永远不去那里。”各位马上就能明白，我们为什么搭档得这么好：查理喜欢研究错误，而我为他提供了充足材料，纺织和保险业务尤其如此。

1985.english:
## Shutdown of Textile Business

In July we decided to close our textile operation, and by yearend this unpleasant job was largely completed.  The history of this business is instructive.

When Buffett Partnership, Ltd., an investment partnership of which I was general partner, bought control of Berkshire Hathaway 21 years ago, it had an accounting net worth of $22 million, all devoted to the textile business.  The company’s intrinsic business value, however, was considerably less because the textile assets were unable to earn returns commensurate with their accounting value.  Indeed, during the previous nine years (the period in which Berkshire and Hathaway operated as a merged company) aggregate sales of $530 million had produced an aggregate loss of $10 million.  Profits had been reported from time to time but the net effect was always one step forward, two steps back.
1985.chinese:
## 关闭纺织业务

7月，我们决定关闭纺织业务；到年底，这件令人不快的工作已大致完成。这项业务的历史，颇有教育意义。

21年前，我担任普通合伙人的投资合伙企业巴菲特合伙有限公司，取得伯克希尔·哈撒韦控制权时，伯克希尔的会计净资产为2200万美元，全部投入纺织业务。但企业内在价值低得多，因为这些纺织资产无法赚取与会计价值相称的回报。事实上，在此前九年——也就是伯克希尔与哈撒韦合并经营的时期——累计销售5.30亿美元，却累计亏损1000万美元。偶尔也会报出利润，但总的结果始终是进一退二。

1985.english:
At the time we made our purchase, southern textile plants - largely non-union - were believed to have an important competitive advantage.  Most northern textile operations had closed and many people thought we would liquidate our business as well.

We felt, however, that the business would be run much better by a long-time employee whom. we immediately selected to be president, Ken Chace.  In this respect we were 100% correct: Ken and his recent successor, Garry Morrison, have been excellent managers, every bit the equal of managers at our more profitable businesses.
1985.chinese:
我们买入时，人们认为南方纺织厂具有重要竞争优势，因为它们大多没有工会。北方多数纺织企业已经关闭，许多人以为我们也会清算。

不过，我们觉得，一位长期任职的员工能把企业经营得好得多，于是立即选他担任总裁，他就是肯·蔡斯。这一点，我们百分之百正确：肯与最近接任的加里·莫里森，都是出色经理人，丝毫不逊于我们那些利润更高企业的经理人。

1985.english:
In early 1967 cash generated by the textile operation was used to fund our entry into insurance via the purchase of National Indemnity Company.  Some of the money came from earnings and some from reduced investment in textile inventories, receivables, and fixed assets.  This pullback proved wise: although much improved by Ken’s management, the textile business never became a good earner, not even in cyclical upturns.

Further diversification for Berkshire followed, and gradually the textile operation’s depressing effect on our overall return diminished as the business became a progressively smaller portion of the corporation.  We remained in the business for reasons that I stated in the 1978 annual report (and summarized at other times also): “(1) our textile businesses are very important employers in their communities, (2) management has been straightforward in reporting on problems and energetic in attacking them, (3) labor has been cooperative and understanding in facing our common problems, and (4) the business should average modest cash returns relative to investment.” I further said, “As long as these conditions prevail - and we expect that they will - we intend to continue to support our textile business despite more attractive alternative uses for capital.”
1985.chinese:
1967年初，我们用纺织业务产生的现金，收购国民赔偿公司，进入保险业。一部分钱来自利润，一部分来自减少在纺织存货、应收账款和固定资产上的投入。事实证明，这种收缩是明智的：尽管肯的管理让纺织业务大为改善，它始终没能成为善于赚钱的生意，连行业景气上行时也不例外。

随后伯克希尔继续多元化，纺织业务占公司的比例逐步缩小，对整体回报的拖累也渐渐减轻。我们仍然维持经营，理由已在1978年年报中说明，其他时候也作过概述：“（1）我们的纺织企业是当地社区非常重要的雇主；（2）管理层坦率报告问题，积极解决问题；（3）员工面对共同困难时，合作而体谅；（4）相对于投资，这项业务平均应能产生 不高但为正的现金回报。”我还说：“只要这些条件继续存在——我们预期会如此——即使资本另有更诱人的用途，我们也打算继续支持纺织业务。”

1985.english: It turned out that I was very wrong about (4).  Though 1979 was moderately profitable, the business thereafter consumed major amounts of cash. By mid-1985 it became clear, even to me, that this condition was almost sure to continue.  Could we have found a buyer who would continue operations, I would have certainly preferred to sell the business rather than liquidate it, even if that meant somewhat lower proceeds for us.  But the economics that were finally obvious to me were also obvious to others, and interest was nil.
1985.chinese: 结果表明，我对第（4）项大错特错。虽然1979年有些利润，此后这项业务却吞掉大量现金。到1985年年中，连我都看清，这种状况几乎肯定还会持续。若能找到愿意继续经营的买家，即使收入略少，我也肯定宁愿出售，而非清算。但我终于看清的经济现实，别人也看得一清二楚，于是无人问津。

1985.english:
I won’t close down businesses of sub-normal profitability merely to add a fraction of a point to our corporate rate of return.  However, I also feel it inappropriate for even an exceptionally profitable company to fund an operation once it appears to have unending losses in prospect.  Adam Smith would disagree with my first proposition, and Karl Marx would disagree with my second; the middle ground is the only position that leaves me comfortable.

I should reemphasize that Ken and Garry have been resourceful, energetic and imaginative in attempting to make our textile operation a success.  Trying to achieve sustainable profitability, they reworked product lines, machinery configurations and distribution arrangements.  We also made a major acquisition, Waumbec Mills, with the expectation of important synergy (a term widely used in business to explain an acquisition that otherwise makes no sense).  But in the end nothing worked and I should be faulted for not quitting sooner. A recent Business Week article stated that 250 textile mills have closed since 1980.  Their owners were not privy to any information that was unknown to me; they simply processed it more objectively.  I ignored Comte’s advice - “the intellect should be the servant of the heart, but not its slave” - and believed what I preferred to believe.
1985.chinese:
我不会仅仅为了让公司整体回报率提高零点几个百分点，就关闭盈利低于正常水平的企业。不过，一旦某项业务看来会无休无止地亏损，我也认为，即使一家格外赚钱的公司，仍不该继续供养它。亚当·斯密会反对我的第一句话，卡尔·马克思会反对第二句；只有中间这块地带，才让我待得安心。

我要再次强调，肯和加里为了把纺织业务办成功，足智多谋、精力充沛，也富于想象。他们重整产品线、机器配置与分销安排，力求获得持续盈利。我们还作过一次大收购，买下沃姆贝克纺织厂，期待重要的“协同效应”——商界广泛使用这个词，来解释一笔除此之外毫无道理的收购。但最后什么都没奏效，没有更早退出，责任在我。《商业周刊》最近一篇文章说，自1980年以来，已有250家纺织厂关闭。它们的所有者并没有掌握什么我不知道的信息，只是处理信息更客观。我无视了孔德的忠告：“理智应当是心灵的仆人，但不应是它的奴隶。”我相信了自己愿意相信的东西。

1985.english: The domestic textile industry operates in a commodity business, competing in a world market in which substantial excess capacity exists.  Much of the trouble we experienced was attributable, both directly and indirectly, to competition from foreign countries whose workers are paid a small fraction of the U.S. minimum wage.  But that in no way means that our labor force deserves any blame for our closing.  In fact, in comparison with employees of American industry generally, our workers were poorly paid, as has been the case throughout the textile business.  In contract negotiations, union leaders and members were sensitive to our disadvantageous cost position and did not push for unrealistic wage increases or unproductive work practices.  To the contrary, they tried just as hard as we did to keep us competitive.  Even during our liquidation period they performed superbly. (Ironically, we would have been better off financially if our union had behaved unreasonably some years ago; we then would have recognized the impossible future that we faced, promptly closed down, and avoided significant future losses.)
1985.chinese: 美国纺织业是一门同质化商品生意，在产能严重过剩的全球市场竞争。我们遭遇的许多困难，直接或间接来自外国竞争，那里的工人工资，仅为美国最低工资的一小部分。但这绝不意味着，我们关闭企业，员工应负任何责任。事实上，与美国工业员工整体相比，我们工人工资偏低，整个纺织业也一向如此。合同谈判中，工会领袖和会员体谅我们的成本劣势，没有提出不切实际的加薪要求，也没有坚持妨碍生产率的工作惯例。相反，他们与我们同样努力，力求保持竞争力。即使清算期间，表现也极其出色。（讽刺的是，若工会早些年不讲道理，我们的财务结果反而会更好；那样，我们便会认清前路走不通，及时关门，避免后来大笔亏损。）

1985.english:
Over the years, we had the option of making large capital expenditures in the textile operation that would have allowed us to somewhat reduce variable costs.  Each proposal to do so looked like an immediate winner.  Measured by standard return-on- investment tests, in fact, these proposals usually promised greater economic benefits than would have resulted from comparable expenditures in our highly-profitable candy and newspaper businesses.

But the promised benefits from these textile investments were illusory.  Many of our competitors, both domestic and foreign, were stepping up to the same kind of expenditures and, once enough companies did so, their reduced costs became the baseline for reduced prices industrywide.  Viewed individually, each company’s capital investment decision appeared cost- effective and rational; viewed collectively, the decisions neutralized each other and were irrational (just as happens when each person watching a parade decides he can see a little better if he stands on tiptoes).  After each round of investment, all the players had more money in the game and returns remained anemic.
1985.chinese:
多年来，我们本可以在纺织业务投入巨额资本开支，把变动成本降低一些。每项提议看起来都像立竿见影的赢家。事实上，按标准投资回报测试，它们承诺的经济收益，通常比把同样资金投入我们高利润的糖果或报纸业务还好。

但这些纺织投资承诺的收益，只是幻影。国内外许多对手也在作同类投入；一旦足够多公司这么做，降低后的成本，就成为全行业降价的新基准。单独看，每家公司的资本投资决定似乎都划算、合理；合起来看，这些决定彼此抵消，成了不合理的事——就像看游行时，人人都决定踮脚，好让自己看得更清楚一点。每轮投资后，所有参与者押进去的钱更多，回报却依旧有气无力。

1985.english: Thus, we faced a miserable choice: huge capital investment would have helped to keep our textile business alive, but would have left us with terrible returns on ever-growing amounts of capital.  After the investment, moreover, the foreign competition would still have retained a major, continuing advantage in labor costs.  A refusal to invest, however, would make us increasingly non-competitive, even measured against domestic textile manufacturers.  I always thought myself in the position described by Woody Allen in one of his movies: “More than any other time in history, mankind faces a crossroads.  One path leads to despair and utter hopelessness, the other to total extinction.  Let us pray we have the wisdom to choose correctly.”
1985.chinese: 于是，我们面对一个悲惨的选择：巨额投资有助于纺织业务活下去，却会让越来越多的资本，只赚到糟糕透顶的回报；而且投资之后，外国对手仍会保有重大、持久的人工成本优势。若拒绝投资，我们又会越来越缺乏竞争力，即使只跟国内纺织厂相比也是如此。我总觉得自己处在伍迪·艾伦某部电影所描述的境地：“人类比历史上任何时候都更面临十字路口。一条路通向绝望和彻底无望，另一条通向完全灭绝。祈祷我们有智慧选对吧。”

1985.english: For an understanding of how the to-invest-or-not-to-invest dilemma plays out in a commodity business, it is instructive to look at Burlington Industries, by far the largest U.S. textile company both 21 years ago and now.  In 1964 Burlington had sales of $1.2 billion against our $50 million.  It had strengths in both distribution and production that we could never hope to match and also, of course, had an earnings record far superior to ours.  Its stock sold at 60 at the end of 1964; ours was 13.
1985.chinese: 想理解同质化商品生意中“投还是不投”的困境，不妨看伯灵顿工业公司。无论21年前还是现在，它都是遥遥领先的美国最大纺织公司。1964年，伯灵顿销售额12亿美元，我们只有5000万美元。它在分销和生产方面的优势，我们望尘莫及；当然，盈利记录也远胜于我们。1964年底，它的股价为60美元，我们为13美元。

1985.english: Burlington made a decision to stick to the textile business, and in 1985 had sales of about $2.8 billion.  During the 1964-85 period, the company made capital expenditures of about $3 billion, far more than any other U.S. textile company and more than $200-per-share on that $60 stock.  A very large part of the expenditures, I am sure, was devoted to cost improvement and expansion.  Given Burlington’s basic commitment to stay in textiles, I would also surmise that the company’s capital decisions were quite rational.
1985.chinese: 伯灵顿决定坚守纺织，1985年销售额约28亿美元。在1964—1985年间，它投入约30亿美元资本开支，远超任何其他美国纺织公司；对应当年60美元的股票，每股投入超过200美元。我相信，很大一部分用于降低成本和扩张。既然伯灵顿已决定留在纺织业，我也推想，其资本配置决定相当合理。

1985.english: Nevertheless, Burlington has lost sales volume in real dollars and has far lower returns on sales and equity now than 20 years ago.  Split 2-for-1 in 1965, the stock now sells at 34 -- on an adjusted basis, just a little over its $60 price in 1964. Meanwhile, the CPI has more than tripled.  Therefore, each share commands about one-third the purchasing power it did at the end of 1964.  Regular dividends have been paid but they, too, have shrunk significantly in purchasing power.
1985.chinese: 尽管如此，按不变美元计，伯灵顿的销售额已下降，如今销售利润率和股东权益回报率也远低于20年前。股票1965年每1股拆为2股，目前售价34美元；折算到同一口径，只略高于1964年的60美元。与此同时，消费者价格指数已涨至原来的三倍多。因此，每股股票如今的购买力，只有1964年底的约三分之一。公司一直定期分红，但股息的购买力也已大幅缩水。

1985.english:
This devastating outcome for the shareholders indicates what can happen when much brain power and energy are applied to a faulty premise.  The situation is suggestive of Samuel Johnson’s horse: “A horse that can count to ten is a remarkable horse - not a remarkable mathematician.” Likewise, a textile company that allocates capital brilliantly within its industry is a remarkable textile company - but not a remarkable business.

My conclusion from my own experiences and from much observation of other businesses is that a good managerial record (measured by economic returns) is far more a function of what business boat you get into than it is of how effectively you row (though intelligence and effort help considerably, of course, in any business, good or bad).  Some years ago I wrote: “When a management with a reputation for brilliance tackles a business with a reputation for poor fundamental economics, it is the reputation of the business that remains intact.” Nothing has since changed my point of view on that matter.  Should you find yourself in a chronically-leaking boat, energy devoted to changing vessels is likely to be more productive than energy devoted to patching leaks.
1985.chinese:
股东这种灾难性的结局，说明把大量才智与精力用在错误前提上，会发生什么。这令人想起塞缪尔·约翰逊说的那匹马：“一匹能数到十的马，是一匹了不起的马，却不是一位了不起的数学家。”同样，在本行业内极善于配置资本的纺织公司，是一家了不起的纺织公司，却不是一家了不起的企业。

依据自身经验及对其他企业的大量观察，我的结论是：良好的管理记录——以经济回报衡量——主要取决于您登上哪条生意之船，而非划得多么卖力。当然，无论好生意坏生意，才智与努力都有相当帮助。几年前我写过：“一群以精明著称的管理者，接手一家以经济特性糟糕著称的企业，最终原封不动留下来的，往往是企业的名声。”此后，没有什么改变我对这件事的看法。若您发现自己坐在一条长期漏水的船上，把精力用来换船，可能比拿来补漏更有成效。

1985.english:
---

There is an investment postscript in our textile saga.  Some investors weight book value heavily in their stock-buying decisions (as I, in my early years, did myself).  And some economists and academicians believe replacement values are of considerable importance in calculating an appropriate price level for the stock market as a whole.  Those of both persuasions would have received an education at the auction we held in early 1986 to dispose of our textile machinery.
1985.chinese:
* * *

我们的纺织故事，还有一段投资后记。有些投资者买股票时，非常看重账面价值，我早年也是如此。有些经济学家与学者，则认为评估整个股市的合理价格水平时，重置价值相当重要。这两派人若参加我们1986年初出售纺织机器的拍卖，大概都能上一课。

1985.english: The equipment sold (including some disposed of in the few months prior to the auction) took up about 750,000 square feet of factory space in New Bedford and was eminently usable.  It originally cost us about $13 million, including $2 million spent in 1980-84, and had a current book value of $866,000 (after accelerated depreciation).  Though no sane management would have made the investment, the equipment could have been replaced new for perhaps $30-$50 million.
1985.chinese: 售出的设备，包括拍卖前几个月卖掉的一些，占据新贝德福德厂房约750,000平方英尺，而且完全可用。它们原始成本约1300万美元，其中200万美元花于1980—1984年；按加速折旧后，目前账面价值为866,000美元。虽然没有头脑清醒的管理层会作这种投资，但若全买新设备替换，或许要花3000万至5000万美元。

1985.english:
Gross proceeds from our sale of this equipment came to $163,122.  Allowing for necessary pre- and post-sale costs, our net was less than zero.  Relatively modern looms that we bought for $5,000 apiece in 1981 found no takers at $50.  We finally sold them for scrap at $26 each, a sum less than removal costs.

Ponder this: the economic goodwill attributable to two paper routes in Buffalo - or a single See’s candy store - considerably exceeds the proceeds we received from this massive collection of tangible assets that not too many years ago, under different competitive conditions, was able to employ over 1,000 people.
1985.chinese:
出售这些设备的总收入为163,122美元。扣除出售前后必要费用，我们的净所得还不到零。1981年以每台5000美元买入、还算现代的织机，开价50美元也无人要，最后只能按废铁每台26美元卖掉，还不够付搬运费。

想想看：布法罗两条送报线路，或一家喜诗糖果店所具有的经济商誉，就远远超过我们卖掉这一大堆有形资产的所得。而就在不太多年前，竞争环境不同时，这些资产还能让超过1000人就业。

1985.english:
Three Very Good Businesses (and a Few Thoughts About Incentive Compensation)

When I was 12, I lived with my grandfather for about four months.  A grocer by trade, he was also working on a book and each night he dictated a few pages to me.  The title - brace yourself - was “How to Run a Grocery Store and a Few Things I Have Learned About Fishing”.  My grandfather was sure that interest in these two subjects was universal and that the world awaited his views.  You may conclude from this section’s title and contents that I was overexposed to Grandpa’s literary style (and personality).
1985.chinese:
## 三家好企业，以及关于激励薪酬的几点想法

12岁时，我在祖父家住过约四个月。他以开杂货店为业，同时也在写一本书，每晚口述几页，让我记录。书名——请做好心理准备——叫《如何经营杂货店，以及我学到的几件钓鱼心得》。祖父确信，人人都对这两个主题感兴趣，全世界正等着聆听他的高见。从本节的标题和内容，各位或许会断定，祖父的文风与性格，对我的熏陶实在过了头。

1985.english: I am merging the discussion of Nebraska Furniture Mart, See’s Candy Shops, and Buffalo Evening News here because the economic strengths, weaknesses, and prospects of these businesses have changed little since I reported to you a year ago.  The shortness of this discussion, however, is in no way meant to minimize the importance of these businesses to us: in 1985 they earned an aggregate of $72 million pre-tax.  Fifteen years ago, before we had acquired any of them, their aggregate earnings were about $8 million pre-tax.
1985.chinese: 我把内布拉斯加家具卖场、喜诗糖果店及《布法罗晚报》放在一起讨论，因为自一年前报告以来，它们经济上的优势、弱点与前景，几乎没有变化。不过，篇幅短绝非表示它们不重要：1985年，三者税前利润合计7200万美元。15年前、我们尚未收购其中任何一家时，它们的税前利润合计约800万美元。

1985.english:
While an increase in earnings from $8 million to $72 million sounds terrific - and usually is - you should not automatically assume that to be the case.  You must first make sure that earnings were not severely depressed in the base year.  If they were instead substantial in relation to capital employed, an even more important point must be examined: how much additional capital was required to produce the additional earnings?

In both respects, our group of three scores well.  First, earnings 15 years ago were excellent compared to capital then employed in the businesses.  Second, although annual earnings are now $64 million greater, the businesses require only about $40 million more in invested capital to operate than was the case then.
1985.chinese:
利润从800万美元增至7200万美元，听起来非常出色，通常也确实如此；但别想当然。首先要确认，基期利润并非低迷得异常。如果当时利润相对所用资本已相当可观，就要检查更重要的一点：为了产生新增利润，究竟需要追加多少资本？

这两项，我们这三家企业都得分不错。第一，15年前的利润，相对当时所用资本已非常好。第二，虽然如今每年利润增加了6400万美元，经营所需的投入资本，却只比当年多约4000万美元。

1985.english: The dramatic growth in earning power of these three businesses, accompanied by their need for only minor amounts of capital, illustrates very well the power of economic goodwill during an inflationary period (a phenomenon explained in detail in the 1983 annual report).  The financial characteristics of these businesses have allowed us to use a very large portion of the earnings they generate elsewhere.  Corporate America, however, has had a different experience: in order to increase earnings significantly, most companies have needed to increase capital significantly also.  The average American business has required about $5 of additional capital to generate an additional $1 of annual pre-tax earnings.  That business, therefore, would have required over $300 million in additional capital from its owners in order to achieve an earnings performance equal to our group of three.
1985.chinese: 这三家企业盈利能力大幅增长，却只需少量新增资本，很好地说明了经济商誉在通胀时期的威力；1983年年报对此已有详解。它们的财务特性，使我们能够把所赚利润的很大一部分用在别处。美国企业整体的经历却不同：多数企业要大幅增利，也必须大幅增加资本。美国一般企业，每增加1美元年度税前利润，需要追加约5美元资本。因此，要取得与我们这组三家相同的利润增长，这样的企业必须从所有者那里追加超过3亿美元资本。

1985.english: When returns on capital are ordinary, an earn-more-by- putting-up-more record is no great managerial achievement.  You can get the same result personally while operating from your rocking chair. just quadruple the capital you commit to a savings account and you will quadruple your earnings.  You would hardly expect hosannas for that particular accomplishment.  Yet, retirement announcements regularly sing the praises of CEOs who have, say, quadrupled earnings of their widget company during their reign - with no one examining whether this gain was attributable simply to many years of retained earnings and the workings of compound interest.
1985.chinese: 资本回报率平常时，“多投钱、多赚钱”的记录，算不上多大的管理功绩。您坐在摇椅里，也能自己办到：只要把储蓄账户的本金变成四倍，利息收入也会变成四倍。您大概不会指望有人为这项成就高唱赞歌。然而，首席执行官退休公告里，却经常歌颂他任内让某家小器件公司利润翻至四倍，而无人检查，增长是否仅仅来自多年留存利润与复利的作用。

1985.english: If the widget company consistently earned a superior return on capital throughout the period, or if capital employed only doubled during the CEO’s reign, the praise for him may be well deserved.  But if return on capital was lackluster and capital employed increased in pace with earnings, applause should be withheld.  A savings account in which interest was reinvested would achieve the same year-by-year increase in earnings - and, at only 8% interest, would quadruple its annual earnings in 18 years.
1985.chinese: 如果这家小器件公司在整个时期始终赚取出色的资本回报，或首席执行官任内资本只增加一倍，那么赞美也许当之无愧。但若回报平平，所用资本与利润同步增长，就该收起掌声。一个把利息再投资的储蓄账户，每年也能实现同样的收益增长；即使利率只有8%，18年后，年收益也能达到原来的四倍。

1985.english:
The power of this simple math is often ignored by companies to the detriment of their shareholders.  Many corporate compensation plans reward managers handsomely for earnings increases produced solely, or in large part, by retained earnings - i.e., earnings withheld from owners.  For example, ten-year, fixed-price stock options are granted routinely, often by companies whose dividends are only a small percentage of earnings.

An example will illustrate the inequities possible under such circumstances.  Let’s suppose that you had a $100,000 savings account earning 8% interest and “managed” by a trustee who could decide each year what portion of the interest you were to be paid in cash.  Interest not paid out would be “retained earnings” added to the savings account to compound.  And let’s suppose that your trustee, in his superior wisdom, set the “pay- out ratio” at one-quarter of the annual earnings.
1985.chinese:
企业经常忽视这套简单算术的威力，结果损害股东。许多公司薪酬计划，对完全或主要由留存利润——也就是扣住不交给所有者的钱——带来的利润增长，给予经理人丰厚奖励。例如，十年期、固定行权价的股票期权，授予起来稀松平常，而授予它们的公司，往往只把利润的一小部分拿去分红。

举个例子，就能看出这种安排可能多么不公平。假设您有一个100,000美元、年利率8%的储蓄账户，由一位受托人“管理”；他每年决定把多少利息以现金付给您。未付出的利息，就是“留存利润”，加入账户继续复利。再假定，受托人凭着过人的智慧，把“分红比率”定为年度收益的四分之一。

1985.english: Under these assumptions, your account would be worth $179,084 at the end of ten years.  Additionally, your annual earnings would have increased about 70% from $8,000 to $13,515 under this inspired management.  And, finally, your “dividends” would have increased commensurately, rising regularly from $2,000 in the first year to $3,378 in the tenth year.  Each year, when your manager’s public relations firm prepared his annual report to you, all of the charts would have had lines marching skyward.
1985.chinese: 在这些假设下，十年末，账户价值会达到179,084美元。此外，在这种英明管理下，您的年收益会增加约70%，从8000美元升至13,515美元。最后，“股息”也相应增长，年年上升，从第一年的2000美元，增至第十年的3378美元。每年，经理人的公关公司替他写给您的年报时，所有图表里的线都会一路冲向天空。

1985.english: Now, just for fun, let’s push our scenario one notch further and give your trustee-manager a ten-year fixed-price option on part of your “business” (i.e., your savings account) based on its fair value in the first year.  With such an option, your manager would reap a substantial profit at your expense - just from having held on to most of your earnings.  If he were both Machiavellian and a bit of a mathematician, your manager might also have cut the pay-out ratio once he was firmly entrenched.
1985.chinese: 现在，纯粹为了好玩，把情境再推进一步：按第一年的公允价值，给这位受托经理人一份十年期固定价期权，允许他买入您这门“生意”——也就是储蓄账户——的一部分。有了期权，他仅仅扣住您大部分收益，就能牺牲您的利益，获得丰厚利润。若他既精通权术，又懂一点数学，等到地位稳固，还可能把分红比率进一步调低。

1985.english:
This scenario is not as farfetched as you might think.  Many stock options in the corporate world have worked in exactly that fashion: they have gained in value simply because management retained earnings, not because it did well with the capital in its hands.

Managers actually apply a double standard to options. Leaving aside warrants (which deliver the issuing corporation immediate and substantial compensation), I believe it is fair to say that nowhere in the business world are ten-year fixed-price options on all or a portion of a business granted to outsiders. Ten months, in fact, would be regarded as extreme.  It would be particularly unthinkable for managers to grant a long-term option on a business that was regularly adding to its capital.  Any outsider wanting to secure such an option would be required to pay fully for capital added during the option period.
1985.chinese:
这情境并不像您想的那么离谱。企业界许多股票期权，正是这样运作的：价值增加，只因为管理层留存利润，而非善于运用手中的资本。

经理人对期权，实际上采用双重标准。先不谈认股权证——它会立即为发行公司带来可观对价——我相信可以公允地说：商界没有什么地方，会把购买整家或部分企业的十年期固定价期权送给外人。事实上，十个月都算极端。若一家企业还不断增加资本，管理层给出长期期权，更是不可想象。外人想拿到这种期权，就必须为期权存续期间新增的资本足额付钱。

1985.english: The unwillingness of managers to do-unto-outsiders, however, is not matched by an unwillingness to do-unto-themselves. (Negotiating with one’s self seldom produces a barroom brawl.) Managers regularly engineer ten-year, fixed-price options for themselves and associates that, first, totally ignore the fact that retained earnings automatically build value and, second, ignore the carrying cost of capital.  As a result, these managers end up profiting much as they would have had they had an option on that savings account that was automatically building up in value.
1985.chinese: 可是，经理人不愿给予外人的待遇，并不妨碍他们给予自己。（自己与自己谈判，很少会谈到像酒吧斗殴那样打起来。）经理人经常为自己和同事设计十年期固定价期权：既完全无视留存利润会自动增加价值，也忽略资本的持有成本。结果，他们获利的方式，几乎就像持有前述自动增值储蓄账户的期权。

1985.english: Of course, stock options often go to talented, value-adding managers and sometimes deliver them rewards that are perfectly appropriate. (Indeed, managers who are really exceptional almost always get far less than they should.) But when the result is equitable, it is accidental.  Once granted, the option is blind to individual performance.  Because it is irrevocable and unconditional (so long as a manager stays in the company), the sluggard receives rewards from his options precisely as does the star.  A managerial Rip Van Winkle, ready to doze for ten years, could not wish for a better “incentive” system.
1985.chinese: 当然，股票期权经常授予有才干、能增值的经理人，有时给他们的奖励完全恰当。（事实上，真正非凡的经理人，拿到的几乎总比应得的少得多。）但如果结果公平，那只是碰巧。期权一经授出，就看不见个人表现了。只要经理人留在公司，它就不可撤回、也不附加业绩条件，懒汉得到的期权奖励与明星完全一样。一个准备昏睡十年的里普·凡·温克尔式经理人，再也想不出更好的“激励”制度。

1985.english: (I can’t resist commenting on one long-term option given an “outsider”: that granted the U.S. Government on Chrysler shares as partial consideration for the government’s guarantee of some lifesaving loans.  When these options worked out well for the government, Chrysler sought to modify the payoff, arguing that the rewards to the government were both far greater than intended and outsize in relation to its contribution to Chrysler’s recovery.  The company’s anguish over what it saw as an imbalance between payoff and performance made national news.  That anguish may well be unique: to my knowledge, no managers - anywhere - have been similarly offended by unwarranted payoffs arising from options granted to themselves or their colleagues.)
1985.chinese: （有一份授予“外人”的长期期权，我忍不住要说说：美国政府为克莱斯勒提供救命贷款担保时，获得了克莱斯勒股票期权，作为部分报酬。当期权使政府获益丰厚时，克莱斯勒却想修改回报，声称政府所得既远超原先意图，也与政府对公司复苏的贡献不相称。公司为这种它眼中的报酬与表现失衡，痛苦不已，还成了全国新闻。这样的痛苦，或许独一无二：据我所知，从没哪家哪里的经理人，会因授给自己或同事的期权产生不应得的收益，而感到同样愤愤不平。）

1985.english: Ironically, the rhetoric about options frequently describes them as desirable because they put managers and owners in the same financial boat.  In reality, the boats are far different. No owner has ever escaped the burden of capital costs, whereas a holder of a fixed-price option bears no capital costs at all.  An owner must weigh upside potential against downside risk; an option holder has no downside.  In fact, the business project in which you would wish to have an option frequently is a project in which you would reject ownership. (I’ll be happy to accept a lottery ticket as a gift - but I’ll never buy one.)
1985.chinese: 讽刺的是，关于期权的宣传，常说它能让经理人与所有者坐上同一条财务之船，所以值得提倡。实际上，两条船大不相同。所有者从未免除资本成本，固定价期权持有人却完全不承担资本成本。所有者必须权衡上行潜力与下行风险，期权持有人却没有相应的下行损失。事实上，您乐于持有期权的项目，往往恰是您拒绝真正持有的项目。（别人送彩票，我很高兴收下；但我绝不自己买。）

1985.english:
In dividend policy also, the option holders’ interests are best served by a policy that may ill serve the owner.  Think back to the savings account example.  The trustee, holding his option, would benefit from a no-dividend policy.  Conversely, the owner of the account should lean to a total payout so that he can prevent the option-holding manager from sharing in the account’s retained earnings.

Despite their shortcomings, options can be appropriate under some circumstances.  My criticism relates to their indiscriminate use and, in that connection, I would like to emphasize three points:
1985.chinese:
股息政策也一样：最有利于期权持有人的政策，可能对所有者不利。回想储蓄账户例子，持有期权的受托人，会从不分红政策中受益；相反，账户所有者应倾向把收益全拿出来，以免持有期权的经理人，分享账户的留存收益。

尽管有这些缺点，某些情况下期权仍可能合适。我批评的是不加区别地使用；对此，想强调三点：

1985.english: First, stock options are inevitably tied to the overall performance of a corporation.  Logically, therefore, they should be awarded only to those managers with overall responsibility. Managers with limited areas of responsibility should have incentives that pay off in relation to results under their control.  The .350 hitter expects, and also deserves, a big payoff for his performance - even if he plays for a cellar- dwelling team.  And the .150 hitter should get no reward - even if he plays for a pennant winner.  Only those with overall responsibility for the team should have their rewards tied to its results.
1985.chinese: 第一，股票期权必然与公司整体表现挂钩。因此，逻辑上只应授给对整体负责的经理人。责任范围有限的经理人，其激励应与自己能控制的结果挂钩。击球率0.350的打者，即使身在垫底球队，也期待、也理应得到丰厚报酬；击球率0.150的打者，即使身在夺冠球队，也不该得到奖励。只有对全队负整体责任的人，报酬才应与全队成绩挂钩。

1985.english: Second, options should be structured carefully.  Absent special factors, they should have built into them a retained- earnings or carrying-cost factor.  Equally important, they should be priced realistically.  When managers are faced with offers for their companies, they unfailingly point out how unrealistic market prices can be as an index of real value.  But why, then, should these same depressed prices be the valuations at which managers sell portions of their businesses to themselves? (They may go further: officers and directors sometimes consult the Tax Code to determine the lowest prices at which they can, in effect, sell part of the business to insiders.  While they’re at it, they often elect plans that produce the worst tax result for the company.) Except in highly unusual cases, owners are not well served by the sale of part of their business at a bargain price - whether the sale is to outsiders or to insiders.  The obvious conclusion: options should be priced at true business value.
1985.chinese: 第二，期权结构应精心设计。没有特殊因素时，应计入留存利润或资本持有成本。还同样重要的是，定价必须切合实际。公司收到收购报价时，经理人总会指出，用市价衡量真实价值多么不可靠。但同样这些低迷的价格，为什么就能成为他们把部分企业卖给自己的估值依据？（他们可能更进一步：高管与董事有时查阅税法，寻找实际上把部分企业卖给内部人所能使用的最低价格。顺手还经常选择对公司税务结果最糟的方案。）除极不寻常的情形外，低价出售部分企业，无论卖给外人还是内部人，都不利于所有者。结论很明显：期权应按真实企业价值定价。

1985.english: Third, I want to emphasize that some managers whom I admire enormously - and whose operating records are far better than mine - disagree with me regarding fixed-price options.  They have built corporate cultures that work, and fixed-price options have been a tool that helped them.  By their leadership and example, and by the use of options as incentives, these managers have taught their colleagues to think like owners.  Such a Culture is rare and when it exists should perhaps be left intact - despite inefficiencies and inequities that may infest the option program. “If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it” is preferable to “purity at any price”.
1985.chinese: 第三，我要强调，有些我极其敬佩、经营成绩远胜于我的经理人，在固定价期权上与我意见不同。他们建立了行之有效的企业文化，而固定价期权正是帮助他们的工具之一。他们通过领导、示范及期权激励，教会同事像所有者一样思考。这种文化很少见；若已存在，也许应保持原状，即使期权计划中可能充斥低效与不公。“没坏就别修”，比“不惜代价追求纯粹”更好。

1985.english: At Berkshire, however, we use an incentive@compensation system that rewards key managers for meeting targets in their own bailiwicks.  If See’s does well, that does not produce incentive compensation at the News - nor vice versa.  Neither do we look at the price of Berkshire stock when we write bonus checks.  We believe good unit performance should be rewarded whether Berkshire stock rises, falls, or stays even.  Similarly, we think average performance should earn no special rewards even if our stock should soar.  “Performance”, furthermore, is defined in different ways depending upon the underlying economics of the business: in some our managers enjoy tailwinds not of their own making, in others they fight unavoidable headwinds.
1985.chinese: 不过，伯克希尔采用的激励薪酬制度，是按关键经理人在自己职责范围内完成目标的情况给奖。喜诗做得好，不会给《晚报》带来奖金，反过来也一样。签奖金支票时，我们也不看伯克希尔股价。我们认为，业务单位表现好，就该有奖，无论伯克希尔股价上涨、下跌还是不动；同样，表现一般，即使股价飞涨，也不该有特别奖励。而且，“表现”的定义，会依企业本身的经济特性而异：有的经理人享受着并非自己造出的顺风，有的则在对抗无法避免的逆风。

1985.english: The rewards that go with this system can be large.  At our various business units, top managers sometimes receive incentive bonuses of five times their base salary, or more, and it would appear possible that one manager’s bonus could top $2 million in 1986. (I hope so.) We do not put a cap on bonuses, and the potential for rewards is not hierarchical.  The manager of a relatively small unit can earn far more than the manager of a larger unit if results indicate he should.  We believe, further, that such factors as seniority and age should not affect incentive compensation (though they sometimes influence basic compensation).  A 20-year-old who can hit .300 is as valuable to us as a 40-year-old performing as well.
1985.chinese: 这套制度下的奖励可以很大。各业务单位的最高经理人，有时拿到基本工资五倍甚至更多的激励奖金；看来，1986年某位经理人的奖金，可能突破200万美元。（我希望如此。）我们不给奖金封顶，潜在奖励也不按职位等级排队。如果结果配得上，较小单位的经理人，赚得可以远多于较大单位的经理人。我们还认为，资历与年龄不应影响激励薪酬，虽然有时会影响基本薪酬。一个击球率0.300的20岁球员，和同样表现的40岁球员，对我们一样有价值。

1985.english:
Obviously, all Berkshire managers can use their bonus money (or other funds, including borrowed money) to buy our stock in the market.  Many have done just that - and some now have large holdings.  By accepting both the risks and the carrying costs that go with outright purchases, these managers truly walk in the shoes of owners.

Now let’s get back - at long last - to our three businesses:

At Nebraska Furniture Mart our basic strength is an exceptionally low-cost operation that allows the business to regularly offer customers the best values available in home furnishings.  NFM is the largest store of its kind in the country.  Although the already-depressed farm economy worsened considerably in 1985, the store easily set a new sales record.  I also am happy to report that NFM’s Chairman, Rose Blumkin (the legendary “Mrs.  B”), continues at age 92 to set a pace at the store that none of us can keep up with.  She’s there wheeling and dealing seven days a week, and I hope that any of you who visit Omaha will go out to the Mart and see her in action.  It will inspire you, as it does me.
1985.chinese:
当然，伯克希尔所有经理人，都可以用奖金或其他资金，包括借款，到市场上买我们的股票。许多人已这么做，有些如今持仓很大。接受直接买入伴随的风险与持有成本，这些经理人才真正站到了所有者的位置。

现在，终于，让我们回到那三家企业：

内布拉斯加家具卖场的根本优势，是极低的经营成本，使它能够经常向顾客提供最划算的家居用品。它是全美同类最大的单店。虽然1985年本已低迷的农业经济又大幅恶化，卖场销售额仍轻松创下新纪录。我也很高兴地报告：卖场董事长、传奇的B夫人罗丝·布卢姆金，92岁仍保持我们谁都跟不上的工作节奏。她每周七天都在店里忙着做买卖；各位若来奥马哈，希望去卖场看看她现场的身手。您也会像我一样，深受鼓舞。

1985.english:
At See’s we continue to get store volumes that are far beyond those achieved by any competitor we know of.  Despite the unmatched consumer acceptance we enjoy, industry trends are not good, and we continue to experience slippage in poundage sales on a same-store basis.  This puts pressure on per-pound costs.  We now are willing to increase prices only modestly and, unless we can stabilize per-shop poundage, profit margins will narrow.

At the News volume gains are also difficult to achieve. Though linage increased during 1985, the gain was more than accounted for by preprints.  ROP linage (advertising printed on our own pages) declined.  Preprints are far less profitable than ROP ads, and also more vulnerable to competition.  In 1985, the News again controlled costs well and our household penetration continues to be exceptional.
1985.chinese:
喜诗的单店销量，仍远超我们所知的任何竞争者。尽管顾客认可度无人能及，行业趋势却不佳，同店销售磅数仍在下滑，给每磅成本带来压力。我们如今只愿小幅提价，除非能稳住每店销售磅数，否则利润率将收窄。

《晚报》的业务量也很难增长。1985年广告行数虽增加，预印广告的增量却比总增量还大；印在我们自有版面上的广告（ROP）行数反而下降。预印广告的盈利能力远不如ROP广告，也更容易受到竞争。1985年，《晚报》再次很好地控制了成本，家庭渗透率继续出类拔萃。

1985.english: One problem these three operations do not have is management.  At See’s we have Chuck Huggins, the man we put in charge the day we bought the business.  Selecting him remains one of our best business decisions.  At the News we have Stan Lipsey, a manager of equal caliber.  Stan has been with us 17 years, and his unusual business talents have become more evident with every additional level of responsibility he has tackled.  And, at the Mart, we have the amazing Blumkins - Mrs. B, Louie, Ron, Irv, and Steve - a three-generation miracle of management.
1985.chinese: 这三项业务，有一个问题是不存在的：管理。喜诗有查克·哈金斯，我们买下企业当天就让他负责，选他至今仍是我们最好的经营决定之一。《晚报》有同样出色的斯坦·利普西。他加入我们已有17年，每多担一层责任，非凡的经营才干便显露得更清楚。家具卖场则有令人惊叹的布卢姆金一家：B夫人、卢伊、罗恩、欧文和史蒂夫，三代共同创造的管理奇迹。

1985.english:
I consider myself extraordinarily lucky to be able to work with managers such as these.  I like them personally as much as I admire them professionally.

## Insurance Operations

Shown below is an updated version of our usual table, listing two key figures for the insurance industry:

```text
                    Yearly Change       Combined Ratio
                     in Premiums      after Policyholder
                     Written (%)          Dividends
                    -------------     ------------------
1972 ...............    10.2                  96.2
1973 ...............     8.0                  99.2
1974 ...............     6.2                 105.4
1975 ...............    11.0                 107.9
1976 ...............    21.9                 102.4
1977 ...............    19.8                  97.2
1978 ...............    12.8                  97.5
1979 ...............    10.3                 100.6
1980 ...............     6.0                 103.1
1981 ...............     3.9                 106.0
1982 ...............     4.4                 109.7
1983 ...............     4.5                 111.9
1984 (Revised) .....     9.2                 117.9
1985 (Estimated) ...    20.9                 118.0
```

## Source: Best’s Aggregates and Averages

The combined ratio represents total insurance costs (losses incurred plus expenses) compared to revenue from premiums: a ratio below 100 indicates an underwriting profit, and one above 100 indicates a loss.

The industry’s 1985 results were highly unusual.  The revenue gain was exceptional, and had insured losses grown at their normal rate of most recent years - that is, a few points above the inflation rate - a significant drop in the combined ratio would have occurred.  But losses in 1985 didn’t cooperate, as they did not in 1984.  Though inflation slowed considerably in these years, insured losses perversely accelerated, growing by 16% in 1984 and by an even more startling 17% in 1985.  The year’s growth in losses therefore exceeds the inflation rate by over 13 percentage points, a modern record.
1985.chinese:
资料来源：Best’s Aggregates and Averages。

综合成本率，是保险成本总额（已发生赔款加费用）与保费收入的比率；低于100表示承保盈利，高于100表示承保亏损。

行业1985年的结果极不寻常。收入增长出众，若保险赔款仍按近年通常的速度增长，也就是比通胀率高几个百分点，综合成本率本应显著下降。但1985年的赔款并不配合，和1984年一样。这两年通胀明显放缓，保险赔款却反常地加速，1984年增长16%，1985年更惊人，达到17%。因此，本年赔款增速超过通胀率13个多百分点，创下现代纪录。

1985.english:
Catastrophes were not the culprit in this explosion of loss cost.  True, there were an unusual number of hurricanes in 1985, but the aggregate damage caused by all catastrophes in 1984 and 1985 was about 2% of premium volume, a not unusual proportion. Nor was there any burst in the number of insured autos, houses, employers, or other kinds of “exposure units”.

A partial explanation for the surge in the loss figures is all the additions to reserves that the industry made in 1985.  As results for the year were reported, the scene resembled a revival meeting: shouting “I’ve sinned, I’ve sinned”, insurance managers rushed forward to confess they had under reserved in earlier years.  Their corrections significantly affected 1985 loss numbers.
1985.chinese:
巨灾不是赔款成本暴增的罪魁。1985年的飓风次数的确异乎寻常，但1984及1985年所有巨灾造成的合计损失，约占保费总额的2%，并不反常。承保汽车、房屋、雇主及其他“风险暴露单位”的数量，也没有突然暴增。

赔款数字激增，部分原因是行业1985年大幅补提准备金。各公司公布年度业绩时，场面像一场宗教复兴布道会：保险经理人高喊“我有罪，我有罪”，纷纷上前忏悔往年准备金提得不够。他们的修正，显著影响了1985年的赔款数字。

1985.english:
A more disturbing ingredient in the loss surge is the acceleration in “social” or “judicial” inflation.  The insurer’s ability to pay has assumed overwhelming importance with juries and judges in the assessment of both liability and damages.  More and more, “the deep pocket” is being sought and found, no matter what the policy wording, the facts, or the precedents.

This judicial inflation represents a wild card in the industry’s future, and makes forecasting difficult. Nevertheless, the short-term outlook is good.  Premium growth improved as 1985 went along (quarterly gains were an estimated 15%, 19%, 24%, and 22%) and, barring a supercatastrophe, the industry’s combined ratio should fall sharply in 1986.
1985.chinese:
更令人不安的是，“社会性”或“司法性”通胀正在加速。陪审团与法官判断责任和赔偿额时，保险公司的支付能力，已变得压倒一切。无论保单如何措辞、事实与判例如何，“财大气粗者”都越来越容易被找出来，要求付款。

司法性通胀，是行业未来的一张变数牌，使预测困难。不过，短期前景不错。1985年保费增速逐步改善，估计四个季度分别为15%、19%、24%和22%；只要没有超级巨灾，1986年行业综合成本率应当大幅下降。

1985.english:
The profit improvement, however, is likely to be of short duration.  Two economic principles will see to that.  First, commodity businesses achieve good levels of profitability only when prices are fixed in some manner or when capacity is short. Second, managers quickly add to capacity when prospects start to improve and capital is available.

In my 1982 report to you, I discussed the commodity nature of the insurance industry extensively.  The typical policyholder does not differentiate between products but concentrates instead on price.  For many decades a cartel-like procedure kept prices up, but this arrangement has disappeared for good.  The insurance product now is priced as any other commodity for which a free market exists: when capacity is tight, prices will be set remuneratively; otherwise, they will not be.
1985.chinese:
不过，利润改善很可能短暂，两条经济原则会保证这一点。第一，同质化商品行业，只有价格受到某种约束，或承保产能短缺时，才能获得良好利润。第二，一旦前景改善且资金可得，经理人就会迅速扩充产能。

1982年报告中，我已详细讨论保险业的同质化商品性质。一般投保人不区分产品，主要盯着价格。几十年来，一套类似卡特尔的机制维持着价格，但这种安排已一去不返。如今保险产品的定价，与其他存在自由市场的同质化商品相同：产能紧张时，价格能带来可观回报；否则就不能。

1985.english: Capacity currently is tight in many lines of insurance - though in this industry, unlike most, capacity is an attitudinal concept, not a physical fact.  Insurance managers can write whatever amount of business they feel comfortable writing, subject only to pressures applied by regulators and Best’s, the industry’s authoritative rating service.  The comfort level of both managers and regulators is tied to capital.  More capital means more comfort, which in turn means more capacity.  In the typical commodity business, furthermore, such as aluminum or steel, a long gestation precedes the birth of additional capacity.  In the insurance industry, capital can be secured instantly.  Thus, any capacity shortage can be eliminated in short order.
1985.chinese: 目前许多险种的承保产能紧张。不过，与多数行业不同，保险产能是态度概念，不是实物事实。只要自己觉得安心，保险经理人就能承揽相应数量的业务，约束只来自监管者及行业权威评级机构贝氏的压力。经理人与监管者的安心程度，都与资本挂钩：资本更多，心里更踏实，也就意味着更多产能。此外，铝、钢铁等典型同质化商品行业，要经过漫长孕育才能产生新产能；保险业却能瞬间筹到资本。因此，任何产能短缺，都能很快消除。

1985.english:
That’s exactly what’s going on right now.  In 1985, about 15 insurers raised well over $3 billion, piling up capital so that they can write all the business possible at the better prices now available.  The capital-raising trend has accelerated dramatically so far in 1986.

If capacity additions continue at this rate, it won’t be long before serious price-cutting appears and next a fall in profitability.  When the fall comes, it will be the fault of the capital-raisers of 1985 and 1986, not the price-cutters of 198X. (Critics should be understanding, however: as was the case in our textile example, the dynamics of capitalism cause each insurer to make decisions that for itself appear sensible, but that collectively slash profitability.)
1985.chinese:
眼下正是如此。1985年，约15家保险公司募集了远超30亿美元的资金，堆起资本，以便尽可能多地承揽如今定价较好的业务。进入1986年以来，这股融资趋势已急剧加速。

若产能继续按这种速度增加，用不了多久，就会出现严重削价，随后盈利下降。届时，该怪的是1985和1986年的融资者，而非198X年的降价者。（不过，批评者也应体谅：与我们的纺织例子一样，资本主义的动力，使每家保险公司都作出对自己似乎合理、合起来却大幅削低利润的决定。）

1985.english: In past reports, I have told you that Berkshire’s strong capital position - the best in the industry - should one day allow us to claim a distinct competitive advantage in the insurance market.  With the tightening of the market, that day arrived.  Our premium volume more than tripled last year, following a long period of stagnation.  Berkshire’s financial strength (and our record of maintaining unusual strength through thick and thin) is now a major asset for us in securing good business.
1985.chinese: 以往报告里，我告诉过各位，伯克希尔的资本实力为行业最佳，总有一天应能让我们在保险市场取得明确的竞争优势。随着市场收紧，那一天到了。在长期停滞之后，去年我们的保费总额增至原来的三倍多。伯克希尔的财务实力，以及我们无论顺逆都坚持异常雄厚实力的记录，如今已是争取好业务的重要资产。

1985.english: We correctly foresaw a flight to quality by many large buyers of insurance and reinsurance who belatedly recognized that a policy is only an IOU - and who, in 1985, could not collect on many of their IOUs.  These buyers today are attracted to Berkshire because of its strong capital position.  But, in a development we did not foresee, we also are finding buyers drawn to us because our ability to insure substantial risks sets us apart from the crowd.
1985.chinese: 我们正确预见，许多大额保险及再保险买家，会转向财务质量更高的承保人。他们迟迟才醒悟，保单只是一张欠条，而且1985年有许多欠条根本兑不出钱。如今，这些买家因伯克希尔雄厚的资本而来。但另一个变化不在预料中：我们承担巨额风险的能力，也使我们脱颖而出，吸引买家。

1985.english: To understand this point, you need a few background facts about large risks.  Traditionally, many insurers have wanted to write this kind of business.  However, their willingness to do so has been almost always based upon reinsurance arrangements that allow the insurer to keep just a small portion of the risk itself while passing on (“laying off”) most of the risk to its reinsurers.  Imagine, for example, a directors and officers (“D & O”) liability policy providing $25 million of coverage. By various “excess-of-loss” reinsurance contracts, the company issuing that policy might keep the liability for only the first $1 million of any loss that occurs.  The liability for any loss above that amount up to $24 million would be borne by the reinsurers of the issuing insurer.  In trade parlance, a company that issues large policies but retains relatively little of the risk for its own account writes a large gross line but a small net line.
1985.chinese: 要理解这一点，先须了解大型风险的一些背景。传统上，许多保险公司都想接这类业务，但几乎总以再保险安排为前提：自己只留下很小一部分风险，把大部分风险转给再保险公司。例如，一份董事及高管责任险（D & O）保单，提供2500万美元保障。通过各种超额赔款再保险合同，签发保单的公司，可能只保留任何一次损失最初100万美元的责任；超过这一金额的其余责任，最高2400万美元，由其再保险公司承担。行话说，开大额保单、却只自留少量风险的公司，是毛承保额大，净自留额小。

1985.english: In any reinsurance arrangement, a key question is how the premiums paid for the policy should be divided among the various “layers” of risk.  In our D & O policy, for example. what part of the premium received should be kept by the issuing company to compensate it fairly for taking the first $1 million of risk and how much should be passed on to the reinsurers to compensate them fairly for taking the risk between $1 million and $25 million?
1985.chinese: 任何再保险安排的关键问题，都是保单保费如何在不同风险“层”之间分配。以前述董事及高管险为例，签单公司承担最初100万美元风险，应留下多少保费才公平？再保险公司承担100万美元至2500万美元之间的风险，又应分得多少才公平？

1985.english:
One way to solve this problem might be deemed the Patrick Henry approach: “I have but one lamp by which my feet are guided, and that is the lamp of experience.” In other words, how much of the total premium would reinsurers have needed in the past to compensate them fairly for the losses they actually had to bear?

Unfortunately, the lamp of experience has always provided imperfect illumination for reinsurers because so much of their business is “long-tail”, meaning it takes many years before they know what their losses are.  Lately, however, the light has not only been dim but also grossly misleading in the images it has revealed.  That is, the courts’ tendency to grant awards that are both huge and lacking in precedent makes reinsurers’ usual extrapolations or inferences from past data a formula for disaster.  Out with Patrick Henry and in with Pogo: “The future ain’t what it used to be.”
1985.chinese:
一种解决办法，可称为帕特里克·亨利法：“指引我脚步的灯只有一盏，就是经验之灯。”换句话说，过去再保险公司需要拿到总保费的多少，才足以公平补偿它们实际承担的赔款？

不幸的是，经验之灯对再保险公司的照明，一向不够完善，因为它们大部分业务属于“长尾”，也就是要多年之后，才能知道损失到底多少。不过近来，灯光不但昏暗，照出的影像还严重误导。法院倾向作出既巨额、又缺乏先例的赔偿判决，让再保险公司惯常依据历史数据作的外推与推断，变成灾难配方。请走帕特里克·亨利，请来漫画人物波戈吧：“未来已经不是从前那个未来了。”

1985.english: The burgeoning uncertainties of the business, coupled with the entry into reinsurance of many unsophisticated participants, worked in recent years in favor of issuing companies writing a small net line: they were able to keep a far greater percentage of the premiums than the risk.  By doing so, the issuing companies sometimes made money on business that was distinctly unprofitable for the issuing and reinsuring companies combined. (This result was not necessarily by intent: issuing companies generally knew no more than reinsurers did about the ultimate costs that would be experienced at higher layers of risk.) Inequities of this sort have been particularly pronounced in lines of insurance in which much change was occurring and losses were soaring; e.g., professional malpractice, D & 0, products liability, etc.  Given these circumstances, it is not surprising that issuing companies remained enthusiastic about writing business long after premiums became woefully inadequate on a gross basis.
1985.chinese: 业务不确定性猛增，再加上许多不老练的参与者进入再保险，近年让净自留额小的签单公司占了便宜：它们留下的保费比例，远大于承担的风险比例。于是，有些业务对签单公司与再保险公司整体明明亏损，签单公司自己却能赚钱。（这不一定出于故意：对较高风险层的最终成本，签单公司通常也不比再保险公司懂得更多。）在变化大、赔款急升的险种，如专业过失、董事及高管责任、产品责任等，这种失衡尤其明显。既然如此，即使从毛额看保费早已低得可怜，签单公司仍长期热衷承揽，也就不足为奇。

1985.english: An example of just how disparate results have been for issuing companies versus their reinsurers is provided by the 1984 financials of one of the leaders in large and unusual risks.  In that year the company wrote about $6 billion of business and kept around $2 1/2 billion of the premiums, or about 40%.  It gave the remaining $3 1/2 billion to reinsurers.  On the part of the business kept, the company’s underwriting loss was less than $200 million - an excellent result in that year.  Meanwhile, the part laid off produced a loss of over $1.5 billion for the reinsurers. Thus, the issuing company wrote at a combined ratio of well under 110 while its reinsurers, participating in precisely the same policies, came in considerably over 140.  This result was not attributable to natural catastrophes; it came from run-of-the- mill insurance losses (occurring, however, in surprising frequency and size).  The issuing company’s 1985 report is not yet available, but I would predict it will show that dramatically unbalanced results continued.
1985.chinese: 大型及特殊风险领域一家领军公司的1984年财报，说明签单公司与再保险公司的结果能相差多远。当年，该公司签下约60亿美元业务，留下约25亿美元保费，约占40%，其余35亿美元交给再保险公司。自留部分的承保亏损不到2亿美元，在那一年已是极好结果；分出部分却让再保险公司亏损超过15亿美元。换言之，签单公司的综合成本率远低于110，而参与完全相同保单的再保险公司，却远高于140。这不是自然巨灾造成的，而是普通保险赔款，只不过发生频率与规模令人吃惊。该公司1985年报告尚未公布，但我预测，结果会显示这种严重失衡仍在继续。

1985.english: A few years such as this, and even slow-witted reinsurers can lose interest, particularly in explosive lines where the proper split in premium between issuer and reinsurer remains impossible to even roughly estimate.  The behavior of reinsurers finally becomes like that of Mark Twain’s cat: having once sat on a hot stove, it never did so again - but it never again sat on a cold stove, either.  Reinsurers have had so many unpleasant surprises in long-tail casualty lines that many have decided (probably correctly) to give up the game entirely, regardless of price inducements.  Consequently, there has been a dramatic pull- back of reinsurance capacity in certain important lines.
1985.chinese: 经历几年这样的结果，即使迟钝的再保险公司也会失去兴趣；尤其在那些风险爆炸性增长、签单人与再保险人连粗略估计合理保费分配都做不到的险种。再保险公司终于像马克·吐温笔下的猫：坐过一次热炉子，再也不坐——连冷炉子也不坐。长尾意外责任险给它们太多难堪的意外，许多公司已决定，不论价格多诱人，都彻底退出这场游戏；这个决定很可能正确。因此，某些重要险种的再保险产能大幅收缩。

1985.english: This development has left many issuing companies under pressure.  They can no longer commit their reinsurers, time after time, for tens of millions per policy as they so easily could do only a year or two ago, and they do not have the capital and/or appetite to take on large risks for their own account.  For many issuing companies, gross capacity has shrunk much closer to net capacity - and that is often small, indeed.
1985.chinese: 这一变化，使许多签单公司承受压力。它们不再能像一两年前那样轻松，反复让再保险公司为每份保单承担数千万美元风险；自己又没有资本或意愿来扛大风险。许多签单公司的毛承保能力，已缩到接近净自留能力，而后者往往实在很小。

1985.english: At Berkshire we have never played the lay-it-off-at-a-profit game and, until recently, that put us at a severe disadvantage in certain lines.  Now the tables are turned: we have the underwriting capability whereas others do not.  If we believe the price to be right, we are willing to write a net line larger than that of any but the largest insurers.  For instance, we are perfectly willing to risk losing $10 million of our own money on a single event, as long as we believe that the price is right and that the risk of loss is not significantly correlated with other risks we are insuring.  Very few insurers are willing to risk half that much on single events - although, just a short while ago, many were willing to lose five or ten times that amount as long as virtually all of the loss was for the account of their reinsurers.
1985.chinese: 伯克希尔从不玩“分出去还能赚一笔”的游戏，直到最近，这使我们在某些险种处于严重劣势。如今形势倒转：别人没有的承保能力，我们有。只要认为价格合适，我们愿意承担的净自留额，除最大型保险公司外，超过其他任何一家。例如，单次事件拿我们自己的1000万美元冒险，我们完全愿意，只要价格合理，且该损失风险与我们所保的其他风险，没有显著相关性。愿为单次事件拿出这一金额一半来冒险的保险公司，都很少；但就在不久前，许多公司却愿冒五倍或十倍的损失风险，只要损失几乎全由再保险公司埋单。

1985.english: In mid-1985 our largest insurance company, National Indemnity Company, broadcast its willingness to underwrite large risks by running an ad in three issues of an insurance weekly. The ad solicited policies of only large size: those with a minimum premium of $1 million.  This ad drew a remarkable 600 replies and ultimately produced premiums totaling about $50 million. (Hold the applause: it’s all long-tail business and it will be at least five years before we know whether this marketing success was also an underwriting success.) Today, our insurance subsidiaries continue to be sought out by brokers searching for large net capacity.
1985.chinese: 1985年年中，我们最大的保险公司国民赔偿，在一份保险周刊连续三期登广告，宣布愿意承保大型风险。广告只征求大单：最低保费100万美元。它竟引来600份回复，最终带来约5000万美元保费。（先别鼓掌：全是长尾业务，至少五年后，才知道营销成功是否也是承保成功。）如今，寻找大额净自留能力的经纪人，继续主动找上我们的保险子公司。

1985.english: As I have said, this period of tightness will pass; insurers and reinsurers will return to underpricing.  But for a year or two we should do well in several segments of our insurance business.  Mike Goldberg has made many important improvements in the operation (prior mismanagement by your Chairman having provided him ample opportunity to do so).  He has been particularly successful recently in hiring young managers with excellent potential.  They will have a chance to show their stuff in 1986.
1985.chinese: 正如我说过，紧张期会过去，保险与再保险公司会重新低价承保。但有一两年，我们几块保险业务应当表现不错。迈克·戈德伯格已作出许多重要改善；各位董事长先前管理不善，给他提供了充足的改善机会。他最近在招聘潜力极佳的年轻经理人上，尤其成功。1986年，他们将有机会展露身手。

1985.english: Our combined ratio has improved - from 134 in 1984 to 111 in 1985 - but continues to reflect past misdeeds.  Last year I told you of the major mistakes I had made in loss-reserving, and promised I would update you annually on loss-development figures. Naturally, I made this promise thinking my future record would be much improved.  So far this has not been the case.  Details on last year’s loss development are on pages 50-52.  They reveal significant underreserving at the end of 1984, as they did in the several years preceding.
1985.chinese: 我们的综合成本率，从1984年的134，改善到1985年的111，但仍在反映过去的错事。去年，我告诉各位自己在赔款准备金上犯的大错，并承诺每年更新损失发展数字。自然，许诺时，我以为未来记录会大有改善。到目前为止，并非如此。去年损失发展的详情见第50—52页；同此前几年一样，数字显示1984年底准备金严重不足。

1985.english: The only bright spot in this picture is that virtually all of the underreserving revealed in 1984 occurred in the reinsurance area - and there, in very large part, in a few contracts that were discontinued several years ago.  This explanation, however, recalls all too well a story told me many years ago by the then Chairman of General Reinsurance Company. He said that every year his managers told him that “except for the Florida hurricane” or “except for Midwestern tornadoes”, they would have had a terrific year.  Finally he called the group together and suggested that they form a new operation - the Except-For Insurance Company - in which they would henceforth place all of the business that they later wouldn’t want to count.
1985.chinese: 这里唯一的亮点是，1984年暴露的准备金不足，几乎全在再保险领域，而且其中很大部分，来自几年前已停止的少数合同。不过，这番解释，实在太像多年前通用再保险公司时任董事长给我讲的故事。他说，每年经理人都告诉他：“要不是佛罗里达飓风”，或“要不是中西部龙卷风”，那一年就会好极了。最后，他把大家召集起来，建议另开一家公司，叫“要不是保险公司”，今后凡是事后不愿算数的业务，统统放进去。

1985.english:
In any business, insurance or otherwise, “except for” should be excised from the lexicon.  If you are going to play the game, you must count the runs scored against you in all nine innings. Any manager who consistently says “except for” and then reports on the lessons he has learned from his mistakes may be missing the only important lesson - namely, that the real mistake is not the act, but the actor.

Inevitably, of course, business errors will occur and the wise manager will try to find the proper lessons in them.  But the trick is to learn most lessons from the experiences of others.  Managers who have learned much from personal experience in the past usually are destined to learn much from personal experience in the future.
1985.chinese:
任何生意，不论保险还是其他行业，都应把“要不是”从字典里删掉。既然上场，就必须把九局里对手拿的分全算上。若一个经理人总说“要不是”，然后汇报从错误中学到什么，可能漏掉了唯一重要的教训：真正的错误，不是所做的事，而是做事的人。

当然，经营错误不可避免，明智经理人会努力从中吸取恰当教训。但诀窍，是尽量从别人经历中学。过去从亲身经历中学过许多东西的经理人，未来通常也注定还要继续亲身学许多东西。

1985.english:
GEICO, 38%-owned by Berkshire, reported an excellent year in 1985 in premium growth and investment results, but a poor year - by its lofty standards - in underwriting.  Private passenger auto and homeowners insurance were the only important lines in the industry whose results deteriorated significantly during the year.  GEICO did not escape the trend, although its record was far better than that of virtually all its major competitors.

Jack Byrne left GEICO at mid-year to head Fireman’s Fund, leaving behind Bill Snyder as Chairman and Lou Simpson as Vice Chairman.  Jack’s performance in reviving GEICO from near- bankruptcy was truly extraordinary, and his work resulted in enormous gains for Berkshire.  We owe him a great deal for that.
1985.chinese:
伯克希尔持股38%的GEICO，1985年保费增长与投资业绩出色，但按它自己的高标准，承保却差。私人乘用车险与房主险，是当年行业中仅有的业绩显著恶化的主要险种。GEICO未能躲过趋势，尽管记录仍远好于几乎所有主要对手。

杰克·伯恩年中离开GEICO，执掌消防员基金；留下比尔·斯奈德任董事长、卢·辛普森任副董事长。杰克使GEICO从濒临破产中复苏，表现确实非凡，也让伯克希尔获得巨大利益。为此，我们欠他很大一份情。

1985.english:
We are equally indebted to Jack for an achievement that eludes most outstanding leaders: he found managers to succeed him who have talents as valuable as his own.  By his skill in identifying, attracting and developing Bill and Lou, Jack extended the benefits of his managerial stewardship well beyond his tenure.

## Fireman’s Fund Quota-Share Contract

Never one to let go of a meal ticket, we have followed Jack Byrne to Fireman’s Fund (“FFIC”) where he is Chairman and CEO of the holding company.
1985.chinese:
我们同样感谢杰克另一项连多数出色领袖都办不到的成就：他找到与自己同样有才干的接班人。凭着识别、吸引及培养比尔和卢的本领，杰克让自己经营管理的好处，延续到任期之外很久。

## 消防员基金成数再保险合同

我们向来舍不得放走一张好饭票，于是跟着杰克·伯恩去了消防员基金（FFIC），他在那里担任控股公司的董事长兼首席执行官。

1985.english: On September 1, 1985 we became a 7% participant in all of the business in force of the FFIC group, with the exception of reinsurance they write for unaffiliated companies.  Our contract runs for four years, and provides that our losses and costs will be proportionate to theirs throughout the contract period.  If there is no extension, we will thereafter have no participation in any ongoing business.  However, for a great many years in the future, we will be reimbursing FFIC for our 7% of the losses that occurred in the September 1, 1985 - August 31, 1989 period.
1985.chinese: 1985年9月1日，我们开始按7%比例，参与FFIC集团全部有效业务，但不包括它们为非关联公司承做的再保险。合同为期四年，期间我们的赔款与费用，始终按比例与其一致。如果不续约，之后我们便不再参与后续持续开展的业务；不过，未来很长很多年，我们仍要向FFIC偿付1985年9月1日至1989年8月31日期间发生赔款中的7%。

1985.english:
Under the contract FFIC remits premiums to us promptly and we reimburse FFIC promptly for expenses and losses it has paid. Thus, funds generated by our share of the business are held by us for investment.  As part of the deal, I’m available to FFIC for consultation about general investment strategy.  I’m not involved, however, in specific investment decisions of FFIC, nor is Berkshire involved in any aspect of the company’s underwriting activities.

Currently FFIC is doing about $3 billion of business, and it will probably do more as rates rise.  The company’s September 1, 1985 unearned premium reserve was $1.324 billion, and it therefore transferred 7% of this, or $92.7 million, to us at initiation of the contract.  We concurrently paid them $29.4 million representing the underwriting expenses that they had incurred on the transferred premium.  All of the FFIC business is written by National Indemnity Company, but two-sevenths of it is passed along to Wesco-Financial Insurance Company (“Wes-FIC”), a new company organized by our 80%-owned subsidiary, Wesco Financial Corporation.  Charlie Munger has some interesting comments about Wes-FIC and the reinsurance business on pages 60- 62.
1985.chinese:
按合同，FFIC及时把保费汇给我们，我们也及时补偿它已支付的费用与赔款。因此，这部分业务产生的资金，由我们持有并投资。交易还包括：FFIC可向我咨询总体投资战略。不过，我不参与它的具体投资决定，伯克希尔也不参与其任何承保活动。

FFIC目前业务量约30亿美元，随着费率上升，可能还会更多。它1985年9月1日的未到期保费准备金为13.24亿美元，因此合同开始时，向我们转来其中的7%，即9270万美元。我们同时支付2940万美元，补偿它为所转保费已发生的承保费用。FFIC这部分业务全部由国民赔偿承接，但其中七分之二再转给韦斯科金融保险公司（Wes-FIC）；后者是我们持股80%的子公司韦斯科金融新设的公司。第60—62页，查理·芒格对Wes-FIC与再保险业务，有一些有趣的评论。

1985.english:
To the Insurance Segment tables on page 41, we have added a new line, labeled Major Quota Share Contracts.  The 1985 results of the FFIC contract are reported there, though the newness of the arrangement makes these results only very rough approximations.

After the end of the year, we secured another quota-share contract, whose 1986 volume should be over $50 million.  We hope to develop more of this business, and industry conditions suggest that we could: a significant number of companies are generating more business than they themselves can prudently handle.  Our financial strength makes us an attractive partner for such companies.
1985.chinese:

年末之后，我们又取得一项成数再保险合同，1986年业务量应超过5000万美元。我们希望开展更多此类业务；行业状况表明，这有可能：相当多公司产生的业务，已超过自身审慎经营所能承受的数量。我们的财务实力，使我们成为它们眼中很有吸引力的伙伴。

1985.english:
We mentioned earlier that in the past decade the investment environment has changed from one in which great businesses were totally unappreciated to one in which they are appropriately recognized.  The Washington Post Company (“WPC”) provides an excellent example.

We bought all of our WPC holdings in mid-1973 at a price of not more than one-fourth of the then per-share business value of the enterprise.  Calculating the price/value ratio required no unusual insights.  Most security analysts, media brokers, and media executives would have estimated WPC’s intrinsic business value at $400 to $500 million just as we did.  And its $100 million stock market valuation was published daily for all to see.  Our advantage, rather, was attitude: we had learned from Ben Graham that the key to successful investing was the purchase of shares in good businesses when market prices were at a large discount from underlying business values.
1985.chinese:
前面提到，过去十年，投资环境已从优秀企业完全不被欣赏，变成它们得到适当认可。《华盛顿邮报》公司（WPC）就是极好的例子。

我们持有的WPC股票，全在1973年年中买入，价格不超过当时企业每股价值的四分之一。算出这个价格与价值之比，并不需要非凡洞察。多数证券分析师、媒体经纪人及媒体企业高管，都会像我们一样，把WPC企业内在价值估在4亿至5亿美元；而1亿美元的股市估值，每天公开，人人可见。我们的优势其实是态度：从本·格雷厄姆那里，我们学到，成功投资的关键，是在市价大幅低于企业本身价值时，买入好企业的股份。

1985.english: Most institutional investors in the early 1970s, on the other hand, regarded business value as of only minor relevance when they were deciding the prices at which they would buy or sell.  This now seems hard to believe.  However, these institutions were then under the spell of academics at prestigious business schools who were preaching a newly-fashioned theory: the stock market was totally efficient, and therefore calculations of business value - and even thought, itself - were of no importance in investment activities. (We are enormously indebted to those academics: what could be more advantageous in an intellectual contest - whether it be bridge, chess, or stock selection than to have opponents who have been taught that thinking is a waste of energy?)
1985.chinese: 相反，20世纪70年代初，大多数机构投资者在决定买卖价格时，觉得企业价值只略有关系。今天听来难以置信。但当时，这些机构被名牌商学院学者迷住了；学者们鼓吹一种时髦的新理论：股市完全有效，所以投资活动中，企业价值计算，甚至思考本身，都无关紧要。（我们实在非常感谢那些学者：在桥牌、国际象棋或选股这样的智力竞赛中，还有什么比对手受教认为思考浪费精力，更能让我们占便宜呢？）

1985.english: Through 1973 and 1974, WPC continued to do fine as a business, and intrinsic value grew.  Nevertheless, by yearend 1974 our WPC holding showed a loss of about 25%, with market value at $8 million against our cost of $10.6 million.  What we had thought ridiculously cheap a year earlier had become a good bit cheaper as the market, in its infinite wisdom, marked WPC stock down to well below 20 cents on the dollar of intrinsic value.
1985.chinese: 1973及1974年，WPC业务持续良好，内在价值增长。尽管如此，到1974年底，我们持股却账面亏损约25%，1060万美元的成本，对应市值只有800万美元。一年前觉得便宜得荒唐的东西，如今更便宜了：市场凭它无穷的智慧，把WPC每1美元内在价值的股价，压到远低于20美分。

1985.english: You know the happy outcome.  Kay Graham, CEO of WPC, had the brains and courage to repurchase large quantities of stock for the company at those bargain prices, as well as the managerial skills necessary to dramatically increase business values. Meanwhile, investors began to recognize the exceptional economics of the business and the stock price moved closer to underlying value.  Thus, we experienced a triple dip: the company’s business value soared upward, per-share business value increased considerably faster because of stock repurchases and, with a narrowing of the discount, the stock price outpaced the gain in per-share business value.
1985.chinese: 圆满结局，各位都知道。WPC首席执行官凯·格雷厄姆，既有智慧和勇气，让公司以这些便宜价格大量回购，又有经营本领，大幅提高企业价值。与此同时，投资者开始认识这门生意非凡的经济特性，股价向内在价值靠拢。于是，我们享了三重好处：企业价值大涨；由于回购，每股企业价值涨得更快；折价收窄，又让股价涨得比每股企业价值还快。

1985.english:
We hold all of the WPC shares we bought in 1973, except for those sold back to the company in 1985’s proportionate redemption.  Proceeds from the redemption plus yearend market value of our holdings total $221 million.

If we had invested our $10.6 million in any of a half-dozen media companies that were investment favorites in mid-1973, the value of our holdings at yearend would have been in the area of $40 - $60 million.  Our gain would have far exceeded the gain in the general market, an outcome reflecting the exceptional economics of the media business.  The extra $160 million or so we gained through ownership of WPC came, in very large part, from the superior nature of the managerial decisions made by Kay as compared to those made by managers of most media companies.  Her stunning business success has in large part gone unreported but among Berkshire shareholders it should not go unappreciated.
1985.chinese:
除1985年按比例赎回时卖回公司的部分，我们仍持有1973年买入的全部WPC股票。赎回所得，加上年末剩余持股市值，合计2.21亿美元。

若把1060万美元投进1973年年中备受追捧的六家媒体公司中的任何一家，年末持股价值会在4000万至6000万美元左右。收益会远超大盘，体现媒体行业非凡的经济特性。而我们持有WPC额外赚到约1.60亿美元，很大程度上来自凯的经营决定，比多数媒体公司经理人的决定更出色。她令人惊叹的经营成功，很少得到报道，但伯克希尔股东不应不懂得珍惜。

1985.english: Our Capital Cities purchase, described in the next section, required me to leave the WPC Board early in 1986.  But we intend to hold indefinitely whatever WPC stock FCC rules allow us to. We expect WPC’s business values to grow at a reasonable rate, and we know that management is both able and shareholder-oriented. However, the market now values the company at over $1.8 billion, and there is no way that the value can progress from that level at a rate anywhere close to the rate possible when the company’s valuation was only $100 million.  Because market prices have also been bid up for our other holdings, we face the same vastly- reduced potential throughout our portfolio.
1985.chinese: 下一节介绍的大都会投资，要求我在1986年初退出WPC董事会。但凡美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）规则允许的WPC股票，我们都打算无限期持有。我们预计WPC企业价值会合理增长，也知道管理层既能干、又心向股东。不过，如今市场给公司的估值超过18亿美元，价值不可能从这一水平，再以任何接近当年估值仅1亿美元时所能达到的速度增长。我们其他持股的市价也已被抬高，所以整个组合的潜在机会，都大大缩小了。

1985.english: You will notice that we had a significant holding in Beatrice Companies at yearend.  This is a short-term arbitrage holding - in effect, a parking place for money (though not a totally safe one, since deals sometimes fall through and create substantial losses).  We sometimes enter the arbitrage field when we have more money than ideas, but only to participate in announced mergers and sales.  We would be a lot happier if the funds currently employed on this short-term basis found a long- term home.  At the moment, however, prospects are bleak.
1985.chinese: 各位会注意到，年末我们持有比阿特丽斯公司一笔不小的股票。这是短期套利持仓，实际上是资金的临时停车场，不过并非绝对安全：交易有时会失败，造成重大损失。当钱比主意多时，我们偶尔做套利，但只参与已经宣布的合并与出售交易。如果目前短期运用的资金能找到长期归宿，我们会高兴得多；眼下前景却黯淡。

1985.english: At yearend our insurance subsidiaries had about $400 million in tax-exempt bonds, of which $194 million at amortized cost were issues of Washington Public Power Supply System (“WPPSS”) Projects 1, 2, and 3. 1 discussed this position fully last year, and explained why we would not disclose further purchases or sales until well after the fact (adhering to the policy we follow on stocks).  Our unrealized gain on the WPPSS bonds at yearend was $62 million, perhaps one-third arising from the upward movement of bonds generally, and the remainder from a more positive investor view toward WPPSS 1, 2, and 3s.  Annual tax- exempt income from our WPPSS issues is about $30 million.
1985.chinese: 年末，保险子公司约有4亿美元免税债券，其中按摊余成本计1.94亿美元，是华盛顿公共供电系统（WPPSS）第1、2、3号项目的债券。去年我已详谈这笔持仓，也解释了为什么只有交易完成很久以后，才会披露新增买入或卖出；这与我们的股票政策一致。年末WPPSS债券的未实现收益为6200万美元，其中或许三分之一来自债券整体上涨，其余来自投资者对第1、2、3号项目看法转好。我们这批WPPSS债券每年免税收入约3000万美元。

1985.english:
Capital Cities/ABC, Inc.

Right after yearend, Berkshire purchased 3 million shares of Capital Cities/ABC, Inc. (“Cap Cities”) at $172.50 per share, the market price of such shares at the time the commitment was made early in March, 1985.  I’ve been on record for many years about the management of Cap Cities: I think it is the best of any publicly-owned company in the country.  And Tom Murphy and Dan Burke are not only great managers, they are precisely the sort of fellows that you would want your daughter to marry.  It is a privilege to be associated with them - and also a lot of fun, as any of you who know them will understand.
1985.chinese:
## 大都会／美国广播公司（Capital Cities/ABC, Inc.）

年末刚过，伯克希尔便以每股172.50美元，买入大都会／美国广播公司300万股；这一价格是1985年3月初作出承诺时的市价。对大都会的管理层，多年来我一直公开表示：我认为他们是全国所有上市公司中最好的。汤姆·墨菲和丹·伯克不仅是杰出经理人，也正是您愿意把女儿嫁给的那种人。能与他们合作，是荣幸，也充满乐趣；认识他们的各位都会明白。

1985.english:
Our purchase of stock helped Cap Cities finance the $3.5 billion acquisition of American Broadcasting Companies.  For Cap Cities, ABC is a major undertaking whose economics are likely to be unexciting over the next few years.  This bothers us not an iota; we can be very patient. (No matter how great the talent or effort, some things just take time: you can’t produce a baby in one month by getting nine women pregnant.)

As evidence of our confidence, we have executed an unusual agreement: for an extended period Tom, as CEO (or Dan, should he be CEO) votes our stock.  This arrangement was initiated by Charlie and me, not by Tom.  We also have restricted ourselves in various ways regarding sale of our shares.  The object of these restrictions is to make sure that our block does not get sold to anyone who is a large holder (or intends to become a large holder) without the approval of management, an arrangement similar to ones we initiated some years ago at GEICO and Washington Post.
1985.chinese:
我们购买股票，帮助大都会筹措35亿美元收购美国广播公司的资金。对大都会而言，ABC是一次重大行动，未来几年经济回报可能并不起眼。我们丝毫不介意，可以很有耐心。（无论才华多大、多么努力，有些事就是需要时间：让九个女人怀孕，也不能一个月生出一个孩子。）

为表明信心，我们签了一个不寻常的协议：在相当长时期内，由作为首席执行官的汤姆，或届时若任首席执行官的丹，代我们行使投票权。安排是查理和我提议的，并非汤姆。我们还对自己出售股份作了多项限制，目的在于，未经管理层批准，不把这笔股份卖给任何大股东或打算成为大股东的人。这与几年前我们主动在GEICO及《华盛顿邮报》作的安排相似。

1985.english: Since large blocks frequently command premium prices, some might think we have injured Berkshire financially by creating such restrictions.  Our view is just the opposite.  We feel the long-term economic prospects for these businesses - and, thus, for ourselves as owners - are enhanced by the arrangements.  With them in place, the first-class managers with whom we have aligned ourselves can focus their efforts entirely upon running the businesses and maximizing long-term values for owners.  Certainly this is much better than having those managers distracted by “revolving-door capitalists” hoping to put the company “in play”. (Of course, some managers place their own interests above those of the company and its owners and deserve to be shaken up - but, in making investments, we try to steer clear of this type.)
1985.chinese: 大宗股权往往能卖出溢价，因此有人可能认为，这些限制损害了伯克希尔的财务利益。我们的看法恰恰相反。我们觉得，这些安排改善了企业的长期经济前景，也改善了我们作为所有者的前景。有了它们，与我们结盟的一流经理人，就能全心经营，为所有者争取最大长期价值。显然，这比让他们被那些想把公司推进收购角逐的“旋转门资本家”分心，要好得多。（当然，有些经理人把自己利益放在公司及所有者之上，确实该受到震动；但投资时，我们尽量绕开这种人。）

1985.english: Today, corporate instability is an inevitable consequence of widely-diffused ownership of voting stock.  At any time a major holder can surface, usually mouthing reassuring rhetoric but frequently harboring uncivil intentions.  By circumscribing our blocks of stock as we often do, we intend to promote stability where it otherwise might be lacking.  That kind of certainty, combined with a good manager and a good business, provides excellent soil for a rich financial harvest.  That’s the economic case for our arrangements.
1985.chinese: 如今，有投票权股票的所有权广泛分散，公司不稳定就是不可避免的后果。随时可能冒出一个大股东，通常嘴上说着安抚的话，心里却常打着不友善的算盘。我们经常限制自己所持大宗股票，是想在本可能缺乏稳定的地方促进稳定。这种确定性，加上优秀经理人与好生意，就是孕育丰厚财务收成的沃土。这是这些安排的经济理由。

1985.english: The human side is just as important.  We don’t want managers we like and admire - and who have welcomed a major financial commitment by us - to ever lose any sleep wondering whether surprises might occur because of our large ownership.  I have told them there will be no surprises, and these agreements put Berkshire’s signature where my mouth is.  That signature also means the managers have a corporate commitment and therefore need not worry if my personal participation in Berkshire’s affairs ends prematurely (a term I define as any age short of three digits).
1985.chinese: 人的一面也同样重要。我们喜欢、敬佩的经理人，欢迎我们投入巨资，我们不希望他们因为我们持股很大，而担心哪天会有意外，甚至睡不好觉。我告诉过他们，不会有意外；这些协议，则让伯克希尔在我说过的话上签了字。签字也意味着公司层面的承诺，因此，即使我过早结束对伯克希尔事务的亲自参与，他们也无须忧虑。所谓“过早”，我的定义是年龄还没到三位数。

1985.english:
Our Cap Cities purchase was made at a full price, reflecting the very considerable enthusiasm for both media stocks and media properties that has developed in recent years (and that, in the case of some property purchases, has approached a mania). it’s no field for bargains.  However, our Cap Cities investment allies us with an exceptional combination of properties and people - and we like the opportunity to participate in size.

Of course, some of you probably wonder why we are now buying Cap Cities at $172.50 per share given that your Chairman, in a characteristic burst of brilliance, sold Berkshire’s holdings in the same company at $43 per share in 1978-80.  Anticipating your question, I spent much of 1985 working on a snappy answer that would reconcile these acts.
1985.chinese:
我们按足价买入大都会，反映近年市场对媒体股票及媒体资产的高度热情；某些媒体资产收购，甚至接近狂热。这里不是捡便宜的地方。不过，这笔投资让我们与非凡的资产和人才组合结盟，而能大规模参与的机会，我们很喜欢。

当然，有些股东大概想问：你们的董事长不是在1978—1980年，以他一贯英明的眼光，把伯克希尔所持同一公司的股票，按每股43美元卖掉了吗，为什么现在却要花172.50美元买？预料到各位会问，我花了1985年大部分时间，想找一句漂亮话，把这两件事说圆。

1985.english:
A little more time, please.

## Acquisition of Scott & Fetzer

Right after yearend we acquired The Scott & Fetzer Company (“Scott Fetzer”) of Cleveland for about $320 million. (In addition, about $90 million of pre-existing Scott Fetzer debt remains in place.) In the next section of this report I describe the sort of businesses that we wish to buy for Berkshire.  Scott Fetzer is a prototype - understandable, large, well-managed, a good earner.

The company has sales of about $700 million derived from 17 businesses, many leaders in their fields.  Return on invested capital is good to excellent for most of these businesses.  Some well-known products are Kirby home-care systems, Campbell Hausfeld air compressors, and Wayne burners and water pumps.
1985.chinese:
请再给我一点时间。

## 收购斯科特与费策公司（Scott & Fetzer）

年末刚过，我们以约3.20亿美元，收购克利夫兰的斯科特与费策公司（Scott Fetzer）。（此外，公司原有约9000万美元债务继续保留。）下一节，我会介绍伯克希尔希望买哪类企业。斯科特与费策就是样板：看得懂、规模大、管理好、能赚钱。

公司销售额约7亿美元，来自17项业务，其中许多是各自领域的领先者。多数业务的投入资本回报，从良好到优异。知名产品包括柯比家居清洁系统、坎贝尔·豪斯菲尔德空气压缩机，以及韦恩燃烧器和水泵。

1985.english:
World Book, Inc. - accounting for about 40% of Scott Fetzer’s sales and a bit more of its income - is by far the company’s largest operation.  It also is by far the leader in its industry, selling more than twice as many encyclopedia sets annually as its nearest competitor.  In fact, it sells more sets in the U.S. than its four biggest competitors combined.

Charlie and I have a particular interest in the World Book operation because we regard its encyclopedia as something special.  I’ve been a fan (and user) for 25 years, and now have grandchildren consulting the sets just as my children did.  World Book is regularly rated the most useful encyclopedia by teachers, librarians and consumer buying guides.  Yet it sells for less than any of its major competitors. Childcraft, another World Book, Inc. product, offers similar value.  This combination of exceptional products and modest prices at World Book, Inc. helped make us willing to pay the price demanded for Scott Fetzer, despite declining results for many companies in the direct- selling industry.
1985.chinese:
世界图书公司（World Book, Inc.）占斯科特与费策销售额约40%，利润占比还略高，是遥遥领先的最大业务。它在本行业也遥遥领先，每年百科全书套数销量，是最接近对手的两倍多。事实上，在美国，它卖出的套数比四大竞争者加起来还多。

查理和我尤其喜欢世界图书，因为我们觉得它的百科全书与众不同。我当了25年的爱好者兼使用者；当年孩子查阅它，如今孙辈也在查阅。教师、图书管理员及消费者购买指南，经常把《世界图书百科全书》评为最实用的百科全书；售价却低于任何主要竞争者。公司的另一产品《儿童天地》（Childcraft），也提供相似的实惠。世界图书这种卓越产品与适中价格的组合，使我们愿意支付卖方对斯科特与费策的要价，尽管直销行业许多公司的业绩正在下降。
