1989.english:
This list of companies is the same as last year's and in only one case has the number of shares changed: Our holdings of Coca-Cola increased from 14,172,500 shares at the end of 1988 to 23,350,000.

This Coca-Cola investment provides yet another example of the incredible speed with which your Chairman responds to investment opportunities, no matter how obscure or well-disguised they may be. I believe I had my first Coca-Cola in either 1935 or 1936. Of a certainty, it was in 1936 that I started buying Cokes at the rate of six for 25 cents from Buffett & Son, the family grocery store, to sell around the neighborhood for 5 cents each. In this excursion into high-margin retailing, I duly observed the extraordinary consumer attractiveness and commercial possibilities of the product.
1989.chinese:
这份公司名单与去年完全一样，只有一项的股数发生变化：可口可乐持股从1988年底的14,172,500股，增至23,350,000股。

这笔可口可乐投资，又一次证明了你们的董事长发现投资机会时，反应有多么神速——不管机会藏得多深、伪装得多好。我想，我第一次喝可口可乐是在1935年或1936年。可以肯定的是，1936年我已经开始从家里的杂货店Buffett & Son按六瓶25美分进货，再以每瓶5美分卖给街坊。在这次高毛利零售业的历险中，我已好好见识过这种产品对消费者的非凡吸引力，以及它蕴藏的商业机会。

1989.english: I continued to note these qualities for the next 52 years as Coke blanketed the world. During this period, however, I carefully avoided buying even a single share, instead allocating major portions of my net worth to street railway companies, windmill manufacturers, anthracite producers, textile businesses, trading-stamp issuers, and the like. (If you think I'm making this up, I can supply the names.) Only in the summer of 1988 did my brain finally establish contact with my eyes.
1989.chinese: 随后的52年里，可口可乐铺遍全球，我也一直留意着这些优点。然而，在这段时间里，我小心翼翼地一股也没买，反倒把个人净资产中的很大一部分投给了有轨电车公司、风车制造商、无烟煤生产商、纺织企业、购物印花券发行商等。（如果你以为这是我编的，我可以把名字报出来。）直到1988年夏天，我的大脑才终于跟眼睛接上了线。

1989.english:
What I then perceived was both clear and fascinating. After drifting somewhat in the 1970's, Coca-Cola had in 1981 become a new company with the move of Roberto Goizueta to CEO. Roberto, along with Don Keough, once my across-the-street neighbor in Omaha, first rethought and focused the company's policies and then energetically carried them out. What was already the world's most ubiquitous product gained new momentum, with sales overseas virtually exploding.

Through a truly rare blend of marketing and financial skills, Roberto has maximized both the growth of his product and the rewards that this growth brings to shareholders. Normally, the CEO of a consumer products company, drawing on his natural inclinations or experience, will cause either marketing or finance to dominate the business at the expense of the other discipline. With Roberto, the mesh of marketing and finance is perfect and the result is a shareholder's dream.
1989.chinese:
那时看到的情形，既清楚又令人着迷。可口可乐在20世纪70年代一度有些失去方向；1981年，罗伯托·戈伊苏埃塔出任首席执行官，公司便焕然一新。罗伯托和唐·基奥——唐曾是我在奥马哈住在街对面的邻居——先重新思考并明确了公司的经营方针，随后大力执行。这个早已无处不在、遍及全球的产品，又获得了新的动力，海外销售几乎呈爆炸式增长。

罗伯托把营销与财务本领融为一体，且融合得极其罕见，既让产品获得最大增长，也让这种增长给股东带来最大回报。通常，消费品公司的首席执行官会受个人天性或经历影响，让营销或财务其中一方占上风，另一方则作出牺牲。罗伯托却使两者严丝合缝，成果正是股东梦寐以求的。

1989.english:
Of course, we should have started buying Coke much earlier, soon after Roberto and Don began running things. In fact, if I had been thinking straight I would have persuaded my grandfather to sell the grocery store back in 1936 and put all of the proceeds into Coca-Cola stock. I've learned my lesson: My response time to the next glaringly attractive idea will be slashed to well under 50 years.

As I mentioned earlier, the yearend prices of our major investees were much higher relative to their intrinsic values than theretofore. While those prices may not yet cause nosebleeds, they are clearly vulnerable to a general market decline. A drop in their prices would not disturb us at all - it might in fact work to our eventual benefit - but it would cause at least a one-year reduction in Berkshire's net worth. We think such a reduction is almost certain in at least one of the next three years. Indeed, it would take only about a 10% year-to-year decline in the aggregate value of our portfolio investments to send Berkshire's net worth down.
1989.chinese:
当然，我们本该早得多就开始买可口可乐，在罗伯托和唐刚接手后不久就买。其实，如果当年脑子清楚，我在1936年就该说服祖父卖掉杂货店，把全部所得买成可口可乐股票。这次我吸取教训了：下次碰到这么明摆着的好主意，我一定把反应时间大幅压缩到50年以内。

如前所述，我们主要被投资公司的年末股价，相对于其内在价值，已经比以往高得多。价格虽还没高到让人流鼻血的地步，但显然很容易随大市下跌。价格下跌丝毫不会使我们不安——实际上，最终可能对我们有利——但会令伯克希尔至少有一个年度的净资产下降。我们认为，未来三年中至少有一年出现这种下降，几乎是肯定的。事实上，投资组合总市值只须比上年下跌约10%，就足以使伯克希尔的净资产下降。

1989.english:
We continue to be blessed with extraordinary managers at our portfolio companies. They are high-grade, talented, and shareholder-oriented. The exceptional results we have achieved while investing with them accurately reflect their exceptional personal qualities.

o     We told you last year that we expected to do little in arbitrage during 1989, and that's the way it turned out. Arbitrage positions are a substitute for short-term cash equivalents, and during part of the year we held relatively low levels of cash. In the rest of the year we had a fairly good- sized cash position and even so chose not to engage in arbitrage. The main reason was corporate transactions that made no economic sense to us; arbitraging such deals comes too close to playing the greater-fool game. (As Wall Streeter Ray DeVoe says: "Fools rush in where angels fear to trade.") We will engage in arbitrage from time to time - sometimes on a large scale - but only when we like the odds.
1989.chinese:
投资组合中的公司继续由一批非凡的经理人掌舵，这是我们的福气。他们品格高尚，才干出众，心里装着股东。与他们一起投资所得的出色成绩，恰恰反映了他们本人出色的素质。

去年我们说，预计1989年很少做套利，结果的确如此。套利头寸是短期现金等价物的替代品，而一年中有一段时间，我们的现金比较少。其余时间现金相当充裕，我们仍选择不做套利。主要原因是，那些公司交易在我们看来毫无经济道理；对这种交易做套利，与玩“总有人比我更傻”的游戏实在太接近了。（正如华尔街的雷·德沃所说：“天使不敢交易的地方，傻瓜抢着往里闯。”）我们会不时做套利，有时规模还很大，但只在我们看好胜算的时候。

1989.english: o     Leaving aside the three convertible preferreds discussed in the next section, we substantially reduced our holdings in both medium- and long-term fixed-income securities. In the long-terms, just about our only holdings have been Washington Public Power Supply Systems (WPPSS) bonds carrying coupons ranging from low to high. During the year we sold a number of the low-coupon issues, which we originally bought at very large discounts. Many of these issues had approximately doubled in price since we purchased them and in addition had paid us 15%-17% annually, tax-free. Our prices upon sale were only slightly cheaper than typical high- grade tax-exempts then commanded. We have kept all of our high- coupon WPPSS issues. Some have been called for redemption in 1991 and 1992, and we expect the rest to be called in the early to mid-1990s.
1989.chinese: 撇开下一节要谈的三种可转换优先股，我们大幅减持了中长期固定收益证券。长期证券方面，几乎唯一的持仓一直是华盛顿公共电力供应系统（WPPSS）的债券，票息有低有高。年内，我们卖出了一些低票息品种，当初买入时折价极大。其中许多债券自买入以来价格已大约翻番，此外每年还给我们带来15%—17%的免税收益。出售价格仅略低于当时通常的高等级免税债券价格。高票息的WPPSS债券则全部保留。有些已通知将在1991年及1992年提前赎回，其余的预计会在20世纪90年代初至中期被提前赎回。

1989.english: We also sold many of our medium-term tax-exempt bonds during the year. When we bought these bonds we said we would be happy to sell them - regardless of whether they were higher or lower than at our time of purchase - if something we liked better came along. Something did - and concurrently we unloaded most of these issues at modest gains. Overall, our 1989 profit from the sale of tax-exempt bonds was about $51 million pre-tax.
1989.chinese: 年内，我们还卖出了许多中期免税债券。买入时就说过，只要出现更中意的东西，无论这些债券的价格比买入时高还是低，我们都乐意卖掉。后来，更中意的东西来了；我们也随之卖出了这些债券中的大部分，略有盈利。总计，1989年出售免税债券的税前利润约为5100万美元。

1989.english: o     The proceeds from our bond sales, along with our excess cash at the beginning of the year and that generated later through earnings, went into the purchase of three convertible preferred stocks. In the first transaction, which took place in July, we purchased $600 million of The Gillette Co. preferred with an 8 3/4% dividend, a mandatory redemption in ten years, and the right to convert into common at $50 per share. We next purchased $358 million of USAir Group, Inc. preferred stock with mandatory redemption in ten years, a dividend of 9 1/4%, and the right to convert into common at $60 per share. Finally, late in the year we purchased $300 million of Champion International Corp. preferred with mandatory redemption in ten years, a 9 1/4% dividend, and the right to convert into common at $38 per share.
1989.chinese: 债券出售所得，加上年初多余的现金，以及后来盈利带来的现金，都用于买入三种可转换优先股。第一笔交易发生在7月：我们买入6亿美元吉列公司优先股，股息率8¾%，十年后强制赎回，并有权按每股50美元转换成普通股。接着买入3.58亿美元全美航空集团（USAir Group, Inc.）优先股，同样十年后强制赎回，股息率9¼%，可按每股60美元转换成普通股。最后，年末买入3亿美元冠军国际公司（Champion International Corp.）优先股，十年后强制赎回，股息率9¼%，可按每股38美元转换成普通股。

1989.english:
Unlike standard convertible preferred stocks, the issues we own are either non-salable or non-convertible for considerable periods of time and there is consequently no way we can gain from short-term price blips in the common stock. I have gone on the board of Gillette, but I am not on the board of USAir or Champion. (I thoroughly enjoy the boards I am on, but can't handle any more.)

Gillette's business is very much the kind we like. Charlie and I think we understand the company's economics and therefore believe we can make a reasonably intelligent guess about its future. (If you haven't tried Gillette's new Sensor razor, go right out and get one.) However, we have no ability to forecast the economics of the investment banking business (in which we have a position through our 1987 purchase of Salomon convertible preferred), the airline industry, or the paper industry. This does not mean that we predict a negative  future for these industries: we're  agnostics, not  atheists. Our  lack of  strong convictions about these businesses, however, means that we must structure our investments in them differently from what we do when we invest in a business appearing to have splendid economic characteristics.
1989.chinese:
与标准的可转换优先股不同，我们持有的这些品种，在相当长一段时期内，要么不能出售，要么不能转换，因此无法靠普通股价格的短暂跳升获利。我已加入吉列董事会，但没有加入全美航空或冠军国际的董事会。（我很喜欢自己任职的几个董事会，不过再多就忙不过来了。）

吉列的生意正是我们很喜欢的类型。查理和我认为，我们懂它的经济特性，因此相信能对未来作出相当明智的估计。（如果你还没试过吉列新推出的Sensor剃须刀，赶快去买一把。）不过，我们没有能力预测投资银行业、航空业或造纸业的经济状况；投资银行业这笔权益，来自1987年买入的所罗门可转换优先股。这并不是说，我们认定这些行业前途黯淡：我们是不可知论者，不是无神论者。不过，既然对这些生意缺乏坚定判断，投资安排就必须与那些在我们看来经济特性极佳的企业有所不同。

1989.english:
In one major respect, however, these purchases are not different: We only want to link up with people whom we like, admire, and trust. John Gutfreund at Salomon, Colman Mockler, Jr. at Gillette, Ed Colodny at USAir, and Andy Sigler at Champion meet this test in spades.

They in turn have demonstrated some confidence in us, insisting in each case that our preferreds have unrestricted voting rights on a fully-converted basis, an arrangement that is far from standard in corporate finance. In effect they are trusting us to be intelligent owners, thinking about tomorrow instead of today, just as we are trusting them to be intelligent managers, thinking about tomorrow as well as today.
1989.chinese:
但在一个重要方面，这些购买并没有两样：我们只愿与自己喜欢、钦佩并信任的人合作。所罗门的约翰·古特弗罗因德、吉列的小科尔曼·莫克勒、全美航空的埃德·科洛德尼，以及冠军国际的安迪·西格勒，全都绰绰有余地符合这个标准。

反过来，他们也表现出对我们的信任：每一笔交易，他们都坚持让我们的优先股按全部转换成普通股后的股数，享有不受限制的表决权。这样的安排，在公司融资中远非常规做法。实际上，他们相信我们会做明智的所有者，着眼明天而不是只顾今天；正如我们相信他们会做明智的经理人，既顾今天，也顾明天。

1989.english:
The preferred-stock structures we have negotiated will provide a mediocre return for us if industry economics hinder the performance of our investees, but will produce reasonably attractive results for us if they can earn a return comparable to that of American industry in general. We believe that Gillette, under Colman's management, will far exceed that return and believe that John, Ed, and Andy will reach it unless industry conditions are harsh.

Under almost any conditions, we expect these preferreds to return us our money plus dividends. If that is all we get, though, the result will be disappointing, because we will have given up flexibility and consequently will have missed some significant opportunities that are bound to present themselves during the decade. Under that scenario, we will have obtained only a preferred-stock yield during a period when the typical preferred stock will have held no appeal for us whatsoever. The only way Berkshire can achieve satisfactory results from its four preferred issues is to have the common stocks of the investee companies do well.
1989.chinese:
如果行业经济状况妨碍被投资公司的表现，我们谈定的优先股结构，只会给我们带来平庸回报；如果这些公司能赚到与美国一般企业相仿的回报，我们的结果就会相当令人满意。我们相信，在科尔曼的管理下，吉列会远远超过这个水平；也相信，除非行业条件恶劣，约翰、埃德和安迪都会达到这个水平。

几乎在任何条件下，我们都预计这些优先股能归还本金并支付股息。不过，若所得仅此而已，结果仍会令人失望：因为我们放弃了灵活性，也就会错过这十年间必然出现的一些重大机会。那种情况下，在一个普通优先股本来对我们毫无吸引力的时期里，我们拿到的就只是优先股的收益率。要让伯克希尔从这四种优先股中取得满意结果，唯一的路是被投资公司的普通股表现良好。

1989.english: Good management and at least tolerable industry conditions will be needed if that is to happen. But we believe Berkshire's investment will also help and that the other shareholders of each investee will profit over the years ahead from our preferred- stock purchase. The help will come from the fact that each company now has a major, stable, and interested shareholder whose Chairman and Vice Chairman have, through Berkshire's investments, indirectly committed a very large amount of their own money to these undertakings. In dealing with our investees, Charlie and I will be supportive, analytical, and objective. We recognize that we are working with experienced CEOs who are very much in command of their own businesses but who nevertheless, at certain moments, appreciate the chance to test  their thinking on someone without ties to their industry or to decisions of the past.
1989.chinese: 这需要出色的管理，以及至少过得去的行业条件。但我们相信，伯克希尔的投资也会有所帮助，而各被投资公司的其他股东，会在今后多年受益于我们买入优先股。帮助来自这样一个事实：每家公司现在都有了一位持股大、稳定而且关心公司事务的股东；这位股东的董事长和副董事长，通过伯克希尔的投资，也间接把自己很大一笔钱投入了这些事业。与被投资公司交往时，查理和我会给予支持，认真分析，并保持客观。我们清楚，与我们共事的是经验丰富、完全掌握自家业务的首席执行官；不过，他们有时仍会觉得，找一位既不属于本行业、也不受以往决策牵绊的人，检验一下自己的想法，是件有益的事。

1989.english: As a group, these convertible preferreds will not produce the returns we can achieve when we find a business with wonderful economic prospects that is unappreciated by the market. Nor will the returns be as attractive as those produced when we make our favorite form of capital deployment, the acquisition of 80% or more of a fine business with a fine management. But both opportunities are rare, particularly in a size befitting our present and anticipated resources.
1989.chinese: 整体而言，这些可转换优先股的回报，比不上我们找到一家经济前景极佳、却未获市场赏识的企业时能取得的回报，也比不上我们最喜欢的资金运用方式——收购一家由优秀管理层经营的优秀企业80%或以上的股权。但这两种机会都很少见，尤其是规模足以容纳我们现有以及预期资金的机会。

1989.english:
In summation, Charlie and I feel that our preferred stock investments should produce returns moderately above those achieved by most fixed-income portfolios and that we can play a minor but enjoyable and constructive role in the investee companies.

## Zero-Coupon Securities

In September, Berkshire issued $902.6 million principal amount of Zero-Coupon Convertible Subordinated Debentures, which are now listed on the New York Stock Exchange. Salomon Brothers handled the underwriting in superb fashion, providing us helpful advice and a flawless execution.
1989.chinese:
总的来说，查理和我认为，这些优先股投资的回报，应当会略高于多数固定收益投资组合；我们也能在被投资公司中，扮演一个作用不大、但愉快且有益的角色。

## 零息证券

9月，伯克希尔发行了到期本金总额为9.026亿美元的零息可转换次级债券，现已在纽约证券交易所上市。所罗门兄弟公司的承销工作十分出色，既给我们提供了有益建议，执行也无可挑剔。

1989.english:
Most bonds, of course, require regular payments of interest, usually semi-annually. A zero-coupon bond, conversely, requires no current interest payments; instead, the investor receives his yield by purchasing the security at a significant discount from maturity value. The effective interest rate is determined by the original issue price, the maturity value, and the amount of time between issuance and maturity.

In our case, the bonds were issued at 44.314% of maturity value and are due in 15 years. For investors purchasing the bonds, that is the mathematical equivalent of a 5.5% current payment compounded semi-annually. Because we received only 44.31 cents on the dollar, our proceeds from this offering were $400 million (less about $9.5 million of offering expenses).
1989.chinese:
多数债券当然要定期付息，通常每半年一次。零息债券则相反，无须支付当期利息；投资者以远低于到期价值的价格买入，从而取得收益。实际利率由原始发行价、到期价值，以及发行日至到期日之间的时间决定。

我们的债券按到期价值的44.314%发行，15年后到期。对买入者而言，从数学上说，这相当于年利率5.5%、每半年付息并按半年复利计算的收益。由于每1美元到期本金，我们只收到44.31美分，本次发行筹得4亿美元，还须扣除约950万美元发行费用。

1989.english: The bonds were issued in denominations of $10,000 and each bond is convertible into .4515 shares of Berkshire Hathaway. Because a $10,000 bond cost $4,431, this means that the conversion price was $9,815 per Berkshire share, a 15% premium to the market price then existing. Berkshire can call the bonds at any time after  September 28, 1992 at their accreted value (the original issue price plus 5.5% compounded semi-annually) and on two specified days, September 28 of 1994 and 1999, the bondholders can require Berkshire to buy the securities at their accreted value.
1989.chinese: 债券面额为10,000美元，每张可转换为0.4515股伯克希尔哈撒韦股票。每张10,000美元债券的购买价为4431美元，因此对应的伯克希尔每股转换价格为9815美元，比当时市价高15%。1992年9月28日之后，伯克希尔可随时按增计价值提前赎回，即原始发行价加上按年利率5.5%、每半年复利一次累积的利息。在另外两个指定日期——1994年9月28日及1999年9月28日——债券持有人可要求伯克希尔按增计价值买回债券。

1989.english: For tax purposes, Berkshire is entitled to deduct the 5.5% interest accrual each year, even though we make no payments to the bondholders. Thus the net effect to us, resulting from the reduced taxes, is positive cash flow. That is a very significant benefit. Some unknowable variables prevent us from calculating our exact effective rate of interest, but under all circumstances it will be well below 5.5%. There is meanwhile a symmetry to the tax law: Any taxable holder of the bonds must pay tax each year on the 5.5% interest, even though he receives no cash.
1989.chinese: 在税务上，即使并未向债券持有人付款，伯克希尔每年也有权扣除按5.5%计提的利息。因此，税款减少给我们带来的净效果，是正的现金流。这项好处相当可观。若干无法预知的变量，使我们算不出确切的实际利率，但无论如何，都会远低于5.5%。税法在另一端也作了对称处理：应税的债券持有人，即使没有收到现金，每年仍须就这5.5%的利息缴税。

1989.english: Neither our bonds nor those of certain other companies that issued similar bonds last year (notably Loews and Motorola) resemble the great bulk of zero-coupon bonds that have been issued in recent years. Of these, Charlie and I have been, and will continue to be, outspoken critics. As I will later explain, such bonds have often been used in the most deceptive of ways and with deadly consequences to investors. But before we tackle that subject, let's travel back to Eden, to a time when the apple had not yet been bitten.
1989.chinese: 我们的债券，以及去年某些其他公司发行的类似债券——尤其是Loews和摩托罗拉——都与近几年发行的绝大多数零息债券很不一样。对后者，查理和我过去一直直言批评，今后也会继续如此。稍后我会解释，这类债券往往被用在极具欺骗性的地方，给投资者带来致命后果。不过，在动手剖析之前，先让我们回到伊甸园，回到苹果还没被咬上一口的年代。

1989.english:
If you're my age you bought your first zero-coupon bonds during World War II, by purchasing the famous Series E U. S. Savings Bond, the most widely-sold bond issue in history. (After the war, these bonds were held by one out of two U. S. households.) Nobody, of course, called the Series E a zero-coupon bond, a term in fact that I doubt had been invented. But that's precisely what the Series E was.

These bonds came in denominations as small as $18.75. That amount purchased a $25 obligation of the United States government due in 10 years, terms that gave the buyer a compounded annual return of 2.9%. At the time, this was an attractive offer: the 2.9% rate was higher than that generally available on Government bonds and the holder faced no market-fluctuation risk, since he could at any time cash in his bonds with only a minor reduction in interest.
1989.chinese:
如果你与我同龄，你买的第一批零息债券，多半是在第二次世界大战期间买的著名美国E系列储蓄债券——历史上销售范围最广的一次债券发行。（战后，美国每两户家庭中，就有一户持有。）当然，当时没人叫它零息债券；事实上，我怀疑这个名词当时还没发明。不过，E系列确确实实就是零息债券。

这种债券的购买金额最低只有18.75美元，可以买到美国政府十年后支付25美元的债务凭证，买方的年复合回报率为2.9%。这在当时很有吸引力：2.9%高于政府债券通常提供的利率，而且持有人不承担市价波动风险，因为随时可以兑现，只须少拿一点利息。

1989.english: A second form of zero-coupon U. S. Treasury issue, also benign and useful, surfaced in the last decade. One problem with a normal bond is that even though it pays a given interest rate - say 10% - the holder cannot be assured that a compounded 10% return will be realized. For that rate to materialize, each semi- annual coupon must be reinvested at 10% as it is received. If current interest rates are, say, only 6% or 7% when these coupons come due, the holder will be unable to compound his money over the life of the bond at the advertised rate. For pension funds or other investors with long-term liabilities, "reinvestment risk" of this type can be a serious problem. Savings Bonds might have solved it, except that they are issued only to individuals and are unavailable in large denominations. What big buyers needed was huge quantities of "Savings Bond Equivalents."
1989.chinese: 另一种同样有益而实用的美国国债零息形式，在过去十年出现了。普通债券有个问题：即使票面利率确定，比如10%，持有人也不能保证实际取得10%的复合回报。要达到这个水平，每次收到半年期利息，都必须再按10%投资。假如付息时市场利率只有6%或7%，那么在债券整个存续期内，资金就无法按所标示的利率复利增长。对养老基金等负有长期债务的投资者，这种“再投资风险”可能是个严重问题。储蓄债券本可解决它，可惜只向个人发行，也没有大面额品种。大买家需要的，是巨量的“储蓄债券等价物”。

1989.english: Enter some ingenious and, in this case, highly useful investment bankers (led, I'm happy to say, by Salomon Brothers). They created the instrument desired by "stripping" the semi- annual coupons from standard Government issues. Each coupon, once detached, takes on the essential character of a Savings Bond since it represents a single sum due sometime in the future. For example, if you strip the 40 semi-annual coupons from a U. S. Government Bond due in the year 2010, you will have 40 zero- coupon bonds, with maturities from six months to 20 years, each of which can then be bundled with other coupons of like maturity and marketed. If current interest rates are, say, 10% for all maturities, the six-month issue will sell for 95.24% of maturity value and the 20-year issue will sell for 14.20%. The purchaser of any given maturity is thus guaranteed a compounded rate of 10% for his entire holding period. Stripping of government bonds has occurred on a large scale in recent years, as long-term investors, ranging from pension funds to individual IRA accounts, recognized these high-grade, zero-coupon issues to be well suited to their needs.
1989.chinese: 于是，一些聪明的投资银行家登场了；这一次，他们也确实大有用处。我很高兴地说，领头的是所罗门兄弟公司。他们把普通政府债券每半年付息的息票“拆开”，造出了所需的工具。每张息票一旦分离，就具备储蓄债券的基本性质，因为它代表未来某一时点应付的一笔确定金额。比如，从一张2010年到期的美国政府债券中，拆出40张半年期息票，就得到40种零息债券，期限从六个月到20年不等；每种再与其他同期限息票打包出售。假设目前各期限利率都是10%，六个月品种的售价是到期价值的95.24%，20年品种则是14.20%。因此，无论买哪一期限，买方在整个持有期都能锁定10%的复合回报。近年来，政府债券拆息的规模很大，因为从养老基金到个人退休账户（IRA）的长期投资者，都认识到这些高等级零息债券很适合自己的需要。

1989.english: But as happens in Wall Street all too often, what the wise do in the beginning, fools do in the end. In the last few years zero-coupon bonds (and their functional equivalent, pay-in-kind bonds, which distribute additional PIK bonds semi-annually as interest instead of paying cash) have been issued in enormous quantities by ever-junkier credits. To these issuers, zero (or PIK) bonds offer one overwhelming advantage:  It is impossible to default on a promise to pay nothing. Indeed, if LDC governments had issued no debt in the 1970's other than long-term zero-coupon obligations, they would now have a spotless record as debtors.
1989.chinese: 可是，华尔街常常如此：聪明人起头做的事，傻瓜最后会跟着做。过去几年，信用质量越来越垃圾的发行人大量发行零息债券，或功能相同的实物付息债券（PIK）；后者每半年以追加PIK债券代替现金付息。对这些发行人，零息债券或PIK债券有一项压倒性的优点：你承诺什么都不付，就不可能在这项承诺上违约。事实上，如果欠发达国家的政府在20世纪70年代只发行长期零息债务，那么它们现在的债务人记录都会洁白无瑕。

1989.english: This principle at work - that you need not default for a long time if you solemnly promise to pay nothing for a long time - has not been lost on promoters and investment bankers seeking to finance ever-shakier deals. But its acceptance by lenders took a while: When the leveraged buy-out craze began some years back, purchasers could borrow only on a reasonably sound basis, in which conservatively-estimated free cash flow - that is, operating earnings plus depreciation and amortization less normalized capital expenditures - was adequate to cover both interest and modest reductions in debt.
1989.chinese: 只要郑重承诺很长时间内什么都不付，就能很长时间不违约——这个道理，自然逃不过那些为越来越不稳妥的交易筹资的交易发起人和投资银行家。不过，贷款人接受它，倒费了些时日。几年前杠杆收购热潮刚起时，买方借钱还须有相当稳健的基础：保守估计的自由现金流，即经营利润加折旧及摊销，再减去正常化资本支出，应足以支付利息，并偿还少量债务。

1989.english: Later, as the adrenalin of deal-makers surged, businesses began to be purchased at prices so high that all free cash flow necessarily had to be allocated to the payment of interest. That left nothing for the paydown of debt. In effect, a Scarlett O'Hara "I'll think about it tomorrow" position in respect to principal payments was taken by borrowers and accepted by a new breed of lender, the buyer of original-issue junk bonds. Debt now became something to be refinanced rather than repaid. The change brings to mind a New Yorker cartoon in which the grateful borrower rises to shake the hand of the bank's lending officer and gushes: "I don't know how I'll ever repay you."
1989.chinese: 后来，交易撮合者肾上腺素高涨，企业收购价也高到必须把全部自由现金流用于付息，还本便分文不剩。实际上，借款人对偿还本金采取了斯嘉丽·奥哈拉那句“明天再想吧”的态度，而新一代贷款人——首次发行垃圾债券的买家——也接受了。债务从此成了需要再融资、而非需要偿还的东西。这种变化，使人想起《纽约客》的一幅漫画：借款人满怀感激，起身握住银行信贷员的手，激动地说：“我真不知道该怎么还你。”

1989.english:
Soon borrowers found even the new, lax standards intolerably binding. To induce lenders to finance even sillier transactions, they introduced an abomination, EBDIT - Earnings Before Depreciation, Interest and Taxes - as the test of a company's ability to pay interest. Using this sawed-off yardstick, the borrower ignored depreciation as an expense on the theory that it did not require a current cash outlay.

Such an attitude is clearly delusional. At 95% of American businesses, capital expenditures that over time roughly approximate depreciation are a necessity and are every bit as real an expense as labor or utility costs. Even a high school dropout knows that to finance a car he must have income that covers not only interest and operating expenses, but also realistically-calculated depreciation. He would be laughed out of the bank if he started talking about EBDIT.
1989.chinese:
很快，借款人连这套新的宽松标准，也觉得束缚得难以忍受。为了诱使贷款人为更荒唐的交易出钱，他们发明了一个讨厌的玩意儿——EBDIT，即扣除折旧、利息和税款之前的利润——用来衡量企业付息能力。拿着这把锯短的尺子，借款人把折旧费用排除在外，理由是它不需要当期付现。

这种想法显然是自欺欺人。美国95%的企业，都必须作出长期来看大致相当于折旧额的资本支出。这与人工费或水电费一样，都是实实在在的费用。即使没读完高中，也知道贷款买车时，收入不但要覆盖利息及使用费用，还要覆盖现实估算的折旧。如果跑到银行谈起EBDIT，人家会笑着把他请出去。

1989.english: Capital outlays at a business can be skipped, of course, in any given month, just as a human can skip a day or even a week of eating. But if the skipping becomes routine and is not made up, the body weakens and eventually dies. Furthermore, a start-and- stop feeding policy will over time produce a less healthy organism, human or corporate, than that produced by a steady diet. As businessmen, Charlie and I relish having competitors who are unable to fund capital expenditures.
1989.chinese: 当然，企业在某个月可以不作资本支出，正如人可以一天、甚至一周不吃饭。但如果经常不吃，又不补回来，身体就会衰弱，最终死去。而且，长期看来，无论人还是公司，时吃时停，都不如饮食稳定来得健康。作为生意人，查理和我很欢迎那些无力支付资本支出的竞争对手。

1989.english:
You might think that waving away a major expense such as depreciation in an attempt to make a terrible deal look like a good one hits the limits of Wall Street's ingenuity. If so, you haven't been paying attention during the past few years. Promoters needed to find a way to justify even pricier acquisitions. Otherwise, they risked - heaven forbid! - losing deals to other promoters with more "imagination."

So, stepping through the Looking Glass, promoters and their investment bankers proclaimed that EBDIT should now be measured against cash interest only, which meant that interest accruing on zero-coupon or PIK bonds could be ignored when the financial feasibility of a transaction was being assessed. This approach not only relegated depreciation expense to the let's-ignore-it corner, but gave similar treatment to what was usually a significant portion of interest expense. To their shame, many professional investment managers went along with this nonsense, though they usually were careful to do so only with clients' money, not their own. (Calling these managers "professionals" is actually too kind; they should be designated "promotees.")
1989.chinese:
为了把糟糕交易打扮成好交易，连折旧这样的大笔费用也一挥手抹掉，你或许觉得这已到了华尔街想象力的极限。如果这么想，说明你过去几年没留心。交易发起人还得找到办法，替更贵的收购辩护。否则——老天保佑，千万别这样！——他们就可能把交易输给更富“想象力”的同行。

于是，发起人和他们的投资银行家穿过镜子，走进了镜中世界，宣布现在只需拿EBDIT与现金利息比较。这意味着，评估一项交易在财务上是否可行时，零息债券或PIK债券累积的应计利息，也可以忽略。这样，不但折旧被扔进“算了，不管它”的角落，通常相当大一部分利息费用也受到了同等待遇。可耻的是，许多专业投资经理也跟着接受这套胡话，只不过他们通常很谨慎：用客户的钱照办，不用自己的钱。（称这些经理为“专业人士”，其实太客气了；该叫他们“被推销成功的人”。）

1989.english: Under this new standard, a business earning, say, $100 million pre-tax and having debt on which $90 million of interest must be paid currently, might use a zero-coupon or PIK issue to incur another $60 million of annual interest that would accrue and compound but not come due for some years. The rate on these issues would typically be very high, which means that the situation in year 2 might be $90 million cash interest plus $69 million accrued interest, and so on as the compounding proceeds. Such high-rate reborrowing schemes, which a few years ago were appropriately confined to the waterfront,  soon became models of modern finance at virtually all major investment banking houses.
1989.chinese: 在这套新标准下，一家税前利润比方说为1亿美元、现有债务每年须付9000万美元现金利息的企业，可以再发行零息债券或PIK债券，每年增加6000万美元利息，虽不断计提、复利累积，却要几年后才到期。这类债券利率通常很高，因此第二年可能就是9000万美元现金利息，加6900万美元应计利息，随后再依此复利增长。几年前，这种高利借新债的套路还被适当地限制在码头一带，转眼间却成了几乎所有大型投资银行奉行的现代金融典范。

1989.english: When they make these offerings, investment bankers display their humorous side: They dispense income and balance sheet projections extending five or more years into the future for companies they barely had heard of a few months earlier. If you are shown such schedules, I suggest that you join in the fun: Ask the investment banker for the one-year budgets that his own firm prepared as the last few years began and then compare these with what actually happened.
1989.chinese: 推销这些证券时，投资银行家也显露出幽默的一面：对一家几个月前还几乎没听说过的公司，他们照样能拿出未来五年乃至更久的利润表和资产负债表预测。如果有人把这样的表格摆到你面前，我建议也来凑个趣：请那位投资银行家拿出他自己公司过去几年年初编制的一年期预算，再和实际结果比一比。

1989.english:
Some time ago Ken Galbraith, in his witty and insightful The Great Crash, coined a new economic term: "the bezzle," defined as the current amount of undiscovered embezzlement. This financial creature has a magical quality: The embezzlers are richer by the amount of the bezzle, while the embezzlees do not yet feel poorer.

Professor Galbraith astutely pointed out that this sum should be added to the National Wealth so that we might know the Psychic National Wealth. Logically, a society that wanted to feel enormously prosperous would both encourage its citizens to embezzle and try not to detect the crime. By this means, "wealth" would balloon though not an erg of productive work had been done.
1989.chinese:
前些年，肯·加尔布雷思在他机智而深刻的《大崩盘》中，创造了一个新的经济学名词：“bezzle”，即当时已经发生、却尚未被发现的侵吞金额。这种金融生物有一种魔力：侵吞者的财富增加了相应金额，被侵吞者却还没觉得自己变穷。

加尔布雷思教授敏锐地指出，应把这笔钱加到国民财富上，才能得出“心理国民财富”。按这个逻辑，一个社会如果想觉得自己富得不得了，就该既鼓励公民侵吞，又尽量别查出来。这样，即便连一丁点生产性劳动也没有，“财富”照样能膨胀。

1989.english: The satirical nonsense of the bezzle is dwarfed by the real- world nonsense of the zero-coupon bond. With zeros, one party to a contract can experience "income" without his opposite experiencing the pain of expenditure. In our illustration, a company capable of earning only $100 million dollars annually - and therefore capable of paying only that much in interest - magically creates "earnings" for bondholders of $150 million. As long as major investors willingly don their Peter Pan wings and repeatedly say "I believe," there is no limit to how much "income" can be created by the zero-coupon bond.
1989.chinese: 拿零息债券现实中的荒唐事来比，“bezzle”这种讽刺性的胡扯就相形见绌了。有了零息债券，合同一方可以享受“收入”，另一方却感觉不到支出的痛。在前面的例子里，一家每年只能赚1亿美元、因此最多也只能支付这么多利息的公司，竟神奇地为债券持有人创造出1.5亿美元“利润”。只要大投资者愿意披上彼得·潘的翅膀，反复念着“我相信”，零息债券能创造多少“收入”，就没有上限。

1989.english:
Wall Street welcomed this invention with the enthusiasm less-enlightened folk might reserve for the wheel or the plow. Here, finally, was an instrument that would let the Street make deals at prices no longer limited by actual earning power. The result, obviously, would be more transactions: Silly prices will always attract sellers. And, as Jesse Unruh might have put it, transactions are the mother's milk of finance.

The zero-coupon or PIK bond possesses one additional attraction for the promoter and investment banker, which is that the time elapsing between folly and failure can be stretched out. This is no small benefit. If the period before all costs must be faced is long, promoters can create a string of foolish deals - and take in lots of fees - before any chickens come home to roost from their earlier ventures.
1989.chinese:
华尔街欢迎这项发明的热情，简直就像那些不够开化的人迎接轮子或犁的发明一样。终于有了一种工具，让华尔街撮合交易时，价格再也不受实际盈利能力约束。显然，结果会是更多交易：荒唐的价格，总会吸引卖家。借用杰西·昂鲁可能会说的话，交易就是金融的母乳。

对交易发起人和投资银行家来说，零息债券或PIK债券还有一层吸引力：可以把犯傻到失败之间的时间拉长。这好处可不小。只要所有成本真正上门的日子还远，发起人就能在早先交易的恶果显现前，再做出一连串愚蠢交易，并收走一大堆费用。

1989.english:
But in the end, alchemy, whether it is metallurgical or financial, fails. A base business can not be transformed into a golden business by tricks of accounting or capital structure. The man claiming to be a financial alchemist may become rich. But gullible investors rather than business achievements will usually be the source of his wealth.

Whatever their weaknesses, we should add, many zero-coupon and PIK bonds will not default. We have in fact owned some and may buy more if their market becomes sufficiently distressed. (We've not, however, even considered buying a new issue from a weak credit.) No financial instrument is evil per se; it's just that some variations have far more potential for mischief than others.
1989.chinese:
但到头来，炼金术总会失败，无论炼的是金属还是金融。靠会计把戏或资本结构把戏，不能把贱金属般的企业变成黄金企业。自称金融炼金术士的人，也许会发财；但财富的来源，通常是轻信的投资者，而不是企业的成就。

不过也该补充，无论有多少弱点，许多零息债券及PIK债券并不会违约。我们事实上也持有过一些；如果市场陷入足够严重的困境，还可能继续买入。（不过，对信用薄弱者新发行的债券，我们连考虑都没考虑过。）没有哪种金融工具天生邪恶，只是有些变种，比另一些有更大的作恶空间。

1989.english: The blue ribbon for mischief-making should go to the zero- coupon issuer unable to make its interest payments on a current basis. Our advice: Whenever an investment banker starts talking about EBDIT - or whenever someone creates a capital structure that does not allow all interest, both payable and accrued, to be comfortably met out of current cash flow net of ample capital expenditures - zip up your wallet. Turn the tables by suggesting that the promoter and his high-priced entourage accept zero- coupon fees, deferring their take until the zero-coupon bonds have been paid in full. See then how much enthusiasm for the deal endures.
1989.chinese: 若论制造祸害的头奖，该颁给那些无力支付当期利息、却发行零息债券的公司。我们的建议是：只要投资银行家开始谈EBDIT，或者有人设计的资本结构，使扣除充足资本支出后的当期现金流，无法轻松覆盖全部利息——包括应付及应计利息——就把钱包拉链拉好。不妨反将一军，建议发起人和他那班收费高昂的随从，也接受“零息费用”：等零息债券全额清偿后，再拿报酬。到时看看，他们对这笔交易还剩多少热情。

1989.english: Our comments about investment bankers may seem harsh. But Charlie and I - in our hopelessly old-fashioned way - believe that they should perform a gatekeeping role, guarding investors against the promoter's propensity to indulge in excess. Promoters, after all, have throughout time exercised the same judgment and restraint in accepting money that alcoholics have exercised in accepting liquor. At a minimum, therefore, the banker's conduct should rise to that of a responsible bartender who, when necessary, refuses the profit from the next drink to avoid sending a drunk out on the highway. In recent years, unfortunately, many leading investment firms have found bartender morality to be an intolerably restrictive standard. Lately, those who have traveled the high road in Wall Street have not encountered heavy traffic.
1989.chinese: 我们对投资银行家的话，或许显得严厉。但查理和我抱着无可救药的老派想法，认为他们应当守门，保护投资者，不让交易发起人过度放纵的倾向伤害投资者。毕竟，自古以来，发起人收钱时的判断力与节制，跟酒鬼接酒时差不多。因此，银行家的操守至少该达到一位负责任的酒保的水平：必要时，宁可不赚下一杯酒的钱，也不让醉汉上公路。遗憾的是，近几年，许多顶尖投资公司发现，酒保的道德标准对自己实在约束得难以忍受。最近，在华尔街走正道的人，可没遇上什么拥堵。

1989.english: One distressing footnote: The cost of the zero-coupon folly will not be borne solely by the direct participants. Certain savings and loan associations were heavy buyers of such bonds, using cash that came from FSLIC-insured deposits. Straining to show splendid earnings, these buyers recorded - but did not receive - ultra-high interest income on these issues. Many of these  associations are now in  major trouble. Had their loans to shaky credits worked, the owners of the associations would have pocketed the profits. In the many cases in which the loans will fail, the taxpayer will pick up the bill. To paraphrase Jackie Mason, at these associations it was the managers who should have been wearing the ski masks.
1989.chinese: 还有一条令人不安的附记：零息债券闹剧的代价，并不只由直接参与者承担。某些储蓄贷款机构大量买入这类债券，用的是受联邦储蓄贷款保险公司（FSLIC）保障的存款。为了拼出漂亮的利润，这些买方把超高利息收入记进账上，却没有收到钱。许多这类机构现在已陷入重大困境。要是贷给信用不稳者的钱顺利收回，利润便进了机构所有者的口袋；而众多贷款失败的账单，却得由纳税人埋单。改用杰基·梅森的说法，在这些机构里，真正该戴滑雪面罩的，是经理人。

1989.english:
Mistakes of the First Twenty-five Years (A Condensed Version)

To quote Robert Benchley, "Having a dog teaches a boy fidelity, perseverance, and to turn around three times before lying down." Such are the shortcomings of experience. Nevertheless, it's a good idea to review past mistakes before committing new ones. So let's take a quick look at the last 25 years.

o     My first mistake, of course, was in buying control of Berkshire. Though I knew its business - textile manufacturing - to be unpromising, I was enticed to buy because the price looked cheap. Stock purchases of that kind had proved reasonably rewarding in my early years, though by the time Berkshire came along in 1965 I was becoming aware that the strategy was not ideal.
1989.chinese:
## 头二十五年的错误（浓缩版）

借用罗伯特·本奇利的话：“养狗能教会一个男孩忠诚、坚持，还有躺下之前先转三圈。”经验就有这样的缺陷。不过，在犯新错误之前，回顾旧错误，总是个好主意。那就让我们快快看一眼过去25年。

我的第一个错误，当然就是买下伯克希尔的控制权。虽然明知它的纺织制造业务前景不佳，我还是被看上去便宜的价格诱惑了。早年，这类股票投资曾给我带来相当不错的回报；不过，到1965年伯克希尔出现时，我已开始意识到，这种策略并不理想。

1989.english: If you buy a stock at a sufficiently low price, there will usually be some hiccup in the fortunes of the business that gives you a chance to unload at a decent profit, even though the long- term performance of the business may be terrible. I call this the "cigar butt" approach to investing. A cigar butt found on the street that has only one puff left in it may not offer much of a smoke, but the "bargain purchase" will make that puff all profit.
1989.chinese: 只要买价足够低，即使企业长期表现可能很糟，经营途中通常仍会有一阵短暂起色，让你有机会卖掉，赚上一笔不错的利润。我把这叫作“捡烟蒂”投资法。在街上捡到一截只剩一口的雪茄，抽起来或许不怎么样，但这笔“便宜买卖”会让那最后一口全是净赚。

1989.english: Unless you are a liquidator, that kind of approach to buying businesses is foolish. First, the original "bargain" price probably will not turn out to be such a steal after all. In a difficult business, no sooner is one problem solved than another surfaces -  never is there just one cockroach in the kitchen. Second, any initial advantage you secure will be quickly eroded by the low return that the business earns. For example, if you buy a business for $8 million that can be sold or liquidated for $10 million and promptly take either course, you can realize a high return. But the investment will disappoint if the business is sold for $10 million in ten years and in the interim has annually earned and distributed only a few percent on cost. Time is the friend of the wonderful business, the enemy of the mediocre.
1989.chinese: 除非你是做清算的，否则用这种方法买企业，是愚蠢的。第一，当初的“便宜”价，最后很可能并没有那么划算。难做的生意，总是一个问题刚解决，下一个又冒出来——厨房里从来不会只有一只蟑螂。第二，企业的低回报，会很快侵蚀你起初取得的任何优势。比如，花800万美元买一家可以卖掉或清算收回1000万美元的企业，并立即采取其中一种办法，回报就很高。但如果十年后才卖得1000万美元，而期间每年赚得并分配的利润，只相当于成本的几个百分点，这笔投资就令人失望。时间是优秀企业的朋友，是平庸企业的敌人。

1989.english: You might think this principle is obvious, but I had to learn it the hard way - in fact, I had to learn it several times over. Shortly after purchasing Berkshire, I acquired a Baltimore department store, Hochschild Kohn, buying through a company called Diversified Retailing that later merged with Berkshire. I bought at a substantial discount from book value, the people were first-class, and the deal included some extras - unrecorded real estate values and a significant LIFO inventory cushion. How could I miss? So-o-o - three years later I was lucky to sell the business for about what I had paid. After ending our corporate marriage to Hochschild Kohn, I had memories like those of the husband in the country song, "My Wife Ran Away With My Best Friend and I Still Miss Him a Lot."
1989.chinese: 你也许觉得这个道理显而易见，我却得吃过苦头才学会——事实上，还不止学了一遍。买下伯克希尔后不久，我通过一家叫多元零售的公司，收购了巴尔的摩的霍克希尔德·科恩百货；多元零售后来并入伯克希尔。买价比账面价值低得多，人员一流，交易还附带一些额外好处：账上没有体现的房地产价值，以及相当可观的后进先出法（LIFO）存货储备。这还能失手吗？结——果——三年后，能按大约原价卖掉，我已算走运。与霍克希尔德·科恩结束这段企业婚姻后，我的回忆，跟那首乡村歌曲里的丈夫差不多：“老婆跟我最好的朋友跑了，我至今还很想他。”

1989.english:
I could give you other personal examples of "bargain- purchase" folly but I'm sure you get the picture:  It's far better to buy a wonderful company at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price. Charlie understood this early; I was a slow learner. But now, when buying companies or common stocks, we look for first-class businesses accompanied by first- class managements.

o     That leads right into a related lesson: Good jockeys will do well on good horses, but not on broken-down nags. Both Berkshire's textile business and Hochschild, Kohn had able and honest people running them. The same managers employed in a business with good economic characteristics would have achieved fine records. But they were never going to make any progress while running in quicksand.
1989.chinese:
我还能再举些自己贪图“便宜买卖”而犯傻的例子，不过我想你已明白：以合理价格买一家优秀公司，远胜于以漂亮价格买一家一般公司。查理很早就懂了，我学得慢。但现在，无论买整家公司还是买普通股，我们都寻找由一流管理层经营的一流企业。

这直接引出另一个相关教训：好骑师骑好马能跑出成绩，骑衰弱不堪的老马就不行。伯克希尔的纺织业务和霍克希尔德·科恩，都由能干而诚实的人经营。同样的经理人，若在经济特性良好的企业任职，本会交出很好的成绩；可在流沙里奔跑，永远也前进不了。

1989.english:
I've said many times that when a management with a reputation for brilliance tackles a business with a reputation for bad economics, it is the reputation of the business that remains intact. I just wish I hadn't been so energetic in creating examples. My behavior has matched that admitted by  Mae West: "I was Snow White, but I drifted."

o     A further related lesson: Easy does it. After 25 years of buying and supervising a great variety of businesses, Charlie and I have not learned how to solve difficult business problems. What we have learned is to avoid them. To the extent we have been successful, it is because we concentrated on identifying one-foot hurdles that we could step over rather than because we acquired any ability to clear seven-footers.
1989.chinese:
我已说过很多次：一支以才华出众著称的管理层，遇上一家以经济特性恶劣著称的企业，最后声誉依旧的，通常是企业。我只盼自己当初别那么积极地制造例证。我的所作所为，倒与梅·韦斯特的自白相符：“我原本是白雪公主，后来走了样。”

另一个相关教训是：挑容易的做。查理和我买下并监督过各式各样的企业，25年下来，仍没学会怎样解决经营难题。我们学会的是避开它们。如果说取得了些成功，那是因为我们专注寻找一英尺高、抬脚就能跨过的栏杆，而不是练出了跨越七英尺高栏的本领。

1989.english: The finding may seem unfair, but in both business and investments it is usually far more profitable to simply stick with the easy and obvious than it is to resolve the difficult. On occasion, tough problems must be tackled as was the case when we started our Sunday paper in Buffalo. In other instances, a great investment opportunity occurs when a marvelous business encounters a one-time huge, but solvable, problem as was the case many years back at both American Express and GEICO. Overall, however, we've done better by avoiding dragons than by slaying them.
1989.chinese: 这个发现或许显得不公平，但在经营与投资中，守住那些简单明了的事，通常比解决难题赚钱得多。有时硬仗也非打不可，比如当年在布法罗创办周日版报纸。另一些时候，出色企业遇到一次性、巨大但可以解决的困难，便会出现极好的投资机会；多年前的美国运通和GEICO就是如此。不过，总体而言，我们靠避开恶龙取得的成绩，比靠屠龙更好。

1989.english: o     My most surprising discovery: the overwhelming importance in business of an unseen force that we might call "the institutional imperative." In business school, I was given no hint of the imperative's existence and I did not intuitively understand it when I entered the business world. I thought then that decent, intelligent, and experienced managers would automatically make rational business decisions. But I learned over time that isn't so. Instead, rationality frequently wilts when the institutional imperative comes into play.
1989.chinese: 最让我意外的发现，是企业里有一股看不见的力量，重要得惊人；不妨称它为“机构惯性”。在商学院，没人提示过我它的存在；刚进入商界时，我也没凭直觉理解它。我当时以为，正派、聪明又有经验的经理人，自然会作出理性经营决策。后来才渐渐明白，事实并非如此。机构惯性一旦发作，理性往往就蔫了。

1989.english: For example: (1) As if governed by Newton's First Law of Motion, an institution will resist any change in its current direction; (2) Just as work expands to fill available time, corporate projects or acquisitions will materialize to soak up available funds; (3) Any business craving of the leader, however foolish, will be quickly supported by detailed rate-of-return and strategic studies prepared by his troops; and (4) The behavior of peer companies, whether they are expanding, acquiring, setting executive compensation or whatever, will be mindlessly imitated.
1989.chinese: 比如：（1）组织仿佛受牛顿第一运动定律支配，会抗拒对现有方向的任何改变；（2）正如工作会膨胀到占满可用时间，公司项目或收购也会冒出来，吸干可用资金；（3）领导者在经营上有任何欲望，无论多么愚蠢，部下都会迅速备好详尽的回报率分析与战略研究，替它撑腰；（4）同行的做法，无论是扩张、收购、制定高管薪酬，还是别的什么，都会被不动脑筋地照搬。

1989.english:
Institutional dynamics, not venality or stupidity, set businesses on these courses, which are too often misguided. After making some expensive mistakes because I ignored the power of the imperative, I have tried to organize and manage Berkshire in ways that minimize its influence. Furthermore, Charlie and I have attempted to concentrate our investments in companies that appear alert to the problem.

o     After some other mistakes, I learned to go into business only with people whom I like, trust, and admire. As I noted before, this policy of itself will not ensure success: A second- class textile or department-store company won't prosper simply because its managers are men that you would be pleased to see your daughter marry. However, an owner - or investor - can accomplish wonders if he manages to associate himself with such people in businesses that possess decent economic characteristics. Conversely, we do not wish to join with managers who lack admirable qualities, no matter how attractive the prospects of their business. We've never succeeded in making a good deal with a bad person.
1989.chinese:
把企业推上这些往往错误道路的，是组织内部的作用力，并非贪腐或愚笨。由于忽略这股惯性的力量，我犯过一些代价高昂的错误；此后，我尽量以能把它的影响降到最低的方式，组织和管理伯克希尔。此外，查理和我也努力把投资集中于那些看来已对这个问题保持警觉的公司。

又犯过一些错误后，我学会只跟自己喜欢、信任并钦佩的人做生意。正如前面所说，光靠这条政策，并不能保证成功：一家二流的纺织或百货公司，不会仅仅因为经理人是你乐意让女儿嫁给的人，就兴旺起来。不过，所有者或投资者若能在经济特性不错的企业中，与这样的人合作，就可能创造非凡成绩。反过来，无论企业前景多诱人，我们都不愿跟缺乏可敬品质的经理人联手。我们从没能跟一个坏人做成一笔好交易。

1989.english: o     Some of my worst mistakes were not publicly visible. These were stock and business purchases whose virtues I understood and yet didn't make. It's no sin to miss a great opportunity outside one's area of competence. But I have passed on a couple of really big purchases that were served up to me on a platter and that I was fully capable of understanding. For Berkshire's shareholders, myself included, the cost of this thumb-sucking has been huge.
1989.chinese: 我最严重的一些错误，外人看不见。那是一些股票或企业，我明白购买的好处，却没有买。错过能力范围以外的好机会，并非罪过；可我错过的几笔真正的大买卖，已经端到面前，而且我完全有能力理解。对伯克希尔所有股东，包括我自己，这种含着拇指迟迟不动手的代价，实在巨大。

1989.english: o     Our consistently-conservative financial policies may appear to have been a mistake, but in my view were not. In retrospect, it is clear that significantly higher, though still conventional, leverage ratios at Berkshire would have produced considerably better returns on equity than the 23.8% we have actually averaged. Even in 1965, perhaps we could have judged there to be a 99% probability that higher leverage would lead to nothing but good. Correspondingly, we might have seen only a 1% chance that some shock factor, external or internal, would cause a conventional debt ratio to produce a result falling somewhere between temporary anguish and default.
1989.chinese: 我们一贯保守的财务政策，也许看上去是个错误，但我认为并不是。回头看，很明显，如果伯克希尔采用高得多、但仍属常规水平的杠杆率，股东权益回报就会显著高于实际平均的23.8%。即使在1965年，我们也许就能判断，加大杠杆有99%的概率只带来好处；相应地，某种内外冲击，使常规负债率带来从暂时苦恼到违约不等后果的概率，或许只有1%。

1989.english: We wouldn't have liked those 99:1 odds - and never will. A small chance of distress or disgrace cannot, in our view, be offset by a large chance of extra returns. If your actions are sensible, you are certain to get good results; in most such cases, leverage just moves things along faster. Charlie and I have never been in a big hurry: We enjoy the process far more than the proceeds - though we have learned to live with those also.
1989.chinese: 这种99比1的胜算，我们当时不会喜欢，以后也永远不会。在我们看来，陷入困境或声名受损的概率再小，也不能靠获得额外回报的高概率来抵消。如果行为明智，就一定能取得良好结果；多数情况下，杠杆只是把进程推快一点。查理和我从没那么着急：我们享受过程，远胜于所得——不过，对后者我们也已经学会适应了。

1989.english:
---

We hope in another 25 years to report on the mistakes of the first 50. If we are around in 2015 to do that, you can count on this section occupying many more pages than it does here.

Miscellaneous

We hope to buy more businesses that are similar to the ones we have, and we can use some help. If you have a business that fits the following criteria, call me or, preferably, write.
1989.chinese:
* * * * * * * * * * * *

希望再过25年，我们还能汇报头50年的错误。如果2015年我们还在，能够写这份报告，你尽可放心：这一节的页数，会比眼下多得多。

## 其他事项

我们希望再买一些与现有企业相似的公司，也需要你帮忙。如果你拥有符合以下标准的企业，请打电话给我，最好来信。

1989.english:
Here's what we're looking for:

(1)  Large purchases (at least $10 million of after-tax earnings),

(2)  demonstrated consistent earning power (future projections are of little interest to us, nor are "turnaround" situations),

(3)  businesses earning good returns on equity while employing little or no debt,

(4)  management in place (we can't supply it),

(5)  simple businesses (if there's lots of technology, we won't understand it),

(6)  an offering price  (we don't want to waste our time or that of the seller by talking,  even  preliminarily, about a transaction when price is unknown).
1989.chinese:
我们寻找的是：

（1）规模较大的收购：税后利润至少1000万美元；

（2）已证明持续而稳定的盈利能力：我们对未来预测没多大兴趣，对“扭亏为盈”的情形也一样；

（3）很少负债或没有负债，却能取得良好股东权益回报的企业；

（4）已有到位的管理层：我们无法提供；

（5）简单的生意：技术成分太多，我们就看不懂；

（6）有明确的报价：价格都不知道，就来讨论交易，即使只是初步接触，我们也不愿浪费自己或卖方的时间。

1989.english:
We will not engage in unfriendly takeovers. We can promise complete confidentiality and a very fast answer - customarily within five minutes - as to whether we're interested. We prefer to buy for cash, but will consider issuing stock when we receive as much in intrinsic business value as we give.

Our favorite form of purchase is one fitting the Blumkin- Friedman-Heldman mold. In cases like these, the company's owner- managers wish to generate significant amounts of cash, sometimes for themselves, but often for their families or inactive shareholders. At the same time, these managers wish to remain significant owners who continue to run their companies just as they have in the past. We think we offer a particularly good fit for owners with such objectives. We invite potential sellers to check us out by contacting people with whom we have done business in the past.
1989.chinese:
我们不做敌意收购。可以保证完全保密，并很快答复是否有兴趣，通常五分钟内就能回答。我们更喜欢现金收购；但如果换回的企业内在价值，不少于交出去的价值，也会考虑发行股票。

我们最喜欢布卢姆金—弗里德曼—赫尔德曼这一类收购。在这类交易里，企业的所有者兼经理人希望变现一大笔钱，有时是为自己，但更多时候是为家人或不参与经营的股东。同时，他们希望继续持有可观股权，照过去的方式管理公司。对怀有这种目标的所有者，我们认为自己尤其合适。我们欢迎有意出售者，向过去与我们做过生意的人打听我们的情况。

1989.english:
Charlie and I frequently get approached about acquisitions that don't come close to meeting our tests:  We've found that if you advertise an interest in buying collies, a lot of people will call hoping to sell you their cocker spaniels. Our interest in new ventures, turnarounds, or auction-like sales can best be expressed by a Goldwynism: "Please include me out."

Besides being interested in the purchase of businesses as described above, we are also interested in the negotiated purchase of large, but not controlling, blocks of stock comparable to those we hold in Capital Cities, Salomon, Gillette, USAir and Champion. Last year we said we had a special interest in large purchases of convertible preferreds. We still have an appetite of that kind, but it is limited since we now are close to the maximum position we feel appropriate for this category of investment.
1989.chinese:
查理和我常接到收购建议，离我们的标准却差得很远。我们发现，只要登广告说想买柯利牧羊犬，就会有许多人打电话来，希望卖给你可卡犬。至于新创企业、困境反转，或拍卖式出售，我们的兴趣，最好用一句戈德温式妙语表达：“请把我列入不参加名单。”

除了上述企业收购，我们也愿通过协商，买入大笔但不取得控制权的股份，类似我们在大都会、所罗门、吉列、全美航空及冠军国际的持仓。去年说过，我们特别有兴趣大笔买入可转换优先股。现在胃口仍在，但有限，因为这类投资已接近我们认为合适的最大持仓水平。

1989.english:
---

Two years ago, I told you about Harry Bottle, who in 1962 quickly cured a major business mess at the first industrial company I controlled, Dempster Mill Manufacturing (one of my "bargain" purchases) and who 24 years later had reappeared to again rescue me, this time from problems at K&W Products, a small Berkshire subsidiary that produces automotive compounds. As I reported, in short order Harry reduced capital employed at K&W, rationalized production, cut costs, and quadrupled profits. You might think he would then have paused for breath. But last year Harry, now 70, attended a bankruptcy auction and, for a pittance, acquired a product line that is a natural for K&W. That company's profitability may well be increased 50% by this coup. Watch this space for future bulletins on Harry's triumphs.
1989.chinese:
* * * * * * * * * * * *

两年前，我向你介绍过哈里·博特尔。1962年，他迅速收拾了我第一家控股工业企业邓普斯特磨坊制造公司的经营烂摊子；这也是我一笔“便宜买卖”。24年后，他又出现来救我，这次是伯克希尔一家制造汽车化学制剂的小子公司K&W Products出了问题。如我当时所说，哈里很快减少了K&W占用的资本，调整生产、削减成本，使利润增至四倍。你也许以为，接下来他总该喘口气了。但去年，已70岁的哈里参加了一场破产拍卖，花极少的钱买下一条与K&W天作之合的产品线。这一妙招，很可能让公司盈利再提高50%。请继续留意本栏，等候哈里今后捷报。

1989.english:
---

With more than a year behind him of trading Berkshire's stock on the New York Stock Exchange, our specialist, Jim Maguire of Henderson Brothers, Inc. ("HBI"), continues his outstanding performance. Before we listed, dealer spreads often were 3% or more of market price. Jim has maintained the spread at 50 points or less, which at current prices is well under 1%. Shareholders who buy or sell benefit significantly from this reduction in transaction costs.
1989.chinese:
* * * * * * * * * * * *

伯克希尔股票在纽约证券交易所交易已超过一年，亨德森兄弟公司（HBI）负责我们股票的专营交易商吉姆·马圭尔，表现继续出色。上市以前，交易商买卖价差往往达到市价的3%或更高。吉姆把价差维持在50点或以下，按现价算，远低于1%。交易成本下降，使买卖股票的股东大受裨益。

1989.english:
Because we are delighted by our experience with Jim, HBI and the NYSE, I said as much in ads that have been run in a series placed by the NYSE. Normally I shun testimonials, but I was pleased in this instance to publicly compliment the Exchange.

---

Last summer we sold the corporate jet that we purchased for $850,000 three years ago and bought another used jet for $6.7 million. Those of you who recall the mathematics of the multiplying bacteria on page 5 will understandably panic: If our net worth continues to increase at current rates, and the cost of replacing planes also continues to rise at the now-established rate of 100% compounded annually, it will not be long before Berkshire's entire net worth is consumed by its jet.
1989.chinese:
我们与吉姆、HBI及纽约证券交易所合作十分愉快，因此在交易所刊登的一系列广告中，我也公开说出了这番评价。通常我不做这类推荐，但这一次，我很乐意公开称赞交易所。

* * * * * * * * * * * *

去年夏天，我们卖掉三年前花85万美元买的公务喷气机，又花670万美元买了一架二手喷气机。记得第5页细菌繁殖算术的读者，想必会惊慌，这是可以理解的：如果净资产继续按目前速度增长，而换飞机的费用也继续按如今已经确立的年复合100%速度上升，用不了多久，伯克希尔全部净资产就会被这架飞机吃光。

1989.english: Charlie doesn't like it when I equate the jet with bacteria; he feels it's degrading to the bacteria. His idea of traveling in style is an air-conditioned bus, a luxury he steps up to only when bargain fares are in effect. My own attitude toward the jet can be summarized by the prayer attributed, apocryphally I'm sure, to St. Augustine as he contemplated leaving a life of secular pleasures to become a priest. Battling the conflict between intellect and glands, he pled: "Help me, Oh Lord, to become chaste - but not yet."
1989.chinese: 查理不喜欢我把飞机比作细菌；他觉得那是侮辱细菌。在他看来，坐带空调的大巴就算体面旅行，而这种奢侈，他也只在票价打折时才舍得享用。至于我对飞机的态度，可以借用据说出自圣奥古斯丁的一句祷告概括——我敢肯定，出处是附会的。相传，他正考虑放弃尘世享乐，去当神父；理智与欲望交战之际，他恳求道：“主啊，请助我守贞——不过先别急。”

1989.english:
Naming the plane has not been easy. I initially suggested "The Charles T. Munger." Charlie countered with "The Aberration." We finally settled on "The Indefensible."

---

About 96.9% of all eligible shares participated in Berkshire's 1989 shareholder-designated contributions program. Contributions made through the program were $5.9 million, and 2,550 charities were recipients.

We urge new shareholders to read the description of our shareholder-designated contributions program that appears on pages 52-53. If you wish to participate in future programs, we strongly urge that you immediately make sure your shares are registered in the name of the actual owner, not in the nominee name of a broker, bank or depository. Shares not so registered on August 31, 1990 will be ineligible for the 1990 program.
1989.chinese:
给飞机取名并不容易。我起初建议叫“查尔斯·T·芒格号”；查理反提议叫“脱轨号”。最后，我们定为“无可辩护号”。

* * * * * * * * * * * *

约96.9%的合资格股份，参加了伯克希尔1989年的股东指定捐赠计划。经该计划捐出590万美元，受益的慈善机构有2550家。

我们请新股东阅读第52—53页对股东指定捐赠计划的说明。如果你想参加未来的计划，我们强烈建议立即确认：股份登记在实际所有者名下，而非经纪商、银行或托管机构的代名账户下。1990年8月31日仍未按此登记的股份，将无资格参加1990年的计划。

1989.english:
---

The annual meeting this year will take place at 9:30 a.m. on Monday, April 30, 1990. Attendance grew last year to about 1,000, very close to the seating capacity of the Witherspoon Hall at Joslyn Museum. So this year's meeting will be moved to the Orpheum Theatre, which is in downtown Omaha, about one-quarter of a mile from the Red Lion Hotel. The Radisson-Redick Tower, a much smaller but nice hotel, is located across the street from the Orpheum. Or you may wish to stay at the Marriott, which is in west Omaha, about 100 yards from Borsheim's. We will have buses at the Marriott that will leave at 8:30 and 8:45 for the meeting and return after it ends.
1989.chinese:
* * * * * * * * * * * *

今年股东年会定于1990年4月30日星期一上午9:30举行。去年出席人数增至约1000人，已非常接近乔斯林博物馆威瑟斯庞大厅的座位上限。因此，今年改在奥马哈市中心的奥菲姆剧院举行，距红狮酒店约四分之一英里。丽笙雷迪克塔酒店规模小得多，但不错，就在剧院街对面。你也可以住西奥马哈的万豪酒店，距波仙珠宝约100码。我们会安排大巴从万豪酒店于上午8:30及8:45发车，前往会场，会议结束后返回。

1989.english:
Charlie and I always enjoy the meeting, and we hope you can make it. The quality of our shareholders is reflected in the quality of the questions we get: We have never attended an annual meeting anywhere that features such a consistently high level of intelligent, owner-related questions.

An attachment to our proxy material explains how you can obtain the card you will need for admission to the meeting. Because weekday parking can be tight around the Orpheum, we have lined up a number of nearby lots for our shareholders to use. The attachment also contains information about them.
1989.chinese:
查理和我总是很享受年会，希望你能来。我们收到的问题质量，体现着股东的素质：我们从没在其他地方参加过一场年会，能如此始终如一地提出高水平、从所有者角度出发的明智问题。

委托投票材料的附件，会说明如何领取参加年会所需的入场证。工作日剧院附近停车可能紧张，因此我们已为股东联系好附近几处停车场；附件也提供相关信息。

1989.english: As usual, we will have buses to take you to Nebraska Furniture Mart and Borsheim's after the meeting and to take you to downtown hotels or to the airport later. I hope that you will allow plenty of time to fully explore the attractions of both stores. Those of you arriving early can visit the Furniture Mart any day of the week; it is open from 10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. on Saturdays, and from noon to 5:30 p.m. on Sundays.
1989.chinese: 照惯例，年会后会有大巴送你到内布拉斯加家具卖场及波仙珠宝，稍后再送往市中心酒店或机场。希望你留出充裕时间，充分逛逛两家店。提前抵达的股东，一周任何一天都可到家具卖场；周六营业时间为上午10:00至下午5:30，周日为中午12:00至下午5:30。

1989.english:
Borsheim's normally is closed on Sunday, but we will open for shareholders and their guests from noon to 6 p.m. on Sunday, April 29th. Ike likes to put on a show, and you can rely on him to produce something very special for our shareholders.

In this letter we've had a lot to say about rates of compounding. If you can bear having your own rate turn negative for a day - not a pretty thought, I admit - visit Ike on the 29th.

Warren E. Buffett March 2, 1990                           Chairman of the Board
1989.chinese:
波仙珠宝通常周日不营业，不过4月29日星期日，会为股东及来宾开放，时间从中午12:00到下午6:00。艾克喜欢办得热闹，你尽可相信，他一定会为股东准备一些特别的东西。

这封信里，我们谈了不少复利增长率。如果你能忍受自己的增长率有一天变成负数——我承认，这念头不怎么美妙——就请29日去找艾克。

沃伦·E·巴菲特  
董事长  
1990年3月2日

1990.english:
BERKSHIRE HATHAWAY INC.

To the Shareholders of Berkshire Hathaway Inc.:

Last year we made a prediction: "A reduction [in Berkshire's net worth] is almost certain in at least one of the next three years." During much of 1990's second half, we were on the road to quickly proving that forecast accurate. But some strengthening in stock prices late in the year enabled us to close 1990 with net worth up by $362 million, or 7.3%. Over the last 26 years (that is, since present management took over) our per-share book value has grown from $19.46 to $4,612.06, or at a rate of 23.2% compounded annually.
1990.chinese:
伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司

致伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司的股东：

去年，我们作过一个预测：“未来三年中至少有一年，伯克希尔净资产下降，几乎是肯定的。”1990年下半年大部分时间，我们都在迅速证明这个预测准确的路上。不过，年末股价有所回升，让1990年收官时，净资产仍增加了3.62亿美元，增幅7.3%。过去26年，也就是现任管理层接手以来，每股账面价值从19.46美元增至4,612.06美元，年复合增长率为23.2%。

1990.english: Our growth rate was lackluster in 1990 because our four major common stock holdings, in aggregate, showed little change in market value. Last year I told you that though these companies - Capital Cities/ABC, Coca-Cola, GEICO, and Washington Post - had fine businesses and superb managements, widespread recognition of these attributes had pushed the stock prices of the four to lofty levels. The market prices of the two media companies have since fallen significantly - for good reasons relating to evolutionary industry developments that I will discuss later - and the price of Coca-Cola stock has increased significantly for what I also believe are good reasons. Overall, yearend 1990 prices of our "permanent four," though far from enticing, were a bit more appealing than they were a year earlier.
1990.chinese: 1990年增长平平，是因为四项主要普通股持仓的总市值几乎没变。去年我说过，虽然这四家公司——大都会／美国广播公司、可口可乐、GEICO及华盛顿邮报——业务出色、管理层卓越，但这些优点已获广泛认识，把股价推到了很高的水平。此后，两家媒体公司的股价大幅下跌，我认为原因充分，涉及行业逐步发生的变化，稍后会谈。可口可乐股价则大幅上涨，我也认为理由充分。总体而言，1990年末，我们“永久四强”的价格，虽远谈不上诱人，还是比一年前略有吸引力。

1990.english:
Berkshire's 26-year record is meaningless in forecasting future results; so also, we hope, is the one-year record. We continue to aim for a 15% average annual gain in intrinsic value. But, as we never tire of telling you, this goal becomes ever more difficult to reach as our equity base, now $5.3 billion, increases.

If we do attain that 15% average, our shareholders should fare well. However, Berkshire's corporate gains will produce an identical gain for a specific shareholder only if he eventually sells his shares at the same relationship to intrinsic value that existed when he bought them. For example, if you buy at a 10% premium to intrinsic value; if intrinsic value subsequently grows at 15% a year; and if you then sell at a 10% premium, your own return will correspondingly be 15% compounded. (The calculation assumes that no dividends are paid.) If, however, you buy at a premium and sell at a smaller premium, your results will be somewhat inferior to those achieved by the company.
1990.chinese:
伯克希尔26年的记录，对预测未来毫无意义；我们也希望，一年的记录同样如此。我们仍以每年平均增长15%的内在价值为目标。但正如我们不厌其烦告诉各位的，随着股权资本基数扩大——如今已达53亿美元——这个目标只会越来越难实现。

如果真能平均达到15%，股东的结果应该不错。不过，某位股东所得的收益，要与伯克希尔自身的增长完全一样，必须满足一个条件：最终卖出时，股价相对于内在价值的关系，与买入时相同。比如，你按高于内在价值10%的价格买入；随后内在价值每年增长15%；最后仍按10%溢价卖出，那么个人回报也相应是年复合15%。（计算假设没有分红。）但如果买入有溢价，卖出时溢价缩小，个人结果就会略逊于公司的成绩。

1990.english: Ideally, the results of every Berkshire shareholder would closely mirror those of the company during his period of ownership. That is why Charlie Munger, Berkshire's Vice Chairman and my partner, and I hope for Berkshire to sell consistently at about intrinsic value. We prefer such steadiness to the value-ignoring volatility of the past two years: In 1989 intrinsic value grew less than did book value, which was up 44%, while the market price rose 85%; in 1990 book value and intrinsic value increased by a small amount, while the market price fell 23%.
1990.chinese: 理想情况下，每位伯克希尔股东在持有期间的成绩，都应紧随公司的成绩。因此，伯克希尔副董事长、我的搭档查理·芒格和我，希望股价能始终保持在内在价值附近。我们更喜欢这种稳定，而非过去两年那种无视价值的波动：1989年，内在价值增长低于账面价值44%的增幅，股价却上涨85%；1990年，账面价值与内在价值仅略有增加，股价却下跌23%。

1990.english:
Berkshire's intrinsic value continues to exceed book value by a substantial margin. We can't tell you the exact differential because intrinsic value is necessarily an estimate; Charlie and I might, in fact, differ by 10% in our appraisals. We do know, however, that we own some exceptional businesses that are worth considerably more than the values at which they are carried on our books.

Much of the extra value that exists in our businesses has been created by the managers now running them. Charlie and I feel free to brag about this group because we had nothing to do with developing the skills they possess: These superstars just came that way. Our job is merely to identify talented managers and provide an environment in which they can do their stuff. Having done it, they send their cash to headquarters and we face our only other task: the intelligent deployment of these funds.
1990.chinese:
伯克希尔的内在价值，仍大幅超过账面价值。确切差额无法告诉各位，因为内在价值必然只是估计；实际上，查理和我的评估可能相差10%。不过，我们知道，手中有些非凡企业，价值远高于账面列示金额。

企业中许多额外价值，是由现任经理人创造的。查理和我尽可为这群人夸口，因为他们的本领并非我们培养：这些超级明星来时就这么出色。我们的工作，只是找出有才干的经理人，提供让他们施展本领的环境。事成之后，他们把现金送回总部，我们就面对唯一的另一项任务：明智地配置这些资金。

1990.english:
My own role in operations may best be illustrated by a small tale concerning my granddaughter, Emily, and her fourth birthday party last fall. Attending were other children, adoring relatives, and Beemer the Clown, a local entertainer who includes magic tricks in his act.

Beginning these, Beemer asked Emily to help him by waving a "magic wand" over "the box of wonders." Green handkerchiefs went into the box, Emily waved the wand, and Beemer removed blue ones. Loose handkerchiefs went in and, upon a magisterial wave by Emily, emerged knotted. After four such transformations, each more amazing than its predecessor, Emily was unable to contain herself. Her face aglow, she exulted: "Gee, I'm really good at this."
1990.chinese:
我在经营中的作用，或许可以用去年秋天孙女艾米莉四岁生日聚会的一件小事说明。参加聚会的，有其他孩子、疼爱她的亲属，还有当地艺人“小丑比默”；他的表演包括魔术。

开始变魔术时，比默请艾米莉帮忙，在“奇妙箱”上挥动“魔杖”。放进去的是绿手帕，艾米莉挥一下，拿出来就成了蓝手帕；放进去的是散开的手帕，她威风凛凛一挥，拿出来便打了结。连续四次变化，一次比一次神奇，艾米莉终于忍不住了。她满脸放光，欢呼道：“哇，我干这个还真厉害！”

1990.english:
And that sums up my contribution to the performance of Berkshire's business magicians - the Blumkins, the Friedman family, Mike Goldberg, the Heldmans, Chuck Huggins, Stan Lipsey and Ralph Schey. They deserve your applause.

## Sources of Reported Earnings

The table below shows the major sources of Berkshire's reported earnings. In this presentation, amortization of Goodwill and other major purchase-price accounting adjustments are not charged against the specific businesses to which they apply, but are instead aggregated and shown separately. This procedure lets you view the earnings of our businesses as they would have been reported had we not purchased them. I've explained in past reports why this form of presentation seems to us to be more useful to investors and managers than one utilizing generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), which require purchase-price adjustments to be made on a business-by-business basis. The total net earnings we show in the table are, of course, identical to the GAAP total in our audited financial statements.
