| 5,000,000 | 富国银行（Wells Fargo & Company） | 289,431 | 289,375 |

1990.english:
Lethargy bordering on sloth remains the cornerstone of our investment style: This year we neither bought nor sold a share of five of our six major holdings. The exception was Wells Fargo, a superbly-managed, high-return banking operation in which we increased our ownership to just under 10%, the most we can own without the approval of the Federal Reserve Board. About one-sixth of our position was bought in 1989, the rest in 1990.

The banking business is no favorite of ours. When assets are twenty times equity - a common ratio in this industry - mistakes that involve only a small portion of assets can destroy a major portion of equity. And mistakes have been the rule rather than the exception at many major banks. Most have resulted from a managerial failing that we described last year when discussing the "institutional imperative:" the tendency of executives to mindlessly imitate the behavior of their peers, no matter how foolish it may be to do so. In their lending, many bankers played follow-the-leader with lemming-like zeal; now they are experiencing a lemming-like fate.
1990.chinese:
接近懒惰的迟缓，仍是我们投资风格的基石：六项主要持仓中，五项今年一股未买、一股未卖。例外是富国银行，一家管理出色、回报很高的银行；我们把持股增至略低于10%，即未经美联储理事会批准可持有的最高水平。现有持仓约六分之一在1989年买入，其余在1990年。

银行业并非我们的偏爱。资产达到股权资本二十倍，是行业常见比例；只涉及一小部分资产的错误，就能毁掉很大一部分股本。许多大银行犯错是常态，而非例外。大多数错误，源于去年谈“机构惯性”时说过的管理缺陷：高管不动脑筋地模仿同业，哪怕这样做再愚蠢。放贷时，许多银行家像旅鼠一样狂热地跟着领头者跑；现在，他们正遭遇旅鼠般的命运。

1990.english:
Because leverage of 20:1 magnifies the effects of managerial strengths and weaknesses, we have no interest in purchasing shares of a poorly-managed bank at a "cheap" price. Instead, our only interest is in buying into well-managed banks at fair prices.

With Wells Fargo, we think we have obtained the best managers in the business, Carl Reichardt and Paul Hazen. In many ways the combination of Carl and Paul reminds me of another - Tom Murphy and Dan Burke at Capital Cities/ABC. First, each pair is stronger than the sum of its parts because each partner understands, trusts and admires the other. Second, both managerial teams pay able people well, but abhor having a bigger head count than is needed. Third, both attack costs as vigorously when profits are at record levels as when they are under pressure. Finally, both stick with what they understand and let their abilities, not their egos, determine what they attempt. (Thomas J. Watson Sr. of IBM followed the same rule: "I'm no genius," he said. "I'm smart in spots - but I stay around those spots.")
1990.chinese:
由于20∶1的杠杆，会放大管理的长处与弱点，我们对按“便宜”价买管理糟糕的银行毫无兴趣。唯一有兴趣的，是按合理价买管理良好的银行。

富国银行让我们觉得，得到了业内最好的经理人卡尔·赖克特和保罗·黑曾。他们让我在许多方面想起另一对搭档：大都会／美国广播公司的汤姆·墨菲和丹·伯克。第一，每对组合都强于两人简单相加，因为彼此理解、信任且钦佩。第二，两组都厚待能人，却厌恶员工超过实际所需。第三，无论利润创纪录还是承压，都同样有力地削减成本。最后，都守住自己懂的事，让能力而非自尊决定尝试什么。（IBM的老托马斯·J·沃森也遵循这个原则：“我不是天才。我只在某些地方聪明，而我就待在那些地方。”）

1990.english: Our purchases of Wells Fargo in 1990 were helped by a chaotic market in bank stocks. The disarray was appropriate: Month by month the foolish loan decisions of once well-regarded banks were put on public display. As one huge loss after another was unveiled - often on the heels of managerial assurances that all was well - investors understandably concluded that no bank's numbers were to be trusted. Aided by their flight from bank stocks, we purchased our 10% interest in Wells Fargo for $290 million, less than five times after-tax earnings, and less than three times pre-tax earnings.
1990.chinese: 1990年买富国，银行股市场的混乱帮了忙。这种混乱有其道理：一度备受推崇的银行，其愚蠢放贷决定，一月又一月摆到公众面前。一笔又一笔巨亏曝光，往往紧跟在管理层保证一切安好之后；投资者因而认为，任何银行数字都不可信，这可以理解。借助他们逃离银行股的机会，我们以2.90亿美元买得富国约10%股权，不到税后利润五倍，也不到税前利润三倍。

1990.english: Wells Fargo is big - it has $56 billion in assets - and has been earning more than 20% on equity and 1.25% on assets. Our purchase of one-tenth of the bank may be thought of as roughly equivalent to our buying 100% of a $5 billion bank with identical financial characteristics. But were we to make such a purchase, we would have to pay about twice the $290 million we paid for Wells Fargo. Moreover, that $5 billion bank, commanding a premium price, would present us with another problem: We would not be able to find a Carl Reichardt to run it. In recent years, Wells Fargo executives have been more avidly recruited than any others in the banking business; no one, however, has been able to hire the dean.
1990.chinese: 富国很大，资产560亿美元；股东权益回报一直超过20%，资产回报为1.25%。买下十分之一，大致相当于买一家财务特性相同、资产50亿美元银行的全部股权。但如果真作那样的收购，所付约为这2.90亿美元的两倍。而且，那家须付溢价的50亿美元银行，还会有个问题：找不到卡尔·赖克特来经营。近几年，富国高管被挖角的热度，超过其他银行，但没人挖得走这位掌门人。

1990.english: Of course, ownership of a bank - or about any other business - is far from riskless. California banks face the specific risk of a major earthquake, which might wreak enough havoc on borrowers to in turn destroy the banks lending to them. A second risk is systemic - the possibility of a business contraction or financial panic so severe that it would endanger almost every highly-leveraged institution, no matter how intelligently run. Finally, the market's major fear of the moment is that West Coast real estate values will tumble because of overbuilding and deliver huge losses to banks that have financed the expansion. Because it is a leading real estate lender, Wells Fargo is thought to be particularly vulnerable.
1990.chinese: 当然，拥有银行或几乎任何企业，都远非毫无风险。加州银行有大地震这种特定风险，地震可能重创借款人，进而毁掉放贷银行。第二是系统性风险：经济收缩或金融恐慌严重到危及几乎所有高杠杆机构，无论经营多聪明。最后，市场眼下最怕的是西海岸房地产过度建设，价格崩跌，令为扩张融资的银行巨亏。富国是主要房地产贷款人，因此被认为尤其脆弱。

1990.english: None of these eventualities can be ruled out. The probability of the first two occurring, however, is low and even a meaningful drop in real estate values is unlikely to cause major problems for well-managed institutions. Consider some mathematics: Wells Fargo currently earns well over $1 billion pre-tax annually after expensing more than $300 million for loan losses. If 10% of all $48 billion of the bank's loans - not just its real estate loans - were hit by problems in 1991, and these produced losses (including foregone interest) averaging 30% of principal, the company would roughly break even.
1990.chinese: 这些情况都不能排除。不过，前两种概率很低；即使房地产明显下跌，也不大可能让管理良好的机构出大问题。算一算：富国目前每年已扣除超过3亿美元贷款损失费用后，税前仍赚远超10亿美元。假如1991年全部480亿美元贷款，不只是房地产贷款，有10%出问题，损失连同放弃的利息平均为本金的30%，公司仍大致能盈亏平衡。

1990.english: A year like that - which we consider only a low-level possibility, not a likelihood - would not distress us. In fact, at Berkshire we would love to acquire businesses or invest in capital projects that produced no return for a year, but that could then be expected to earn 20% on growing equity. Nevertheless, fears of a California real estate disaster similar to that experienced in New England caused the price of Wells Fargo stock to fall almost 50% within a few months during 1990. Even though we had bought some shares at the prices prevailing before the fall, we welcomed the decline because it allowed us to pick up many more shares at the new, panic prices.
1990.chinese: 这样的年份，我们认为只是小概率可能，并非很可能发生；即使出现，也不会不安。实际上，伯克希尔很愿收购某些企业或投资资本项目，哪怕一年没有回报，只要随后预期能在不断增长的股本上赚20%。然而，对加州发生类似新英格兰房地产灾难的恐惧，使富国股价在1990年几个月里跌近50%。虽然我们已按下跌前价格买过一些，仍欢迎下跌，因为可以按恐慌后的新价格多买许多。

1990.english: Investors who expect to be ongoing buyers of investments throughout their lifetimes should adopt a similar attitude toward market fluctuations; instead many illogically become euphoric when stock prices rise and unhappy when they fall. They show no such confusion in their reaction to food prices: Knowing they are forever going to be buyers of food, they welcome falling prices and deplore price increases. (It's the seller of food who doesn't like declining prices.) Similarly, at the Buffalo News we would cheer lower prices for newsprint - even though it would mean marking down the value of the large inventory of newsprint we always keep on hand - because we know we are going to be perpetually buying the product.
1990.chinese: 预计终生不断买入投资的人，也应这样看市场波动；但许多人毫无道理地涨时狂喜，跌时不快。对食品价格，他们却没这样糊涂：知道自己永远要买食品，就欢迎降价、痛恨涨价。（不喜欢降价的是食品卖家。）同理，布法罗新闻报会为新闻纸降价欢呼，即使必须调低常备大批存货的价值，因为知道自己会不断购买。

1990.english:
Identical reasoning guides our thinking about Berkshire's investments. We will be buying businesses - or small parts of businesses, called stocks - year in, year out as long as I live (and longer, if Berkshire's directors attend the seances I have scheduled). Given these intentions, declining prices for businesses benefit us, and rising prices hurt us.

The most common cause of low prices is pessimism - some times pervasive, some times specific to a company or industry. We want to do business in such an environment, not because we like pessimism but because we like the prices it produces. It's optimism that is the enemy of the rational buyer.
1990.chinese:
同样的道理指导伯克希尔投资。只要我还活着，每年都会买企业，或称为股票的企业小部分；如果董事们参加我已安排好的降灵会，死后也会继续。既然打算如此，企业价格下降对我们有益，上涨反而有害。

低价最常见的原因是悲观，有时弥漫全市场，有时针对某公司或行业。我们想在这种环境中做买卖，不是喜欢悲观，而是喜欢它带来的价格。乐观，才是理性买方的敌人。

1990.english:
None of this means, however, that a business or stock is an intelligent purchase simply because it is unpopular; a contrarian approach is just as foolish as a follow-the-crowd strategy. What's required is thinking rather than polling. Unfortunately, Bertrand Russell's observation about life in general applies with unusual force in the financial world: "Most men would rather die than think. Many do."

---

Our other major portfolio change last year was large additions to our holdings of RJR Nabisco bonds, securities that we first bought in late 1989. At yearend 1990 we had $440 million invested in these securities, an amount that approximated market value. (As I write this, however, their market value has risen by more than $150 million.)
1990.chinese:
不过，这绝非说，只因不受欢迎，某企业或股票就值得明智地买入；单靠逆向行事的办法，与随大流同样愚蠢。需要的是思考，不是民意调查。遗憾的是，伯特兰·罗素对一般人生的观察，在金融界格外适用：“多数人宁愿死，也不愿思考。许多人确实如此。”

* * * * * * * * * * * *

去年，投资组合另一主要变化，是大幅增持RJR纳贝斯克债券，我们在1989年末首次买入。1990年底，投入达4.40亿美元，与市值大致相同。（不过，写这封信时，市值已上涨超过1.50亿美元。）

1990.english: Just as buying into the banking business is unusual for us, so is the purchase of below-investment-grade bonds. But opportunities that interest us and that are also large enough to have a worthwhile impact on Berkshire's results are rare. Therefore, we will look at any category of investment, so long as we understand the business we're buying into and believe that price and value may differ significantly. (Woody Allen, in another context, pointed out the advantage of open-mindedness: "I can't understand why more people aren't bi-sexual because it doubles your chances for a date on Saturday night.")
1990.chinese: 正如买银行不常见，买低于投资级的债券，对我们也不常见。但既让我们有兴趣、规模又足以对伯克希尔成绩产生有意义影响的机会，很少。因此，只要懂得所买的企业，并相信价格与价值可能显著不同，任何投资类别都会考虑。（伍迪·艾伦在另一场合指出过开放心态的好处：“我不明白为什么没有更多人是双性恋，那样周六晚上约到人的机会就翻倍了。”）

1990.english:
In the past we have bought a few below-investment-grade bonds with success, though these were all old-fashioned "fallen angels" - bonds that were initially of investment grade but that were downgraded when the issuers fell on bad times. In the 1984 annual report we described our rationale for buying one fallen angel, the Washington Public Power Supply System.

A kind of bastardized fallen angel burst onto the investment scene in the 1980s - "junk bonds" that were far below investment- grade when issued. As the decade progressed, new offerings of manufactured junk became ever junkier and ultimately the predictable outcome occurred: Junk bonds lived up to their name. In 1990 - even before the recession dealt its blows - the financial sky became dark with the bodies of failing corporations.
1990.chinese:
过去，我们成功买过少量低于投资级的债券，不过都是老式“堕落天使”：发行时原为投资级，发行人后来遭遇逆境，评级才被调低。1984年年报中，说明过买入华盛顿公共电力供应系统这只堕落天使的理由。

20世纪80年代，一种变了种的堕落天使冲进投资市场：“垃圾债券”，发行时就远低于投资级。随着十年过去，人造垃圾的新发品种越来越垃圾，预料中的结果终于出现：垃圾债券没有辜负自己的名字。1990年，甚至经济衰退还没开始打击，金融天空就已被倒下的公司尸体遮暗。

1990.english: The disciples of debt assured us that this collapse wouldn't happen: Huge debt, we were told, would cause operating managers to focus their efforts as never before, much as a dagger mounted on the steering wheel of a car could be expected to make its driver proceed with intensified care. We'll acknowledge that such an attention-getter would produce a very alert driver. But another certain consequence would be a deadly - and unnecessary - accident if the car hit even the tiniest pothole or sliver of ice. The roads of business are riddled with potholes; a plan that requires dodging them all is a plan for disaster.
1990.chinese: 债务的信徒向我们保证，崩塌不会发生。他们说，巨债会让经营经理人前所未有地专注，正如在汽车方向盘上装把匕首，驾驶人自然会开得格外小心。我们承认，这种提醒会让司机高度警觉。但另一项必然后果是：只要撞上最小的坑，或一小片冰，就会发生致命且完全没必要的事故。商业道路满是坑洼，要求全部躲开的计划，就是招灾计划。

1990.english:
In the final chapter of The Intelligent Investor Ben Graham forcefully rejected the dagger thesis: "Confronted with a challenge to distill the secret of sound investment into three words, we venture the motto, Margin of Safety." Forty-two years after reading that, I still think those are the right three words. The failure of investors to heed this simple message caused them staggering losses as the 1990s began.

At the height of the debt mania, capital structures were concocted that guaranteed failure: In some cases, so much debt was issued that even highly favorable business results could not produce the funds to service it. One particularly egregious "kill- 'em-at-birth" case a few years back involved the purchase of a mature television station in Tampa, bought with so much debt that the interest on it exceeded the station's gross revenues. Even if you assume that all labor, programs and services were donated rather than purchased, this capital structure required revenues to explode - or else the station was doomed to go broke. (Many of the bonds that financed the purchase were sold to now-failed savings and loan associations; as a taxpayer, you are picking up the tab for this folly.)
1990.chinese:
本·格雷厄姆在《聪明的投资者》最后一章，有力驳斥了匕首论：“若要把稳健投资的秘诀浓缩成三个词，我们愿提出这句格言：Margin of Safety——安全边际。”读过42年之后，我仍认为这三个英文词完全正确。投资者未听从这条简单信息，使他们在20世纪90年代开局便遭受惊人损失。

债务狂热顶峰时，设计出来的资本结构，简直保证失败。有些债务多到即使经营结果极其有利，也挣不出足够资金偿债。几年前，坦帕一家成熟电视台的收购，便是尤其离谱的“出生即扼杀”案例：举债多到利息超过电视台全部营业收入。即使假设全部劳务、节目和服务都是白送，不须购买，这种结构仍要求收入爆炸式增长，否则注定破产。（许多收购融资债券卖给了如今已倒闭的储蓄贷款机构；作为纳税人，你正在替这场愚行埋单。）

1990.english: All of this seems impossible now. When these misdeeds were done, however, dagger-selling investment bankers pointed to the "scholarly" research of academics, which reported that over the years the higher interest rates received from low-grade bonds had more than compensated for their higher rate of default. Thus, said the friendly salesmen, a diversified portfolio of junk bonds would produce greater net returns than would a portfolio of high-grade bonds. (Beware of past-performance "proofs" in finance: If history books were the key to riches, the Forbes 400 would consist of librarians.)
1990.chinese: 今天看，这一切似乎不可能。但作恶当时，贩卖匕首的投资银行家，拿出了学者们的“学术”研究：多年来，低等级债券较高的利息，足以补偿更高违约率，还绰绰有余。因此，这些友善的推销员说，分散投资垃圾债券，净回报会高于高等级债券组合。（当心金融领域那些以往绩作“证明”的说法：如果读历史书就能致富，《福布斯》400富豪榜上，该全是图书管理员。）

1990.english: There was a flaw in the salesmen's logic - one that a first- year student in statistics is taught to recognize. An assumption was being made that the universe of newly-minted junk bonds was identical to the universe of low-grade fallen angels and that, therefore, the default experience of the latter group was meaningful in predicting the default experience of the new issues. (That was an error similar to checking the historical death rate from Kool-Aid before drinking the version served at Jonestown.)
1990.chinese: 推销员逻辑有个漏洞，统计学一年级学生就该学会识别。他们假定，新造的垃圾债券总体，与低等级堕落天使的总体相同，因此后者违约经历，能够预测新发债券的违约经历。（这就像喝琼斯镇端出的那种Kool-Aid之前，先查普通Kool-Aid饮料历史上的死亡率。）

1990.english: The universes were of course dissimilar in several vital respects. For openers, the manager of a fallen angel almost invariably yearned to regain investment-grade status and worked toward that goal. The junk-bond operator was usually an entirely different breed. Behaving much as a heroin user might, he devoted his energies not to finding a cure for his debt-ridden condition, but rather to finding another fix. Additionally, the fiduciary sensitivities of the executives managing the typical fallen angel were often, though not always, more finely developed than were those of the junk-bond-issuing financiopath.
1990.chinese: 两类总体当然有几项至关重要的区别。首先，堕落天使的经理人，几乎总想重获投资级，并朝此努力；垃圾债券经营者通常完全是另一种人。他像海洛因吸食者一样，把精力用来再找一剂，而不是医治债台高筑的病。此外，典型堕落天使的高管，对受托责任的敏感度，往往虽非总是，也比发行垃圾债券的“金融病态者”发展得完善。

1990.english:
Wall Street cared little for such distinctions. As usual, the Street's enthusiasm for an idea was proportional not to its merit, but rather to the revenue it would produce. Mountains of junk bonds were sold by those who didn't care to those who didn't think - and there was no shortage of either.

Junk bonds remain a mine field, even at prices that today are often a small fraction of issue price. As we said last year, we have never bought a new issue of a junk bond. (The only time to buy these is on a day with no "y" in it.) We are, however, willing to look at the field, now that it is in disarray.
1990.chinese:
华尔街对这些区别不大在乎。照例，对一个主意的热情，与它的优点不成比例，却与能带来的收入成比例。成山垃圾债券，由不在乎的人，卖给不思考的人；两种人都不缺。

垃圾债券依然是雷区，即使如今价格往往只是发行价的一小部分。正如去年所说，我们从未买过新发垃圾债券。（唯一适合买入的日子，是英文名称中没有字母“y”的那一天。）不过，如今市场一团混乱，我们愿意看看这个领域。

1990.english:
In the case of RJR Nabisco, we feel the Company's credit is considerably better than was generally perceived for a while and that the yield we receive, as well as the potential for capital gain, more than compensates for the risk we incur (though that is far from nil). RJR has made asset sales at favorable prices, has added major amounts of equity, and in general is being run well.

However, as we survey the field, most low-grade bonds still look unattractive. The handiwork of the Wall Street of the 1980s is even worse than we had thought: Many important businesses have been mortally wounded. We will, though, keep looking for opportunities as the junk market continues to unravel.
1990.chinese:
就RJR纳贝斯克而言，我们认为信用状况，比一度普遍想象的好得多；利息收益加上潜在资本利得，足以补偿所冒风险还有余，虽然风险远非零。RJR以有利价格出售了资产，补充大量股本，总体经营良好。

不过，环顾全场，多数低等级债券仍无吸引力。20世纪80年代华尔街的手艺，比我们原先想象还糟：许多重要企业已受致命伤。但在垃圾债市场继续瓦解时，我们还会寻找机会。

1990.english:
## Convertible Preferred Stocks

We continue to hold the convertible preferred stocks described in earlier reports: $700 million of Salomon Inc, $600 million of The Gillette Company, $358 million of USAir Group, Inc. and $300 million of Champion International Corp. Our Gillette holdings will be converted into 12 million shares of common stock on April 1. Weighing interest rates, credit quality and prices of the related common stocks, we can assess our holdings in Salomon and Champion at yearend 1990 as worth about what we paid, Gillette as worth somewhat more, and USAir as worth substantially less.
1990.chinese:
## 可转换优先股

我们继续持有过去报告所述的可转换优先股：所罗门7亿美元、吉列6亿美元、全美航空3.58亿美元，以及冠军国际3亿美元。吉列持仓将在4月1日转换成1200万股普通股。综合利率、信用质量及相关普通股价格评估，1990年末，所罗门和冠军国际大约值买入价，吉列略高，全美航空则低得多。

1990.english: In making the USAir purchase, your Chairman displayed exquisite timing: I plunged into the business at almost the exact moment that it ran into severe problems. (No one pushed me; in tennis parlance, I committed an "unforced error.") The company's troubles were brought on both by industry conditions and by the post-merger difficulties it encountered in integrating Piedmont, an affliction I should have expected since almost all airline mergers have been followed by operational turmoil.
1990.chinese: 购买全美航空时，你们的董事长展现了精妙绝伦的时机把握：几乎就在企业陷入严重问题的那一刻，我一头扎了进去。（没人推我；用网球术语说，这是“非受迫性失误”。）困难既来自行业，也来自合并后整合皮埃蒙特航空的问题。后一项本该料到，因为几乎每次航空合并之后，都会有运营混乱。

1990.english: In short order, Ed Colodny and Seth Schofield resolved the second problem: The airline now gets excellent marks for service. Industry-wide problems have proved to be far more serious. Since our purchase, the economics of the airline industry have deteriorated at an alarming pace, accelerated by the kamikaze pricing tactics of certain carriers. The trouble this pricing has produced for all carriers illustrates an important truth: In a business selling a commodity-type product, it's impossible to be a lot smarter than your dumbest competitor.
1990.chinese: 埃德·科洛德尼和塞思·斯科菲尔德很快解决了第二项问题，如今服务评价出色。但全行业问题严重得多。买入以后，航空业经济状况以令人警觉的速度恶化，某些航空公司自杀式定价又推了一把。这些价格给全行业造成的麻烦，说明一个重要道理：销售同质商品的生意里，你不可能比最笨的对手聪明很多。

1990.english:
However, unless the industry is decimated during the next few years, our USAir investment should work out all right. Ed and Seth have decisively addressed the current turbulence by making major changes in operations. Even so, our investment is now less secure than at the time I made it.

Our convertible preferred stocks are relatively simple securities, yet I should warn you that, if the past is any guide, you may from time to time read inaccurate or misleading statements about them. Last year, for example, several members of the press calculated the value of all our preferreds as equal to that of the common stock into which they are convertible. By their logic, that is, our Salomon preferred, convertible into common at $38, would be worth 60% of face value if Salomon common were selling at $22.80. But there is a small problem with this line of reasoning: Using it, one must conclude that all of the value of a convertible preferred resides in the conversion privilege and that the value of a non-convertible preferred of Salomon would be zero, no matter what its coupon or terms for redemption.
1990.chinese:
不过，除非未来几年行业遭到严重摧残，全美航空投资应仍能有过得去的结果。埃德和塞思果断调整经营，处理当前颠簸。即便如此，投资如今的安全程度，已不及当初买入时。

我们的可转换优先股相对简单，但我得提醒：若过去可作参考，各位仍可能不时读到不准或误导性的说法。比如去年，几位新闻从业者把全部优先股，按可以转换得到的普通股价值计算。依此逻辑，所罗门普通股若卖22.80美元，按38美元转换的优先股，就只值面额60%。不过，这个推理有个小问题：必须由此断定，可转换优先股全部价值都来自转换权；而所罗门不可转换的优先股，不管股息率、赎回条件如何，都一文不值。

1990.english:
The point you should keep in mind is that most of the value of our convertible preferreds is derived from their fixed-income characteristics. That means the securities cannot be worth less than the value they would possess as non-convertible preferreds and may be worth more because of their conversion options.

---

I deeply regret having to end this section of the report with a note about my friend, Colman Mockler, Jr., CEO of Gillette, who died in January. No description better fitted Colman than "gentleman" - a word signifying integrity, courage and modesty. Couple these qualities with the humor and exceptional business ability that Colman possessed and you can understand why I thought it an undiluted pleasure to work with him and why I, and all others who knew him, will miss Colman so much.
1990.chinese:
各位应记住：我们的可转换优先股，大部分价值来自固定收益特征。这意味着，价值不会低于假如不可转换时的优先股价值，还可能因为转换选择权而更高。

* * * * * * * * * * * *

很遗憾，这一节不得不以一则有关朋友的消息结束：吉列首席执行官小科尔曼·莫克勒于1月去世。没有什么称谓比“绅士”更适合他，这个词意味着诚信、勇气和谦逊。再加上幽默及非凡经营才干，各位就能理解，与他共事为何是十足的乐事，以及我和所有认识他的人，为何如此怀念他。

1990.english: A few days before Colman died, Gillette was richly praised in a Forbes cover story. Its theme was simple: The company's success in shaving products has come not from marketing savvy (though it exhibits that talent repeatedly) but has instead resulted from its devotion to quality. This mind-set has caused it to consistently focus its energies on coming up with something better, even though its existing products already ranked as the class of the field. In so depicting Gillette, Forbes in fact painted a portrait of Colman.
1990.chinese: 去世前几天，《福布斯》封面文章盛赞吉列，主题很简单：剃须产品的成功，源于对质量的执着，而非营销精明，尽管营销本领也屡次展现。这种心态让公司不断专注改进，即使已有产品早已居行业之首。《福布斯》这样描绘吉列，其实也为科尔曼画了一幅肖像。

1990.english:
Help! Help!

Regular readers know that I shamelessly utilize the annual letter in an attempt to acquire businesses for Berkshire. And, as we constantly preach at the Buffalo News, advertising does work: Several businesses have knocked on our door because someone has read in these pages of our interest in making acquisitions. (Any good ad salesman will tell you that trying to sell something without advertising is like winking at a girl in the dark.)
1990.chinese:
## 帮帮忙！帮帮忙！

常读报告的各位知道，为伯克希尔收购企业，我毫不羞涩地利用每年这封信。正如布法罗新闻报不断宣传的，广告确实有效：已有几家企业上门，就是因为有人从这里读到我们的收购兴趣。（任何好广告推销员都会告诉你，想卖东西却不登广告，就像黑暗中向姑娘眨眼。）

1990.english:
In Appendix B (on pages 26-27) I've reproduced the essence of a letter I wrote a few years back to the owner/manager of a desirable business. If you have no personal connection with a business that might be of interest to us but have a friend who does, perhaps you can pass this report along to him.

Here's the sort of business we are looking for:

(1) Large purchases (at least $10 million of after-tax earnings),
1990.chinese:
附录B，第26—27页，重印了几年前我写给一家中意企业的所有者兼经理人的信的要旨。如果你本人没与可能适合我们的企业有联系，却有朋友与之相关，不妨把报告转给他。

我们寻找的企业是：

（1）大规模收购：税后利润至少1000万美元；

1990.english:
(2) Demonstrated consistent earning power (future projections are of little interest to us, nor are "turnaround" situations),

(3) Businesses earning good returns on equity while employing little or no debt,

(4) Management in place (we can't supply it),

(5) Simple businesses (if there's lots of technology, we won't understand it),

(6) An offering price (we don't want to waste our time or that of the seller by talking, even preliminarily, about a transaction when price is unknown).
1990.chinese:
（2）已证明持续而稳定的盈利能力：未来预测没多大吸引力，“扭亏为盈”的情形也一样；

（3）很少或没有负债，却有良好股东权益回报的企业；

（4）已有到位的管理层：我们无法提供；

（5）简单的生意：技术成分太多，我们就看不懂；

（6）明确的报价：价格还不知道，就来讨论交易，哪怕初步接触，我们也不愿浪费自己或卖方的时间。

1990.english:
We will not engage in unfriendly takeovers. We can promise complete confidentiality and a very fast answer - customarily within five minutes - as to whether we're interested. We prefer to buy for cash, but will consider issuing stock when we receive as much in intrinsic business value as we give.

Our favorite form of purchase is one fitting the Blumkin- Friedman-Heldman mold. In cases like these, the company's owner- managers wish to generate significant amounts of cash, sometimes for themselves, but often for their families or inactive shareholders. At the same time, these managers wish to remain significant owners who continue to run their companies just as they have in the past. We think we offer a particularly good fit for owners with such objectives. We invite potential sellers to check us out by contacting people with whom we have done business in the past.
1990.chinese:
我们不做敌意收购。保证完全保密，并很快答复是否有兴趣，通常五分钟内。更喜欢现金购买；但若收到的企业内在价值，不少于交出去的价值，也会考虑发行股票。

我们最喜欢布卢姆金—弗里德曼—赫尔德曼这一类收购。企业所有者兼经理人想变现一大笔钱，有时为自己，但常为家人或不参与经营的股东。同时，他们又希望保留可观股权，照过去的方式继续经营。对这些目标，我们认为自己尤其合适。欢迎有意出售者向过去与我们做过生意的人打听。

1990.english:
Charlie and I frequently get approached about acquisitions that don't come close to meeting our tests: We've found that if you advertise an interest in buying collies, a lot of people will call hoping to sell you their cocker spaniels. A line from a country song expresses our feeling about new ventures, turnarounds, or auction-like sales: "When the phone don't ring, you'll know it's me."

Besides being interested in the purchase of businesses as described above, we are also interested in the negotiated purchase of large, but not controlling, blocks of stock comparable to those we hold in Capital Cities, Salomon, Gillette, USAir, and Champion. We are not interested, however, in receiving suggestions about purchases we might make in the general stock market.
1990.chinese:
查理和我常收到远不符合标准的收购建议。我们发现，广告说想买柯利牧羊犬，就会有许多人来电，想卖自己的可卡犬。至于新创企业、困境反转，或拍卖式出售，一句乡村歌词道出了心情：“电话没响时，你就知道那是我。”

除了上述企业收购，我们也愿协商买入大笔但不控股的股份，类似大都会、所罗门、吉列、全美航空和冠军国际的持仓。不过，我们对该在一般股票市场买什么的推荐，没有兴趣。

1990.english:
Miscellaneous

Ken Chace has decided not to stand for reelection as a director at our upcoming annual meeting. We have no mandatory retirement age for directors at Berkshire (and won't!), but Ken, at 75 and living in Maine, simply decided to cut back his activities.

Ken was my immediate choice to run the textile operation after Buffett Partnership, Ltd. assumed control of Berkshire early in 1965. Although I made an economic mistake in sticking with the textile business, I made no mistake in choosing Ken: He ran the operation well, he was always 100% straight with me about its problems, and he generated the funds that allowed us to diversify into insurance.
1990.chinese:
## 其他事项

肯·蔡斯决定不在即将召开的年会上竞选连任董事。伯克希尔没有董事强制退休年龄，以后也不会有！不过，住在缅因州的肯已75岁，只是决定减少活动。

1965年初，巴菲特合伙企业取得伯克希尔控制权后，我立即选定肯管理纺织业务。坚持纺织业，是我在经济上犯的错误；选择肯，却没有错。他经营得很好，对问题始终百分之百坦诚，并创造了让我们转入保险业的资金。

1990.english:
My wife, Susan, will be nominated to succeed Ken. She is now the second largest shareholder of Berkshire and if she outlives me will inherit all of my stock and effectively control the company. She knows, and agrees, with my thoughts on successor management and also shares my view that neither Berkshire nor its subsidiary businesses and important investments should be sold simply because some very high bid is received for one or all.

I feel strongly that the fate of our businesses and their managers should not depend on my health - which, it should be added, is excellent - and I have planned accordingly. Neither my estate plan nor that of my wife is designed to preserve the family fortune; instead, both are aimed at preserving the character of Berkshire and returning the fortune to society.
1990.chinese:
我的妻子苏珊将获提名接替肯。她现为伯克希尔第二大股东；若活得比我久，将继承我的全部股票，实际控制公司。她了解并同意我的接班管理安排，也赞同：不能仅因有人对全部或某一部分出价极高，就卖掉伯克希尔、子公司或重要投资。

我坚信，企业及经理人的命运，不该取决于我的健康，顺带说，我身体极好；因此已作相应安排。我和妻子的遗产计划，都不是为了保住家族财富，而是为了保住伯克希尔的特质，并把财富回馈社会。

1990.english:
Were I to die tomorrow, you could be sure of three things: (1) None of my stock would have to be sold; (2) Both a controlling shareholder and a manager with philosophies similar to mine would follow me; and (3) Berkshire's earnings would increase by $1 million annually, since Charlie would immediately sell our corporate jet, The Indefensible (ignoring my wish that it be buried with me).

---
1990.chinese:
如果明天我就去世，三件事可以确定：（1）我的股票一股也无须出售；（2）会有理念与我相似的控股股东和经理人接班；（3）伯克希尔年利润会增加100万美元，因为查理会立即卖掉公务机“无可辩护号”，不理会我让它陪葬的心愿。

* * * * * * * * * * * *

1990.english:
About 97.3% of all eligible shares participated in Berkshire's 1990 shareholder-designated contributions program. Contributions made through the program were $5.8 million, and 2,600 charities were recipients.

We suggest that new shareholders read the description of our shareholder-designated contributions program that appears on pages 54-55. To participate in future programs, you must make sure your shares are registered in the name of the actual owner, not in the nominee name of a broker, bank or depository. Shares not so registered on August 31, 1991 will be ineligible for the 1991 program.
1990.chinese:
约97.3%的合资格股份，参加了伯克希尔1990年股东指定捐赠计划。经计划捐出580万美元，受益慈善机构2600家。

建议新股东阅读第54—55页对计划的说明。要参加未来计划，须确保股票登记在实际所有者名下，而非经纪商、银行或托管机构的代名账户。1991年8月31日未按此登记的股份，无资格参加1991年计划。

1990.english:
In addition to the shareholder-designated contributions that Berkshire distributes, managers of our operating businesses make contributions, including merchandise, averaging about $1.5 million annually. These contributions support local charities, such as The United Way, and produce roughly commensurate benefits for our businesses.

However, neither our operating managers nor officers of the parent company use Berkshire funds to make contributions to broad national programs or charitable activities of special personal interest to them, except to the extent they do so as shareholders. If your employees, including your CEO, wish to give to their alma maters or other institutions to which they feel a personal attachment, we believe they should use their own money, not yours.
1990.chinese:
除股东指定捐赠外，自营业务经理人每年平均还捐约150万美元，包括商品，支持联合劝募等地方慈善，并给企业带来大致相称的好处。

不过，除作为股东参与外，自营经理人或母公司高管，都不拿伯克希尔资金，捐给广泛的全国性项目，或个人特别感兴趣的慈善活动。你的员工，包括首席执行官，如果想捐给母校或有私人感情的其他机构，我们认为，该用自己的钱，不该用你的钱。

1990.english:
---

The annual meeting this year will be held at the Orpheum Theater in downtown Omaha at 9:30 a.m. on Monday, April 29, 1991. Attendance last year grew to a record 1,300, about a 100-fold increase from ten years ago.

We recommend getting your hotel reservations early at one of these hotels: (1) The Radisson-Redick Tower, a small (88 rooms) but nice hotel across the street from the Orpheum; (2) the much larger Red Lion Hotel, located about a five-minute walk from the Orpheum; or (3) the Marriott, located in West Omaha about 100 yards from Borsheim's and a twenty minute drive from downtown. We will have buses at the Marriott that will leave at 8:30 and 8:45 for the meeting, and return after it ends.
1990.chinese:
* * * * * * * * * * * *

今年年会定于1991年4月29日星期一上午9:30，在奥马哈市中心奥菲姆剧院举行。去年出席人数创下1300人纪录，约为十年前的100倍。

建议提早预订以下酒店之一：（1）丽笙雷迪克塔酒店，只有88间客房，规模小但不错，就在剧院街对面；（2）红狮酒店大得多，步行至剧院约五分钟；（3）万豪酒店，在西奥马哈，距波仙约100码，到市中心开车二十分钟。我们会安排大巴，上午8:30及8:45从万豪出发，会议结束后返回。

1990.english:
Charlie and I always enjoy the meeting, and we hope you can make it. The quality of our shareholders is reflected in the quality of the questions we get: We have never attended an annual meeting anywhere that features such a consistently high level of intelligent, owner-related questions.

An attachment to our proxy material explains how you can obtain the card you will need for admission to the meeting. Because weekday parking can be tight around the Orpheum, we have lined up a number of nearby lots for our shareholders to use. The attachment also contains information about them.
1990.chinese:
查理和我总是很享受年会，希望各位能来。问题的质量，体现股东的素质：我们从没在别处参加过年会，能如此始终如一，提出高水平、从所有者角度出发的明智问题。

委托投票材料的附件，会说明如何取得年会入场证。工作日剧院附近停车可能紧张，我们已联系附近若干停车场供股东使用；附件也有相关信息。

1990.english: As usual, we will have buses to take you to Nebraska Furniture Mart and Borsheim's after the meeting and to take you to downtown hotels or to the airport later. I hope that you will allow plenty of time to fully explore the attractions of both stores. Those of you arriving early can visit the Furniture Mart any day of the week; it is open from 10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. on Saturdays, and from noon to 5:30 p.m. on Sundays. While there, stop at the See's Candy cart and see for yourself the dawn of synergism at Berkshire.
1990.chinese: 照惯例，年会后大巴会送各位去内布拉斯加家具卖场及波仙，稍后再送往市中心酒店或机场。希望留足时间，充分逛逛两家店。提前来的股东，一周任何一天都能去家具卖场；周六上午10:00至下午5:30营业，周日中午12:00至下午5:30。在那里，也请停一停喜诗糖果车，亲眼见证伯克希尔协同效应的曙光。

1990.english:
Borsheim's normally is closed on Sunday, but we will open for shareholders and their guests from noon to 6 p.m. on Sunday, April 28. At our Sunday opening last year you made Ike very happy: After totaling the day's volume, he suggested to me that we start holding annual meetings quarterly. Join us at Borsheim's even if you just come to watch; it's a show you shouldn't miss.

Last year the first question at the annual meeting was asked by 11-year-old Nicholas Kenner, a third-generation shareholder from New York City. Nicholas plays rough: "How come the stock is down?" he fired at me. My answer was not memorable.
1990.chinese:
波仙通常周日歇业，但4月28日星期日会为股东及来宾开放，中午12:00至下午6:00。去年周日专场，让艾克十分开心：算完当天销量，他建议我把年会改成每季度一次。就算只来看看，也请到波仙相聚；这场好戏不容错过。

去年年会第一个问题，来自纽约市11岁的尼古拉斯·肯纳，一位第三代股东。尼古拉斯出手可不客气：“股价怎么跌了？”他朝我开火。我的回答没什么值得记住的。

1990.english:
We hope that other business engagements won't keep Nicholas away from this year's meeting. If he attends, he will be offered the chance to again ask the first question; Charlie and I want to tackle him while we're fresh. This year, however, it's Charlie's turn to answer.

March 1, 1991

## Warren E. Buffett

## Chairman of the Board

## APPENDIX A

## U. S. STEEL ANNOUNCES SWEEPING MODERNIZATION SCHEME*

* An unpublished satire by Ben Graham, written in 1936 and given by the author to Warren Buffett in 1954.
1990.chinese:
希望其他商务活动不会让尼古拉斯缺席今年年会。如果来了，会再让他问第一个问题；查理和我想趁精力充沛，先应付他。不过，今年轮到查理回答。

1991年3月1日

沃伦·E·巴菲特

董事长

## 附录A

### 美国钢铁公司宣布全面现代化大计*

*本·格雷厄姆1936年写成、此前未发表的一篇讽刺文章，作者于1954年赠予沃伦·巴菲特。

1990.english: Myron C. Taylor, Chairman of U. S. Steel Corporation, today announced the long awaited plan for completely modernizing the world's largest industrial enterprise. Contrary to expectations, no changes will be made in the company's manufacturing or selling policies. Instead, the bookkeeping system is to be entirely revamped. By adopting and further improving a number of modern accounting and financial devices the corporation's earning power will be amazingly transformed. Even under the subnormal conditions of 1935, it is estimated that the new bookkeeping methods would have yielded a reported profit of close to $50 per share on the common stock. The scheme of improvement is the result of a comprehensive survey made by Messrs. Price, Bacon, Guthrie & Colpitts; it includes the following six points:
1990.chinese: 美国钢铁公司董事长迈伦·C·泰勒今日宣布，期待已久、旨在使全球最大工业企业彻底现代化的计划，现已出台。出乎意料的是，公司制造或销售政策将不作任何改变，取而代之的是彻底改造簿记制度。通过采用并进一步改进若干现代会计和财务手段，公司的盈利能力将得到惊人转变。据估计，即使在1935年低于正常的经营状况下，新簿记方法也能使普通股报告每股接近50美元利润。改进方案来自Price、Bacon、Guthrie及Colpitts诸位作出的全面调查，包括以下六点：

1990.english:
1. Writing down of Plant Account to Minus $1,000,000,000.

2. Par value of common stock to be reduced to 1¢.

3. Payment of all wages and salaries in option warrants.

4. Inventories to be carried at $1.

5. Preferred Stock to be replaced by non-interest bearing bonds redeemable at 50% discount.

6. A $1,000,000,000 Contingency Reserve to be established.

The official statement of this extraordinary Modernization Plan follows in full:

The Board of Directors of U. S. Steel Corporation is pleased to announce that after intensive study of the problems arising from changed conditions in the industry, it has approved a comprehensive plan for remodeling the Corporation's accounting methods. A survey by a Special Committee, aided and abetted by Messrs. Price, Bacon, Guthrie & Colpitts, revealed that our company has lagged somewhat behind other American business enterprises in utilizing certain advanced bookkeeping methods, by means of which the earning power may be phenomenally enhanced without requiring any cash outlay or any changes in operating or sales conditions. It has been decided not only to adopt these newer methods, but to develop them to a still higher stage of perfection. The changes adopted by the Board may be summarized under six heads, as follows:
1990.chinese:
1. 将厂房账户减记至负10亿美元。

2. 将普通股面值降至1美分。

3. 以认股权证支付全部工薪。

4. 全部存货按1美元入账。

5. 以不计息、按面额五折赎回的债券，取代优先股。

6. 设立10亿美元或有事项准备金。

现将这一非凡现代化计划的正式声明全文列示如下：

美国钢铁公司董事会欣然宣布，深入研究行业环境变化带来的问题后，已批准全面重塑公司会计方法的计划。特别委员会在Price、Bacon、Guthrie及Colpitts诸位协助并助纣为虐之下所作调查，显示在利用某些先进簿记方法方面，我们稍落后于其他美国企业。借助这些方法，无须付出现金，也无须改变经营或销售状况，便可让盈利能力惊人提高。如今决定，不但采用这些新方法，还要把它们发展到更高的完善境界。董事会采纳的变化，可归纳为以下六项：

1990.english:
1. Fixed Assets to be written down to Minus $1,000,000,000.

Many representative companies have relieved their income accounts of all charges for depreciation by writing down their plant account to $1. The Special Committee points out that if their plants are worth only $1, the fixed assets of U. S. Steel Corporation are worth a good deal less than that sum. It is now a well-recognized fact that many plants are in reality a liability rather than an asset, entailing not only depreciation charges, but taxes, maintenance, and other expenditures. Accordingly, the Board has decided to extend the write-down policy initiated in the 1935 report, and to mark down the Fixed Assets from $1,338,522,858.96 to a round Minus $1,000,000,000.
1990.chinese:
#### 1. 固定资产减记至负10亿美元。

许多有代表性的公司，把厂房账户减记至1美元，便让利润表免除了全部折旧费用。特别委员会指出，如果它们的厂房只值1美元，美国钢铁公司的固定资产，显然比这点钱还不值。如今大家已公认，许多厂房其实是负债，而非资产，不但产生折旧，还有税款、维护及其他支出。因此，董事会决定，扩展1935年报告中启动的减记政策，把固定资产从1,338,522,858.96美元，减至整整负10亿美元。

1990.english:
The advantages of this move should be evident. As the plant wears out, the liability becomes correspondingly reduced. Hence, instead of the present depreciation charge of some $47,000,000 yearly there will be an annual appreciation credit of 5%, or $50,000,000. This will increase earnings by no less than $97,000,000 per annum.

## 2. Reduction of Par Value of Common Stock to 1¢, and

3. Payment of Salaries and Wages in Option Warrants.

Many corporations have been able to reduce their overhead expenses substantially by paying a large part of their executive salaries in the form of options to buy stock, which carry no charge against earnings. The full possibilities of this modern device have apparently not been adequately realized. The Board of Directors has adopted the following advanced form of this idea:
1990.chinese:
好处应当一目了然：厂房越磨损，负债便相应减少。因此，不再每年计提约4700万美元折旧，而是每年确认5%、即5000万美元的增值收益。每年利润由此增加，不少于9700万美元。

#### 2. 普通股面值降至1美分，以及

#### 3. 以认股权证支付工薪。

许多公司，以不计入利润费用的股票购买期权，支付大部分高管薪酬，从而大幅削减管理费用。这种现代工具的全部潜力，显然尚未得到充分发挥。董事会已采纳以下更先进的版本：

1990.english:
The entire personnel of the Corporation are to receive their compensation in the form of rights to buy common stock at $50 per share, at the rate of one purchase right for each $50 of salary and/or wages in their present amounts. The par value of the common stock is to be reduced to 1¢.

The almost incredible advantages of this new plan are evident from the following:

A. The payroll of the Corporation will be entirely eliminated, a saving of $250,000,000 per annum, based on 1935 operations.
1990.chinese:
全体员工的报酬，都改为按每股50美元购买普通股的权利；按现有工薪金额，每50美元工资或薪金，获得一份认购权。普通股面值则降至1美分。

新计划几乎令人难以置信的好处，可见如下：

A. 公司工薪支出将彻底消失。以1935年经营为基础，每年节省2.5亿美元。

1990.english: B. At the same time, the effective compensation of all our employees will be increased severalfold. Because of the large earnings per share to be shown on our common stock under the new methods, it is certain that the shares will command a price in the market far above the option level of $50 per share, making the readily realizable value of these option warrants greatly in excess of the present cash wages that they will replace.
1990.chinese: B. 同时，所有员工的实际报酬将增加数倍。新方法使普通股显示巨额每股利润，因此市价必定远高于50美元行权价；认股权证随时可以变现的价值，也就远超过其所取代的现金工资。

1990.english:
C. The Corporation will realize an additional large annual profit through the exercise of these warrants. Since the par value of the common stock will be fixed at 1¢, there will be a gain of $49.99 on each share subscribed for. In the interest of conservative accounting, however, this profit will not be included in the income account, but will be shown separately as a credit to Capital Surplus.

D. The Corporation's cash position will be enormously strengthened. In place of the present annual cash outgo of $250,000,000 for wages (1935 basis), there will be annual cash inflow of $250,000,000 through exercise of the subscription warrants for 5,000,000 shares of common stock. The Company's large earnings and strong cash position will permit the payment of a liberal dividend which, in turn, will result in the exercise of these option warrants immediately after issuance which, in turn, will further improve the cash position which, in turn, will permit a higher dividend rate -- and so on, indefinitely.
1990.chinese:
C. 权证行使，还会让公司每年实现另一笔巨额利润。既然普通股面值定为1美分，每认购一股，就有49.99美元收益。不过，为坚持稳健会计，这项利润不会纳入利润表，而会单列贷记资本公积。

D. 公司的现金状况将大大增强。按1935年基础，现时每年2.5亿美元工薪现金流出，将变成行使500万股普通股认购权证所带来的每年2.5亿美元现金流入。丰厚利润与充裕现金，使公司能派丰厚股息；股息又使权证一发行便获行使；行权又进一步改善现金状况；现金改善又容许更高股息率——如此循环，无穷无尽。

1990.english:
4. Inventories to be carried at $1.

Serious losses have been taken during the depression due to the necessity of adjusting inventory value to market. Various enterprises -- notably in the metal and cotton-textile fields -- have successfully dealt with this problem by carrying all or part of their inventories at extremely low unit prices. The U. S. Steel Corporation has decided to adopt a still more progressive policy, and to carry its entire inventory at $1. This will be effected by an appropriate write-down at the end of each year, the amount of said write-down to be charged to the Contingency Reserve hereinafter referred to.
1990.chinese:
#### 4. 全部存货按1美元入账。

大萧条期间，存货必须调整至市价，因而计提巨额损失。许多企业，尤其金属和棉纺织企业，以极低单位价格记录全部或部分存货，已成功解决这个问题。美国钢铁公司决定采取更进步政策，把全部存货记为1美元。每年末作相应减记，减记金额计入后文所述或有事项准备金。

1990.english: The benefits to be derived from this new method are very great. Not only will it obviate all possibility of inventory depreciation, but it will substantially enhance the annual earnings of the Corporation. The inventory on hand at the beginning of the year, valued at $1, will be sold during the year at an excellent profit. It is estimated that our income will be increased by means of this method to the extent of at least $150,000,000 per annum which, by a coincidence, will about equal the amount of the write-down to be made each year against Contingency Reserve.
1990.chinese: 新方法的好处极大。不但免去存货减值的一切可能，还会大幅增加年度利润。年初价值1美元的库存，会在年内卖出，获利丰厚。据估计，这种方法每年将使利润增加至少1.5亿美元；巧的是，恰好大约等于每年从或有事项准备金中扣除的存货减记。

1990.english: A minority report of the Special Committee recommends that Accounts Receivable and Cash also be written down to $1, in the interest of consistency and to gain additional advantages similar to those just discussed. This proposal has been rejected for the time being because our auditors still require that any recoveries of receivables and cash so charged off be credited to surplus instead of to the year's income. It is expected, however, that this auditing rule -- which is rather reminiscent of the horse-and-buggy days -- will soon be changed in line with modern tendencies. Should this occur, the minority report will be given further and favorable consideration.
1990.chinese: 特别委员会的少数派报告，为求一致，并取得类似额外好处，建议把应收账款及现金也减记至1美元。这项建议暂遭否决，因为审计师仍要求，把此类已冲销应收款及现金的任何收回，计入盈余，而非当年利润。不过，预计这条颇有马车时代遗风的审计规则，很快会顺应现代趋势改变。届时，将重新并有利地考虑少数派报告。

1990.english:
5. Replacement of Preferred Stock by Non-Interest-Bearing Bonds Redeemable at 50% Discount.

During the recent depression many companies have been able to offset their operating losses by including in income profits arising from repurchases of their own bonds at a substantial discount from par. Unfortunately the credit of U. S. Steel Corporation has always stood so high that this lucrative source of revenue has not hitherto been available to it. The Modernization Scheme will remedy this condition.
1990.chinese:
#### 5. 以不计息、按面额五折赎回的债券，取代优先股。

最近大萧条期间，许多公司把大幅低于面值回购自身债券所得的收益计入利润，从而抵消经营亏损。不幸的是，美国钢铁公司的信用一向太高，这条有利可图的收入来源，以往竟无从利用。现代化计划将纠正这种情况。

1990.english:
It is proposed that each share of preferred stock be exchanged for $300 face value of non-interest-bearing sinking-fund notes, redeemable by lot at 50% of face value in 10 equal annual installments. This will require the issuance of $1,080,000,000 of new notes, of which $108,000,000 will be retired each year at a cost to the Corporation of only $54,000,000, thus creating an annual profit of the same amount.

Like the wage-and/or-salary plan described under 3. above, this arrangement will benefit both the Corporation and its preferred stockholders. The latter are assured payment for their present shares at 150% of par value over an average period of five years. Since short-term securities yield practically no return at present, the non-interest-bearing feature is of no real importance. The Corporation will convert its present annual charge of $25,000,000 for preferred dividends into an annual bond-retirement profit of $54,000,000 -- an aggregate yearly gain of $79,000,000.
1990.chinese:
拟将每股优先股，换成面值300美元的不计息偿债基金票据，分十个年度等额抽签、按面值50%赎回。为此，将发行10.80亿美元新票据，每年注销1.08亿美元，只须花5400万美元，从而创造同额年度利润。

像前述第3项工薪计划一样，这种安排对公司及优先股股东都有利。后者可以在平均五年内，确保按现有股份面值150%取得付款。眼下短期证券几乎没有收益，所以不计息并无真正影响。公司将把每年2500万美元优先股股息支出，变成每年5400万美元债券注销利润，每年合计获益7900万美元。

1990.english:
6. Establishment of a Contingency Reserve of $1,000,000,000.

The Directors are confident that the improvements hereinbefore described will assure the Corporation of a satisfactory earning power under all conditions in the future. Under modern accounting methods, however, it is unnecessary to incur the slightest risk of loss through adverse business developments of any sort, since all these may be provided for in advance by means of a Contingency Reserve.

The Special Committee has recommended that the Corporation create such a Contingency Reserve in the fairly substantial amount of $1,000,000,000. As previously set forth, the annual write-down of inventory to $1 will be absorbed by this reserve. To prevent eventual exhaustion of the Contingency Reserve, it has been further decided that it be replenished each year by transfer of an appropriate sum from Capital Surplus. Since the latter is expected to increase each year by not less than $250,000,000 through the exercise of the Stock Option Warrants (see 3. above), it will readily make good any drains on the Contingency Reserve.
1990.chinese:
#### 6. 设立10亿美元或有事项准备金。

董事们相信，上述改进将确保公司在未来任何情况下，都有满意的盈利能力。不过，按现代会计方法，根本不必因任何不利经营变化，承担哪怕一丁点亏损风险；因为一切均可借或有事项准备金事先安排。

特别委员会建议，公司设立规模颇为可观的10亿美元或有事项准备金。如前所述，每年把存货减记至1美元，均由该准备金吸收。为防最终用尽，还决定每年从资本公积转入适当金额，予以补充。后者预期通过认股权证行使，每年增加不少于2.5亿美元，见前述第3项，因此能够轻松补足准备金的任何消耗。

1990.english: In setting up this arrangement, the Board of Directors must confess regretfully that they have been unable to improve upon the devices already employed by important corporations in transferring large sums between Capital, Capital Surplus, Contingency Reserves and other Balance Sheet Accounts. In fact, it must be admitted that our entries will be somewhat too simple, and will lack that element of extreme mystification that characterizes the most advanced procedure in this field. The Board of Directors, however, have insisted upon clarity and simplicity in framing their Modernization Plan, even at the sacrifice of possible advantage to the Corporation's earning power.
1990.chinese: 建立这套安排时，董事会遗憾地承认，未能超越一些重要公司已经采用的手法：在资本、资本公积、或有事项准备金及其他资产负债表账户之间，大笔搬钱。事实上，必须承认，我们的分录未免太简单，缺少这个领域最先进做法所特有的那种极端令人摸不着头脑的成分。不过，董事会坚持，现代化计划必须清楚简单，即使牺牲公司盈利能力可能得到的好处，也在所不惜。

1990.english:
*Given a Stated Value differing from Par Value, in accordance with the laws of the State of Virginia, where the company will be re-incorporated.

It is perhaps unnecessary to point out to our stockholders that modern accounting methods give rise to balance sheets differing somewhat in appearance from those of a less advanced period. In view of the very large earning power that will result from these changes in the Corporation's Balance Sheet, it is not expected that undue attention will be paid to the details of assets and liabilities.
1990.chinese:
*公司将在弗吉尼亚州重新注册，按照该州法律，赋予普通股一个不同于面值的规定价值。

或许无须向股东指出，现代会计方法带来的资产负债表，外观会与不那么先进时代的报表略有不同。鉴于这些资产负债表变动，将产生极大的盈利能力，预计人们不会过分关注资产及负债的细节。

1990.english: In conclusion, the Board desires to point out that the combined procedure, whereby plant will be carried at a minus figure, our wage bill will be eliminated, and inventory will stand on our books at virtually nothing, will give U. S. Steel Corporation an enormous competitive advantage in the industry. We shall be able to sell our products at exceedingly low prices and still show a handsome margin of profit. It is the considered view of the Board of Directors that under the Modernization Scheme we shall be able to undersell all competitors to such a point that the anti-trust laws will constitute the only barrier to 100% domination of the industry.
1990.chinese: 最后，董事会想指出，把厂房记作负数、消灭工资账单、把存货记得几乎一文不值，这套综合程序，将给美国钢铁公司带来巨大行业竞争优势。我们能以极低价格售出产品，仍显示丰厚利润。董事会审慎认为，现代化计划会让我们以低价胜过全部竞争者，达到反托拉斯法成为阻止100%统治行业的唯一障碍的程度。

1990.english: In making this statement, the Board is not unmindful of the possibility that some of our competitors may seek to offset our new advantages by adopting similar accounting improvements. We are confident, however, that U. S. Steel will be able to retain the loyalty of its customers, old and new, through the unique prestige that will accrue to it as the originator and pioneer in these new fields of service to the user of steel. Should necessity arise, moreover, we believe we shall be able to maintain our deserved superiority by introducing still more advanced bookkeeping methods, which are even now under development in our Experimental Accounting Laboratory.
1990.chinese: 作出上述声明时，董事会并非没有想到，某些对手可能采用类似会计改进，抵消我们的新优势。不过，我们相信，凭借开创这些钢铁用户服务新领域所带来的独特声望，美国钢铁能留住新老顾客的忠诚。而且如有必要，我们相信，仍能引入更先进的簿记方法，保持应有优势；这些方法，此刻正在我们的实验会计研究室开发。

1990.english:
## APPENDIX B

## Some Thoughts on Selling Your Business*

*This is an edited version of a letter I sent some years ago to a man who had indicated that he might want to sell his family business. I present it here because it is a message I would like to convey to other prospective sellers. -- W.E.B.

Dear _____________:

Here are a few thoughts pursuant to our conversation of the other day.

Most business owners spend the better part of their lifetimes building their businesses. By experience built upon endless repetition, they sharpen their skills in merchandising, purchasing, personnel selection, etc. It's a learning process, and mistakes made in one year often contribute to competence and success in succeeding years.
1990.chinese:
## 附录B

### 关于出售企业的一些想法*

*这是一封信的编辑版本。几年前，一位先生表示可能想卖掉家族企业，我写了这封信。现在刊出，是因为也想把这番话传达给其他潜在卖方。——W.E.B.（沃伦·E·巴菲特）

亲爱的_____________：

接着前几天的交谈，谈几点想法。

多数企业所有者，把一生中大半时光用于建立企业。通过无数次重复积累经验，磨炼销售、采购、人员选拔等本领。这是学习过程：某年犯的错误，往往有助于后来几年的能力与成功。

1990.english: In contrast, owner-managers sell their business only once -- frequently in an emotionally-charged atmosphere with a multitude of pressures coming from different directions. Often, much of the pressure comes from brokers whose compensation is contingent upon consummation of a sale, regardless of its consequences for both buyer and seller. The fact that the decision is so important, both financially and personally, to the owner can make the process more, rather than less, prone to error. And, mistakes made in the once-in-a-lifetime sale of a business are not reversible.
1990.chinese: 相比之下，所有者兼经理人一生只卖一次企业，往往处在情绪激荡、各方压力纷至沓来的气氛里。许多压力常来自中介，他们的报酬取决于交易完成，不管给买卖双方带来什么后果。这个决定对所有者的财务与个人意义如此重大，反而可能使过程更易出错，而非更少。况且，一生一次卖企业所犯的错误，无法逆转。

1990.english: Price is very important, but often is not the most critical aspect of the sale. You and your family have an extraordinary business -- one of a kind in your field -- and any buyer is going to recognize that. It's also a business that is going to get more valuable as the years go by. So if you decide not to sell now, you are very likely to realize more money later on. With that knowledge you can deal from strength and take the time required to select the buyer you want.
1990.chinese: 价格很重要，却常不是出售中最关键的一面。你和家人拥有非凡企业，在本领域独一无二，任何买家都会认识到。而且，随着时间过去，它会越来越值钱。所以，若现在不卖，日后很可能卖得更多。知道这一点，就可以站在有利位置，从容花时间挑选想要的买家。

1990.english:
If you should decide to sell, I think Berkshire Hathaway offers some advantages that most other buyers do not. Practically all of these buyers will fall into one of two categories:

(1) A company located elsewhere but operating in your business or in a business somewhat akin to yours. Such a buyer -- no matter what promises are made -- will usually have managers who feel they know how to run your business operations and, sooner or later, will want to apply some hands-on "help." If the acquiring company is much larger, it often will have squads of managers, recruited over the years in part by promises that they will get to run future acquisitions. They will have their own way of doing things and, even though your business record undoubtedly will be far better than theirs, human nature will at some point cause them to believe that their methods of operating are superior. You and your family probably have friends who have sold their businesses to larger companies, and I suspect that their experiences will confirm the tendency of parent companies to take over the running of their subsidiaries, particularly when the parent knows the industry, or thinks it does.
1990.chinese:
如果决定卖，我认为伯克希尔有些优势，多数买家并不具备。这些买家，几乎都会落入以下两类之一：

（1）位于别处，但经营相同或相近业务的公司。这种买方，无论作何保证，其经理人通常都觉得，自己懂得如何管理你的企业，早晚会想亲手提供一些“帮助”。如果收购方大得多，往往有成群经理人，多年来招募他们时，部分就是以今后可管理收购企业相许。他们有自己的做法；哪怕你的经营记录无疑好得多，人性终究会使他们认定，自家方法更优。你和家人大概有朋友把企业卖给过大公司；我想，他们的经历会印证：母公司往往接管子公司的经营，尤其母公司懂这个行业，或自以为懂时。

1990.english: (2) A financial maneuverer, invariably operating with large amounts of borrowed money, who plans to resell either to the public or to another corporation as soon as the time is favorable. Frequently, this buyer's major contribution will be to change accounting methods so that earnings can be presented in the most favorable light just prior to his bailing out. I'm enclosing a recent article that describes this sort of transaction, which is becoming much more frequent because of a rising stock market and the great supply of funds available for such transactions.
1990.chinese: （2）财务操盘者，一贯靠大量借款运作，计划一有合适时机，就转卖给公众或其他公司。此类买方的主要贡献，常常是改变会计方法，在抽身前，把利润包装得最好。我附上一篇近期文章，介绍这种交易；由于股市上涨、可用资金庞大，这类交易正日益增多。

1990.english:
If the sole motive of the present owners is to cash their chips and put the business behind them -- and plenty of sellers fall in this category -- either type of buyer that I've just described is satisfactory. But if the sellers' business represents the creative work of a lifetime and forms an integral part of their personality and sense of being, buyers of either type have serious flaws.

Berkshire is another kind of buyer -- a rather unusual one. We buy to keep, but we don't have, and don't expect to have, operating people in our parent organization. All of the businesses we own are run autonomously to an extraordinary degree. In most cases, the managers of important businesses we have owned for many years have not been to Omaha or even met each other. When we buy a business, the sellers go on running it just as they did before the sale; we adapt to their methods rather than vice versa.
1990.chinese:
如果现所有者唯一动机，就是把筹码兑成现金，从此把企业抛在身后，许多卖方确属此类，那么上述两种买方都可以。但如果企业代表卖方一生创造的成果，是人格和自我认同不可分割的一部分，这两类买方都有严重缺陷。

伯克希尔是另一种买家，而且相当少见。买来就是为了保留，但母公司既没有、也不打算配备经营人员。旗下全部企业，享有极大自治。多数情况下，拥有多年的重要企业的经理人，从没来过奥马哈，甚至彼此没见过。收购后，卖方照出售前一样继续管理；是我们适应他们的方法，而不是相反。

1990.english:
We have no one -- family, recently recruited MBAs, etc. -- to whom we have promised a chance to run businesses we have bought from owner-managers. And we won't have.

You know of some of our past purchases. I'm enclosing a list of everyone from whom we have ever bought a business, and I invite you to check with them as to our performance versus our promises. You should be particularly interested in checking with the few whose businesses did not do well in order to ascertain how we behaved under difficult conditions.
1990.chinese:
我们不曾答应任何人，无论家人、刚招来的MBA等，让他们去经营从所有者兼经理人手里买来的企业。以后也不会。

你知道我们过去的一些收购。我附上历来向我们出售企业的全部人员名单，请你核实：实际表现与承诺是否相符。尤其应该找那几个后来经营不佳的卖方，看看我们在困难条件下如何行事。

1990.english:
Any buyer will tell you that he needs you personally -- and if he has any brains, he most certainly does need you. But a great many buyers, for the reasons mentioned above, don't match their subsequent actions to their earlier words. We will behave exactly as promised, both because we have so promised, and because we need to in order to achieve the best business results.

This need explains why we would want the operating members of your family to retain a 20% interest in the business. We need 80% to consolidate earnings for tax purposes, which is a step important to us. It is equally important to us that the family members who run the business remain as owners. Very simply, we would not want to buy unless we felt key members of present management would stay on as our partners. Contracts cannot guarantee your continued interest; we would simply rely on your word.
1990.chinese:
任何买家都会说，需要你本人；只要有点脑子，也确实一定需要。但出于上述理由，许多买家后来做的，与早先说的不一致。我们会完全照承诺行事，既因为已经答应，也因为只有如此，才能取得最佳经营结果。

这正是我们希望参与经营的家族成员保留20%股权的原因。我们需要80%，以便为税务目的合并利润，这一步很重要。同样重要的是，管理企业的家族成员继续做所有者。说得简单些，除非觉得现有管理层关键成员会留下做伙伴，否则我们不想买。合同无法保证持续投入，我们只会依靠你的承诺。

1990.english:
The areas I get involved in are capital allocation and selection and compensation of the top man. Other personnel decisions, operating strategies, etc. are his bailiwick. Some Berkshire managers talk over some of their decisions with me; some don't. It depends upon their personalities and, to an extent, upon their own personal relationship with me.

If you should decide to do business with Berkshire, we would pay in cash. Your business would not be used as collateral for any loan by Berkshire. There would be no brokers involved.
1990.chinese:
我介入的领域，是资本配置，以及最高负责人的选择与薪酬。其他人事决定、经营战略等，归他负责。有些伯克希尔经理人与我商量某些决定，有些不商量；取决于个性，也在一定程度上取决于他们与我的私人关系。

如果决定与伯克希尔交易，我们会付现金。你的企业不会被伯克希尔拿去作任何贷款抵押。也不会有中介介入。

1990.english: Furthermore, there would be no chance that a deal would be announced and that the buyer would then back off or start suggesting adjustments (with apologies, of course, and with an explanation that banks, lawyers, boards of directors, etc. were to be blamed). And finally, you would know exactly with whom you are dealing. You would not have one executive negotiate the deal only to have someone else in charge a few years later, or have the president regretfully tell you that his board of directors required this change or that (or possibly required sale of your business to finance some new interest of the parent's).
1990.chinese: 此外，不会出现宣布交易后，买方又退缩或开始提议调整的事，当然还附带道歉，解释责任在银行、律师、董事会等。最后，你会确切知道在与谁打交道：不会由一名高管谈妥交易，几年后却换别人接手，也不会让总裁遗憾地通知，董事会要求这样那样的改变，甚至要求卖掉你的企业，去资助母公司的新兴趣。

1990.english: It's only fair to tell you that you would be no richer after the sale than now. The ownership of your business already makes you wealthy and soundly invested. A sale would change the form of your wealth, but it wouldn't change its amount. If you sell, you will have exchanged a 100%-owned valuable asset that you understand for another valuable asset -- cash -- that will probably be invested in small pieces (stocks) of other businesses that you understand less well. There is often a sound reason to sell but, if the transaction is a fair one, the reason is not so that the seller can become wealthier.
1990.chinese: 公平地说，出售后，你不会比现在更富。拥有这家企业，已经让你富有，投资也稳健。出售改变的是财富形式，不是金额。若卖出，你就是把一家100%拥有、自己理解的宝贵资产，换成另一项宝贵资产——现金；现金大概又会投向一些你不那么了解的其他企业的小部分，即股票。出售常有充分理由，但交易若公平，理由并非让卖方变得更有钱。

1990.english:
I will not pester you; if you have any possible interest in selling, I would appreciate your call. I would be extraordinarily proud to have Berkshire, along with the key members of your family, own _______; I believe we would do very well financially; and I believe you would have just as much fun running the business over the next 20 years as you have had during the past 20.

Sincerely,

## /s/ Warren E. Buffett
1990.chinese:
我不会纠缠；如果你有任何出售兴趣，来电会令我十分感激。伯克希尔若能与家族关键成员共同拥有_______，我会非常自豪；相信财务结果会很好，也相信今后二十年，你经营企业的乐趣，会与过去二十年一样多。

此致

／签名／沃伦·E·巴菲特

1991.english:
BERKSHIRE HATHAWAY INC.

To the Shareholders of Berkshire Hathaway Inc.:

Our gain in net worth during 1991 was $2.1 billion, or 39.6%. Over the last 27 years (that is, since present management took over) our per-share book value has grown from $19 to $6,437, or at a rate of 23.7% compounded annually.

The size of our equity capital - which now totals $7.4 billion - makes it certain that we cannot maintain our past rate of gain or, for that matter, come close to doing so. As Berkshire grows, the universe of opportunities that can significantly influence the company's performance constantly shrinks. When we were working with capital of $20 million, an idea or business producing $1 million of profit added five percentage points to our return for the year. Now we need a $370 million idea (i.e., one contributing over $550 million of pre-tax profit) to achieve the same result. And there are many more ways to make $1 million than to make $370 million.
1991.chinese:
伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司

致伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司的股东：

1991年，我们的净资产增加21亿美元，增幅39.6%。过去27年，也就是现任管理层接手以来，每股账面价值从19美元增至6437美元，年复合增长率为23.7%。

股权资本如今达到74亿美元，注定我们无法维持过去的增长率，甚至接近也不可能。伯克希尔越大，能显著影响成绩的机会范围就越小。当初用2000万美元资本经营，一个赚100万美元的点子或企业，就能让年度回报增加五个百分点。如今，要有赚3.70亿美元的点子，也就是贡献超过5.50亿美元税前利润，才能取得同样效果。赚100万美元的办法，远比赚3.70亿美元多。

1991.english:
Charlie Munger, Berkshire's Vice Chairman, and I have set a goal of attaining a 15% average annual increase in Berkshire's intrinsic value. If our growth in book value is to keep up with a 15% pace, we must earn $22 billion during the next decade. Wish us luck - we'll need it.

Our outsized gain in book value in 1991 resulted from a phenomenon not apt to be repeated:  a dramatic rise in the price- earnings ratios of Coca-Cola and Gillette. These two stocks accounted for nearly $1.6 billion of our $2.1 billion growth in net worth last year. When we loaded up on Coke three years ago, Berkshire's net worth was $3.4 billion; now our Coke stock alone is worth more than that.
1991.chinese:
伯克希尔副董事长查理·芒格和我，把内在价值平均每年增长15%定为目标。账面价值要跟上15%的步伐，未来十年就须赚220亿美元。祝我们好运吧，我们会需要的。

1991年账面价值大增，来自一种不太可能重演的现象：可口可乐和吉列的市盈率大幅上升。去年净资产增加21亿美元，其中近16亿美元来自这两只股票。三年前大举买入可口可乐时，伯克希尔净资产为34亿美元；如今，单是可口可乐股票，就不止值这个数。

1991.english: Coca-Cola and Gillette are two of the best companies in the world and we expect their earnings to grow at hefty rates in the years ahead. Over time, also, the value of our holdings in these stocks should grow in rough proportion. Last year, however, the valuations of these two companies rose far faster than their earnings. In effect, we got a double-dip benefit, delivered partly by the excellent earnings growth and even more so by the market's reappraisal of these stocks. We believe this reappraisal was warranted. But it can't recur annually:  We'll have to settle for a single dip in the future.
1991.chinese: 可口可乐和吉列，是全球最好的公司中的两家，我们预计未来几年利润会强劲增长。长期来看，持仓价值也应大体按同样比例增长。不过，去年两家公司的估值上涨，远快于利润增长。实际上，我们享受了双份好处：部分来自出色的利润增长，更多来自市场重新评价这些股票。我们认为重估有其道理，但它不可能年年重演；今后只能满足于单份了。

1991.english:
## A Second Job

In 1989 when I - a happy consumer of five cans of Cherry Coke daily - announced our purchase of $1 billion worth of Coca- Cola stock, I described the move as a rather extreme example of putting our money where my mouth was. On August 18 of last year, when I was elected Interim Chairman of Salomon Inc, it was a different story: I put my mouth where our money was.
1991.chinese:
## 第二份工作

1989年，我这个每天乐喝五罐樱桃味可乐的消费者，宣布买入价值10亿美元可口可乐股票时，把这称作“把钱投到自己嘴巴所在之处”的极端例子。去年8月18日获选所罗门临时董事长，情形却倒过来：这次，是把我的嘴巴放到了我们的钱所在之处。

1991.english: You've all read of the events that led to my appointment. My decision to take the job carried with it an implicit but important message: Berkshire's operating managers are so outstanding that I knew I could materially reduce the time I was spending at the company and yet remain confident that its economic progress would not skip a beat. The Blumkins, the Friedman family, Mike Goldberg, the Heldmans, Chuck Huggins, Stan Lipsey, Ralph Schey and Frank Rooney (CEO of H.H. Brown, our latest acquisition, which I will describe later) are all masters of their operations and need no help from me. My job is merely to treat them right and to allocate the capital they generate. Neither function is impeded by my work at Salomon.
1991.chinese: 导致这次任命的事情，各位都已读到。接下工作这个决定，还含着一条重要信息：伯克希尔经营经理人太出色了，我知道，即使大幅减少花在公司的时间，也完全能相信经济进展不会漏掉一个节拍。布卢姆金一家、弗里德曼一家、迈克·戈德伯格、赫尔德曼一家、查克·哈金斯、斯坦·利普西、拉尔夫·谢伊，以及弗兰克·鲁尼，都是各自业务的大师，不需我帮忙；弗兰克是最新收购的H.H.布朗公司首席执行官，稍后会介绍。我的工作，只是好好对待他们，并配置他们创造的资本。这两件事，都不受所罗门工作影响。

1991.english: The role that Charlie and I play in the success of our operating units can be illustrated by a story about  George Mira, the one-time quarterback of the University of Miami, and his coach, Andy Gustafson. Playing Florida and near its goal line, Mira dropped back to pass. He spotted an open receiver but found his right shoulder in the unshakable grasp of a Florida linebacker. The right-handed Mira thereupon switched the ball to his other hand and threw the only left-handed pass of his life - for a touchdown. As the crowd erupted, Gustafson calmly turned to a reporter and declared: "Now that's what I call coaching."
1991.chinese: 查理和我对自营企业成功的作用，可以借迈阿密大学前四分卫乔治·米拉和教练安迪·古斯塔夫森的故事说明。对阵佛罗里达队，快到对方球门线时，米拉后撤准备传球。他看到一位无人盯防的接球队员，右肩却被对方线卫死死抓住。惯用右手的米拉，便把球换到另一只手，完成一生唯一一次左手传球，达阵得分。观众沸腾时，古斯塔夫森平静地转向记者说：“这就叫执教。”

1991.english:
Given the managerial stars we have at our operating units, Berkshire's performance is not affected if Charlie or I slip away from time to time. You should note, however, the "interim" in my Salomon title. Berkshire is my first love and one that will never fade: At the Harvard Business School last year, a student asked me when I planned to retire and I replied, "About five to ten years after I die."

## Sources of Reported Earnings
1991.chinese:
自营企业已有这样的管理明星，查理或我偶尔溜开，伯克希尔表现不会受影响。不过，请注意我在所罗门头衔中的“临时”二字。伯克希尔是我的初恋，永不褪色。去年在哈佛商学院，一位学生问我何时打算退休，我回答：“大概死后五至十年。”

## 报表利润的来源

1991.english: The table below shows the major sources of Berkshire's reported earnings. In this presentation, amortization of Goodwill and other major purchase-price accounting adjustments are not charged against the specific businesses to which they apply, but are instead aggregated and shown separately. This procedure lets you view the earnings of our businesses as they would have been reported had we not purchased them. I've explained in past reports why this form of presentation seems to us to be more useful to investors and managers than one utilizing generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), which require purchase- price adjustments to be made on a business-by-business basis. The total net earnings we show in the table are, of course, identical to the GAAP total in our audited financial statements.
1991.chinese: 下表列出伯克希尔报表利润的主要来源。商誉摊销及其他重大收购价格会计调整，不分摊到各自对应的具体企业，而是汇总后单列。这样，各位能看到，如果我们没买下这些企业，它们本来会报告怎样的利润。过去的报告已解释，为何我们认为，这比公认会计原则（GAAP）要求的逐企业收购价格调整，对投资者和经理人更有用。当然，表中净利润总额，与经审计财务报表的GAAP总额完全相同。

1991.english: A large amount of additional information about these businesses is given on pages 33-47, where you also will find our segment earnings reported on a GAAP basis. However, we will not in this letter discuss each of our non-insurance operations, as we have in the past. Our businesses have grown in number - and will continue to grow - so it now makes sense to rotate coverage, discussing one or two in detail each year.

*Excludes interest expense of Scott Fetzer Financial Group and Mutual Savings & Loan.

## "Look-Through" Earnings

We've previously discussed look-through earnings, which consist of: (1) the operating earnings reported in the previous section, plus; (2) the retained operating earnings of major investees that, under GAAP accounting, are not reflected in our profits, less; (3) an allowance for the tax that would be paid by Berkshire if these retained earnings of investees had instead been distributed to us.
1991.chinese:
*不包括斯科特与费策金融集团及互助储蓄与贷款协会的利息费用。

## “穿透”利润

过去已讨论过穿透利润，包括：（1）上一节报告的经营利润；加上（2）主要被投资公司留存、按GAAP不体现在我们利润中的经营利润份额；减去（3）假如这些留存利润改为分给我们，伯克希尔应缴的假设税额。

1991.english:
I've told you that over time look-through earnings must increase at about 15% annually if our intrinsic business value is to grow at that rate. Indeed, since present management took over in 1965, our look-through earnings have grown at almost the identical 23% rate of gain recorded for book value.

Last year, however, our look-through earnings did not grow at all but rather declined by 14%. To an extent, the decline was precipitated by two forces that I discussed in last year's report and that I warned you would have a negative effect on look-through earnings.
1991.chinese:
我说过，要让企业内在价值每年增长15%，长期来看，穿透利润也须大约同速增长。事实上，自现任管理层1965年接手以来，穿透利润的增长，与账面价值所记录的23%几乎完全相同。

不过，去年穿透利润完全没有增长，反而下降14%。部分原因，是上年报告谈过、并提醒会有负面影响的两股力量。

1991.english: First, I told you that our media earnings - both direct and look-through - were "sure to decline" and they in fact did. The second force came into play on April 1, when the call of our Gillette preferred stock required us to convert it into common. The after-tax earnings in 1990 from our preferred had been about $45 million, an amount somewhat higher than the combination in 1991 of three months of dividends on our preferred plus nine months of look-through earnings on the common.
1991.chinese: 第一，我说，媒体利润，无论直接计入还是穿透计算，都“肯定下降”，事实确实如此。第二股力量在4月1日生效：吉列优先股被通知赎回，迫使我们转换成普通股。1990年优先股税后利润约4500万美元，略高于1991年的组合，即三个月优先股股息，加九个月普通股穿透利润。

1991.english:
Two other outcomes that I did not foresee also hurt look- through earnings in 1991. First, we had a break-even result from our interest in Wells Fargo (dividends we received from the company were offset by negative retained earnings). Last year I said that such a result at Wells was "a low-level possibility - not a likelihood." Second, we recorded significantly lower - though still excellent - insurance profits.

We also believe that investors can benefit by focusing on their own look-through earnings. To calculate these, they should determine the underlying earnings attributable to the shares they hold in their portfolio and total these. The goal of each investor should be to create a portfolio (in effect, a "company") that will deliver him or her the highest possible look-through earnings a decade or so from now.
