1992.english: The combined ratio represents total insurance costs (losses incurred plus expenses) compared to revenue from premiums:  A ratio below 100 indicates an underwriting profit, and one above 100 indicates a loss.  The higher the ratio, the worse the year. When the investment income that an insurer earns from holding policyholders' funds ("the float") is taken into account, a combined ratio in the 106 - 110 range typically produces an overall break-even result, exclusive of earnings on the funds provided by shareholders.
1992.chinese: 综合成本率表示保险总成本（已发生赔款加费用）相对于保费收入的比例：低于100表示承保盈利，高于100则表示亏损。比例越高，意味着这一年越糟糕。若将保险公司持有投保人资金——也就是“浮存金”——所获得的投资收益计算在内，综合成本率处于106至110之间时，通常可以使公司大致达到整体收支平衡；这里不包括由股东提供的资金所产生的收益。

1992.english: About four points in the industry's 1992 combined ratio can be attributed to Hurricane Andrew, which caused the largest insured loss in history.  Andrew destroyed a few small insurers. Beyond that, it awakened some larger companies to the fact that their reinsurance protection against catastrophes was far from adequate.  (It's only when the tide goes out that you learn who's been swimming naked.)  One major insurer escaped insolvency solely because it had a wealthy parent that could promptly supply a massive transfusion of capital.
1992.chinese: 1992年全行业综合成本率中，约有4个百分点可以归因于安德鲁飓风（Hurricane Andrew），它造成了有史以来规模最大的保险损失。安德鲁使几家小型保险公司破产，也让一些规模较大的公司意识到，自己针对重大灾难购买的再保险保障远远不够。（只有退潮时，你才知道谁一直在裸泳。）有一家大型保险公司之所以没有资不抵债，完全是因为它有一家富有的母公司，可以迅速为其大量注入资本。

1992.english:
Bad as it was, however, Andrew could easily have been far more damaging if it had hit Florida 20 or 30 miles north of where it actually did and had hit Louisiana further east than was the case.  All in all, many companies will rethink their reinsurance programs in light of the Andrew experience.

As you know we are a large writer - perhaps the largest in the world - of "super-cat" coverages, which are the policies that other insurance companies buy to protect themselves against major catastrophic losses.  Consequently, we too took our lumps from Andrew, suffering losses from it of about $125 million, an amount roughly equal to our 1992 super-cat premium income.  Our other super-cat losses, though, were negligible.  This line of business therefore produced an overall loss of only $2 million for the year.  (In addition, our investee, GEICO, suffered a net loss from Andrew, after reinsurance recoveries and tax savings, of about $50 million, of which our share is roughly $25 million. This loss did not affect our operating earnings, but did reduce our look-through earnings.)
1992.chinese:
尽管损失已经如此惨重，如果安德鲁袭击佛罗里达州的地点比实际位置向北偏20或30英里，并且袭击路易斯安那州的地点更偏东，它造成的破坏就可能严重得多。总的来说，许多公司会根据安德鲁的经历重新审视自己的再保险安排。

正如各位所知，我们是“超级巨灾”（super-cat）保障的大型承保者——或许是全球最大的承保者。这是其他保险公司为防范重大灾难损失而购买的保险。因此，安德鲁也使我们遭受损失，损失约1.25亿美元，金额大致相当于我们1992年超级巨灾业务的保费收入。不过，我们在其他超级巨灾事件上的损失几乎可以忽略。因此，这项业务全年的总亏损只有200万美元。（此外，我们的被投资公司GEICO在扣除再保险赔款和税收节省后，因安德鲁产生约5,000万美元净损失，我们应占约2,500万美元。这项损失没有影响我们的财报经营利润，却减少了穿透利润。）

1992.english: In last year's report I told you that I hoped that our super-cat business would over time achieve a 10% profit margin. But I also warned you that in any given year the line was likely to be "either enormously profitable or enormously unprofitable." Instead, both 1991 and 1992 have come in close to a break-even level.  Nonetheless, I see these results as aberrations and stick with my prediction of huge annual swings in profitability from this business.
1992.chinese: 我在上一年度报告中说过，希望超级巨灾保险业务长期取得10%的利润率。但我也提醒各位，在任何单一年份，这项业务都可能“要么利润异常丰厚，要么亏损异常巨大”。结果，1991年和1992年都接近盈亏平衡。尽管如此，我认为这两个年份反而是例外，仍然坚持对这项业务年度利润将剧烈波动的预测。

1992.english: Let me remind you of some characteristics of our super-cat policies.  Generally, they are activated only when two things happen.  First, the direct insurer or reinsurer we protect must suffer losses of a given amount - that's the policyholder's "retention" - from a catastrophe; and second, industry-wide insured losses from the catastrophe must exceed some minimum level, which usually is $3 billion or more.  In most cases, the policies we issue cover only a specific geographical area, such as a portion of the U.S., the entire U.S., or everywhere other than the U.S.  Also, many policies are not activated by the first super-cat that meets the policy terms, but instead cover only a "second-event" or even a third- or fourth-event.  Finally, some policies are triggered only by a catastrophe of a specific type, such as an earthquake.  Our exposures are large: We have one policy that calls for us to pay $100 million to the policyholder if a specified catastrophe occurs.  (Now you know why I suffer eyestrain:  from watching The Weather Channel.)
1992.chinese: 请允许我提醒各位，我们的超级巨灾保险合同具有一些特点。通常，只有同时满足两个条件，保障才会触发。第一，我们提供保障的直接保险公司或再保险公司，必须因某场灾难遭受超过一定金额的损失——这就是保单持有人的“自留额”；第二，该灾难造成的全行业保险损失必须超过某个最低水平，通常为30亿美元或更多。大多数合同只覆盖某个指定地理区域，例如美国部分地区、整个美国，或美国以外的所有地区。许多保单也不保障第一场符合条件的超级巨灾，而只对“第二次事件”，甚至第三、第四次事件提供保障。还有一些保单只在发生特定类型灾难（例如地震）时触发。我们承担的风险敞口相当大：有一份保单规定，只要发生指定灾难，就必须向投保人支付1亿美元。（现在你们知道我为什么眼睛疲劳了：因为我总盯着天气频道。）

1992.english: Currently, Berkshire is second in the U.S. property-casualty industry in net worth (the leader being State Farm, which neither buys nor sells reinsurance).  Therefore, we have the capacity to assume risk on a scale that interests virtually no other company. We have the appetite as well:  As Berkshire's net worth and earnings grow, our willingness to write business increases also. But let me add that means good business.  The saying, "a fool and his money are soon invited everywhere," applies in spades in reinsurance, and we actually reject more than 98% of the business we are offered.  Our ability to choose between good and bad proposals reflects a management strength that matches our financial strength:  Ajit Jain, who runs our reinsurance operation, is simply the best in this business.  In combination, these strengths guarantee that we will stay a major factor in the super-cat business so long as prices are appropriate.
1992.chinese: 目前，伯克希尔在美国财产及意外责任保险行业的净资产排名第二，第一是State Farm，它既不购买也不出售再保险。因此，我们具备承担几乎没有其他公司愿意涉足的大规模风险的能力，而且我们也有这样的意愿：随着伯克希尔净资产和利润增长，我们承保业务的意愿也随之增强。不过请允许我补充，指的是*好业务*。“傻瓜有钱，自然处处有人请”这句俗话，在再保险行业尤其适用。事实上，我们拒绝的业务超过收到提案的98%。能够在好坏业务中作出选择，反映了与我们财务实力相匹配的管理优势：负责再保险业务的阿吉特·贾因（Ajit Jain），是这个行业最出色的人。两项优势结合起来，可以确保只要价格合适，我们就会一直是超级巨灾保险行业的重要参与者。

1992.english: What constitutes an appropriate price, of course, is difficult to determine.  Catastrophe insurers can't simply extrapolate past experience.  If there is truly "global warming," for example, the odds would shift, since tiny changes in atmospheric conditions can produce momentous changes in weather patterns.  Furthermore, in recent years there has been a mushrooming of population and insured values in U.S. coastal areas that are particularly vulnerable to hurricanes, the number one creator of super-cats.  A hurricane that caused x dollars of damage 20 years ago could easily cost 10x now.
1992.chinese: 当然，什么价格才算适当，判断起来并不容易。巨灾保险公司不能简单根据过去的经验向未来推算。比如，如果真的存在“全球变暖”，灾难发生的概率就会改变，因为大气条件哪怕发生很小变化，都可能给天气模式带来巨大影响。此外，近年来美国沿海地区人口和保险标的价值大幅增加，而这些地区特别容易受到飓风袭击——飓风是造成超级巨灾的首要原因。20年前造成x美元损失的飓风，如今可能轻易造成10x美元损失。

1992.english: Occasionally, also, the unthinkable happens.  Who would have guessed, for example, that a major earthquake could occur in Charleston, S.C.? (It struck in 1886, registered an estimated 6.6 on the Richter scale, and caused 60 deaths.)  And who could have imagined that our country's most serious quake would occur at New Madrid, Missouri, which suffered an estimated 8.7 shocker in 1812.  By comparison, the 1989 San Francisco quake was a 7.1 - and remember that each one-point Richter increase represents a ten-fold increase in strength.  Someday, a U.S. earthquake occurring far from California will cause enormous losses for insurers.
1992.chinese: 偶尔，原本不可想象的事情也会发生。比如，谁能预料南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿会发生大地震？（1886年发生的那场地震，估计为里氏6.6级，造成60人死亡。）又有谁能想到，美国最严重的地震会发生在密苏里州的新马德里？1812年当地遭遇了估计8.7级的强震。相比之下，1989年旧金山地震为7.1级。还要记住，里氏震级每增加一级，所测得的地震振幅便增加十倍。总有一天，美国某个远离加利福尼亚州的地方会发生地震，使保险公司遭受巨大损失。

1992.english: When viewing our quarterly figures, you should understand that our accounting for super-cat premiums differs from our accounting for other insurance premiums.  Rather than recording our super-cat premiums on a pro-rata basis over the life of a given policy, we defer recognition of revenue until a loss occurs or until the policy expires.  We take this conservative approach because the likelihood of super-cats causing us losses is particularly great toward the end of the year.  It is then that weather tends to kick up:  Of the ten largest insured losses in U.S. history, nine occurred in the last half of the year.  In addition, policies that are not triggered by a first event are unlikely, by their very terms, to cause us losses until late in the year.
1992.chinese: 阅读我们的季度报告时，各位应当了解，超级巨灾保费的会计处理方式不同于其他保险保费。我们没有按照保单有效期按比例确认超级巨灾保费收入，而是把收入确认推迟到损失发生或保单到期时。之所以采取这种谨慎方法，是因为超级巨灾在年底前给我们造成损失的可能性尤其高：天气往往在下半年变得更加恶劣，美国历史上十次最大保险损失中，有九次发生在下半年。此外，根据合同规定，不能被第一次事件触发的保单，在年内较晚之前，也不大可能给我们造成损失。

1992.english:
The bottom-line effect of our accounting procedure for super-cats is this:  Large losses may be reported in any quarter of the year, but significant profits will only be reported in the fourth quarter.

---

As I've told you in each of the last few years, what counts in our insurance business is "the cost of funds developed from insurance," or in the vernacular, "the cost of float."  Float - which we generate in exceptional amounts - is the total of loss reserves, loss adjustment expense reserves and unearned premium reserves minus agents' balances, prepaid acquisition costs and deferred charges applicable to assumed reinsurance.  The cost of float is measured by our underwriting loss.
1992.chinese:
这种超级巨灾保险会计方法的最终效果是：巨额亏损可能在一年中的任何季度报告，但重大利润只会在第四季度报告。

---

正如近几年每封信都告诉各位的，保险业务真正重要的是“保险业务形成的资金成本”，通俗地说，就是“浮存金成本”。我们能够产生异常大量的浮存金，其计算方法是：将赔款准备金、理赔费用准备金和未到期保费准备金相加，再扣除应收代理人款项、预付保单取得成本以及分入再保险相关的递延费用。浮存金的成本由承保亏损衡量。

1992.english: Last year, our insurance operation again generated funds at a cost below that incurred by the U.S. Government on its newly-issued long-term bonds.  This means that in 21 years out of the 26 years we have been in the insurance business we have beaten the Government's rate, and often we have done so by a wide margin. (If, on average, we didn't beat the Government's rate, there would be no economic reason for us to be in the business.)
1992.chinese: 去年，我们保险业务再次以低于美国政府新发行长期国债的成本取得了资金。这意味着，在我们进入保险业的26年里，有21年的资金成本低于政府的借款利率，而且很多时候差距很大。（如果我们的平均成本不低于政府利率，那么我们就没有从事这门生意的经济理由。）

1992.english: In 1992, as in previous years, National Indemnity's commercial auto and general liability business, led by Don Wurster, and our homestate operation, led by Rod Eldred, made excellent contributions to our low cost of float.  Indeed, both of these operations recorded an underwriting profit last year, thereby generating float at a less-than-zero cost.  The bulk of our float, meanwhile, comes from large transactions developed by Ajit.  His efforts are likely to produce a further growth in float during 1993.
1992.chinese: 1992年，与过去一样，由唐·沃斯特（Don Wurster）领导的国民赔偿保险公司商业汽车及一般责任险业务，以及由罗德·埃尔德雷德（Rod Eldred）领导的本州保险业务，都为我们保持低浮存金成本作出了出色贡献。事实上，这两项业务去年均取得了承保盈利，也就是以低于零的成本产生浮存金。与此同时，我们的大部分浮存金来自阿吉特开发的大型交易。他的努力很可能使1993年的浮存金进一步增长。

1992.english:
Charlie and I continue to like the insurance business, which we expect to be our main source of earnings for decades to come. The industry is huge; in certain sectors we can compete world-wide; and Berkshire possesses an important competitive advantage.  We will look for ways to expand our participation in the business, either indirectly as we have done through GEICO or directly as we did by acquiring Central States Indemnity.

## Common Stock Investments

Below we list our common stock holdings having a value of over $100 million.  A small portion of these investments belongs to subsidiaries of which Berkshire owns less than 100%.
1992.chinese:
查理和我仍然喜欢保险业务，我们预计它将在未来几十年继续成为伯克希尔的主要利润来源。这个行业规模巨大；在某些领域，我们可以在全球开展竞争；而伯克希尔具有重要的竞争优势。我们将寻找扩大参与程度的办法，既可以像投资GEICO那样间接参与，也可以像收购中央各州赔偿保险公司那样直接参与。

## 普通股投资

下表列示我们市值超过1亿美元的普通股持仓。这些投资中的一小部分属于伯克希尔持股不足100%的子公司。

1992.english:
Leaving aside splits, the number of shares we held in these companies changed during 1992 in only four cases:  We added moderately to our holdings in Guinness and Wells Fargo, we more than doubled our position in Freddie Mac, and we established a new holding in General Dynamics.  We like to buy.

Selling, however, is a different story.  There, our pace of activity resembles that forced upon a traveler who found himself stuck in tiny Podunk's only hotel.  With no T.V. in his room, he faced an evening of boredom.  But his spirits soared when he spied a book on the night table entitled "Things to do in Podunk." Opening it, he found just a single sentence: "You're doing it."
1992.chinese:
不计股票拆分，1992年我们持有的上述公司股份数量只有四处发生变化：适度增持了健力士和富国银行，房地美持股增加了一倍以上，并首次买入通用动力。我们喜欢买入。

不过，卖出则是另一回事。我们的卖出速度，像一个旅行者被困在偏僻的波当克小镇（Podunk）唯一一家旅馆里一样。他的房间里没有电视，面对无聊的一晚，心情十分沮丧。突然，他发现床头柜上有一本书，书名叫《在这个小镇里能做的事》。他兴奋地翻开，却只看到一句话：“你现在做的就是。”

1992.english: We were lucky in our General Dynamics purchase.  I had paid little attention to the company until last summer, when it announced it would repurchase about 30% of its shares by way of a Dutch tender.  Seeing an arbitrage opportunity, I began buying the stock for Berkshire, expecting to tender our holdings for a small profit.  We've made the same sort of commitment perhaps a half- dozen times in the last few years, reaping decent rates of return for the short periods our money has been tied up.
1992.chinese: 我们买入通用动力时有些运气。直到去年夏天，我对这家公司都没有投入多少关注。后来，它宣布将通过荷兰式招标回购约30%的股票。我看到一个套利机会，便开始为伯克希尔买入，打算把股票参与回购，获取一笔小额利润。过去几年我们大概做过六次类似交易，资金占用期较短，获得的回报还不错。

1992.english:
But then I began studying the company and the accomplishments of Bill Anders in the brief time he'd been CEO.  And what I saw made my eyes pop:  Bill had a clearly articulated and rational strategy; he had been focused and imbued with a sense of urgency in carrying it out; and the results were truly remarkable.

In short order, I dumped my arbitrage thoughts and decided that Berkshire should become a long-term investor with Bill.  We were helped in gaining a large position by the fact that a tender greatly swells the volume of trading in a stock.  In a one-month period, we were able to purchase 14% of the General Dynamics shares that remained outstanding after the tender was completed.
1992.chinese:
不过，后来我开始研究公司，以及比尔·安德斯（Bill Anders）出任首席执行官不久所取得的成绩。看到的情况让我眼睛都瞪圆了：比尔的战略表达清楚、合乎理性，执行时专心致志，又有强烈的紧迫感，取得的成果十分出色。

我很快放弃了套利的念头，决定伯克希尔应该成为与比尔共同长期持有公司的投资者。招标回购会显著增加股票成交量，这有助于我们建立大额持仓。在一个月内，我们买入了回购完成后通用动力流通股的14%。

1992.english:
---

Our equity-investing strategy remains little changed from what it was fifteen years ago, when we said in the 1977 annual report: "We select our marketable equity securities in much the way we would evaluate a business for acquisition in its entirety.  We want the business to be one (a) that we can understand; (b) with favorable long-term prospects; (c) operated by honest and competent people; and (d) available at a very attractive price."  We have seen cause to make only one change in this creed: Because of both market conditions and our size, we now substitute "an attractive price" for "a very attractive price."
1992.chinese:
---

我们的股票投资策略与15年前相比基本没有改变。当时我们在1977年年报中说：“我们挑选可交易股票的方法，与评估一家可被整体收购的企业基本相同。我们希望这门生意（a）能够理解；（b）长期前景良好；（c）由诚实且有能力的人经营；（d）可以用非常有吸引力的价格买到。”此后，我们只发现有一处需要修改：考虑到市场环境和我们的规模，现在我们把“非常有吸引力的价格”改为“有吸引力的价格”。

1992.english:
But how, you will ask, does one decide what's "attractive"? In answering this question, most analysts feel they must choose between two approaches customarily thought to be in opposition: "value" and "growth."  Indeed, many investment professionals see any mixing of the two terms as a form of intellectual cross- dressing.

We view that as fuzzy thinking (in which, it must be confessed, I myself engaged some years ago).  In our opinion, the two approaches are joined at the hip:  Growth is always a component in the calculation of value, constituting a variable whose importance can range from negligible to enormous and whose impact can be negative as well as positive.
1992.chinese:
不过，你们可能会问，如何判断价格是否“有吸引力”？回答这个问题时，大多数分析师认为，必须在通常被视为对立的两条道路中选择：一条是“价值”，另一条是“成长”。事实上，许多投资专业人士认为，把这两个词混在一起，简直是在思想上玩“异装”。

我们认为，这是一种含混不清的思考方式（必须承认，几年前我本人也曾如此）。在我们看来，这两种方法根本无法分开：成长始终是计算价值的一个组成部分。它是一个变量，其重要性可以从微不足道到极其巨大不等，而且对价值的影响既可能是正面的，也可能是负面的。

1992.english:
In addition, we think the very term "value investing" is redundant.  What is "investing" if it is not the act of seeking value at least sufficient to justify the amount paid?  Consciously paying more for a stock than its calculated value - in the hope that it can soon be sold for a still-higher price - should be labeled speculation (which is neither illegal, immoral nor - in our view - financially fattening).

Whether appropriate or not, the term "value investing" is widely used.  Typically, it connotes the purchase of stocks having attributes such as a low ratio of price to book value, a low price- earnings ratio, or a high dividend yield.  Unfortunately, such characteristics, even if they appear in combination, are far from determinative as to whether an investor is indeed buying something for what it is worth and is therefore truly operating on the principle of obtaining value in his investments.  Correspondingly, opposite characteristics - a high ratio of price to book value, a high price-earnings ratio, and a low dividend yield - are in no way inconsistent with a "value" purchase.
1992.chinese:
此外，我们认为，“价值投资”这个词本身就是多余的。如果投资不是寻找至少足以证明所付价格合理的价值，那它还能是什么？明知一只股票的价格超过估算出的价值，却希望很快以更高价格卖给别人，这应当叫作投机。（投机既不违法，也不道德败坏，但在我们看来，也不会让钱包长胖。）

不论是否恰当，“价值投资”一词已得到广泛使用。它通常指购买具有低市净率、低市盈率或高股息率等特征的股票。遗憾的是，即使这些特征同时存在，也远不足以证明投资者确实以与价值相当的价格买到了资产，从而真正遵循了获得价值的投资原则。相应地，反面的特征——高市净率、高市盈率和低股息率——也完全可能与“价值”购买相容。

1992.english: Similarly, business growth, per se, tells us little about value.  It's true that growth often has a positive impact on value, sometimes one of spectacular proportions.  But such an effect is far from certain.  For example, investors have regularly poured money into the domestic airline business to finance profitless (or worse) growth.  For these investors, it would have been far better if Orville had failed to get off the ground at Kitty Hawk: The more the industry has grown, the worse the disaster for owners.
1992.chinese: 同样，企业增长本身也不能告诉我们多少关于价值的信息。成长确实经常对价值产生正面影响，有时甚至十分惊人，但这种结果远非必然。比如，投资者不断向美国国内航空业投入资金，支持毫无利润、甚至亏损的增长。对于这些投资者，如果奥维尔·莱特当年在小鹰镇未能飞离地面，结果反而更好：整个行业增长得越多，所有者遭受的灾难就越严重。

1992.english:
Growth benefits investors only when the business in point can invest at incremental returns that are enticing - in other words, only when each dollar used to finance the growth creates over a dollar of long-term market value.  In the case of a low-return business requiring incremental funds, growth hurts the investor.

In The Theory of Investment Value, written over 50 years ago, John Burr Williams set forth the equation for value, which we condense here:  The value of any stock, bond or business today is determined by the cash inflows and outflows - discounted at an appropriate interest rate - that can be expected to occur during the remaining life of the asset.  Note that the formula is the same for stocks as for bonds.  Even so, there is an important, and difficult to deal with, difference between the two:  A bond has a coupon and maturity date that define future cash flows; but in the case of equities, the investment analyst must himself estimate the future "coupons."  Furthermore, the quality of management affects the bond coupon only rarely - chiefly when management is so inept or dishonest that payment of interest is suspended.  In contrast, the ability of management can dramatically affect the equity "coupons."
1992.chinese:
只有当企业能够以诱人的增量回报率进行投资时，增长才有利于投资者。换句话说，每投入1美元支持增长，都必须创造超过1美元的长期市场价值。对于需要持续增加资金、却只能赚取低回报的企业，成长会损害投资者的利益。

50多年前，约翰·伯尔·威廉姆斯（John Burr Williams）在《投资价值理论》中提出了估值公式，我们可以将其简化如下：任何股票、债券或企业今天的价值，都取决于该资产剩余存续期间预计会发生的现金流入与流出，按适当利率折算到今天的金额。请注意，股票与债券适用同一个公式。但两者之间有一个重要而且难以处理的区别：债券有票息和到期日，这些条款确定了未来的现金流；股票则不同，分析师必须自行估计其未来的“票息”。此外，管理层的素质很少影响债券票息——主要情形是，无能或不诚实到了导致停付利息的程度。相比之下，管理者的能力可能极大地影响股票的“票息”。

1992.english: The investment shown by the discounted-flows-of-cash calculation to be the cheapest is the one that the investor should purchase - irrespective of whether the business grows or doesn't, displays volatility or smoothness in its earnings, or carries a high price or low in relation to its current earnings and book value.  Moreover, though the value equation has usually shown equities to be cheaper than bonds, that result is not inevitable: When bonds are calculated to be the more attractive investment, they should be bought.
1992.chinese: 按折现现金流计算最便宜的投资，就是投资者应该购买的那一项；无论企业是否增长、利润波动还是平稳、相对于当前利润和账面价值的价格高还是低，都是如此。而且，尽管价值计算通常显示股票比债券便宜，但这并不是必然的。如果计算表明债券更有吸引力，就应该购买债券。

1992.english: Leaving the question of price aside, the best business to own is one that over an extended period can employ large amounts of incremental capital at very high rates of return.  The worst business to own is one that must, or will, do the opposite - that is, consistently employ ever-greater amounts of capital at very low rates of return.  Unfortunately, the first type of business is very hard to find:  Most high-return businesses need relatively little capital.  Shareholders of such a business usually will benefit if it pays out most of its earnings in dividends or makes significant stock repurchases.
1992.chinese: 暂且不考虑价格，最值得拥有的企业，是能够在较长时期内以很高的回报率投入大量新增资本的企业。最糟糕的企业恰好相反：它必须或将会持续投入越来越多的资本，却只能获得很低的回报率。遗憾的是，前一种企业非常难找：大多数高回报企业只需要相对较少的资本。这种企业的股东，通常会因公司将大部分利润作为股息分配，或大量回购股票而受益。

1992.english: Though the mathematical calculations required to evaluate equities are not difficult, an analyst - even one who is experienced and intelligent - can easily go wrong in estimating future "coupons."  At Berkshire, we attempt to deal with this problem in two ways.  First, we try to stick to businesses we believe we understand.  That means they must be relatively simple and stable in character.  If a business is complex or subject to constant change, we're not smart enough to predict future cash flows.  Incidentally, that shortcoming doesn't bother us.  What counts for most people in investing is not how much they know, but rather how realistically they define what they don't know.  An investor needs to do very few things right as long as he or she avoids big mistakes.
1992.chinese: 虽然评价股票所需的数学计算并不困难，但即使经验丰富、聪明的分析师，在估计未来的“票息”时也很容易出错。在伯克希尔，我们尝试用两种方法处理这一问题。首先，我们尽量只投资自己认为能够理解的企业。这意味着，它们的经营特性必须相对简单、稳定。如果一家企业十分复杂，或者不断发生变化，我们就没有足够的智慧预测未来现金流。顺便说一句，这种不足并不困扰我们。对大多数人而言，投资中重要的不是知道多少，而是能否现实地界定自己不知道什么。一个投资者只要避免重大错误，正确做的事情其实不需要太多。

1992.english:
Second, and equally important, we insist on a margin of safety in our purchase price.  If we calculate the value of a common stock to be only slightly higher than its price, we're not interested in buying.  We believe this margin-of-safety principle, so strongly emphasized by Ben Graham, to be the cornerstone of investment success.

其次，同样重要的是，我们坚持购买价格必须留有安全边际。如果计算得出一只普通股的价值只比股价高一点点，我们不会有兴趣购买。我们相信，这项由本杰明·格雷厄姆极力强调的安全边际原则，是投资成功的基石。

1992.english:
(1) Carrying value in our financial statements (2) Fair value as determined by Charlie and me

During 1992 we added to our holdings of ACF debentures, had some of our WPPSS bonds called, and sold our RJR Nabisco position.

Over the years, we've done well with fixed-income investments, having realized from them both large capital gains (including $80 million in 1992) and exceptional current income.  Chrysler Financial, Texaco, Time-Warner, WPPSS and RJR Nabisco were particularly good investments for us.  Meanwhile, our fixed-income losses have been negligible:  We've had thrills but so far no spills.
1992.chinese:
¹ 财务报表中的账面价值。² 查理和我确定的公允价值。

1992年，我们增持了ACF的债券，部分华盛顿州公共电力供应系统债券被提前赎回，并卖出了RJR纳贝斯克（RJR Nabisco）的持仓。

多年来，我们在固定收益投资上表现不错，不仅取得了大额资本利得（1992年就有8,000万美元），也获得了优异的经常性收入。克莱斯勒金融、德士古、时代华纳、华盛顿州公共电力供应系统和RJR纳贝斯克都是特别成功的投资。与此同时，固定收益投资几乎没有给我们带来损失：一路经历了不少惊险，却还没有真正摔过跟头。

1992.english: Despite the success we experienced with our Gillette preferred, which converted to common stock in 1991, and despite our reasonable results with other negotiated purchases of preferreds, our overall performance with such purchases has been inferior to that we have achieved with purchases made in the secondary market. This is actually the result we expected.  It corresponds with our belief that an intelligent investor in common stocks will do better in the secondary market than he will do buying new issues.
1992.chinese: 尽管我们投资吉列优先股取得了成功——它在1991年转换为普通股——其他协议购买的优先股也有合理表现，但总体而言，这类协议投资的结果仍然逊于我们在二级市场直接购买证券的表现。这其实符合我们的预期，也符合我们的看法：聪明的普通股投资者，在二级市场通常会比参与新股发行获得更好的结果。

1992.english: The reason has to do with the way prices are set in each instance.  The secondary market, which is periodically ruled by mass folly, is constantly setting a "clearing" price.  No matter how foolish that price may be, it's what counts for the holder of a stock or bond who needs or wishes to sell, of whom there are always going to be a few at any moment.  In many instances, shares worth x in business value have sold in the market for 1/2x or less.
1992.chinese: 原因与两种市场中的定价方式有关。二级市场不时受到群体性愚蠢支配，但始终会形成一个能够成交的“出清价格”。不管这个价格多么荒唐，对于需要或希望卖出股票、债券的持有人而言，它就是有效价格；而市场中任何时刻总会有少数这样的卖方。许多情况下，内在商业价值为x的股票，会在市场上以1/2x甚至更低价格成交。

1992.english: The new-issue market, on the other hand, is ruled by controlling stockholders and corporations, who can usually select the timing of offerings or, if the market looks unfavorable, can avoid an offering altogether.  Understandably, these sellers are not going to offer any bargains, either by way of a public offering or in a negotiated transaction:  It's rare you'll find x for 1/2x here.  Indeed, in the case of common-stock offerings, selling shareholders are often motivated to unload only when they feel the market is overpaying.  (These sellers, of course, would state that proposition somewhat differently, averring instead that they simply resist selling when the market is underpaying for their goods.)
1992.chinese: 另一方面，新发行市场由控股股东和公司主导，他们通常可以选择发行时机；如果市场行情不好，就干脆不发行。可以理解，这些卖方不会通过公开发行或协议交易主动提供便宜货：在这里几乎找不到价值x却只卖1/2x的资产。事实上，就普通股发行而言，卖出股票的股东往往只有在认为市场价格过高时才愿意出售。（当然，这些卖方会换个说法，声称他们只是拒绝在市场价格过低时出售自己的资产。）

1992.english: To date, our negotiated purchases, as a group, have fulfilled but not exceeded the expectation we set forth in our 1989 Annual Report:  "Our preferred stock investments should produce returns modestly above those achieved by most fixed-income portfolios."  In truth, we would have done better if we could have put the money that went into our negotiated transactions into open-market purchases of the type we like.  But both our size and the general strength of the markets made that difficult to do.
1992.chinese: 到目前为止，我们的协议投资整体实现了、但没有超出1989年年报提出的预期：“我们的优先股投资回报应当略高于大多数固定收益投资组合的回报。”事实上，如果能够将用于协议投资的资金投入我们喜欢的公开市场机会，结果会更好。但我们的规模和当时市场整体走强，使这件事难以实现。

1992.english:
There was one other memorable line in the 1989 Annual Report: "We have no ability to forecast the economics of the investment banking business, the airline industry, or the paper industry."  At the time some of you may have doubted this confession of ignorance. Now, however, even my mother acknowledges its truth.

In the case of our commitment to USAir, industry economics had soured before the ink dried on our check.  As I've previously mentioned, it was I who happily jumped into the pool; no one pushed me.  Yes, I knew the industry would be ruggedly competitive, but I did not expect its leaders to engage in prolonged kamikaze behavior.  In the last two years, airline companies have acted as if they are members of a competitive tontine, which they wish to bring to its conclusion as rapidly as possible.
1992.chinese:
1989年年报还有一句值得回忆的话：“我们没有能力预测投资银行业务、航空业或造纸业的经济特性。”当时各位中的某些人或许怀疑我是否真的如此无知。如今，连我母亲都承认这是事实了。

至于我们对全美航空的投资，支票上的墨迹尚未干透，行业经济状况就开始恶化。我以前提到过，是我自己高高兴兴跳进这个游泳池的，没有人推我。没错，我知道行业竞争会异常激烈，但没有预料到行业领头羊会长期采取神风特攻队式的行为。过去两年，航空公司表现得仿佛参加了一种“最后幸存者赢得奖金”的互助赌局，而且大家都想尽快把它进行到结局。

1992.english: Amidst this turmoil, Seth Schofield, CEO of USAir, has done a truly extraordinary job in repositioning the airline.  He was particularly courageous in accepting a strike last fall that, had it been lengthy,  might well have bankrupted the company. Capitulating to the striking union, however, would have been equally disastrous:  The company was burdened with wage costs and work rules that were considerably more onerous than those encumbering its major competitors, and it was clear that over time any high-cost producer faced extinction.  Happily for everyone, the strike was settled in a few days.
1992.chinese: 在这种混乱之中，全美航空首席执行官塞思·斯科菲尔德（Seth Schofield）在重整公司方面做得极为出色。去年秋天，他勇敢地承受了一场罢工；如果持续太久，这场罢工很可能让公司破产。不过，向罢工工会屈服同样会带来灾难：公司承担的工资成本和工作规则负担都远高于主要竞争对手，很明显，任何高成本的生产者最终都难以生存。幸运的是，罢工在几天内就得到解决。

1992.english:
A competitively-beset business such as USAir requires far more managerial skill than does a business with fine economics. Unfortunately, though, the near-term reward for skill in the airline business is simply survival, not prosperity.

In early 1993, USAir took a major step toward assuring survival - and eventual prosperity - by accepting British Airways' offer to make a substantial, but minority, investment in the company.  In connection with this transaction, Charlie and I were asked to join the USAir board.  We agreed, though this makes five outside board memberships for me, which is more than I believe advisable for an active CEO.  Even so, if an investee's management and directors believe it particularly important that Charlie and I join its board, we are glad to do so.  We expect the managers of our investees to work hard to increase the value of the businesses they run, and there are times when large owners should do their bit as well.
1992.chinese:
像全美航空这样面临激烈竞争的企业，需要的管理本领远多于一家经济特性良好的企业。然而不幸的是，在航空业里，出色管理的短期回报只是活下来，而不是繁荣发展。

1993年初，全美航空为确保生存、并最终走向繁荣采取了重大举措：接受英国航空公司提出的投资方案，由其持有公司一笔相当大的少数股权。与这项交易相关，查理和我受邀加入全美航空董事会，我们接受了邀请。这样一来，我担任的外部董事职务达到五个，比我认为一个在职首席执行官应当承担的数量更多。不过，如果被投资企业的管理层和董事认为查理和我加入董事会特别重要，我们仍愿意效劳。我们期待所投资公司的管理者努力提高企业价值，有些时候，大股东也应该承担自己的责任。

1992.english:
## Two New Accounting Rules and a Plea for One More

A new accounting rule having to do with deferred taxes becomes effective in 1993.  It undoes a dichotomy in our books that I have described in previous annual reports and that relates to the accrued taxes carried against the unrealized appreciation in our investment portfolio.  At yearend 1992, that appreciation amounted to $7.6 billion.  Against $6.4 billion of that, we carried taxes at the current 34% rate.  Against the remainder of $1.2 billion, we carried an accrual of 28%, the tax rate in effect when that portion of the appreciation occurred.  The new accounting rule says we must henceforth accrue all deferred tax at the current rate, which to us seems sensible.
1992.chinese:
## 两项新会计规则，以及我对第三项规则的呼吁

1993年，一项关于递延所得税的新会计规则开始生效。它消除了我们账面上一种不一致的处理方式。我在过去的年报中曾谈到过这种差异，它涉及我们为投资组合未实现增值计提的所得税。1992年末，这类增值总额为76亿美元。其中64亿美元按现行34%的税率计提税款，余下12亿美元仍按这部分增值发生时适用的28%税率计提。新规则要求我们今后全部按照现行税率计提递延所得税。在我们看来，这是合理的。

1992.english:
The new marching orders mean that in the first quarter of 1993 we will apply a 34% rate to all of our unrealized appreciation, thereby increasing the tax liability and reducing net worth by $70 million.  The new rule also will cause us to make other minor changes in our calculation of deferred taxes.

Future changes in tax rates will be reflected immediately in the liability for deferred taxes and, correspondingly, in net worth.  The impact could well be substantial.  Nevertheless, what is important in the end is the tax rate at the time we sell securities, when unrealized appreciation becomes realized.
1992.chinese:
新命令意味着，1993年第一季度我们将对全部未实现增值采用34%的税率，使所得税负债增加、净资产减少7,000万美元。新规则还会使我们对递延所得税的计算作出其他一些较小调整。

今后税率变化会立即反映在递延所得税负债中，并相应影响净资产，影响可能相当可观。不过最终重要的是我们出售证券、未实现增值变成已实现增值时适用的税率。

1992.english: Another major accounting change, whose implementation is required by January 1, 1993, mandates that businesses recognize their present-value liability for post-retirement health benefits. Though GAAP has previously required recognition of pensions to be paid in the future, it has illogically ignored the costs that companies will then have to bear for health benefits.  The new rule will force many companies to record a huge balance-sheet liability (and a consequent reduction in net worth) and also henceforth to recognize substantially higher costs when they are calculating annual profits.
1992.chinese: 另一项重大会计变化，要求最迟于1993年1月1日执行：企业必须确认退休后医疗福利义务的现值负债。GAAP以前要求确认未来养老金义务，却不合逻辑地忽略企业未来必须承担的医疗福利成本。新规则将迫使许多公司在资产负债表上记录巨额负债（相应减少净资产），今后计算年度利润时，也必须确认明显增加的费用。

1992.english: In making acquisitions, Charlie and I have tended to avoid companies with significant post-retirement liabilities.  As a result, Berkshire's present liability and future costs for post- retirement health benefits - though we now have 22,000 employees - are inconsequential.  I need to admit, though, that we had a near miss:  In 1982 I made a huge mistake in committing to buy a company burdened by extraordinary post-retirement health obligations. Luckily, though, the transaction fell through for reasons beyond our control.  Reporting on this episode in the 1982 annual report, I said:  "If we were to introduce graphics to this report, illustrating favorable business developments of the past year, two blank pages depicting this blown deal would be the appropriate centerfold."  Even so, I wasn't expecting things to get as bad as they did.  Another buyer appeared, the business soon went bankrupt and was shut down, and thousands of workers found those bountiful health-care promises to be largely worthless.
1992.chinese: 在收购企业时，查理和我倾向于回避那些承担重大退休后福利义务的公司。因此，虽然伯克希尔现在有22,000名员工，我们当前承担的退休后医疗福利负债和未来成本仍然微不足道。不过，我必须承认，我们曾经险些酿成大祸：1982年，我承诺购买一家背负异常沉重退休后医疗福利义务的公司，这是一个巨大的错误。幸运的是，交易由于我们无法控制的原因流产了。在1982年年报中回顾这件事时，我曾写道：“如果年报要增加图片来表现去年经营上的好消息，那么，中间跨页最合适的插图，就是代表这笔交易流产的两张白纸。”即便如此，我也没有料到情况会变得那么糟糕。后来另一位买家接手，这家企业不久就破产关闭，数千名员工发现那些丰厚的医疗福利承诺大部分成了空话。

1992.english: In recent decades, no CEO would have dreamed of going to his board with the proposition that his company become an insurer of uncapped post-retirement health benefits that other corporations chose to install.  A CEO didn't need to be a medical expert to know that lengthening life expectancies and soaring health costs would guarantee an insurer a financial battering from such a business. Nevertheless, many a manager blithely committed his own company to a self-insurance plan embodying precisely the same promises - and thereby doomed his shareholders to suffer the inevitable consequences.  In health-care, open-ended promises have created open-ended liabilities that in a few cases loom so large as to threaten the global competitiveness of major American industries.
1992.chinese: 过去几十年间，没有哪位首席执行官会梦想着向董事会提议，让自己的公司成为其他企业所承诺的、赔付金额没有上限的退休后医疗福利的保险人。管理者无须成为医疗专家，就知道寿命延长和医疗成本飞涨必将重创承保这种业务的保险公司。然而，许多管理者却轻率地承诺，由自己的企业承担完全一样的福利责任，实行自我保险计划，从而注定让股东承担后果。在医疗保健领域，没有上限的承诺创造了没有上限的负债；少数情况下，这些负债规模已大到威胁美国一些重要行业的全球竞争力。

1992.english: I believe part of the reason for this reckless behavior was that accounting rules did not, for so long, require the booking of post-retirement health costs as they were incurred.  Instead, the rules allowed cash-basis accounting, which vastly understated the liabilities that were building up.  In effect, the attitude of both managements and their accountants toward these liabilities was "out-of-sight, out-of-mind."  Ironically, some of these same managers would be quick to criticize Congress for employing "cash- basis" thinking in respect to Social Security promises or other programs creating future liabilities of size.
1992.chinese: 我认为，这种鲁莽行为的部分原因，在于会计准则长期不要求在退休后医疗福利成本形成时就予入账。规则反而允许现金收付制会计处理，严重低估了不断积累的负债。事实上，管理者和会计师对这些负债采取的态度是“眼不见，心不烦”。讽刺的是，其中一些管理者会立即批评国会在社会保障承诺或其他产生巨额未来负债的计划上采用同样的“现金收付制”思路。

1992.english:
Managers thinking about accounting issues should never forget one of Abraham Lincoln's favorite riddles:  "How many legs does a dog have if you call his tail a leg?"  The answer:  "Four, because calling a tail a leg does not make it a leg."  It behooves managers to remember that Abe's right even if an auditor is willing to certify that the tail is a leg.

---
1992.chinese:
考虑会计问题的管理者，不应忘记林肯最喜欢的一则谜语：“如果你把狗的尾巴称为一条腿，那么狗有几条腿？”答案是：“四条，因为把尾巴叫作腿，不会使它真正变成腿。”管理者最好记住，即使审计师愿意签字证明尾巴是一条腿，林肯的答案仍然正确。

---

1992.english: The most egregious case of let's-not-face-up-to-reality behavior by executives and accountants has occurred in the world of stock options.  In Berkshire's 1985 annual report, I laid out my opinions about the use and misuse of options.  But even when options are structured properly, they are accounted for in ways that make no sense.  The lack of logic is not accidental:  For decades, much of the business world has waged war against accounting rulemakers, trying to keep the costs of stock options from being reflected in the profits of the corporations that issue them.
1992.chinese: 管理人员和会计师最严重的拒绝面对现实的例子，发生在股票期权领域。1985年年报中，我曾阐述自己关于股票期权使用与滥用的观点。然而，即使期权安排合理，对它们的会计处理仍然毫无道理。这种缺乏逻辑并非偶然：几十年来，商界许多人士一直与会计准则制定者交战，试图阻止公司发行股票期权的成本反映在利润里。

1992.english:
Typically, executives have argued that options are hard to value and that therefore their costs should be ignored.  At other times managers have said that assigning a cost to options would injure small start-up businesses.  Sometimes they have even solemnly declared that "out-of-the-money" options (those with an exercise price equal to or above the current market price) have no value when they are issued.

Oddly, the Council of Institutional Investors has chimed in with a variation on that theme, opining that options should not be viewed as a cost because they "aren't dollars out of a company's coffers."  I see this line of reasoning as offering exciting possibilities to American corporations for instantly improving their reported profits.  For example, they could eliminate the cost of insurance by paying for it with options.  So if you're a CEO and subscribe to this "no cash-no cost" theory of accounting, I'll make you an offer you can't refuse:  Give us a call at Berkshire and we will happily sell you insurance in exchange for a bundle of long- term options on your company's stock.
1992.chinese:
高管们通常辩称，期权难以估值，所以应该忽略其成本。有时又声称，确认期权成本会伤害小型初创企业。有时甚至一本正经地宣称，“价外”期权（行权价等于或高于当前市价的期权）在授予时没有价值。

令人奇怪的是，机构投资者委员会也附和了其中一种说法，认为期权不应被视为成本，因为它们“不会让公司的金库流出美元”。在我看来，这种逻辑为美国公司瞬间改善财报利润提供了激动人心的可能性。比如，公司可以通过用期权支付保费来消除保险成本。因此，如果你是一位首席执行官，而且赞同这种“没有现金支出就没有成本”的会计理论，我愿意给你一个无法拒绝的提议：打电话给伯克希尔，我们很乐意用保险交换一大包贵公司股票的长期期权。

1992.english: Shareholders should understand that companies incur costs when they deliver something of value to another party and not just when cash changes hands.  Moreover, it is both silly and cynical to say that an important item of cost should not be recognized simply because it can't be quantified with pinpoint precision.  Right now, accounting abounds with imprecision.  After all, no manager or auditor knows how long a 747 is going to last, which means he also does not know what the yearly depreciation charge for the plane should be.  No one knows with any certainty what a bank's annual loan loss charge ought to be.  And the estimates of losses that property-casualty companies make are notoriously inaccurate.
1992.chinese: 股东应该理解，只要公司向他人交付有价值的东西，就会发生经济成本，而不仅仅是在现金发生转移时才有成本。再者，因为一项重要成本不能被精确到小数点后若干位，就主张不应确认它，既愚蠢又虚伪。如今的会计本来就充满估计误差。毕竟，没有管理者或审计师知道一架波音747飞机究竟能使用多少年，因此也不知道每年的正确折旧费用是多少。没有人能够确切知道银行每年应计提多少贷款损失。财产保险公司对损失的估计更是出了名的不准确。

1992.english: Does this mean that these important items of cost should be ignored simply because they can't be quantified with absolute accuracy?  Of course not.  Rather, these costs should be estimated by honest and experienced people and then recorded.  When you get right down to it, what other item of major but hard-to-precisely- calculate cost - other, that is, than stock options - does the accounting profession say should be ignored in the calculation of earnings?
1992.chinese: 难道这意味着，因为这些重要成本无法绝对精确地量化，就可以把它们忽略吗？当然不是。相反，应当由诚实且有经验的人估计这些成本，然后予以确认。说到底，除了股票期权之外，还有哪项重大但难以精确计算的成本，会计界却主张计算利润时应该忽略？

1992.english: Moreover, options are just not that difficult to value. Admittedly, the difficulty is increased by the fact that the options given to executives are restricted in various ways.  These restrictions affect value.  They do not, however, eliminate it.  In fact, since I'm in the mood for offers, I'll make one to any executive who is granted a restricted option, even though it may be out of the money:  On the day of issue, Berkshire will pay him or her a substantial sum for the right to any future gain he or she realizes on the option.  So if you find a CEO who says his newly- issued options have little or no value, tell him to try us out.  In truth, we have far more confidence in our ability to determine an appropriate price to pay for an option than we have in our ability to determine the proper depreciation rate for our corporate jet.
1992.chinese: 此外，期权估值其实没有那么困难。诚然，授予管理人员的期权附带各种限制，使估值难度增加。这些限制会影响价值，却不会消除价值。既然我今天兴致正高，索性再向任何获得受限制期权的高管提出一项交易——即使期权目前处于价外状态也没有关系：在授予当天，伯克希尔愿意支付一笔可观金额，以取得该高管将来从期权中获得的任何收益。因此，如果你发现某位首席执行官宣称新授予的期权几乎没有价值，就请他来找我们。实际上，对于如何为一份期权确定合适的出价，我们比如何为公司公务机确定正确的折旧率更有信心。

1992.english:
It seems to me that the realities of stock options can be summarized quite simply:  If options aren't a form of compensation, what are they?  If compensation isn't an expense, what is it?  And, if expenses shouldn't go into the calculation of earnings, where in the world should they go?

The accounting profession and the SEC should be shamed by the fact that they have long let themselves be muscled by business executives on the option-accounting issue.  Additionally, the lobbying that executives engage in may have an unfortunate by- product:  In my opinion, the business elite risks losing its credibility on issues of significance to society - about which it may have much of value to say - when it advocates the incredible on issues of significance to itself.
1992.chinese:
在我看来，股票期权的现实可以用三个简单问题概括：如果期权不是一种薪酬，那它是什么？如果薪酬不是费用，那它是什么？如果费用不应该计入利润的计算，那它到底应该放到哪里去？

会计界和美国证券交易委员会理应为自己长期以来在期权会计问题上被企业高管施压而屈服感到羞愧。此外，高管们的游说可能带来一个不幸的副作用：在关乎自身利益的问题上，他们为难以置信的观点辩护，可能使商界精英失去在社会重要问题上的公信力，而对于那些问题，他们本来有可能提出很有价值的意见。

1992.english:
Miscellaneous

We have two pieces of regrettable news this year.  First, Gladys Kaiser, my friend and assistant for twenty-five years, will give up the latter post after the 1993 annual meeting, though she will certainly remain my friend forever.  Gladys and I have been a team, and though I knew her retirement was coming, it is still a jolt.

Secondly, in September, Verne McKenzie relinquished his role as Chief Financial Officer after a 30-year association with me that began when he was the outside auditor of Buffett Partnership, Ltd. Verne is staying on as a consultant, and though that job description is often a euphemism, in this case it has real meaning. I expect Verne to continue to fill an important role at Berkshire but to do so at his own pace.  Marc Hamburg, Verne's understudy for five years, has succeeded him as Chief Financial Officer.
1992.chinese:
## 其他事项

今年有两条令人遗憾的消息。第一，我相识多年、担任我助理25年的朋友格拉迪丝·凯泽（Gladys Kaiser），将在1993年股东大会后卸下助理职务，不过她当然永远都是我的朋友。格拉迪丝和我一直是一个团队。虽然我早知道她会退休，事情真正发生时仍然让我感到震动。

第二，去年9月，弗恩·麦肯齐（Verne McKenzie）在与我合作30年后，卸下了首席财务官职务。我们最初的合作始于他担任巴菲特合伙企业外部审计师之时。弗恩将继续担任顾问，尽管“顾问”这个职位名称常常只是一个委婉的说法，但在这里它具有实实在在的意义。我期望他继续在伯克希尔发挥重要作用，只是按照自己的节奏工作。过去五年一直跟随弗恩学习的马克·汉堡（Marc Hamburg），已经接任首席财务官。

1992.english: I recall that one woman, upon being asked to describe the perfect spouse, specified an archeologist: "The older I get," she said, "the more he'll be interested in me."  She would have liked my tastes:  I treasure those extraordinary Berkshire managers who are working well past normal retirement age and who concomitantly are achieving results much superior to those of their younger competitors.  While I understand and empathize with the decision of Verne and Gladys to retire when the calendar says it's time, theirs is not a step I wish to encourage.  It's hard to teach a new dog old tricks.
1992.chinese: 我记得曾有一位女士被问及理想伴侣应该是什么样的人，她选择了考古学家，并解释说：“我年龄越大，他就会对我越感兴趣。”她一定会喜欢我的品味：我十分珍视那些超过通常退休年龄仍在工作的伯克希尔优秀管理者，他们取得的成绩往往远胜年轻竞争者。对于弗恩和格拉迪丝按照日历提醒的时间退休，我完全理解并感同身受，但我不希望鼓励别人效仿。要教一只新狗学会老把戏，实在不容易。

1992.english:
---

I am a moderate in my views about retirement compared to Rose Blumkin, better known as Mrs. B.  At 99, she continues to work seven days a week.  And about her, I have some particularly good news.

You will remember that after her family sold 80% of Nebraska Furniture Mart (NFM) to Berkshire in 1983, Mrs. B continued to be Chairman and run the carpet operation.  In 1989, however, she left because of a managerial disagreement and opened up her own operation next door in a large building that she had owned for several years.  In her new business, she ran the carpet section but leased out other home-furnishings departments.
1992.chinese:
---

论对退休的看法，我比罗丝·布卢姆金（Rose Blumkin），也就是人们熟知的B夫人，温和得多。她已经99岁，仍然每周工作七天。关于她，我还有一些特别好的消息。

各位记得，1983年她的家族把内布拉斯加家具卖场（NFM）80%的权益出售给伯克希尔之后，B夫人仍担任董事长，并负责地毯业务。但在1989年，由于一次管理分歧，她离开了公司，在隔壁一栋多年前就属于她的大楼里开办自己的企业。在新店里，她亲自负责地毯部门，其他家居用品部门则出租给别人经营。

1992.english:
At the end of last year, Mrs. B decided to sell her building and land to NFM.  She'll continue, however, to run her carpet business at its current location (no sense slowing down just when you're hitting full stride).  NFM will set up shop alongside her, in that same building, thereby making a major addition to its furniture business.

I am delighted that Mrs. B has again linked up with us.  Her business story has no parallel and I have always been a fan of hers, whether she was a partner or a competitor.  But believe me, partner is better.
1992.chinese:
去年年末，B夫人决定将自己的大楼和土地出售给NFM。不过，她会继续在原址经营地毯业务（正处于巅峰状态，当然没有必要慢下来）。NFM则将在同一栋楼里与她比邻开店，大幅扩充家具业务。

我很高兴B夫人再次与我们走到一起。她的商业经历无与伦比，不论她是我们的伙伴还是竞争对手，我一直是她的支持者。但请相信我，当伙伴更好。

1992.english:
This time around, Mrs. B graciously offered to sign a non- compete agreement - and I, having been incautious on this point when she was 89, snapped at the deal.  Mrs. B belongs in the Guinness Book of World Records on many counts.  Signing a non- compete at 99 merely adds one more.

---

Ralph Schey, CEO of Scott Fetzer and a manager who I hope is with us at 99 also, hit a grand slam last year when that company earned a record $110 million pre-tax.  What's even more impressive is that Scott Fetzer achieved such earnings while employing only $116 million of equity capital.  This extraordinary result is not the product of leverage:  The company uses only minor amounts of borrowed money (except for the debt it employs - appropriately - in its finance subsidiary).
1992.chinese:
这一次，B夫人慷慨地提出愿意签署竞业禁止协议。我在她89岁时曾在这一问题上考虑不周，这次便立刻抓住了机会。B夫人有许多成就都值得写进《吉尼斯世界纪录大全》，99岁时签署竞业禁止协议，只不过又添了一项。

---

斯科特与费策公司首席执行官拉尔夫·谢伊（Ralph Schey）也是我希望能与我们合作到99岁的经理人。去年，他打出了一记满垒本垒打：公司创下1.10亿美元的税前利润纪录。更令人印象深刻的是，斯科特与费策取得这些利润，所使用的股东权益资本只有1.16亿美元。这一异常出色的成绩并非依靠杠杆：除金融子公司适当使用的债务外，公司只借入了极少量资金。

1992.english: Scott Fetzer now operates with a significantly smaller investment in both inventory and fixed assets than it had when we bought it in 1986.  This means the company has been able to distribute more than 100% of its earnings to Berkshire during our seven years of ownership while concurrently increasing its earnings stream - which was excellent to begin with - by a lot.  Ralph just keeps on outdoing himself, and Berkshire shareholders owe him a great deal.
1992.chinese: 现在，斯科特与费策占用的存货和固定资产资金，都显著低于我们1986年收购时的水平。这意味着，在我们持有公司的七年间，它向伯克希尔分配的现金累计超过了其利润的100%，同时还使原本已经十分出色的利润水平进一步大幅提高。拉尔夫不断超越自己，伯克希尔股东非常感谢他。

1992.english:
---

Those readers with particularly sharp eyes will note that our corporate expense fell from $5.6 million in 1991 to $4.2 million in 1992.  Perhaps you will think that I have sold our corporate jet, The Indefensible.  Forget it!  I find the thought of retiring the plane even more revolting than the thought of retiring the Chairman.  (In this matter I've demonstrated uncharacteristic flexibility:  For years I argued passionately against corporate jets.  But finally my dogma was run over by my karma.)
1992.chinese:
---

眼尖的读者会发现，总部费用从1991年的560万美元下降到1992年的420万美元。也许各位会以为我卖掉了公司公务机——那架名叫“无可辩护号”的飞机。想都别想！我发现，让飞机退休的念头，比让董事长退休更令我反感。（这件事上，我展示了不符合自己平时性格的灵活性：多年来，我曾慷慨激昂地反对公司公务机，最后却是自己的业力撞翻了教条。）

1992.english: Our reduction in corporate overhead actually came about because those expenses were especially high in 1991, when we incurred a one-time environmental charge relating to alleged pre- 1970 actions of our textile operation.  Now that things are back to normal, our after-tax overhead costs are under 1% of our reported operating earnings and less than 1/2 of 1% of our look-through earnings.  We have no legal, personnel, public relations, investor relations, or strategic planning departments.  In turn this means we don't need support personnel such as guards, drivers, messengers, etc.  Finally, except for Verne, we employ no consultants.  Professor Parkinson would like our operation - though Charlie, I must say, still finds it outrageously fat.
1992.chinese: 总部费用的下降，实际上是因为1991年的费用特别高，那一年我们为纺织业务据称在1970年以前的活动计提了一笔一次性环境费用。如今情况恢复正常，总部税后费用不到财报经营利润的1%，也不到穿透利润的0.5%。我们没有法务、人事、公共关系、投资者关系或战略规划部门。因此，我们也不需要保安、司机、信使等支持人员。最后，除了弗恩之外，我们不聘请顾问。研究组织规模膨胀的帕金森教授一定会喜欢我们的经营方式——不过不得不说，查理仍认为我们的总部臃肿得不可理喻。

1992.english: At some companies, corporate expense runs 10% or more of operating earnings.  The tithing that operations thus makes to headquarters not only hurts earnings, but more importantly slashes capital values.  If the business that spends 10% on headquarters' costs achieves earnings at its operating levels identical to those achieved by the business that incurs costs of only 1%, shareholders of the first enterprise suffer a 9% loss in the value of their holdings simply because of corporate overhead.  Charlie and I have observed no correlation between high corporate costs and good corporate performance.  In fact, we see the simpler, low-cost operation as more likely to operate effectively than its bureaucratic brethren.  We're admirers of the Wal-Mart, Nucor, Dover, GEICO, Golden West Financial and Price Co. models.
1992.chinese: 有些公司的总部费用占经营利润的10%甚至更多。业务部门向总部缴纳的这笔“什一税”不仅降低利润，更重要的是削减资本价值。假设两家企业在业务层面取得完全相同的利润，其中一家将10%用于总部费用，另一家只花1%，那么前一家企业的股东仅仅因为总部开支，持股价值就会损失9%。查理和我没有观察到高总部费用与良好公司业绩之间存在相关关系。事实上，我们认为组织简洁、成本低廉的企业，比官僚机构庞大的企业更有可能高效经营。我们欣赏沃尔玛、纽柯、都福、GEICO、Golden West Financial和Price Co.等公司的模式。

1992.english:
---

Late last year Berkshire's stock price crossed $10,000. Several shareholders have mentioned to me that the high price causes them problems:  They like to give shares away each year and find themselves impeded by the tax rule that draws a distinction between annual gifts of $10,000 or under to a single individual and those above $10,000.  That is, those gifts no greater than $10,000 are completely tax-free; those above $10,000 require the donor to use up a portion of his or her lifetime exemption from gift and estate taxes, or, if that exemption has been exhausted, to pay gift taxes.
1992.chinese:
---

去年年末，伯克希尔股价突破10,000美元。有几位股东向我提到，高股价给他们带来了麻烦：他们喜欢每年赠送股票，但税法把一年向同一个人赠送不超过10,000美元的礼物，与超过10,000美元的礼物区别对待。也就是说，价值不超过10,000美元的礼物完全免税；超过这一数额，则必须消耗赠与者终身享有的部分赠与及遗产税免税额度；如果额度已耗尽，就必须缴纳赠与税。

1992.english:
I can suggest three ways to address this problem.  The first would be useful to a married shareholder, who can give up to $20,000 annually to a single recipient, as long as the donor files a gift tax return containing his or her spouse's written consent to gifts made during the year.

Secondly, a shareholder, married or not, can make a bargain sale.  Imagine, for example, that Berkshire is selling for $12,000 and that one wishes to make only a $10,000 gift.  In that case, sell the stock to the giftee for $2,000.  (Caution:  You will be taxed on the amount, if any, by which the sales price to your giftee exceeds your tax basis.)
1992.chinese:
我可以提出三种解决方法。第一种适用于已婚股东：只要赠与者提交赠与税申报表，并附上配偶同意当年赠与的书面声明，就可以每年向同一个受赠人赠送最多20,000美元的礼物。

第二，无论是否已婚，股东都可以采取低价出售的方式。例如，假设伯克希尔每股售价为12,000美元，而你只想赠送价值10,000美元的礼物，那么可以把股票以2,000美元的价格卖给受赠人。（请注意：如果出售所得超过股票的税务成本，超出部分须缴税。）

1992.english:
Finally, you can establish a partnership with people to whom you are making gifts, fund it with Berkshire shares, and simply give percentage interests in the partnership away each year.  These interests can be for any value that you select.  If the value is $10,000 or less, the gift will be tax-free.

We issue the customary warning:  Consult with your own tax advisor before taking action on any of the more esoteric methods of gift-making.
1992.chinese:
第三，你可以与受赠人设立合伙企业，以伯克希尔股票出资，然后每年赠送合伙企业一定比例的权益。这些权益可以对应你选择的任何价值。如果不超过10,000美元，赠与就可以免税。

我们照例提醒各位：在采取任何较为复杂的赠与方法之前，请咨询自己的税务顾问。

1992.english: We hold to the view about stock splits that we set forth in the 1983 Annual Report.  Overall, we believe our owner-related policies - including the no-split policy - have helped us assemble a body of shareholders that is the best associated with any widely- held American corporation.  Our shareholders think and behave like rational long-term owners and view the business much as Charlie and I do.  Consequently, our stock consistently trades in a price range that is sensibly related to intrinsic value.
1992.chinese: 关于股票拆分，我们坚持1983年年报阐述的观点。总体而言，我们相信，与股东有关的政策——包括不拆股政策——帮助我们形成了一群在美国广泛持股上市公司中最出色的股东。我们的股东像理性的长期所有者那样思考和行动，看待公司的方式与查理和我基本一致。因此，伯克希尔股价始终在与内在价值具有合理联系的范围内交易。

1992.english: Additionally, we believe that our shares turn over far less actively than do the shares of any other widely-held company.  The frictional costs of trading - which act as a major "tax" on the owners of many companies - are virtually non-existent at Berkshire. (The market-making skills of Jim Maguire, our New York Stock Exchange specialist, definitely help to keep these costs low.) Obviously a split would not change this situation dramatically. Nonetheless, there is no way that our shareholder group would be upgraded by the new shareholders enticed by a split.  Instead we believe that modest degradation would occur.
1992.chinese: 此外，我们相信，与任何其他广泛持股公司相比，伯克希尔股票的换手活动都少得多。交易的摩擦成本，对许多公司所有者而言相当于一项沉重的“税”，但在伯克希尔几乎可以忽略不计。（纽约证券交易所特约做市商吉姆·马奎尔（Jim Maguire）的做市能力无疑也帮助压低了这些成本。）显然，拆股不会使这种情况发生剧烈变化。不过，拆股吸引来的新股东，无法提高我们股东群体的质量。相反，我们认为质量可能略有下降。

1992.english:
---

As I mentioned earlier, on December 16th we called our zero- coupon, convertible debentures for payment on January 4, 1993. These obligations bore interest at 5 1/2%, a low cost for funds when they were issued in 1989, but an unattractive rate for us at the time of call.

The debentures could have been redeemed at the option of the holder in September 1994, and 5 1/2% money available for no longer than that is not now of interest to us.  Furthermore, Berkshire shareholders are disadvantaged by having a conversion option outstanding.  At the time we issued the debentures, this disadvantage was offset by the attractive interest rate they carried; by late 1992, it was not.
1992.chinese:
---

正如我前面提到的，去年12月16日，我们宣布赎回零息可转换债券，并于1993年1月4日支付。这些债券于1989年发行，计息率为5.5%，在当时属于低成本资金，但到决定赎回时，对我们而言已不再有吸引力。

债券持有人本可以选择在1994年9月要求赎回，但如今我们对一笔最多只能使用到那时、成本却达5.5%的资金已经没有兴趣。此外，未到期的转股权会给伯克希尔股东带来不利影响。发行债券时，较低的利率足以补偿这一不利影响；到1992年末，就不再如此了。

1992.english:
In general, we continue to have an aversion to debt, particularly the short-term kind.  But we are willing to incur modest amounts of debt when it is both properly structured and of significant benefit to shareholders.

---

About 97% of all eligible shares participated in Berkshire's 1992 shareholder-designated contributions program.  Contributions made through the program were $7.6 million, and 2,810 charities were recipients.  I'm considering increasing these contributions in the future at a rate greater than the increase in Berkshire's book value, and I would be glad to hear from you as to your thinking about this idea.
1992.chinese:
总体而言，我们仍然不喜欢债务，尤其是短期债务。不过，如果债务结构合理，而且能为股东带来重大利益，我们也愿意适度举债。

---

约97%的符合条件股份参与了伯克希尔1992年股东指定捐赠计划。通过这一计划捐出了760万美元，共有2,810家慈善机构获得捐赠。我正在考虑今后让捐赠总额的增速超过伯克希尔账面价值的增长率，也很希望听到各位对此的看法。

1992.english:
We suggest that new shareholders read the description of our shareholder-designated contributions program that appears on pages 48-49. To participate in future programs, you must make sure your shares are registered in the name of the actual owner, not in the nominee name of a broker, bank or depository.  Shares not so registered on August 31, 1993 will be ineligible for the 1993 program.

In addition to the shareholder-designated contributions that Berkshire distributes, managers of our operating businesses make contributions, including merchandise, averaging about $2.0 million annually.  These contributions support local charities, such as The United Way, and produce roughly commensurate benefits for our businesses.
1992.chinese:
我们建议新股东阅读原年报第48—49页对股东指定捐赠计划的介绍。若想参加今后的计划，请确保股份登记在实际所有人名下，而不是以经纪商、银行或托管机构的代持名义登记。1993年8月31日尚未按此办理的股份，将无法参加1993年的计划。

除了伯克希尔通过股东指定计划分配的捐款，我们旗下各经营企业的管理者也会进行捐赠，包括实物商品，平均每年价值约200万美元。这些捐赠支持联合劝募会等地方慈善机构，并为我们的企业带来大体相当的利益。

1992.english:
However, neither our operating managers nor officers of the parent company use Berkshire funds to make contributions to broad national programs or charitable activities of special personal interest to them, except to the extent they do so as shareholders. If your employees, including your CEO, wish to give to their alma maters or other institutions to which they feel a personal attachment, we believe they should use their own money, not yours.

---
1992.chinese:
不过，除了以股东身份参与捐赠的情形外，无论经营企业管理者还是母公司高管，都不会使用伯克希尔资金捐助全国性的大型活动，或捐给与自己有特殊私人关系的慈善事业。如果你的雇员——包括首席执行官——希望向母校或其他有私人感情的机构捐款，我们认为他们应该用自己的钱，而不是你的钱。

---

1992.english:
This year the Annual Meeting will be held at the Orpheum Theater in downtown Omaha at 9:30 a.m. on Monday, April 26, 1993. A record 1,700 people turned up for the meeting last year, but that number still leaves plenty of room at the Orpheum.

We recommend that you get your hotel reservations early at one of these hotels: (1) The Radisson-Redick Tower, a small (88 rooms) but nice hotel across the street from the Orpheum; (2) the much larger Red Lion Hotel, located about a five-minute walk from the Orpheum; or (3) the Marriott, located in West Omaha about 100 yards from Borsheim's, which is a twenty minute drive from downtown. We will have buses at the Marriott that will leave at 8:30 and 8:45 for the meeting and return after it ends.
1992.chinese:
今年的股东大会将于1993年4月26日星期一上午9时30分，在奥马哈市中心的奥菲姆剧院举行。去年有创纪录的1,700人到会，但剧院仍然有足够座位。

我们建议各位尽早预订以下酒店之一：（1）Radisson-Redick Tower，一家只有88间客房但条件不错的小酒店，就在奥菲姆剧院对面；（2）规模大得多的Red Lion Hotel，步行到剧院约五分钟；（3）位于奥马哈西部的万豪酒店，距波仙珠宝约100码，驾车到市中心约20分钟。我们将安排巴士于上午8时30分和8时45分从万豪出发前往会场，并在会议结束后送大家返回。

1992.english:
Charlie and I always enjoy the meeting, and we hope you can make it. The quality of our shareholders is reflected in the quality of the questions we get: We have never attended an annual meeting anywhere that features such a consistently high level of intelligent, owner-related questions.

An attachment to our proxy material explains how you can obtain the card you will need for admission to the meeting. With the admission card, we will enclose information about parking facilities located near the Orpheum. If you are driving, come a little early. Nearby lots fill up quickly and you may have to walk a few blocks.
1992.chinese:
查理和我一直很喜欢股东大会，希望各位能够出席。我们股东的素质，反映在他们提出的问题质量上：我们从未参加过其他任何一家公司的股东大会，能持续听到如此高水平、真正从所有者角度提出的问题。

委托投票材料的附件说明了如何取得参加会议所需的入场卡。我们会随入场卡附上奥菲姆剧院附近停车设施的信息。如果驾车前来，请稍早一些到达。附近停车场很快就会停满，你可能需要步行几个街区。

1992.english: As usual, we will have buses to take you to Nebraska Furniture Mart and Borsheim's after the meeting and to take you from there to downtown hotels or the airport later. I hope that you will allow plenty of time to fully explore the attractions of both stores. Those of you arriving early can visit the Furniture Mart any day of the week; it is open from 10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. on Saturdays and from noon to 5:30 p.m. on Sundays. While there, stop at the See's Candy Cart and find out for yourself why Charlie and I are a good bit wider than we were back in 1972 when we bought See's.
1992.chinese: 照例，会议结束后我们会安排巴士送各位前往内布拉斯加家具卖场和波仙珠宝，之后再送往市中心酒店或机场。我希望各位留出充足时间，好好逛逛这两家商店。提前到达奥马哈的股东可以在一周中的任何一天前往家具城；星期六营业时间是上午10时至下午5时30分，星期日中午12时至下午5时30分。到那里时，请顺便在喜诗糖果售卖车停留，亲自体会一下为什么查理和我如今的腰围，比1972年收购喜诗时宽了不少。

1992.english:
Borsheim's normally is closed on Sunday but will be open for shareholders and their guests from noon to 6 p.m. on Sunday, April 25.  Charlie and I will be in attendance, sporting our jeweler's loupes, and ready to give advice about gems to anyone foolish enough to listen.  Also available will be plenty of Cherry Cokes, See's candies, and other lesser goodies.  I hope you will join us.

Warren E. Buffett March 1, 1993                             Chairman of the Board
1992.chinese:
波仙珠宝星期日通常不营业，但将在4月25日星期日中午12时至下午6时专门向股东及其来宾开放。查理和我届时也会在场，戴着珠宝鉴定放大镜，只要有人傻得肯听，我们就准备给他出出宝石方面的主意。现场也会有大量樱桃味可口可乐、喜诗糖果和其他没那么重要的美食。我希望各位前来。

沃伦·E·巴菲特  
董事长  
1993年3月1日

1993.english:
BERKSHIRE HATHAWAY INC.

To the Shareholders of Berkshire Hathaway Inc.:

Our per-share book value increased 14.3% during 1993.  Over the last 29 years (that is, since present management took over) book value has grown from $19 to $8,854, or at a rate of 23.3% compounded annually.

During the year, Berkshire's net worth increased by $1.5 billion, a figure affected by two negative and two positive non- operating items.  For the sake of completeness, I'll explain them here.  If you aren't thrilled by accounting, however, feel free to fast-forward through this discussion:
1993.chinese:
伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司

致伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司的股东：

1993年，我们的每股账面价值增长14.3%。过去29年，也就是现任管理层接手以来，账面价值从每股19美元增至8,854美元，年复合增长率为23.3%。

年内，伯克希尔净资产增加15亿美元，其中受到两项负面、两项正面的非经营性因素影响。为交代完整，我在这里解释一下。不过，如果会计没法让你兴奋，尽管快进跳过这一段：

1993.english: 1.     The first negative was produced by a change in Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) having to do with the taxes we accrue against unrealized appreciation in the securities we carry at market value.  The old rule said that the tax rate used should be the one in effect when the appreciation took place.  Therefore, at the end of 1992, we were using a rate of 34% on the $6.4 billion of gains generated after 1986 and 28% on the $1.2 billion of gains generated before that.  The new rule stipulates that the current tax rate should be applied to all gains.  The rate in the first quarter of 1993, when this rule went into effect, was 34%. Applying that rate to our pre-1987 gains reduced net worth by $70 million.
1993.chinese: 1. 第一项负面影响，来自公认会计原则（GAAP）的一项变化，涉及按市价列账证券的未实现增值应计税款。旧规则要求使用增值发生时的税率。因此，1992年末，我们对1986年之后形成的64亿美元增值采用34%的税率，对此前形成的12亿美元增值采用28%。新规则要求，全部增值适用现行税率。这项规则于1993年第一季度生效，当时税率为34%；把它用于1987年以前的增值，使净资产减少7,000万美元。

1993.english: 2.     The second negative, related to the first, came about because the corporate tax rate was raised in the third quarter of 1993 to 35%.  This change required us to make an additional charge of 1% against all of our unrealized gains, and that charge penalized net worth by $75 million. Oddly, GAAP required both this charge and the one described above to be deducted from the earnings we report, even though the unrealized appreciation that gave rise to the charges was never included in earnings, but rather was credited directly to net worth.
1993.chinese: 2. 第二项负面影响与第一项有关：1993年第三季度，公司税率升至35%，全部未实现增值须再计提1%税款，净资产因此减少7,500万美元。奇怪的是，GAAP要求，这项和前述税款都从报表利润中扣除，虽然引发税款的未实现增值从未计入利润，而是直接记入净资产。

1993.english: 3.     Another 1993 change in GAAP affects the value at which we carry the securities that we own. In recent years, both the common stocks and certain common-equivalent securities held by our insurance companies have been valued at market, whereas equities held by our non- insurance subsidiaries or by the parent company were carried at their aggregate cost or market, whichever was lower.  Now GAAP says that all common stocks should be carried at market, a rule we began following in the fourth quarter of 1993.  This change produced a gain in Berkshire's reported net worth of about $172 million.
1993.chinese: 3. 1993年GAAP的另一项变化，影响我们持有证券的列账价值。近几年，保险公司持有的普通股，以及某些具有普通股性质的证券，都按市价列账；非保险子公司及母公司持有的股票，却按总成本与总市值孰低计价。如今，GAAP要求全部普通股按市价列账；我们从1993年第四季度开始执行，报表净资产因此增加约1.72亿美元。

1993.english: 4.     Finally, we issued some stock last year.  In a transaction described in last year's Annual Report, we issued 3,944 shares in early January, 1993 upon the conversion of $46 million convertible debentures that we had called for redemption.  Additionally, we issued 25,203 shares when we acquired Dexter Shoe, a purchase discussed later in this report.  The overall result was that our shares outstanding increased by 29,147 and our net worth by about $478 million.  Per-share book value also grew, because the shares issued in these transactions carried a price above their book value.
1993.chinese: 4. 最后，去年我们发行了一些股票。如上年年报所述，1993年1月初，4,600万美元已通知赎回的可转换债券转股，我们为此发行了3,944股。此外，收购稍后将谈到的德克斯特鞋业时，又发行了25,203股。总计，流通股增加29,147股，净资产增加约4.78亿美元。每股账面价值也有所提高，因为这些交易的股票发行价格高于每股账面价值。

1993.english: Of course, it's per-share intrinsic value, not book value, that counts.  Book value is an accounting term that measures the capital, including retained earnings, that has been put into a business.  Intrinsic value is a present-value estimate of the cash that can be taken out of a business during its remaining life.  At most companies, the two values are unrelated. Berkshire, however, is an exception:  Our book value, though significantly below our intrinsic value, serves as a useful device for tracking that key figure.  In 1993, each measure grew by roughly 14%, advances that I would call satisfactory but unexciting.
1993.chinese: 当然，重要的是每股内在价值，而非账面价值。账面价值是会计术语，衡量投入企业的资本，包括留存利润；内在价值则是对企业剩余寿命中可取出现金的现值估计。多数公司中，两者并无关联。伯克希尔却是例外：我们的账面价值虽明显低于内在价值，却是追踪后者的有用工具。1993年，两者都增长了大约14%。这样的增长，我会称之为令人满意，但谈不上令人兴奋。

1993.english: These gains, however, were outstripped by a much larger gain - 39% - in Berkshire's market price.  Over time, of course, market price and intrinsic value will arrive at about the same destination.  But in the short run the two often diverge in a major way, a phenomenon I've discussed in the past.  Two years ago, Coca-Cola and Gillette, both large holdings of ours, enjoyed market price increases that dramatically outpaced their earnings gains.  In the 1991 Annual Report, I said that the stocks of these companies could not continuously overperform their businesses.
1993.chinese: 不过，这两项增长，都被伯克希尔股价39%的更大涨幅甩在了后面。长期看，市场价格与内在价值当然会到达大致相同的目的地；但短期内，两者往往相差很远，这种现象我以前谈过。两年前，我们的两项大持仓——可口可乐与吉列——股价上涨远超利润增长。我在1991年年报中说过，这些公司的股票不可能不断跑赢企业本身。

1993.english: From 1991 to 1993, Coke and Gillette increased their annual operating earnings per share by 38% and 37% respectively, but their market prices moved up only 11% and 6%.  In other words, the companies overperformed their stocks, a result that no doubt partly reflects Wall Street's new apprehension about brand names. Whatever the reason, what will count over time is the earnings performance of these companies.  If they prosper, Berkshire will also prosper, though not in a lock-step manner.
1993.chinese: 1991至1993年，可口可乐与吉列的年度每股营业利润分别增长38%与37%，股价却只上涨11%与6%。换句话说，企业跑赢了股票；这无疑有一部分反映了华尔街新近对品牌的担忧。不论原因是什么，长期重要的是这些企业的盈利表现。如果它们兴旺，伯克希尔也会兴旺，虽然步调不会完全一致。

1993.english: Let me add a lesson from history:  Coke went public in 1919 at $40 per share.  By the end of 1920 the market, coldly reevaluating Coke's future prospects, had battered the stock down by more than 50%, to $19.50.  At yearend 1993, that single share, with dividends reinvested, was worth more than $2.1 million.  As Ben Graham said:  "In the short-run, the market is a voting machine - reflecting a voter-registration test that requires only money, not intelligence or emotional stability - but in the long- run, the market is a weighing machine."
1993.chinese: 再补一课历史：可口可乐1919年上市，每股40美元；到1920年末，市场冷酷地重新评估前景，把股价打到19.50美元，跌幅超过50%。而到1993年末，若把股息再投资，那一股已值超过210万美元。正如本·格雷厄姆所说：“短期看，市场是投票机，选民登记只查有没有钱，不查智力或情绪是否稳定；长期看，市场是称重机。”

1993.english: So how should Berkshire's over-performance in the market last year be viewed?  Clearly, Berkshire was selling at a higher percentage of intrinsic value at the end of 1993 than was the case at the beginning of the year.  On the other hand, in a world of 6% or 7% long-term interest rates, Berkshire's market price was not inappropriate if - and you should understand that this is a huge if - Charlie Munger, Berkshire's Vice Chairman, and I can attain our long-standing goal of increasing Berkshire's per-share intrinsic value at an average annual rate of 15%.  We have not retreated from this goal.  But we again emphasize, as we have for many years, that the growth in our capital base makes 15% an ever-more difficult target to hit.
1993.chinese: 那么，该怎样看待去年伯克希尔股价跑赢企业本身的表现？显然，1993年末，股价相对于内在价值的比例高于年初。另一方面，在长期利率为6%或7%的世界里，如果——请明白，这是一个巨大的“如果”——伯克希尔副董事长查理·芒格和我，能达到长期以来每股内在价值年均增长15%的目标，那么这样的市场价格也并非不合适。我们没有放弃这个目标。但仍要像多年来一样强调：资本基数越大，15%就越难达到。

1993.english:
What we have going for us is a growing collection of good- sized operating businesses that possess economic characteristics ranging from good to terrific, run by managers whose performance ranges from terrific to terrific.  You need have no worries about this group.

The capital-allocation work that Charlie and I do at the parent company, using the funds that our managers deliver to us, has a less certain outcome:  It is not easy to find new businesses and managers comparable to those we have.  Despite that difficulty, Charlie and I relish the search, and we are happy to report an important success in 1993.
1993.chinese:
我们有利的一面，是拥有越来越多规模可观的自营企业：经济特性从良好到极佳，经理人的表现则从极佳到极佳。对这群人，你们大可放心。

查理和我在母公司运用经理人交来的资金，进行资本配置，结果就没那么确定了：要找到与现有企业和经理人相媲美的新对象，并不容易。尽管如此，我们仍很享受寻找的过程，也很高兴报告，1993年取得了一项重要成功。

1993.english:
## Dexter Shoe

What we did last year was build on our 1991 purchase of H. H. Brown, a superbly-run manufacturer of work shoes, boots and other footwear.  Brown has been a real winner:  Though we had high hopes to begin with, these expectations have been considerably exceeded thanks to Frank Rooney, Jim Issler and the talented managers who work with them.  Because of our confidence in Frank's team, we next acquired Lowell Shoe, at the end of 1992.  Lowell was a long-established manufacturer of women's and nurses' shoes, but its business needed some fixing.  Again, results have surpassed our expectations.  So we promptly jumped at the chance last year to acquire Dexter Shoe of Dexter, Maine, which manufactures popular-priced men's and women's shoes. Dexter, I can assure you, needs no fixing:  It is one of the best-managed companies Charlie and I have seen in our business lifetimes.
1993.chinese:
## 德克斯特鞋业

去年，我们在1991年收购H.H.布朗的基础上继续扩展。布朗制造工作鞋、靴及其他鞋类，经营极佳，确实是个大赢家。我们原本就寄予厚望，但在弗兰克·鲁尼、吉姆·伊斯勒及其优秀团队的努力下，实际表现仍大幅超过预期。因为信任弗兰克的团队，1992年末，我们又收购了洛厄尔鞋业。这是一家历史悠久的女鞋及护士鞋制造商，只是业务需要整顿。结果再次超出预期。因此，去年一有机会，我们就迅速买下了位于缅因州德克斯特、生产大众价位男女鞋的德克斯特鞋业。我可以保证，它不需要整顿：这是查理和我从商以来见过的管理最好的公司之一。

1993.english: Harold Alfond, who started working in a shoe factory at 25 cents an hour when he was 20, founded Dexter in 1956 with $10,000 of capital.  He was joined in 1958 by Peter Lunder, his nephew. The two of them have since built a business that now produces over 7.5 million pairs of shoes annually, most of them made in Maine and the balance in Puerto Rico.  As you probably know, the domestic shoe industry is generally thought to be unable to compete with imports from low-wage countries.  But someone forgot to tell this to the ingenious managements of Dexter and H. H. Brown and to their skilled labor forces, which together make the U.S. plants of both companies highly competitive against all comers.
1993.chinese: 哈罗德·阿尔方德20岁进入鞋厂，时薪25美分；1956年，他以1万美元创办德克斯特，侄子彼得·伦德于1958年加入。两人把企业发展到如今每年生产超过750万双鞋，大部分在缅因州制造，其余在波多黎各。各位大概知道，美国制鞋业通常被认为无法与低工资国家的进口鞋竞争。不过，似乎有人忘了把这事告诉德克斯特和H.H.布朗足智多谋的管理层，以及熟练的工人。他们合力使两家公司设在美国的工厂，都有能力迎战任何对手。

1993.english:
Dexter's business includes 77 retail outlets, located primarily in the Northeast.  The company is also a major manufacturer of golf shoes, producing about 15% of U.S. output. Its bread and butter, though, is the manufacture of traditional shoes for traditional retailers, a job at which it excels:  Last year both Nordstrom and J.C. Penney bestowed special awards upon Dexter for its performance as a supplier during 1992.

Our 1993 results include Dexter only from our date of merger, November 7th.  In 1994, we expect Berkshire's shoe operations to have more than $550 million in sales, and we would not be surprised if the combined pre-tax earnings of these businesses topped $85 million.  Five years ago we had no thought of getting into shoes.  Now we have 7,200 employees in that industry, and I sing "There's No Business Like Shoe Business" as I drive to work.  So much for strategic plans.
1993.chinese:
德克斯特的业务还包括77家零售店，主要在美国东北部。它也是重要的高尔夫球鞋制造商，约占美国产量的15%。不过，主要饭碗仍是为传统零售商生产传统鞋款，而这件事，它做得极好。去年，诺德斯特龙与J.C.彭尼都为德克斯特1992年的供应商表现颁发了特别奖项。

1993年的业绩中，德克斯特仅从合并日11月7日起计入。预计1994年，伯克希尔鞋业销售额将超过5.50亿美元；这些企业的合计税前利润若超过8,500万美元，我们也不会意外。五年前，我们根本没想过进入鞋业；如今已有7,200名鞋业员工，我开车上班时唱的都是“没有哪门生意比得上鞋生意”。战略规划，也就这么回事。

1993.english: At Berkshire, we have no view of the future that dictates what businesses or industries we will enter.  Indeed, we think it's usually poison for a corporate giant's shareholders if it embarks upon new ventures pursuant to some grand vision.  We prefer instead to focus on the economic characteristics of businesses that we wish to own and the personal characteristics of managers with whom we wish to associate - and then to hope we get lucky in finding the two in combination.  At Dexter, we did.
1993.chinese: 在伯克希尔，我们没有一幅未来蓝图，规定自己必须进入哪些企业或行业。实际上，我们认为，大公司如果按某个宏伟愿景开拓新事业，对股东而言通常就是毒药。我们更愿意专注于想拥有的企业的经济特性，以及想合作的经理人的个人品质，然后盼着运气好，让两者同时出现。德克斯特就是如此。

1993.english:
---

And now we pause for a short commercial:  Though they owned a business jewel, we believe that Harold and Peter (who were not interested in cash) made a sound decision in exchanging their Dexter stock for shares of Berkshire.  What they did, in effect, was trade a 100% interest in a single terrific business for a smaller interest in a large group of terrific businesses.  They incurred no tax on this exchange and now own a security that can be easily used for charitable or personal gifts, or that can be converted to cash in amounts, and at times, of their own choosing.  Should members of their families desire to, they can pursue varying financial paths without running into the complications that often arise when assets are concentrated in a private business.
1993.chinese:
---

现在暂停一下，插播一段小广告：哈罗德与彼得原本拥有一颗企业珍宝，但我们仍认为，他们把德克斯特股票换成伯克希尔股票，是明智的决定——两人本来就不想要现金。实质上，他们把一家极好企业的100%权益，换成了一大组极好企业中较小的权益。这次交换无须缴税，如今持有的证券又便于用作慈善捐赠或个人赠与，也可以在自己选择的时间、按自己选择的金额兑现。家人如果愿意，还能各走不同的财务道路，不必遇上资产集中于私人企业时常见的复杂问题。

1993.english: For tax and other reasons, private companies also often find it difficult to diversify outside their industries.  Berkshire, in contrast, can diversify with ease.  So in shifting their ownership to Berkshire, Dexter's shareholders solved a reinvestment problem.  Moreover, though Harold and Peter now have non-controlling shares in Berkshire, rather than controlling shares in Dexter, they know they will be treated as partners and that we will follow owner-oriented practices.  If they elect to retain their Berkshire shares, their investment result from the merger date forward will exactly parallel my own result.  Since I have a huge percentage of my net worth committed for life to Berkshire shares - and since the company will issue me neither restricted shares nor stock options - my gain-loss equation will always match that of all other owners.
1993.chinese: 出于税务及其他原因，私人企业往往难以在本行业以外分散投资，伯克希尔却很容易做到。因此，把所有权转到伯克希尔，也替德克斯特股东解决了再投资问题。此外，哈罗德与彼得虽然从德克斯特的控股股东，变成伯克希尔的非控股股东，却知道我们会把他们当作伙伴，坚持以所有者利益为重的做法。如果他们选择继续持股，合并日之后的投资结果就会与我的完全一致。我把个人净资产中极大的一部分终生投入伯克希尔股票；公司也不会给我限制性股票或股票期权，因此，我的盈亏关系始终与其他所有者一致。

1993.english:
Additionally, Harold and Peter know that at Berkshire we can keep our promises:  There will be no changes of control or culture at Berkshire for many decades to come.  Finally, and of paramount importance, Harold and Peter can be sure that they will get to run their business - an activity they dearly love - exactly as they did before the merger.  At Berkshire, we do not tell .400 hitters how to swing.

What made sense for Harold and Peter probably makes sense for a few other owners of large private businesses.  So, if you have a business that might fit, let me hear from you.  Our acquisition criteria are set forth in the appendix on page 22.
1993.chinese:
哈罗德与彼得还知道，伯克希尔能够信守承诺：未来数十年，伯克希尔的控制权和文化都不会改变。最后，也是最重要的一点，他们可以确信，自己能够像合并前一样，继续经营自家企业——这件事是他们真心热爱的。在伯克希尔，我们不会教打击率四成的好手怎样挥棒。

适合哈罗德与彼得的办法，大概也适合少数其他大型私人企业的所有者。因此，如果你的企业可能合适，请告诉我。我们的收购标准列在第22页的附录中。

1993.english:
## Sources of Reported Earnings

The table below shows the major sources of Berkshire's reported earnings.  In this presentation, amortization of Goodwill and other major purchase-price accounting adjustments are not charged against the specific businesses to which they apply, but are instead aggregated and shown separately.  This procedure lets you view the earnings of our businesses as they would have been reported had we not purchased them.  I've explained in past reports why this form of presentation seems to us to be more useful to investors and managers than one utilizing GAAP, which requires purchase-price adjustments to be made on a business-by-business basis.  The total net earnings we show in the table are, of course, identical to the GAAP total in our audited financial statements.
