Considering the similarity of this year's list and the last, you may decide your management is hopelessly comatose.  But we continue to think that it is usually foolish to part with an interest in a business that is both understandable and durably wonderful.  Business interests of that kind are simply too hard to replace.

Interestingly, corporate managers have no trouble understanding that point when they are focusing on a business they operate:  A parent company that owns a subsidiary with superb long- term economics is not likely to sell that entity regardless of price.  "Why," the CEO would ask, "should I part with my crown jewel?"  Yet that same CEO, when it comes to running his personal investment portfolio, will offhandedly - and even impetuously - move from business to business when presented with no more than superficial arguments by his broker for doing so.  The worst of these is perhaps, "You can't go broke taking a profit."  Can you imagine a CEO using this line to urge his board to sell a star subsidiary?  In our view, what makes sense in business also makes sense in stocks:  An investor should ordinarily hold a small piece of an outstanding business with the same tenacity that an owner would exhibit if he owned all of that business.
1993.chinese:
今年的名单与去年如此相似，你们也许会认定，管理层已经昏迷得无药可救。不过，我们仍然认为：对于一门既看得懂、又能长期保持卓越的生意，卖掉其中的权益通常是愚蠢的。这种企业权益实在太难找替代品。

有意思的是，公司管理者面对自己经营的业务时，完全理解这一点：母公司若拥有一家长期经济特性出色的子公司，通常不会卖掉它，无论别人出什么价。首席执行官会问：“我为什么要把王冠上的明珠卖掉？”可是，同一位首席执行官管理个人投资组合时，只要经纪人搬出几句肤浅的理由，就会随随便便，甚至一时冲动，从一家企业跳到另一家企业。其中最糟糕的一句也许是：“获利了结，怎么也不会破产。”你能想象，一位首席执行官拿这句话劝董事会卖掉明星子公司吗？在我们看来，经营企业时讲得通的道理，投资股票时也讲得通：投资者持有一家优秀企业的一小部分权益，通常应当像拥有整家企业的业主那样，坚定地持有。

1993.english: Earlier I mentioned the financial results that could have been achieved by investing $40 in The Coca-Cola Co. in 1919.  In 1938, more than 50 years after the introduction of Coke, and long after the drink was firmly established as an American icon, Fortune did an excellent story on the company.  In the second paragraph the writer reported:  "Several times every year a weighty and serious investor looks long and with profound respect at Coca-Cola's record, but comes regretfully to the conclusion that he is looking too late.  The specters of saturation and competition rise before him."
1993.chinese: 前面我提过，1919年把40美元投进可口可乐，能取得怎样的财务结果。1938年，距可口可乐问世已经五十多年，这种饮料也早已成为美国的象征，《财富》杂志为这家公司写了一篇出色的报道。作者在第二段写道：“每年总有那么几次，一位审慎而认真的投资者，怀着深深的敬意，久久审视可口可乐的业绩记录，最后却遗憾地得出结论：自己看得太晚了。市场饱和与竞争的幽灵在他眼前浮现。”

1993.english: Yes, competition there was in 1938 and in 1993 as well.  But it's worth noting that in 1938 The Coca-Cola Co. sold 207 million cases of soft drinks (if its gallonage then is converted into the 192-ounce cases used for measurement today) and in 1993 it sold about 10.7 billion cases, a 50-fold increase in physical volume from a company that in 1938 was already dominant in its very major industry.  Nor was the party over in 1938 for an investor:  Though the $40 invested in 1919 in one share had (with dividends reinvested) turned into $3,277 by the end of 1938, a fresh $40 then invested in Coca-Cola stock would have grown to $25,000 by yearend 1993.
1993.chinese: 是的，1938年有竞争，1993年同样有。但值得看看：1938年，可口可乐卖出了2.07亿箱饮料——把当年的加仑数换算成如今计量所用的每箱192盎司——1993年则卖出约107亿箱。实物销量增长了50倍，而早在1938年，这家公司就已经在一个规模极大的行业中占据主导地位。对投资者来说，1938年的盛宴也远未结束：1919年投入40美元购买的一股股票，到1938年底，若把股息再投资，已经变成3,277美元；而在1938年重新投入的40美元，到1993年底也会增长到25,000美元。

1993.english:
I can't resist one more quote from that 1938 Fortune story: "It would be hard to name any company comparable in size to Coca- Cola and selling, as Coca-Cola does, an unchanged product that can point to a ten-year record anything like Coca-Cola's."  In the 55 years that have since passed, Coke's product line has broadened somewhat, but it's remarkable how well that description still fits.

Charlie and I decided long ago that in an investment lifetime it's just too hard to make hundreds of smart decisions.  That judgment became ever more compelling as Berkshire's capital mushroomed and the universe of investments that could significantly affect our results shrank dramatically.  Therefore, we adopted a strategy that required our being smart - and not too smart at that - only a very few times.  Indeed, we'll now settle for one good idea a year.  (Charlie says it's my turn.)
1993.chinese:
我忍不住还要引用那篇1938年《财富》报道中的一句话：“很难再找出一家规模与可口可乐相当、同样出售一种始终未变的产品，同时还能拿出近似可口可乐那样十年业绩记录的公司。”此后55年，可口可乐的产品线有所扩展，但这段描述至今依然如此贴切，实在令人惊叹。

很久以前，查理和我就认定：一辈子投资，要做出几百个明智决定，实在太难。随着伯克希尔资本迅速膨胀，而能够显著影响我们业绩的投资范围急剧缩小，这一判断越来越有说服力。因此，我们采用了一种策略：只需要在极少数时候聪明一下，而且还不必聪明得过头。事实上，如今一年能有一个好主意，我们就知足了。（查理说，该轮到我了。）

1993.english: The strategy we've adopted precludes our following standard diversification dogma.  Many pundits would therefore say the strategy must be riskier than that employed by more conventional investors.  We disagree.  We believe that a policy of portfolio concentration may well decrease risk if it raises, as it should, both the intensity with which an investor thinks about a business and the comfort-level he must feel with its economic characteristics before buying into it.  In stating this opinion, we define risk, using dictionary terms, as "the possibility of loss or injury."
1993.chinese: 我们采用的策略，使我们无法遵循通常的分散投资教条。因此，许多专家会说，它必定比传统投资者的做法风险更高。我们不同意。如果集中投资能够使投资者更深入地思考一家企业，并且要求自己在买入前，对企业经济特性有更充分的把握——理应如此——那么，集中持仓完全可能降低风险。表达这一观点时，我们采用字典里的定义，把风险理解为“遭受损失或伤害的可能性”。

1993.english: Academics, however, like to define investment "risk" differently, averring that it is the relative volatility of a stock or portfolio of stocks - that is, their volatility as compared to that of a large universe of stocks.  Employing data bases and statistical skills, these academics compute with precision the "beta" of a stock - its relative volatility in the past - and then build arcane investment and capital-allocation theories around this calculation.  In their hunger for a single statistic to measure risk, however, they forget a fundamental principle:  It is better to be approximately right than precisely wrong.
1993.chinese: 然而，学术界喜欢给投资“风险”下另一种定义，断言它就是一只股票或一个股票组合的相对波动性，即与大范围股票整体的波动相比，波动有多大。他们运用数据库和统计技巧，精确计算股票的“贝塔系数”——过去的相对波动性——再围绕这一计算，构建深奥的投资与资本配置理论。然而，他们急于用单一统计量衡量风险，却忘了一个基本原则：大致正确，胜过精确地错误。

1993.english: For owners of a business - and that's the way we think of shareholders - the academics' definition of risk is far off the mark, so much so that it produces absurdities.  For example, under beta-based theory, a stock that has dropped very sharply compared to the market - as had Washington Post when we bought it in 1973 - becomes "riskier" at the lower price than it was at the higher price.  Would that description have then made any sense to someone who was offered the entire company at a vastly-reduced price?
1993.chinese: 对企业所有者而言——我们正是这样看待股东的——学术界的风险定义偏离实际太远，以至于会得出荒谬的结果。例如，按以贝塔系数为基础的理论，一只股价相对大盘急剧下跌的股票——就像我们1973年买入时的《华盛顿邮报》——价格更低时，竟会比价格更高时“风险更大”。假如有人获准以大幅降低的价格买下整家公司，这种说法对他有任何道理吗？

1993.english: In fact, the true investor welcomes volatility.  Ben Graham explained why in Chapter 8 of The Intelligent Investor.  There he introduced "Mr. Market," an obliging fellow who shows up every day to either buy from you or sell to you, whichever you wish.  The more manic-depressive this chap is, the greater the opportunities available to the investor.  That's true because a wildly fluctuating market means that irrationally low prices will periodically be attached to solid businesses.  It is impossible to see how the availability of such prices can be thought of as increasing the hazards for an investor who is totally free to either ignore the market or exploit its folly.
1993.chinese: 事实上，真正的投资者欢迎波动。本·格雷厄姆在《聪明的投资者》第8章解释了原因。他在那里介绍了“市场先生”：这位热心人每天都来，任你选择，既可以向你买，也可以卖给你。这位老兄越是时而狂热、时而沮丧，投资者得到的机会就越多。因为市场剧烈波动，意味着坚实可靠的企业会不时被标上低得不合理的价格。投资者完全可以不理市场，也可以利用它的愚蠢；对这样的人来说，竟把这种低价机会视为风险增加，实在令人无法理解。

1993.english: In assessing risk, a beta purist will disdain examining what a company produces, what its competitors are doing, or how much borrowed money the business employs.  He may even prefer not to know the company's name.  What he treasures is the price history of its stock.  In contrast, we'll happily forgo knowing the price history and instead will seek whatever information will further our understanding of the company's business.  After we buy a stock, consequently, we would not be disturbed if markets closed for a year or two.  We don't need a daily quote on our 100% position in See's or H. H. Brown to validate our well-being.  Why, then, should we need a quote on our 7% interest in Coke?
1993.chinese: 评估风险时，贝塔系数的忠实信徒不屑于考察公司生产什么、竞争对手在干什么，或者企业借了多少钱。他甚至可能宁愿连公司名字都不知道。他珍视的是股价历史。我们却乐意放弃股价历史，转而搜集一切有助于理解公司业务的信息。因此，买入股票后，即使市场关闭一两年，我们也不会不安。我们拥有喜诗糖果或H.H.布朗100%的权益，并不需要每日报价来证明自己过得好好的。那么，为什么持有可口可乐7%的权益，就非得有报价呢？

1993.english: In our opinion, the real risk that an investor must assess is whether his aggregate after-tax receipts from an investment (including those he receives on sale) will, over his prospective holding period, give him at least as much purchasing power as he had to begin with, plus a modest rate of interest on that initial stake.  Though this risk cannot be calculated with engineering precision, it can in some cases be judged with a degree of accuracy that is useful.  The primary factors bearing upon this evaluation are:
1993.chinese: 在我们看来，投资者真正必须评估的风险是：在预期持有期内，一项投资带来的税后总收入，包括出售时收到的钱，能否至少提供与最初投入相当的购买力，再加上这笔初始资金的一点适度利息。虽然无法像工程计算那样精确计量这种风险，但在某些情况下，我们仍能作出准确到足以派上用场的判断。影响这一评估的主要因素是：

1）能够多有把握地评估企业的长期经济特性；

2）能够多有把握地评估管理层，包括其充分发挥企业潜力的能力，以及明智运用现金流的能力；

3）能够多有把握地相信管理层会把经营成果交给股东，而不是装进自己的口袋；

4）买入这家企业的价格；

1993.english:
5) The levels of taxation and inflation that will be experienced and that will determine the degree by which an investor's purchasing-power return is reduced from his gross return.

These factors will probably strike many analysts as unbearably fuzzy, since they cannot be extracted from a data base of any kind. But the difficulty of precisely quantifying these matters does not negate their importance nor is it insuperable.  Just as Justice Stewart found it impossible to formulate a test for obscenity but nevertheless asserted, "I know it when I see it," so also can investors - in an inexact but useful way - "see" the risks inherent in certain investments without reference to complex equations or price histories.
1993.chinese:
5）未来将经历的税收与通货膨胀水平；两者会决定投资者的购买力回报，相对于总回报缩水多少。

许多分析师大概会觉得，这些因素模糊得令人难以忍受，因为没有哪一种数据库能把它们提取出来。不过，难以精确量化，并不削弱它们的重要性，这种困难也并非无法克服。正如斯图尔特大法官发现无法为淫秽内容制定一套判定标准，却仍然说“我一看就知道”一样，投资者也能以一种不精确却有用的方式，“看出”某些投资内在的风险，而无须依赖复杂公式或股价历史。

1993.english: Is it really so difficult to conclude that Coca-Cola and Gillette possess far less business risk over the long term than, say, any computer company or retailer?  Worldwide, Coke sells about 44% of all soft drinks, and Gillette has more than a 60% share (in value) of the blade market.  Leaving aside chewing gum, in which Wrigley is dominant, I know of no other significant businesses in which the leading company has long enjoyed such global power.
1993.chinese: 判断可口可乐和吉列的长期经营风险，远低于比如任何一家电脑公司或零售商，真有那么难吗？在全球范围内，可口可乐售出的饮料约占所有软饮料的44%；吉列在刀片市场的份额，按销售额计则超过60%。除了箭牌占主导地位的口香糖业务，我还不知道哪一项规模可观的生意，其领先企业能长期拥有这样的全球影响力。

1993.english: Moreover, both Coke and Gillette have actually increased their worldwide shares of market in recent years.  The might of their brand names, the attributes of their products, and the strength of their distribution systems give them an enormous competitive advantage, setting up a protective moat around their economic castles.  The average company, in contrast, does battle daily without any such means of protection.  As Peter Lynch says, stocks of companies selling commodity-like products should come with a warning label:  "Competition may prove hazardous to human wealth."
1993.chinese: 此外，可口可乐和吉列近年来实际上还扩大了全球市场份额。它们强大的品牌、产品本身的特点，以及有力的分销体系，赋予它们巨大的竞争优势，在各自的经济城堡周围筑起了护城河。相反，一般公司天天出门打仗，却没有这样的防护。正如彼得·林奇所说，那些出售同质化产品的公司，其股票应当贴上警示标签：“竞争可能危害人类财富。”

1993.english: The competitive strengths of a Coke or Gillette are obvious to even the casual observer of business.  Yet the beta of their stocks is similar to that of a great many run-of-the-mill companies who possess little or no competitive advantage.  Should we conclude from this similarity that the competitive strength of Coke and Gillette gains them nothing when business risk is being measured? Or should we conclude that the risk in owning a piece of a company - its stock - is somehow divorced from the long-term risk inherent in its business operations?  We believe neither conclusion makes sense and that equating beta with investment risk also makes no sense.
1993.chinese: 哪怕只是粗略观察商业的人，也能看出可口可乐或吉列的竞争实力。然而，它们股票的贝塔系数，却与许多几乎没有竞争优势、甚至毫无优势的普通公司相似。我们该据此断定，衡量经营风险时，可口可乐和吉列的竞争实力毫无用处吗？还是该断定，拥有公司一部分权益——也就是股票——的风险，竟然与其经营活动内在的长期风险脱了钩？我们认为，这两个结论都说不通，把贝塔系数等同于投资风险也同样说不通。

1993.english: The theoretician bred on beta has no mechanism for differentiating the risk inherent in, say, a single-product toy company selling pet rocks or hula hoops from that of another toy company whose sole product is Monopoly or Barbie.  But it's quite possible for ordinary investors to make such distinctions if they have a reasonable understanding of consumer behavior and the factors that create long-term competitive strength or weakness. Obviously, every investor will make mistakes.  But by confining himself to a relatively few, easy-to-understand cases, a reasonably intelligent, informed and diligent person can judge investment risks with a useful degree of accuracy.
1993.chinese: 在贝塔系数理论中成长起来的理论家，没有办法区分两类风险：一家玩具公司只卖宠物石头或呼啦圈，另一家则只卖大富翁或芭比娃娃。不过，普通投资者只要对消费者行为，以及造就长期竞争强弱的因素有合理认识，就完全能够作出这种区分。显然，每个投资者都会犯错。但一个智力尚可、掌握信息又勤勉的人，只要把范围限制在少数几个容易理解的案例中，就能把投资风险判断到足以派上用场的准确程度。

1993.english: In many industries, of course, Charlie and I can't determine whether we are dealing with a "pet rock" or a "Barbie."  We couldn't solve this problem, moreover, even if we were to spend years intensely studying those industries.  Sometimes our own intellectual shortcomings would stand in the way of understanding, and in other cases the nature of the industry would be the roadblock.  For example, a business that must deal with fast-moving technology is not going to lend itself to reliable evaluations of its long-term economics.  Did we foresee thirty years ago what would transpire in the television-manufacturing or computer industries?  Of course not.  (Nor did most of the investors and corporate managers who enthusiastically entered those industries.) Why, then, should Charlie and I now think we can predict the future of other rapidly-evolving businesses?  We'll stick instead with the easy cases.  Why search for a needle buried in a haystack when one is sitting in plain sight?
1993.chinese: 当然，在许多行业里，查理和我分辨不出，眼前究竟是“宠物石头”，还是“芭比娃娃”。而且，即使埋头钻研那些行业好几年，我们也解决不了这个问题。有时候，是我们自己的智力局限妨碍了理解；另一些时候，障碍在行业本身。例如，一家必须应对技术快速变化的企业，就很难让人可靠地评估其长期经济特性。三十年前，我们预见到电视机制造业或电脑业后来会发生什么了吗？当然没有。（当年热情投身这些行业的大多数投资者和公司管理者也没有。）那么，查理和我如今凭什么认为，自己能预测其他迅速演变行业的未来？我们还是坚持做容易的题吧。眼前明明摆着一根针，何必到草堆里再找一根？

1993.english: Of course, some investment strategies - for instance, our efforts in arbitrage over the years - require wide diversification. If significant risk exists in a single transaction, overall risk should be reduced by making that purchase one of many mutually- independent commitments.  Thus, you may consciously purchase a risky investment - one that indeed has a significant possibility of causing loss or injury - if you believe that your gain, weighted for probabilities, considerably exceeds your loss, comparably weighted, and if you can commit to a number of similar, but unrelated opportunities.  Most venture capitalists employ this strategy.  Should you choose to pursue this course, you should adopt the outlook of the casino that owns a roulette wheel, which will want to see lots of action because it is favored by probabilities, but will refuse to accept a single, huge bet.
1993.chinese: 当然，有些投资策略需要广泛分散，例如我们多年来从事的套利。如果单笔交易存在重大风险，就应当把它作为许多相互独立投资中的一笔，来降低整体风险。因此，你可以有意识地买入一项风险较高的投资——也就是确实有相当大可能造成损失或伤害的投资——前提是，你相信按概率加权的收益远超同样加权后的损失，而且还能参与一批类似、彼此却不相关的机会。大多数风险投资家采用的就是这种策略。如果选择走这条路，你就应当像经营轮盘赌的赌场那样思考：因为概率有利于自己，所以希望赌局越多越好，但拒绝接受一笔巨额下注。

1993.english: Another situation requiring wide diversification occurs when an investor who does not understand the economics of specific businesses nevertheless believes it in his interest to be a long- term owner of American industry.  That investor should both own a large number of equities and space out his purchases.  By periodically investing in an index fund, for example, the know- nothing investor can actually out-perform most investment professionals.  Paradoxically, when "dumb" money acknowledges its limitations, it ceases to be dumb.
1993.chinese: 还有一种情形也需要广泛分散：投资者虽然不了解具体企业的经济特性，却仍然认为，长期持有美国工业的权益符合自己的利益。这种投资者应当持有大量不同股票，并且分期买入。例如，定期投资指数基金，什么都不懂的投资者实际上也能跑赢大多数投资专业人士。看似矛盾的是：“傻钱”一旦承认自己的局限，就不再傻了。

1993.english: On the other hand, if you are a know-something investor, able to understand business economics and to find five to ten sensibly- priced companies that possess important long-term competitive advantages, conventional diversification makes no sense for you. It is apt simply to hurt your results and increase your risk.  I cannot understand why an investor of that sort elects to put money into a business that is his 20th favorite rather than simply adding that money to his top choices - the businesses he understands best and that present the least risk, along with the greatest profit potential.  In the words of the prophet Mae West:  "Too much of a good thing can be wonderful."
1993.chinese: 另一方面，如果你是个懂一些门道的投资者，能够理解企业的经济特性，并找到五到十家价格合理、具有重大长期竞争优势的公司，那么，传统的分散投资对你就毫无意义。它很可能只会拖累你的业绩、增加你的风险。我无法理解，这样的投资者为什么要把钱投给自己排名第20喜欢的企业，而不继续投入最中意的那些公司——自己最了解、风险最低，同时盈利潜力最大的企业。借用先知梅·韦斯特的话：“好东西多得过头，也可以美妙极了。”

1993.english:
## Corporate Governance

At our annual meetings, someone usually asks "What happens to this place if you get hit by a truck?"  I'm glad they are still asking the question in this form.  It won't be too long before the query becomes:  "What happens to this place if you don't get hit by a truck?"

Such questions, in any event, raise a reason for me to discuss corporate governance, a hot topic during the past year.  In general, I believe that directors have stiffened their spines recently and that shareholders are now being treated somewhat more like true owners than was the case not long ago.  Commentators on corporate governance, however, seldom make any distinction among three fundamentally different manager/owner situations that exist in publicly-held companies.  Though the legal responsibility of directors is identical throughout, their ability to effect change differs in each of the cases.  Attention usually falls on the first case, because it prevails on the corporate scene.  Since Berkshire falls into the second category, however, and will someday fall into the third, we will discuss all three variations.
1993.chinese:
## 公司治理

每到年会，通常总有人问：“要是你被卡车撞了，这里怎么办？”我很高兴，他们现在还是这样问。用不了多久，问题就会变成：“要是你一直没被卡车撞，这里怎么办？”

无论如何，这类问题给了我一个理由，谈谈过去一年热门的公司治理话题。总体上，我认为近来董事们的腰杆比以前硬了，股东也比不久前更像真正的所有者那样受到对待。不过，评论公司治理的人，很少区分上市公司中三种根本不同的管理者与所有者关系。虽然三种情况下董事的法律责任相同，但他们推动改变的能力各不一样。人们通常把注意力放在第一种，因为它在公司世界里最普遍。不过，伯克希尔属于第二种，将来又会进入第三种，因此，三种情况我们都来谈谈。

1993.english: The first, and by far most common, board situation is one in which a corporation has no controlling shareholder.  In that case, I believe directors should behave as if there is a single absentee owner, whose long-term interest they should try to further in all proper ways.  Unfortunately, "long-term" gives directors a lot of wiggle room.  If they lack either integrity or the ability to think independently, directors can do great violence to shareholders while still claiming to be acting in their long-term interest.  But assume the board is functioning well and must deal with a management that is mediocre or worse.  Directors then have the responsibility for changing that management, just as an intelligent owner would do if he were present.  And if able but greedy managers over-reach and try to dip too deeply into the shareholders' pockets, directors must slap their hands.
1993.chinese: 第一种，也是最常见的情况，是公司没有控股股东。我认为，这时董事应当假设公司只有一位不在场的业主，并以一切正当方式增进其长期利益。不幸的是，“长期”给了董事很大的回旋余地。缺乏诚信，或缺少独立思考能力的董事，即使严重损害股东利益，仍能声称自己是在为股东的长期利益着想。不过，假设董事会运作良好，面对的管理层却平庸甚至更差，那么，董事就有责任更换管理层，正如一位明智的业主亲自在场时会做的那样。如果管理者虽然能干，却贪得无厌，想把手伸进股东口袋掏得太深，董事也必须把那只手拍回去。

1993.english: In this plain-vanilla case, a director who sees something he doesn't like should attempt to persuade the other directors of his views.  If he is successful, the board will have the muscle to make the appropriate change.  Suppose, though, that the unhappy director can't get other directors to agree with him.  He should then feel free to make his views known to the absentee owners.  Directors seldom do that, of course.  The temperament of many directors would in fact be incompatible with critical behavior of that sort.  But I see nothing improper in such actions, assuming the issues are serious.  Naturally, the complaining director can expect a vigorous rebuttal from the unpersuaded directors, a prospect that should discourage the dissenter from pursuing trivial or non-rational causes.
1993.chinese: 在这种最普通的情形下，一位董事若看到自己不赞同的事情，应当设法说服其他董事。成功了，董事会就有力量作出适当改变。可是，假如这位不满的董事无法让其他人同意，他就应当可以自由地向不在场的业主表明自己的看法。当然，董事很少这样做。事实上，许多董事的性情，也容不得自己采取这样的批评行动。但只要问题重大，我看不出这样做有什么不妥。自然，那些没有被说服的董事，会有力反驳提出异议的人；想到这一点，异议者也就不该为琐碎或不合情理的事情穷追不舍。

1993.english:
For the boards just discussed, I believe the directors ought to be relatively few in number - say, ten or less - and ought to come mostly from the outside.  The outside board members should establish standards for the CEO's performance and should also periodically meet, without his being present, to evaluate his performance against those standards.

The requisites for board membership should be business savvy, interest in the job, and owner-orientation.  Too often, directors are selected simply because they are prominent or add diversity to the board.  That practice is a mistake.  Furthermore, mistakes in selecting directors are particularly serious because appointments are so hard to undo:  The pleasant but vacuous director need never worry about job security.
1993.chinese:
对于刚才讨论的这类董事会，我认为人数应当相对较少，比如十人或更少，而且多数应当来自公司外部。外部董事应当为首席执行官设定业绩标准，并定期在他不出席的情况下开会，按这些标准评估他的表现。

担任董事的必要条件，应当是懂生意、对这份工作有兴趣，以及站在所有者立场上思考。人们选董事，往往只因为某人有名望，或能增加董事会的多样性。这种做法是错误的。而且，选错董事尤其严重，因为任命一旦作出，就很难撤回：一个和和气气却腹中空空的董事，永远不用担心饭碗。

1993.english: The second case is that existing at Berkshire, where the controlling owner is also the manager.  At some companies, this arrangement is facilitated by the existence of two classes of stock endowed with disproportionate voting power.  In these situations, it's obvious that the board does not act as an agent between owners and management and that the directors cannot effect change except through persuasion.  Therefore, if the owner/manager is mediocre or worse - or is over-reaching - there is little a director can do about it except object.  If the directors having no connections to the owner/manager make a unified argument, it may well have some effect.  More likely it will not.
1993.chinese: 第二种情况，就是伯克希尔目前的情况：控股所有者同时也是管理者。有些公司设置两类投票权不成比例的股票，使这种安排更容易实现。显然，在这些情况下，董事会并不充当所有者与管理层之间的代理人，董事除了说服之外，也无法促成改变。因此，如果身兼业主与管理者的人平庸甚至更差，或者索取过度，董事除了反对，几乎无计可施。如果与这位业主兼管理者毫无关联的董事联合起来进言，也许多少会有些作用。但更可能没有。

1993.english:
If change does not come, and the matter is sufficiently serious, the outside directors should resign.  Their resignation will signal their doubts about management, and it will emphasize that no outsider is in a position to correct the owner/manager's shortcomings.

The third governance case occurs when there is a controlling owner who is not involved in management.  This case, examples of which are Hershey Foods and Dow Jones, puts the outside directors in a potentially useful position.  If they become unhappy with either the competence or integrity of the manager, they can go directly to the owner (who may also be on the board) and report their dissatisfaction.  This situation is ideal for an outside director, since he need make his case only to a single, presumably interested owner, who can forthwith effect change if the argument is persuasive.  Even so, the dissatisfied director has only that single course of action.  If he remains unsatisfied about a critical matter, he has no choice but to resign.
1993.chinese:
如果情况没有改变，而且问题足够严重，外部董事就应当辞职。辞职会传达出他们对管理层的疑虑，也会突出一个事实：没有任何外部人士能够纠正这位业主兼管理者的缺点。

第三种治理情况是：存在控股所有者，但他不参与管理。好时食品和道琼斯就是例子。这种安排使外部董事有可能发挥很大作用。如果他们对管理者的能力或诚信感到不满，就可以直接找到所有者——他也可能是董事——表达不满。对外部董事而言，这种情况很理想，因为他只须向一个想必关心自己利益的所有者说明问题；只要理由充分，所有者就能立即推动改变。即便如此，不满的董事也只有这一条路可走。如果在重大问题上仍得不到满意的结果，他就只能辞职。

1993.english: Logically, the third case should be the most effective in insuring first-class management.  In the second case the owner is not going to fire himself, and in the first case, directors often find it very difficult to deal with mediocrity or mild over- reaching.  Unless the unhappy directors can win over a majority of the board - an awkward social and logistical task, particularly if management's behavior is merely odious, not egregious - their hands are effectively tied.  In practice, directors trapped in situations of this kind usually convince themselves that by staying around they can do at least some good.  Meanwhile, management proceeds unfettered.
1993.chinese: 从逻辑上说，第三种情况最有利于确保一流管理。第二种情况下，业主不会把自己解雇；第一种情况下，董事又常常发现，很难应付平庸或轻度索取过度的管理层。除非持异议的董事能争取董事会多数支持，否则实际上就束手无策；无论从人际关系还是实际组织上说，这都是一件尴尬而麻烦的事，尤其当管理层的行为只是令人厌恶，还没到恶劣透顶的程度时。现实中，陷入这种处境的董事通常会说服自己：只要留下，至少还能做点好事。与此同时，管理层继续不受约束地行事。

1993.english: In the third case, the owner is neither judging himself nor burdened with the problem of garnering a majority.  He can also insure that outside directors are selected who will bring useful qualities to the board.  These directors, in turn, will know that the good advice they give will reach the right ears, rather than being stifled by a recalcitrant management.  If the controlling owner is intelligent and self-confident, he will make decisions in respect to management that are meritocratic and pro-shareholder. Moreover - and this is critically important - he can readily correct any mistake he makes.
1993.chinese: 在第三种情况下，所有者既不是在评判自己，也无须为争取多数支持而烦恼。他还可以确保选出的外部董事，能为董事会带来有用的素质。这些董事也会知道，自己提出的好建议能传到该听的人耳中，不会被顽固的管理层堵住。如果控股所有者聪明而自信，就会依据实际表现、站在股东立场上，作出有关管理层的决定。还有极其关键的一点：他若犯错，很容易纠正。

1993.english:
At Berkshire we operate in the second mode now and will for as long as I remain functional.  My health, let me add, is excellent. For better or worse, you are likely to have me as an owner/manager for some time.

After my death, all of my stock will go to my wife, Susie, should she survive me, or to a foundation if she dies before I do. In neither case will taxes and bequests require the sale of consequential amounts of stock.
1993.chinese:
在伯克希尔，目前我们按第二种模式运作，只要我还能正常履职，就会继续如此。顺便说一句，我身体很好。不管是好是坏，你们大概还得让我这个业主兼管理者再干上一阵。

我去世后，如果妻子苏茜还健在，我的全部股票都会交给她；如果她先于我去世，则会交给一家基金会。无论哪种情况，都不会因为纳税或遗赠，而需要出售数量可观的股票。

1993.english: When my stock is transferred to either my wife or the foundation, Berkshire will enter the third governance mode, going forward with a vitally interested, but non-management, owner and with a management that must perform for that owner.  In preparation for that time, Susie was elected to the board a few years ago, and in 1993 our son, Howard, joined the board.  These family members will not be managers of the company in the future, but they will represent the controlling interest should anything happen to me. Most of our other directors are also significant owners of Berkshire stock, and each has a strong owner-orientation.  All in all, we're prepared for "the truck."
1993.chinese: 当我的股票转交给妻子或基金会时，伯克希尔就会进入第三种治理模式：有一位切身关心公司、却不参与管理的所有者，以及必须为这位所有者交出成绩的管理层。为此，苏茜几年前已经当选董事；1993年，我们的儿子霍华德也加入了董事会。这些家人将来不会担任公司管理者，但如果我出了什么事，他们会代表控股权益。我们的其他董事，大多也持有相当数量的伯克希尔股票，而且每个人都有强烈的所有者意识。总而言之，我们已经为“那辆卡车”做好了准备。

1993.english:
## Shareholder-Designated Contributions

About 97% of all eligible shares participated in Berkshire's 1993 shareholder-designated contributions program.  Contributions made through the program were $9.4 million and 3,110 charities were recipients.

Berkshire's practice in respect to discretionary philanthropy - as contrasted to its policies regarding contributions that are clearly related to the company's business activities - differs significantly from that of other publicly-held corporations. There, most corporate contributions are made pursuant to the wishes of the CEO (who often will be responding to social pressures), employees (through matching gifts), or directors (through matching gifts or requests they make of the CEO).
1993.chinese:
## 股东指定捐款

1993年，伯克希尔股东指定捐款计划的参与股份，约占全部合资格股份的97%。计划合计捐出940万美元，3,110家慈善机构获赠。

伯克希尔对于自主决定的慈善捐赠，采取的做法与其他上市公司大不相同；这里不包括那些与公司经营活动明确相关的捐款。在其他上市公司，大多数公司捐款是按照首席执行官的意愿作出的——而他往往是在回应社交压力——或者按员工的意愿，通过配捐作出；再或者按董事的意愿，通过配捐或由董事向首席执行官提出请求作出。

1993.english: At Berkshire, we believe that the company's money is the owners' money, just as it would be in a closely-held corporation, partnership, or sole proprietorship.  Therefore, if funds are to be given to causes unrelated to Berkshire's business activities, it is the charities favored by our owners that should receive them. We've yet to find a CEO who believes he should personally fund the charities favored by his shareholders.  Why, then, should they foot the bill for his picks?
1993.chinese: 在伯克希尔，我们相信，公司的钱就是所有者的钱，正如在股权集中的公司、合伙企业或独资企业中一样。因此，如果把钱捐给与伯克希尔经营活动无关的事业，那么，受益的就应当是所有者喜爱的慈善机构。我们还没碰到哪位首席执行官认为，自己应该掏腰包，资助股东喜欢的慈善机构。既然如此，股东为什么该为他挑中的机构埋单呢？

1993.english: Let me add that our program is easy to administer.  Last fall, for two months, we borrowed one person from National Indemnity to help us implement the instructions that came from our 7,500 registered shareholders.  I'd guess that the average corporate program in which employee gifts are matched incurs far greater administrative costs.  Indeed, our entire corporate overhead is less than half the size of our charitable contributions.  (Charlie, however, insists that I tell you that $1.4 million of our $4.9 million overhead is attributable to our corporate jet, The Indefensible.)
1993.chinese: 还要补充一点：我们的计划很容易管理。去年秋天，我们从国民赔偿公司借调了一名员工，工作两个月，协助落实7,500名登记股东发来的指示。我猜，一般公司为员工捐款配捐的计划，管理成本要高得多。实际上，我们整个公司总部的费用，还不到慈善捐款的一半。（不过，查理坚持要我告诉大家：490万美元总部费用中，有140万美元花在了公司专机“无可辩护号”上。）

1993.english:
Below is a list showing the largest categories to which our shareholders have steered their contributions.

(a) 347 churches and synagogues received 569 gifts (b) 283 colleges and universities received 670 gifts (c) 244 K-12 schools (about two-thirds secular, one- third religious) received 525 gifts (d) 288 institutions dedicated to art, culture or the humanities received 447 gifts (e) 180 religious social-service organizations (split about equally between Christian and Jewish) received 411 gifts (f) 445 secular social-service organizations (about 40% youth-related) received 759 gifts (g) 153 hospitals received 261 gifts (h) 186 health-related organizations (American Heart Association, American Cancer Society, etc.) received 320 gifts
1993.chinese:
下表列出股东指定捐款流向的几个最大类别。

（a）347座教堂和犹太会堂，收到569笔捐款。

（b）283所学院和大学，收到670笔捐款。

（c）244所从幼儿园到12年级的学校，收到525笔捐款；其中约三分之二为非宗教学校，三分之一为宗教学校。

（d）288家从事艺术、文化或人文学科的机构，收到447笔捐款。

（e）180家宗教社会服务机构，收到411笔捐款；基督教与犹太教机构大约各占一半。

（f）445家非宗教社会服务机构，收到759笔捐款；其中约40%与青少年有关。

（g）153家医院，收到261笔捐款。

（h）186家健康相关机构，例如美国心脏协会、美国癌症协会等，收到320笔捐款。

1993.english: Three things about this list seem particularly interesting to me.  First, to some degree it indicates what people choose to give money to when they are acting of their own accord, free of pressure from solicitors or emotional appeals from charities.  Second, the contributions programs of publicly-held companies almost never allow gifts to churches and synagogues, yet clearly these institutions are what many shareholders would like to support. Third, the gifts made by our shareholders display conflicting philosophies:  130 gifts were directed to organizations that believe in making abortions readily available for women and 30 gifts were directed to organizations (other than churches) that discourage or are opposed to abortion.
1993.chinese: 关于这份名单，有三点让我觉得特别有意思。第一，它在一定程度上表明：不受募捐者施压，也不受慈善机构情感诉求影响时，人们自主决定会把钱捐给谁。第二，上市公司的捐款计划，几乎从不允许捐给教堂和犹太会堂；但显然，这正是许多股东希望支持的机构。第三，股东的捐款呈现出相互冲突的理念：130笔捐款流向主张让女性容易获得堕胎服务的机构，另有30笔流向劝阻或反对堕胎的机构——不包括教堂。

1993.english: Last year I told you that I was thinking of raising the amount that Berkshire shareholders can give under our designated- contributions program and asked for your comments.  We received a few well-written letters opposing the entire idea, on the grounds that it was our job to run the business and not our job to force shareholders into making charitable gifts.  Most of the shareholders responding, however, noted the tax efficiency of the plan and urged us to increase the designated amount.  Several shareholders who have given stock to their children or grandchildren told me that they consider the program a particularly good way to get youngsters thinking at an early age about the subject of giving.  These people, in other words, perceive the program to be an educational, as well as philanthropic, tool.  The bottom line is that we did raise the amount in 1993, from $8 per share to $10.
1993.chinese: 去年，我告诉大家，正在考虑提高股东指定捐款计划的额度，并征求意见。我们收到几封写得很好的信，反对整个计划，理由是我们的职责是经营企业，而不是强迫股东捐钱。不过，大多数回复的股东都提到，这项计划在税收上有效率，并敦促我们提高指定额度。一些把股票赠给子女或孙辈的股东告诉我，他们认为，这项计划特别有助于让年轻人尽早思考捐赠这件事。也就是说，在他们眼里，它既是慈善工具，也是教育工具。最终结果是，1993年，我们确实把额度从每股8美元提高到10美元。

1993.english:
In addition to the shareholder-designated contributions that Berkshire distributes, our operating businesses make contributions, including merchandise, averaging about $2.5 million annually. These contributions support local charities, such as The United Way, and produce roughly commensurate benefits for our businesses.

We suggest that new shareholders read the description of our shareholder-designated contributions program that appears on pages 50-51.  To participate in future programs, you must make sure your shares are registered in the name of the actual owner, not in the nominee name of a broker, bank or depository.  Shares not so registered on August 31, 1994 will be ineligible for the 1994 program.
1993.chinese:
除了伯克希尔按股东指定发放的捐款，我们旗下经营企业每年还平均捐赠约250万美元，其中包括商品。这些捐赠支持联合劝募会之类的地方慈善机构，也为我们的企业带来大致相称的益处。

建议新股东阅读第50—51页关于股东指定捐款计划的说明。要参加今后的计划，务必让股票登记在实际所有者名下，而非经纪商、银行或托管机构的代名人名下。1994年8月31日未按上述方式登记的股份，将没有资格参加1994年的计划。

1993.english:
## A Few Personal Items

Mrs. B - Rose Blumkin - had her 100th birthday on December 3, 1993.  (The candles cost more than the cake.)  That was a day on which the store was scheduled to be open in the evening.  Mrs. B, who works seven days a week, for however many hours the store operates, found the proper decision quite obvious:  She simply postponed her party until an evening when the store was closed.
1993.chinese:
## 几件私事

B夫人——罗丝·布卢姆金——于1993年12月3日迎来百岁生日。（蜡烛比蛋糕还贵。）那天，商店按计划晚上也营业。B夫人每周工作七天，店开多久，她就工作多久；对她来说，该怎么决定再清楚不过：她干脆把生日晚会推迟到商店晚上不营业的那一天。

1993.english: Mrs. B's story is well-known but worth telling again.  She came to the United States 77 years ago, unable to speak English and devoid of formal schooling.  In 1937, she founded the Nebraska Furniture Mart with $500.  Last year the store had sales of $200 million, a larger amount by far than that recorded by any other home furnishings store in the United States.  Our part in all of this began ten years ago when Mrs. B sold control of the business to Berkshire Hathaway, a deal we completed without obtaining audited financial statements, checking real estate records, or getting any warranties.  In short, her word was good enough for us.
1993.chinese: B夫人的故事广为人知，但值得再讲一遍。77年前，她来到美国，不会说英语，也没有受过正规教育。1937年，她用500美元创办了内布拉斯加家具卖场。去年，这家店销售额达到2亿美元，远远超过美国其他任何一家家居用品商店。我们参与这个故事，是从十年前开始的：当时，B夫人把企业控股权卖给伯克希尔·哈撒韦。完成交易时，我们没有索取经审计的财务报表，没有核查不动产登记，也没有要求任何保证。简而言之，她说的话，对我们就够了。

1993.english:
Naturally, I was delighted to attend Mrs. B's birthday party. After all, she's promised to attend my 100th.

---

Katharine Graham retired last year as the chairman of The Washington Post Company, having relinquished the CEO title three years ago.  In 1973, we purchased our stock in her company for about $10 million.  Our holding now garners $7 million a year in dividends and is worth over $400 million.  At the time of our purchase, we knew that the economic prospects of the company were good.  But equally important, Charlie and I concluded that Kay would prove to be an outstanding manager and would treat all shareholders honorably.  That latter consideration was particularly important because The Washington Post Company has two classes of stock, a structure that we've seen some managers abuse.
1993.chinese:
能出席B夫人的生日晚会，我自然十分高兴。毕竟，她已经答应来参加我的百岁生日。

---

凯瑟琳·格雷厄姆去年卸任《华盛顿邮报》公司董事长，三年前她已交出首席执行官职务。1973年，我们以约1,000万美元买下她公司的股票。如今，这项持仓每年给我们带来700万美元股息，市值超过4亿美元。买入时，我们知道公司的经济前景不错。但同样重要的是，查理和我判断，凯会成为一位出色的管理者，而且会诚实公正地对待所有股东。后一点尤其重要，因为《华盛顿邮报》公司设有两类股票；我们见过一些管理者滥用这种结构。

1993.english:
All of our judgments about this investment have been validated by events.  Kay's skills as a manager were underscored this past year when she was elected by Fortune's Board of Editors to the Business Hall of Fame.  On behalf of our shareholders, Charlie and I had long ago put her in Berkshire's Hall of Fame.

---

Another of last year's retirees was Don Keough of Coca-Cola, although, as he puts it, his retirement lasted "about 14 hours." Don is one of the most extraordinary human beings I've ever known - a man of enormous business talent, but, even more important, a man who brings out the absolute best in everyone lucky enough to associate with him.  Coca-Cola wants its product to be present at the happy times of a person's life.  Don Keough, as an individual, invariably increases the happiness of those around him.  It's impossible to think about Don without feeling good.
1993.chinese:
后来发生的一切，验证了我们对这项投资的全部判断。过去一年，《财富》杂志编辑委员会把凯选入商业名人堂，再次彰显了她的管理才干。而查理和我，早已代表股东，把她请进了伯克希尔的名人堂。

---

去年另一位退休的人，是可口可乐的唐·基奥。不过，用他自己的话说，他的退休“持续了大约14个小时”。唐是我认识的最非凡的人之一：他商业才能极高，但更重要的是，凡是有幸与他共事的人，他都能激发出他们最好的一面。可口可乐希望，在人们一生的快乐时刻，自己的产品都在场。而唐·基奥本人，总能让身边的人更加快乐。想到唐，就不可能心情不好。

1993.english: I will edge up to how I met Don by slipping in a plug for my neighborhood in Omaha:  Though Charlie has lived in California for 45 years, his home as a boy was about 200 feet away from the house where I now live; my wife, Susie, grew up 1 1/2 blocks away; and we have about 125 Berkshire shareholders in the zip code.  As for Don, in 1958 he bought the house directly across the street from mine. He was then a coffee salesman with a big family and a small income.
1993.chinese: 先容我给自己在奥马哈住的街区打个小广告，再慢慢说到我是怎样认识唐的。查理虽然已经在加利福尼亚住了45年，但他小时候的家，距我现在的房子大约只有200英尺；我妻子苏茜在一个半街区外长大；我们这个邮政编码区里，大约住着125名伯克希尔股东。至于唐，他在1958年买下了我家正对面的房子。当时，他是个卖咖啡的，家里人口多，收入却不多。

1993.english: The impressions I formed in those days about Don were a factor in my decision to have Berkshire make a record $1 billion investment in Coca-Cola in 1988-89.  Roberto Goizueta had become CEO of Coke in 1981, with Don alongside as his partner.  The two of them took hold of a company that had stagnated during the previous decade and moved it from $4.4 billion of market value to $58 billion in less than 13 years.  What a difference a pair of managers like this makes, even when their product has been around for 100 years.
1993.chinese: 那些年，唐给我留下的印象，是我在1988—1989年决定让伯克希尔向可口可乐作出创纪录的10亿美元投资时，考虑的因素之一。罗伯托·戈伊苏埃塔于1981年出任可口可乐首席执行官，唐在他身旁搭档。两人接手的是一家在此前十年停滞不前的公司，不到13年，就把它的市值从44亿美元推高到580亿美元。即使产品已经存在了100年，这样一对管理者，仍然能带来天壤之别。

1993.english:
---

Frank Rooney did double duty last year.  In addition to leading H. H. Brown to record profits - 35% above the 1992 high - he also was key to our merger with Dexter.

Frank has known Harold Alfond and Peter Lunder for decades, and shortly after our purchase of H. H. Brown, told me what a wonderful operation they managed.  He encouraged us to get together and in due course we made a deal.  Frank told Harold and Peter that Berkshire would provide an ideal corporate "home" for Dexter, and that assurance undoubtedly contributed to their decision to join with us.
1993.chinese:
---

弗兰克·鲁尼去年身兼两项重任。他不但带领H.H.布朗创造了利润新高，比1992年的最高纪录还高出35%，也在我们与德克斯特的合并中发挥了关键作用。

弗兰克认识哈罗德·阿尔方德和彼得·伦德已经几十年。我们买下H.H.布朗后不久，他就告诉我，两人经营着一家多么出色的企业。他鼓励我们见面，后来我们达成了交易。弗兰克向哈罗德和彼得保证，伯克希尔会为德克斯特提供一个理想的企业“家园”；这番保证，无疑促成了他们加入我们的决定。

1993.english:
I've told you in the past of Frank's extraordinary record in building Melville Corp. during his 23 year tenure as CEO.  Now, at 72, he's setting an even faster pace at Berkshire.  Frank has a low-key, relaxed style, but don't let that fool you.  When he swings, the ball disappears far over the fence.

## The Annual Meeting

This year the Annual Meeting will be held at the Orpheum Theater in downtown Omaha at 9:30 a.m. on Monday, April 25, 1994. A record 2,200 people turned up for the meeting last year, but the theater can handle many more.  We will have a display in the lobby featuring many of our consumer products - candy, spray guns, shoes, cutlery, encyclopedias, and the like.  Among my favorites slated to be there is a See's candy assortment that commemorates Mrs. B's 100th birthday and that features her picture, rather than Mrs. See's, on the package.
1993.chinese:
以前我曾讲过，弗兰克担任梅尔维尔公司首席执行官23年，把公司发展壮大的非凡业绩。如今，他72岁了，在伯克希尔却跑出了更快的速度。弗兰克作风低调、从容，可别让这一点骗了你。他一挥棒，球就飞过围栏，远得不见踪影。

## 股东年会

今年的股东年会，将于1994年4月25日星期一上午9:30，在奥马哈市中心的奥菲姆剧院举行。去年有创纪录的2,200人到场，不过，剧院还能容纳多得多的人。我们会在大厅展示许多消费品，包括糖果、喷枪、鞋、刀具、百科全书等。其中，我特别喜欢的一款，是纪念B夫人百岁生日的喜诗什锦糖果：包装上印的是她的照片，而不是喜诗夫人的照片。

1993.english: We recommend that you promptly get hotel reservations at one of these hotels: (1) The Radisson-Redick Tower, a small (88 rooms) but nice hotel across the street from the Orpheum; (2) the much larger Red Lion Hotel, located about a five-minute walk from the Orpheum; or (3) the Marriott, located in West Omaha about 100 yards from Borsheim's, which is a twenty-minute drive from downtown. We will have buses at the Marriott that will leave at 8:30 and 8:45 for the meeting and return after it ends.
1993.chinese: 建议大家尽快预订以下酒店之一：（1）雷迪森—雷迪克大厦酒店，规模不大，只有88间客房，但很不错，就在奥菲姆剧院对面；（2）规模大得多的红狮酒店，步行到剧院大约五分钟；（3）位于西奥马哈的万豪酒店，距波仙珠宝约100码，从市中心开车过去约二十分钟。我们会安排巴士在上午8:30和8:45从万豪酒店出发，前往会场，会议结束后送大家返回。

1993.english:
An attachment to our proxy material explains how you can obtain the card you will need for admission to the meeting.  With the admission card, we will enclose information about parking facilities located near the Orpheum.  If you are driving, come a little early.  Nearby lots fill up quickly and you may have to walk a few blocks.

As usual, we will have buses to take you to Nebraska Furniture Mart and Borsheim's after the meeting and to take you from there to downtown hotels or the airport later.  Those of you arriving early can visit the Furniture Mart any day of the week; it is open from 10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. on Saturdays and from noon to 5:30 p.m. on Sundays.  Borsheim's normally is closed on Sunday but will be open for shareholders and their guests from noon to 6 p.m. on Sunday, April 24.
1993.chinese:
委托投票材料的附件会说明，如何取得入场所需的卡片。随入场卡寄出的，还会有奥菲姆剧院附近停车设施的信息。自己开车的话，请早到一点。附近停车场很快就满，你可能得走上几个街区。

和往年一样，会后我们会安排巴士，送大家去内布拉斯加家具卖场和波仙珠宝，稍后再从那里送往市中心酒店或机场。提早抵达的股东，一周中任何一天都可以逛家具卖场；星期六营业时间为上午10:00至下午5:30，星期日为中午12:00至下午5:30。波仙珠宝通常星期日休息，但4月24日星期日，会专门为股东及来宾从中午12:00营业到下午6:00。

1993.english:
In past trips to Borsheim's, many of you have met Susan Jacques.  Early in 1994, Susan was made President and CEO of the company, having risen in 11 years from a $4-an-hour job that she took at the store when she was 23.  Susan will be joined at Borsheim's on Sunday by many of the managers of our other businesses, and Charlie and I will be there as well.

On the previous evening, Saturday, April 23, there will be a baseball game at Rosenblatt Stadium between the Omaha Royals and the Nashville Sounds (which could turn out to be Michael Jordan's team).  As you may know, a few years ago I bought 25% of the Royals (a capital-allocation decision for which I will not become famous) and this year the league has cooperatively scheduled a home stand at Annual Meeting time.
1993.chinese:
过去到过波仙珠宝的许多股东，都见过苏珊·雅克。1994年初，苏珊被任命为公司总裁兼首席执行官。她23岁时到店里工作，时薪4美元，用了11年升到现在的位置。星期日，我们其他许多企业的管理者也会来到波仙珠宝，与苏珊一起接待大家；查理和我也会在场。

前一天晚上，也就是4月23日星期六，奥马哈皇家队与纳什维尔声音队将在罗森布拉特球场比赛；声音队届时说不定会成为迈克尔·乔丹效力的球队。大家也许知道，几年前我买下了皇家队25%的权益——这笔资本配置决定，不会让我名扬四海。今年，联盟很给面子，在股东年会期间安排了主场系列赛。

1993.english:
I will throw the first pitch on the 23rd, and it's a certainty that I will improve on last year's humiliating performance.  On that occasion, the catcher inexplicably called for my "sinker" and I dutifully delivered a pitch that barely missed my foot.  This year, I will go with my high hard one regardless of what the catcher signals, so bring your speed-timing devices.  The proxy statement will include information about obtaining tickets to the game.  I regret to report that you won't have to buy them from scalpers.

Warren E. Buffett March 1, 1994                       Chairman of the Board
1993.chinese:
23日我会投开场球，而且肯定比去年那次丢脸的表现强。上回，捕手不知怎么想的，竟要我投“下沉球”；我老老实实照办，球差一点就砸到自己的脚。今年，不管捕手打什么手势，我都要投我的高位快速球，所以请带好你们的测速设备。委托投票说明书中，会介绍如何取得比赛门票。遗憾地告诉大家，你们无须找黄牛买票。

沃伦·E.巴菲特  
董事会主席  
1994年3月1日

1994.english:
BERKSHIRE HATHAWAY INC.

To the Shareholders of Berkshire Hathaway Inc.:

Our gain in net worth during 1994 was $1.45 billion or 13.9%. Over the last 30 years (that is, since present management took over) our per-share book value has grown from $19 to $10,083, or at a rate of 23% compounded annually.

Charlie Munger, Berkshire's Vice Chairman and my partner, and I make few predictions.  One we will confidently offer, however, is that the future performance of Berkshire won't come close to matching the performance of the past.
1994.chinese:
伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司

致伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司的股东：

1994年，我们的净资产增加14.5亿美元，增长13.9%。过去30年，也就是现任管理层接手以来，每股账面价值从19美元增至10,083美元，年复合增长率为23%。

伯克希尔副董事长、我的伙伴查理·芒格和我，很少作预测。不过，有一项我们可以有把握地告诉大家：伯克希尔未来的表现，将远远比不上过去。

1994.english:
The problem is not that what has worked in the past will cease to work in the future.  To the contrary, we believe that our formula - the purchase at sensible prices of businesses that have good underlying economics and are run by honest and able people - is certain to produce reasonable success.  We expect, therefore, to keep on doing well.

A fat wallet, however, is the enemy of superior investment results.  And Berkshire now has a net worth of $11.9 billion compared to about $22 million when Charlie and I began to manage the company.  Though there are as many good businesses as ever, it is useless for us to make purchases that are inconsequential in relation to Berkshire's capital.  (As Charlie regularly reminds me, "If something is not worth doing at all, it's not worth doing well.")  We now consider a security for purchase only if we believe we can deploy at least $100 million in it.  Given that minimum, Berkshire's investment universe has shrunk dramatically.
1994.chinese:
问题并不是过去有效的办法将来会失灵。恰恰相反，我们相信自己的做法——以合理价格买入经济特性良好、由诚实能干的人经营的企业——必定能够带来相当不错的成果。因此，我们预期自己还会继续做得不错。

不过，鼓鼓的钱包是卓越投资业绩的敌人。如今伯克希尔净资产为119亿美元，而查理和我开始管理公司时，只有约2,200万美元。虽然好企业和过去一样多，但买入相对于伯克希尔资本而言无足轻重的东西，对我们没有用。（正如查理经常提醒我的：“一件事如果根本不值得做，也就不值得把它做好。”）如今，只有认为至少能在某项证券上投入1亿美元，我们才会考虑买入。有了这道最低门槛，伯克希尔的投资范围便大幅缩小了。

1994.english: Nevertheless, we will stick with the approach that got us here and try not to relax our standards.  Ted Williams, in The Story of My Life, explains why:  "My argument is, to be a good hitter, you've got to get a good ball to hit.  It's the first rule in the book.  If I have to bite at stuff that is out of my happy zone, I'm not a .344 hitter.  I might only be a .250 hitter."  Charlie and I agree and will try to wait for opportunities that are well within our own "happy zone."
1994.chinese: 尽管如此，我们仍会坚持把自己带到今天这一步的办法，努力不放松标准。特德·威廉斯在《我的一生》中解释了原因：“我的看法是，要做一个好打者，得有好球可打。这是第一条规则。如果连舒适区以外的球也非挥棒不可，我就不会是打击率三成四四的打者，可能只有两成五。”查理和我赞同这一点，会努力等待那些稳稳落在我们自己‘舒适区’里的机会。

1994.english:
We will continue to ignore political and economic forecasts, which are an expensive distraction for many investors and businessmen.  Thirty years ago, no one could have foreseen the huge expansion of the Vietnam War, wage and price controls, two oil shocks, the resignation of a president, the dissolution of the Soviet Union, a one-day drop in the Dow of 508 points, or treasury bill yields fluctuating between 2.8% and 17.4%.

But, surprise - none of these blockbuster events made the slightest dent in Ben Graham's investment principles.  Nor did they render unsound the negotiated purchases of fine businesses at sensible prices.  Imagine the cost to us, then, if we had let a fear of unknowns cause us to defer or alter the deployment of capital.  Indeed, we have usually made our best purchases when apprehensions about some macro event were at a peak.  Fear is the foe of the faddist, but the friend of the fundamentalist.
1994.chinese:
我们会继续忽略政治和经济预测。对许多投资者与企业家来说，这些预测分散精力，而且代价高昂。三十年前，没有人能够预见越南战争大幅升级、工资和物价管制、两次石油冲击、总统辞职、苏联解体、道琼斯指数一天跌508点，或国库券收益率在2.8%至17.4%之间波动。

然而，意外吧——这些惊天动地的大事，没有一件动摇本·格雷厄姆投资原则分毫；它们也没有使以合理价格通过协商买进好企业这件事变得不明智。那么，想一想：如果我们因为害怕未知，而推迟或改变资本配置，会付出多大代价？事实上，我们最好的收购，通常正是在大家对某个宏观事件最忧心的时候完成的。恐惧是追逐风潮者的敌人，却是着眼基本面者的朋友。

1994.english:
A different set of major shocks is sure to occur in the next 30 years.  We will neither try to predict these nor to profit from them.  If we can identify businesses similar to those we have purchased in the past, external surprises will have little effect on our long-term results.

What we promise you - along with more modest gains - is that during your ownership of Berkshire, you will fare just as Charlie and I do.  If you suffer, we will suffer; if we prosper, so will you.  And we will not break this bond by introducing compensation arrangements that give us a greater participation in the upside than the downside.
1994.chinese:
未来30年，肯定会出现另一批重大冲击。我们既不打算预测，也不试图靠它们赚钱。如果能找到与过去买入的那些企业相似的生意，外部意外事件对我们的长期成果就不会有多大影响。

除了更温和的增长，我们还向各位保证：持有伯克希尔期间，你们的境遇将与查理和我完全相同。你们受损，我们也受损；我们兴旺，你们也兴旺。我们不会引入那种上涨时让自己多分、下跌时却少担的薪酬安排，来打破这层纽带。

1994.english:
We further promise you that our personal fortunes will remain overwhelmingly concentrated in Berkshire shares:  We will not ask you to invest with us and then put our own money elsewhere.  In addition, Berkshire dominates both the investment portfolios of most members of our families and of a great many friends who belonged to partnerships that Charlie and I ran in the 1960's.  We could not be more motivated to do our best.

Luckily, we have a good base from which to work.  Ten years ago, in 1984, Berkshire's insurance companies held securities having a value of $1.7 billion, or about $1,500 per Berkshire share.  Leaving aside all income and capital gains from those securities, Berkshire's pre-tax earnings that year were only about $6 million.  We had earnings, yes, from our various manufacturing, retailing and service businesses, but they were almost entirely offset by the combination of underwriting losses in our insurance business, corporate overhead and interest expense.
1994.chinese:
我们还保证，个人财富的绝大部分，将继续集中在伯克希尔股票上。我们不会请各位和我们一起投资，自己却把钱放到别处。此外，我们大多数家人的投资组合，以及许多朋友的投资组合，也都以伯克希尔为主；这些朋友曾是查理和我在20世纪60年代经营的合伙企业的合伙人。要说尽力而为的动力，我们已经强得不能再强了。

幸运的是，我们有一个良好的基础。十年前，也就是1984年，伯克希尔保险公司持有的证券市值为17亿美元，折合伯克希尔每股约1,500美元。若把这些证券带来的全部收入与资本利得剔除，伯克希尔那一年的税前利润只有约600万美元。我们的制造、零售和服务企业确实赚了钱，但几乎全部被保险承保亏损、总部费用和利息费用抵消了。

1994.english:
Now we hold securities worth $18 billion, or over $15,000 per Berkshire share.  If you again exclude all income from these securities, our pre-tax earnings in 1994 were about $384 million. During the decade, employment has grown from 5,000 to 22,000 (including eleven people at World Headquarters).

We achieved our gains through the efforts of a superb corps of operating managers who get extraordinary results from some ordinary-appearing businesses.  Casey Stengel described managing a baseball team as "getting paid for home runs other fellows hit."  That's my formula at Berkshire, also.
1994.chinese:
如今，我们持有的证券价值180亿美元，折合伯克希尔每股超过15,000美元。如果同样剔除这些证券带来的全部收入，1994年的税前利润约为3.84亿美元。十年间，员工人数由5,000人增至22,000人，其中包括‘全球总部’的十一人。

这些进步，来自一批杰出的经营管理者：他们从一些看起来普普通通的企业里，做出了非同寻常的成绩。凯西·斯滕格尔把管理棒球队形容为：“别人打出本垒打，你领报酬。”我在伯克希尔用的也是这套办法。

1994.english: The businesses in which we have partial interests are equally important to Berkshire's success.  A few statistics will illustrate their significance:  In 1994, Coca-Cola sold about 280 billion 8-ounce servings and earned a little less than a penny on each.  But pennies add up.  Through Berkshire's 7.8% ownership of Coke, we have an economic interest in 21 billion of its servings, which produce "soft-drink earnings" for us of nearly $200 million.  Similarly, by way of its Gillette stock, Berkshire has a 7% share of the world's razor and blade market (measured by revenues, not by units), a proportion according us about $250 million of sales in 1994.  And, at Wells Fargo, a $53 billion bank, our 13% ownership translates into a $7 billion "Berkshire Bank" that earned about $100 million during 1994.
1994.chinese: 那些我们只持有部分权益的企业，对伯克希尔的成功同样重要。几组数字可以说明它们的分量：1994年，可口可乐卖出约2,800亿份8盎司装饮料，每份赚取的利润略低于一美分。不过，一分一分也能积少成多。伯克希尔持有可口可乐7.8%的股份，因此在经济利益上，我们拥有其中210亿份饮料，为我们带来近2亿美元的‘软饮料利润’。同样，通过吉列股票，伯克希尔拥有全球剃须刀及刀片市场7%的份额——按收入计，而非按件数——1994年对应销售额约2.5亿美元。再看富国银行，这家银行规模为530亿美元；我们的13%权益，相当于一家70亿美元的‘伯克希尔银行’，1994年赚取了约1亿美元。

1994.english:
It's far better to own a significant portion of the Hope diamond than 100% of a rhinestone, and the companies just mentioned easily qualify as rare gems.  Best of all, we aren't limited to simply a few of this breed, but instead possess a growing collection.

Stock prices will continue to fluctuate - sometimes sharply - and the economy will have its ups and down.  Over time, however, we believe it highly probable that the sort of businesses we own will continue to increase in value at a satisfactory rate.
1994.chinese:
拥有‘希望之钻’的一大块权益，远胜于拥有一颗水钻的100%。刚才提到的公司，毫无疑问都是稀世珍宝。更妙的是，我们并不限于寥寥几颗，而是拥有一批日渐丰富的收藏。

股价会继续波动，有时还会剧烈波动，经济也会有起有伏。不过，从长期看，我们相信，自己所拥有的这类企业，极有可能继续以令人满意的速度增值。

1994.english:
## Book Value and Intrinsic Value

We regularly report our per-share book value, an easily calculable number, though one of limited use.  Just as regularly, we tell you that what counts is intrinsic value, a number that is impossible to pinpoint but essential to estimate.

For example, in 1964, we could state with certitude that Berkshire's per-share book value was $19.46.  However, that figure considerably overstated the stock's intrinsic value since all of the company's resources were tied up in a sub-profitable textile business.  Our textile assets had neither going-concern nor liquidation values equal to their carrying values.  In 1964, then, anyone inquiring into the soundness of Berkshire's balance sheet might well have deserved the answer once offered up by a Hollywood mogul of dubious reputation:  "Don't worry, the liabilities are solid."
1994.chinese:
## 账面价值与内在价值

我们定期公布每股账面价值。这是个容易计算、用途却有限的数字。同样，我们也一再告诉大家：重要的是内在价值，一个无法精确确定，却必须估计的数字。

例如，1964年，我们可以确切地说，伯克希尔每股账面价值为19.46美元。不过，这个数字大大高估了股票的内在价值，因为公司所有资源都被困在一家盈利表现欠佳的纺织企业里。我们的纺织资产，无论持续经营价值还是清算价值，都达不到账面金额。所以，1964年若有人询问伯克希尔资产负债表是否可靠，恐怕很适合用一位名声不怎么好的好莱坞大亨曾经说过的话回答：“别担心，负债可都是实打实的。”

1994.english: Today, Berkshire's situation has reversed:  Many of the businesses we control are worth far more than their carrying value.  (Those we don't control, such as Coca-Cola or Gillette, are carried at current market values.)  We continue to give you book value figures, however, because they serve as a rough, albeit significantly understated, tracking measure for Berkshire's intrinsic value.  Last year, in fact, the two measures moved in concert:  Book value gained 13.9%, and that was the approximate gain in intrinsic value also.
1994.chinese: 如今，伯克希尔的情况反过来了：我们控股的许多企业，价值远高于列账金额。（可口可乐、吉列之类我们不控股的公司，则按当前市值列账。）不过，我们仍然提供账面价值数字，因为它能粗略追踪伯克希尔的内在价值，虽然明显偏低。事实上，去年两项指标同步变动：账面价值增长13.9%，内在价值的增幅也大致如此。

1994.english: We define intrinsic value as the discounted value of the cash that can be taken out of a business during its remaining life.  Anyone calculating intrinsic value necessarily comes up with a highly subjective figure that will change both as estimates of future cash flows are revised and as interest rates move.  Despite its fuzziness, however, intrinsic value is all- important and is the only logical way to evaluate the relative attractiveness of investments and businesses.
1994.chinese: 我们把内在价值定义为：企业剩余寿命中能够取出的现金的折现值。任何人计算内在价值，都必然得出一个高度主观的数字；随着对未来现金流的估计修正，或利率变化，这个数字也会改变。不过，尽管模糊，内在价值仍然极其重要，而且是评价不同投资和企业相对吸引力的唯一合乎逻辑的方法。

1994.english:
To see how historical input (book value) and future output (intrinsic value) can diverge, let's look at another form of investment, a college education.  Think of the education's cost as its "book value."  If it is to be accurate, the cost should include the earnings that were foregone by the student because he chose college rather than a job.

For this exercise, we will ignore the important non-economic benefits of an education and focus strictly on its economic value.  First, we must estimate the earnings that the graduate will receive over his lifetime and subtract from that figure an estimate of what he would have earned had he lacked his education.  That gives us an excess earnings figure, which must then be discounted, at an appropriate interest rate, back to graduation day.  The dollar result equals the intrinsic economic value of the education.
1994.chinese:
要看历史投入，也就是账面价值，如何与未来产出，也就是内在价值，发生背离，不妨看另一种投资：大学教育。把教育成本当成它的‘账面价值’。要算得准确，成本还应包括学生因选择上大学而没有工作，所放弃的收入。

在这个例子中，我们暂且不谈教育那些重要的非经济益处，只看经济价值。首先，估计毕业生一生能够获得的收入，再减去假如没有受这番教育，他本来能赚到的收入估计值。所得就是超额收入，然后用适当利率，把它折现回毕业那一天。算出来的金额，就是这份教育的内在经济价值。

1994.english:
Some graduates will find that the book value of their education exceeds its intrinsic value, which means that whoever paid for the education didn't get his money's worth.  In other cases, the intrinsic value of an education will far exceed its book value, a result that proves capital was wisely deployed.  In all cases, what is clear is that book value is meaningless as an indicator of intrinsic value.

Now let's get less academic and look at Scott Fetzer, an example from Berkshire's own experience.  This account will not only illustrate how the relationship of book value and intrinsic value can change but also will provide an accounting lesson that I know you have been breathlessly awaiting.  Naturally, I've chosen here to talk about an acquisition that has turned out to be a huge winner.
1994.chinese:
有些毕业生会发现，所受教育的账面价值超过其内在价值；也就是说，为教育买单的人没有花得物有所值。另一些人所受教育的内在价值，则会远超账面价值，证明资本配置得很明智。无论哪一种情况，都清楚地说明：用账面价值来衡量内在价值，没有意义。

现在，少来点学院派讨论，来看伯克希尔自己的例子——斯科特与费策。这段经历不仅能说明账面价值与内在价值的关系如何改变，还能顺便上一堂会计课；我知道，各位早已屏息以待。当然，我特意挑了一桩大获成功的收购来讲。

1994.english:
Berkshire purchased Scott Fetzer at the beginning of 1986. At the time, the company was a collection of 22 businesses, and today we have exactly the same line-up - no additions and no disposals.  Scott Fetzer's main operations are World Book, Kirby, and Campbell Hausfeld, but many other units are important contributors to earnings as well.

We paid $315.2 million for Scott Fetzer, which at the time had $172.6 million of book value.  The $142.6 million premium we handed over indicated our belief that the company's intrinsic value was close to double its book value.
1994.chinese:
伯克希尔于1986年初买下斯科特与费策。当时，它旗下有22项业务，如今阵容完全相同，没有增加，也没有出售。主要业务是世界图书、柯比和坎贝尔·豪斯菲尔德，不过，其他许多单位也为利润作出了重要贡献。

我们为斯科特与费策支付了3.152亿美元，当时它的账面价值为1.726亿美元。多付出的1.426亿美元溢价，表明我们认为，它的内在价值接近账面价值的两倍。

1994.english: Because it had excess cash when our deal was made, Scott Fetzer was able to pay Berkshire dividends of $125 million in 1986, though it earned only $40.3 million.  I should mention that we have not introduced leverage into Scott Fetzer's balance sheet.  In fact, the company has gone from very modest debt when we purchased it to virtually no debt at all (except for debt used by its finance subsidiary).  Similarly, we have not sold plants and leased them back, nor sold receivables, nor the like. Throughout our years of ownership, Scott Fetzer has operated as a conservatively-financed and liquid enterprise.
1994.chinese: 交易时，斯科特与费策有多余现金，因此，尽管1986年只赚了4,030万美元，仍能向伯克希尔支付1.25亿美元股息。我得说明，我们并没有给斯科特与费策的资产负债表加杠杆。事实上，公司从收购时只有少量债务，变成了几乎完全没有债务，只有金融子公司使用的债务除外。同样，我们没有把厂房卖掉再租回来，也没有出售应收账款，诸如此类的事都没有做。在我们持有期间，斯科特与费策始终是一家融资保守、流动性充足的企业。

1994.english:
As you can see, Scott Fetzer's earnings have increased steadily since we bought it, but book value has not grown commensurately.  Consequently, return on equity, which was exceptional at the time of our purchase, has now become truly extraordinary.  Just how extraordinary is illustrated by comparing Scott Fetzer's performance to that of the Fortune 500, a group it would qualify for if it were a stand-alone company.

Had Scott Fetzer been on the 1993 500 list - the latest available for inspection - the company's return on equity would have ranked 4th.  But that is far from the whole story.  The top three companies in return on equity were Insilco, LTV and Gaylord Container, each of which emerged from bankruptcy in 1993 and none of which achieved meaningful earnings that year except for those they realized when they were accorded debt forgiveness in bankruptcy proceedings.  Leaving aside such non-operating windfalls, Scott Fetzer's return on equity would have ranked it first on the Fortune 500, well ahead of number two.  Indeed, Scott Fetzer's return on equity was double that of the company ranking tenth.
1994.chinese:
大家可以看到，自收购以来，斯科特与费策的利润持续增长，账面价值却没有相应增加。因此，收购时就已经很出色的股东权益回报率，如今变得非同寻常。把它与《财富》500强比较，就能看出究竟有多出色；如果它是一家独立公司，本来就有资格进入这份名单。

假如斯科特与费策列入1993年《财富》500强——这是目前能查到的最新一期——它的股东权益回报率会排第4。但这还远不是全部。排名前三的是英西尔科、LTV和盖洛德集装箱公司，三家都于1993年走出破产程序；除了在破产程序中获债务减免所确认的收益，没有一家在当年取得有意义的利润。剔除这些非经营性的意外收益，斯科特与费策就会排在500强之首，远超第2名。事实上，它的股东权益回报率，是第10名公司的两倍。

1994.english:
You might expect that Scott Fetzer's success could only be explained by a cyclical peak in earnings, a monopolistic position, or leverage.  But no such circumstances apply.  Rather, the company's success comes from the managerial expertise of CEO Ralph Schey, of whom I'll tell you more later.

First, however, the promised accounting lesson:  When we paid a $142.6 million premium over book value for Scott Fetzer, that figure had to be recorded on Berkshire's balance sheet. I'll spare you the details of how this worked (these were laid out in an appendix to our 1986 Annual Report) and get to the bottom line:  After a premium is initially recorded, it must in almost all cases be written off over time through annual charges that are shown as costs in the acquiring company's earnings statement.
1994.chinese:
各位也许会以为，只有盈利处于周期高峰、垄断地位或杠杆，才能解释斯科特与费策的成功。但这些情况一个也不存在。公司的成功，来自首席执行官拉尔夫·谢伊的管理本领，稍后我会再谈他。

不过，先上说好的会计课：买下斯科特与费策时，我们在账面价值之上多付了1.426亿美元，这笔金额必须记在伯克希尔的资产负债表上。具体怎样入账，我就不折腾各位了，1986年年报的附录里已经详述过。直接说结果：溢价初次入账后，几乎在所有情况下，都必须逐年核销，每年的扣除额，作为成本列入收购方的利润表。

1994.english: The following table shows, first, the annual charges Berkshire has made to gradually extinguish the Scott Fetzer acquisition premium and, second, the premium that remains on our books.  These charges have no effect on cash or the taxes we pay, and are not, in our view, an economic cost (though many accountants would disagree with us).  They are merely a way for us to reduce the carrying value of Scott Fetzer on our books so that the figure will eventually match the net worth that Scott Fetzer actually employs in its business.
1994.chinese: 下表首先列出伯克希尔为逐步核销斯科特与费策收购溢价而计入的年度费用，其次列出账上尚余的溢价。这些费用不影响现金，也不影响我们缴纳的税款；在我们看来，它们不是经济成本，虽然许多会计师不会同意。它们只是降低斯科特与费策在我们账上列账价值的一种办法，最终使该金额与斯科特与费策实际用于经营的净资产一致。

1994.english: Note that by the end of 1994 the premium was reduced to $54.2 million.  When this figure is added to Scott Fetzer's year- end book value of $94 million, the total is $148.2 million, which is the current carrying value of Scott Fetzer on Berkshire's books.  That amount is less than half of our carrying value for the company when it was acquired.  Yet Scott Fetzer is now earning about twice what it then did.  Clearly, the intrinsic value of the business has consistently grown, even though we have just as consistently marked down its carrying value through purchase-premium charges that reduced Berkshire's earnings and net worth.
1994.chinese: 请注意，到1994年末，溢价已经降至5,420万美元。加上斯科特与费策年末9,400万美元账面价值，合计1.482亿美元，也就是它目前在伯克希尔账上的列账价值。这个数额，还不到收购时列账价值的一半，可斯科特与费策如今的利润却约为当时的两倍。显然，企业内在价值一直在增长；与此同时，我们也一直通过收购溢价费用调低列账价值，减少伯克希尔的报表利润与净资产。

1994.english:
The difference between Scott Fetzer's intrinsic value and its carrying value on Berkshire's books is now huge.  As I mentioned earlier - but am delighted to mention again - credit for this agreeable mismatch goes to Ralph Schey, a focused, smart and high-grade manager.

The reasons for Ralph's success are not complicated.  Ben Graham taught me 45 years ago that in investing it is not necessary to do extraordinary things to get extraordinary results.  In later life, I have been surprised to find that this statement holds true in business management as well.  What a manager must do is handle the basics well and not get diverted. That's precisely Ralph's formula.  He establishes the right goals and never forgets what he set out to do.  On the personal side, Ralph is a joy to work with.  He's forthright about problems and is self-confident without being self-important.
1994.chinese:
如今，斯科特与费策的内在价值与伯克希尔账上列账价值之间，差距已经很大。前面提过，我也乐意再提一遍：这种令人愉快的不匹配，功劳属于拉尔夫·谢伊，一位专注、聪明、品格出众的管理者。

拉尔夫成功的原因并不复杂。45年前，本·格雷厄姆教我：投资中，不必做非凡的事，也能取得非凡的结果。后来，我惊讶地发现，这句话在企业管理中也成立。管理者必须把基本功做好，别分心。这正是拉尔夫的办法。他设定正确目标，从不忘记自己最初要做什么。就个人相处而言，和他共事很愉快。他直言不讳地谈问题，自信却不自大。

1994.english:
He is also experienced.  Though I don't know Ralph's age, I do know that, like many of our managers, he is over 65.  At Berkshire, we look to performance, not to the calendar.  Charlie and I, at 71 and 64 respectively, now keep George Foreman's picture on our desks.  You can make book that our scorn for a mandatory retirement age will grow stronger every year.

## Intrinsic Value and Capital Allocation

Understanding intrinsic value is as important for managers as it is for investors.  When managers are making capital allocation decisions - including decisions to repurchase shares - it's vital that they act in ways that increase per-share intrinsic value and avoid moves that decrease it.  This principle may seem obvious but we constantly see it violated.  And, when misallocations occur, shareholders are hurt.
1994.chinese:
他也经验丰富。我不知道拉尔夫的年纪，但知道他和我们的许多经理人一样，已经超过65岁。在伯克希尔，我们看表现，不看日历。查理和我分别71岁、64岁，如今桌上都摆着乔治·福尔曼的照片。各位可以放心下注：对于强制退休年龄，我们的不屑只会一年比一年更深。

## 内在价值与资本配置

理解内在价值，对管理者和投资者同样重要。管理者作资本配置决定，包括回购股票时，至关重要的是：采取能够提高每股内在价值的行动，避免降低它。这个原则看似显而易见，我们却不断看到它被违背。而资本一旦配错，受损的就是股东。

1994.english: For example, in contemplating business mergers and acquisitions, many managers tend to focus on whether the transaction is immediately dilutive or anti-dilutive to earnings per share (or, at financial institutions, to per-share book value).  An emphasis of this sort carries great dangers.  Going back to our college-education example, imagine that a 25-year-old first-year MBA student is considering merging his future economic interests with those of a 25-year-old day laborer.  The MBA student, a non-earner, would find that a "share-for-share" merger of his equity interest in himself with that of the day laborer would enhance his near-term earnings (in a big way!).  But what could be sillier for the student than a deal of this kind?
1994.chinese: 例如，考虑企业合并与收购时，许多管理者往往只关注交易会立即摊薄还是增厚每股收益；金融机构则看每股账面价值。这种侧重点有很大危险。回到大学教育的例子：设想一个25岁、正在读MBA一年级的学生，考虑把自己未来的经济利益，与一位同样25岁的日薪工人合并。这个MBA学生目前没有收入，如果把自己身上的权益，与日薪工人身上的权益‘一股换一股’地合并，短期收入就会增加，而且增幅很大！可对这个学生来说，还有什么交易比这更傻呢？

1994.english: In corporate transactions, it's equally silly for the would- be purchaser to focus on current earnings when the prospective acquiree has either different prospects, different amounts of non-operating assets, or a different capital structure.  At Berkshire, we have rejected many merger and purchase opportunities that would have boosted current and near-term earnings but that would have reduced per-share intrinsic value. Our approach, rather, has been to follow Wayne Gretzky's advice: "Go to where the puck is going to be, not to where it is."  As a result, our shareholders are now many billions of dollars richer than they would have been if we had used the standard catechism.
1994.chinese: 企业交易也是如此。如果拟收购对象有不同的前景、不同数量的非经营性资产，或不同的资本结构，买方还只盯着当前利润，同样愚蠢。在伯克希尔，我们拒绝过许多能提高当前及近期利润、却会降低每股内在价值的合并与收购机会。我们采用的，是韦恩·格雷茨基的忠告：“去冰球将要到的地方，而不是它现在所在的地方。”因此，与遵循那套标准教条相比，如今我们的股东多拥有了数十亿美元。

1994.english: The sad fact is that most major acquisitions display an egregious imbalance:  They are a bonanza for the shareholders of the acquiree; they increase the income and status of the acquirer's management; and they are a honey pot for the investment bankers and other professionals on both sides.  But, alas, they usually reduce the wealth of the acquirer's shareholders, often to a substantial extent.  That happens because the acquirer typically gives up more intrinsic value than it receives.  Do that enough, says John Medlin, the retired head of Wachovia Corp., and "you are running a chain letter in reverse."
1994.chinese: 令人难过的事实是，大多数大型收购都表现出极不平衡的结果：被收购方股东发了财，收购方管理层增加了收入和地位，双方投行及其他专业人士也找到了蜜罐。唉，收购方股东的财富却通常减少，而且往往减少很多。这是因为，买方交出去的内在价值，通常超过收到的内在价值。美联银行公司退休负责人约翰·梅德林说，这种事做多了，“你就是在倒着玩连锁信游戏”。

1994.english: Over time, the skill with which a company's managers allocate capital has an enormous impact on the enterprise's value.  Almost by definition, a really good business generates far more money (at least after its early years) than it can use internally.  The company could, of course, distribute the money to shareholders by way of dividends or share repurchases.  But often the CEO asks a strategic planning staff, consultants or investment bankers whether an acquisition or two might make sense.  That's like asking your interior decorator whether you need a $50,000 rug.
1994.chinese: 从长期看，管理层配置资本的本领，会极大影响企业价值。几乎按定义来说，一家真正优秀的企业，至少在初创期之后，产生的钱会远远超过内部能够使用的钱。当然，公司可以通过股息或股票回购，把钱还给股东。但首席执行官往往会去问战略规划人员、顾问或投资银行家：收购一两家公司是不是有道理？这就像问你的室内装潢师，自己是不是需要一张5万美元的地毯。

1994.english: The acquisition problem is often compounded by a biological bias:  Many CEO's attain their positions in part because they possess an abundance of animal spirits and ego.  If an executive is heavily endowed with these qualities - which, it should be acknowledged, sometimes have their advantages - they won't disappear when he reaches the top.  When such a CEO is encouraged by his advisors to make deals, he responds much as would a teenage boy who is encouraged by his father to have a normal sex life.  It's not a push he needs.
1994.chinese: 收购问题还常常被一种生物本能放大：许多首席执行官能够坐上这个位置，部分原因正是他们精力充沛、自我意识强烈。如果某位高管拥有大量这些特质——得承认，有时候它们确有好处——当他升到顶层时，这些特质也不会消失。这样的首席执行官，若再受到顾问鼓励去做交易，反应就会像一个父亲鼓励他过正常性生活的青春期男孩。他哪里还需要别人推这一把。

1994.english: Some years back, a CEO friend of mine - in jest, it must be said - unintentionally described the pathology of many big deals. This friend, who ran a property-casualty insurer, was explaining to his directors why he wanted to acquire a certain life insurance company.  After droning rather unpersuasively through the economics and strategic rationale for the acquisition, he abruptly abandoned the script.  With an impish look, he simply said:  "Aw, fellas, all the other kids have one."
1994.chinese: 几年前，一位首席执行官朋友，无意间说出了许多大交易的病根；先说明，他当时是在开玩笑。他经营一家财产及意外责任保险公司，正在向董事们解释，为什么想收购某家人寿保险公司。他絮絮叨叨地讲完经济理由和战略理由，实在没什么说服力，忽然把讲稿扔到一边，露出调皮的神情，只说了一句：“哎呀，伙计们，别的孩子都有一个嘛。”

1994.english: At Berkshire, our managers will continue to earn extraordinary returns from what appear to be ordinary businesses. As a first step, these managers will look for ways to deploy their earnings advantageously in their businesses.  What's left, they will send to Charlie and me.  We then will try to use those funds in ways that build per-share intrinsic value.  Our goal will be to acquire either part or all of businesses that we believe we understand, that have good, sustainable underlying economics, and that are run by managers whom we like, admire and trust.
1994.chinese: 在伯克希尔，我们的经理人将继续从看似普通的企业中，赚取非同寻常的回报。第一步，他们会在自家企业里，寻找有利可图的利润再投资途径。剩下的钱，会交给查理和我。然后，我们会设法把这些资金用于提高每股内在价值。我们的目标，是买下自己认为能够理解、基础经济特性良好而且能够持续、由我们喜爱、敬佩和信任的管理者经营的企业，部分权益或整家企业都可以。

1994.english:
Compensation

At Berkshire, we try to be as logical about compensation as about capital allocation.  For example, we compensate Ralph Schey based upon the results of Scott Fetzer rather than those of Berkshire.  What could make more sense, since he's responsible for one operation but not the other?  A cash bonus or a stock option tied to the fortunes of Berkshire would provide totally capricious rewards to Ralph.  He could, for example, be hitting home runs at Scott Fetzer while Charlie and I rang up mistakes at Berkshire, thereby negating his efforts many times over. Conversely, why should option profits or bonuses be heaped upon Ralph if good things are occurring in other parts of Berkshire but Scott Fetzer is lagging?
1994.chinese:
## 薪酬

在伯克希尔，我们希望对待薪酬，也像对待资本配置一样合乎逻辑。例如，我们按斯科特与费策的业绩，而非伯克希尔的业绩，来支付拉尔夫·谢伊薪酬。他负责的是前者，不是后者，还有什么比这更合理？若现金奖金或股票期权与伯克希尔整体命运挂钩，拉尔夫得到的回报就会完全反复无常。例如，他可能在斯科特与费策打出一个又一个本垒打，查理和我却在伯克希尔接连犯错，损失远远抵消他的努力。反过来，如果伯克希尔其他部分表现出色，斯科特与费策却落后，凭什么还要把期权收益或奖金大把送给拉尔夫呢？

1994.english:
In setting compensation, we like to hold out the promise of large carrots, but make sure their delivery is tied directly to results in the area that a manager controls.  When capital invested in an operation is significant, we also both charge managers a high rate for incremental capital they employ and credit them at an equally high rate for capital they release.

The product of this money's-not-free approach is definitely visible at Scott Fetzer.  If Ralph can employ incremental funds at good returns, it pays him to do so:  His bonus increases when earnings on additional capital exceed a meaningful hurdle charge. But our bonus calculation is symmetrical:  If incremental investment yields sub-standard returns, the shortfall is costly to Ralph as well as to Berkshire.  The consequence of this two- way arrangement is that it pays Ralph - and pays him well - to send to Omaha any cash he can't advantageously use in his business.
1994.chinese:
设定薪酬时，我们愿意许诺大大的胡萝卜，但一定确保，能不能拿到，直接取决于经理人所能掌控领域的成果。如果某项业务投入资本较多，我们还会对经理人新增使用的资本按较高费率计费；若他释放资本，也按同样高的费率记功。

这种‘钱不是白拿的’办法，在斯科特与费策的效果清清楚楚。如果拉尔夫能够让新增资金取得良好回报，这样做就对他有利：新增资本的利润超过按一定门槛回报率计提的资本费用，他的奖金就增加。不过，我们的奖金算法是对称的：如果新增投资回报不达标，差额不仅让伯克希尔付出代价，拉尔夫也得承担。这个双向安排的结果是，把不能在自家企业有效运用的现金交给奥马哈，对拉尔夫有利，而且很有利。

1994.english:
It has become fashionable at public companies to describe almost every compensation plan as aligning the interests of management with those of shareholders.  In our book, alignment means being a partner in both directions, not just on the upside. Many "alignment" plans flunk this basic test, being artful forms of "heads I win, tails you lose."

A common form of misalignment occurs in the typical stock option arrangement, which does not periodically increase the option price to compensate for the fact that retained earnings are building up the wealth of the company.  Indeed, the combination of a ten-year option, a low dividend payout, and compound interest can provide lush gains to a manager who has done no more than tread water in his job.  A cynic might even note that when payments to owners are held down, the profit to the option-holding manager increases.  I have yet to see this vital point spelled out in a proxy statement asking shareholders to approve an option plan.
1994.chinese:
上市公司如今流行把几乎所有薪酬计划，都说成是让管理层与股东利益一致。在我们看来，利益一致，意味着不论上涨还是下跌都做伙伴，而不只是分享上涨。许多“利益一致”计划过不了这个基本测试，不过是把‘正面我赢，反面你输’包装得更巧妙。

一种常见的利益不一致，出现在典型股票期权安排中：留存利润不断增加公司财富，期权行权价却不作定期上调来反映这一点。事实上，十年期期权、低股息派发率和复利结合起来，足以让一个工作表现只是原地踏步的经理人，获得丰厚收益。刻薄一点的人甚至会指出：给所有者支付的钱越少，持有期权的经理人获利反而越多。我还没有在哪份请股东批准期权计划的委托投票说明书里，看到把这个关键问题讲清楚。

1994.english: I can't resist mentioning that our compensation arrangement with Ralph Schey was worked out in about five minutes, immediately upon our purchase of Scott Fetzer and without the "help" of lawyers or compensation consultants.  This arrangement embodies a few very simple ideas - not the kind of terms favored by consultants who cannot easily send a large bill unless they have established that you have a large problem (and one, of course, that requires an annual review).  Our agreement with Ralph has never been changed.  It made sense to him and to me in 1986, and it makes sense now.  Our compensation arrangements with the managers of all our other units are similarly simple, though the terms of each agreement vary to fit the economic characteristics of the business at issue, the existence in some cases of partial ownership of the unit by managers, etc.
1994.chinese: 我忍不住要提一下：收购斯科特与费策后，我们立刻花了大约五分钟，就与拉尔夫·谢伊谈妥薪酬安排，没有律师或薪酬顾问的‘帮助’。这项安排体现的，只是几个非常简单的想法，不是顾问偏爱的那类条款；毕竟，他们得先证明你有个大问题，才好开出大账单，而且这个问题当然还需要每年复查。我们与拉尔夫的协议从未改过。1986年，他和我都觉得合理，今天也一样。与其他所有单位经理人的薪酬安排，也同样简单，不过，各项协议的条款会因企业经济特性不同，以及某些单位由经理人持有部分权益等情况，分别调整。

1994.english:
In all instances, we pursue rationality.  Arrangements that pay off in capricious ways, unrelated to a manager's personal accomplishments, may well be welcomed by certain managers.  Who, after all, refuses a free lottery ticket?  But such arrangements are wasteful to the company and cause the manager to lose focus on what should be his real areas of concern.  Additionally, irrational behavior at the parent may well encourage imitative behavior at subsidiaries.

At Berkshire, only Charlie and I have the managerial responsibility for the entire business.  Therefore, we are the only parties who should logically be compensated on the basis of what the enterprise does as a whole.  Even so, that is not a compensation arrangement we desire.  We have carefully designed both the company and our jobs so that we do things we enjoy with people we like.  Equally important, we are forced to do very few boring or unpleasant tasks.  We are the beneficiaries as well of the abundant array of material and psychic perks that flow to the heads of corporations.  Under such idyllic conditions, we don't expect shareholders to ante up loads of compensation for which we have no possible need.
1994.chinese:
无论哪种情况，我们追求的都是合理。某些经理人，可能很欢迎那些结果反复无常、与个人成绩无关的安排。毕竟，谁会拒绝一张免费的彩票？但这种安排浪费公司资源，也使经理人忽略自己真正应当关注的领域。此外，母公司的不理性行为，很可能引来子公司的效仿。

在伯克希尔，只有查理和我对整个企业负有管理责任。因此，从逻辑上说，只有我们才应当按企业整体表现获得薪酬。即便如此，我们也不想要这样的安排。我们精心设计了公司和自己的工作，让自己能与喜欢的人一起，做喜欢的事。同样重要的是，我们几乎不必勉强去做无聊或不愉快的工作。公司负责人能享有的种种物质与精神上的优待，我们也一应享有。在这样田园诗般的条件下，我们并不指望股东再掏出大笔薪酬，而这些钱我们根本不可能用得上。

1994.english:
Indeed, if we were not paid at all, Charlie and I would be delighted with the cushy jobs we hold.  At bottom, we subscribe to Ronald Reagan's creed:  "It's probably true that hard work never killed anyone, but I figure why take the chance."

## Sources of Reported Earnings

The table on the next page shows the main sources of Berkshire's reported earnings.  In this presentation, purchase- premium charges of the type we discussed in our earlier analysis of Scott Fetzer are not assigned to the specific businesses to which they apply, but are instead aggregated and shown separately.  This procedure lets you view the earnings of our businesses as they would have been reported had we not purchased them.  This form of presentation seems to us to be more useful to investors and managers than one utilizing GAAP, which requires purchase premiums to be charged off, business-by-business.  The total earnings we show in the table are, of course, identical to the GAAP total in our audited financial statements.
1994.chinese:
事实上，即使分文不付，查理和我也会乐呵呵地干着现在这两份轻松美差。说到底，我们信奉罗纳德·里根的信条：“努力工作大概确实从没累死过人，不过我想，何必冒这个险呢？”
