1994.english:
## "Look-Through" Earnings

In past reports, we've discussed look-through earnings, which we believe more accurately portray the earnings of Berkshire than does our GAAP result.  As we calculate them, look-through earnings consist of: (1) the operating earnings reported in the previous section, plus; (2) the retained operating earnings of major investees that, under GAAP accounting, are not reflected in our profits, less; (3) an allowance for the tax that would be paid by Berkshire if these retained earnings of investees had instead been distributed to us.  The "operating earnings" of which we speak here exclude capital gains, special accounting items and major restructuring charges.
1994.chinese:
## “穿透”盈余

以前的报告里，我们谈过穿透盈余。我们认为，它比GAAP结果更能准确反映伯克希尔的盈利情况。按我们的算法，穿透盈余包括：（1）上一节列报的营业利润，加上（2）主要被投资企业留存的营业利润——按GAAP，这部分不计入我们的利润，再减去（3）假如被投资企业把这些留存利润分配给我们，伯克希尔所应缴税款的估计额。这里所说的‘营业利润’，不包括资本利得、特殊会计项目和重大重组费用。

1994.english:
If our intrinsic value is to grow at our target rate of 15%, our look-through earnings, over time, must also increase at about that pace.  When I first explained this concept a few years back, I told you that meeting this 15% goal would require us to generate look-through earnings of about $1.8 billion by 2000.  Because we've since issued about 3% more shares, that figure has grown to $1.85 billion.

We are now modestly ahead of schedule in meeting our goal, but to a significant degree that is because our super-cat insurance business has recently delivered earnings far above trend-line expectancy (an outcome I will discuss in the next section).  Giving due weight to that abnormality, we still expect to hit our target but that, of course, is no sure thing.
1994.chinese:
如果内在价值要达到每年15%的增长目标，长期看，穿透盈余也必须以大致相同的速度增长。几年前，初次解释这个概念时，我告诉各位，要实现15%的目标，到2000年，穿透盈余须达到约18亿美元。此后，我们增发了约3%的股份，所以这个数字已经提高到18.5亿美元。

目前，进度略微领先于目标，不过，在相当大程度上，这是因为超级巨灾保险业务近来的利润，远高于按长期趋势预期的水平；下一节我会讨论这个结果。充分考虑到这种异常之后，我们仍然预期能够达到目标，但当然并无把握。

## Insurance Operations

As we've explained in past reports, what counts in our insurance business is, first, the amount of "float" we develop and, second, its cost to us.  Float is money we hold but don't own.  In an insurance operation, float arises because most policies require that premiums be prepaid and, more importantly, because it usually takes time for an insurer to hear about and resolve loss claims.
1994.chinese:
（1）不包括归属于韦斯科少数股东权益的股份。

（4）采用的税率为14%，即伯克希尔收到股息时缴纳的税率。

## 保险业务

正如以前报告里解释过的，我们保险业务的关键，第一是产生多少‘浮存金’，第二是它的成本。浮存金，是我们持有、却不归我们所有的钱。保险业务之所以产生浮存金，一方面是大多数保单要求预付保费；更重要的是，保险公司通常需要时间，才能得知发生了赔案，并把它处理完。

1994.english:
Typically, the premiums that an insurer takes in do not cover the losses and expenses it must pay.  That leaves it running an "underwriting loss" - and that loss is the cost of float.

An insurance business is profitable over time if its cost of float is less than the cost the company would otherwise incur to obtain funds.  But the business has a negative value if the cost of its float is higher than market rates for money.
1994.chinese:
通常，保险公司收到的保费，不足以覆盖必须支付的赔款与费用。因此，它会出现‘承保亏损’，这项亏损就是浮存金成本。

从长期看，如果浮存金成本，低于公司通过其他方式取得资金所需付出的成本，保险业务就是盈利的；但如果浮存金成本高于市场资金利率，这门生意的价值就是负的。

1994.english: As the numbers in the following table show, Berkshire's insurance business has been an enormous winner.  For the table, we have compiled our float -  which we generate in exceptional amounts relative to our premium volume - by adding loss reserves, loss adjustment reserves, funds held under reinsurance assumed and unearned premium reserves and then subtracting agents' balances, prepaid acquisition costs, prepaid taxes and deferred charges applicable to assumed reinsurance.  Our cost of float is determined by our underwriting loss or profit.  In those years when we have had an underwriting profit, such as the last two, our cost of float has been negative, and we have determined our insurance earnings by adding underwriting profit to float income.
1994.chinese: 下表数字表明，伯克希尔的保险业务是个大赢家。我们产生的浮存金，相对于保费规模格外多。表中浮存金的计算方法是：把赔款准备金、理赔费用准备金、分入再保险项下留存资金，以及未到期保费准备金相加，再减去代理人应收余额、预付保单取得成本、预付税款，以及分入再保险相关递延费用。浮存金成本由承保亏损或利润决定。像过去两年这样，取得承保利润时，浮存金成本就是负数；我们把承保利润与浮存金投资收益相加，来确定保险收益。

1994.english:
Charlie and I are delighted that our float grew in 1994 and are even more pleased that it proved to be cost-free.  But our message this year echoes the one we delivered in 1993:  Though we have a fine insurance business, it is not as good as it currently looks.

The reason we must repeat this caution is that our "super-cat" business (which sells policies that insurance and reinsurance companies buy to protect themselves from the effects of mega- catastrophes) was again highly profitable.  Since truly major catastrophes occur infrequently, our super-cat business can be expected to show large profits in most years but occasionally to record a huge loss.  In other words, the attractiveness of our super-cat business will take many years to measure.  Certainly 1994 should be regarded as close to a best-case.  Our only significant losses arose from the California earthquake in January.  I will add that we do not expect to suffer a major loss from the early-1995 Kobe earthquake.
1994.chinese:
1994年浮存金增长，让查理和我很高兴；而且它无须付出成本，更让我们欣喜。不过，今年要说的话，与1993年一样：我们的保险业务虽好，却没有眼下看起来那么好。

我们必须重申这一提醒，是因为‘超级巨灾’业务再次获得高额利润。这项业务出售的保单，由保险及再保险公司购买，用来抵御特大灾害的影响。真正重大的灾害并不常见，因此，我们的超级巨灾业务，预期大多数年份利润很高，偶尔却会出现巨额亏损。换句话说，这门生意究竟多有吸引力，得用许多年才能衡量。1994年当然应视为接近最理想情形的一年。我们唯一的重大损失，来自1月的加利福尼亚地震。再补充一句，我们预期不会因1995年初的神户地震遭受重大损失。

1994.english:
Super-cat policies are small in number, large in size and non- standardized.  Therefore, the underwriting of this business requires far more judgment than, say, the underwriting of auto policies, for which a mass of data is available.  Here Berkshire has a major advantage:  Ajit Jain, our super-cat manager, whose underwriting skills are the finest.  His value to us is simply enormous.

In addition, Berkshire has a special advantage in the super- cat business because of our towering financial strength, which helps us in two ways.  First, a prudent insurer will want its protection against true mega-catastrophes - such as a $50 billion windstorm loss on Long Island or an earthquake of similar cost in California - to be absolutely certain.  But that same insurer knows that the disaster making it dependent on a large super-cat recovery is also the disaster that could cause many reinsurers to default. There's not much sense in paying premiums for coverage that will evaporate precisely when it is needed.  So the certainty that Berkshire will be both solvent and liquid after a catastrophe of unthinkable proportions is a major competitive advantage for us.
1994.chinese:
超级巨灾保单数量少、金额大，而且不标准化。因此，这项业务的承保，比方说汽车险承保，需要多得多的判断；汽车险有大量数据可用。伯克希尔在这里有个重大优势：主管超级巨灾业务的阿吉特·贾因，他的承保本领无人能及。他对我们的价值，实在巨大。

此外，我们极为雄厚的财力，还给超级巨灾业务带来一项特殊优势，并从两方面起作用。第一，谨慎的保险公司，希望自己面对真正特大灾害时的保障绝对可靠，例如长岛一场造成500亿美元损失的风灾，或加利福尼亚一场造成同等损失的地震。但这家保险公司也明白：使它必须依赖巨额超级巨灾赔款的那场灾难，同样可能让许多再保险公司无力履约。付钱买的保障，偏偏在最需要时消失，有什么意义？所以，即使遭遇规模难以想象的灾害，伯克希尔依然肯定具备偿付能力和充足流动性，这就是我们的重大竞争优势。

1994.english:
The second benefit of our capital strength is that we can write policies for amounts that no one else can even consider.  For example, during 1994, a primary insurer wished to buy a short-term policy for $400 million of California earthquake coverage and we wrote the policy immediately.  We know of no one else in the world who would take a $400 million risk, or anything close to it, for their own account.

Generally, brokers attempt to place coverage for large amounts by spreading the burden over a number of small policies.  But, at best, coverage of that sort takes considerable time to arrange.  In the meantime, the company desiring reinsurance is left holding a risk it doesn't want and that may seriously threaten its well- being.  At Berkshire, on the other hand, we will quote prices for coverage as great as $500 million on the same day that we are asked to bid.  No one else in the industry will do the same.
1994.chinese:
资本实力的第二项好处，是我们能承保别人连想都不敢想的金额。例如，1994年，一家原保险公司想买一张短期保单，提供4亿美元加利福尼亚地震保障，我们立即承保。据我们所知，全世界没有其他人，会自行承担4亿美元，甚至接近这一金额的风险。

通常，经纪人会把巨额保障拆成许多小保单，分散安排。不过，即使最顺利，安排这种保障也相当费时间。在这期间，需要再保险的公司，还得自己担着不愿承担、甚至可能严重威胁自身安危的风险。相比之下，在伯克希尔，我们收到询价的当天，就能为高达5亿美元的保障报出价格。业内没有别人能这样做。

1994.english:
By writing coverages in large lumps, we obviously expose Berkshire to lumpy financial results.  That's totally acceptable to us:  Too often, insurers (as well as other businesses) follow sub- optimum strategies in order to "smooth" their reported earnings. By accepting the prospect of volatility, we expect to earn higher long-term returns than we would by pursuing predictability.

Given the risks we accept, Ajit and I constantly focus on our "worst case," knowing, of course, that it is difficult to judge what this is, since you could conceivably have a Long Island hurricane, a California earthquake, and Super Cat X all in the same year.  Additionally, insurance losses could be accompanied by non- insurance troubles.  For example, were we to have super-cat losses from a large Southern California earthquake, they might well be accompanied by a major drop in the value of our holdings in See's, Wells Fargo and Freddie Mac.
1994.chinese:
一笔笔承保这么大的金额，显然会使伯克希尔的财务结果大起大落。我们完全可以接受这一点。太多保险公司，以及其他企业，为了‘平滑’报表利润，采取了并非最优的策略。我们接受业绩可能波动，预期由此取得的长期回报，会高于一味追求可预测性的做法。

考虑到承接的风险，阿吉特和我一直盯着‘最坏情形’。当然，我们知道，很难判断究竟什么才算最坏，因为长岛飓风、加利福尼亚地震和某场未知的超级巨灾X，完全可能在同一年发生。此外，保险损失还可能伴随保险业务之外的麻烦。例如，南加利福尼亚大地震若给我们带来超级巨灾赔款，也很可能同时使我们持有的喜诗糖果、富国银行和房地美权益大幅贬值。

1994.english:
All things considered, we believe our worst-case insurance loss from a super-cat is now about $600 million after-tax, an amount that would slightly exceed Berkshire's annual earnings from other sources.  If you are not comfortable with this level of exposure, the time to sell your Berkshire stock is now, not after the inevitable mega-catastrophe.

Our super-cat volume will probably be down in 1995.  Prices for garden-variety policies have fallen somewhat, and the torrent of capital that was committed to the reinsurance business a few years ago will be inclined to chase premiums, irrespective of their adequacy.  Nevertheless, we have strong relations with an important group of clients who will provide us with a substantial amount of business in 1995.
1994.chinese:
综合各项因素，我们认为，目前一场超级巨灾可能造成的最坏保险损失，约为税后6亿美元，略高于伯克希尔一年从其他来源赚取的利润。如果你对这种风险敞口不放心，那么该卖伯克希尔股票的时候是现在，而不是等到那场不可避免的特大灾害发生之后。

1995年，我们的超级巨灾业务量大概会减少。一般保单价格已有所下降；几年前涌进再保险行业的大批资本，往往会不顾保费是否足够，一味追逐保费收入。不过，我们与一批重要客户关系牢固，1995年，它们仍会给我们带来相当数量的业务。

1994.english:
Berkshire's other insurance operations had excellent results in 1994.  Our homestate operation, led by Rod Eldred; our workers' compensation business, headed by Brad Kinstler; our credit card operation, managed by the Kizer family; National Indemnity's traditional auto and general liability business, led by Don Wurster - all of these generated significant underwriting profits accompanied by substantial float.

We can conclude this section as we did last year:  All in all, we have a first-class insurance business.  Though its results will be highly volatile, this operation possesses an intrinsic value that exceeds its book value by a large amount - larger, in fact, than is the case at any other Berkshire business.
1994.chinese:
伯克希尔其他保险业务，在1994年也取得了出色成绩。罗德·埃尔德雷德领导的本州保险业务、布拉德·金斯特勒负责的工伤赔偿保险业务、基泽家族管理的信用卡保险业务，以及唐·沃斯特领导的国民赔偿公司传统汽车险及一般责任险业务，都创造了可观的承保利润和大量浮存金。

这一节，可以用与去年同样的话收尾：总的来说，我们拥有一流的保险业务。尽管业绩会大幅波动，但这项业务的内在价值，远远超过账面价值；事实上，这个差额比伯克希尔任何其他业务都大。

1994.english:
## Common Stock Investments

Below we list our common stockholdings having a value of over $300 million.  A small portion of these investments belongs to subsidiaries of which Berkshire owns less than 100%.

```text
                                                         12/31/94
  Shares     Company                                 Cost         Market
  ------     -------                              ----------    ----------
                                                       (000s omitted)
 27,759,941  American Express Company. .......... $  723,919    $  818,918
 20,000,000  Capital Cities/ABC, Inc. ...........    345,000     1,705,000
100,000,000  The Coca-Cola Company. .............  1,298,888     5,150,000
 12,761,200  Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp.
                ("Freddie Mac") .................    270,468       644,441
  6,854,500  Gannett Co., Inc. ..................    335,216       365,002
 34,250,000  GEICO Corp. ........................     45,713     1,678,250
 24,000,000  The Gillette Company ...............    600,000     1,797,000
 19,453,300  PNC Bank Corporation ...............    503,046       410,951
  1,727,765  The Washington Post Company ........      9,731       418,983
  6,791,218  Wells Fargo & Company ..............    423,680       984,727
```

Our investments continue to be few in number and simple in concept:  The truly big investment idea can usually be explained in a short paragraph.  We like a business with enduring competitive advantages that is run by able and owner-oriented people.  When these attributes exist, and when we can make purchases at sensible prices, it is hard to go wrong (a challenge we periodically manage to overcome).

Investors should remember that their scorecard is not computed using Olympic-diving methods:  Degree-of-difficulty doesn't count. If you are right about a business whose value is largely dependent on a single key factor that is both easy to understand and enduring, the payoff is the same as if you had correctly analyzed an investment alternative characterized by many constantly shifting and complex variables.
1994.chinese:
我们的投资，仍然数量不多、思路简单：真正重大的投资想法，通常一小段话就能解释清楚。我们喜欢具有持久竞争优势、由能干且站在所有者立场上思考的人经营的企业。具备这些条件，又能以合理价格买入，想出错都难——不过，这个难关，我们时不时还是能攻克。

投资者应当记住，投资成绩并不按奥运会跳水的办法评分：难度系数不加分。如果一家企业的价值，主要取决于一个容易理解、又能持久的关键因素，你判断对了，所得回报，与正确分析另一项由许多复杂、不断变化的变量决定的投资机会，并无区别。

1994.english:
We try to price, rather than time, purchases.  In our view, it is folly to forego buying shares in an outstanding business whose long-term future is predictable, because of short-term worries about an economy or a stock market that we know to be unpredictable.  Why scrap an informed decision because of an uninformed guess?

We purchased National Indemnity in 1967, See's in 1972, Buffalo News in 1977, Nebraska Furniture Mart in 1983, and Scott Fetzer in 1986 because those are the years they became available and because we thought the prices they carried were acceptable.  In each case, we pondered what the business was likely to do, not what the Dow, the Fed, or the economy might do.  If we see this approach as making sense in the purchase of businesses in their entirety, why should we change tack when we are purchasing small pieces of wonderful businesses in the stock market?
1994.chinese:
我们买入时，力求选对价格，而非选对时机。在我们看来，明知经济和股市的短期走向无法预测，却因为担忧这些短期走向，而放弃购买长期前景可预测的优秀企业股票，是愚蠢的。为什么要让一个没把握的猜测，推翻一个有根据的决定？

我们在1967年买入国民赔偿公司、1972年买入喜诗糖果、1977年买入《布法罗新闻报》、1983年买入内布拉斯加家具卖场、1986年买入斯科特与费策，是因为它们在那些年份有机会买到，而且价格在我们看来可以接受。每次，我们考虑的都是企业可能怎样发展，而非道琼斯指数、美联储或经济会怎样。买下整家企业时，我们认为这种做法合理，那么，在股市买入优秀企业的一小部分时，为什么要改弦更张呢？

1994.english: Before looking at new investments, we consider adding to old ones.  If a business is attractive enough to buy once, it may well pay to repeat the process.  We would love to increase our economic interest in See's or Scott Fetzer, but we haven't found a way to add to a 100% holding.  In the stock market, however, an investor frequently gets the chance to increase his economic interest in businesses he knows and likes.  Last year we went that direction by enlarging our holdings in Coca-Cola and American Express.
1994.chinese: 考虑新投资之前，我们先考虑给旧投资加码。如果一家企业值得买一次，再买一些也可能很划算。我们很想增加在喜诗糖果或斯科特与费策的经济权益，可至今还没找到把100%持股再往上加的办法。不过，在股市上，投资者常常有机会增加在自己熟悉、喜欢的企业中的经济权益。去年，我们就这样增持了可口可乐和美国运通。

1994.english: Our history with American Express goes way back and, in fact, fits the pattern of my pulling current investment decisions out of past associations.  In 1951, for example, GEICO shares comprised 70% of my personal portfolio and GEICO was also the first stock I sold - I was then 20 - as a security salesman (the sale was 100 shares to my Aunt Alice who, bless her, would have bought anything I suggested).  Twenty-five years later, Berkshire purchased a major stake in GEICO at the time it was threatened with insolvency.  In another instance, that of the Washington Post, about half of my initial investment funds came from delivering the paper in the 1940's.  Three decades later Berkshire purchased a large position in the company two years after it went public.  As for Coca-Cola, my first business venture - this was in the 1930's - was buying a six-pack of Coke for 25 cents and selling each bottle for 5 cents. It took only fifty years before I finally got it:  The real money was in the syrup.
1994.chinese: 我们与美国运通的渊源很久，实际上，也符合我的一种老习惯：从过去的交往中，找出今天的投资决定。例如，1951年，GEICO占我个人投资组合的70%；当时我20岁，做证券推销员，卖出的第一只股票也是GEICO，100股，买家是艾丽斯姨妈。她人真好，不管我推荐什么，她都会买。二十五年后，GEICO濒临资不抵债，伯克希尔买入了大量股份。再比如《华盛顿邮报》，我最初的投资资金，约有一半来自20世纪40年代送这份报纸的收入。三十年后，在公司上市两年时，伯克希尔大量买入了它的股票。至于可口可乐，20世纪30年代，我的第一门生意，就是花25美分买一组六瓶可乐，再以每瓶5美分卖出去。只用了五十年，我终于悟出来了：真正的大钱，在糖浆里。

1994.english: My American Express history includes a couple of episodes:  In the mid-1960's, just after the stock was battered by the company's infamous salad-oil scandal, we put about 40% of Buffett Partnership Ltd.'s capital into the stock - the largest investment the partnership had ever made.  I should add that this commitment gave us over 5% ownership in Amex at a cost of $13 million.  As I write this, we own just under 10%, which has cost us $1.36 billion. (Amex earned $12.5 million in 1964 and $1.4 billion in 1994.)
1994.chinese: 我与美国运通的历史，包括几段往事。20世纪60年代中期，公司那桩臭名昭著的色拉油丑闻把股价砸得很惨，随后，我们把巴菲特合伙企业有限公司约40%的资本投入这只股票，是合伙企业有史以来最大的一笔投资。我还得补一句，那次花了1,300万美元，就买到美国运通超过5%的股份。写这封信时，我们持有略低于10%，成本为13.6亿美元。（美国运通1964年赚取1,250万美元，1994年则赚取14亿美元。）

1994.english: My history with Amex's IDS unit, which today contributes about a third of the earnings of the company, goes back even further.  I first purchased stock in IDS in 1953 when it was growing rapidly and selling at a price-earnings ratio of only 3.  (There was a lot of low-hanging fruit in those days.)  I even produced a long report - do I ever write a short one? - on the company that I sold for $1 through an ad in the Wall Street Journal.
1994.chinese: 我与美国运通旗下IDS的渊源更早。如今，这个单位贡献了公司约三分之一的利润。1953年，我首次买入IDS股票，当时它增长迅速，市盈率却只有3倍。（那年月，伸手就能摘到的果子还真不少。）我甚至为它写了一篇长报告——我什么时候写过短的？——在《华尔街日报》登广告，每份卖1美元。

1994.english:
Obviously American Express and IDS (recently renamed American Express Financial Advisors) are far different operations today from what they were then.  Nevertheless, I find that a long-term familiarity with a company and its products is often helpful in evaluating it.

## Mistake Du Jour

Mistakes occur at the time of decision.  We can only make our mistake-du-jour award, however, when the foolishness of the decision become obvious.  By this measure, 1994 was a vintage year with keen competition for the gold medal.  Here, I would like to tell you that the mistakes I will describe originated with Charlie. But whenever I try to explain things that way, my nose begins to grow.
1994.chinese:
显然，今天的美国运通和IDS——最近改名为美国运通财务顾问公司——与当年已经大不相同。不过，我发现，长期熟悉一家公司及其产品，往往有助于评价它。

## 今日特供：错误

错误在作决定时就已经犯下。不过，‘今日错误奖’，得等到那个决定的愚蠢显露无遗，才能颁发。按这个标准，1994年真是个丰收年，金牌争夺异常激烈。说到这里，我很想告诉大家，下面这些错误，源头都在查理。不过，每次试着这样解释，我的鼻子就开始变长。

1994.english:
And the nominees are . . .

Late in 1993 I sold 10 million shares of Cap Cities at $63; at year-end 1994, the price was $85.25.  (The difference is $222.5 million for those of you who wish to avoid the pain of calculating the damage yourself.)  When we purchased the stock at $17.25 in 1986, I told you that I had previously sold our Cap Cities holdings at $4.30 per share during 1978-80, and added that I was at a loss to explain my earlier behavior.  Now I've become a repeat offender. Maybe it's time to get a guardian appointed.
1994.chinese:
入围者有……

1993年末，我以每股63美元卖掉1,000万股大都会公司股票；到1994年末，价格是85.25美元。（差额为2.225亿美元，替那些不想亲自计算损失、再痛一回的股东算好了。）1986年，我们以17.25美元买入时，我曾告诉各位：1978—1980年，我已经以每股4.30美元卖过我们持有的大都会股票，并且实在无法解释自己当年的举动。如今，我又成了惯犯。也许该给我指定个监护人了。

1994.english: Egregious as it is, the Cap Cities decision earns only a silver medal.  Top honors go to a mistake I made five years ago that fully ripened in 1994:  Our $358 million purchase of USAir preferred stock, on which the dividend was suspended in September. In the 1990 Annual Report I correctly described this deal as an "unforced error," meaning that I was neither pushed into the investment nor misled by anyone when making it.  Rather, this was a case of sloppy analysis, a lapse that may have been caused by the fact that we were buying a senior security or by hubris.  Whatever the reason, the mistake was large.
1994.chinese: 大都会的决定虽然糟糕，也只能拿银牌。最高荣誉，属于我五年前犯下、在1994年彻底熟透的一个错误：花3.58亿美元买下全美航空（USAir）优先股，该股于9月停止派息。在1990年年报里，我正确地把这笔交易称为‘非受迫性失误’，意思是，投资时既没有人逼我，也没有人误导我。实际情况是，我的分析马虎；也许因为买的是清偿顺位较高的证券，也许因为狂妄自大，才犯了这个疏漏。不管什么原因，错误都很大。

1994.english:
Before this purchase, I simply failed to focus on the problems that would inevitably beset a carrier whose costs were both high and extremely difficult to lower.  In earlier years, these life- threatening costs posed few problems.  Airlines were then protected from competition by regulation, and carriers could absorb high costs because they could pass them along by way of fares that were also high.

When deregulation came along, it did not immediately change the picture:  The capacity of low-cost carriers was so small that the high-cost lines could, in large part, maintain their existing fare structures.  During this period, with the longer-term problems largely invisible but slowly metastasizing, the costs that were non-sustainable became further embedded.
1994.chinese:
买入前，我根本没有把注意力放在一个问题上：一家成本既高、又极难降低的航空公司，必然会遇到怎样的麻烦。早些年，这些危及生存的成本并未造成多少问题。当时，监管保护航空公司免受竞争；高成本能够承受，因为可以通过同样高的票价，把成本转嫁出去。

放松管制到来时，局面并没有立即改变：低成本航空公司的运力太小，高成本航空公司大体还能维持原有票价结构。在这一时期，长期问题大多尚未显现，却在慢慢扩散；不可持续的成本，反而扎得更深了。

1994.english: As the seat capacity of the low-cost operators expanded, their fares began to force the old-line, high-cost airlines to cut their own.  The day of reckoning for these airlines could be delayed by infusions of capital (such as ours into USAir), but eventually a fundamental rule of economics prevailed:  In an unregulated commodity business, a company must lower its costs to competitive levels or face extinction.  This principle should have been obvious to your Chairman, but I missed it.
1994.chinese: 随着低成本公司的座位运力扩大，它们的票价开始迫使老牌高成本航空公司降价。注入资本，例如我们投给USAir的资金，可以把算总账的日子往后拖；但最终，一条基本经济规律还是占了上风：在没有管制的同质化业务里，公司必须把成本降至有竞争力的水平，否则就会灭亡。你们的董事长本该看清这个原则，可我漏掉了。

1994.english: Seth Schofield, CEO of USAir, has worked diligently to correct the company's historical cost problems but, to date, has not managed to do so.  In part, this is because he has had to deal with a moving target, the result of certain major carriers having obtained labor concessions and other carriers having benefitted from "fresh-start" costs that came out of bankruptcy proceedings. (As Herb Kelleher, CEO of Southwest Airlines, has said: "Bankruptcy court for airlines has become a health spa.") Additionally, it should be no surprise to anyone that those airline employees who contractually receive above-market salaries will resist any reduction in these as long as their checks continue to clear.
1994.chinese: USAir首席执行官塞思·斯科菲尔德一直勤奋努力，试图纠正公司历史遗留的成本问题，但迄今未能做到。部分原因是，他面对的是一个不断移动的靶子：一些大型航空公司获得了劳方让步，另一些则受益于破产程序带来的“重新起步”的成本结构。（正如西南航空首席执行官赫布·凯莱赫所说：“破产法庭已经成了航空公司的养生馆。”）此外，按合同拿着高于市场水平薪水的航空公司员工，只要工资支票还能兑现，就会抗拒任何减薪，对此谁都不该意外。

1994.english:
Despite this difficult situation, USAir may yet achieve the cost reductions it needs to maintain its viability  long-term.  But it is far from sure that will happen.

Accordingly, we wrote our USAir investment down to $89.5 million, 25 cents on the dollar at yearend 1994.  This valuation reflects both a possibility that our preferred will have its value fully or largely restored and an opposite possibility that the stock will eventually become worthless.  Whatever the outcome, we will heed a prime rule of investing:  You don't have to make it back the way that you lost it.
1994.chinese:
尽管处境困难，USAir仍可能实现必要的成本削减，使自己能够长期生存。不过，能否做到，远没有把握。

因此，1994年末，我们把USAir投资减记至8,950万美元，也就是每投入1美元，账上只剩25美分。这个估值既反映了优先股可能全部或大部分恢复价值，也反映了它最终可能一文不值。无论结果如何，我们都会遵守投资的一条重要规则：不必用亏钱的那条路，把钱赚回来。

1994.english:
The accounting effects of our USAir writedown are complicated. Under GAAP accounting, insurance companies are required to carry all stocks on their balance sheets at estimated market value. Therefore, at the end of last year's third quarter, we were carrying our USAir preferred at $89.5 million, or 25% of cost.  In other words, our net worth was at that time reflecting a value for USAir that was far below our $358 million cost.

But in the fourth quarter, we concluded that the decline in value was, in accounting terms, "other than temporary," and that judgment required us to send the writedown of $269 million through our income statement.  The amount will have no other fourth-quarter effect.  That is, it will not reduce our net worth, because the diminution of value had already been reflected.
1994.chinese:
USAir减记的会计影响相当复杂。按GAAP，保险公司资产负债表上的全部股票，都必须按估计市值列账。因此，在去年第三季度末，我们已经把USAir优先股按8,950万美元，也就是成本的25%列账。换句话说，当时我们的净资产，已经反映出USAir价值远低于3.58亿美元成本。

但第四季度，我们判定价值下跌按会计术语来说‘并非暂时性’，因此，必须把2.69亿美元减记计入利润表。这个金额不会再给第四季度带来其他影响。也就是说，它不会再减少净资产，因为贬值早已反映过了。

1994.english:
Charlie and I will not stand for reelection to USAir's board at the upcoming annual meeting.  Should Seth wish to consult with us, however, we will be pleased to be of any help that we can.

Miscellaneous

Two CEO's who have done great things for Berkshire shareholders retired last year:  Dan Burke of Capital Cities/ABC and Carl Reichardt of Wells Fargo.  Dan and Carl encountered very tough industry conditions in recent years.  But their skill as managers allowed the businesses they ran to emerge from these periods with record earnings, added luster, and bright prospects. Additionally, Dan and Carl prepared well for their departure and left their companies in outstanding hands.  We owe them our gratitude.
1994.chinese:
在即将举行的股东年会上，查理和我将不再竞选USAir董事。不过，如果塞思想与我们商量，我们仍很乐意尽力提供帮助。

## 其他事项

去年，两位为伯克希尔股东作出卓越贡献的首席执行官退休：大都会／美国广播公司的丹·伯克，以及富国银行的卡尔·赖克特。近年来，两人所在行业都经历了十分艰难的环境。但凭借管理本领，他们带领的企业走出这段时期时，利润创下纪录，声誉更盛，前景光明。此外，两人也为离任作了充分准备，把公司交到了极为出色的人手里。我们应当感谢他们。

1994.english:
---

About 95.7% of all eligible shares participated in Berkshire's 1994 shareholder-designated contributions program.  Contributions made through the program were $10.4 million and 3,300 charities were recipients.

Every year a few shareholders miss participating in the program because they either do not have their shares registered in their own names on the prescribed record date or because they fail to get the designation form back to us within the 60-day period allowed for its return.  Since we don't make exceptions when requirements aren't met, we urge that both new shareholders and old read the description of our shareholder-designated contributions program that appears on pages 50-51.
1994.chinese:
---

1994年，伯克希尔股东指定捐款计划的参与股份，约占全部合资格股份的95.7%。计划捐款合计1,040万美元，3,300家慈善机构获赠。

每年都有少数股东错过参与计划：或者没有在规定登记日把股份登记在自己名下，或者没能在允许的60天内，把指定捐款表寄回。我们对不符合要求的情况不作例外处理，因此，敦促新老股东都阅读第50—51页关于股东指定捐款计划的说明。

1994.english:
To participate in future programs, you must make sure your shares are registered in the name of the actual owner, not in the nominee name of a broker, bank or depository.  Shares not so registered on August 31, 1995 will be ineligible for the 1995 program.

---

We made only one minor acquisition during 1994 - a small retail shoe chain - but our interest in finding good candidates remains as keen as ever.  The criteria we employ for purchases or mergers is detailed in the appendix on page 21.
1994.chinese:
要参加今后的计划，务必让股票登记在实际所有者名下，而非经纪商、银行或托管机构的代名人名下。1995年8月31日未按上述方式登记的股份，将没有资格参加1995年的计划。

---

1994年，我们只作了一笔小收购：一家小型鞋类零售连锁店。不过，我们寻找优秀收购对象的兴趣，一点也没有减弱。购买或合并所用的标准，详列于第21页附录。

1994.english: Last spring, we offered to merge with a large, family- controlled business on terms that included a Berkshire convertible preferred stock.  Though we failed to reach an agreement, this episode made me realize that we needed to ask our shareholders to authorize preferred shares in case we wanted in the future to move quickly if a similar acquisition opportunity were to appear. Accordingly, our proxy presents a proposal that you authorize a large amount of preferred stock, which will be issuable on terms set by the Board of Directors.  You can be sure that Charlie and I will not use these shares without being completely satisfied that we are receiving as much in intrinsic value as we are giving.
1994.chinese: 去年春天，我们提出与一家大型家族控股企业合并，条件中包括伯克希尔可转换优先股。虽然未能达成协议，但这件事让我意识到，应该请股东授权发行优先股，以便将来遇到类似收购机会时迅速行动。因此，委托投票材料提出一项议案，请各位授权大量优先股，由董事会决定具体发行条件。各位可以放心：只有完全确信收到的内在价值，至少等于交出去的内在价值，查理和我才会使用这些股票。

1994.english:
---

Charlie and I hope you can come to the Annual Meeting - at a new site.  Last year, we slightly overran the Orpheum Theater's seating capacity of 2,750, and therefore we will assemble at 9:30 a.m. on Monday, May 1, 1995, at the Holiday Convention Centre.  The main ballroom at the Centre can handle 3,300, and if need be, we will have audio and video equipment in an adjacent room capable of handling another 1,000 people.
1994.chinese:
---

查理和我希望，各位能来参加股东年会，这次换了新场地。去年，人数略微超过奥菲姆剧院2,750人的座位容量，因此，今年我们将于1995年5月1日星期一上午9:30，在假日会议中心相聚。中心的大宴会厅可容纳3,300人；如有需要，我们还会在邻近房间安排音视频设备，那里另可容纳1,000人。

1994.english:
Last year we displayed some of Berkshire's products at the meeting, and as a result sold about 800 pounds of candy, 507 pairs of shoes, and over $12,000 of World Books and related publications. All these goods will be available again this year.  Though we like to think of the meeting as a spiritual experience, we must remember that even the least secular of religions includes the ritual of the collection plate.

Of course, what you really should be purchasing is a video tape of the 1995 Orange Bowl.  Your Chairman views this classic nightly, switching to slow motion for the fourth quarter.  Our cover color this year is a salute to Nebraska's football coach, Tom Osborne, and his Cornhuskers, the country's top college team.  I urge you to wear Husker red to the annual meeting and promise you that at least 50% of your managerial duo will be in appropriate attire.
1994.chinese:
去年，我们在年会上展示了一些伯克希尔产品，结果卖出约800磅糖果、507双鞋，以及超过12,000美元的世界图书及相关出版物。今年，这些商品还会有。虽然我们愿意把年会想成一次精神体验，但得记住，即使最超凡脱俗的宗教，也有传递募捐盘的仪式。

当然，各位真正该买的，是1995年橘子碗比赛的录像带。你们的董事长每天晚上都看这场经典赛事，到第四节还要切换成慢动作。今年年报封面的颜色，是向内布拉斯加橄榄球队教练汤姆·奥斯本，以及他的玉米剥皮工队致敬；他们是全美头号大学球队。我敦促各位穿上球队的红色来参加年会，并保证，管理层两人组至少有50%，会穿得很合适。

1994.english: We recommend that you promptly get hotel reservations for the meeting, as we expect a large crowd.  Those of you who like to be downtown (about six miles from the Centre) may wish to stay at the Radisson Redick Tower, a small (88 rooms) but nice hotel or at the much larger Red Lion Hotel a few blocks away.  In the vicinity of the Centre are the Holiday Inn (403 rooms), Homewood Suites (118 rooms) and Hampton Inn (136 rooms).  Another recommended spot is the Marriott, whose west Omaha location is about 100 yards from Borsheim's and a ten-minute drive from the Centre.  There will be buses at the Marriott that will leave at 8:45 and 9:00 for the meeting and return after it ends.
1994.chinese: 我们预期到场人数很多，建议大家尽快订好酒店。喜欢住市中心的股东，那里距会议中心约六英里，可以考虑雷迪森—雷迪克大厦酒店，规模不大，只有88间客房，但很不错；也可选择几个街区外、规模大得多的红狮酒店。会议中心附近有假日酒店，403间客房；霍姆伍德套房酒店，118间；以及汉普顿酒店，136间。另一个推荐地点是万豪酒店，位于西奥马哈，距波仙珠宝约100码，距会议中心约十分钟车程。我们会安排巴士，上午8:45和9:00从万豪酒店出发，前往会场，会后送大家返回。

1994.english:
An attachment to our proxy material explains how you can obtain the card you will need for admission to the meeting.  A good-sized parking area is available at the Centre, while those who stay at the Holiday Inn, Homewood Suites and Hampton Inn will be able to walk to the meeting.

As usual, we will have buses to take you to the Nebraska Furniture Mart and Borsheim's after the meeting and to take you from there to hotels or the airport later.  I hope you make a special effort to visit the Nebraska Furniture Mart because it has opened the Mega Mart, a true retailing marvel that sells electronics, appliances, computers, CD's, cameras and audio equipment.  Sales have been sensational since the opening, and you will be amazed by both the variety of products available and their display on the floor.
1994.chinese:
委托投票材料的附件会说明，如何取得年会入场卡。会议中心有一片相当大的停车场；住在假日酒店、霍姆伍德套房酒店和汉普顿酒店的股东，则可以步行到会场。

和往年一样，会后我们会安排巴士，送各位去内布拉斯加家具卖场和波仙珠宝，稍后再送往酒店或机场。我希望大家特意去家具卖场看看，因为那里新开了Mega Mart，一家真正令人惊叹的零售店，销售电子产品、家电、电脑、CD、照相机和音响设备。开业以来，销售表现极为出色；无论商品种类之丰富，还是卖场陈列，都会让各位惊叹。

1994.english: The Mega Mart, adjacent to NFM's main store, is on our 64-acre site about two miles north of the Centre.  The stores are open from 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. on Fridays, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Saturdays and noon to 6 p.m. on Sundays.  When you're there be sure to say hello to Mrs. B, who, at 101, will be hard at work in our Mrs. B's Warehouse.  She never misses a day at the store - or, for that matter, an hour.
1994.chinese: Mega Mart紧邻家具卖场主店，位于我们64英亩的场地内，在会议中心以北约两英里。商店星期五上午10:00至晚上9:00营业，星期六上午10:00至下午6:00，星期日中午12:00至下午6:00。到那里，别忘了和B夫人打个招呼：101岁的她，还会在B夫人仓储店里埋头工作。她一天都不会缺勤；真要说起来，连一个小时也不会。

1994.english:
Borsheim's normally is closed on Sunday but will be open for shareholders and their guests from noon to 6 p.m. on Sunday.  This is always a special day, and we will try to have a few surprises. Usually this is the biggest sales day of the year, so for more reasons than one Charlie and I hope to see you there.

On Saturday evening, April 29, there will be a baseball game at Rosenblatt Stadium between the Omaha Royals and the Buffalo Bisons.  The Buffalo team is owned by my friends, Mindy and Bob Rich, Jr., and I'm hoping they will attend.  If so, I will try to entice Bob into a one-pitch duel on the mound.  Bob is a capitalist's Randy Johnson - young, strong and athletic - and not the sort of fellow you want to face early in the season.  So I will need plenty of vocal support.
1994.chinese:
波仙珠宝通常星期日休息，但这一天会为股东及来宾，从中午12:00营业至下午6:00。这向来是个特别的日子，我们会设法准备一些惊喜。通常，这也是全年销售额最高的一天，因此，查理和我盼着在那里见到各位，理由可不止一个。

4月29日星期六晚上，奥马哈皇家队与布法罗野牛队，将在罗森布拉特球场比赛。布法罗队属于我的朋友明迪和小鲍勃·里奇，我希望他们也会来。如果来了，我会设法引鲍勃上投手丘，来一场一球对决。鲍勃是资本家中的兰迪·约翰逊，年轻、强壮、运动能力出众；赛季刚开始，你可不想碰上这样的对手。所以，我需要各位多多呐喊助威。

1994.english:
The proxy statement will include information about obtaining tickets to the game.  About 1,400 shareholders attended the event last year.  Opening the game that night, I had my stuff and threw a strike that the scoreboard reported at eight miles per hour.  What many fans missed was that I shook off the catcher's call for my fast ball and instead delivered my change-up.  This year it will be all smoke.

Warren E. Buffett March 7, 1995                               Chairman of the Board
1994.chinese:
委托投票说明书会介绍如何取得比赛门票。去年，约1,400名股东到场。那天晚上为比赛开场时，我状态很好，投了个好球，记分牌显示时速八英里。许多球迷没注意到的是：捕手要我投快速球，我摇头拒绝，改投了变速球。今年，我要全力飙快速球。

沃伦·E.巴菲特  
董事会主席  
1995年3月7日

1995.english:
BERKSHIRE HATHAWAY INC.

To the Shareholders of Berkshire Hathaway Inc.:

Our gain in net worth during 1995 was $5.3 billion, or 45.0%.  Per-share book value grew by a little less, 43.1%, because we paid stock for two acquisitions, increasing our shares outstanding by 1.3%.  Over the last 31 years (that is, since present management took over) per-share book value has grown from $19 to $14,426, or at a rate of 23.6% compounded annually.

There's no reason to do handsprings over 1995's gains.  This was a year in which any fool could make a bundle in the stock market.  And we did.  To paraphrase President Kennedy, a rising tide lifts all yachts.
1995.chinese:
伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司

致伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司的股东：

1995年，我们的净资产增加了53亿美元，增幅45.0%。每股账面价值增长略低，为43.1%，因为我们在两项收购中支付了股票，使流通股数量增加1.3%。过去31年，也就是现任管理层接手以来，每股账面价值从19美元增至14,426美元，年复合增长率为23.6%。

犯不着为1995年的成绩翻跟头庆祝。这一年，随便哪个傻瓜都能在股市赚上一大笔。我们也赚了。套用肯尼迪总统的话说：涨潮时，所有游艇都跟着升高。

1995.english:
Putting aside the financial results, there was plenty of good news at Berkshire last year:  We negotiated three acquisitions of exactly the type we desire.  Two of these, Helzberg's Diamond Shops and R.C. Willey Home Furnishings, are included in our 1995 financial statements, while our largest transaction, the purchase of GEICO, closed immediately after the end of the year.  (I'll tell you more about all three acquisitions later in the report.)

These new subsidiaries roughly double our revenues.  Even so, the acquisitions neither materially increased our shares outstanding nor our debt.  And, though these three operations employ over 11,000 people, our headquarters staff grew only from 11 to 12.  (No sense going crazy.)
1995.chinese:
财务成绩先放一边，伯克希尔去年还有不少好消息：我们谈成了三项收购，家家都正合心意。其中，赫尔茨伯格钻石店与R.C.威利家居已纳入1995年财务报表；最大的一笔——收购GEICO——则在年末刚过时完成。（本报告稍后会详细介绍这三项收购。）

这些新子公司使我们的营业收入大约翻了一番。即便如此，收购既没有显著增加流通股，也没有显著增加债务。三家企业合计雇用超过11,000人，总部员工却只从11人增至12人。（总不能一下子忘乎所以嘛。）

1995.english: Charlie Munger, Berkshire's Vice Chairman and my partner, and I want to build a collection of companies - both wholly- and partly-owned - that have excellent economic characteristics and that are run by outstanding managers.  Our favorite acquisition is the negotiated transaction that allows us to purchase 100% of such a business at a fair price.  But we are almost as happy when the stock market offers us the chance to buy a modest percentage of an outstanding business at a pro-rata price well below what it would take to buy 100%.  This double-barrelled approach - purchases of entire businesses through negotiation or purchases of part-interests through the stock market - gives us an important advantage over capital-allocators who stick to a single course.  Woody Allen once explained why eclecticism works:  "The real advantage of being bisexual is that it doubles your chances for a date on Saturday night."
1995.chinese: 伯克希尔副董事长、我的合伙人查理·芒格和我，希望建立起一组企业——既有全资持有的，也有部分持有的——它们具有出色的经济特性，并由优秀的管理者经营。我们最喜欢的收购，是通过协商，以公允的价格买下这样一家企业的100%股权。不过，如果股票市场让我们有机会，以远低于收购全部股权所需价格的按比例价格，买进一家优秀企业的一小部分，我们也几乎一样高兴。这种双管齐下的办法——通过协商买下整家公司，或通过股市买进部分权益——使我们相较于只走一条路的资本配置者，拥有一项重要优势。伍迪·艾伦曾解释过，为什么兼收并蓄行得通：“双性恋真正的好处，是星期六晚上约到人的机会多了一倍。”

1995.english: Over the years, we've been Woody-like in our thinking, attempting to increase our marketable investments in wonderful businesses, while simultaneously trying to buy similar businesses in their entirety.  The following table illustrates our progress on both fronts.  In the tabulation, we show the marketable securities owned per share of Berkshire at ten-year intervals.  A second column lists our per-share operating earnings (before taxes and purchase-price adjustments but after interest and corporate overhead) from all other activities.  In other words, the second column shows what we earned excluding the dividends, interest and capital gains that we realized from investments. Purchase-price accounting adjustments are ignored for reasons we have explained at length in previous reports and which, as an act of mercy, we won't repeat.  (We'll be glad to send masochists the earlier explanations, however.)
1995.chinese: 多年来，我们的想法颇有伍迪的风范：一方面努力增加在优秀企业中的证券投资，另一方面也设法把类似企业整个买下来。下表说明了我们在两条战线上取得的进展。表中每隔十年列示伯克希尔每股所拥有的有价证券；另一栏则列示其余所有业务的每股营业利润，口径为税前、收购价格会计调整前，但已经扣除利息及公司总部费用。换句话说，第二栏剔除了投资带来的股息、利息与资本利得。我们忽略收购价格会计调整，理由在过去报告里已经详细解释过；这次大发慈悲，就不再重复了。（不过，喜欢自讨苦吃的读者若想看，我们很乐意把以前的解释寄去。）

1995.english:
These results have not sprung from some master plan that we concocted in 1965.  In a general way, we knew then what we hoped to accomplish but had no idea what specific opportunities might make it possible.  Today we remain similarly unstructured:  Over time, we expect to improve the figures in both columns but have no road map to tell us how that will come about.

We proceed with two advantages:  First, our operating managers are outstanding and, in most cases, have an unusually strong attachment to Berkshire.  Second, Charlie and I have had considerable experience in allocating capital and try to go at that job rationally and objectively.  The giant disadvantage we face is size:  In the early years, we needed only good ideas, but now we need good big ideas.  Unfortunately, the difficulty of finding these grows in direct proportion to our financial success, a problem that increasingly erodes our strengths.
1995.chinese:
这些成绩，并非来自我们1965年就设计好的一张宏伟蓝图。当时，我们大致知道希望达成什么，却不知道会有哪些具体机会帮助我们实现目标。如今，我们还是这样没有章法：随着时间推移，我们希望两栏数字都能改善，但手里没有路线图，告诉我们究竟怎么走到那里。

往前走，我们有两项优势。第一，我们的经营管理者非常出色，而且大多对伯克希尔有着非同寻常的深厚感情。第二，查理和我在资本配置方面积累了相当丰富的经验，也努力以理性、客观的态度做好这件事。摆在眼前的巨大劣势，是规模：早年，我们只需要好主意；如今，我们需要的是既好、又够大的主意。不幸的是，找这种主意的难度，与我们的财务成就成正比。这个问题正在越来越多地侵蚀我们的优势。

1995.english:
I will have more to say about Berkshire's prospects later in this report, when I discuss our proposed recapitalization.

Acquisitions

It may seem strange that we exult over a year in which we made three acquisitions, given that we have regularly used these pages to question the acquisition activities of most managers. Rest assured, Charlie and I haven't lost our skepticism:  We believe most deals do damage to the shareholders of the acquiring company.  Too often, the words from HMS Pinafore apply:  "Things are seldom what they seem, skim milk masquerades as cream." Specifically, sellers and their representatives invariably present financial projections having more entertainment value than educational value.  In the production of rosy scenarios, Wall Street can hold its own against Washington.
1995.chinese:
本报告稍后讨论拟议的股本重组时，我会进一步谈伯克希尔的前景。

## 收购

我们经常在这里质疑多数管理者的收购活动，如今却因为一年买了三家公司而欢欣鼓舞，看起来或许有点奇怪。各位放心，查理和我的怀疑态度并没有消失：我们认为，大多数交易都会损害收购方股东的利益。《皮娜弗号军舰》里的那句话，实在太常用得上：“世事鲜如眼前所见，脱脂奶也扮成奶油来卖。”具体地说，卖方及其代表拿出的财务预测，总是娱乐价值大于教育价值。论编织玫瑰色前景，华尔街与华盛顿相比，绝不会落在下风。

1995.english: In any case, why potential buyers even look at projections prepared by sellers baffles me.  Charlie and I never give them a glance, but instead keep in mind the story of the man with an ailing horse.  Visiting the vet, he said:  "Can you help me? Sometimes my horse walks just fine and sometimes he limps."  The vet's reply was pointed:  "No problem - when he's walking fine, sell him."  In the world of mergers and acquisitions, that horse would be peddled as Secretariat.
1995.chinese: 说到底，潜在买家为什么居然肯看卖方编制的预测，我始终想不通。查理和我从不瞟上一眼，倒是一直记着那个马有毛病的人的故事。他去找兽医，说：“能帮帮我吗？我的马有时走得好好的，有时却一瘸一拐。”兽医的答复一针见血：“没问题——等它走得好好的时候，把它卖掉。”到了并购世界，这匹马会被当成赛马名驹“秘书处”推销。

1995.english:
At Berkshire, we have all the difficulties in perceiving the future that other acquisition-minded companies do.  Like they also, we face the inherent problem that the seller of a business practically always knows far more about it than the buyer and also picks the time of sale - a time when the business is likely to be walking "just fine."

Even so, we do have a few advantages, perhaps the greatest being that we don't have a strategic plan.  Thus we feel no need to proceed in an ordained direction (a course leading almost invariably to silly purchase prices) but can instead simply decide what makes sense for our owners.  In doing that, we always mentally compare any move we are contemplating with dozens of other opportunities open to us, including the purchase of small pieces of the best businesses in the world via the stock market. Our practice of making this comparison - acquisitions against passive investments - is a discipline that managers focused simply on expansion seldom use.
1995.chinese:
在伯克希尔，想看清未来，我们面对的困难与其他热衷收购的公司并无二致。我们也同样躲不开一个天生的难题：企业卖方几乎总比买方了解得多得多，而且卖方还能挑出售时间——通常正是企业走得“好好的”时候。

即便如此，我们仍有几项优势，其中最大的一项，或许就是我们没有战略规划。因此，我们不觉得非得朝某个预先规定的方向走不可——那条路几乎总会把人带到愚蠢的收购价格上。我们只需判断，怎样做对我们的所有者划算。作判断时，我们总在心里把正在考虑的行动，与其他几十种可选机会作比较，其中包括通过股市买进世界上最优秀企业的一小部分。把收购与被动投资这样相互比较，是一种约束；一心只想扩张的管理者，很少采用这种约束。

1995.english:
Talking to Time Magazine a few years back, Peter Drucker got to the heart of things:  "I will tell you a secret: Dealmaking beats working.  Dealmaking is exciting and fun, and working is grubby.  Running anything is primarily an enormous amount of grubby detail work . . . dealmaking is romantic, sexy.  That's why you have deals that make no sense."

In making acquisitions, we have a further advantage:  As payment, we can offer sellers a stock backed by an extraordinary collection of outstanding businesses.  An individual or a family wishing to dispose of a single fine business, but also wishing to defer personal taxes indefinitely, is apt to find Berkshire stock a particularly comfortable holding.  I believe, in fact, that this calculus played an important part in the two acquisitions for which we paid shares in 1995.
1995.chinese:
几年前，彼得·德鲁克接受《时代》杂志采访时，说到了要害：“我告诉你一个秘密：谈交易比干活过瘾。谈交易刺激、有趣；干活却琐碎又费劲。经营任何事情，主要都是大量琐碎费劲的细节工作……谈交易却浪漫、性感。于是，就有了那些毫无道理的交易。”

收购时，我们还有一项优势：可以用股票作为对价，而这只股票背后，是一批非同寻常的优秀企业。一个个人或家族，既想出售一家优良企业，又想无限期递延个人税款，很可能会觉得持有伯克希尔股票特别安心。我相信，这笔算盘，事实上在1995年那两项以股票支付的收购中，发挥了重要作用。

1995.english: Beyond that, sellers sometimes care about placing their companies in a corporate home that will both endure and provide pleasant, productive working conditions for their managers.  Here again, Berkshire offers something special.  Our managers operate with extraordinary autonomy.  Additionally, our ownership structure enables sellers to know that when I say we are buying to keep, the promise means something.  For our part, we like dealing with owners who care what happens to their companies and people.  A buyer is likely to find fewer unpleasant surprises dealing with that type of seller than with one simply auctioning off his business.
1995.chinese: 此外，卖方有时还关心，自己的企业能否找到一个长久的归宿，既能延续下去，也让管理者工作愉快、有所作为。在这方面，伯克希尔又有特别之处。我们的经理人享有极大的自主权。而我们的所有权结构，也让卖方知道：当我说买下来就是为了长久持有时，这句话是有分量的。我们自己也喜欢与关心公司和员工将来会怎样的所有者打交道。与这样的人做交易，买方遇到不愉快意外的可能性，往往小于与那些只顾拍卖企业的人做交易。

1995.english: In addition to the foregoing being an explanation of our acquisition style, it is, of course, a not-so-subtle sales pitch. If you own or represent a business earning $25 million or more before tax, and it fits the criteria listed on page 23, just give me a call.  Our discussion will be confidential.  And if you aren't interested now, file our proposition in the back of your mind:  We are never going to lose our appetite for buying companies with good economics and excellent management.
1995.chinese: 以上既是对我们收购风格的说明，当然也是一番不怎么掩饰的推销。如果各位拥有或代表一家税前利润达到2,500万美元、并符合第23页标准的企业，给我打个电话就行。谈话内容会保密。现在若没兴趣，也请把我们的提议放在心里留个底：对于经济特性良好、管理层优秀的企业，我们买进的胃口永远不会消失。

1995.english: Concluding this little dissertation on acquisitions, I can't resist repeating a tale told me last year by a corporate executive.  The business he grew up in was a fine one, with a long-time record of leadership in its industry.  Its main product, however, was distressingly glamorless.  So several decades ago, the company hired a management consultant who - naturally - advised diversification, the then-current fad. ("Focus" was not yet in style.)  Before long, the company acquired a number of businesses, each after the consulting firm had gone through a long - and expensive - acquisition study.  And the outcome?  Said the executive sadly, "When we started, we were getting 100% of our earnings from the original business.  After ten years, we were getting 150%."
1995.chinese: 这篇收购小论文收尾之前，我忍不住要复述一位企业高管去年告诉我的故事。他从小就在其中成长的那家企业，生意很好，长期在行业中居于领先地位。遗憾的是，主打产品实在毫不起眼。于是，几十年前，公司请来一位管理顾问；顾问当然建议多元化——那正是当时的时髦玩意。（“聚焦”那时还没流行起来。）没过多久，公司买下了一批企业，每一笔收购之前，顾问公司都先做了又漫长、又昂贵的研究。结果呢？那位高管伤心地说：“起初，我们100%的利润来自原来的主业。十年以后，这个比例变成了150%。”

1995.english:
## Helzberg's Diamond Shops

A few years back, management consultants popularized a technique called "management by walking around" (MBWA).  At Berkshire, we've instituted ABWA (acquisitions by walking around).

In May 1994, a week or so after the Annual Meeting, I was crossing the street at 58th and Fifth Avenue in New York, when a woman called out my name.  I listened as she told me she'd been to, and had enjoyed, the Annual Meeting.  A few seconds later, a man who'd heard the woman stop me did so as well.  He turned out to be Barnett Helzberg, Jr., who owned four shares of Berkshire and had also been at our meeting.
1995.chinese:
## 赫尔茨伯格钻石店

几年前，管理顾问把一种叫作“走动式管理”（MBWA）的技巧炒得很热。在伯克希尔，我们实行的是ABWA——走动式收购。

1994年5月，股东大会过后约一周，我在纽约第五大道与第58街交叉口过马路时，一位女士喊出了我的名字。我停下来，听她说起自己参加过股东大会，而且很喜欢。几秒钟后，一位男士听见她叫住了我，也上前把我拦下。他是小巴尼特·赫尔茨伯格，持有四股伯克希尔股票，也参加了我们的大会。

1995.english:
In our few minutes of conversation, Barnett said he had a business we might be interested in.  When people say that, it usually turns out they have a lemonade stand - with potential, of course, to quickly grow into the next Microsoft.  So I simply asked Barnett to send me particulars.  That, I thought to myself. will be the end of that.

Not long after, Barnett sent me the financial statements of Helzberg's Diamond Shops.  The company had been started by his grandfather in 1915 from a single store in Kansas City and had developed by the time we met into a group with 134 stores in 23 states.  Sales had grown from $10 million in 1974 to $53 million in 1984 and $282 million in 1994.  We weren't talking lemonade stands.
1995.chinese:
短短几分钟的交谈中，巴尼特说，他有一家企业，我们或许会感兴趣。通常，别人这么说，拿出来的往往是个卖柠檬水的小摊——当然，都有迅速成长为下一个微软的潜力。所以，我只请巴尼特寄些具体资料来。心里想着：这事大概也就到此为止了。

没过多久，巴尼特寄来了赫尔茨伯格钻石店的财务报表。这家公司由他的祖父于1915年创办，起初只有堪萨斯城的一家店；到我们认识时，已发展成遍布23个州、拥有134家门店的集团。销售额从1974年的1,000万美元，增至1984年的5,300万美元，再增至1994年的2.82亿美元。我们谈的可不是柠檬水小摊。

1995.english: Barnett, then 60, loved the business but also wanted to feel free of it.  In 1988, as a step in that direction, he had brought in Jeff Comment, formerly President of Wanamaker's, to help him run things.  The hiring of Jeff turned out to be a homerun, but Barnett still found that he couldn't shake a feeling of ultimate responsibility.  Additionally, he owned a valuable asset that was subject to the vagaries of a single, very competitive industry, and he thought it prudent to diversify his family's holdings.
1995.chinese: 当时60岁的巴尼特深爱这门生意，却也希望能从中解脱。1988年，为朝这个方向迈一步，他请来原沃纳梅克百货总裁杰夫·科门特，帮他打理业务。请杰夫这一招，堪称一记本垒打，但巴尼特发现，自己仍摆脱不了那种最终责任在肩的感觉。此外，他拥有的是一项价值很高、却受制于单一且竞争激烈行业起伏的资产；他认为，让家族持有的资产更为分散，是明智之举。

1995.english: Berkshire was made to order for him.  It took us awhile to get together on price, but there was never any question in my mind that, first, Helzberg's was the kind of business that we wanted to own and, second, Jeff was our kind of manager.  In fact, we would not have bought the business if Jeff had not been there to run it.  Buying a retailer without good management is like buying the Eiffel Tower without an elevator.
1995.chinese: 伯克希尔简直是为他量身定做的。我们花了一些时间才就价格达成一致，但我心里从来没有怀疑过两点：第一，赫尔茨伯格正是我们想拥有的企业；第二，杰夫正是我们喜欢的管理者。事实上，若没有杰夫在那儿经营，我们就不会收购。买一家没有优秀管理层的零售企业，好比买下埃菲尔铁塔，却没配电梯。

1995.english:
We completed the Helzberg purchase in 1995 by means of a tax-free exchange of stock, the only kind of transaction that interested Barnett.  Though he was certainly under no obligation to do so, Barnett shared a meaningful part of his proceeds from the sale with a large number of his associates.  When someone behaves that generously, you know you are going to be treated right as a buyer.

The average Helzberg's store has annual sales of about $2 million, far more than competitors operating similarly-sized stores achieve.  This superior per-store productivity is the key to Helzberg's excellent profits.  If the company continues its first-rate performance - and we believe it will - it could grow rather quickly to several times its present size.
1995.chinese:
1995年，我们通过免税换股完成了赫尔茨伯格的收购；巴尼特只对这种交易方式有兴趣。他原本完全没有义务这样做，却把出售所得中相当可观的一部分，分给了许多同事。一个人如此慷慨，身为买方，你就知道自己也会受到厚道的对待。

赫尔茨伯格每家门店年均销售额约200万美元，远高于经营同等规模门店的竞争对手。这种出众的单店产出，是公司利润优异的关键。如果它继续保持一流水准——我们相信会如此——规模可能很快就会增长到目前的数倍。

1995.english: Helzberg's, it should be added, is an entirely different sort of operation from Borsheim's, our Omaha jewelry business, and the two companies will operate independently of each other. Borsheim's had an excellent year in 1995, with sales up 11.7%. Susan Jacques, its 36-year-old CEO, had an even better year, giving birth to her second son at the start of the Christmas season.  Susan has proved to be a terrific leader in the two years since her promotion.
1995.chinese: 还要说明，赫尔茨伯格与我们在奥马哈经营的波仙珠宝，完全是两种不同类型的生意，两家公司将各自独立经营。波仙1995年成绩优异，销售额增长11.7%。它36岁的首席执行官苏珊·雅克斯这一年过得更好：圣诞销售季刚开始，她就生下了第二个儿子。苏珊获晋升后的这两年，已经证明自己是一位出色的领导者。

1995.english:
## R.C. Willey Home Furnishings

It was Nebraska Furniture Mart's Irv Blumkin who did the walking around in the case of R.C. Willey, long the leading home furnishings business in Utah.  Over the years, Irv had told me about the strengths of that company.  And he had also told Bill Child, CEO of R.C. Willey, how pleased the Blumkin family had been with its Berkshire relationship.  So in early 1995, Bill mentioned to Irv that for estate tax and diversification reasons, he and the other owners of R.C. Willey might be interested in selling.
1995.chinese:
## R.C.威利家居

R.C.威利长期是犹他州家居业的龙头。这次负责“走动”的，是内布拉斯加家具卖场的欧文·布拉姆金。多年来，欧文一直向我介绍这家公司的长处；他也向R.C.威利的首席执行官比尔·蔡尔德说起，布拉姆金家族与伯克希尔合作有多么愉快。因此，1995年初，比尔对欧文提起，出于遗产税和分散投资的考虑，他和R.C.威利的其他所有者，或许有意出售。

1995.english:
From that point forward, things could not have been simpler. Bill sent me some figures, and I wrote him a letter indicating my idea of value.  We quickly agreed on a number, and found our personal chemistry to be perfect.  By mid-year, the merger was completed.

R.C. Willey is an amazing story.  Bill took over the business from his father-in-law in 1954 when sales were about $250,000.  From this tiny base, Bill employed Mae West's philosophy:  "It's not what you've got - it's what you do with what you've got."  Aided by his brother, Sheldon, Bill has built the company to its 1995 sales volume of $257 million, and it now accounts for over 50% of the furniture business in Utah.  Like Nebraska Furniture Mart, R.C. Willey sells appliances, electronics, computers and carpets in addition to furniture. Both companies have about the same sales volume, but NFM gets all of its business from one complex in Omaha, whereas R.C. Willey will open its sixth major store in the next few months.
1995.chinese:
此后，一切简单得不能再简单。比尔寄来一些数字，我回了一封信，说明自己对价值的看法。我们很快就价格达成一致，彼此也十分投缘。到年中，合并便完成了。

R.C.威利的故事相当惊人。1954年，比尔从岳父手中接下这门生意，销售额大约只有25万美元。从这样小的基数起步，他践行了梅·韦斯特的哲学：“要紧的不是你有什么，而是你拿已有的东西做了什么。”在弟弟谢尔登帮助下，比尔把公司1995年的销售额做到了2.57亿美元，如今占犹他州家具业务的50%以上。与内布拉斯加家具卖场一样，R.C.威利除了家具，还销售家电、电子产品、电脑与地毯。两家公司销售额大致相当，但内布拉斯加家具卖场全部生意都来自奥马哈的一处综合卖场，R.C.威利却将在未来几个月开出第六家大型门店。

1995.english: Retailing is a tough business.  During my investment career, I have watched a large number of retailers enjoy terrific growth and superb returns on equity for a period, and then suddenly nosedive, often all the way into bankruptcy.  This shooting-star phenomenon is far more common in retailing than it is in manufacturing or service businesses.  In part, this is because a retailer must stay smart, day after day.  Your competitor is always copying and then topping whatever you do.  Shoppers are meanwhile beckoned in every conceivable way to try a stream of new merchants.  In retailing, to coast is to fail.
1995.chinese: 零售是一门艰难的生意。在我的投资生涯中，见过许多零售商，先是一段时间增长惊人、股东权益回报极高，随后却突然一头栽下去，往往一路栽到破产。这种流星现象，在零售业远比制造业或服务业常见。部分原因在于，零售商必须天天保持聪明。无论你做什么，竞争对手总在模仿，然后做得比你更好。与此同时，顾客又受到各种想象得到的招徕，去光顾层出不穷的新商家。在零售业，想靠惯性往前滑，就等着失败吧。

1995.english: In contrast to this have-to-be-smart-every-day business, there is what I call the have-to-be-smart-once business.  For example, if you were smart enough to buy a network TV station very early in the game, you could put in a shiftless and backward nephew to run things, and the business would still do well for decades.  You'd do far better, of course, if you put in Tom Murphy, but you could stay comfortably in the black without him. For a retailer, hiring that nephew would be an express ticket to bankruptcy.
1995.chinese: 与这种“每天都得聪明”的生意相对，还有一种我称为“只需聪明一次”的生意。比如，在行业很早期，你若够聪明，买进了一家电视网附属电视台，即使派个懒散又不开窍的侄子来管理，几十年里生意仍会不错。当然，请汤姆·墨菲来管，成绩会好得多；不过，没有他，也照样能舒舒服服地赚钱。零售商若雇了那位侄子，拿到的就是一张直达破产的快车票。

1995.english: The two retailing businesses we purchased this year are blessed with terrific managers who love to compete and have done so successfully for decades.  Like the CEOs of our other operating units, they will operate autonomously:  We want them to feel that the businesses they run are theirs.  This means no second-guessing by Charlie and me.  We avoid the attitude of the alumnus whose message to the football coach is "I'm 100% with you - win or tie."  Our basic goal as an owner is to behave with our managers as we like our owners to behave with us.
1995.chinese: 我们今年收购的两家零售企业，幸运地拥有出色的管理者。他们热爱竞争，而且几十年来都竞争得很成功。与我们其他经营单位的首席执行官一样，他们将自主经营：我们希望他们觉得，自己经营的企业就是自己的。这意味着，查理和我不会在一旁指手画脚。我们不会像有些校友那样，对橄榄球队教练说：“我百分之百支持你——只要赢球或者打平。”作为所有者，我们的基本目标，是像我们希望自己的所有者对待我们那样，去对待经理人。

1995.english: As we add more operations, I'm sometimes asked how many people I can handle reporting to me.  My answer to that is simple:  If I have one person reporting to me and he is a lemon, that's one too many, and if I have managers like those we now have, the number can be almost unlimited.  We are lucky to have Bill and Sheldon associated with us, and we hope that we can acquire other businesses that bring with them managers of similar caliber.
1995.chinese: 随着旗下业务越来越多，有人会问，我究竟能管得了多少名向我汇报的人。回答很简单：如果只有一个人向我汇报，而他是个废物，那一个都嫌多；如果经理人都像我们现在这些人，人数几乎可以没有上限。比尔和谢尔登加入我们，是我们的幸运。我们希望还能收购其他企业，把同样水准的管理者也一并请进来。

1995.english:
## GEICO Corporation

Right after yearend, we completed the purchase of 100% of GEICO, the seventh largest auto insurer in the United States, with about 3.7 million cars insured.  I've had a 45-year association with GEICO, and though the story has been told before, it's worth a short recap here.

I attended Columbia University's business school in 1950-51, not because I cared about the degree it offered, but because I wanted to study under Ben Graham, then teaching there.  The time I spent in Ben's classes was a personal high, and quickly induced me to learn all I could about my hero.  I turned first to Who's Who in America, finding there, among other things, that Ben was Chairman of Government Employees Insurance Company, to me an unknown company in an unfamiliar industry.
1995.chinese:
## GEICO公司

年末刚过，我们就完成了对GEICO全部股权的收购。它是美国第七大汽车保险公司，承保车辆约370万辆。我与GEICO的交往已经有45年，故事虽讲过，仍值得在这里简短回顾一下。

1950—1951年，我到哥伦比亚大学商学院就读，不是因为在意它颁的学位，而是想跟当时在那里教书的本·格雷厄姆学习。上本的课，是我个人生活中的一段高峰，也很快促使我尽可能了解这位心目中的英雄。我先查了《美国名人录》，其中一项资料说，本担任政府雇员保险公司董事长。那家公司我没听过，所在的行业我也陌生。

1995.english: A librarian next referred me to Best's Fire and Casualty insurance manual, where I learned that GEICO was based in Washington, DC.  So on a Saturday in January, 1951, I took the train to Washington and headed for GEICO's downtown headquarters. To my dismay, the building was closed, but I pounded on the door until a custodian appeared.  I asked this puzzled fellow if there was anyone in the office I could talk to, and he said he'd seen one man working on the sixth floor.
1995.chinese: 接着，一位图书管理员推荐我查《贝氏火灾及意外保险手册》，我才知道GEICO总部设在华盛顿特区。于是，1951年1月的一个星期六，我搭火车去了华盛顿，直奔它在市中心的总部。令我沮丧的是，大楼关着门。我不停敲门，直到一位管理员出现。我问这位一头雾水的先生，办公室里有没有人可以聊聊。他说，见过一个人在六楼工作。

1995.english: And thus I met Lorimer Davidson, Assistant to the President, who was later to become CEO.  Though my only credentials were that I was a student of Graham's, "Davy" graciously spent four hours or so showering me with both kindness and instruction.  No one has ever received a better half-day course in how the insurance industry functions nor in the factors that enable one company to excel over others.  As Davy made clear, GEICO's method of selling - direct marketing - gave it an enormous cost advantage over competitors that sold through agents, a form of distribution so ingrained in the business of these insurers that it was impossible for them to give it up.  After my session with Davy, I was more excited about GEICO than I have ever been about a stock.
1995.chinese: 就这样，我见到了当时的总裁助理、后来担任首席执行官的洛里默·戴维森。我的全部资历，无非是格雷厄姆的学生，但“戴维”仍慷慨地花了大约四小时，对我既热情又悉心指点。关于保险行业怎样运作、一家公司靠什么超越同行，恐怕没有人上过比这更好的半日课程。戴维讲得很清楚：GEICO的直销方式，使它相较于通过代理人卖保险的竞争者，拥有巨大的成本优势；代理人分销在那些公司的经营中根深蒂固，以致根本无法放弃。与戴维谈完，我对GEICO的兴奋，超过此前对任何一只股票的兴奋。

1995.english: When I finished at Columbia some months later and returned to Omaha to sell securities, I naturally focused almost exclusively on GEICO.  My first sales call - on my Aunt Alice, who always supported me 100% - was successful.  But I was then a skinny, unpolished 20-year-old who looked about 17, and my pitch usually failed.  Undaunted, I wrote a short report late in 1951 about GEICO for "The Security I Like Best" column in The Commercial and Financial Chronicle, a leading financial publication of the time.  More important, I bought stock for my own account.
1995.chinese: 几个月后，我完成哥伦比亚大学的学业，回奥马哈推销证券，自然几乎把全部精力放在GEICO上。第一次登门推销，找的是永远百分之百支持我的艾丽斯姨妈，成功了。但当时的我，瘦瘦的，不太懂人情世故，明明20岁，看上去却像17岁，因此推销通常失败。我并不气馁。1951年末，我为当时重要财经刊物《商业与金融纪事》的“我最喜欢的证券”专栏，写了一篇介绍GEICO的短文。更重要的是，我自己买了它的股票。

1995.english: You may think this odd, but I have kept copies of every tax return I filed, starting with the return for 1944.  Checking back, I find that I purchased GEICO shares on four occasions during 1951, the last purchase being made on September 26.  This pattern of persistence suggests to me that my tendency toward self-intoxication was developed early.  I probably came back on that September day from unsuccessfully trying to sell some prospect and decided - despite my already having more than 50% of my net worth in GEICO - to load up further.  In any event, I accumulated 350 shares of GEICO during the year, at a cost of $10,282.  At yearend, this holding was worth $13,125, more than 65% of my net worth.
1995.chinese: 各位可能觉得奇怪：我从1944年开始提交的每一份报税表，副本都留着。翻回去查，我发现1951年自己分四次买入GEICO，最后一次是9月26日。这种锲而不舍的买法让我觉得，我自我陶醉的毛病，看来很早就养成了。那个9月的一天，我很可能又向某位潜在客户推销失败，回来便决定继续加仓——尽管自己超过一半的净资产已经投在GEICO上。不管怎样，那一年我一共积累了350股，成本10,282美元。到年末，这些股票价值13,125美元，占我净资产的65%以上。

1995.english:
You can see why GEICO was my first business love.  Furthermore, just to complete this stroll down memory lane, I should add that I earned most of the funds I used to buy GEICO shares by delivering The Washington Post, the chief product of a company that much later made it possible for Berkshire to turn $10 million into $500 million.

Alas, I sold my entire GEICO position in 1952 for $15,259, primarily to switch into Western Insurance Securities.  This act of infidelity can partially be excused by the fact that Western was selling for slightly more than one times its current earnings, a p/e ratio that for some reason caught my eye.  But in the next 20 years, the GEICO stock I sold grew in value to about $1.3 million, which taught me a lesson about the inadvisability of selling a stake in an identifiably-wonderful company.
1995.chinese:
各位现在明白，为什么GEICO是我在商业上的初恋了。为了把这段往事回味完整，还得补充一句：买GEICO股票所用的资金，大部分是我送《华盛顿邮报》赚来的。这份报纸所属的公司，在很久以后又让伯克希尔有机会把1,000万美元变成了5亿美元。

可惜，1952年，我把GEICO全部卖掉，卖得15,259美元，主要是为了换成西部保险证券公司。那只股票当时的价格，只比当期每股利润高一点点，这个市盈率不知怎的就勾住了我的眼睛，多少能替我的见异思迁开脱一下。不过，随后20年，我卖掉的那些GEICO股票，价值增长到约130万美元。这给我上了一课：一家公司的优秀已经看得明明白白时，卖掉它的权益，可不是什么好主意。

1995.english:
In the early 1970's, after Davy retired, the executives running GEICO made some serious errors in estimating their claims costs, a mistake that led the company to underprice its policies - and that almost caused it to go bankrupt.  The company was saved only because Jack Byrne came in as CEO in 1976 and took drastic remedial measures.

Because I believed both in Jack and in GEICO's fundamental competitive strength, Berkshire purchased a large interest in the company during the second half of 1976, and also made smaller purchases later.  By yearend 1980, we had put $45.7 million into GEICO and owned 33.3% of its shares.  During the next 15 years, we did not make further purchases.  Our interest in the company, nonetheless, grew to about 50% because it was a big repurchaser of its own shares.
1995.chinese:
20世纪70年代初，戴维退休以后，经营GEICO的高管在估计赔款成本时犯下严重错误，导致保单定价过低，几乎让公司破产。直到1976年，杰克·伯恩出任首席执行官，采取大刀阔斧的补救措施，公司才得救。

我既相信杰克，也相信GEICO根本上的竞争实力，因此伯克希尔在1976年下半年大量买入该公司股份，之后又作了少量增持。到1980年末，我们累计投入4,570万美元，持有33.3%的股份。此后15年，我们没有再买。不过，因为GEICO大量回购自己的股票，我们的持股比例仍增长到约50%。

1995.english:
Then, in 1995, we agreed to pay $2.3 billion for the half of the company we didn't own.  That is a steep price.  But it gives us full ownership of a growing enterprise whose business remains exceptional for precisely the same reasons that prevailed in 1951.  In addition, GEICO has two extraordinary managers:  Tony Nicely, who runs the insurance side of the operation, and Lou Simpson, who runs investments.

Tony, 52, has been with GEICO for 34 years.  There's no one I would rather have managing GEICO's insurance operation.  He has brains, energy, integrity and focus.  If we're lucky, he'll stay another 34 years.
1995.chinese:
随后，在1995年，我们同意花23亿美元，买下尚未持有的另一半公司。这个价格不便宜。不过，我们由此完整拥有了一家仍在成长的企业；它的业务依然出类拔萃，原因与1951年一模一样。此外，GEICO还有两位非凡的经理人：托尼·奈斯利负责保险业务，卢·辛普森负责投资。

托尼52岁，已在GEICO工作34年。要我为GEICO保险业务挑一位负责人，没有谁比他更让我满意。他聪明、精力充沛、正直而专注。如果我们走运，希望他再干34年。

1995.english: Lou runs investments just as ably.  Between 1980 and 1995, the equities under Lou's management returned an average of 22.8% annually vs. 15.7% for the S&P.  Lou takes the same conservative, concentrated approach to investments that we do at Berkshire, and it is an enormous plus for us to have him on board.  One point that goes beyond Lou's GEICO work:  His presence on the scene assures us that Berkshire would have an extraordinary professional immediately available to handle its investments if something were to happen to Charlie and me.
1995.chinese: 卢管理投资，同样本领出众。1980—1995年，他管理的股票年均回报22.8%，同期标普指数为15.7%。他的投资方法，与我们在伯克希尔一样，审慎而集中。他能加入，对我们是极大的加分。还有一点，超出了他在GEICO的职责范围：有卢在，我们就知道，万一查理和我出了什么事，伯克希尔立刻就能找到一位非凡的专业人士，接手投资。

1995.english: GEICO, of course, must continue both to attract good policyholders and keep them happy.  It must also reserve and price properly.  But the ultimate key to the company's success is its rock-bottom operating costs, which virtually no competitor can match.  In 1995, moreover, Tony and his management team pushed underwriting and loss adjustment expenses down further to 23.6% of premiums, nearly one percentage point below 1994's ratio.  In business, I look for economic castles protected by unbreachable "moats."  Thanks to Tony and his management team, GEICO's moat widened in 1995.
1995.chinese: 当然，GEICO必须继续吸引优质投保人，并让他们满意；准备金也必须计提适当，保单也必须定价合理。不过，决定公司成功的根本关键，是低得不能再低、几乎没有对手能企及的经营成本。1995年，托尼和他的管理团队又把承保及理赔费用压低到保费的23.6%，比1994年下降近一个百分点。做生意，我寻找的是由无法攻破的“护城河”保护的经济城堡。多亏托尼和他的团队，GEICO的护城河在1995年又拓宽了。

1995.english:
Finally, let me bring you up to date on Davy.  He's now 93 and remains my friend and teacher.  He continues to pay close attention to GEICO and has always been there when the company's CEOs - Jack Byrne, Bill Snyder and Tony - have needed him.  Our acquisition of 100% of GEICO caused Davy to incur a large tax. Characteristically, he still warmly supported the transaction.

Davy has been one of my heroes for the 45 years I've known him, and he's never let me down.  You should understand that Berkshire would not be where it is today if Davy had not been so generous with his time on a cold Saturday in 1951.  I've often thanked him privately, but it is fitting that I use this report to thank him on behalf of Berkshire's shareholders.
1995.chinese:
最后，向各位介绍一下戴维的近况。他如今93岁，仍是我的朋友和老师。他一直密切关心GEICO；历任首席执行官——杰克·伯恩、比尔·斯奈德和托尼——需要他时，他总在那里。我们收购GEICO全部股权，使戴维要交一大笔税。可他仍然热情支持这笔交易，这正是他的为人。

相识45年来，戴维一直是我心目中的英雄之一，从未让我失望。各位应当知道，如果不是他在1951年那个寒冷的星期六，慷慨地拿出自己的时间，伯克希尔就不会有今天。我私下已多次谢过他，不过，借这份报告代表伯克希尔全体股东向他致谢，再合适不过。

1995.english:
## Insurance Operations

In addition to acquiring GEICO, we enjoyed other favorable developments in insurance during 1995.

As we've explained in past reports, what counts in our insurance business is, first, the amount of "float" we generate and, second, its cost to us.  Float is money we hold but don't own.  In an insurance operation, float arises because most policies require that premiums be prepaid and, more importantly, because it usually takes time for an insurer to hear about and resolve loss claims.
1995.chinese:
## 保险业务

除了收购GEICO，1995年，我们在保险业务方面还有其他可喜进展。

正如过去报告中解释过的，我们的保险业务，关键有两点：第一，产生多少“浮存金”；第二，这些钱的成本是多少。浮存金，是我们持有、却不属于我们的钱。保险业务之所以产生浮存金，是因为多数保单要求预付保费；更重要的是，保险公司通常需要过一段时间，才会获悉损失索赔，并最终处理完毕。

1995.english: Typically, the premiums that an insurer takes in do not cover the losses and expenses it must pay.  That leaves it running an "underwriting loss" - and that loss is the cost of float.  An insurance business is profitable over time if its cost of float is less than the cost the company would otherwise incur to obtain funds.  But the business has a negative value if the cost of its float is higher than market rates for money.
1995.chinese: 通常，保险公司收到的保费，不够支付必须承担的赔款与费用，于是便出现“承保亏损”；这项亏损，就是浮存金的成本。如果浮存金成本低于公司以其他方式筹资所需的成本，这门保险生意长期而言就能盈利；如果浮存金成本高于市场资金价格，这门生意的价值便是负的。

1995.english: As the numbers in the following table show, Berkshire's insurance business has been a huge winner.  For the table, we have calculated our float -  which we generate in exceptional amounts relative to our premium volume - by adding loss reserves, loss adjustment reserves, funds held under reinsurance assumed and unearned premium reserves, and then subtracting agents' balances, prepaid acquisition costs, prepaid taxes and deferred charges applicable to assumed reinsurance.  Our cost of float is determined by our underwriting loss or profit.  In those years when we have had an underwriting profit, such as the last three, our cost of float has been negative, which means we have calculated our insurance earnings by adding underwriting profit to float income.
1995.chinese: 下表数字说明，伯克希尔的保险业务是一大赢家。我们产生的浮存金，相对于保费收入而言，数量格外可观。表中的浮存金，计算方法是将赔款准备金、理赔费用准备金、分入再保险项下持有资金及未到期保费准备金相加，再减去代理人往来余额、预付业务获取成本、预付税款及与分入再保险有关的递延费用。浮存金成本由承保亏损或利润决定。像过去三年这样取得承保利润时，浮存金成本就是负数，也就是说，我们计算保险收益时，是把承保利润与浮存金的投资收入相加。

1995.english:
Since 1967, when we entered the insurance business, our float has grown at an annual compounded rate of 20.7%.  In more years than not, our cost of funds has been less than nothing.  This access to "free" money has boosted Berkshire's performance in a major way.

Any company's level of profitability is determined by three items:  (1) what its assets earn; (2) what its liabilities cost; and (3) its utilization of "leverage" - that is, the degree to which its assets are funded by liabilities rather than by equity. Over the years, we have done well on Point 1, having produced high returns on our assets.  But we have also benefitted greatly - to a degree that is not generally well-understood - because our liabilities have cost us very little.  An important reason for this low cost is that we have obtained float on very advantageous terms. The same cannot be said by many other property and casualty insurers, who may generate plenty of float, but at a cost that exceeds what the funds are worth to them.  In those circumstances, leverage becomes a disadvantage.
1995.chinese:
自1967年进入保险业以来，我们的浮存金年复合增长率为20.7%。多数年份，资金成本甚至比零还低。能够取得这种“免费”的钱，极大地提升了伯克希尔的业绩。

任何公司的盈利水平，都由三件事决定：（1）资产赚取多少收益；（2）负债付出多少成本；（3）怎样运用“杠杆”，也就是资产有多大程度靠负债、而非股东权益提供资金。多年来，第一点我们做得很好，资产取得了很高的回报。但我们也从负债成本极低这件事中获益甚大，获益之深，通常并没有得到充分理解。成本低的一个重要原因，就是我们以非常有利的条件取得了浮存金。许多其他财产及意外保险公司可不能这样说；它们或许产生大量浮存金，成本却超过了这些钱对它们的价值。这种情况下，杠杆就成了坏处。

1995.english: Since our float has cost us virtually nothing over the years, it has in effect served as equity.  Of course, it differs from true equity in that it doesn't belong to us.  Nevertheless, let's assume that instead of our having $3.4 billion of float at the end of 1994, we had replaced it with $3.4 billion of equity.  Under this scenario, we would have owned no more assets than we did during 1995.  We would, however, have had somewhat lower earnings because the cost of float was negative last year.  That is, our float threw off profits.  And, of course, to obtain the replacement equity, we would have needed to sell many new shares of Berkshire.  The net result - more shares, equal assets and lower earnings - would have materially reduced the value of our stock.  So you can understand why float wonderfully benefits a business - if it is obtained at a low cost.
1995.chinese: 多年来，我们的浮存金几乎没有成本，因此实际上起着股东权益的作用。当然，它与真正的股东权益不同：这些钱并不属于我们。尽管如此，不妨假设，1994年末我们没有那34亿美元浮存金，而是用34亿美元股东权益取而代之。这样，1995年我们拥有的资产不会比实际更多，利润却会略低，因为去年的浮存金成本是负的——也就是说，浮存金本身还产生了承保利润。而为了筹到替代的股东权益，我们当然得发行许多伯克希尔新股。净结果是：股数更多，资产相同，利润更低，我们每股股票的价值就会显著下降。所以，各位可以理解，浮存金若以低成本取得，对企业有多么大的好处。

1995.english:
Our acquisition of GEICO will immediately increase our float by nearly $3 billion, with additional growth almost certain.  We also expect GEICO to operate at a decent underwriting profit in most years, a fact that will increase the probability that our total float will cost us nothing.  Of course, we paid a very substantial price for the GEICO float, whereas virtually all of the gains in float depicted in the table were developed internally.

Our enthusiasm over 1995's insurance results must be tempered once again because we had our third straight year of good fortune in the super-cat business.  In this operation, we sell policies that insurance and reinsurance companies buy to protect themselves from the effects of mega-catastrophes.  Since truly major catastrophes occur infrequently, our super-cat business can be expected to show large profits in most years but occasionally to record a huge loss.  In other words, the attractiveness of our super-cat business will take many years to measure.  We know that the results of years like the past three will be at least partially offset by some truly terrible year in the future.  We just hope that "partially" turns out to be the proper adverb.
1995.chinese:
收购GEICO，会立即使我们的浮存金增加近30亿美元，之后继续增长几乎可以肯定。我们也预期，GEICO在多数年份能取得不错的承保利润，这又会增加我们全部浮存金零成本的可能性。当然，为了获得GEICO的浮存金，我们付出了相当高的价格；上表所列浮存金增长，则几乎全部来自内部发展。

对于1995年的保险成绩，我们又得给自己的热情降降温，因为超级巨灾业务已经连续第三年交了好运。我们在这项业务中出售保单，供保险及再保险公司抵御特大灾难的影响。真正重大的灾难很少发生，因此，我们的超级巨灾业务，预计多数年份会取得高额利润，偶尔却会出现巨额亏损。换句话说，这门生意究竟有多大吸引力，需要许多年才能衡量。我们知道，过去三年这样的成绩，至少有一部分会被未来某个糟糕透顶的年份抵消。只希望到时，“一部分”这三个字还用得上。

1995.english: There were plenty of catastrophes last year, but no super-cats of the insured variety.  The Southeast had a close call when Opal, sporting winds of 150 miles per hour, hovered off Florida. However, the storm abated before hitting land, and so a second Andrew was dodged.  For insurers, the Kobe earthquake was another close call:  The economic damage was huge - perhaps even a record - but only a tiny portion of it was insured.  The insurance industry won't always be that lucky.
1995.chinese: 去年灾难不少，但就承保损失而言，并没有出现超级巨灾。“奥帕尔”飓风以每小时150英里的风速在佛罗里达州近海盘旋时，美国东南部着实险了一回。不过，风暴登陆前减弱，第二场“安德鲁”就这样躲过去了。对保险公司来说，神户地震又是一次擦肩而过：经济损失极为巨大，甚至可能创了纪录，但投保的只占极小一部分。保险业不会永远这么幸运。

1995.english: Ajit Jain is the guiding genius of our super-cat business and writes important non-cat business as well. In insurance, the term "catastrophe" is applied to an event, such as a hurricane or earthquake, that causes a great many insured losses. The other deals Ajit enters into usually cover only a single large loss. A simplified description of three transactions from last year will illustrate both what I mean and Ajit's versatility. We insured: (1) The life of Mike Tyson for a sum that is large initially and that, fight-by-fight, gradually declines to zero over the next few years; (2) Lloyd's against more than 225 of its "names" dying during the year; and (3) The launch, and a year of orbit, of two Chinese satellites. Happily, both satellites are orbiting, the Lloyd's folk avoided abnormal mortality, and if Mike Tyson looked any healthier, no one would get in the ring with him.
1995.chinese: 阿吉特·贾因是我们超级巨灾业务的掌舵天才，也承保重要的非巨灾业务。在保险业，“巨灾”指飓风或地震等造成大量承保损失的事件。阿吉特承接的其他交易，通常只承保单一的大额损失。把去年三笔交易简化说明一下，就能看出我的意思，也能看出阿吉特的多才多艺。我们承保了：（1）迈克·泰森的寿险，最初保额很高，随后几年每打一场拳赛，保额便逐步降低，直到零；（2）劳合社一年内死亡的个人承保成员超过225人的风险；（3）两颗中国卫星的发射及在轨运行一年。可喜的是，两颗卫星都在轨道上，劳合社成员没有出现异常死亡，而迈克·泰森若再健康一点，恐怕就没人敢与他同上拳台了。

1995.english: Berkshire is sought out for many kinds of insurance, both super-cat and large single-risk, because: (1) our financial strength is unmatched, and insureds know we can and will pay our losses under the most adverse of circumstances; (2) we can supply a quote faster than anyone in the business; and (3) we will issue policies with limits larger than anyone else is prepared to write. Most of our competitors have extensive reinsurance treaties and lay off much of their business.  While this helps them avoid shock losses, it also hurts their flexibility and reaction time.  As you know, Berkshire moves quickly to seize investment and acquisition opportunities; in insurance we respond with the same exceptional speed.  In another important point, large coverages don't frighten us but, on the contrary, intensify our interest.  We have offered a policy under which we could have lost $1 billion; the largest coverage that a client accepted was $400 million.
1995.chinese: 许多超级巨灾及单一大额风险的保险业务，会找上伯克希尔，原因有三：（1）我们的财力无人可比，被保险人知道，即便在最恶劣的情况下，我们也有能力、而且一定会履行赔付义务；（2）我们报价比同行任何人都快；（3）我们愿意签发的保单限额，比任何其他人愿意承接的都大。多数竞争对手订有大量再保险协议，把相当多业务转分出去。这虽能帮助它们躲开突发巨额损失，却也损害了灵活性与反应速度。各位知道，伯克希尔抓投资与收购机会，行动很快；做保险，我们也有同样非同寻常的速度。还有一点很重要：大额保障不会吓退我们，反而更能引起我们的兴趣。我们曾提出过一张可能使自己损失10亿美元的保单；客户实际接受的最大保障额，是4亿美元。

1995.english: We will get hit from time to time with large losses.  Charlie and I, however, are quite willing to accept relatively volatile results in exchange for better long-term earnings than we would otherwise have had.  In other words, we prefer a lumpy 15% to a smooth 12%.  Since most managers opt for smoothness, we are left with a competitive advantage that we try to maximize.  We do, though, monitor our aggregate exposure in order to keep our "worst case" at a level that leaves us comfortable.
1995.chinese: 我们时不时会遭受巨额损失。不过，查理和我很愿意接受相对起伏较大的业绩，换取高于其他做法的长期利润。换句话说，我们宁愿要磕磕绊绊的15%，也不要平平稳稳的12%。多数经理人都选择平稳，这就给我们留下了一项竞争优势，我们努力把它发挥到最大。不过，我们会监控总体风险敞口，使“最坏情形”保持在自己能安心接受的水平。

1995.english: Indeed, our worst case from a "once-in-a-century" super-cat is far less severe - relative to net worth - than that faced by many well-known primary companies writing great numbers of property policies.  These insurers don't issue single huge-limit policies as we do, but their small policies, in aggregate, can create a risk of staggering size.  The "big one" would blow right through the reinsurance covers of some of these insurers, exposing them to uncapped losses that could threaten their survival.  In our case, losses would be large, but capped at levels we could easily handle.
1995.chinese: 事实上，面对“百年一遇”的超级巨灾，以净资产为比较基准，我们的最坏情形，远轻于许多承保大量财产险保单的知名原保险公司。这些公司不像我们那样签发单张限额巨大的保单，但小保单加在一起，风险规模可能惊人。真正的“大灾”一来，会直接冲破其中一些公司的再保险保障，使它们暴露在没有上限、足以威胁生存的损失之下。我们的损失也会很大，但有上限，而且在轻松可以应付的范围内。

1995.english: Prices are weakening in the super-cat field.  That is understandable considering the influx of capital into the reinsurance business a few years ago and the natural desire of those holding the capital to employ it.  No matter what others may do, we will not knowingly write business at inadequate rates.  We unwittingly did this in the early 1970's and, after more than 20 years, regularly receive significant bills stemming from the mistakes of that era.  My guess is that we will still be getting surprises from that business 20 years from now.  A bad reinsurance contract is like hell:  easy to enter and impossible to exit.
1995.chinese: 超级巨灾领域的价格正在走弱。几年前大批资本涌入再保险业，拿着资本的人又自然想把钱用出去，价格走弱不难理解。不管别人怎么做，我们都不会明知费率不足，仍去承保。20世纪70年代初，我们曾在不知不觉中干过这种事；二十多年过去了，那时的错误，仍定期给我们送来金额可观的账单。我猜，再过20年，那批业务还会带来意外。糟糕的再保险合同就像地狱：进去容易，出来无门。

1995.english: I actively participated in those early reinsurance decisions, and Berkshire paid a heavy tuition for my education in the business.  Unfortunately, reinsurance students can't attend school on scholarship.  GEICO, incidentally, suffered a similar, disastrous experience in the early 1980's, when it plunged enthusiastically into the writing of reinsurance and large risks. GEICO's folly was brief, but it will be cleaning things up for at least another decade.  The well-publicized problems at Lloyd's further illustrate the perils of reinsurance and also underscore how vital it is that the interests of the people who write insurance business be aligned - on the downside as well as the upside - with those of the people putting up the capital.
