When that kind of symmetry is missing, insurers almost invariably run into trouble, though its existence may remain hidden for some time.
1995.chinese: 早年的那些再保险决策，我积极参与过；为了让我学会这门生意，伯克希尔付了昂贵的学费。遗憾的是，再保险学生可拿不到奖学金。顺便说一句，GEICO在20世纪80年代初，也经历过类似的灾难：它曾热情高涨地一头扎进再保险与大额风险承保业务。GEICO犯傻的时间虽短，清理后果却至少还要再花十年。劳合社广为人知的麻烦，进一步说明了再保险的危险，也凸显出一件事有多重要：承保业务的人，与出资本的人，利益必须一致；赚钱时如此，亏钱时也如此。少了这种对称，保险公司几乎必然会出问题，尽管问题可能藏上一阵子才露面。

1995.english: A small, apocryphal story about an insurance CEO who was visited by an analyst tells a lot about this industry.  To the analyst's questions about his business, the CEO had nothing but gloomy answers:  Rates were ridiculously low; the reserves on his balance sheet weren't adequate for ordinary claims, much less those likely to arise from asbestos and environmental problems; most of his reinsurers had long since gone broke, leaving him holding the sack.  But then the CEO brightened:  "Still, things could be a lot worse," he said.  "It could be my money."  At Berkshire, it's our money.
1995.chinese: 有个未经证实的小故事：一位分析师拜访保险公司首席执行官。故事对这个行业很有说明力。分析师问起业务，那位首席执行官的回答无不灰暗：费率低得荒唐；资产负债表上的准备金，连普通索赔都不够付，更别提石棉与环境问题可能带来的索赔；他的大多数再保险人早已破产，烂摊子全落在自己手里。说着说着，他却精神起来：“不过，情况还可能糟得多呢，”他说，“要是赔的是我自己的钱，那才叫惨。”在伯克希尔，赔的就是我们自己的钱。

1995.english: Berkshire's other insurance operations, though relatively small, performed magnificently in 1995.  National Indemnity's traditional business had a combined ratio of 84.2 and developed, as usual, a large amount of float compared to premium volume.  Over the last three years, this segment of our business, run by Don Wurster, has had an average combined ratio of 85.6.  Our homestate operation, managed by Rod Eldred, grew at a good rate in 1995 and achieved a combined ratio of 81.4.  Its three-year combined ratio is an amazing 82.4.  Berkshire's California workers' compensation business, run by Brad Kinstler, faced fierce price-cutting in 1995 and lost a great many renewals when we refused to accept inadequate rates.  Though this operation's volume dropped materially, it produced an excellent underwriting profit.  Finally, John Kizer, at Central States Indemnity, continues to do an extraordinary job. His premium volume was up 23% in 1995, and underwriting profit grew by 59%.  Ajit, Don, Rod, Brad and John are all under 45, an embarrassing fact demolishing my theory that managers only hit their stride after they reach 70.
1995.chinese: 伯克希尔的其他保险业务虽然相对较小，1995年表现却极为出色。国民赔偿公司的传统业务，综合成本率为84.2，照例相对于保费收入产生了大量浮存金。唐·沃斯特经营的这部分业务，过去三年平均综合成本率为85.6。罗德·埃尔德雷德管理的本州保险业务，1995年增长良好，综合成本率为81.4，三年综合成本率更达到惊人的82.4。布拉德·金斯特勒负责的加利福尼亚工伤赔偿保险业务，1995年遭遇激烈削价竞争；我们拒绝接受不足的费率，因此失去了许多续保。业务量虽大幅下滑，承保利润却非常出色。最后，中央州赔偿公司的约翰·基泽，继续干得非凡：1995年保费收入增长23%，承保利润增长59%。阿吉特、唐、罗德、布拉德和约翰，全都不到45岁。真让人尴尬，他们把我的理论彻底推翻了——我原以为，经理人要过了70岁，才真正进入状态。

1995.english:
To sum up, we entered 1995 with an exceptional insurance operation of moderate size.  By adding GEICO, we entered 1996 with a business still better in quality, much improved in its growth prospects, and doubled in size.  More than ever, insurance is our core strength.

## Sources of Reported Earnings

The table below shows the main sources of Berkshire's reported earnings.  In this presentation, purchase-premium charges are not assigned to the specific businesses to which they apply, but are instead aggregated and shown separately.  This procedure lets you view the earnings of our businesses as they would have been reported had we not purchased them.  This form of presentation seems to us to be more useful to investors and managers than one utilizing GAAP, which requires purchase-premiums to be charged off, business-by-business.  The total earnings we show in the table are, of course, identical to the GAAP total in our audited financial statements.
1995.chinese:
总的来说，步入1995年时，我们拥有一项规模中等、品质非凡的保险业务。加上GEICO以后，步入1996年时，这项业务的品质更上一层，增长前景大为改善，规模也翻了一番。保险，如今比以往任何时候都更是我们的核心实力。

## 报表利润来源

下表列出伯克希尔报表利润的主要来源。列示时，收购溢价费用没有分配到对应的各项业务，而是汇总后单列。这样，各位看到的业务利润，就相当于假设我们从未收购过它们时，它们各自会报告的利润。美国公认会计原则（GAAP）要求逐项业务扣除收购溢价费用；相比之下，我们认为这里的列示方法，对投资者和管理者更有用。当然，表中的利润总额，与经审计财务报表中的GAAP总额完全一致。

1995.english:
(1) Includes R.C. Willey from June 29, 1995. (2) Includes Helzberg's from April 30, 1995. (3) Jewelry earnings were included in "Other" in 1994. (4) Excludes interest expense of Finance Businesses.

A large amount of information about these businesses is given on pages 41-52, where you will also find our segment earnings reported on a GAAP basis.  In addition, on pages 57-63, we have rearranged Berkshire's financial data into four segments on a non- GAAP basis, a presentation that corresponds to the way Charlie and I think about the company.  Our intent is to supply you with the financial information that we would wish you to give us if our positions were reversed.
1995.chinese:
（1）自1995年6月29日起包括R.C.威利。

（2）自1995年4月30日起包括赫尔茨伯格。

（3）1994年的珠宝业务利润列入“其他”。

（4）不包括金融业务的利息费用。

有关这些业务的大量资料，见第41—52页，那里也列示按GAAP计算的分部利润。此外，第57—63页按照非GAAP口径，将伯克希尔的财务数据重新分为四个部分，列示方式与查理和我思考公司时采用的方式一致。我们的用意，是把立场对调时，我们希望各位提供给我们的那些财务资料，提供给各位。

1995.english: At Berkshire, we believe in Charlie's dictum - "Just tell me the bad news; the good news will take care of itself" - and that is the behavior we expect of our managers when they are reporting to us.  Consequently, I also owe you - Berkshire's owners - a report on three operations that, though they continued to earn decent (or better) returns on invested capital, experienced a decline in earnings last year.  Each encountered a different type of problem.
1995.chinese: 在伯克希尔，我们信奉查理的格言：“只管把坏消息告诉我，好消息会自己照顾自己。”经理人向我们汇报时，我们期待的正是这种做法。因此，我也欠各位——伯克希尔的所有者——一份报告，说明三项业务的情况：尽管它们的投入资本回报依然不错，甚至很好，去年的利润却下降了。每项业务遇到的问题，各不相同。

1995.english: Our shoe business operated in an industry that suffered depressed earnings throughout last year, and many of our competitors made only marginal profits or worse.  That means we at least maintained, and in some instances widened, our competitive superiority.  So I have no doubt that our shoe operations will climb back to top-grade earnings in the future.  In other words, though the turn has not yet occurred, we believe you should view last year's figures as reflecting a cyclical problem, not a secular one.
1995.chinese: 我们的鞋业，所在行业去年全年利润低迷；许多竞争对手只有微利，甚至更糟。这意味着，我们至少保持了竞争优势，有些方面还扩大了优势。因此，我毫不怀疑，我们的鞋业今后会重新取得一流的盈利成绩。换句话说，虽然转机尚未到来，但我们认为，各位应把去年数字看作周期性问题的反映，而非长期趋势出了问题。

1995.english: The Buffalo News, though still doing very well in comparison to other newspapers, is another story.  In this case, industry trends are not good.  In the 1991 Annual Report, I explained that newspapers had lost a notch in their economic attractiveness from the days when they appeared to have a bullet-proof franchise. Today, the industry retains its excellent economics, but has lost still another notch.  Over time, we expect the competitive strength of newspapers to gradually erode, though the industry should nevertheless remain a fine business for many years to come.
1995.chinese: 《布法罗新闻报》则是另一回事，尽管与其他报纸相比，它的表现仍然很好。这一行业的趋势并不理想。在1991年年报里，我解释过，与看上去拥有刀枪不入的特许经营优势的那些年相比，报纸在经济吸引力上已降了一档。如今，行业经济特性依然优良，却又降了一档。随着时间推移，我们预期报纸的竞争实力会逐渐削弱，尽管在未来许多年里，这一行业仍应是一门好生意。

1995.english: Berkshire's most difficult problem is World Book, which operates in an industry beset by increasingly tough competition from CD-ROM and on-line offerings.  True, we are still profitable, a claim that perhaps no other print encyclopedia can make.  But our sales and earnings trends have gone in the wrong direction.  At the end of 1995, World Book made major changes in the way it distributes its product, stepped up its efforts with electronic products and sharply reduced its overhead costs.  It will take time for us to evaluate the effects of these initiatives, but we are confident they will significantly improve our viability.
1995.chinese: 伯克希尔最棘手的问题，是世界图书。它所在的行业，正面对CD-ROM光盘及在线产品日益激烈的竞争。确实，我们仍有利润，这一点也许没有其他纸质百科全书能做到；但销售额与利润的趋势，都走错了方向。1995年末，世界图书大幅改变了产品分销方式，加强电子产品方面的努力，并大幅削减管理费用。评估这些措施的效果还需要时间，但我们相信，它们会显著增强公司的生存能力。

1995.english:
All of our operations, including those whose earnings fell last year, benefit from exceptionally talented and dedicated managers.  Were we to have the choice of any other executives now working in their industries, there is not one of our managers we would replace.

Many of our managers don't have to work for a living, but simply go out and perform every day for the same reason that wealthy golfers stay on the tour:  They love both doing what they do and doing it well.  To describe them as working may be a misnomer - they simply prefer spending much of their time on a productive activity at which they excel to spending it on leisure activities.  Our job is to provide an environment that will keep them feeling this way, and so far we seem to have succeeded: Thinking back over the 1965-95 period, I can't recall that a single key manager has left Berkshire to join another employer.
1995.chinese:
我们全部业务，包括去年利润下降的那些，都受益于才能非凡、尽心尽力的管理者。即使能任意挑选各自行业里目前任职的其他高管，我们也不会替换现有经理人中的任何一位。

我们的许多经理人，并不需要靠工作谋生。他们每天照常上场，原因与富有的高尔夫球手仍坚持巡回赛一样：他们既喜欢自己做的事，也喜欢把事情做好。说他们是在“工作”，或许都不太恰当；他们不过是更愿意把大部分时间，花在自己擅长、又有产出的活动上，而不是休闲活动上。我们的工作，就是提供一个环境，让他们一直保持这种感觉。到目前为止，我们似乎成功了：回想1965—1995年，我想不起有哪一位关键经理人，曾离开伯克希尔去替另一个雇主工作。

We continue in our Rip Van Winkle mode:  Five of our six top positions at yearend 1994 were left untouched during 1995.  The sixth was American Express, in which we increased our ownership to about 10%.

1995.chinese:
我们继续维持“里普·范·温克尔”式的长睡不动：1994年末最大的六项持仓，有五项在1995年原封未动。第六项是美国运通，我们把持股比例提高到了约10%。

1996年初，两件大事改变了我们的持仓。第一，我们买下此前尚未持有的GEICO股票，使它成为全资子公司。第二，我们用大都会的股份，换取了现金与迪士尼股票的组合。

1995.english: In the Disney merger, Cap Cities shareholders had a choice of actions.  If they chose, they could exchange each of their Cap Cities shares for one share of Disney stock plus $65.  Or they could ask for - though not necessarily get - all cash or all stock, with their ultimate allotment of each depending on the choices made by other shareholders and certain decisions made by Disney.  For our 20 million shares, we sought stock, but do not know, as this report goes to press, how much we were allocated.  We are certain, however, to receive something over 20 million Disney shares.  We have also recently bought Disney stock in the market.
1995.chinese: 在与迪士尼合并的交易中，大都会股东有几种选择。如果愿意，每股大都会股票可以换一股迪士尼股票，外加65美元；也可以申请全部收取现金或全部收取股票，但未必如愿。最后分到多少现金、多少股票，要取决于其他股东的选择，以及迪士尼作出的某些决定。对于我们持有的2,000万股，我们申请收取股票；不过，本报告付印时，还不知道最终分配了多少。但可以肯定的是，我们将收到略多于2,000万股迪士尼股票。最近，我们还在市场上买进了迪士尼股票。

1995.english:
One more bit of history:  I first became interested in Disney in 1966, when its market valuation was less than $90 million, even though the company had earned around $21 million pre-tax in 1965 and was sitting with more cash than debt.  At Disneyland, the $17 million Pirates of the Caribbean ride would soon open.  Imagine my excitement - a company selling at only five times rides!

Duly impressed, Buffett Partnership Ltd. bought a significant amount of Disney stock at a split-adjusted price of 31¢ per share. That decision may appear brilliant, given that the stock now sells for $66.  But your Chairman was up to the task of nullifying it: In 1967 I sold out at 48¢ per share.
1995.chinese:
再讲一段历史：1966年，我第一次对迪士尼产生兴趣。那时，公司总市值不到9,000万美元，尽管1965年税前利润约为2,100万美元，而且账上现金比债务还多。迪士尼乐园里，耗资1,700万美元的“加勒比海盗”游乐项目即将开放。想想我有多兴奋——整家公司，居然只卖五个游乐项目的价钱！

深受打动后，巴菲特合伙企业有限公司大量买入迪士尼股票，按拆股调整后的价格计算，每股31美分。如今股价66美元，这个决定看上去或许英明得很。不过，各位的董事长完全有本领把英明化为乌有：1967年，我以每股48美分全卖了。

1995.english:
Oh well - we're happy to be once again a large owner of a business with both unique assets and outstanding management.

## 可转换优先股

许多股东还记得，1987—1991年期间，伯克希尔曾通过非公开交易买入五项可转换优先股。现在似乎正适合谈谈它们的近况。具体如下：

| 公司 | 股息率 | 购入年份 | 成本（百万美元） | 市值或相应所得（百万美元） |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 冠军国际公司 | 9¼% | 1989 | 300 | 388（1） |
| 第一帝国州公司 | 9% | 1991 | 40 | 110 |
| 吉列公司 | 8¾% | 1989 | 600 | 2,502（2） |
| 所罗门公司 | 9% | 1987 | 700 | 728（3） |
| USAir集团 | 9¼% | 1989 | 358 | 215 |

1995.english:
(1) Proceeds from sale of common we received through conversion in 1995. (2) 12/31/95 value of common we received through conversion in 1991. (3) Includes $140 we received in 1995 from partial redemption.

In each case we had the option of sticking with these preferreds as fixed-income securities or converting them into common stock.  Initially, their value to us came primarily from their fixed-income characteristics.  The option we had to convert was a kicker.

Our $300 million private purchase of American Express "Percs" - described in the 1991 Annual Report - is not included in the table because that security was a modified form of common stock whose fixed-income characteristics contributed only a minor portion of its initial value.  Three years after we bought them, the Percs automatically were converted to common stock.  In contrast, the five securities in the table were set to become common stocks only if we wished them to - a crucial difference.
1995.chinese:
（1）1995年转换取得普通股后，出售普通股所得。

（2）1991年转换取得的普通股，在1995年12月31日的价值。

（3）包括1995年部分赎回时，我们收到的1.40亿美元。

每项投资，我们都可以选择继续把优先股作为固定收益证券持有，也可以转换为普通股。最初，它们对我们的价值，主要来自固定收益特征；转换权则是额外的甜头。

表中没有列入我们以3亿美元非公开买入的美国运通“PERCS”——1991年年报里介绍过——因为那种证券，是一种变形的普通股，固定收益特征只占其最初价值的一小部分。买入三年后，PERCS自动转换为普通股。相反，表中五项证券，只有在我们愿意时才会变成普通股，这个区别至关重要。

1995.english: When we purchased our convertible securities, I told you that we expected to earn after-tax returns from them that "moderately" exceeded what we could earn from the medium-term fixed-income securities they replaced.  We beat this expectation - but only because of the performance of a single issue.  I also told you that these securities, as a group, would "not produce the returns we can achieve when we find a business with wonderful economic prospects." Unfortunately, that prediction was fulfilled.  Finally, I said that "under almost any conditions, we expect these preferreds to return us our money plus dividends."  That's one I would like to have back.  Winston Churchill once said that "eating my words has never given me indigestion."  My assertion, however, that it was almost impossible for us to lose money on our preferreds has caused me some well-deserved heartburn.
1995.chinese: 买入这些可转换证券时，我告诉过各位，我们预期其税后回报，将“适度”高于被它们替代的中期固定收益证券。我们超过了这个预期，但完全靠其中一项投资的表现。我还说过，把这些证券作为一个整体来看，其回报“达不到我们找到一家经济前景极佳的企业时能够取得的回报”。遗憾的是，这个预测兑现了。最后，我还说：“几乎在任何情况下，我们都预期这些优先股会把本金连同股息还给我们。”这一句，我倒真想收回来。温斯顿·丘吉尔曾说：“把自己说过的话吞回去，从来没让我消化不良。”然而，我断言这些优先股几乎不可能让我们赔钱，确实让我尝到了活该的烧心滋味。

1995.english:
Our best holding has been Gillette, which we told you from the start was a superior business.  Ironically, though, this is also the purchase in which I made my biggest mistake - of a kind, however, never recognized on financial statements.

We paid $600 million in 1989 for Gillette preferred shares that were convertible into 48 million (split-adjusted) common shares.  Taking an alternative route with the $600 million, I probably could have purchased 60 million shares of common from the company.  The market on the common was then about $10.50, and given that this would have been a huge private placement carrying important restrictions, I probably could have bought the stock at a discount of at least 5%.  I can't be sure about this, but it's likely that Gillette's management would have been just as happy to have Berkshire opt for common.
1995.chinese:
表现最好的是吉列，我们从一开始就告诉各位，它是一家出众的企业。讽刺的是，我最大的错误，也恰恰出在这笔投资上；不过，那是一种永远不会在财务报表中确认的错误。

1989年，我们花6亿美元买入吉列优先股，可转换为4,800万股普通股，股数已按拆股调整。如果拿这6亿美元走另一条路，我很可能可以直接向公司买下6,000万股普通股。当时普通股市价约10.50美元；考虑到这将是一笔附带重要限制的大规模私募，我大概至少能拿到5%的折扣。这一点我不能确定，但吉列管理层很可能同样乐于让伯克希尔选择普通股。

1995.english: But I was far too clever to do that.  Instead, for less than two years, we received some extra dividend income (the difference between the preferred's yield and that of the common), at which point the company - quite properly - called the issue, moving to do that as quickly as was possible.  If I had negotiated for common rather than preferred, we would have been better off at yearend 1995 by $625 million, minus the "excess" dividends of about $70 million.
1995.chinese: 可惜，我聪明得很，怎么肯那么干。结果，我们只多收了不到两年的股息——优先股收益率与普通股收益率之差——公司就立即在允许的最早时点，完全合情合理地赎回了这批证券。如果当初谈的是普通股，而非优先股，到1995年末，我们本可多出6.25亿美元，再减去约7,000万美元的“额外”股息。

1995.english:
In the case of Champion, the ability of the company to call our preferred at 115% of cost forced a move out of us last August that we would rather have delayed.  In this instance, we converted our shares just prior to the pending call and offered them to the company at a modest discount.

Charlie and I have never had a conviction about the paper industry - actually, I can't remember ever owning the common stock of a paper producer in my 54 years of investing - so our choice in August was whether to sell in the market or to the company. Champion's management had always been candid and honorable in dealing with us and wished to repurchase common shares, so we offered our stock to the company.  Our Champion capital gain was moderate - about 19% after tax from a six-year investment - but the preferred delivered us a good after-tax dividend yield throughout our holding period.  (That said, many press accounts have overstated the after-tax yields earned by property-casualty insurance companies on dividends paid to them.  What the press has failed to take into account is a change in the tax law that took effect in 1987 and that significantly reduced the dividends received credit applicable to insurers.  For details, see our 1986 Annual Report.)
1995.chinese:
冠军国际的情况是，公司有权按成本的115%赎回我们的优先股，这迫使我们在去年8月采取了一项原本更愿意推迟的行动。我们赶在即将赎回之前转换股份，再以小幅折价，把普通股出售给公司。

查理和我，对造纸业从来没有形成过坚定的投资判断。事实上，投资54年来，我想不起自己曾持有过哪家造纸企业的普通股。因此，8月时，我们的选择只是在市场卖，还是卖给公司。冠军国际管理层与我们打交道，一直坦诚、守信，又有回购普通股的意愿，所以我们把股票提供给了公司。这笔六年投资的税后资本利得约19%，算是温和；不过，在整个持有期里，优先股一直给我们带来不错的税后股息收益率。（话虽如此，许多新闻报道，夸大了财产及意外保险公司收取股息时取得的税后收益率。报道没有考虑到，1987年生效的一项税法变更，大幅降低了适用于保险公司的股息收入税收优惠。详情见1986年年报。）

1995.english:
Our First Empire preferred will be called on March 31, 1996, the earliest date allowable.  We are comfortable owning stock in well-run banks, and we will convert and keep our First Empire common shares.  Bob Wilmers, CEO of the company, is an outstanding banker, and we love being associated with him.

Our other two preferreds have been disappointing, though the Salomon preferred has modestly outperformed the fixed-income securities for which it was a substitute.  However, the amount of management time Charlie and I have devoted to this holding has been vastly greater than its economic significance to Berkshire. Certainly I never dreamed I would take a new job at age 60 - Salomon interim chairman, that is - because of an earlier purchase of a fixed-income security.
1995.chinese:
第一帝国州优先股将在1996年3月31日，也就是允许的最早日期，被赎回。持有经营良好的银行股票，我们很安心，因此会转换为第一帝国州普通股，并继续持有。公司首席执行官鲍勃·威尔默斯，是一位出色的银行家，能与他合作，我们很高兴。

另外两项优先股投资则令人失望，尽管所罗门优先股的表现，略好于被它替代的固定收益证券。不过，查理和我花在这项持仓上的管理时间，与它对伯克希尔的经济意义相比，实在多得太不成比例。我当然从没做梦想到，早先买了一项固定收益证券，竟会让我60岁又换一份新工作——也就是所罗门临时董事长。

1995.english:
Soon after our purchase of the Salomon preferred in 1987, I wrote that I had "no special insights regarding the direction or future profitability of investment banking."  Even the most charitable commentator would conclude that I have since proved my point.

To date, our option to convert into Salomon common has not proven of value.  Furthermore, the Dow Industrials have doubled since I committed to buy the preferred, and the brokerage group has performed equally as well.  That means my decision to go with Salomon because I saw value in the conversion option must be graded as very poor.  Even so, the preferred has continued under some trying conditions to deliver as a fixed-income security, and the 9% dividend is currently quite attractive.
1995.chinese:
1987年买入所罗门优先股后不久，我写道，自己“对投资银行业的走向或未来盈利能力，并无特别见解”。即使最宽厚的评论者，也只能承认，此后的事实充分证明了我这句话。

到目前为止，转换为所罗门普通股的权利，并未显示出价值。而自我承诺买入优先股以来，道琼斯工业指数已经翻倍，券商板块表现也同样好。这意味着，我因为看中转换权价值而选择所罗门的决定，必须打一个很差的分数。即便如此，在一些艰难环境下，这项优先股仍持续履行了固定收益证券的功能，目前9%的股息率，也相当有吸引力。

1995.english: Unless the preferred is converted, its terms require redemption of 20% of the issue on October 31 of each year, 1995-99, and $140 million of our original $700 million was taken on schedule last year.  (Some press reports labeled this a sale, but a senior security that matures is not "sold.")  Though we did not elect to convert the preferred that matured last year, we have four more bites at the conversion apple, and I believe it quite likely that we will yet find value in our right to convert.
1995.chinese: 除非转换为普通股，否则按条款，1995—1999年每年10月31日，都要赎回发行总额的20%。去年，我们最初投入的7亿美元，已有1.40亿美元如期收回。（一些新闻报道把这称为出售，但优先证券到期，并不叫“卖掉”。）虽然去年到期的优先股，我们没有选择转换，不过，转换这只苹果，我们还有四次下嘴的机会。我相信，最终从转换权中找到价值，可能性相当大。

1995.english: I discussed the USAir investment at length in last year's report.  The company's results improved in 1995, but it still faces significant problems.  On the plus side for us is the fact that our preferred is structurally well-designed:  For example, though we have not been paid dividends since June 1994, the amounts owed us are compounding at 5% over the prime rate.  On the minus side is the fact that we are dealing with a weak credit.
1995.chinese: 去年报告里，我已经详细讨论过USAir投资。1995年，公司业绩改善，但仍面临重大问题。对我们有利的一面，是这项优先股的条款结构设计得不错。例如，自1994年6月以来，我们虽未收到股息，但欠付金额，按最优惠贷款利率加5个百分点的利率复利累积。不利的一面，则是我们面对的，是一个信用薄弱的债务人。

1995.english: We feel much better about our USAir preferred than we did a year ago, but your guess is as good as mine as to its ultimate value.  (Indeed, considering my record with this investment, it's fair to say that your guess may be better than mine.)  At yearend we carried our preferred (in which there is no public market) at 60% of par, though USAir also has outstanding a junior preferred that is significantly inferior to ours in all respects except conversion price and that was then trading at 82% of par.  As I write this, the junior issue has advanced to 97% of par.  Let's hope the market is right.
1995.chinese: 如今，对于USAir优先股，我们的感觉比一年前好得多；不过，它最终值多少，各位的猜测，与我的一样有准头。（事实上，考虑到我在这项投资上的纪录，说各位可能比我猜得准，也是公道的。）年末，我们把这项没有公开交易市场的优先股，按面值的60%列账。与此同时，USAir另有一项在转换价格以外、各方面都明显逊于我们的次级优先股，当时却以面值82%的价格交易。写这封信时，那项次级证券已涨至面值的97%。但愿市场是对的。

1995.english:
Overall, our preferreds have performed well, but that is true only because of one huge winner, Gillette.  Leaving aside Gillette, our preferreds as a group have delivered us after-tax returns no more than equal to those we could have earned from the medium-term fixed-income issues that they replaced.

## A Proposed Recapitalization

At the Annual Meeting you will be asked to approve a recapitalization of Berkshire, creating two classes of stock.  If the plan is adopted, our existing common stock will be designated as Class A Common Stock and a new Class B Common Stock will be authorized.
1995.chinese:
总体而言，我们的优先股表现不错，但完全靠一个大赢家——吉列。剔除吉列以后，其余优先股合在一起，税后回报充其量只相当于被它们替代的中期固定收益证券。

## 拟议的股本重组

股东大会上，将请各位批准伯克希尔的股本重组，设立两类股票。如果方案通过，现有普通股将被定为A类普通股，同时授权发行新的B类普通股。

1995.english:
Each share of the "B" will have the rights of 1/30th of an "A" share with these exceptions:  First, a B share will have 1/200th of the vote of an A share (rather than 1/30th of the vote).  Second, the B will not be eligible to participate in Berkshire's shareholder-designated charitable contributions program.

When the recapitalization is complete, each share of A will become convertible, at the holder's option and at any time, into 30 shares of B.  This conversion privilege will not extend in the opposite direction.  That is, holders of B shares will not be able to convert them into A shares.
1995.chinese:
每股B类股，将享有每股A类股三十分之一的权利，但有两项例外。第一，每股B类股的投票权，为每股A类股的二百分之一，而非三十分之一。第二，B类股不能参与伯克希尔的股东指定慈善捐款计划。

股本重组完成后，每股A类股的持有人，都可以自行选择在任何时候，将其转换为30股B类股。反方向则没有这种转换权，也就是说，B类股持有人不能把股票转换为A类股。

1995.english:
We expect to list the B shares on the New York Stock Exchange, where they will trade alongside the A stock.  To create the shareholder base necessary for a listing - and to ensure a liquid market in the B stock - Berkshire expects to make a public offering for cash of at least $100 million of new B shares.  The offering will be made only by means of a prospectus.

The market will ultimately determine the price of the B shares.  Their price, though, should be in the neighborhood of 1/30th of the price of the A shares.
1995.chinese:
我们预期，B类股会在纽约证券交易所上市，与A类股并行交易。为建立上市所需的股东基础，并确保B类股市场具有流动性，伯克希尔预计将公开发行至少1亿美元的新B类股，收取现金。发行只会通过招股说明书进行。

B类股的价格，最终由市场决定。不过，它的价格应当在A类股的三十分之一附近。

1995.english:
Class A shareholders who wish to give gifts may find it convenient to convert a share or two of their stock into Class B shares.  Additionally, arbitrage-related conversions will occur if demand for the B is strong enough to push its price to slightly above 1/30th of the price of A.

However, because the Class A stock will entitle its holders to full voting rights and access to Berkshire's contributions program, these shares will be superior to the Class B shares and we would expect most shareholders to remain holders of the Class A - which is precisely what the Buffett and Munger families plan to do, except in those instances when we ourselves might convert a few shares to facilitate gifts.  The prospect that most shareholders will stick to the A stock suggests that it will enjoy a somewhat more liquid market than the B.
1995.chinese:
希望赠与股票的A类股股东，或许会觉得，把一两股转换为B类股很方便。此外，如果对B类股的需求旺盛，使价格略高于A类股的三十分之一，也会发生与套利有关的转换。

不过，A类股持有人享有完整投票权，也能参与伯克希尔捐款计划，因此A类股优于B类股。我们预期，多数股东会继续持有A类股；巴菲特与芒格两家人的打算，正是如此，只有为了方便赠与时，才可能转换少量股份。多数股东很可能继续留在A类股，这意味着A类股市场的流动性，可能会比B类股略好一些。

1995.english: There are tradeoffs for Berkshire in this recapitalization. But they do not arise from the proceeds of the offering - we will find constructive uses for the money - nor in any degree from the price at which we will sell the B shares.  As I write this - with Berkshire stock at $36,000 - Charlie and I do not believe it undervalued.  Therefore, the offering we propose will not diminish the per-share intrinsic value of our existing stock.  Let me also put our thoughts about valuation more baldly:  Berkshire is selling at a price at which Charlie and I would not consider buying it.
1995.chinese: 这次股本重组，对伯克希尔有利有弊。但这些取舍，不在于发行所得——我们会为资金找到有益的用途——也丝毫不在于B类股的发行价格。写这封信时，伯克希尔股价36,000美元，查理和我都不认为它被低估。因此，我们提出的发行，不会降低现有股票的每股内在价值。关于估值，不妨说得更直白一点：伯克希尔目前的卖价，是查理和我不会考虑买入的价位。

1995.english:
What Berkshire will incur by way of the B stock are certain added costs, including those involving the mechanics of handling a larger number of shareholders.  On the other hand, the stock should be a convenience for people wishing to make gifts.  And those of you who have hoped for a split have gained a do-it-yourself method of bringing one about.

We are making this move, though, for other reasons - having to do with the appearance of expense-laden unit trusts purporting to be low-priced "clones" of Berkshire and sure to be aggressively marketed.  The idea behind these vehicles is not new:  In recent years, a number of people have told me about their wish to create an "all-Berkshire" investment fund to be sold at a low dollar price.  But until recently, the promoters of these investments heard out my objections and backed off.
1995.chinese:
发行B类股，确实会给伯克希尔增加某些成本，包括处理更多股东事务的日常成本。另一方面，这种股票应当能为希望赠与的人提供方便。而一直盼着拆股的各位，也有了一种自己动手实现拆股的办法。

不过，我们采取这一步，另有原因：市场上出现了一些费用高昂的单位信托，自称是低价的伯克希尔“克隆品”，而且可以肯定，会受到大力推销。这类工具背后的点子并不新鲜。近几年，不少人告诉我，希望设立一只“全仓伯克希尔”的投资基金，以较低的金额出售份额。但直到最近，这些投资的发起人，还都听取了我的反对意见，打消了念头。

1995.english:
I did not discourage these people because I prefer large investors over small.  Were it possible, Charlie and I would love to turn $1,000 into $3,000 for multitudes of people who would find that gain an important answer to their immediate problems.

In order to quickly triple small stakes, however, we would have to just as quickly turn our present market capitalization of $43 billion into $129 billion (roughly the market cap of General Electric, America's most highly valued company).  We can't come close to doing that. The very best we hope for is - on average - to double Berkshire's per-share intrinsic value every five years, and we may well fall far short of that goal.
1995.chinese:
我劝退他们，并不是因为偏爱大投资者、不喜欢小投资者。如果可能，查理和我巴不得让许许多多人手里的1,000美元变成3,000美元；这笔收益，对他们解决眼前困难，会是重要的帮助。

不过，要让小额投资迅速变成三倍，就得同样迅速地让我们目前430亿美元的市值变成1,290亿美元，大约相当于美国市值最高的公司——通用电气。我们远远做不到。我们最好的期望，是平均每五年，让伯克希尔每股内在价值翻一番；而实际结果，很可能远达不到这个目标。

1995.english:
In the end, Charlie and I do not care whether our shareholders own Berkshire in large or small amounts.  What we wish for are shareholders of any size who are knowledgeable about our operations, share our objectives and long-term perspective, and are aware of our limitations, most particularly those imposed by our large capital base.

The unit trusts that have recently surfaced fly in the face of these goals.  They would be sold by brokers working for big commissions, would impose other burdensome costs on their shareholders, and would be marketed en masse to unsophisticated buyers, apt to be seduced by our past record and beguiled by the publicity Berkshire and I have received in recent years.  The sure outcome:  a multitude of investors destined to be disappointed.
1995.chinese:
归根结底，查理和我并不在乎，股东持有伯克希尔的金额是多是少。无论大小，我们希望股东了解我们的业务，认同我们的目标和长期眼光，并清楚我们的局限，尤其是庞大资本基础所带来的局限。

最近出现的单位信托，与这些目标背道而驰。经纪人会为了高额佣金出售它们；它们还会给股东加上其他沉重费用，并大规模推销给经验不足的买家。这些买家，很容易被我们过去的纪录吸引，被近几年伯克希尔和我受到的宣传迷住。必然的结果是：一大批注定会失望的投资者。

1995.english:
Through our creation of the B stock - a low-denomination product far superior to Berkshire-only trusts - we hope to make the clones unmerchandisable.

But both present and prospective Berkshire shareholders should pay special attention to one point:  Though the per-share intrinsic value of our stock has grown at an excellent rate during the past five years, its market price has grown still faster.  The stock, in other words, has outperformed the business.

That kind of market overperformance cannot persist indefinitely, neither for Berkshire nor any other stock.  Inevitably, there will be periods of underperformance as well.  The price volatility that results, though endemic to public markets, is not to our liking.  What we would prefer instead is to have the market price of Berkshire precisely track its intrinsic value. Were the stock to do that, every shareholder would benefit during his period of ownership in exact proportion to the progress Berkshire itself made in the period.
1995.chinese:
我们希望，通过发行B类股——一种远优于纯伯克希尔信托的低面额产品——让这些克隆品卖不出去。

不过，现有及潜在的伯克希尔股东，都应特别注意一点：过去五年，我们股票的每股内在价值增长很出色，市场价格却涨得更快。换句话说，股票跑赢了企业。

这种市场表现持续领先企业本身的情况，无论对伯克希尔，还是对其他股票，都不可能无限延续。表现落后的时期，也必然会到来。由此产生的价格波动，虽是公开市场的固有现象，却不合我们的心意。我们更希望，伯克希尔市价能够准确跟随内在价值。若能如此，每位股东持有期间取得的利益，就会与伯克希尔在同一期间取得的进步，完全成比例。

1995.english: Obviously, the market behavior of Berkshire's stock will never conform to this ideal.  But we will come closer to this goal than we would otherwise if our present and prospective shareholders are informed, business-oriented and not exposed to high-commission salesmanship when making their investment decisions.  To that end, we are better off if we can blunt the merchandising efforts of the unit trusts - and that is the reason we are creating the B stock.
1995.chinese: 显然，伯克希尔股票的市场表现，永远不可能完全符合这种理想。不过，如果现有及潜在股东了解情况、着眼企业本身，并且在作投资决定时，不受到高佣金推销的影响，我们就会比原本更接近目标。为此，若能削弱单位信托的推销势头，对我们有好处；这就是我们发行B类股的原因。

1995.english:
We look forward to answering your questions about the recapitalization at the Annual Meeting.

Miscellaneous

Berkshire isn't the only American corporation utilizing the new, exciting ABWA strategy.  At about 1:15 p.m. on July 14, 1995, Michael Eisner, CEO of The Walt Disney Company, was walking up Wildflower Lane in Sun Valley.  At the same time, I was leaving a lunch at Herbert Allen's home on that street to meet Tom Murphy, CEO of Cap Cities/ABC, for a golf game.
1995.chinese:
我们期待在股东大会上，回答各位有关股本重组的问题。

## 杂项

采用ABWA这种新鲜、刺激的战略的美国公司，并不只有伯克希尔一家。1995年7月14日下午约1时15分，华特迪士尼公司首席执行官迈克尔·艾斯纳，正沿太阳谷的野花巷往上走。与此同时，我刚在这条街上的赫伯特·艾伦家吃完午饭，出门去找大都会／美国广播公司首席执行官汤姆·墨菲打高尔夫。

1995.english: That morning, speaking to a large group of executives and money managers assembled by Allen's investment bank, Michael had made a brilliant presentation about Disney, and upon seeing him, I offered my congratulations.  We chatted briefly - and the subject of a possible combination of Disney and Cap Cities came up.  This wasn't the first time a merger had been discussed, but progress had never before been made, in part because Disney wanted to buy with cash and Cap Cities desired stock.
1995.chinese: 当天上午，艾伦的投资银行召集了一大批企业高管与资金经理，迈克尔向他们出色地介绍了迪士尼。见到他，我便上前祝贺。我们简短聊了几句，谈起迪士尼与大都会有没有可能合并。合并并非第一次被讨论，但此前一直没有进展；部分原因，是迪士尼想付现金，大都会却想收股票。

1995.english:
Michael and I waited a few minutes for Murph to arrive, and in the short conversation that ensued, both Michael and Murph indicated they might bend on the stock/cash question.  Within a few weeks, they both did, at which point a contract was put together in three very busy days.

The Disney/Cap Cities deal makes so much sense that I'm sure it would have occurred without that chance encounter in Sun Valley. But when I ran into Michael that day on Wildflower Lane, he was heading for his plane, so without that accidental meeting the deal certainly wouldn't have happened in the time frame it did.  I believe both Disney and Cap Cities will benefit from the fact that we all serendipitously met that day.
1995.chinese:
迈克尔和我等了几分钟，墨菲来了。随后的短暂交谈中，两人都表示，股票与现金的问题，或许可以变通。几周之内，他们确实都作了让步；接着，在忙得不可开交的三天里，一份合同便谈成了。

迪士尼与大都会的交易，如此合乎道理，我相信，即使没有太阳谷那次偶遇，它也会发生。不过，那天我在野花巷碰到迈克尔时，他正要去乘飞机，所以没有这次意外碰面，交易肯定不会在实际发生的那个时间完成。我相信，那天大家碰巧遇到一起，迪士尼与大都会都会因此受益。

1995.english:
---

It's appropriate that I say a few words here about Murph.  To put it simply, he is as fine an executive as I have ever seen in my long exposure to business.  Equally important, he possesses human qualities every bit the equal of his managerial qualities.  He's an extraordinary friend, parent, husband and citizen.  In those rare instances in which Murph's personal interests diverged from those of shareholders, he unfailingly favored the owners.  When I say that I like to be associated with managers whom I would love to have as a sibling, in-law, or trustee of my will, Murph is the exemplar of what I mean.
1995.chinese:
---

在这里，谈几句墨菲很合适。简单说，在我漫长的商业经历中，他是我见过的最优秀的高管之一。同样重要的是，他的为人，丝毫不逊于他的管理才能。作为朋友、父亲、丈夫和公民，他都出类拔萃。极少数时候，他的个人利益与股东利益出现分歧，他也总是毫不例外地站在所有者一边。我说过，喜欢与那些自己愿意认作兄弟姐妹、姻亲，或遗嘱受托人的经理人合作；墨菲就是最好的例子。

1995.english:
If Murph should elect to run another business, don't bother to study its value - just buy the stock.  And don't later be as dumb as I was two years ago when I sold one-third of our holdings in Cap Cities for $635 million (versus the $1.27 billion those shares would bring in the Disney merger).

---

About 96.3% of all eligible shares participated in Berkshire's 1995 shareholder-designated contributions program.  Contributions made were $11.6 million and 3,600 charities were recipients.  A full description of the shareholder-designated contributions program appears on pages 54-55.
1995.chinese:
如果墨菲决定再去经营一家企业，各位不用费心研究估值了，直接买股票便是。往后也别像我两年前那样犯傻：我以6.35亿美元，卖掉了我们大都会持仓的三分之一；若留到与迪士尼合并，这些股份本可换来12.7亿美元。

---

1995年伯克希尔股东指定捐款计划，约有96.3%的合资格股份参与。捐款总额为1,160万美元，受赠慈善机构达3,600家。计划的完整说明，见第54—55页。

1995.english: Every year a few shareholders miss out on the program because they don't have their shares registered in their own names on the prescribed record date or because they fail to get their designation form back to us within the 60-day period allowed.  That second problem pained me especially this year because two good friends with substantial holdings missed the deadline.  We had to deny their requests to be included because we can't make exceptions for some shareholders while refusing to make them for others.
1995.chinese: 每年，都有少数股东错过计划：有的是因为在规定的登记日，股份没有登记在自己名下；有的是因为未能在允许的60天内，把指定受赠机构的表格寄还。今年，后一种情况尤其令我难受，因为两位持股相当多的好朋友，也错过了截止日期。我们只能拒绝他们要求补参加的请求，因为不能为某些股东破例，却不给另一些股东同样的待遇。

1995.english:
To participate in future programs, you must own Class A shares that are registered in the name of the actual owner, not the nominee name of a broker, bank or depository.  Shares not so registered on August 31, 1996, will be ineligible for the 1996 program.  When you get the form, return it promptly so that it does not get put aside or forgotten.

---
1995.chinese:
要参加今后的计划，各位必须持有A类股，并把股票登记在实际所有者名下，而非经纪人、银行或存托机构的代名人名下。截至1996年8月31日，若股份仍未作这种登记，就没有资格参加1996年计划。收到表格后，请尽快寄回，免得放在一旁，最后忘了。

---

1995.english: When it comes to our Annual Meetings, Charlie and I are managerial oddballs:  We thoroughly enjoy the event.  So come join us on Monday, May 6.  At Berkshire, we have no investor relations department and don't use financial analysts as a channel for disseminating information, earnings "guidance," or the like. Instead, we prefer direct manager-to-owner communication and believe that the Annual Meeting is the ideal place for this interchange of ideas.  Talking to you there is efficient for us and also democratic in that all present simultaneously hear what we have to say.
1995.chinese: 说起股东大会，查理和我算是管理界的怪人：我们打心眼里喜欢这件事。所以，请在5月6日星期一来与我们相聚。伯克希尔没有投资者关系部门，也不借助证券分析师来传播信息、提供盈利“指引”之类。我们更喜欢管理者与所有者直接交流，认为股东大会正是交换想法的理想场合。在那里与各位交谈，对我们有效率，也很民主：所有到场的人，都能同时听到我们的话。

1995.english: Last year, for the first time, we had the Annual Meeting at the Holiday Convention Centre and the logistics seemed to work. The ballroom there was filled with about 3,200 people, and we had a video feed into a second room holding another 800 people.  Seating in the main room was a little tight, so this year we will probably configure it to hold 3,000.  This year we will also have two rooms for the overflow.
1995.chinese: 去年，我们首次在假日会议中心举办股东大会，组织安排看来行得通。主宴会厅坐满了约3,200人，另一个房间通过视频转播，又容纳了800人。主厅座位有点挤，所以今年可能改为安排3,000人。今年还会准备两个分会场，供主厅坐不下的股东使用。

1995.english:
All in all, we will be able to handle 5,000 shareholders.  The meeting will start at 9:30 a.m., but be warned that last year the main ballroom was filled shortly after 8:00 a.m.

Shareholders from 49 states attended our 1995 meeting - where were you, Vermont? - and a number of foreign countries, including Australia, Sweden and Germany, were represented.  As always, the meeting attracted shareholders who were interested in Berkshire's business - as contrasted to shareholders who are primarily interested in themselves - and the questions were all good. Charlie and I ate lunch on stage and answered questions for about five hours.
1995.chinese:
总共，我们可以接待5,000位股东。会议上午9时30分开始，不过提醒各位：去年主宴会厅在上午8点刚过，就已坐满。

1995年大会，有来自49个州的股东参加——佛蒙特州，各位上哪儿去了？——也有澳大利亚、瑞典、德国等外国的代表。和往常一样，大会吸引的是关心伯克希尔生意的股东，而非主要关心自己的股东，提的问题都很好。查理和我在台上吃午饭，回答问题大约五个小时。

1995.english:
We feel that if owners come from all over the world, we should try to make sure they have an opportunity to ask their questions. Most shareholders leave about noon, but a thousand or so hardcore types usually stay to see whether we will drop.  Charlie and I are in training to last at least five hours again this year.

We will have our usual array of Berkshire products at the meeting and this year will add a sales representative from GEICO. At the 1995 meeting, we sold 747 pounds of candy, 759 pairs of shoes, and over $17,500 of World Books and related publications. In a move that might have been dangerous had our stock been weak, we added knives last year from our Quikut subsidiary and sold 400 sets of these.  (We draw the line at soft fruit, however.)  All of these goods will again be available this year.  We don't consider a cultural event complete unless a little business is mixed in.
1995.chinese:
我们觉得，所有者从世界各地赶来，我们就应尽量确保他们有机会提问。多数股东中午左右就离开，但通常还有一千来位铁杆留下，看我们会不会先趴下。查理和我正在训练，争取今年也至少撑足五小时。

会上照例会摆出一批伯克希尔产品，今年还会增加一位GEICO销售代表。1995年大会，我们卖了747磅糖果、759双鞋，以及超过17,500美元的世界图书和相关出版物。去年，我们还加卖Quikut子公司出品的刀具，售出400套；倘若当时股价疲软，这招可能很危险。（不过，熟软水果，我们可坚决不卖。）今年这些商品仍会全部供应。我们认为，一场文化活动，不掺点生意，总不算圆满。

1995.english: Because we expect a large crowd for the meeting, we recommend that you promptly get both plane and hotel reservations.  Those of you who like to be downtown (about six miles from the Centre) may wish to stay at the Radisson Redick Tower, a small (88 rooms) but nice hotel, or at the much larger Red Lion Hotel a few blocks away. In the vicinity of the Centre are the Holiday Inn (403 rooms), Homewood Suites (118 rooms) and Hampton Inn (136 rooms).  Another recommended spot is the Marriott, whose west Omaha location is about 100 yards from Borsheim's and a ten-minute drive from the Centre.  There will be buses at the Marriott that will leave at 7:30, 8:00 and 8:30 for the meeting and return after it ends.
1995.chinese: 预计参会人数很多，我们建议各位尽快订好机票与酒店。喜欢住市中心的股东，可以考虑拉迪森雷迪克塔酒店，虽小，只有88间房，却很不错；或是几条街外、规模大得多的红狮酒店。市中心距会议中心约六英里。会议中心附近，有假日酒店403间客房、霍姆伍德套房酒店118间、汉普顿酒店136间。另一个推荐去处是万豪酒店，位于奥马哈西部，距波仙珠宝约100码，开车到会议中心约十分钟。我们会安排巴士，上午7时30分、8时和8时30分从万豪出发前往会场，散会后送回。

1995.english: An attachment to our proxy material explains how you can obtain the card you will need for admission to the meeting.  A good-sized parking area is available at the Centre, while those who stay at the Holiday Inn, Homewood Suites and Hampton Inn will be able to walk to the meeting.  As usual, we will have buses to take you to the Nebraska Furniture Mart and Borsheim's after the meeting and to take you from there to hotels or the airport later.
1995.chinese: 委托投票材料的附件，会说明如何领取参加会议所需的入场卡。会议中心有面积不小的停车场；住在假日、霍姆伍德套房及汉普顿三家酒店的股东，则可以步行到场。照例，散会后会有巴士送各位去内布拉斯加家具卖场与波仙珠宝，稍后再从那里送往酒店或机场。

1995.english: NFM's main store, on its 64-acre site about two miles north of the Centre, is open from 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. on weekdays, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Saturdays, and noon to 6 p.m. on Sundays.  Rose Blumkin - "Mrs. B" - is now 102, but will be hard at work in Mrs. B's Warehouse.  She was honored in November at the opening of The Rose, a classic downtown theater of the 20's that has been magnificently restored, but that would have been demolished had she not saved it. Ask her to tell you the story.
1995.chinese: 内布拉斯加家具卖场主店，占地64英亩，位于会议中心以北约两英里。工作日营业时间为上午10时至晚上9时，星期六上午10时至下午6时，星期日中午12时至下午6时。罗斯·布拉姆金——也就是B夫人——如今102岁，仍将在B夫人仓储店里辛勤工作。去年11月，“罗斯剧院”开幕时，她受到表彰。这是一座市中心的20年代经典剧院，修复得十分漂亮；若不是她救下来，早就会被拆掉。请她讲给各位听听。

1995.english: Borsheim's normally is closed on Sunday but will be open for shareholders and their guests from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. on May 5th. Additionally, we will have a special opening for shareholders on Saturday, the 4th, from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m.  Last year, on Shareholders Day, we wrote 1,733 tickets in the six hours we were open - which is a sale every 13 seconds.  Remember, though, that records are made to be broken.
1995.chinese: 波仙珠宝星期日通常不开门，但5月5日，将于上午10时至下午6时，向股东及其来宾开放。此外，5月4日星期六晚上6时至9时，还会为股东特别营业。去年股东日，开门六小时里，我们开出了1,733张销售单，相当于每13秒成交一笔。不过，请记住，纪录就是用来打破的。

1995.english:
At Borsheim's, we will also have the world's largest faceted diamond on display.  Two years in the cutting, this inconspicuous bauble is 545 carats in size.  Please inspect this stone and let it guide you in determining what size gem is appropriate for the one you love.

On Saturday evening, May 4, there will be a baseball game at Rosenblatt Stadium between the Omaha Royals and the Louisville Redbirds.  I expect to make the opening pitch - owning a quarter of the team assures me of one start per year - but our manager, Mike Jirschele, will probably make his usual mistake and yank me immediately after.  About 1,700 shareholders attended last year's game.  Unfortunately, we had a rain-out, which greatly disappointed the many scouts in the stands.  But the smart ones will be back this year, and I plan to show them my best stuff.
1995.chinese:
波仙还将展出世界上最大的刻面钻石。经过两年切割，这颗“不起眼”的小玩意，足有545克拉。请各位仔细看看，再让它指引自己判断：送给心爱的人，多大的宝石才算合适。

5月4日星期六晚上，罗森布拉特球场将举办奥马哈皇家队对路易斯维尔红鸟队的棒球赛。我预计会投出开场第一球——拥有球队四分之一，保证了我每年有一次先发机会——不过，我们的经理迈克·吉尔舍尔，大概又会照例犯错，投完立刻把我换下。去年约有1,700位股东看球。遗憾的是，比赛因雨取消，让看台上众多球探大失所望。但聪明的球探今年还会回来；我打算把看家本领亮给他们看。

1995.english:
Our proxy statement will include information about obtaining tickets to the game.  We will also offer an information packet this year listing restaurants that will be open on Sunday night and describing various things that you can do in Omaha on the weekend.

For years, I've unsuccessfully tried to get my grade school classmate, "Pal" Gorat, to open his steakhouse for business on the Sunday evening preceding the meeting.  But this year he's relented. Gorat's is a family-owned enterprise that has thrived for 52 years, and if you like steaks, you'll love this place. I've told Pal he will get a good crowd, so call Gorat's at 402-551-3733 for a reservation.  You'll spot me there - I'll be the one eating the rare T-bone with a double order of hash browns.

Warren E. Buffett March 1, 1996                                Chairman of the Board
1995.chinese:
我们的委托投票说明书，将介绍怎样取得球赛门票。今年还会提供一份资料包，列出星期日晚上营业的餐馆，并介绍周末在奥马哈可参加的各项活动。

多年来，我一直劝小学同学“帕尔”·戈拉特，在股东大会前的星期日晚上，把他的牛排馆打开营业，始终没成功。今年，他终于松口了。戈拉特牛排馆是一家兴旺了52年的家族企业；如果各位喜欢牛排，一定会喜欢这里。我已对帕尔说，会有很多人来，所以请打402-551-3733预约。到时各位会看到我——那个吃着一分熟T骨牛排、再加双份薯饼的人，就是我。

沃伦·E·巴菲特  
董事会主席  
1996年3月1日

1996.english:
BERKSHIRE HATHAWAY INC.

## Chairman's Letter

To the Shareholders of Berkshire Hathaway Inc.:

Our gain in net worth during 1996 was $6.2 billion, or 36.1%.  Per- share book value, however, grew by less, 31.8%, because the number of Berkshire shares increased:  We issued stock in acquiring FlightSafety International and also sold new Class B shares.*   Over the last 32 years (that is, since present management took over) per-share book value has grown from $19 to $19,011, or at a rate of 23.8% compounded annually.
1996.chinese:
伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司

董事长致股东信

致伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司的股东：

1996年，我们的净资产增加了62亿美元，增幅为36.1%。不过，每股账面价值的增幅略低，为31.8%，因为伯克希尔的股份数量增加了：我们为收购飞安国际公司（FlightSafety International）发行了股票，还出售了新设立的B类股。* 在过去32年里，也就是现任管理层接手以来，每股账面价值从19美元增至19,011美元，年复合增长率为23.8%。

1996.english:
* Each Class B share has an economic interest equal to 1/30th of that possessed by a Class A share, which is the new designation for the only stock that Berkshire had outstanding before May 1996. Throughout this report, we state all per-share figures in terms of "Class A equivalents," which are the sum of the Class A shares outstanding and 1/30th of the Class B shares outstanding.

For technical reasons, we have restated our 1995 financial statements, a matter that requires me to present one of my less-than- thrilling explanations of accounting arcana.  I'll make it brief.
1996.chinese:
* 每股B类股所享有的经济权益，相当于每股A类股的1/30。A类股是对伯克希尔在1996年5月以前唯一发行在外的股票所使用的新名称。本报告所有每股数据，均按“A类等价股”计算，即A类流通股数加上B类流通股数的1/30。

出于技术原因，我们重述了1995年的财务报表。这意味着，我又得给各位讲一段并不怎么引人入胜的会计玄学。我尽量长话短说。

1996.english: The restatement was required because GEICO became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Berkshire on January 2, 1996, whereas it was previously classified as an investment.  From an economic viewpoint - taking into account major tax efficiencies and other benefits we gained - the value of the 51% of GEICO we owned at year-end 1995 increased significantly when we acquired the remaining 49% of the company two days later. Accounting rules applicable to this type of "step acquisition," however, required us to write down the value of our 51% at the time we moved to 100%.  That writedown - which also, of course, reduced book value - amounted to $478.4 million.  As a result, we now carry our original 51% of GEICO at a value that is both lower than its market value at the time we purchased the remaining 49% of the company and lower than the value at which we carry that 49% itself.
1996.chinese: 之所以需要重述，是因为盖可保险公司（GEICO）于1996年1月2日成为伯克希尔的全资子公司，而此前它一直被归类为一项投资。从经济角度看，考虑到我们获得的显著税务效益和其他好处，1995年年底所持有的盖可51%股权，在两天后我们收购其余49%股权时，价值大幅提升。然而，适用于这类“分步收购”的会计规则，却要求我们在持股比例升至100%时，调低原有51%股权的账面价值。这笔减记为4.784亿美元，当然也相应降低了我们的账面净资产。因此，我们现在记录原有51%盖可股权的账面金额，既低于收购其余49%股权时这部分股权的市值，也低于那49%股权本身的入账金额。

1996.english: There is an offset, however, to the reduction in book value I have just described:  Twice during 1996 we issued Berkshire shares at a premium to book value, first in May when we sold the B shares for cash and again in December when we used both A and B shares as part-payment for FlightSafety.  In total, the three non-operational items affecting book value contributed less than one percentage point to our 31.8% per- share gain last year.
1996.chinese: 不过，刚才所说的账面价值下降，也有抵消因素。1996年，我们曾两次以高于每股账面价值的价格发行伯克希尔股票：一次是5月出售B类股募集现金，另一次是12月以A类股和B类股支付收购飞安国际的部分对价。总体而言，这三项非经营性事项对去年每股账面价值31.8%的增幅，净贡献不足一个百分点。

1996.english: I dwell on this rise in per-share book value because it roughly indicates our economic progress during the year.  But, as Charlie Munger, Berkshire's Vice Chairman, and I have repeatedly told you, what counts at Berkshire is intrinsic value, not book value.  The last time you got that message from us was in the Owner's Manual, sent to you in June after we issued the Class B shares.  In that manual, we not only defined certain key terms - such as intrinsic value -  but also set forth our economic principles.
1996.chinese: 我之所以详细说明每股账面价值的增长，是因为它大致反映了我们这一年的经济进展。但正如伯克希尔副董事长查理·芒格和我反复告诉各位的，伯克希尔真正看重的是内在价值，而不是账面价值。我们最近一次强调这一点，是在发行B类股之后，于6月寄给各位的《股东手册》中。那本手册既解释了内在价值等重要术语，也阐明了我们的经济原则。

1996.english:
For many years, we have listed these principles in the front of our annual report, but in this report, on pages 58 to 67, we reproduce the entire Owner's Manual.  In this letter, we will occasionally refer to the manual so that we can avoid repeating certain definitions and explanations.  For example, if you wish to brush up on "intrinsic value," see pages 64 and 65.

Last year, for the first time, we supplied you with a table that Charlie and I believe will help anyone trying to estimate Berkshire's intrinsic value.  In the updated version of that table, which follows, we trace two key indices of value.  The first column lists our per-share ownership of investments (including cash and equivalents) and the second column shows our per-share earnings from Berkshire's operating businesses before taxes and purchase-accounting adjustments but after all interest and corporate overhead expenses.  The operating-earnings column excludes all dividends, interest and capital gains that we realized from the investments presented in the first column.  In effect, the two columns show what Berkshire would have reported had it been broken into two parts.
1996.chinese:
多年来，我们一直把这些原则列在年报前部；而本次年报在第58至67页刊载了完整的《股东手册》。这封信会不时引用该手册，以免重复某些定义和解释。例如，若想重温“内在价值”的含义，请参阅第64和65页。

去年，我们首次向各位提供了一张表。查理和我认为，它能帮助任何有意估算伯克希尔内在价值的人。下面是这张表的更新版，列出了两项重要的价值指标。第一栏是每股所对应的投资资产，包括现金及现金等价物；第二栏是伯克希尔经营业务的每股利润，在扣除全部利息及总部管理费用后、所得税及收购会计调整前计算。经营利润这一栏，不包含我们从第一栏投资资产中取得的任何股息、利息和资本利得。实际上，这两栏展示的是：假如把伯克希尔拆成两部分，各自会报告怎样的数据。

1996.english:
As the table tells you, our investments per share increased in 1996 by 29.0% and our non-investment earnings grew by 63.2%.  Our goal is to keep the numbers in both columns moving ahead at a reasonable (or, better yet, unreasonable) pace.

Our expectations, however, are tempered by two realities.  First, our past rates of growth cannot be matched nor even approached: Berkshire's equity capital is now large - in fact, fewer than ten businesses in America have capital larger -  and an abundance of funds tends to dampen returns.  Second, whatever our rate of progress, it will not be smooth:  Year-to-year moves in the first column of the table above will be influenced in a major way by fluctuations in securities markets; the figures in the second column will be affected by wide swings in the profitability of our catastrophe-reinsurance business.
1996.chinese:
如表所示，1996年我们的每股投资资产增长了29.0%，非投资业务的利润增长了63.2%。我们的目标，是让两栏数字都以合理的速度向前增长；如果能快得“不合理”，那当然更好。

但有两个现实因素，让我们的预期不能过于乐观。第一，过去的增长速度不可能重现，甚至无法接近。伯克希尔的股东权益规模如今已经很大，实际上，全美国资本规模超过我们的企业还不到十家，而资金过多往往会压低回报率。第二，无论增长速度如何，过程都不会平稳：上表第一栏的年度变化会在很大程度上受到证券市场波动的影响；第二栏的数据，则会受到巨灾再保险业务盈利大幅起伏的影响。

1996.english: In the table, the donations made pursuant to our shareholder- designated contributions program are charged against the second column, though we view them as a shareholder benefit rather than as an expense. All other corporate expenses are also charged against the second column. These costs may be lower than those of any other large American corporation:  Our after-tax headquarters expense amounts to less than two basis points (1/50th of 1%) measured against net worth.  Even so, Charlie used to think this expense percentage outrageously high, blaming it on my use of Berkshire's corporate jet, The Indefensible.  But Charlie has recently experienced a "counter-revelation":  With our purchase of FlightSafety, whose major activity is the training of corporate pilots, he now rhapsodizes at the mere mention of jets.
1996.chinese: 表中，按“股东指定捐赠计划”作出的捐赠计入第二栏的扣减项，尽管我们把它视为股东获得的一项利益，而非费用。其他所有总部费用也在第二栏扣除。这些费用可能比美国任何一家其他大型企业都低：我们税后总部费用占净资产的比例不到两个基点，即1%的五十分之一。即便如此，查理过去还是觉得这个比例高得离谱，并把责任归咎于我使用伯克希尔那架名为“无可辩解号”的公务机。不过，查理最近有了一番“反向顿悟”：自从我们收购以培训公务机飞行员为主业的飞安国际，他如今一听见喷气式飞机就赞不绝口。

1996.english: Seriously, costs matter.  For example, equity mutual funds incur corporate expenses - largely payments to the funds' managers - that average about 100 basis points, a levy likely to cut the returns their investors earn by 10% or more over time.  Charlie and I make no promises about Berkshire's results.  We do promise you, however, that virtually all of the gains Berkshire makes will end up with shareholders.  We are here to make money with you, not off you.
1996.chinese: 说正经的，费用确实重要。比如，股票型共同基金的运营费用，主要是支付给基金管理人的费用，平均约为100个基点。长此以往，这笔收费很可能使投资者所得回报减少10%甚至更多。查理和我不对伯克希尔的业绩作任何保证。但我们可以保证：伯克希尔创造的收益，几乎都会归属于股东。我们来这里，是为了和各位一起赚钱，而不是从各位身上赚钱。

1996.english:
## The Relationship of Intrinsic Value to Market Price

In last year's letter, with Berkshire shares selling at $36,000, I told you:  (1) Berkshire's gain in market value in recent years had outstripped its gain in intrinsic value, even though the latter gain had been highly satisfactory; (2) that kind of overperformance could not continue indefinitely; (3) Charlie and I did not at that moment consider Berkshire to be undervalued.

Since I set down those cautions, Berkshire's intrinsic value has increased very significantly - aided in a major way by a stunning performance at GEICO that I will tell you more about later - while the market price of our shares has changed little.  This, of course, means that in 1996 Berkshire's stock underperformed the business. Consequently, today's price/value relationship is both much different from what it was a year ago and, as Charlie and I see it, more appropriate.
1996.chinese:
## 内在价值与市场价格的关系

去年写信时，伯克希尔的股价为36,000美元。我当时告诉各位三件事：第一，虽然内在价值的增长已经十分令人满意，但近几年市值的增长仍然超过了内在价值的增长；第二，这种超越不可能无限持续；第三，查理和我当时并不认为伯克希尔的股价被低估了。

自从我写下这些提醒，伯克希尔的内在价值已经显著增加，其中很大一部分要归功于盖可的出色表现，后文我会详述；与此同时，我们的股价变化却不大。这当然意味着，1996年伯克希尔股票的表现落后于企业本身。因此，今天价格与价值之间的关系，和一年前已经大不相同；在查理和我看来，也更为恰当。

1996.english:
Over time, the aggregate gains made by Berkshire shareholders must of necessity match the business gains of the company.  When the stock temporarily overperforms or underperforms the business, a limited number of shareholders - either sellers or buyers - receive outsized benefits at the expense of those they trade with.  Generally, the sophisticated have an edge over the innocents in this game.

Though our primary goal is to maximize the amount that our shareholders, in total, reap from their ownership of Berkshire, we wish also to minimize the benefits going to some shareholders at the expense of others.  These are goals we would have were we managing a family partnership, and we believe they make equal sense for the manager of a public company.  In a partnership, fairness requires that partnership interests be valued equitably when partners enter or exit; in a public company, fairness prevails when market price and intrinsic value are in sync.  Obviously, they won't always meet that ideal, but a manager - by his policies and communications - can do much to foster equity.
1996.chinese:
长期来看，伯克希尔全体股东获得的总收益，必然与公司的经营成果相匹配。当股票表现暂时领先或落后于企业表现时，一小部分股东，无论是卖方还是买方，会以其交易对手的利益为代价，获得超额好处。在这样的游戏里，老练者通常比缺乏经验的人更占优势。

我们的首要目标，是让全体股东作为一个整体，从持有伯克希尔中获得尽可能多的收益；同时，我们也希望尽量减少一些股东通过牺牲另一些股东而获得的利益。如果经营一家家族合伙企业，我们也会坚持这两个目标。我们认为，它们对上市公司的管理者同样适用。在合伙企业中，合伙人加入或退出时，必须公允地评估其权益，才称得上公平；在上市公司中，市场价格与内在价值相符时，才有这种公平。显然，两者不可能总是处于理想状态，但管理者可以通过政策和沟通，为公平做很多事。

1996.english: Of course, the longer a shareholder holds his shares, the more bearing Berkshire's business results will have on his financial experience - and the less it will matter what premium or discount to intrinsic value prevails when he buys and sells his stock.  That's one reason we hope to attract owners with long-term horizons.  Overall, I think we have succeeded in that pursuit.  Berkshire probably ranks number one among large American corporations in the percentage of its shares held by owners with a long-term view.
1996.chinese: 当然，股东持有股份的时间越长，伯克希尔的经营成果对其投资回报的影响就越大；买入和卖出时，股价相对内在价值是溢价还是折价，影响就越小。这是我们希望吸引长期持有者的原因之一。总体而言，我认为我们在这方面做得不错。就长期投资者所持股份的比例而言，伯克希尔在美国大型企业中很可能排名第一。

1996.english:
Acquisitions of 1996

We made two acquisitions in 1996, both possessing exactly the qualities we seek - excellent business economics and an outstanding manager.

The first acquisition was Kansas Bankers Surety (KBS), an insurance company whose name describes its specialty.  The company, which does business in 22 states, has an extraordinary underwriting record, achieved through the efforts of Don Towle, an extraordinary manager.  Don has developed first-hand relationships with hundreds of bankers and knows every detail of his operation.  He thinks of himself as running a company that is "his," an attitude we treasure at Berkshire.  Because of its relatively small size, we placed KBS with Wesco, our 80%-owned subsidiary, which has wanted to expand its insurance operations.
1996.chinese:
## 1996年的收购

1996年，我们完成了两项收购。两家公司都恰好具备我们寻找的特质：出色的经济特性，以及优秀的管理者。

第一项收购是堪萨斯银行家保证保险公司（Kansas Bankers Surety，简称KBS）。从名称就能看出，这家保险公司的专业领域。它在22个州经营业务，凭借一位非凡的管理者唐·托尔（Don Towle）的努力，取得了极为出色的承保业绩。唐与数百位银行家建立了直接联系，对公司的每一个经营细节都了如指掌。他把公司当作“自己的”事业来经营，这正是伯克希尔珍视的态度。由于KBS的规模相对较小，我们将它归入持股80%的子公司韦斯科（Wesco）；韦斯科一直希望扩大保险业务。

1996.english: You might be interested in the carefully-crafted and sophisticated acquisition strategy that allowed Berkshire to nab this deal.  Early in 1996 I was invited to the 40th birthday party of my nephew's wife, Jane Rogers.  My taste for social events being low, I immediately, and in my standard, gracious way, began to invent reasons for skipping the event. The party planners then countered brilliantly by offering me a seat next to a man I always enjoy, Jane's dad, Roy Dinsdale - so I went.
1996.chinese: 各位也许有兴趣了解，我们究竟采用了怎样一套精心策划、老练高明的收购战略，才拿下这笔交易。1996年年初，我受邀参加侄媳妇简·罗杰斯（Jane Rogers）的40岁生日聚会。我一向不太喜欢社交活动，于是立刻拿出自己惯常的“优雅风度”，开始编造不去的理由。聚会筹办者随后使出妙招：他们答应把我安排在简的父亲罗伊·丁斯代尔（Roy Dinsdale）身边。我一直很喜欢和罗伊交谈，于是就去了。

1996.english:
The party took place on January 26.  Though the music was loud - Why must bands play as if they will be paid by the decibel? - I just managed to hear Roy say he'd come from a directors meeting at Kansas Bankers Surety, a company I'd always admired.  I shouted back that he should let me know if it ever became available for purchase.

On February 12, I got the following letter from Roy:  "Dear Warren: Enclosed is the annual financial information on Kansas Bankers Surety. This is the company that we talked about at Janie's party.  If I can be of any further help, please let me know."  On February 13, I told Roy we would pay $75 million for the company - and before long we had a deal. I'm now scheming to get invited to Jane's next party.
1996.chinese:
聚会在1月26日举行。音乐声很大——乐队为什么非得表现得像按分贝拿报酬一样？——但我还是勉强听到罗伊说，他刚参加完KBS的董事会。那是一家我始终很欣赏的公司。我便大声回应，如果这家公司有一天愿意出售，一定要告诉我。

2月12日，我收到罗伊的来信：“亲爱的沃伦：随信附上堪萨斯银行家保证保险公司的年度财务资料，就是我们在简妮的聚会上谈到的那家公司。如有其他需要帮忙的地方，请告诉我。”2月13日，我告诉罗伊，我们愿意出价7,500万美元收购。不久之后，交易就达成了。我现在正在盘算，怎样才能收到简下次聚会的邀请。

1996.english: Our other acquisition in 1996 - FlightSafety International, the world's leader in the training of pilots - was far larger, at about $1.5 billion, but had an equally serendipitous origin.  The heroes of this story are first, Richard Sercer, a Tucson aviation consultant, and second, his wife, Alma Murphy, an ophthalmology graduate of Harvard Medical School, who in 1990 wore down her husband's reluctance and got him to buy Berkshire stock.  Since then, the two have attended all our Annual Meetings, but I didn't get to know them personally.
1996.chinese: 1996年的另一项收购，是全球飞行员培训行业的领军企业飞安国际。交易规模大得多，约为15亿美元，但缘起同样偶然。这个故事有两位功臣：一位是图森的航空顾问理查德·瑟塞尔（Richard Sercer）；另一位是他的妻子阿尔玛·墨菲（Alma Murphy），她毕业于哈佛医学院眼科专业。1990年，她不断劝说，终于让原本不情愿的丈夫买入了伯克希尔股票。从那以后，两人每年都参加我们的股东大会，不过我并不认识他们本人。

1996.english: Fortunately, Richard had also been a long-time shareholder of FlightSafety, and it occurred to him last year that the two companies would make a good fit.  He knew our acquisition criteria, and he thought that Al Ueltschi, FlightSafety's 79-year-old CEO, might want to make a deal that would both give him a home for his company and a security in payment that he would feel comfortable owning throughout his lifetime. So in July, Richard wrote Bob Denham, CEO of Salomon Inc, suggesting that he explore the possibility of a merger.
1996.chinese: 幸运的是，理查德也是飞安国际的长期股东。去年，他想到这两家公司也许很适合结合。他了解我们的收购标准，也认为飞安国际79岁的首席执行官阿尔·乌尔奇（Al Ueltschi），或许愿意达成这样一笔交易：既为公司找到合适的归宿，又获得一种自己终身持有也能安心的证券作为对价。于是，7月间，理查德写信给所罗门公司首席执行官鲍勃·德纳姆（Bob Denham），建议他探讨合并的可能性。

1996.english: Bob took it from there, and on September 18, Al and I met in New York.  I had long been familiar with FlightSafety's business, and in about 60 seconds I knew that Al was exactly our kind of manager.  A month later, we had a contract.  Because Charlie and I wished to minimize the issuance of Berkshire shares, the transaction we structured gave FlightSafety shareholders a choice of cash or stock but carried terms that encouraged those who were tax-indifferent to take cash.  This nudge led to about 51% of FlightSafety's shares being exchanged for cash, 41% for Berkshire A and 8% for Berkshire B.
1996.chinese: 随后，鲍勃接手推进此事。9月18日，我和阿尔在纽约见面。我早已熟悉飞安国际的业务，而见面大约60秒后，我就知道阿尔正是我们喜欢的那类管理者。一个月后，我们签订了合同。查理和我希望尽量减少伯克希尔新股的发行，因此在交易安排上，让飞安国际的股东可以选择现金或股票，同时通过条款设计，鼓励那些两种选择在税务上没有差别的股东接受现金。这一引导使约51%的飞安国际股份兑换成现金，41%兑换成伯克希尔A类股，8%兑换成B类股。

1996.english: Al has had a lifelong love affair with aviation and actually piloted Charles Lindbergh.  After a barnstorming career in the 1930s, he began working for Juan Trippe, Pan Am's legendary chief.  In 1951, while still at Pan Am, Al founded FlightSafety, subsequently building it into a simulator manufacturer and a worldwide trainer of pilots (single-engine, helicopter, jet and marine).  The company operates in 41 locations, outfitted with 175 simulators of planes ranging from the very small, such as Cessna 210s, to Boeing 747s.  Simulators are not cheap - they can cost as much as $19 million  - so this business, unlike many of our operations, is capital intensive.  About half of the company's revenues are derived from the training of corporate pilots, with most of the balance coming from airlines and the military.
1996.chinese: 阿尔一生热爱航空，甚至曾经驾驶飞机搭载过查尔斯·林德伯格。20世纪30年代，他曾从事巡回飞行表演，之后开始为泛美航空的传奇掌门人胡安·特里普（Juan Trippe）工作。1951年，仍在泛美任职的阿尔创办了飞安国际，并逐渐将它发展成模拟器制造商，以及面向全球的驾驶人员培训机构，培训范围包括单引擎飞机、直升机、喷气式飞机和船舶。公司在41个地点开展业务，配备175台飞机模拟器，机型从塞斯纳210这样的小型飞机，一直到波音747。模拟器价格不菲，一台最高可达1,900万美元。因此，与我们的许多其他业务不同，这是一门资本密集型生意。公司大约一半收入来自公务机飞行员培训，其余大部分来自航空公司和军方。

1996.english:
Al may be 79, but he looks and acts about 55.  He will run operations just as he has in the past:  We never fool with success.  I have told him that though we don't believe in splitting Berkshire stock, we will split his age 2-for-1 when he hits 100.

An observer might conclude from our hiring practices that Charlie and I were traumatized early in life by an EEOC bulletin on age discrimination.  The real explanation, however, is self-interest:  It's difficult to teach a new dog old tricks.  The many Berkshire managers who are past 70 hit home runs today at the same pace that long ago gave them reputations as young slugging sensations.  Therefore, to get a job with us, just employ the tactic of the 76-year-old who persuaded a dazzling beauty of 25 to marry him.  "How did you ever get her to accept?" asked his envious contemporaries.  The comeback:  "I told her I was 86."
1996.chinese:
阿尔虽然已经79岁，但外表和行动都像55岁。他会继续像过去一样管理公司：成功的做法，我们从不乱动。我告诉他，虽然我们不赞成拆分伯克希尔股票，但等他100岁时，我们会把他的年龄来一次“一拆二”。

旁观者看了我们的用人方式，可能会以为查理和我早年被平等就业机会委员会关于年龄歧视的通告吓坏了。真正的解释却是自利：要教一只新狗学会老把戏，可不容易。伯克希尔许多年过70的管理者，如今打出本垒打的频率，仍与他们当年凭强劲打击而声名鹊起时一样。因此，想在我们这里找到工作，不妨学学那位76岁老人：他成功说服一位25岁的美丽女子嫁给自己。同龄人羡慕地问：“你到底怎么让她答应的？”他答道：“我告诉她，我86岁了。”

1996.english:
---

And now we pause for our usual commercial:  If you own a large business with good economic characteristics and wish to become associated with an exceptional collection of businesses having similar characteristics, Berkshire may well be the home you seek.  Our requirements are set forth on page 21.  If your company meets them - and if I fail to make the next birthday party you attend - give me a call.
1996.chinese:
* * *

现在暂停一下，插播我们例行的广告。如果你拥有一家经济特性良好的大型企业，希望与一批同样出色的企业结为伙伴，那么伯克希尔或许正是你寻找的归宿。我们的要求列在第21页。如果你的公司符合这些要求，而我又没能出席你参加的下一场生日聚会，请给我打电话。

1996.english:
## Insurance Operations - Overview

Our insurance business was terrific in 1996.  In both primary insurance, where GEICO is our main unit, and in our "super-cat" reinsurance business, results were outstanding.

As we've explained in past reports, what counts in our insurance business is, first, the amount of "float" we generate and, second, its cost to us.  These are matters that are important for you to understand because float is a major component of Berkshire's intrinsic value that is not reflected in book value.
1996.chinese:
## 保险业务概况

1996年，我们的保险业务表现非常出色。无论是以盖可为主的直接保险业务，还是我们的“超级巨灾”再保险业务，都取得了优异的业绩。

正如我们在以往报告中解释的，保险业务最重要的有两件事：一是能产生多少“浮存金”，二是这些资金的成本是多少。各位需要理解这两点，因为浮存金是伯克希尔内在价值的重要组成部分，却没有体现在账面价值中。

1996.english: To begin with, float is money we hold but don't own.  In an insurance operation, float arises because premiums are received before losses are paid.  Secondly, the premiums that an insurer takes in typically do not cover the losses and expenses it eventually must pay. That leaves it running an "underwriting loss," which is the cost of float.  An insurance business has value if its cost of float over time is less than the cost the company would otherwise incur to obtain funds. But the business is an albatross if the cost of its float is higher than market rates for money.
1996.chinese: 首先，浮存金是由我们持有、却并不属于我们的钱。在保险业务中，保费收取在先，赔款支付在后，由此形成浮存金。其次，保险公司收到的保费，通常不足以覆盖最终必须支付的赔款和费用，因此会出现“承保亏损”，这就是浮存金的成本。如果一家保险公司的浮存金长期成本，低于它通过其他方式筹集资金的成本，那么这门生意就有价值；如果高于市场资金成本，这门生意就会成为沉重的负担。

1996.english: As the numbers in the following table show, Berkshire's insurance business has been a huge winner.  For the table, we have calculated our float -  which we generate in large amounts relative to our premium volume - by adding loss reserves, loss adjustment reserves, funds held under reinsurance assumed and unearned premium reserves, and then subtracting agents' balances, prepaid acquisition costs, prepaid taxes and deferred charges applicable to assumed reinsurance.  Our cost of float is determined by our underwriting loss or profit.  In those years when we have had an underwriting profit, such as the last four, our cost of float has been negative.  In effect, we have been paid for holding money.
1996.chinese: 下表说明，伯克希尔的保险业务取得了巨大的成功。相对于保费收入，我们产生的浮存金很多。表中浮存金的计算方式，是将赔款准备金、理赔费用准备金、分入再保险项下的留存资金及未到期保费准备金相加，再扣除代理人应付保费余额、预付保单取得成本、预付税款，以及分入再保险相关的递延费用。浮存金成本取决于承保亏损或承保利润。在实现承保利润的年份，例如过去四年，我们的浮存金成本为负。也就是说，别人还付钱让我们持有这些资金。

1996.english:
Since 1967, when we entered the insurance business, our float has grown at an annual compounded rate of 22.3%.  In more years than not, our cost of funds has been less than nothing.  This access to "free" money has boosted Berkshire's performance in a major way.  Moreover, our acquisition of GEICO materially increases the probability that we can continue to obtain "free" funds in increasing amounts.

## Super-Cat Insurance

As in the past three years, we once again stress that the good results we are reporting for Berkshire stem in part from our super-cat business having a lucky year.  In this operation, we sell policies that insurance and reinsurance companies buy to protect themselves from the effects of mega-catastrophes.  Since truly major catastrophes are rare occurrences, our super-cat business can be expected to show large profits in most years - and to record a huge loss occasionally.  In other words, the attractiveness of our super-cat business will take a great many years to measure.  What you must understand, however, is that a truly terrible year in the super-cat business is not a possibility - it's a certainty.  The only question is when it will come.
1996.chinese:
自1967年进入保险业以来，我们的浮存金以22.3%的年复合增长率增加。在大多数年份，资金成本甚至低于零。获得这种“免费”资金的能力，极大地推动了伯克希尔的业绩。而收购盖可，又显著提高了我们继续获得越来越多“免费”资金的可能性。

## 超级巨灾保险

和过去三年一样，我们再次强调：伯克希尔所报告的良好业绩，部分来自超级巨灾业务度过了幸运的一年。我们在这项业务中出售保单，保险公司和再保险公司购买它们，以防范特大灾难带来的损失。真正重大的灾难很少发生，因此，可以预期我们的超级巨灾业务在大多数年份都会取得丰厚利润，偶尔则遭受巨额亏损。换句话说，要经过很多年，才能衡量这门生意究竟有多大吸引力。但各位必须理解，超级巨灾业务遭遇极其糟糕的一年，不是“可能”，而是“必然”。唯一的问题，是它什么时候到来。

1996.english: I emphasize this lugubrious point because I would not want you to panic and sell your Berkshire stock upon hearing that some large catastrophe had cost us a significant amount.  If you would tend to react that way, you should not own Berkshire shares now, just as you should entirely avoid owning stocks if a crashing market would lead you to panic and sell.  Selling fine businesses on "scary" news is usually a bad decision.  (Robert Woodruff, the business genius who built Coca-Cola over many decades and who owned a huge position in the company, was once asked when it might be a good time to sell Coke stock.  Woodruff had a simple answer:  "I don't know.  I've never sold any.")
1996.chinese: 我强调这个令人沮丧的事实，是因为我不希望各位一听到某场大灾难让我们损失惨重，就惊慌失措地卖掉伯克希尔股票。如果你会作出这种反应，那么现在就不该持有伯克希尔；同样，如果股市暴跌会让你恐慌抛售，你就应该彻底远离股票。因为“可怕”的消息而出售优秀企业，通常是糟糕的决定。罗伯特·伍德拉夫花了数十年打造可口可乐，是一位商业天才，也持有大量可口可乐股票。有一次，有人问他，什么时候适合卖出可口可乐股票。他的回答很简单：“我不知道，我从来没卖过。”

1996.english: In our super-cat operation, our customers are insurers that are exposed to major earnings volatility and that wish to reduce it.  The product we sell -  for what we hope is an appropriate price -  is our willingness to shift that volatility to our own books.  Gyrations in Berkshire's earnings don't bother us in the least:  Charlie and I would much rather earn a lumpy 15% over time than a smooth 12%.  (After all, our earnings swing wildly on a daily and weekly basis - why should we demand that smoothness accompany each orbit that the earth makes of the sun?)  We are most comfortable with that thinking, however, when we have shareholder/partners who can also accept volatility, and that's why we regularly repeat our cautions.
1996.chinese: 在超级巨灾业务中，我们的客户是那些盈利波动很大、希望降低这种波动的保险公司。我们出售的产品，就是愿意把这种波动转移到自己的账上，并希望为此收到合适的价格。伯克希尔盈利的起伏，丝毫不会困扰我们。查理和我宁愿长期取得起伏不定的15%回报，也不愿取得平平稳稳的12%回报。毕竟，我们的盈利按日、按周来看本来就剧烈波动，为什么非要要求地球每绕太阳一圈，盈利就必须平稳呢？不过，只有股东伙伴也能接受波动时，我们才能最安心地坚持这种思路。这就是我们不断重申这些提醒的原因。

1996.english: We took on some major super-cat exposures during 1996.  At mid-year we wrote a contract with Allstate that covers Florida hurricanes, and though there are no definitive records that would allow us to prove this point, we believe that to have then been the largest single catastrophe risk ever assumed by one company for its own account.  Later in the year, however, we wrote a policy for the California Earthquake Authority that goes into effect on April 1, 1997, and that exposes us to a loss more than twice that possible under the Florida contract.  Again we retained all the risk for our own account.  Large as these coverages are, Berkshire's after-tax "worst-case" loss from a true mega-catastrophe is probably no more than $600 million, which is less than 3% of our book value and 1.5% of our market value.  To gain some perspective on this exposure, look at the table on page 2 and note the much greater volatility that security markets have delivered us.
1996.chinese: 1996年，我们承担了几笔重大的超级巨灾风险。年中，我们与好事达保险公司（Allstate）签订了一份承保佛罗里达飓风风险的合同。虽然没有完整记录可以证明，但我们相信，当时这是有史以来由单家公司自行承担的最大一笔单项巨灾风险。不过，同年稍晚，我们又为加州地震局（California Earthquake Authority）签了一份保单，1997年4月1日生效，其潜在赔付额超过佛罗里达合同的两倍。这次，我们也将风险全部留在自己账上。虽然这些保障金额很大，但真正发生特大灾难时，伯克希尔在“最坏情形”下的税后损失，很可能不超过6亿美元，低于账面净资产的3%，也低于市值的1.5%。若想把这一风险放在适当背景下理解，不妨看看第2页的表格，证券市场带给我们的波动要大得多。

1996.english: In the super-cat business, we have three major competitive advantages. First, the parties buying reinsurance from us know that we both can and will pay under the most adverse of circumstances.  Were a truly cataclysmic disaster to occur, it is not impossible that a financial panic would quickly follow.  If that happened, there could well be respected reinsurers that would have difficulty paying at just the moment that their clients faced extraordinary needs. Indeed, one reason we never "lay off" part of the risks we insure is that we have reservations about our ability to collect from others when disaster strikes.  When it's Berkshire promising, insureds know with certainty that they can collect promptly.
1996.chinese: 在超级巨灾业务中，我们有三项主要竞争优势。第一，向我们购买再保险的客户知道，即使处于最恶劣的环境，我们也有能力、并且愿意支付赔款。如果发生真正毁灭性的灾难，随后迅速出现一场金融恐慌，并非不可能。如果真的如此，一些素有声誉的再保险公司，可能恰恰在客户急需资金的时候难以赔付。事实上，我们从不把承保风险的一部分再转给别人，原因之一就是：灾难来临时，我们对能否从对方那里拿到赔款有所保留。如果作出承诺的是伯克希尔，被保险人就能确信，自己会及时拿到钱。

1996.english: Our second advantage - somewhat related - is subtle but important. After a mega-catastrophe, insurers might well find it difficult to obtain reinsurance even though their need for coverage would then be particularly great.  At such a time, Berkshire would without question have very substantial capacity available - but it will naturally be our long-standing clients that have first call on it.  That business reality has made major insurers and reinsurers throughout the world realize the desirability of doing business with us.  Indeed, we are currently getting sizable "stand- by" fees from reinsurers that are simply nailing down their ability to get coverage from us should the market tighten.
1996.chinese: 第二项优势与第一项多少有关，虽然不那么显眼，却十分重要。特大灾难之后，保险公司对再保险保障的需求会格外强烈，但它们可能很难买到。到那时，伯克希尔无疑仍会拥有非常可观的承保能力，不过，自然要优先满足长期客户。这一商业现实，让世界各地的大型保险和再保险公司都认识到，与我们保持业务往来的好处。事实上，目前有些再保险公司已向我们支付相当可观的“备用保障费”，仅仅是为了确保市场承保能力收紧时，仍能从我们这里获得保障。

1996.english:
Our final competitive advantage is that we can provide dollar coverages of a size neither matched nor approached elsewhere in the industry.  Insurers looking for huge covers know that a single call to Berkshire will produce a firm and immediate offering.

A few facts about our exposure to California earthquakes - our largest risk - seem in order.  The Northridge quake of 1994 laid homeowners' losses on insurers that greatly exceeded what computer models had told them to expect.  Yet the intensity of that quake was mild compared to the "worst- case" possibility for California.  Understandably, insurers became - ahem - shaken and started contemplating a retreat from writing earthquake coverage into their homeowners' policies.
1996.chinese:
最后一项竞争优势，是我们能提供的单笔保障金额，业内其他公司既无法匹敌，也无法接近。需要巨额保障的保险公司知道，只要给伯克希尔打一个电话，就能立即得到确定的报价。

关于我们最大的风险——加州地震——有必要补充一些事实。1994年北岭地震给保险公司带来的住宅保险赔款，远远超出了计算机模型的预测。但与加州可能发生的“最坏情形”相比，那次地震的强度还算温和。不难理解，保险公司也被“震”得不轻，开始考虑不再在住宅保险中提供地震保障。

1996.english: In a thoughtful response, Chuck Quackenbush, California's insurance commissioner, designed a new residential earthquake policy to be written by a state-sponsored insurer, The California Earthquake Authority.  This entity, which went into operation on December 1, 1996, needed large layers of reinsurance - and that's where we came in.  Berkshire's layer of approximately $1 billion will be called upon if the Authority's aggregate losses in the period ending March 31, 2001 exceed about $5 billion.  (The press originally reported larger figures, but these would have applied only if all California insurers had entered into the arrangement; instead only 72% signed up.)
1996.chinese: 加州保险专员查克·夸肯布什（Chuck Quackenbush）作出了审慎的应对：他设计了一种新的住宅地震保单，由州政府推动设立的保险机构——加州地震局——承保。这一机构于1996年12月1日开始运营，需要大规模的分层再保险保障，我们由此参与进来。若截至2001年3月31日的合同期间内，该机构累计损失超过约50亿美元，就会触发伯克希尔承担的约10亿美元保障层。媒体最初报道的数字更大，但那只有在加州所有保险公司都参与这一安排时才成立；实际上，参与比例只有72%。

1996.english: So what are the true odds of our having to make a payout during the policy's term?  We don't know - nor do we think computer models will help us, since we believe the precision they project is a chimera.  In fact, such models can lull decision-makers into a false sense of security and thereby increase their chances of making a really huge mistake.  We've already seen such debacles in both insurance and investments.  Witness "portfolio insurance," whose destructive effects in the 1987 market crash led one wag to observe that it was the computers that should have been jumping out of windows.
1996.chinese: 那么，在保单有效期内，我们需要赔付的真实概率是多少？我们不知道。我们也不认为计算机模型能帮上忙，因为在我们看来，它们展示出来的精确性只是一种幻象。实际上，这类模型可能使决策者产生虚假的安全感，反而增加犯下严重错误的概率。这样的惨败，我们在保险和投资领域都已经见过。看看“投资组合保险”就知道了：它在1987年股灾中造成的破坏，让一位爱开玩笑的人说，该跳窗的是那些计算机。

1996.english: Even if perfection in assessing risks is unattainable, insurers can underwrite sensibly.  After all, you need not know a man's precise age to know that he is old enough to vote nor know his exact weight to recognize his need to diet.  In insurance, it is essential to remember that virtually all surprises are unpleasant, and with that in mind we try to price our super-cat exposures so that about 90% of total premiums end up being eventually paid out in losses and expenses.  Over time, we will find out how smart our pricing has been, but that will not be quickly.  The super- cat business is just like the investment business in that it often takes a long time to find out whether you knew what you were doing.
1996.chinese: 即使无法完美评估风险，保险公司仍可以理性承保。毕竟，你不必知道一个人的准确年龄，也能判断他是否已经达到投票年龄；也不必知道他的准确体重，才能看出他需要减肥。在保险业，必须牢记：几乎所有意外都是坏消息。带着这一认识，我们为超级巨灾风险定价时，力求让最终赔款和费用约占总保费的90%。时间会告诉我们，这些价格定得是否明智，但答案不会很快揭晓。超级巨灾业务和投资业务一样，常常要等很久，才能知道自己当初究竟是否明白在做什么。

1996.english: What I can state with certainty, however, is that we have the best person in the world to run our super-cat business:  Ajit Jain, whose value to Berkshire is simply enormous.  In the reinsurance field, disastrous propositions abound.  I know that because I personally embraced all too many of these in the 1970s and also because GEICO has a large runoff portfolio made up of foolish contracts written in the early-1980s, able though its then-management was.  Ajit, I can assure you, won't make mistakes of this type.
1996.chinese: 不过，有一点我可以肯定：我们有全世界最适合掌管超级巨灾业务的人——阿吉特·贾恩（Ajit Jain）。他对伯克希尔的价值极其巨大。再保险领域充斥着会酿成灾难的交易。我知道这一点，是因为20世纪70年代我本人接下了太多这样的业务；也因为盖可至今仍有一大批停止承接新业务、却尚待逐步结清的旧合同，它们来自20世纪80年代初的愚蠢承保决定，尽管当时的管理层也很能干。我可以向各位保证，阿吉特不会犯这类错误。

1996.english:
I have mentioned that a mega-catastrophe might cause a catastrophe in the financial markets, a possibility that is unlikely but not far-fetched. Were the catastrophe a quake in California of sufficient magnitude to tap our coverage, we would almost certainly be damaged in other ways as well. For example, See's, Wells Fargo and Freddie Mac could be hit hard.  All in all, though, we can handle this aggregation of exposures.

In this respect, as in others, we try to "reverse engineer" our future at Berkshire, bearing in mind Charlie's dictum:  "All I want to know is where I'm going to die so I'll never go there."  (Inverting really works: Try singing country western songs backwards and you will quickly regain your house, your car and your wife.)  If we can't tolerate a possible consequence, remote though it may be, we steer clear of planting its seeds. That is why we don't borrow big amounts and why we make sure that our super-cat business losses, large though the maximums may sound, will not put a major dent in Berkshire's intrinsic value.
1996.chinese:
我刚才提到，特大灾难可能在金融市场上引发另一场灾难。这个概率不大，但绝非无稽之谈。如果加州地震的严重程度足以触发我们的赔付责任，我们几乎肯定还会在其他方面受到损害。例如，喜诗糖果、富国银行和房地美都可能遭受重创。不过，把所有这些风险加在一起，我们依然承受得起。

在这件事上，和在其他事情上一样，我们都试着用逆向思考来安排伯克希尔的未来，并牢记查理那句话：“我只想知道自己会死在哪里，这样我就永远不去那里。”倒过来想确实有用：试着把乡村歌曲倒着唱，你很快就会找回房子、车子和妻子。如果某种可能的后果是我们无法承受的，即使概率再小，我们也不会埋下祸根。这就是我们不大举举债的原因，也是我们为什么一定要确保：超级巨灾业务的最大损失，虽然听起来金额惊人，却不会重创伯克希尔的内在价值。

1996.english:
## Insurance - GEICO and Other Primary Operations

When we moved to total ownership of GEICO early last year, our expectations were high - and they are all being exceeded.  That is true from both a business and personal perspective:  GEICO's operating chief, Tony Nicely, is a superb business manager and a delight to work with. Under almost any conditions, GEICO would be an exceptionally valuable asset.
