
During 1997, both parts of our business grew at a satisfactory rate, with investments increasing by $9,543 per share, or 33.5%, and operating earnings growing by $296.43 per share, or 70.3%. One important caveat: Because we were lucky in our super-cat insurance business (to be discussed later) and because GEICO's underwriting gain was well above what we can expect in most years, our 1997 operating earnings were much better than we anticipated and also more than we expect for 1998.
1997.chinese: 1997年，我们两部分业务的增长都令人满意：每股投资增加9,543美元，增幅33.5%；每股营业利润增加296.43美元，增幅70.3%。但有一个重要提醒：由于超级巨灾保险业务交了好运，稍后会讨论，加上GEICO承保利润远高于多数年份可以预期的水平，1997年的营业利润，远超我们原先预期，也超过我们对1998年的预期。

1997.english: Our rate of progress in both investments and operations is certain to fall in the future. For anyone deploying capital, nothing recedes like success. My own history makes the point: Back in 1951, when I was attending Ben Graham's class at Columbia, an idea giving me a $10,000 gain improved my investment performance for the year by a full 100 percentage points. Today, an idea producing a $500 million pre-tax profit for Berkshire adds one percentage point to our performance. It's no wonder that my annual results in the 1950s were better by nearly thirty percentage points than my annual gains in any subsequent decade. Charlie's experience was similar. We weren't smarter then, just smaller. At our present size, any performance superiority we achieve will be minor.
1997.chinese: 今后，无论投资还是经营业务，我们的进步速度肯定都会下降。对配置资本的人来说，没有什么比成功更能让下一次成功退远。我的经历就能说明问题。1951年，我在哥伦比亚大学上本·格雷厄姆的课时，一个赚1万美元的点子，就能把当年的投资回报提高整整100个百分点。如今，一个为伯克希尔创造5亿美元税前利润的点子，只能给业绩增加一个百分点。难怪我20世纪50年代的年度成绩，比此后任何一个十年期间的年度收益，都高出近30个百分点。查理的经历也类似。当年我们并不是更聪明，只是更小。以目前的规模，哪怕能够取得超额表现，优势也只会很微小。

1997.english: We will be helped, however, by the fact that the businesses to which we have already allocated capital -- both operating subsidiaries and companies in which we are passive investors -- have splendid long-term prospects. We are also blessed with a managerial corps that is unsurpassed in ability and focus. Most of these executives are wealthy and do not need the pay they receive from Berkshire to maintain their way of life. They are motivated by the joy of accomplishment, not by fame or fortune.
1997.chinese: 不过，有一点会帮助我们：已经配置了资本的那些企业，无论是经营子公司，还是我们作为被动投资者持股的公司，长期前景都很出色。我们也很幸运，拥有一支能力与专注程度无人能及的管理队伍。多数高管已经富有，不靠伯克希尔付给他们的薪酬，也能维持生活方式。推动他们的是有所成就的快乐，而非名声或财富。

1997.english:
Though we are delighted with what we own, we are not pleased with our prospects for committing incoming funds. Prices are high for both businesses and stocks. That does not mean that the prices of either will fall -- we have absolutely no view on that matter -- but it does mean that we get relatively little in prospective earnings when we commit fresh money.

Under these circumstances, we try to exert a Ted Williams kind of discipline. In his book The Science of Hitting, Ted explains that he carved the strike zone into 77 cells, each the size of a baseball. Swinging only at balls in his "best" cell, he knew, would allow him to bat .400; reaching for balls in his "worst" spot, the low outside corner of the strike zone, would reduce him to .230. In other words, waiting for the fat pitch would mean a trip to the Hall of Fame; swinging indiscriminately would mean a ticket to the minors.
1997.chinese:
虽然对已经拥有的企业非常满意，但对投入新增资金的前景，我们并不满意。企业和股票的价格都很高。这不意味着两者的价格会跌——在这件事上，我们完全没有看法——但确实意味着，投入新资金时，能够买到的预期利润相对很少。

在这种情况下，我们努力实行特德·威廉斯式的纪律。在《击球的科学》中，特德解释，他把好球区划成77个小格，每格一颗棒球大小。他知道，只对落入“最佳”格子的球挥棒，打击率就能达到四成；若伸手去打“最差”的位置，也就是好球区外侧下角，打击率就会降至两成三。换句话说，等待最甜美的好球，会把你送进名人堂；不分青红皂白乱挥棒，则会送你去小联盟。

1997.english: If they are in the strike zone at all, the business "pitches" we now see are just catching the lower outside corner. If we swing, we will be locked into low returns. But if we let all of today's balls go by, there can be no assurance that the next ones we see will be more to our liking. Perhaps the attractive prices of the past were the aberrations, not the full prices of today. Unlike Ted, we can't be called out if we resist three pitches that are barely in the strike zone; nevertheless, just standing there, day after day, with my bat on my shoulder is not my idea of fun.
1997.chinese: 如今见到的商业机会，即使勉强落在好球区，也只是擦着外侧下角。如果挥棒，我们就会被锁进低回报里；但如果把眼前的球都放过去，也没人能保证下一批会更合心意。或许，过去那些有吸引力的价格才是异常，而今天足价的价格才是常态。与特德不同，即使我们连放三个勉强擦进好球区的球，也不会被判三振出局。不过，日复一日站在那里，球棒搭在肩上，也实在不是我觉得好玩的事。

1997.english:
## Unconventional Commitments

When we can't find our favorite commitment -- a well-run and sensibly-priced business with fine economics -- we usually opt to put new money into very short-term instruments of the highest quality. Sometimes, however, we venture elsewhere. Obviously we believe that the alternative commitments we make are more likely to result in profit than loss. But we also realize that they do not offer the certainty of profit that exists in a wonderful business secured at an attractive price. Finding that kind of opportunity, we know that we are going to make money -- the only question being when. With alternative investments, we think that we are going to make money. But we also recognize that we will sometimes realize losses, occasionally of substantial size.
1997.chinese:
## 非传统投资

找不到最喜欢的投资——经济特性优良、经营得当、价格合理的企业——时，我们通常把新资金投进最高品质的超短期工具。不过，有时也会往别处探一探。显然，我们相信，所作的这些替代投资，盈利的可能性高于亏损；但也清楚，它们不具备以诱人价格买到优秀企业时，那种赚钱的确定性。找到后一种机会，我们知道自己会赚钱，唯一的问题是什么时候。对于替代投资，我们认为自己会赚钱；但也承认，有时会亏，偶尔还会亏得不少。

1997.english: We had three non-traditional positions at yearend. The first was derivative contracts for 14.0 million barrels of oil, that being what was then left of a 45.7 million barrel position we established in 1994-95. Contracts for 31.7 million barrels were settled in 1995-97, and these supplied us with a pre-tax gain of about $61.9 million. Our remaining contracts expire during 1998 and 1999. In these, we had an unrealized gain of $11.6 million at yearend. Accounting rules require that commodity positions be carried at market value. Therefore, both our annual and quarterly financial statements reflect any unrealized gain or loss in these contracts. When we established our contracts, oil for future delivery seemed modestly underpriced. Today, though, we have no opinion as to its attractiveness.
1997.chinese: 年末，我们有三项非传统持仓。第一项是涉及1,400万桶石油的衍生品合约，是1994—1995年建立的4,570万桶头寸的剩余部分。1995—1997年间，3,170万桶的合约已经结算，为我们带来约6,190万美元税前收益。剩余合约将在1998和1999年到期；年末，它们有1,160万美元未实现收益。会计规则要求，商品头寸按市价列账，因此，我们的年度与季度财务报表，都反映这些合约的未实现收益或损失。建立头寸时，远期交付石油的价格，似乎略微偏低；不过，如今它是否有吸引力，我们没有看法。

1997.english: Our second non-traditional commitment is in silver. Last year, we purchased 111.2 million ounces. Marked to market, that position produced a pre-tax gain of $97.4 million for us in 1997. In a way, this is a return to the past for me: Thirty years ago, I bought silver because I anticipated its demonetization by the U.S. Government. Ever since, I have followed the metal's fundamentals but not owned it. In recent years, bullion inventories have fallen materially, and last summer Charlie and I concluded that a higher price would be needed to establish equilibrium between supply and demand. Inflation expectations, it should be noted, play no part in our calculation of silver's value.
1997.chinese: 第二项非传统投资，是白银。去年，我们买入1.112亿盎司，按市价计量，这项头寸在1997年产生9,740万美元税前收益。某种意义上，这是我重返旧日：三十年前，我买过白银，因为预期美国政府会取消其货币用途。此后，我一直跟踪白银的基本面，却没有持有。近几年，白银库存显著下降；去年夏天，查理和我判断，需要更高价格才能使供需达到平衡。应当说明，通胀预期，完全没有参与我们对白银价值的计算。

1997.english: Finally, our largest non-traditional position at yearend was $4.6 billion, at amortized cost, of long-term zero-coupon obligations of the U.S. Treasury. These securities pay no interest. Instead, they provide their holders a return by way of the discount at which they are purchased, a characteristic that makes their market prices move rapidly when interest rates change. If rates rise, you lose heavily with zeros, and if rates fall, you make outsized gains. Since rates fell in 1997, we ended the year with an unrealized pre-tax gain of $598.8 million in our zeros. Because we carry the securities at market value, that gain is reflected in yearend book value.
1997.chinese: 最后，年末最大的一项非传统持仓，是按摊余成本计算46亿美元的美国财政部长期零息债务。这些证券不支付利息，而是靠买入时的折价，为持有人提供回报；这一特性，使其市价在利率变动时迅速变化。利率上升，持有零息债券会损失惨重；利率下降，则能取得格外丰厚的收益。1997年利率下行，因此年末，我们的零息债券有5.988亿美元税前未实现收益。由于按市价列账，这项收益已经反映在年末账面价值里。

1997.english: In purchasing zeros, rather than staying with cash-equivalents, we risk looking very foolish: A macro-based commitment such as this never has anything close to a 100% probability of being successful. However, you pay Charlie and me to use our best judgment -- not to avoid embarrassment -- and we will occasionally make an unconventional move when we believe the odds favor it. Try to think kindly of us when we blow one. Along with President Clinton, we will be feeling your pain: The Munger family has more than 90% of its net worth in Berkshire and the Buffetts more than 99%.
1997.chinese: 买入零息债券，而非继续持有现金等价物，我们冒着显得愚蠢透顶的风险：这种基于宏观因素的投资，成功概率从来不可能接近100%。不过，各位付钱给查理和我，是让我们运用最佳判断，而不是让我们躲开难堪。因此，当我们认为胜算有利时，偶尔会采取非传统行动。搞砸时，请尽量对我们宽厚一点。我们会像克林顿总统一样，感受各位的痛：芒格家族超过90%的净资产在伯克希尔，巴菲特家则超过99%。

1997.english:
## How We Think About Market Fluctuations

A short quiz: If you plan to eat hamburgers throughout your life and are not a cattle producer, should you wish for higher or lower prices for beef? Likewise, if you are going to buy a car from time to time but are not an auto manufacturer, should you prefer higher or lower car prices? These questions, of course, answer themselves.

But now for the final exam: If you expect to be a net saver during the next five years, should you hope for a higher or lower stock market during that period? Many investors get this one wrong. Even though they are going to be net buyers of stocks for many years to come, they are elated when stock prices rise and depressed when they fall. In effect, they rejoice because prices have risen for the "hamburgers" they will soon be buying. This reaction makes no sense. Only those who will be sellers of equities in the near future should be happy at seeing stocks rise. Prospective purchasers should much prefer sinking prices.
1997.chinese:
## 我们怎样看待市场波动

来个小测验：如果你打算一辈子吃汉堡，却不是养牛的，会盼着牛肉涨价，还是降价？同样，如果你隔一阵就要买辆车，却不是汽车制造商，会希望车价更高，还是更低？这些问题，当然不答自明。

现在来期末考试：如果预期未来五年，你会持续净储蓄，那么，你希望这五年股市更高，还是更低？许多投资者答错这一题。虽然往后许多年，他们都会是股票的净买家，却在涨价时兴高采烈、跌价时垂头丧气。实际上，他们是在庆祝自己不久就要买的“汉堡”涨价了。这种反应毫无道理。只有近期准备卖股票的人，才应为上涨高兴。准备买入的人，理应更喜欢价格下跌。

1997.english:
For shareholders of Berkshire who do not expect to sell, the choice is even clearer. To begin with, our owners are automatically saving even if they spend every dime they personally earn: Berkshire "saves" for them by retaining all earnings, thereafter using these savings to purchase businesses and securities. Clearly, the more cheaply we make these buys, the more profitable our owners' indirect savings program will be.

Furthermore, through Berkshire you own major positions in companies that consistently repurchase their shares. The benefits that these programs supply us grow as prices fall: When stock prices are low, the funds that an investee spends on repurchases increase our ownership of that company by a greater amount than is the case when prices are higher. For example, the repurchases that Coca-Cola, The Washington Post and Wells Fargo made in past years at very low prices benefitted Berkshire far more than do today's repurchases, made at loftier prices.
1997.chinese:
对不打算卖出的伯克希尔股东，选择更加清楚。首先，即便把个人挣来的每一分钱都花光，我们的所有者仍在自动储蓄：伯克希尔保留全部利润，替他们“储蓄”，随后用这些钱购买企业与证券。显然，买得越便宜，所有者这项间接储蓄计划，就越赚钱。

此外，通过伯克希尔，各位大量持有一些持续回购自身股票的公司。价格越跌，这些回购计划给我们的好处越大：股价低时，被投资公司花同样的钱回购，我们在其中的所有权比例，就比股价高时增加得更多。比如，可口可乐、《华盛顿邮报》和富国银行，过去以极低价格进行的回购，给伯克希尔带来的好处，远大于今天在高价位上的回购。

1997.english:
At the end of every year, about 97% of Berkshire's shares are held by the same investors who owned them at the start of the year. That makes them savers. They should therefore rejoice when markets decline and allow both us and our investees to deploy funds more advantageously.

So smile when you read a headline that says "Investors lose as market falls." Edit it in your mind to "Disinvestors lose as market falls -- but investors gain." Though writers often forget this truism, there is a buyer for every seller and what hurts one necessarily helps the other. (As they say in golf matches: "Every putt makes someone happy.")
1997.chinese:
每到年末，伯克希尔约97%的股份，仍由年初持有它们的同一批投资者拥有。这说明他们是储蓄者。因此，市场下跌，让我们和被投资企业能更有利地配置资金时，他们应当高兴。

所以，看到“市场下跌，投资者损失惨重”这样的标题，请微笑。在心里把它改成：“市场下跌，撤资者受损，投资者受益。”作者们虽然经常忘记这个简单道理，但每一位卖家，都有对应的买家；伤害一方的，必然帮助另一方。（高尔夫比赛里有句话：“每一次推杆，总有人高兴。”）

1997.english: We gained enormously from the low prices placed on many equities and businesses in the 1970s and 1980s. Markets that then were hostile to investment transients were friendly to those taking up permanent residence. In recent years, the actions we took in those decades have been validated, but we have found few new opportunities. In its role as a corporate "saver," Berkshire continually looks for ways to sensibly deploy capital, but it may be some time before we find opportunities that get us truly excited.
1997.chinese: 20世纪70年代和80年代，许多股票与企业价格低廉，我们从中获益极大。那时的市场，对投资过客不友好，对打算永久安家的人，却很友好。近几年，我们在那些年代采取的行动得到了验证，但新机会很少。作为一名公司形式的“储蓄者”，伯克希尔不断寻找合理配置资本的方法；不过，或许还得等上一阵，才能找到让我们真正兴奋的机会。

1997.english:
## Insurance Operations -- Overview

What does excite us, however, is our insurance business. GEICO is flying, and we expect that it will continue to do so. Before we expound on that, though, let's discuss "float" and how to measure its cost. Unless you understand this subject, it will be impossible for you to make an informed judgment about Berkshire's intrinsic value.

To begin with, float is money we hold but don't own. In an insurance operation, float arises because premiums are received before losses are paid, an interval that sometimes extends over many years. During that time, the insurer invests the money. Typically, this pleasant activity carries with it a downside: The premiums that an insurer takes in usually do not cover the losses and expenses it eventually must pay. That leaves it running an "underwriting loss," which is the cost of float. An insurance business has value if its cost of float over time is less than the cost the company would otherwise incur to obtain funds. But the business is a lemon if its cost of float is higher than market rates for money.
1997.chinese:
## 保险业务概况

不过，我们的保险业务确实让人兴奋。GEICO正在腾飞，我们预期它还会飞下去。但在详谈以前，先讨论浮存金及其成本的衡量。不了解这个问题，就不可能对伯克希尔内在价值作出有根据的判断。

首先，浮存金是我们持有、却不属于我们的钱。在保险业务中，保费先收，赔款后付，两者之间有时相隔多年，这便产生了浮存金。在这段时间里，保险公司把钱拿去投资。不过，这项愉快的活动，通常附带着不愉快的一面：收取的保费，往往不足以支付最终承担的赔款与费用，于是出现“承保亏损”，它就是浮存金的成本。如果长期浮存金成本，低于公司以其他方式筹资所需的成本，这门保险生意便有价值；若高于市场资金价格，这门生意就是个赔钱货。

1997.english: A caution is appropriate here: Because loss costs must be estimated, insurers have enormous latitude in figuring their underwriting results, and that makes it very difficult for investors to calculate a company's true cost of float. Estimating errors, usually innocent but sometimes not, can be huge. The consequences of these miscalculations flow directly into earnings. An experienced observer can usually detect large-scale errors in reserving, but the general public can typically do no more than accept what's presented, and at times I have been amazed by the numbers that big-name auditors have implicitly blessed. As for Berkshire, Charlie and I attempt to be conservative in presenting its underwriting results to you, because we have found that virtually all surprises in insurance are unpleasant ones.
1997.chinese: 这里应当提醒一点：赔款成本必须估计，因此，保险公司在计算承保结果时，有极大裁量空间，投资者也就很难算出真实的浮存金成本。估计错误，通常是无意的，有时却未必，数额可能十分巨大。误算的后果，会直接流入利润。经验丰富的观察者，通常能够发现准备金计提中的重大错误；普通公众往往只能接受报出来的数字。有时，知名审计机构默许的数字，真让我吃惊。在伯克希尔，查理和我努力审慎地向各位报告承保结果，因为我们发现，保险业的意外，几乎全都令人不快。

1997.english: As the numbers in the following table show, Berkshire's insurance business has been a huge winner. For the table, we have calculated our float -- which we generate in large amounts relative to our premium volume -- by adding net loss reserves, loss adjustment reserves, funds held under reinsurance assumed and unearned premium reserves, and then subtracting agents' balances, prepaid acquisition costs, prepaid taxes and deferred charges applicable to assumed reinsurance. Our cost of float is determined by our underwriting loss or profit. In those years when we have had an underwriting profit, such as the last five, our cost of float has been negative. In effect, we have been paid for holding money.
1997.chinese: 下表数字说明，伯克希尔保险业务是一大赢家。相对于保费收入，我们产生了大量浮存金。表中的浮存金，计算方法是将净赔款准备金、理赔费用准备金、分入再保险项下持有资金及未到期保费准备金相加，再减去代理人往来余额、预付业务获取成本、预付税款及与分入再保险有关的递延费用。浮存金成本，由承保亏损或利润决定。像过去五年这样取得承保利润时，我们的浮存金成本就是负的。实际上，别人付钱给我们，让我们替他们拿着钱。

1997.english:
Since 1967, when we entered the insurance business, our float has grown at an annual compounded rate of 21.7%. Better yet, it has cost us nothing, and in fact has made us money. Therein lies an accounting irony: Though our float is shown on our balance sheet as a liability, it has had a value to Berkshire greater than an equal amount of net worth would have had.

The expiration of several large contracts will cause our float to decline during the first quarter of 1998, but we expect it to grow substantially over the long term. We also believe that our cost of float will continue to be highly favorable.
1997.chinese:
自1967年进入保险业以来，我们的浮存金年复合增长率为21.7%。更好的是，它不但没有成本，事实上还替我们赚了钱。这里有一桩会计上的反讽：浮存金虽在资产负债表上列为负债，对伯克希尔的价值，却比同额净资产还高。

几份大合同到期，将使浮存金在1998年第一季度下降，不过，我们预期长期仍会显著增长。我们也相信，浮存金成本将继续非常有利。

1997.english:
## Super-Cat Insurance

Occasionally, however, the cost of our float will spike severely. That will occur because of our heavy involvement in the super-cat business, which by its nature is the most volatile of all insurance lines. In this operation, we sell policies that insurance and reinsurance companies purchase in order to limit their losses when mega-catastrophes strike. Berkshire is the preferred market for sophisticated buyers: When the "big one" hits, the financial strength of super-cat writers will be tested, and Berkshire has no peer in this respect.
1997.chinese:
## 超级巨灾保险

不过，浮存金成本偶尔也会猛烈蹿升。原因在于，我们大量参与超级巨灾业务；从性质上说，它是所有险种中波动最大的一类。我们出售的保单，由保险及再保险公司购买，用来在特大灾难袭来时限制损失。对内行买家，伯克希尔是首选承保方：真正的“大灾”来临时，超级巨灾承保人的财力会受到考验，而在这方面，伯克希尔没有对手。

1997.english: Since truly major catastrophes are rare occurrences, our super-cat business can be expected to show large profits in most years -- and to record a huge loss occasionally. In other words, the attractiveness of our super-cat business will take a great many years to measure. What you must understand, however, is that a truly terrible year in the super-cat business is not a possibility -- it's a certainty. The only question is when it will come.
1997.chinese: 真正的重大灾难很少发生，因此，超级巨灾业务预计多数年份利润丰厚，偶尔却会录得巨额亏损。换句话说，这门生意究竟多有吸引力，要经过很多很多年才能衡量。不过，各位必须明白：超级巨灾业务出现一个糟糕透顶的年份，并非一种可能，而是必然。唯一的问题，是它何时到来。

1997.english: Last year, we were very lucky in our super-cat operation. The world suffered no catastrophes that caused huge amounts of insured damage, so virtually all premiums that we received dropped to the bottom line. This pleasant result has a dark side, however. Many investors who are "innocents" -- meaning that they rely on representations of salespeople rather than on underwriting knowledge of their own -- have come into the reinsurance business by means of purchasing pieces of paper that are called "catastrophe bonds." The second word in this term, though, is an Orwellian misnomer: A true bond obliges the issuer to pay; these bonds, in effect, are contracts that lay a provisional promise to pay on the purchaser.
1997.chinese: 去年，我们的超级巨灾业务非常幸运。世界上没有发生造成巨额承保损失的灾难，所以，收到的保费几乎全部落进了利润。不过，这个愉快结果，也有阴暗的一面。许多“天真”的投资者，也就是依赖销售人员的陈述、而非自己承保知识的人，通过购买一种叫“巨灾债券”的纸片，进入了再保险业。不过，这个名称中的“债券”，实在是奥威尔式的名不副实：真正的债券，要求发行人付款；这些所谓债券，实际上却是让买方作出附条件付款承诺的合同。

1997.english:
This convoluted arrangement came into being because the promoters of the contracts wished to circumvent laws that prohibit the writing of insurance by entities that haven't been licensed by the state. A side benefit for the promoters is that calling the insurance contract a "bond" may also cause unsophisticated buyers to assume that these instruments involve far less risk than is actually the case.

Truly outsized risks will exist in these contracts if they are not properly priced. A pernicious aspect of catastrophe insurance, however, makes it likely that mispricing, even of a severe variety, will not be discovered for a very long time. Consider, for example, the odds of throwing a 12 with a pair of dice -- 1 out of 36. Now assume that the dice will be thrown once a year; that you, the "bond-buyer," agree to pay $50 million if a 12 appears; and that for "insuring" this risk you take in an annual "premium" of $1 million. That would mean you had significantly underpriced the risk. Nevertheless, you could go along for years thinking you were making money -- indeed, easy money. There is actually a 75.4% probability that you would go for a decade without paying out a dime. Eventually, however, you would go broke.
1997.chinese:
之所以弄出这样迂回的安排，是因为合同推销者想绕开法律；法律禁止未经州政府许可的机构承保。对推销者还有一个附带好处：把保险合同称为“债券”，也可能使不懂行的买家以为，这些工具的风险远低于实际水平。

这些合同若定价不当，就会存在极大的风险。不过，巨灾保险有一种恶劣特性，使错误定价即使相当严重，也很可能长时间不被发现。比如，掷两颗骰子，点数之和为12的概率，是三十六分之一。现在假设，每年掷一次；你这位“债券买家”同意，如果掷出12，就支付5,000万美元；作为“承保”这项风险的报酬，每年收取100万美元“保费”。这意味着，你把风险价格定得大大偏低。尽管如此，你仍可能多年都以为自己在赚钱，而且赚得轻轻松松。事实上，十年里一分钱也不用赔的概率，有75.4%。不过，最终你会破产。

1997.english: In this dice example, the odds are easy to figure. Calculations involving monster hurricanes and earthquakes are necessarily much fuzzier, and the best we can do at Berkshire is to estimate a range of probabilities for such events. The lack of precise data, coupled with the rarity of such catastrophes, plays into the hands of promoters, who typically employ an "expert" to advise the potential bond-buyer about the probability of losses. The expert puts no money on the table. Instead, he receives an up-front payment that is forever his no matter how inaccurate his predictions. Surprise: When the stakes are high, an expert can invariably be found who will affirm -- to return to our example -- that the chance of rolling a 12 is not 1 in 36, but more like 1 in 100. (In fairness, we should add that the expert will probably believe that his odds are correct, a fact that makes him less reprehensible -- but more dangerous.)
1997.chinese: 在骰子的例子里，概率容易计算。涉及超级飓风与地震，计算必然模糊得多；在伯克希尔，我们充其量只能估计这些事件的概率范围。数据缺乏精度，灾难又罕见，正好让推销者有机可乘。他们通常请一位“专家”，向潜在债券买家说明损失概率。专家自己不把钱摆上桌，而是预先收取报酬；预测再不准，这钱也永远归他。惊喜来了：只要赌注够大，总能找到一位专家来证明——回到我们的例子——掷出12的概率，并非三十六分之一，更接近百分之一。（公道地说，专家很可能真相信自己的概率正确；这使他没那么可责，却更危险。）

1997.english: The influx of "investor" money into catastrophe bonds -- which may well live up to their name -- has caused super-cat prices to deteriorate materially. Therefore, we will write less business in 1998. We have some large multi-year contracts in force, however, that will mitigate the drop. The largest of these are two policies that we described in last year's report -- one covering hurricanes in Florida and the other, signed with the California Earthquake Authority, covering earthquakes in that state. Our "worst-case" loss remains about $600 million after-tax, the maximum we could lose under the CEA policy. Though this loss potential may sound large, it is only about 1% of Berkshire's market value. Indeed, if we could get appropriate prices, we would be willing to significantly increase our "worst-case" exposure.
1997.chinese: “投资者”的钱涌进巨灾债券——它们很可能真的给人带来一场巨灾——使超级巨灾价格显著恶化。因此，1998年我们会少做一些业务。不过，手里仍有几份多年期大合同，可以缓和下降。最大的是去年报告介绍过的两张保单：一张承保佛罗里达飓风；另一张与加利福尼亚地震管理局签订，承保该州地震。“最坏情形”损失，仍为约6亿美元税后，也就是加州地震管理局保单下可能赔付的最高额。这个潜在损失听来很大，却只约为伯克希尔市值的1%。事实上，只要价格合适，我们愿意大幅提高“最坏情形”的风险敞口。

1997.english:
Our super-cat business was developed from scratch by Ajit Jain, who has contributed to Berkshire's success in a variety of other ways as well. Ajit possesses both the discipline to walk away from business that is inadequately priced and the imagination to then find other opportunities. Quite simply, he is one of Berkshire's major assets. Ajit would have been a star in whatever career he chose; fortunately for us, he enjoys insurance.

Insurance -- GEICO (1-800-555-2756) and Other Primary Operations
1997.chinese:
超级巨灾业务，是阿吉特·贾因从零建立起来的；他还以许多其他方式，为伯克希尔的成功作出贡献。阿吉特既有纪律，能放弃价格不足的业务，又有想象力，随后找到其他机会。简单说，他是伯克希尔的一项主要资产。无论选择什么职业，他都会是明星；幸运的是，他喜欢保险。

## 保险业务 GEICO（1-800-555-2756）及其他原保险业务

1997.english: Last year I wrote about GEICO's Tony Nicely and his terrific management skills. If I had known then what he had in store for us in 1997, I would have searched for still greater superlatives. Tony, now 54, has been with GEICO for 36 years and last year was his best. As CEO, he has transmitted vision, energy and enthusiasm to all members of the GEICO family -- raising their sights from what has been achieved to what can be achieved.
1997.chinese: 去年，我写过GEICO的托尼·奈斯利及其出众的管理本领。如果当时知道他在1997年会带来什么，我就得再找几个更夸张的最高级形容词。托尼如今54岁，已在GEICO工作36年，去年是他最好的一年。作为首席执行官，他把愿景、干劲和热情传递给GEICO大家庭的每位成员，使大家的眼光，从已经取得什么，转向还能够取得什么。

1997.english: We measure GEICO's performance by first, the net increase in its voluntary auto policies (that is, not including policies assigned us by the state) and, second, the profitability of "seasoned" auto business, meaning policies that have been with us for more than a year and are thus past the period in which acquisition costs cause them to be money-losers. In 1996, in-force business grew 10%, and I told you how pleased I was, since that rate was well above anything we had seen in two decades. Then, in 1997, growth jumped to 16%.
1997.chinese: 衡量GEICO表现，首先看自愿投保汽车保单的净增长，不包括州政府分派给我们的保单；其次看“成熟”汽车险业务的盈利能力，也就是投保超过一年、已经度过因获客成本而亏钱阶段的保单。1996年，有效保单增长10%，我当时说过自己多么高兴，因为这一增长率，远高于此前二十年见过的任何水平。接着，1997年增长跃升到16%。

1997.english:
Below are the new business and in-force figures for the last five years:

New Voluntary      Voluntary Auto Years           Auto Policies    Policies in Force

```text
1993              354,882           2,011,055
1994              396,217           2,147,549
1995              461,608           2,310,037
1996              617,669           2,543,699
1997              913,176           2,949,439
```

Of course, any insurer can grow rapidly if it gets careless about underwriting. GEICO's underwriting profit for the year, though, was 8.1% of premiums, far above its average. Indeed, that percentage was higher than we wish it to be: Our goal is to pass on most of the benefits of our low-cost operation to our customers, holding ourselves to about 4% in underwriting profit. With that in mind, we reduced our average rates a bit during 1997 and may well cut them again this year. Our rate changes varied, of course, depending on the policyholder and where he lives; we strive to charge a rate that properly reflects the loss expectancy of each driver.
1997.chinese: 当然，任何保险公司，只要在承保上不讲究，都能快速增长。不过，GEICO全年的承保利润，占保费8.1%，远高于平均水平。事实上，这个百分比，比我们希望的还高：我们的目标，是把低成本经营带来的好处，大部分让给客户，把自己的承保利润控制在约4%。为此，1997年我们略微下调了平均费率，今年很可能再降。当然，费率调整因投保人及居住地而异；我们力求收费恰当反映每名驾驶者的预期赔款损失。

1997.english:
GEICO is not the only auto insurer obtaining favorable results these days. Last year, the industry recorded profits that were far better than it anticipated or can sustain. Intensified competition will soon squeeze margins very significantly. But this is a development we welcome: Long term, a tough market helps the low-cost operator, which is what we are and intend to remain.

Last year I told you about the record 16.9% profit-sharing contribution that GEICO's associates had earned and explained that two simple variables set the amount: policy growth and profitability of seasoned business. I further explained that 1996's performance was so extraordinary that we had to enlarge the chart delineating the possible payouts. The new configuration didn't make it through 1997: We enlarged the chart's boundaries again and awarded our 10,500 associates a profit-sharing contribution amounting to 26.9% of their base compensation, or $71 million. In addition, the same two variables -- policy growth and profitability of seasoned business -- determined the cash bonuses that we paid to dozens of top executives, starting with Tony.
1997.chinese:
近来取得好成绩的汽车保险公司，并非只有GEICO。去年，全行业利润远超预期，也远非可以持续的水平。竞争加剧，很快就会显著挤压利润率。不过，我们欢迎这个变化：长期而言，艰难市场有利于低成本经营者。我们现在就是，而且打算一直做下去。

去年，我告诉各位，GEICO同事赢得了创纪录的16.9%利润分享缴款，并解释，金额由两个简单变量决定：保单增长，以及成熟业务的盈利能力。我还说明，1996年表现太出色，不得不扩大列示潜在奖励的表格范围。这张新表没能撑过1997年：我们又把边界往外扩了一圈，给10,500名同事的利润分享缴款，达到基本薪酬的26.9%，金额7,100万美元。此外，同样两个变量——保单增长与成熟业务盈利能力——也决定了发给托尼等数十位高管的现金奖金。

1997.english: At GEICO, we are paying in a way that makes sense for both our owners and our managers. We distribute merit badges, not lottery tickets: In none of Berkshire's subsidiaries do we relate compensation to our stock price, which our associates cannot affect in any meaningful way. Instead, we tie bonuses to each unit's business performance, which is the direct product of the unit's people. When that performance is terrific -- as it has been at GEICO -- there is nothing Charlie and I enjoy more than writing a big check.
1997.chinese: 在GEICO，我们付报酬的方式，对所有者和管理者都有道理。我们发的是功勋章，不是彩票：伯克希尔所有子公司，都不把薪酬与我们的股价挂钩，因为同事们无法对股价施加有意义的影响。相反，我们把奖金与各单位的经营表现相联系；经营表现，才是该单位员工努力的直接产物。表现像GEICO这样出色时，查理和我最喜欢的事，莫过于开出一张大支票。

1997.english: GEICO's underwriting profitability will probably fall in 1998, but the company's growth could accelerate. We're planning to step on the gas: GEICO's marketing expenditures this year will top $100 million, up 50% from 1997. Our market share today is only 3%, a level of penetration that should increase dramatically in the next decade. The auto insurance industry is huge -- it does about $115 billion of volume annually -- and there are tens of millions of drivers who would save substantial money by switching to us.
1997.chinese: 1998年，GEICO的承保盈利能力可能下降，但增长速度或许会加快。我们准备踩下油门：今年营销支出将超过1亿美元，比1997年增加50%。目前，我们的市场份额只有3%，未来十年，这一渗透水平应当大幅提高。汽车保险业规模庞大，年业务量约1,150亿美元，数千万驾驶者若转到我们这里，可以省下不少钱。

1997.english:
---

In the 1995 report, I described the enormous debt that you and I owe to Lorimer Davidson. On a Saturday early in 1951, he patiently explained the ins and outs of both GEICO and its industry to me -- a 20-year-old stranger who'd arrived at GEICO's headquarters uninvited and unannounced. Davy later became the company's CEO and has remained my friend and teacher for 47 years. The huge rewards that GEICO has heaped on Berkshire would not have materialized had it not been for his generosity and wisdom. Indeed, had I not met Davy, I might never have grown to understand the whole field of insurance, which over the years has played such a key part in Berkshire's success.
1997.chinese:
---

1995年报告里，我描述过，各位和我欠洛里默·戴维森多么大一份情。1951年初的一个星期六，他耐心地向我解释GEICO及保险业的来龙去脉；当时我不过是个20岁的陌生人，不请自来，也没有事先通知，就到了GEICO总部。戴维后来成了公司首席执行官，47年来，一直是我的朋友和老师。若非他的慷慨与智慧，GEICO为伯克希尔带来的巨大回报，就不会出现。事实上，若没见过戴维，我或许永远也不会逐渐理解整个保险领域；而这些年来，它在伯克希尔的成功中，发挥了如此关键的作用。

1997.english:
Davy turned 95 last year, and it's difficult for him to travel. Nevertheless, Tony and I hope that we can persuade him to attend our annual meeting, so that our shareholders can properly thank him for his important contributions to Berkshire. Wish us luck.

---

Though they are, of course, far smaller than GEICO, our other primary insurance operations turned in results last year that, in aggregate, were fully as stunning. National Indemnity's traditional business had an underwriting profit of 32.9% and, as usual, developed a large amount of float compared to premium volume. Over the last three years, this segment of our business, run by Don Wurster, has had a profit of 24.3%. Our homestate operation, managed by Rod Eldred, recorded an underwriting profit of 14.1% even though it continued to absorb the expenses of geographical expansion. Rod's three-year record is an amazing 15.1%. Berkshire's workers' compensation business, run out of California by Brad Kinstler, had a modest underwriting loss in a difficult environment; its three-year underwriting record is a positive 1.5%. John Kizer, at Central States Indemnity, set a new volume record while generating good underwriting earnings. At Kansas Bankers Surety, Don Towle more than lived up to the high expectations we had when we purchased the company in 1996.
1997.chinese:
戴维去年满95岁，出门旅行已很困难。不过，托尼和我希望能劝他参加股东大会，让股东们有机会，好好感谢他为伯克希尔作出的重要贡献。祝我们好运吧。

---

其他原保险业务的规模，当然远小于GEICO，不过，去年的总体成绩，同样令人惊叹。国民赔偿公司的传统业务，承保利润率32.9%，照例相对于保费收入，产生了大量浮存金。唐·沃斯特负责的这部分业务，过去三年利润率为24.3%。罗德·埃尔德雷德管理的本州保险业务，虽然继续负担地域扩张费用，承保利润率仍达14.1%，三年纪录更达到惊人的15.1%。布拉德·金斯特勒在加州管理的工伤赔偿保险业务，在艰难环境中出现小额承保亏损，三年承保纪录则为正1.5%。中央州赔偿公司的约翰·基泽，一边取得良好承保利润，一边把业务量推至新纪录。堪萨斯银行家担保公司的唐·托尔，则远远超过了我们1996年收购时对他的高度期待。

1997.english:
In aggregate, these five operations recorded an underwriting profit of 15.0%. The two Dons, along with Rod, Brad and John, have created significant value for Berkshire, and we believe there is more to come.

## Look-Through Earnings

Reported earnings are a poor measure of economic progress at Berkshire, in part because the numbers shown in the table presented earlier include only the dividends we receive from investees -- though these dividends typically represent only a small fraction of the earnings attributable to our ownership. Not that we mind this division of money, since on balance we regard the undistributed earnings of investees as more valuable to us than the portion paid out. The reason is simple: Our investees often have the opportunity to reinvest earnings at high rates of return. So why should we want them paid out?
1997.chinese:
## 穿透盈余

报表利润，不能很好地衡量伯克希尔的经济进展。部分原因是，前表只列入从被投资企业收到的股息，而股息通常只占按我们持股比例应归属利润的一小部分。这种资金分配方式，我们并不介意；整体上，我们认为，被投资企业未分配的利润，对我们的价值，高于分出来的部分。原因很简单：它们经常有机会把利润再投资，取得高回报。既然如此，我们干吗非要拿出来？

1997.english: To depict something closer to economic reality at Berkshire than reported earnings, though, we employ the concept of "look-through" earnings. As we calculate these, they consist of: (1) the operating earnings reported in the previous section, plus; (2) our share of the retained operating earnings of major investees that, under GAAP accounting, are not reflected in our profits, less; (3) an allowance for the tax that would be paid by Berkshire if these retained earnings of investees had instead been distributed to us. When tabulating "operating earnings" here, we exclude purchase-accounting adjustments as well as capital gains and other major non-recurring items.
1997.chinese: 为了更贴近伯克希尔的经济现实，而非只看报表利润，我们采用“穿透盈余”概念。我们的计算包括：（1）上节报告的营业利润；加上（2）主要被投资企业留存的、按我们持股比例应归属的营业利润，这部分按GAAP不反映在我们的利润里；减去（3）假如这些留存利润分配给我们，伯克希尔应当支付的估计税款。这里列示“营业利润”时，我们剔除购买会计调整、资本利得及其他重大非经常项目。

## 1997年的收购

1997年，我们同意收购星星家具，以及国际冰雪皇后，后者于1998年初完成。这两家公司完全符合我们的标准：容易理解，经济特性出色，由优秀的人经营。

1997.english:
The Star transaction has an interesting history. Whenever we buy into an industry whose leading participants aren't known to me, I always ask our new partners, "Are there any more at home like you?" Upon our purchase of Nebraska Furniture Mart in 1983, therefore, the Blumkin family told me about three outstanding furniture retailers in other parts of the country. At the time, however, none was for sale.

Many years later, Irv Blumkin learned that Bill Child, CEO of R.C. Willey -- one of the recommended three -- might be interested in merging, and we promptly made the deal described in the 1995 report. We have been delighted with that association -- Bill is the perfect partner. Furthermore, when we asked Bill about industry standouts, he came up with the remaining two names given me by the Blumkins, one of these being Star Furniture of Houston. But time went by without there being any indication that either of the two was available.
1997.chinese:
星星家具交易的来历很有意思。每当买入一个我不熟悉主要参与者的行业，我总会问新伙伴：“你们这一行，还有像你们这样的吗？”因此，1983年买下内布拉斯加家具卖场时，布拉姆金家族给我介绍了全国其他地区三家优秀的家具零售商。不过，当时没有一家想卖。

许多年以后，欧文·布拉姆金获悉，三家推荐企业之一、R.C.威利的首席执行官比尔·蔡尔德，或许有意合并，我们随即完成了1995年报告中介绍的那笔交易。我们对这段合作十分满意，比尔是完美的伙伴。此外，问他行业里还有哪些佼佼者时，他说出的其余两个名字，恰好与布拉姆金家族当年告诉我的相同，其中一家就是休斯敦的星星家具。不过，时间不断过去，两家都没有露出愿意出售的意思。

1997.english:
On the Thursday before last year's annual meeting, however, Bob Denham of Salomon told me that Melvyn Wolff, the long-time controlling shareholder and CEO of Star, wanted to talk. At our invitation, Melvyn came to the meeting and spent his time in Omaha confirming his positive feelings about Berkshire. I, meanwhile, looked at Star's financials, and liked what I saw.

A few days later, Melvyn and I met in New York and made a deal in a single, two-hour session. As was the case with the Blumkins and Bill Child, I had no need to check leases, work out employment contracts, etc. I knew I was dealing with a man of integrity and that's what counted.
1997.chinese:
然而，去年股东大会前的星期四，所罗门的鲍勃·德纳姆告诉我，星星家具长期控股股东兼首席执行官梅尔文·沃尔夫，希望谈谈。应我们的邀请，梅尔文来到大会，并利用在奥马哈的时间，确认了自己对伯克希尔的良好印象。与此同时，我看了星星家具的财务资料，所见令我满意。

几天后，梅尔文和我在纽约见面，一次两小时的交谈，就把交易敲定。与布拉姆金家族及比尔·蔡尔德的情况一样，我不用检查租约，也不用拟定雇用合同等等。我知道，自己在与一位正直的人打交道，这才要紧。

1997.english:
Though the Wolff family's association with Star dates back to 1924, the business struggled until Melvyn and his sister Shirley Toomin took over in 1962. Today Star operates 12 stores -- ten in Houston and one each in Austin and Bryan -- and will soon move into San Antonio as well. We won't be surprised if Star is many times its present size a decade from now.

Here's a story illustrating what Melvyn and Shirley are like: When they told their associates of the sale, they also announced that Star would make large, special payments to those who had helped them succeed -- and then defined that group as everyone in the business. Under the terms of our deal, it was Melvyn and Shirley's money, not ours, that funded this distribution. Charlie and I love it when we become partners with people who behave like that.
1997.chinese:
沃尔夫家族与星星家具的渊源，可以追溯到1924年，但直到1962年梅尔文与妹妹雪莉·图明接手之前，企业一直经营艰难。如今，星星家具经营12家门店：休斯敦十家，奥斯汀与布赖恩各一家；不久也将进驻圣安东尼奥。如果十年后，规模达到今天的许多倍，我们不会吃惊。

讲个故事，说明梅尔文与雪莉是什么样的人。告诉同事们公司出售的消息时，他们同时宣布，星星家具将特别发放大笔奖金，感谢那些帮助他们取得成功的人；随后，他们把这群人定义为公司每一个人。按交易条款，这笔分配出自梅尔文和雪莉自己的钱，不是我们的。查理和我最喜欢与这样做事的人成为伙伴。

1997.english:
The Star transaction closed on July 1. In the months since, we've watched Star's already-excellent sales and earnings growth accelerate further. Melvyn and Shirley will be at the annual meeting, and I hope you get a chance to meet them.

Next acquisition: International Dairy Queen. There are 5,792 Dairy Queen stores operating in 23 countries -- all but a handful run by franchisees -- and in addition IDQ franchises 409 Orange Julius operations and 43 Karmelkorn operations. In 190 locations, "treat centers" provide some combination of the three products.
1997.chinese:
星星家具交易于7月1日完成。此后几个月，我们看到，本来已经很好的销售与利润增长，又进一步加速。梅尔文和雪莉都会参加股东大会，希望各位有机会认识他们。

下一项收购：国际冰雪皇后。23个国家共有5,792家冰雪皇后门店，除极少数外，全部由加盟商经营。此外，国际冰雪皇后还拥有409家Orange Julius和43家Karmelkorn的特许经营业务。在190个地点，“甜食中心”提供上述三类产品的某种组合。

1997.english:
For many years IDQ had a bumpy history. Then, in 1970, a Minneapolis group led by John Mooty and Rudy Luther took control. The new managers inherited a jumble of different franchising agreements, along with some unwise financing arrangements that had left the company in a precarious condition. In the years that followed, management rationalized the operation, extended food service to many more locations, and, in general, built a strong organization.

Last summer Mr. Luther died, which meant his estate needed to sell stock. A year earlier, Dick Kiphart of William Blair & Co., had introduced me to John Mooty and Mike Sullivan, IDQ's CEO, and I had been impressed with both men. So, when we got the chance to merge with IDQ, we offered a proposition patterned on our FlightSafety acquisition, extending selling shareholders the option of choosing either cash or Berkshire shares having a slightly lower immediate value. By tilting the consideration as we did, we encouraged holders to opt for cash, the type of payment we by far prefer. Even then, only 45% of IDQ shares elected cash.
1997.chinese:
多年来，国际冰雪皇后发展坎坷。1970年，由约翰·穆蒂与鲁迪·卢瑟率领的明尼阿波利斯投资团体，取得控制权。新管理层接下的是一堆杂乱的特许经营协议，以及若干不明智的融资安排；后者已把公司推到危险境地。此后的岁月里，管理层理顺业务，把食品供应扩展到更多门店，总体上建立起一家强健的企业。

去年夏天，卢瑟先生去世，他的遗产因此需要出售股票。一年前，威廉·布莱尔公司的迪克·基法特，把约翰·穆蒂与国际冰雪皇后首席执行官迈克·沙利文介绍给我，两位都给我留下了很好的印象。因此，得到合并机会时，我们提出了类似收购飞安国际时的方案：卖方股东可以选择现金，或者即时价值略低一点的伯克希尔股票。这样倾斜对价，是为了鼓励股东选现金，因为我们远远更喜欢现金支付。即便如此，仍只有45%的国际冰雪皇后股份选择现金。

1997.english:
Charlie and I bring a modicum of product expertise to this transaction: He has been patronizing the Dairy Queens in Cass Lake and Bemidji, Minnesota, for decades, and I have been a regular in Omaha. We have put our money where our mouth is.

## A Confession

I've mentioned that we strongly prefer to use cash rather than Berkshire stock in acquisitions. A study of the record will tell you why: If you aggregate all of our stock-only mergers (excluding those we did with two affiliated companies, Diversified Retailing and Blue Chip Stamps), you will find that our shareholders are slightly worse off than they would have been had I not done the transactions. Though it hurts me to say it, when I've issued stock, I've cost you money.
1997.chinese:
查理和我，在这笔交易上也带来了一点产品专长：几十年来，他一直光顾明尼苏达州卡斯莱克和贝米吉的冰雪皇后，我则是奥马哈店的常客。这回，我们把钱放进了嘴巴常去的地方。

## 一份坦白

我提到过，我们收购时，强烈偏爱现金，而非伯克希尔股票。研究一下纪录，就知道原因：如果把全部纯换股合并加在一起，剔除与多元化零售和蓝筹印花这两家关联公司的交易，就会发现，与我什么也没做相比，我们股东的境况反而略差。说出来很痛，但每当我发行股票，我都让各位损失了钱。

1997.english:
Be clear about one thing: This cost has not occurred because we were misled in any way by sellers or because they thereafter failed to manage with diligence and skill. On the contrary, the sellers were completely candid when we were negotiating our deals and have been energetic and effective ever since.

Instead, our problem has been that we own a truly marvelous collection of businesses, which means that trading away a portion of them for something new almost never makes sense. When we issue shares in a merger, we reduce your ownership in all of our businesses -- partly-owned companies such as Coca-Cola, Gillette and American Express, and all of our terrific operating companies as well. An example from sports will illustrate the difficulty we face: For a baseball team, acquiring a player who can be expected to bat .350 is almost always a wonderful event -- except when the team must trade a .380 hitter to make the deal.
1997.chinese:
有一件事必须说清：这种代价，绝不是因为卖方以任何方式误导了我们，也不是因为他们后来经营不够勤勉、能干。相反，谈交易时，卖方完全坦诚；交易以后，也始终干劲十足、卓有成效。

真正的问题，是我们已经拥有一组极为出色的企业。因此，拿其中一部分换新东西，几乎从来不划算。合并时发行股票，就会减少各位在我们全部企业里的所有权，包括可口可乐、吉列、美国运通这类部分持有的公司，也包括全部优秀的经营公司。用体育打个比方，就知道困难在哪：一支棒球队，能得到一个预期打击率三成五的球员，几乎总是好事；但如果为了成交，必须送走一个打击率三成八的球员，就另当别论了。

1997.english: Because our roster is filled with .380 hitters, we have tried to pay cash for acquisitions, and here our record has been far better. Starting with National Indemnity in 1967, and continuing with, among others, See's, Buffalo News, Scott Fetzer and GEICO, we have acquired -- for cash -- a number of large businesses that have performed incredibly well since we bought them. These acquisitions have delivered Berkshire tremendous value -- indeed, far more than I anticipated when we made our purchases.
1997.chinese: 我们的阵容里，满是三成八的打者，所以我们努力用现金收购，在这方面，纪录好得多。从1967年国民赔偿公司开始，接着是喜诗、《布法罗新闻报》、斯科特与费策和GEICO等，我们用现金买下了一批大企业；买入以后，它们的表现好得惊人。这些收购给伯克希尔带来巨大价值，事实上，远超我当初买入时的预期。

1997.english:
We believe that it is almost impossible for us to "trade up" from our present businesses and managements. Our situation is the opposite of Camelot's Mordred, of whom Guenevere commented, "The one thing I can say for him is that he is bound to marry well. Everybody is above him." Marrying well is extremely difficult for Berkshire.

So you can be sure that Charlie and I will be very reluctant to issue shares in the future. In those cases when we simply must do so -- when certain shareholders of a desirable acquiree insist on getting stock -- we will include an attractive cash option in order to tempt as many of the sellers to take cash as is possible.
1997.chinese:
我们认为，从现有企业与管理层出发，想通过交换升级，几乎不可能。我们的处境，与《卡米洛特》里的莫德雷德恰好相反。桂妮薇儿评价他说：“我唯一能替他说的，就是他肯定娶得好。随便谁都比他强。”对伯克希尔，想高攀一门好亲事，实在太难。

所以，各位可以放心，今后查理和我会极不愿意发行股票。某些确实必须这样做的情形，比如想收购的好公司，某些股东坚持要股票，我们也会附上诱人的现金选项，尽可能吸引更多卖方收取现金。

1997.english: Merging with public companies presents a special problem for us. If we are to offer any premium to the acquiree, one of two conditions must be present: Either our own stock must be overvalued relative to the acquiree's, or the two companies together must be expected to earn more than they would if operated separately. Historically, Berkshire has seldom been overvalued. In this market, moreover, undervalued acquirees are almost impossible to find. That other possibility -- synergy gains -- is usually unrealistic, since we expect acquirees to operate after we've bought them just as they did before. Joining with Berkshire does not normally raise their revenues nor cut their costs.
1997.chinese: 与上市公司合并，对我们有个特殊问题。只要向被收购方支付任何溢价，必须符合两个条件之一：要么，我们自己的股票，相对于对方估值过高；要么，两家公司合并后的预期利润，高于各自独立经营之和。历史上，伯克希尔很少被高估。而在眼下的市场，被低估的收购对象，也几乎找不到。另一个可能，也就是协同收益，通常并不现实；我们希望收购之后，对方仍像从前那样经营。加入伯克希尔，通常既不会增加它们的收入，也不会削减成本。

1997.english: Indeed, their reported costs (but not their true ones) will rise after they are bought by Berkshire if the acquiree has been granting options as part of its compensation packages. In these cases, "earnings" of the acquiree have been overstated because they have followed the standard -- but, in our view, dead wrong -- accounting practice of ignoring the cost to a business of issuing options. When Berkshire acquires an option-issuing company, we promptly substitute a cash compensation plan having an economic value equivalent to that of the previous option plan. The acquiree's true compensation cost is thereby brought out of the closet and charged, as it should be, against earnings.
1997.chinese: 事实上，如果被收购公司原来把期权作为薪酬的一部分，买入后，它的报表成本会增加，真实成本却不会。原先，它们遵照通行的会计惯例，忽略发行期权给企业带来的成本，因而高报了“利润”；在我们看来，这种惯例错得彻底。伯克希尔收购发放期权的公司后，会迅速换成经济价值与原期权计划相当的现金薪酬计划。于是，对方真实的薪酬成本，被从柜子里拉到明处，并且理所当然地，从利润中扣除。

1997.english: The reasoning that Berkshire applies to the merger of public companies should be the calculus for all buyers. Paying a takeover premium does not make sense for any acquirer unless a) its stock is overvalued relative to the acquiree's or b) the two enterprises will earn more combined than they would separately. Predictably, acquirers normally hew to the second argument because very few are willing to acknowledge that their stock is overvalued. However, voracious buyers -- the ones that issue shares as fast as they can print them -- are tacitly conceding that point. (Often, also, they are running Wall Street's version of a chain-letter scheme.)
1997.chinese: 伯克希尔对上市公司合并所作的分析，应该成为所有买家的算法。除非（a）收购方股票相对于被收购方高估，或者（b）两家企业合并后的利润，高于分别经营之和，否则任何买家支付收购溢价，都没有道理。不出所料，收购方通常抓住第二点，因为肯承认自己股票高估的，寥寥无几。不过，那些贪得无厌、股票印多快就发多快的买家，已经默默承认了这一点。（此外，它们经常还在经营华尔街版本的连锁信骗局。）

1997.english: In some mergers there truly are major synergies -- though oftentimes the acquirer pays too much to obtain them -- but at other times the cost and revenue benefits that are projected prove illusory. Of one thing, however, be certain: If a CEO is enthused about a particularly foolish acquisition, both his internal staff and his outside advisors will come up with whatever projections are needed to justify his stance. Only in fairy tales are emperors told that they are naked.
1997.chinese: 有些合并，确实存在重大协同效益，虽然收购方往往为此付得太多；但另一些时候，预测中的成本与收入好处，最后证明只是幻影。不过，有一件事可以确定：如果首席执行官热衷于一项格外愚蠢的收购，他的内部员工与外部顾问，会拿出任何所需预测，证明他的立场正确。只有童话里，皇帝才会被告知自己没穿衣服。

1997.english:

We made net sales during the year that amounted to about 5% of our beginning portfolio. In these, we significantly reduced a few of our holdings that are below the $750 million threshold for itemization, and we also modestly trimmed a few of the larger positions that we detail. Some of the sales we made during 1997 were aimed at changing our bond-stock ratio moderately in response to the relative values that we saw in each market, a realignment we have continued in 1998.
1997.chinese:
*成本为计税成本，合计比GAAP成本低18亿美元。

全年净卖出，约占年初投资组合的5%。其中，若干低于7.5亿美元逐项列示门槛的持仓，被我们大幅削减；表内一些较大持仓，也作了小幅缩减。1997年部分出售，旨在根据我们对债券与股票市场相对价值的看法，适度调整股债比例。这种调整，在1998年仍在继续。

1997.english:
Our reported positions, we should add, sometimes reflect the investment decisions of GEICO's Lou Simpson. Lou independently runs an equity portfolio of nearly $2 billion that may at times overlap the portfolio that I manage, and occasionally he makes moves that differ from mine.

Though we don't attempt to predict the movements of the stock market, we do try, in a very rough way, to value it. At the annual meeting last year, with the Dow at 7,071 and long-term Treasury yields at 6.89%, Charlie and I stated that we did not consider the market overvalued if 1) interest rates remained where they were or fell, and 2) American business continued to earn the remarkable returns on equity that it had recently recorded. So far, interest rates have fallen -- that's one requisite satisfied -- and returns on equity still remain exceptionally high. If they stay there -- and if interest rates hold near recent levels -- there is no reason to think of stocks as generally overvalued. On the other hand, returns on equity are not a sure thing to remain at, or even near, their present levels.
1997.chinese:
还要补充，报告中的持仓，有时也反映了GEICO的卢·辛普森的投资决定。卢独立管理近20亿美元的股票组合，有时与我管理的组合重叠，偶尔也会采取与我不同的行动。

虽然不试图预测股市走势，我们仍会极粗略地估计它的价值。去年股东大会上，道指7,071点，长期国债收益率6.89%，查理和我表示，只要（1）利率维持当时水平或下降，（2）美国企业继续取得近期那种非凡的股东权益回报，我们就不认为市场高估。到目前，利率下降了，一个条件得到满足；股东权益回报也仍然异常高。如果回报保持在那里，而且利率维持近期水平附近，就没有理由认为股票整体高估。不过，另一方面，股东权益回报能否保持在目前水平，甚至附近，并没有保证。

1997.english: In the summer of 1979, when equities looked cheap to me, I wrote a Forbes article entitled "You pay a very high price in the stock market for a cheery consensus." At that time skepticism and disappointment prevailed, and my point was that investors should be glad of the fact, since pessimism drives down prices to truly attractive levels. Now, however, we have a very cheery consensus. That does not necessarily mean this is the wrong time to buy stocks: Corporate America is now earning far more money than it was just a few years ago, and in the presence of lower interest rates, every dollar of earnings becomes more valuable. Today's price levels, though, have materially eroded the "margin of safety" that Ben Graham identified as the cornerstone of intelligent investing.
1997.chinese: 1979年夏天，股票在我看来很便宜，我为《福布斯》写了一篇文章，题为《在股市，乐观一致要付出高昂代价》。当时，怀疑与失望占上风；我的意思是，投资者应为此高兴，因为悲观把价格压到真正诱人的水平。不过，如今大家一致乐观。这不一定意味着，现在买股票的时机不对：美国企业赚的钱，远多于短短几年前，而利率较低，使每一美元利润都更值钱。不过，今天的价位，确实大幅侵蚀了本·格雷厄姆视为理性投资基石的“安全边际”。

1997.english:
---

In last year's annual report, I discussed Coca-Cola, our largest holding. Coke continues to increase its market dominance throughout the world, but, tragically, it has lost the leader responsible for its outstanding performance. Roberto Goizueta, Coke's CEO since 1981, died in October. After his death, I read every one of the more than 100 letters and notes he had written me during the past nine years. Those messages could well serve as a guidebook for success in both business and life.
1997.chinese:
---

去年年报中，我讨论过我们最大的持仓可口可乐。它继续增强全球市场优势，但令人悲痛的是，缔造其出色表现的领导者去世了。自1981年担任首席执行官的罗伯托·戈伊苏埃塔，于10月去世。之后，我把过去九年他写给我的一百多封信与便笺，一封一封重读。那些文字，足可以成为商业与人生的成功指南。

1997.english: In these communications, Roberto displayed a brilliant and clear strategic vision that was always aimed at advancing the well-being of Coke shareholders. Roberto knew where he was leading the company, how he was going to get there, and why this path made the most sense for his owners -- and, equally important, he had a burning sense of urgency about reaching his goals. An excerpt from one handwritten note he sent to me illustrates his mind-set: "By the way, I have told Olguita that what she refers to as an obsession, you call focus. I like your term much better." Like all who knew Roberto, I will miss him enormously.
1997.chinese: 在这些通信里，罗伯托展现出卓越、清晰的战略眼光，始终以增进可口可乐股东福祉为目标。他知道，要把公司带到哪里，怎样到达，以及为什么这条路对所有者最合理；同样重要的是，对于实现目标，他有一种炽热的紧迫感。他给我的一张手写便笺，足以说明其心态：“顺便说一句，我告诉奥尔吉塔了：她说我痴迷的那个毛病，你叫它专注。我更喜欢你的说法。”和所有认识他的人一样，我会非常想念罗伯托。

1997.english:
Consistent with his concern for the company, Roberto prepared for a seamless succession long before it seemed necessary. Roberto knew that Doug Ivester was the right man to take over and worked with Doug over the years to ensure that no momentum would be lost when the time for change arrived. The Coca-Cola Company will be the same steamroller under Doug as it was under Roberto.

## Convertible Preferreds

Two years ago, I gave you an update on the five convertible preferreds that we purchased through private placements in the 1987-1991 period. At the time of that earlier report, we had realized a small profit on the sale of our Champion International holding. The four remaining preferred commitments included two, Gillette and First Empire State, that we had converted into common stock in which we had large unrealized gains, and two others, USAir and Salomon, that had been trouble-prone. At times, the last two had me mouthing a line from a country song: "How can I miss you if you won't go away?"
1997.chinese:
一如他对公司的关切，早在看起来还没必要时，罗伯托就已为平稳接班作好准备。他知道，道格·伊维斯特是接手的合适人选，多年来与道格合作，确保换班时不丢掉任何势头。在道格领导下，可口可乐公司仍会像罗伯托时代一样，是一台势不可挡的压路机。

## 可转换优先股

两年前，我向各位更新过五项可转换优先股的情况。它们是我们1987—1991年间通过私募买入的。写那份报告时，冠军国际持仓已出售，取得小额利润。余下四项中，吉列与第一帝国州已经转为普通股，积累了巨额未实现收益；另外两项，USAir与所罗门，则麻烦不断。有时，后两项让我不由得念起一首乡村歌曲的歌词：“你一直赖着不走，叫我怎么想念你？”

1997.english:
Since I delivered that report, all four holdings have grown significantly in value. The common stocks of both Gillette and First Empire have risen substantially, in line with the companies' excellent performance. At yearend, the $600 million we put into Gillette in 1989 had appreciated to $4.8 billion, and the $40 million we committed to First Empire in 1991 had risen to $236 million.

Our two laggards, meanwhile, have come to life in a very major way. In a transaction that finally rewarded its long-suffering shareholders, Salomon recently merged into Travelers Group. All of Berkshire's shareholders -- including me, very personally -- owe a huge debt to Deryck Maughan and Bob Denham for, first, playing key roles in saving Salomon from extinction following its 1991 scandal and, second, restoring the vitality of the company to a level that made it an attractive acquisition for Travelers. I have often said that I wish to work with executives that I like, trust and admire. No two fit that description better than Deryck and Bob.
1997.chinese:
那份报告发表以后，四项持仓的价值都显著增长。吉列与第一帝国州普通股大涨，与公司出色的经营表现一致。年末，我们1989年投进吉列的6亿美元，已升值到48亿美元；1991年投入第一帝国州的4,000万美元，则增至2.36亿美元。

与此同时，两个落后分子，也大大活过来了。最近，所罗门并入旅行者集团，终于给长期受苦的股东带来回报。伯克希尔全体股东，包括我本人，都欠德里克·莫恩与鲍勃·德纳姆极大的人情：首先，1991年丑闻之后，他们在挽救所罗门免于灭亡的过程中，发挥了关键作用；其次，他们恢复了公司活力，使它足以成为旅行者眼中有吸引力的收购对象。我常说，希望与自己喜欢、信任并钦佩的高管共事。没有谁比德里克与鲍勃更符合这句话。

1997.english: Berkshire's final results from its Salomon investment won't be tallied for some time, but it is safe to say that they will be far better than I anticipated two years ago. Looking back, I think of my Salomon experience as having been both fascinating and instructional, though for a time in 1991-92 I felt like the drama critic who wrote: "I would have enjoyed the play except that I had an unfortunate seat. It faced the stage."
1997.chinese: 所罗门投资的最终成绩，还得过一阵才能结算，不过可以肯定，会远好于我两年前的预期。回头看，这段经历既引人入胜，又很有教育意义；但1991—1992年的某段时间，我觉得自己很像那位戏剧评论家。他写道：“要不是座位实在不幸，我本来会很喜欢这出戏。我的座位正对着舞台。”

1997.english:
The resuscitation of US Airways borders on the miraculous. Those who have watched my moves in this investment know that I have compiled a record that is unblemished by success. I was wrong in originally purchasing the stock, and I was wrong later, in repeatedly trying to unload our holdings at 50 cents on the dollar.

Two changes at the company coincided with its remarkable rebound: 1) Charlie and I left the board of directors and 2) Stephen Wolf became CEO. Fortunately for our egos, the second event was the key: Stephen Wolf's accomplishments at the airline have been phenomenal.
1997.chinese:
美国航空公司的起死回生，几乎堪称奇迹。一直留意我在这项投资中举动的人都知道，我的纪录纯粹得很，没有被任何成功玷污。当初买股票，我错了；后来一再想按每美元本金50美分的价格脱手，我也错了。

公司惊人反弹的同时，发生了两个变化：（1）查理和我退出董事会；（2）斯蒂芬·沃尔夫出任首席执行官。幸好，为了照顾我们的自尊，关键是第二件：斯蒂芬·沃尔夫在这家航空公司的成就，非同寻常。

1997.english:
There still is much to do at US Airways, but survival is no longer an issue. Consequently, the company made up the dividend arrearages on our preferred during 1997, adding extra payments to compensate us for the delay we suffered. The company's common stock, furthermore, has risen from a low of $4 to a recent high of $73.

Our preferred has been called for redemption on March 15. But the rise in the company's stock has given our conversion rights, which we thought worthless not long ago, great value. It is now almost certain that our US Airways shares will produce a decent profit -- that is, if my cost for Maalox is excluded -- and the gain could even prove indecent.
1997.chinese:
美国航空仍有很多工作要做，但生存已不再是问题。因此，1997年，公司补齐了优先股欠付股息，并额外付款，补偿我们经历的延迟。此外，普通股已从4美元低点，涨到最近73美元的高点。

我们的优先股已被通知，将于3月15日赎回。不过，普通股上涨，使不久前还以为毫无用处的转换权，变得价值可观。如今，几乎可以肯定，这笔美国航空投资会取得一笔体面的利润，前提是不把我买Maalox胃药的钱算进去；说不定，赚得还会多到“不体面”。

1997.english:
Next time I make a big, dumb decision, Berkshire shareholders will know what to do: Phone Mr. Wolf.

---

In addition to the convertible preferreds, we purchased one other private placement in 1991, $300 million of American Express Percs. This security was essentially a common stock that featured a tradeoff in its first three years: We received extra dividend payments during that period, but we were also capped in the price appreciation we could realize. Despite the cap, this holding has proved extraordinarily profitable thanks to a move by your Chairman that combined luck and skill -- 110% luck, the balance skill.
1997.chinese:
下次我再作一个又大又蠢的决定，伯克希尔股东就知道该怎么办了：给沃尔夫先生打电话。

---

除了可转换优先股，1991年我们还买过另一笔私募证券，即3亿美元的美国运通PERCS。它本质上是普通股，但头三年有一项交换条件：我们多收股息，同时可获得的股价升值也有上限。尽管有上限，这项持仓仍然格外赚钱，得益于各位董事长一招运气与本领相结合的行动——110%靠运气，剩下的靠本领。

1997.english: Our Percs were due to convert into common stock in August 1994, and in the month before I was mulling whether to sell upon conversion. One reason to hold was Amex's outstanding CEO, Harvey Golub, who seemed likely to maximize whatever potential the company had (a supposition that has since been proved -- in spades). But the size of that potential was in question: Amex faced relentless competition from a multitude of card-issuers, led by Visa. Weighing the arguments, I leaned toward sale.
1997.chinese: PERCS原定1994年8月转为普通股，前一个月，我一直琢磨转换后要不要卖。一项支持持有的理由，是美国运通出色的首席执行官哈维·戈卢布，他看上去很可能把公司潜力发挥到最大；后来，这一点得到了十足证明。不过，潜力究竟有多大，仍有疑问：美国运通面对Visa带头、众多发卡机构接踵而来的激烈竞争。权衡以后，我倾向卖出。

1997.english: Here's where I got lucky. During that month of decision, I played golf at Prouts Neck, Maine with Frank Olson, CEO of Hertz. Frank is a brilliant manager, with intimate knowledge of the card business. So from the first tee on I was quizzing him about the industry. By the time we reached the second green, Frank had convinced me that Amex's corporate card was a terrific franchise, and I had decided not to sell. On the back nine I turned buyer, and in a few months Berkshire owned 10% of the company.
1997.chinese: 运气就在这里来了。在那个作决定的月份，我与赫兹首席执行官弗兰克·奥尔森，在缅因州普劳茨内克打高尔夫。弗兰克是个出色的管理者，对信用卡业务了如指掌。因此，从第一个发球台起，我就不断请教行业情况。走到第二洞果岭时，他已让我相信，美国运通公司卡是一项极好的特许经营业务，我也决定不卖了。打后九洞时，我转而想买；几个月内，伯克希尔便持有公司10%的股份。

1997.english:
We now have a $3 billion gain in our Amex shares, and I naturally feel very grateful to Frank. But George Gillespie, our mutual friend, says that I am confused about where my gratitude should go. After all, he points out, it was he who arranged the game and assigned me to Frank's foursome.

## Quarterly Reports to Shareholders

In last year's letter, I described the growing costs we incur in mailing quarterly reports and the problems we have encountered in delivering them to "street-name" shareholders. I asked for your opinion about the desirability of our continuing to print reports, given that we now publish our quarterly and annual communications on the Internet, at our site, www.berkshirehathaway.com. Relatively few shareholders responded, but it is clear that at least a small number who want the quarterly information have no interest in getting it off the Internet. Being a life-long sufferer from technophobia, I can empathize with this group.
1997.chinese:
如今，美国运通持仓有30亿美元收益，我自然十分感谢弗兰克。不过，我们共同的朋友乔治·吉莱斯皮说，我把该感谢谁弄糊涂了。他指出，毕竟，安排那场球、把我与弗兰克分进同一个四人组的，是他。

## 致股东的季度报告

去年信中，我说起邮寄季报的费用日增，以及送达以经纪人名义持股的股东时遇到的问题。既然季度与年度沟通资料，都已在www.berkshirehathaway.com网站公布，我便请各位说说，是否值得继续印刷报告。回复的股东不多，不过很清楚，至少有一小部分想看季度资料的人，对上网获取毫无兴趣。本人一辈子饱受科技恐惧症困扰，对他们深有同感。

1997.english:
The cost of publishing quarterlies, however, continues to balloon, and we have therefore decided to send printed versions only to shareholders who request them. If you wish the quarterlies, please complete the reply card that is bound into this report. In the meantime, be assured that all shareholders will continue to receive the annual report in printed form.

Those of you who enjoy the computer should check out our home page. It contains a large amount of current information about Berkshire and also all of our annual letters since 1977. In addition, our website includes links to the home pages of many Berkshire subsidiaries. On these sites you can learn more about our subsidiaries' products and -- yes -- even place orders for them.
1997.chinese:
不过，季报出版成本仍不断膨胀，因此我们决定，只向提出要求的股东发送印刷版。想收到季报，请填好装订在本报告里的回执卡。与此同时，各位可以放心：所有股东，仍会继续收到印刷年报。

喜欢电脑的股东，请看看我们的主页。那里有大量伯克希尔近况，以及自1977年以来全部年度致股东信。此外，网站也链接了许多子公司的主页；在那里，可以进一步了解它们的产品，而且——没错——还可以直接下订单。

1997.english: We are required to file our quarterly information with the SEC no later than 45 days after the end of each quarter. One of our goals in posting communications on the Internet is to make this material information -- in full detail and in a form unfiltered by the media -- simultaneously available to all interested parties at a time when markets are closed. Accordingly, we plan to send our 1998 quarterly information to the SEC on three Fridays, May 15, August 14, and November 13, and on those nights to post the same information on the Internet. This procedure will put all of our shareholders, whether they be direct or "street-name," on an equal footing. Similarly, we will post our 1998 annual report on the Internet on Saturday, March 13, 1999, and mail it at about the same time.
1997.chinese: 我们必须在每季度结束后45天以内，向美国证券交易委员会提交季度资料。把沟通内容放上网，一个目标就是在休市时，使所有感兴趣的人，能够同时获得完整、未经媒体过滤的重要信息。因此，我们计划于1998年5月15日、8月14日及11月13日这三个星期五，向证券交易委员会提交季度资料，并在当晚，把相同资料公布到网上。这种做法，让直接登记及以经纪人名义持股的股东，都处在同一起跑线上。同样，我们将在1999年3月13日星期六，把1998年年报放上网，并在大致同一时间寄出。

1997.english:
## Shareholder-Designated Contributions

About 97.7% of all eligible shares participated in Berkshire's 1997 shareholder-designated contributions program. Contributions made were $15.4 million, and 3,830 charities were recipients. A full description of the program appears on pages 52 - 53.

Cumulatively, over the 17 years of the program, Berkshire has made contributions of $113.1 million pursuant to the instructions of our shareholders. The rest of Berkshire's giving is done by our subsidiaries, which stick to the philanthropic patterns that prevailed before they were acquired (except that their former owners themselves take on the responsibility for their personal charities). In aggregate, our subsidiaries made contributions of $8.1 million in 1997, including in-kind donations of $4.4 million.
1997.chinese:
## 股东指定捐款

1997年伯克希尔股东指定捐款计划，约有97.7%的合资格股份参加。捐款总额1,540万美元，受赠慈善机构3,830家。完整计划见第52—53页。

计划实行17年来，伯克希尔按股东指示，累计捐出1.131亿美元。其余捐赠，由子公司进行；它们延续收购前的慈善做法，但原所有者个人慈善活动，改由他们自己负责。1997年，子公司合计捐赠810万美元，其中包括价值440万美元的实物捐赠。

1997.english: Every year a few shareholders miss out on our contributions program because they don't have their shares registered in their own names on the prescribed record date or because they fail to get the designation form back to us within the 60-day period allowed. Charlie and I regret this. But if replies are received late, we have to reject them because we can't make exceptions for some shareholders while refusing to make them for others.
1997.chinese: 每年，都有少数股东错过捐款计划：有的在规定登记日，未把股票登记在自己名下；有的未在允许的60天内，把指定表格寄还。查理和我对此遗憾。不过，回复迟到，我们只能拒绝，因为不能为某些股东破例，却不给其他股东同样待遇。

1997.english:
To participate in future programs, you must own Class A shares that are registered in the name of the actual owner, not the nominee name of a broker, bank or depository. Shares not so registered on August 31, 1998, will be ineligible for the 1998 program. When you get the contributions form from us, return it promptly so that it does not get put aside or forgotten.

## The Annual Meeting

Woodstock Weekend at Berkshire will be May 2-4 this year. The finale will be the annual meeting, which will begin at 9:30 a.m. on Monday, May 4. Last year we met at Aksarben Coliseum, and both our staff and the crowd were delighted with the venue. There was only one crisis: The night before the meeting, I lost my voice, thereby fulfilling Charlie's wildest fantasy. He was crushed when I showed up the next morning with my speech restored.
1997.chinese:
参加今后计划，必须持有A类股，并登记在实际所有者名下，而非经纪人、银行或存托机构的代名人名下。截至1998年8月31日，未作这种登记的股份，将无资格参加1998年计划。收到捐款表格时，请尽快寄回，免得放在一旁，最后忘了。

## 股东大会

今年伯克希尔的“伍德斯托克周末”，定于5月2—4日。压轴节目是股东大会，5月4日星期一上午9时30分开始。去年在阿克萨本体育馆举办，员工与观众都很满意场地。只有一场危机：大会前夜，我嗓子哑了，查理最狂野的梦想就这样实现了。第二天早上，我恢复声音到场时，他大受打击。

1997.english:
Last year about 7,500 attended the meeting. They represented all 50 states, as well as 16 countries, including Australia, Brazil, Israel, Saudi Arabia, Singapore and Greece. Taking into account several overflow rooms, we believe that we can handle more than 11,000 people, and that should put us in good shape this year even though our shareholder count has risen significantly. Parking is ample at Aksarben; acoustics are excellent; and seats are comfortable.

The doors will open at 7 a.m. on Monday and at 8:30 we will again feature the world premiere of a movie epic produced by Marc Hamburg, our CFO. The meeting will last until 3:30, with a short break at noon. This interval will permit the exhausted to leave unnoticed and allow time for the hardcore to lunch at Aksarben's concession stands. Charlie and I enjoy questions from owners, so bring up whatever is on your mind.
1997.chinese:
去年约7,500人参会，来自全美50个州，以及澳大利亚、巴西、以色列、沙特阿拉伯、新加坡、希腊等16个国家。算上几个分会场，我们相信能容纳超过11,000人；即使股东人数显著增加，今年也应绰绰有余。阿克萨本停车位充足，音响效果很好，座椅舒适。

星期一早上7时开门，8时30分，将再次奉上由首席财务官马克·汉堡制作的电影巨作，举行全球首映。大会将持续至下午3时30分，中午短暂休息，让精疲力尽的人悄悄退场，也让铁杆股东有时间去体育馆餐饮摊位吃午饭。查理和我喜欢所有者提问，所以，心里有什么，尽管问。

1997.english: Berkshire products will again be for sale in the halls outside the meeting room. Last year -- not that I pay attention to this sort of thing -- we again set sales records, moving 2,500 pounds of See's candy, 1,350 pairs of Dexter shoes, $75,000 of World Books and related publications, and 888 sets of Quikut knives. We also took orders for a new line of apparel, featuring our Berkshire logo, and sold about 1,000 polo, sweat, and T-shirts. At this year's meeting, we will unveil our 1998 collection.
1997.chinese: 会场外走廊，仍将出售伯克希尔产品。去年——当然，我并不在意这种事——销售又创纪录：2,500磅喜诗糖果、1,350双德克斯特鞋、75,000美元的世界图书及相关出版物，还有888套Quikut刀具。我们还接受了新推出的伯克希尔标志服饰订单，卖出约1,000件Polo衫、运动衫和T恤。今年大会，我们将发布1998年系列。

1997.english: GEICO will again be on hand with a booth staffed by star associates from its regional offices. Find out whether you can save money by shifting your auto insurance to GEICO. About 40% of those who check us out learn that savings are possible. The proportion is not 100% because insurers differ in their underwriting judgments, with some favoring drivers who live in certain geographical areas and work at certain occupations more than we do. We believe, however, that we more frequently offer the low price than does any other national carrier selling insurance to all comers. In the GEICO informational material that accompanies this report, you will see that in 38 states we now offer a special discount of as much as 8% to our shareholders. We also have applications pending that would extend this discount to drivers in other states.
1997.chinese: GEICO照例会设展位，由各地区办事处的明星员工接待。来看看，把汽车保险转到GEICO，能不能省钱。查询的人中，约40%会发现可以省。之所以不是100%，是因为各保险公司的承保判断不同；某些公司，对某些地区、某些职业的驾驶者，比我们更青睐。不过，我们相信，与其他面向公众销售保险的全国性保险公司相比，我们给出最低价格的次数更多。随本报告附上的GEICO资料会说明，如今在38个州，股东可享最高8%的特别折扣。我们也正在申请，把优惠扩展到其他州的驾驶者。

1997.english: An attachment to the proxy material that is enclosed with this report explains how you can obtain the card you will need for admission to the meeting. We expect a large crowd, so get plane, hotel and car reservations promptly. American Express (800-799-6634) will be happy to help you with arrangements. As usual, we will have buses at the larger hotels that will take you to and from the meeting and also deliver you to Nebraska Furniture Mart, Borsheim's and the airport after its conclusion. You are likely, however, to find a car handy.
1997.chinese: 随本报告寄出的委托投票材料附件，会说明如何领取入场卡。预计人很多，请尽快预订机票、酒店及租车。美国运通（800-799-6634）很乐意协助安排。照例，大酒店会有巴士接送大会；结束后，也送各位去内布拉斯加家具卖场、波仙珠宝与机场。不过，有辆车多半仍会方便。

1997.english:
NFM's main store, located on a 75-acre site about a mile from Aksarben, is open from 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. on weekdays, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Saturdays, and noon to 6 p.m. on Sundays. During the period from May 1 to May 5, shareholders who present NFM with the coupon that will accompany their meeting ticket will be entitled to a discount that is otherwise restricted to its employees.

Borsheim's normally is closed on Sunday but will be open for shareholders from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. on May 3rd. Last year was our second-best shareholder's day, exceeded only by 1996's. I regard this slippage as an anomaly and hope that you will prove me right this year. Charlie will be available for autographs. He smiles, however, only if the paper he signs is a Borsheim's sales ticket. Shareholders who wish to visit on Saturday (10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.) or on Monday (10 a.m.-8 p.m.) should be sure to identify themselves as Berkshire owners so that Susan Jacques, Borsheim's CEO, can make you especially welcome. Susan, I should add, had a fabulous year in 1997. As a manager, she is everything that an owner hopes for.
1997.chinese:
内布拉斯加家具卖场主店，占地75英亩，距阿克萨本约一英里。工作日上午10时至晚上9时营业，星期六上午10时至下午6时，星期日中午12时至下午6时。5月1—5日期间，股东出示随会议入场票寄出的优惠券，即可享受通常只供员工使用的折扣。

波仙珠宝星期日通常休息，不过5月3日，将于上午10时至下午6时为股东开放。去年是第二好的股东日，仅次于1996年。我把这点退步视为偶然，希望各位今年能证明我是对的。查理会在那里签名；不过，只有签在波仙销售单上，他才会微笑。想在星期六上午10时至下午5时30分，或星期一上午10时至晚上8时光顾的股东，请说明自己是伯克希尔所有者，让首席执行官苏珊·雅克斯好好欢迎各位。还要补一句，苏珊1997年干得非常漂亮；作为管理者，她具备所有者希望的一切。

1997.english:
On Sunday afternoon we will also have a special treat for bridge players in the mall outside of Borsheim's. There, Bob Hamman -- a legend of the game for more than three decades -- will take on all comers. Join in and dazzle Bob with your skill.

My favorite steakhouse, Gorat's, opens one Sunday a year -- for Berkshire shareholders on the night before the annual meeting. Last year the restaurant started serving at 4 p.m. and finished about 1:30 a.m, an endurance trial that was the result of taking 1,100 reservations vs. a seating capacity of 235. If you make a reservation and then can't attend, be sure to let Gorat's know promptly, since it goes to great effort to help us and we want to reciprocate. You can make reservations beginning on April 1st (but not before) by calling 402-551-3733. Last year I had to leave Gorat's a little early because of my voice problem, but this year I plan to leisurely savor every bite of my rare T-bone and double order of hash browns.
1997.chinese:
星期日下午，波仙门外商场里，还为桥牌爱好者准备了特别节目。三十多年来的桥牌传奇鲍勃·哈曼，将在那里接受任何人的挑战。来吧，让鲍勃见识各位高超的牌技。

我最喜欢的戈拉特牛排馆，每年只在一个星期日开门，就是股东大会前夜，为伯克希尔股东营业。去年，餐馆下午4时开始，直到凌晨约1时30分才结束，堪称耐力测试：店里只有235个座位，却接下1,100个预约。若订了位却不能来，请务必及时通知；戈拉特为帮助我们下足功夫，我们也希望投桃报李。4月1日起可以致电402-551-3733订位，但别提前打。去年嗓子有问题，我不得不早走；今年打算从容享用一分熟T骨牛排与双份薯饼，每一口都好好品味。

1997.english: After this warmup, Charlie and I will head for the Dairy Queen on 114th, just south of Dodge. There are 12 great Dairy Queens in metropolitan Omaha, but the 114th Street location is the best suited to handle the large crowd that we expect. South of the property, there are hundreds of parking spaces on both sides of the street. Also, this Dairy Queen will extend its Sunday hours to 11 p.m. in order to accommodate our shareholders.
1997.chinese: 热身之后，查理和我会去道奇路以南、第114街上的冰雪皇后。奥马哈都会区有12家很棒的冰雪皇后，不过，第114街店最适合接待预期的大批股东。店面南边，街道两侧有数百个停车位；为了招待股东，这家店星期日还会延长营业到晚上11时。

1997.english: The 114th Street operation is now run by two sisters, Coni Birge and Deb Novotny, whose grandfather put up the building in 1962 at what was then the outer edge of the city. Their mother, Jan Noble, took over in 1972, and Coni and Deb continue as third generation owner-managers. Jan, Coni and Deb will all be on hand Sunday evening, and I hope that you meet them. Enjoy one of their hamburgers if you can't get into Gorat's. And then, around eight o'clock, join me in having a Dusty Sundae for dessert. This item is a personal specialty -- the Dairy Queen will furnish you a copy of my recipe -- and will be offered only on Shareholder Sunday.
1997.chinese: 第114街店如今由科妮·伯奇与黛布·诺沃特尼姐妹经营。1962年，她们的祖父在当时的城市边缘建起店面；1972年，母亲简·诺布尔接手，如今科妮与黛布作为第三代所有者兼管理者，继续经营。星期日晚上，简、科妮与黛布都会到场，希望各位认识她们。如果进不了戈拉特，可以在这里享用汉堡。晚上8点左右，再与我一起，来份“尘土圣代”当甜点。这是我的私家拿手配方，店里会送各位一份食谱，而且只在股东星期日供应。

1997.english:
The Omaha Royals and Albuquerque Dukes will play baseball on Saturday evening, May 2nd, at Rosenblatt Stadium. As usual, your Chairman, shamelessly exploiting his 25% ownership of the team, will take the mound. But this year you will see something new.

In past games, much to the bafflement of the crowd, I have shaken off the catcher's first call. He has consistently asked for my sweeping curve, and I have just as regularly resisted. Instead, I have served up a pathetic fast ball, which on my best day was clocked at eight miles per hour (with a following wind).
1997.chinese:
5月2日星期六晚上，奥马哈皇家队将与阿尔伯克基公爵队，在罗森布拉特球场打棒球。照例，各位的董事长，将厚着脸皮利用自己25%的球队所有权，登上投手丘。不过，今年会有新鲜玩意给各位看。

过去几次比赛，我总摇头拒绝捕手的第一个暗号，观众很困惑。他老是要我投那个横扫式曲球，我也总是坚持不投。相反，我送上的是惨不忍睹的快速球；我状态最好的一天，测速每小时八英里，还得顺风。

1997.english: There's a story behind my unwillingness to throw the curve ball. As some of you may know, Candy Cummings invented the curve in 1867 and used it to great effect in the National Association, where he never won less than 28 games in a season. The pitch, however, drew immediate criticism from the very highest of authorities, namely Charles Elliott, then president of Harvard University, who declared, "I have heard that this year we at Harvard won the baseball championship because we have a pitcher who has a fine curve ball. I am further instructed that the purpose of the curve ball is to deliberately deceive the batter. Harvard is not in the business of teaching deception." (I'm not making this up.)
1997.chinese: 不愿投曲球，背后有个故事。有些股东或许知道，坎迪·卡明斯1867年发明了曲球，并在全国协会比赛中大显身手，一个赛季从未少赢28场。不过，这种投法，立刻受到最高权威的批评，那就是当时的哈佛大学校长查尔斯·埃利奥特。他宣称：“听说今年我们哈佛赢得棒球冠军，因为有一名投手，曲球投得很好。又有人告诉我，曲球的目的，是蓄意欺骗打者。哈佛不教人欺骗。”（这可不是我编的。）

1997.english:
Ever since I learned of President Elliott's moral teachings on this subject, I have scrupulously refrained from using my curve, however devastating its effect might have been on hapless batters. Now, however, it is time for my karma to run over Elliott's dogma and for me to quit holding back. Visit the park on Saturday night and marvel at the majestic arc of my breaking ball.

Our proxy statement includes information about obtaining tickets to the game. We will also provide an information packet describing the local hot spots, including, of course, those 12 Dairy Queens.

Come to Omaha -- the cradle of capitalism -- in May and enjoy yourself.

Warren E. Buffett February 27, 1998                               Chairman of the Board
1997.chinese:
自从知道埃利奥特校长在这件事上的道德教诲，我就严格克制，不投曲球，尽管它原本可能把那些倒霉打者收拾得很惨。不过，如今该让我的“业力”碾过埃利奥特的“教条”，别再藏着掖着了。星期六晚上来球场，欣赏我那变化球气势恢宏的弧线吧。

委托投票说明书包含领取球票的资料。我们还会提供一个介绍本地热门去处的资料包，当然包括那12家冰雪皇后。

五月来奥马哈——资本主义的摇篮——好好玩吧。

沃伦·E·巴菲特  
董事会主席  
1998年2月27日

1998.english:
BERKSHIRE HATHAWAY INC.

To the Shareholders of Berkshire Hathaway Inc.:

Our gain in net worth during 1998 was $25.9 billion, which increased the per-share book value of both our Class A and Class B stock by 48.3%. Over the last 34 years (that is, since present management took over) per-share book value has grown from $19 to $37,801, a rate of 24.7% compounded annually.* Normally, a gain of 48.3% would call for handsprings — but not this year. Remember Wagner, whose music has been described as better than it sounds? Well, Berkshire’s progress in 1998 — though more than satisfactory — was not as good as it looks. That’s because most of that 48.3% gain came from our issuing shares in acquisitions. To explain: Our stock sells at a large premium over book value, which means that any issuing of shares we do — whether for cash or as consideration in a merger — instantly increases our per-share book-value figure, even though we’ve earned not a dime. What happens is that we get more per-share book value in such transactions than we give up. These transactions, however, do not deliver us any immediate gain in per-share intrinsic value, because in this respect what we give and what we get are roughly equal. And, as Charlie Munger, Berkshire’s Vice Chairman and my partner, and I can’t tell you too often (though you may feel that we try), it’s the per-share gain in intrinsic value that counts rather than the per-share gain in book value. Though Berkshire’s intrinsic value grew very substantially in 1998, the gain fell well short of the 48.3% recorded for book value. Nevertheless, intrinsic value still far exceeds book value. (For a more extensive discussion of these terms, and other investment and accounting concepts, please refer to our Owner’s Manual, on pages 56-64, in which we set forth our owner-related business principles. Intrinsic value is discussed on pages 61 and 62.) We entered 1999 with the best collection of businesses and managers in our history. The two companies we acquired in 1998, General Re and Executive Jet, are first-class in every way — more about both later — and the performance of our operating businesses last year exceeded my hopes. GEICO, once again, simply shot the lights out. On the minus side, several of the public companies in which we have major investments experienced significant operating shortfalls that neither they nor I anticipated early in the year. Consequently, our equity portfolio did not perform nearly as well as did the S&P 500. The problems of these companies are almost certainly temporary, and Charlie and I believe that their long-term prospects are excellent. In our last three annual reports, we furnished you a table that we regard as central to estimating Berkshire's intrinsic value. In the updated version of that table, which follows, we trace our two key components of value, including General Re on a pro-forma basis as if we had owned it throughout the year. The first column lists our per-share ownership of investments (including cash and equivalents but excluding securities held in our financial products operation) and the second column shows our per-share earnings from Berkshire's operating businesses before taxes and purchase-accounting adjustments (discussed on pages 62 and 63), but after all interest and corporate expenses. The second column excludes all dividends, interest and capital gains that we realized from the investments presented in the first column. In effect, the columns show how Berkshire would look if it were split into two parts, with one entity holding our investments and the other operating all of our businesses and bearing all corporate costs.

*All figures used in this report apply to Berkshire's A shares, the successor to the only stock that the company had outstanding before 1996. The B shares have an economic interest equal to 1/30th that of the A.
